english: Yes, many wild weeds host plant viruses without dying from them. Insects feed on these infected weeds and then move into your field, transferring the hidden germs directly into your crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, koo mli jwɛi babaoo ŋmɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei amli ni amɛgbooo kɛjɛɛɛ mli. Kplukai yeɔ jwɛi ni hela emɔ amɛ nɛɛ ni amɛfãa kɛyaa oŋmɔji amli. Kɛtsɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni okɛwoɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cocoa trees turning yellow and the branches swelling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ aniji miifu lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease, which is caused by a virus. Small insects called mealybugs carry the virus from tree to tree, which attacks the tree's internal flow of nutrients and causes the stems to swell.
ga: Enɛ ji kookoo tsei ni efuu lɛ he okadi, ni muawai kɛbaa. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs lɛ hiɛɔ hela nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. ni tutuaa niyenii mli nibii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Why do my cassava leaves look twisted with patchy yellow spots on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Your cassava likely has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is caused by a virus. It is spread by small whiteflies that suck sap from sick plants and inject the virus into healthy ones, making the leaves grow distorted.
ga: Ekolɛ o-cassava lɛ yɛ cassava mosaic hela, ni hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛbaa. Whiteflies bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛwoɔ hela lɛ amɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai ni etsake

english: If my crop gets a viral disease, will adding more fertilizer cure it?
ga: Kɛji akɛ hela ko emɔ mi tsei lɛ Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaha esɛɛ aya?

english: No, fertilizer cannot cure a plant virus. Fertilizer gives food to the plant, but the virus stays inside the plant's sap for its entire life. Adding fertilizer might help it survive a bit longer, but it will still carry and spread the disease.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ atsa tsei amli helai. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii. Shi hela lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nu mli yɛ ewala be fɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ awo lɛ fɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua lɛ ni ehi shi be fioo, shi ebaanyɛ ehiɛ helai lolo ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: What is the best thing to do if I find a crop in my field that has a viral disease?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ofee kɛji ona ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni hela ko ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ yɔɔ mli?

english: The safest step is to uproot the infected plant completely and destroy it away from the field. Because there is no chemical cure for plant viruses, removing sick plants stops insects from spreading the germ to the rest of your healthy crops.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ji ni ajie tsei fɛɛ ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni akpata amɛhiɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsofai bɛ ni akɛ tsaa muawai yɛ tsei amli. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa kooloi bibii agbɛ hela amɛshwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves that create protective shade and retain soil moisture, helping young cocoa plants survive during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo buɔ mɔ he ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How does planting beans around my maize help my crops grow better without buying extra fertilizer?
ga: Beans ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te ŋmãa baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe ŋmãa babaoo?

english: Beans and other legumes naturally take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Nearby maize plants feed on this stored nitrogen to grow taller and greener without chemical inputs.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Ejɛɔ ebɔɔ su mli ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellow maize leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to create energy. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy green foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tsei ni he hiaa koni akɛfee hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does burning cleared weeds harm my farmland before I plant?
ga: Te jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ yeɔ midumɔi lɛ awui tɛŋŋ dani miduɔ lɛ?

english: Burning kills useful earthworms and soil organisms that break down organic matter into crop nutrients. It also strips the soil of natural moisture and leaves topsoil exposed to erosion.
ga: Shãa kpataa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni gbálaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli kɛfeɔ tsei amli niyenii lɛ ahiɛ. Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my land dry out quickly just a day or two after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ pɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɔ waa gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ pɛ lɛ, mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Soil dries rapidly when it lacks organic matter like dry grass mulch or compost. Covering the soil around crop stems with dry mulch blocks direct heat from the sun and traps moisture in the ground longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaatsi dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: What causes my cassava leaves to curl up and show yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Leaf curling with yellow spots is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant stem varieties is the best way to keep your cassava farm healthy.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji cassava mosaic hela ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Tsoi srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha o-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars destroying the funnel leaves of my young maize crop so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miifite mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni ji cone lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that targets young maize leaves. Inspecting plants early and applying recommended bio-pesticides like neem tree extracts early in the morning can stop them from destroying the yield.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni amɛtutuaa ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Tsei amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ neem tso mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii leebi lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ akafite eŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants get stressed from extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent watering and slight shade during peak heat help flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo fioo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ tomato nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out small and bent instead of long and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep, stone-free soil to stretch out easily. Clay soil or hard soil mounds restrict the tuber from expanding naturally, resulting in small and misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni tɛi bɛ nɔ koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa loo gɔji baatsi bulb lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni efite.

english: Hybrid seeds lose their special growth vigor and yield capacity after the first harvest. Replanting saved hybrid seeds often results in small cobs, uneven crop growth, and lower yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ laajeɔ amɛdalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo nyɛmɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ, dumɔwui bibii baa. Tsei adalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ ba shi

english: Why do I need to clear the grass and build high mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ ni matswa gɔŋ dani madu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep underground and need soft, loose earth to expand. Building mounds loosens hard soil so the yam roots can easily grow big and long without hitting tough ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Gɔŋ ni ooofee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, sweet potato shishifãi baanyɛ adara ni amɛfee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa.

english: How do I know if my farmland is better suited for growing cassava or maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Maize needs rich soil and plenty of water to give good yields. Cassava is much tougher and can still survive and produce food in poorer, drier soil where maize might fail.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ nu babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ewo ŋmãa kpakpa. Cassava wa waa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi ni ewo niyenii yɛ shikpɔji ni ohiafoi yɔɔ nɔ, ni egbi yɛ he ni ŋmãa baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I cut down all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like baby plants that easily burn under strong, direct sunlight. Keeping taller trees provides the shade and cool soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii tamɔ tsei bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ aná hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehe miihia ni kookoo bibioo lɛ ahi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why should I leave space between my pepper plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ pepper tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients, leading to small harvests. Spacing them lets air flow through, which keeps them healthy and prevents diseases.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii, ni no haa yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa. He ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua bo ni oná hewalɛ, ni ebaatsi helai srɔtoi anaa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my cowpea plants without turning into bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pea pods lɛ?

english: Bean plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, hot dry winds, or a lack of water. The plant sheds flowers to save its energy until conditions improve.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing tall with dark green leaves but no tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miida ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi tomato bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them spend all their energy growing stems and leaves instead of flowers. Tomatoes need balanced nutrients like phosphorus and potassium to produce fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii kɛ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium he miihia tomato koni enyɛ ewo aduawai.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain can be a false alarm followed by weeks of dry sun. If the seed sprouts and the soil dries out completely, the tender young shoot will dry up and die.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee amale ŋmɛlɛtswaa. Hulu la ni mli egbi otsii komɛi nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tsobii bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: How do I know when my green plantains are fully ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-plantains eŋɔli lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Plantains are ready to harvest while still green when the fruits look round and full, and the sharp ridges on their skin become smooth and rounded.
ga: Plantains efee klalo akɛ abaakpa be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo, beni aduawai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyi obɔ lɛ. ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes curling up and getting yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled and yellow leaves usually mean the cassava has Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties stops this from happening.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei lɛ yɛ mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛji woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baatsi enɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetables look pale and grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo waa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the food, water, and sunlight that your crops need. When weeds take over, your plants starve and turn pale because they aren't getting enough nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ ye nɔ lɛ Otsei lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ejaakɛ amɛnáaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are suffering from a disease or just lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela emɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ loo nu efo mli kɛkɛ?

english: Diseased cocoa trees often show swelling on stems, red veins on leaves, or black rotting pods, whereas drought-stressed trees usually just drop dry leaves without stem deformities or spots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ fuumɔ kpo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. red lines on leaves or black rotting pods Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hɔmɔ emɔ amɛ lɛ shwieɔ baai ni egboi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ ni efiteɔ loo nɔ ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nɔ ko bɛ amɛhe yɛ amɛtso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut down my cocoa tree completely if only a few branches look sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo cacao tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji akɛ niji fioo komɛi pɛ hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus travel throughout the whole sap system of the tree. Because there is no chemical cure once inside, cutting down the tree is the only way to stop insects from carrying the virus to your healthy trees.
ga: Helai tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ fãa gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsaa helai komɛi bɛ kɛji akɛ abote mli shikome. Tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ kooloi ni kɛ helai baa otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy seasons when there is too much shade and moisture around the trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela, ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i babaoo yɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Can spraying chemicals cure a cocoa tree that is already infected with a virus?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsa kookoo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ momo lɛ?

english: No, spraying chemicals cannot cure a tree that is already infected inside. Chemicals are used to kill the insects that carry the disease so they do not spread it to healthy trees.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsaŋ tso ni hela emɔ lɛ yɛ emli lɛ. Akɛ tsofai gbeɔ koolooi ni kɛ helai baa lɛ. Koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: When is the right time of year to apply chemicals to my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni sa ni mikɛ tsofai baatsu nii yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: In Ghana, spraying is typically done during the rainy season and early minor season when pests like capsids and fungal diseases like Black Pod are most active.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ashɛreɔ tsofa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids kɛ fungal helai tamɔ black pods lɛ tsuɔ nii waa.

english: What is the best tool to use when clearing thick, diseased cocoa trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni ji dɛŋdade ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛ́ ajieɔ kookoo tsei ni mli edɔ ni helai emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Motorized chainsaws are best for cutting thick trunks quickly close to the soil level, while sharp cutlasses work well for clearing smaller branches and brush.
ga: Chainsaw ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha tsei ni mli tse lɛ afolɔ. oya ni ebɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Be mli ni ŋmei ni mli wa Tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha niji bibii kɛ brɔshi ni ajieɔ lɛ.

english: What should I plant on my farm right after cutting down infected cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifo kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: You should plant fast-growing crops like plantain or cassava first to provide shade and income while preparing the land and soil before planting new hybrid cocoa seedlings.
ga: Esa akɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava klɛŋklɛŋ koni eha hulutsoo kɛ shika aba yɛ be mli ni osaa shikpɔŋ kɛ sũ lɛ hu dani odu cocoa hybrid dumɔwui heei.

english: Trees drop flowers when they are under stress from prolonged drought, nutrient-poor soil, or heavy pest attacks, which prevents the tree from supporting pod development.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛyɔɔ hɔmɔ he haomɔ shishi be kakadaŋŋ. shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui waa Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye abua pod lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa roots are shallow and cannot reach deep water. Without temporary shade trees like plantains to protect them, the harsh sun dries out the young leaves and roots.
ga: Kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛyashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ, tamɔ plantains ni buɔ he lɛ Hulu la ni naa wa baaha baai bibii kɛ shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: How long does a new cocoa tree usually take to start giving me pods?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana start producing pods in about 2 to 3 years under good care, unlike older traditional varieties that took 5 or more years.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee tsofai ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ blema kookoo henɔi ni hiɔ shi afii 5 loo nɔ ni fe nakai lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them directly in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or cassava around them creates living shade that protects the young cocoa leaves from scorching and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ he fɛɛ he. Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I heap the soil into high mounds before planting my yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabua sũ ŋmɔtɔ naa dani madu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, soft soil to expand properly underground. Making high earthen mounds loosens the soil, allows the roots to grow large without stress, and prevents heavy rains from rotting the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni haomɔ ko bɛ he. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing on cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and removing affected plants early helps protect the rest of your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ lɛ. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ kɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: What causes small holes in my cabbage leaves, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are caused by small caterpillars like the diamondback moth larva feeding on the leaves. Spraying with safe biological treatments or neem tree extract helps control them without contaminating your crop.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ daimondback ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii, ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem tso mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye amɛnɔ ni ekɛ muji akafite otsei lɛ.

english: How do I know if my maize crops need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If the lower leaves of your maize plants start turning yellow from the tip downward in a V-shape, it means the soil lacks nitrogen. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure will help the plants regain their deep green color and grow strong stalks.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛba shi yɛ V su mli Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛsu ni mli kwɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very big leaves but not producing many fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi ewooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When tomato plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing leaves instead of flowers and fruit. Switching to fertilizers richer in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to bloom and set plenty of tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni amɛdaraa lɛ he nii moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo tomato babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without growing any peppers during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni eduuu pepper ko yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High heat and dry weather stress the pepper plant, forcing it to drop its flowers to save water. Keeping the soil covered with mulch and watering regularly during dry periods helps the plant keep its blossoms so peppers can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni awoɔ lɛ nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ fɔfɔi anɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii anyɛ afee.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops right after the first rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit naturally in the top layer of the soil and are adapted to sprout instantly with the first drops of water. Clearing weeds within the first three to four weeks of planting ensures your crops get the light, water, and food they need to grow taller than the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni atsakeɔ koni ekɛ nu klɛŋklɛŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ akwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Jwɛi ni agbeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ loo ejwɛ ni akɛduɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa onibii lɛ naa la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara fe jwɛi lɛ.

english: Is it good for me to plant beans together with my maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛfata ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very helpful because beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil as plant food. This feeds the maize crop while allowing you to harvest two different foods from the same field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa ejaakɛ ŋmãa jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tsei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii yɛ be mli ni ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii srɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do the maize seeds I save from my previous harvest produce smaller cobs when I replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii kɛji mikɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from high-yielding hybrid maize varieties lose their strength and quality after the first harvest. Buying fresh, certified seeds every planting season ensures uniform crop growth, better disease resistance, and higher yields.
ga: Abɛi ni ji hybrid dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ baa shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui heei, ni ana he odaseyeli hemɔ daa dalɛ be naa nɔmimaa akɛ tso lɛ daa daa. Helai ahewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo baa

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive strong direct sunlight. They need shade from fast-growing crops like plantains or shade trees during their first two years to protect their leaves from scorching and to keep the soil moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam plants make food through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so all the leaves get full sunlight to produce large tubers, while also keeping the leaves away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛfeɔ niyenii. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛfee bulbs agboi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make leaves green and healthy. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a family of plants that trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. Planting them improves soil fertility naturally for crops like maize that need lots of nutrients.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ akwɛmɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the central leaf whorl of maize plants. They eat tender leaves quickly and need early treatment with recommended sprays or biological controls to save the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii oya ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe mra.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that attack the leaves and spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf curl disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni tutuaa baai ni egbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa tsei amli Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai shwiemɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell. If you plant too early, the hot, dry ground will kill the young sprouts before the main rainy season fully established itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ gbeɔ tsei bibii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ shi kwraa.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot in the ground when my field gets flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu ho yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy water settles in the field without draining away, the roots suffocate and fungal diseases attack them, causing them to rot underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ muji lɛ ba shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieee nu kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ tutuaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crops produce very small harvests if I let weeds grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ wooo yibii fioo pɛ kɛji miha jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; they aggressively drink the water and suck up the soil nutrients meant for your crops, leaving your crops weak and reducing your total yield.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ nu kɛ miishɛɛ ni amɛmuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa onibii fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients during flowering, which stops the flowers from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: What does crop booster medicine actually do inside my cocoa tree to make it produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni tsofa ni haa tso lɛ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ yɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ mli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Just like food gives humans energy to work, liquid crop boosters and fertilizers provide essential minerals that trees use to grow strong leaves, fight off sickness, and carry heavy pods.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii haa adesai hewalɛ koni amɛtsu nii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni haa tsei hewalɛ ni ji nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hu haa tsei lɛ amli nibii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. wuɔ hela kɛ tsɔne ni tsii lɛ

english: How can I tell if a farm medicine recommended by a neighbor is safe for my soil and crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔ mli tsofa ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mishikpɔŋ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Approved crop medicines come with clear label instructions from agricultural authorities; unapproved or mixed chemicals can burn plant roots, damage the soil over time, and leave harmful chemical residues on your crop.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni jɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe lɛ. Tsofai loo nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã. Efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. ni oshi tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni eshwɛ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it bad to spray liquid medicine or fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ makɛ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the crop medicine off the leaves and out of the soil into nearby gutters before the roots and leaves have a chance to absorb it, wasting your money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsofa lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa nubui ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. dani shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ shika ni afite lɛ

english: Why do so many small flowers fall off my cocoa tree without ever turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: A tree makes thousands of flowers, but if it lacks enough nutrients, sunlight, or water, it deliberately drops excess flowers so it can focus its energy on keeping just a few pods healthy.
ga: Tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, hulu la loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama fɔfɔi fioo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni eeeha amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do cocoa pods grow directly out of the thick main trunk instead of on thin branches like other fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ tso titri ni mli wa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ niji bibii anɔ tamɔ aduawai krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow flowers and pods on old wood and main trunks so that the tree structure can easily support the heavy weight of full cocoa pods without snapping.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ tso momo kɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ anyɛ akwɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ anɔ mlɛo ni efoŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the ground is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Hot sun makes leaves lose water faster than small roots can suck it up from the soil, so the leaves temporarily wilt to protect themselves from drying out until the cool evening.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. ni abaanyɛ aŋɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli No hewɔ lɛ, baai lɛ gboɔ be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi yɛ fɛ̃i mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is stressed from lack of water, missing key nutrients in the soil, or being attacked by sap-sucking pests that drain its strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Niyenii mli nibii titrii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu mli nu lɛ efite ni ehewalɛ efo mli.

english: Why do black spots spread so quickly across cocoa pods when the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by tiny fungal organisms that love cold, wet weather, and splashing rain drops carry these fungi from pod to pod very quickly across the farm.
ga: Fungi bibii kɛ pods diji baa. No sumɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ. Ni nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ woɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do pests like akate bugs attack soft young cocoa leaves instead of the tough green ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ akademii lɛ tutuaa kookoo baai bibii lɛ moŋ fe baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Young leaves and shoots are tender, filled with sweet sap, and easy for insects to pierce, whereas older leaves are tough, thick, and harder for pests to chew.
ga: Baai lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ. ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii boteɔ mli oya Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, baai ni egbɔ lɛ wa, amɛhe wa, ni ewa akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaye.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when they grow under very thick forest shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ eda yɛ koo ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need controlled sunlight to make food through their leaves; too much shade leaves the tree weak and unable to build up enough energy to make flowers and pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni akudɔɔ koni amɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ amɛfee niyenii. Shade babaoo haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ejie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Excess rainwater washes away key nutrients like nitrogen from the topsoil and suffocates the plant roots, preventing them from taking up the food they need to stay green.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhiɛ amɛŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is typically caused by a viral disease spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, which suck sap from the leaves and weaken the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ

english: What happens if I plant my corn seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the certified seeds from the store perform better than seeds I save from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni shwapoi lɛ ekpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought certified seeds are specially bred for high vigor and disease resistance, whereas saved seeds naturally lose these strong traits after the first harvest.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapoi amli ni awo he odase lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ sui nɛɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mifo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive tender leaves that scorch under direct sunlight; they require taller shade plants to protect them and keep the soil moist while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni kɛlɛ fe hulutsoo ni baabu amɛhe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my pepper plants after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-pepper tsei lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo amɛmli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb nutrients faster than cultivated crops, using the fertilizer to grow rapidly unless they are cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya, ja ajie amɛ oya.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my tomato plants without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil is too dry, or when there are not enough insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ

english: Why does breaking up hard soil deeply help my yam tubers grow much larger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli kwɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ?

english: Loosening hard soil removes physical barriers, allowing root crops like yams to expand smoothly underground and reach deep water during dry periods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii kɛyaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni shishifãi yɔɔ mli, tamɔ sweet potatoes, koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛyashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why does planting beans make my soil better for growing maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii adumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my harvested grains rot so quickly when I store them immediately after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains contain high moisture levels that create an ideal environment for mold and insects; thoroughly sun-drying grains before storage prevents spoilage.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo, ni no haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii. Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani okɛto koni amɛkafite.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young oil palm trees turning yellow and brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on oil palms usually indicate a lack of nitrogen or potassium in the soil, or that the plant is struggling to absorb water during dry periods. Applying balanced fertilizer or organic compost around the root base helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ mu tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo potassium bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli atsu nii ni ebɔle he. Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains or leguminous trees during their first two years to protect their leaves from sunburn and conserve soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains loo legumes mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Koni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl inward during hot periods as a natural survival mechanism to reduce water evaporation from their surface. Once the temperature drops or the field receives water, the leaves naturally uncurl and open up again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni akɛbaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi loo nu ná lɛ Baai lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛgbele ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes small ragged holes to appear on my young maize leaves early in the season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Small holes on tender maize leaves are typically caused by fall armyworms or stalk borers feeding on the leaves. Inspecting the central funnel of the plant early allows you to manage them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fall armyworms loo stem borers ni yeɔ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsuɔ he nii dani efiteɔ he ni edara yɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha nikpamɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ hewɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce many thick leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baai ni mli tse waa shi amɛshishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes yam plants to spend all their energy growing leaves above ground instead of expanding tubers below. Balancing soil nutrients and avoiding heavy nitrogen fertilizers late in the season encourages larger tuber growth.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni aaakwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ajie nitrogen ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ baawo bulbs wuji lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl upward like tiny spoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ spun bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by microscopic pests like mites or thrips sucking sap from the underside of the leaves, or by a viral infection transmitted by insects. Inspecting under the leaves helps identify the pests early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ kooloi amli baa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛbaa lɛ mli Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni anaa tsɛŋemɔ helai mra.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers but no fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fail to set fruit when temperatures get too high, when there is extreme drought stress, or when there are no bees and wind to shake the flowers for pollination. Keeping the soil moist helps protect flower development.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni hɔmɔ ni naa wa ko ba Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy rains and winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not penetrate deep into the soil. As the heavy fruit bunch grows, the top becomes heavy, so propping the stem with strong wooden poles gives them the support needed to stay upright.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eboteee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ da Aduawai lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans on my land improve the growth of my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant dies and decays, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo ni efite. Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight because their young leaves dry out quickly. They need temporary shade crops like plantains planted around them to block the intense heat while they establish deep roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi egbɛ eshwã amɛmli waa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava stems keep growing very tall, but the roots underneath remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daraaa lolo.

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or grow in soil with excess leaves, the plant spends all its energy producing tall stems and green leaves above ground instead of growing tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛji tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo akwɛ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baai babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛma ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tips mean the corn crop is starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food that keeps leaves dark green and healthy so the plant can grow big cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Eji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my young corn leaves have ragged holes and small green dropping inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Efoɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the central leaf funnel of the maize plant to feed on fresh tender leaves while hiding from predators and heat.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii heei yɛ be mli ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ kɛ latsaa lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily after heavy rain or strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have very shallow roots near the surface. When heavy fruit bunches grow on top or when tiny pests in the soil attack the root roots, the plant loses its grip in wet soil and falls over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Beni aduawai akui ni tsii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni baa lɛ ba. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, etutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: When heat is too intense or water is irregular, tomato plants experience stress and drop their flowers to conserve water and energy rather than trying to develop fruits.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa Tomato tsei lɛ naa haomɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes in the ground for my yam leaves to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa tsei koni sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need their leaves lifted high off the damp ground so they can catch full sunlight to make energy, while keeping the leaves away from wet soil fungi and ground pests.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akafee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of food from the soil. Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots, enriching the ground for the next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni akɛ sɛɛnamɔ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt and droop during hot afternoons even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can suck it up from the wet soil. The plant droops temporarily to protect itself from losing more water, usually standing back up by nightfall.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baashwie baai lɛ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu kroko ni baafite lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ ebaanyɛ ete shi yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree branches during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: The Black Pod disease is caused by microscopic fungal germs that spread rapidly in cool, damp, and shady conditions during heavy rains when water droplets bounce germs from the soil or infected trees onto healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei bibioo ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Beni nu mli nui shwieɔ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and turn yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living umbrellas that block the sun and trap moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha sũ lɛ afee hulutsoo ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know which direction to stick cassava stems into the soil when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small buds or 'eyes' along the cassava stem where old leaves used to grow. These buds must point upwards toward the sky; planting them upside down forces the leaves and roots to grow in the wrong direction, severely reducing your harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ he yɛ he ni baai momoi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ be ko ni eho lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu nɔ ko ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Yam vines naturally spread out to catch sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum sun to make food, which then travels down to expand the underground yam tuber for a larger yield.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ koni ekɛha hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsi ohe kɛba shi koni oyagbala sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green. The plant automatically moves the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the young top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli. Tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting cowpeas or beans improves the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans work with tiny soil organisms to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the bean plant finishes growing and decays, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil to naturally fertilize the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni ŋmei tso lɛ daa ni efiteɔ lɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo tsei krokomɛi amli ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crops with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Akɛ jwɛi loo baai ŋmɔɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dried leaves or grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the ground cool, stops moisture from evaporating under the hot sun, and blocks light so weed seeds cannot sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. kɛ hulutsoo koni jwɛi dumɔwui akakwɛ̃.

english: What makes the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly like small cups?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔtɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant sap, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Applying neem oil or soapy water helps clear these insects before they damage the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why am I finding small holes in the middle leaves of my young maize and brown powder inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Powda ko ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ abifao ŋmei baa lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep center funnel of the maize plant to eat new leaves. Catching them early and dropping recommended bio-pesticides or wood ash into the funnel kills the pest.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ bio-insecticide loo tso sũ ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbeɔ lɛ awo funnel lɛ mli lɛ baagbe kooloi lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers, but the flowers just fall off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato?

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Extreme heat damages the flower's pollen, causing the plant to shed flowers to conserve water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ. Ha tsei afɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto nu.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: If too many shoots (suckers) grow around one main plantain stem, they compete for water, fertilizer, and sunlight. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only one strong follower stem, allowing the main tree to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ suckers (shoots) babaoo yɛ ni miida yɛ tso titri kome he lɛ, Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la he. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso titri lɛ woɔ plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen or the ground is soaked with too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving drainage will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛ nu babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, which feeds the land so your next crop grows stronger without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts and Nuts Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. ni ji niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ No hewɔ lɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in soaked soil for too long because they cannot breathe. Planting your cassava on high mounds or ridges helps extra water drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: The first rain is often followed by a sudden dry heat wave that can scorch young sprouts. Waiting until the rainy season fully settles ensures the soil stays wet enough for the seeds to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba shi kwraa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What is making my plantain trees fall over easily before the fruits are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ kwraa?

english: Tiny worms called nematodes or plantain root weevils eat away the root system underground, weakening the tree's hold on the earth. Supporting stems with wooden poles and using clean suckers prevents this.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo plantain shishifãi lɛ yeɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni akɛfiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ ni okɛ tsɔne ni haa nu mli nu ni he tse tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by a plant virus spread by small insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects early and keeping the plants watered stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ni nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off instead of turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaatsɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by hot dry winds, lack of soil water, or attacks by insects like mirids. Keeping good shade trees and controlling pests helps the flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatu ni tswaa lɛ tswa tso lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ he hulutsoo jogbaŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their small green peppers before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ pepper bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ? Ani amɛbaagbee shi dani amɛdara?

english: Pepper plants shed their young fruit when they don't get water regularly or when the sun gets too hot. Mulching the soil with dry leaves helps keep moisture in the ground so the fruits stay on.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baawo yibii bibii kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu daa loo kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi koni aduawai lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are my harvested yams coming out short and crooked instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ kpo kuku ni ebɔleɔ shi moŋ ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams bend and stay small when the soil is too hard or full of rocks. Planting them in deep, loose, well-cleared soil mounds allows the yam tubers to expand straight downwards.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ bibioo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli tse jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya shi.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if I put fertilizer in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops, leaving your crops weak even if you feed the soil well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ okɛ niyenii ha shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ po.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my young cocoa trees when setting up a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei ahe beni miito ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and moisture, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I leave space between my maize seeds instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing allows every plant to get enough food to grow thick stalks and large corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves in dry weather to save water and prevent themselves from dying of thirst. Once the rains return, the plant will grow fresh green leaves and continue producing tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kumai he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baaya nɔ akwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaawo bulbs.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up into small cups instead of spreading out flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up to protect the plant from extreme heat or because tiny insects like whiteflies are sucking their sap. Keeping the soil moist and controlling insects prevents leaf curl.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies miinu amɛ nu lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ kooloi bibii ni akudɔɔ lɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by hot weather, poor watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. nu ni ehiii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet and dark conditions. Pruning excess tree branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm to keep the pods dry.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Why do I see small holes and brown sawdust inside the centers of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar eating the soft leaves inside the stem. Checking your field early and applying recommended sprays keeps the pests from destroying the crop yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Odumɔi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting and smelling bad inside the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Root rot happens when heavy rainwater stays trapped around the roots for too long. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds helps extra water drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ nu ni naa wa hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and a heavy bunch of fruit makes the top of the tree very heavy. Supporting the stem with a strong wooden pole helps the tree carry the weight until harvest.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ haa tso lɛ yiteŋ feɔ tsii waa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etereɔ etsiimɔ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up in the air where they can catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow faster and look greener when planted near the river bank compared to my land further up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ faa lɛ naa lɛ kɛ akɛto mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Soil near rivers stays moist longer and carries dissolved nutrients from upstream, allowing plants to constantly drink water and absorb food without suffering from heat stress.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faai lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ faa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ yaa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nuɔ nu be fɛɛ be ni amɛmuɔ niyenii ni dɔlɛ he haomɔ ko bɛ amɛhe.

english: Is river water safe to pour directly on my young vegetable crops every afternoon?
ga: Ani faa mli nu lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaafɔse mi-aduawai bibii lɛ anɔ daa gbɛkɛ?

english: It is safe, but watering in the hot afternoon causes water droplets on leaves to act like tiny magnifying glasses under the sun, scorching the leaves and evaporating before reaching the roots.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe, shi nu ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni no haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ lasu dani amɛshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize farm curl up into tight tubes during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to hide leaf surfaces from the hot sun, preventing moisture from escaping so the plant doesn't dry out completely.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛteeɔ baa lɛ hiɛ kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje mli. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ egbiko kwraa.

english: How do I know if my crops are suffering from lack of water or if the soil is just too hot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu efo miŋmɔshi nibii amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ?

english: When soil is too hot, plants wilt temporarily in midday but bounce back by evening; when plants lack water, leaves stay limp and start turning yellow or crispy at the edges even at night.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko yɛ shwane mli. Shi efoɔ esɛɛ gbɛkɛ. Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nu lɛ Baai lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛnaagbɛ gbɛkɛ po.

english: Why does covering the soil around my plants with dry palm fronds or grass keep them alive longer in dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmei loo jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, blocks direct sunlight from drying out the ground, keeping the soil cool and locking moisture around the roots so plants drink longer between rains.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni emɔɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anu nu be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ

english: Why do my cassava plants shed all their leaves when the weather stays dry for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves on purpose during drought to stop water from escaping through the leaves, saving its water energy underground in the roots until rain returns.
ga: Akɛ yiŋtoo shwieɔ cassava baai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli. Ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu hewalɛ toɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato plants drop their flowers before producing fruit during hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: High heat damages plant pollen and stresses the crop, causing it to abort flowers to save energy for staying alive rather than trying to feed growing fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen ni ehaa tso lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ akpa nitsumɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni ehi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why do young cocoa pods dry up and turn black on the branch when rainfall becomes irregular?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need steady water to support growing pods; when rainfall stops suddenly, the tree panics and stops feeding young pods, causing them to dry up and die.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni eye ebua amɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa lɛ Tso lɛ he fee lɛ gbeyei ni ekpa ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeli. ha amɛgbi ni amɛgboi

english: Why does fertilizer burn my crop leaves if I apply it when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shãa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai kɛji mikɛwo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires water to dissolve into a gentle liquid food; without water, concentrated fertilizer salts draw remaining moisture out of plant roots, drying them out from the inside.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ nu koni etsɔ nu ni mli jɔ. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baajie ŋmeii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli. ni egbi kɛjɛ emli

english: Why is it better to plant my seeds immediately after the first major rainfall rather than right before it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ fe nɔ ni aaadu dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ?

english: Planting after rain puts seeds in warm, moist soil that softens the seed coat instantly, giving roots the water they need to sprout before the scorching sun dries out the topsoil.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ashishifã lɛ afee blɛoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli gĩɔ.

english: How do I know that my maize crop is fully mature and ready for harvesting from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?
