english: Your maize is mature when the outer leaves turn papery brown and dry up. If you press a kernel with your thumbnail and it feels hard without leaving a soft dent, the crop has finished storing starch and is ready to harvest.
ga: O-corn lɛ egbɔ kɛji kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ woji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmei nyɛ kernel lɛ nɔ ni enu he akɛ ewa ni eshiuuu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbe e-starch lɛ naa naa, ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why does my rice crop grow so well in standing water when my maize crop dies if water collects around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli beni mi-ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special air channels in their stems that bring oxygen from the air down to their roots under water. Maize roots lack these channels, so standing water suffocates maize roots while allowing rice to thrive.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsui krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ gbɛi nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ daa.

english: Why do the stems of my cassava plants grow very tall while the tubers under the soil remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ kɛlɛ shi shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ daraaa lolo lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and tall stems above ground instead of sending sugars down to expand the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu sugar kɛba shi koni ekɛkwɛ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: What happens to my yam crop if I do not train the vines to climb tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mitsɔseee wain tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yam vines need tall sticks to lift their leaves up to capture direct sunlight. If the vines lay flat on the ground, the leaves shade each other and rot against hot wet soil, resulting in much smaller tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia niji kakadaji koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji wain tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa.

english: Why does the main plantain trunk die after I harvest a single bunch of plantain from it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tso titri lɛ gboɔ beni mikpa tso kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain trunk is designed by nature to flower and bear fruit only once. After fruiting, the main trunk naturally dies so that all soil nutrients and moisture can flow into the young suckers growing at its base.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ. Beni tso lɛ wo yibii sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ tso titri lɛ gboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni sũ mli niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ anyɛ atsɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and burn when there are no shade trees near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees like plantain or forest trees to filter the sun, the strong heat damages their delicate leaf cells and dries out their moisture faster than roots can absorb it.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo kooi bɛ ni baatsi hulu la lɛ naa lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli wala yibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why do my tall maize stalks bend over and fall flat on the ground during a strong wind storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei kakadaji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: This is called lodging, and it happens when plants grow too tall and top-heavy due to overcrowded planting, shallow root systems, or excess fertilizer, making them unable to support their own weight in strong winds.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ abobaahe. Ni ebaa kɛji tso ko da tsɔ ni etsii yɛ dumɔ ni adu fe nine, shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛhiɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsiimɔ lɛ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my cowpea plants fall off when heavy rains fall during the flowering stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain physically knocks delicate blossoms off the plant and washes away pollen before insects can fertilize them. Extreme water stress also causes the plant to drop flowers to protect its main stem.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni efoɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli dani kooloi bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛboteɔ gbalashihilɛ mli. Nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa hu haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he.

english: Why are my tomato fruits splitting open on the vine right when they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ tswaa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛji amɛje shishi amɛfee tɔrɔmɔɔ pɛ?

english: Fruit cracking happens when a heavy rainfall or sudden heavy watering follows a dry period. The inside of the tomato absorbs water quickly and expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Yibii amli fãmɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo nu ni hoɔ trukaa babaoo nyiɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why are the fresh leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking into tight clusters?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense response caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of young leaves, or by viruses transmitted by insects that disrupt normal leaf growth.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji hebuu hetoo ni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ kɛbaa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi bibii ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops after preparing my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ beni misaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting depends heavily on the timing of rainfall. You should plant right after the first steady rains begin so the soil has enough moisture to help your seeds germinate and grow.
ga: Dumɔ damɔ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ nɔ waa. Esa akɛ odu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa ni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Why should I clear and divide my farm plot into blocks before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni majara mli awo blɔkii amli dani madu nii?

english: Preparing your land into structured plots or blocks helps manage rainfall runoff, makes weeding much easier, and allows you to care for each section of your farm systematically.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooosaa ofee shikpɔji loo blɔkii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ fã fɛɛ fã nɔ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo naa

english: Can I use seeds saved from my last harvest, or do I need to buy new seeds for the next planting season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: While some crops allow saved seeds, buying fresh, high-quality seeds for a new planting cycle ensures better germination rates and yields healthier plants that resist diseases.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi haa anyɛɔ ahereɔ dumɔwui ayiwala moŋ, shi dumɔwui heei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aheɔ kɛha dumɔwui heei lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ ni eha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni helai nyɛŋ aye amɛnɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops suffer when the rains stop unexpectedly during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ awui kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa yɛ be mli ni amɛduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Crops rely on continuous rainfall to pull nutrients from the soil. When rains fail, the plants get stressed, growth slows down, and the overall harvest is reduced.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ haoɔ, ni no haa amɛdaraa oya. ni ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ ba shi.

english: How often do I need to weed my farm before my crops are ready for harvest?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Weeding should be done regularly throughout the growing period because weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ daa yɛ be fɛɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: What happens to my crops if I leave weeds on my farm for two or three months without clearing them?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mishi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ ni mijieee amɛ?

english: Leaving weeds unchecked for several months allows them to overpower your crops, stealing essential moisture and nutrients, which results in a poor harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi lɛ nyɔji babaoo ni okwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye onibii anɔ kunim. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni ejuɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji nikpamɔ ni ehiii kwraa.

english: How do I determine when my crops have reached full maturity for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ shi kɛha nikpamɔ?

english: Crops show physical signs when ready, such as leaves turning yellow or drying up, which usually happens a few months after proper field care and planting.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii akpo kɛji amɛfee klalo, tamɔ baai ni baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni amɛgbi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli kɛjɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I keep my harvested crops from spoiling quickly after picking them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mikpamɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite oya beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Using a proper food preservation system, such as drying grains thoroughly or storing produce in cool, covered structures, keeps moisture and pests away from your harvest.
ga: Niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni sa, tamɔ ŋmaa ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nibii ni anáa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni aha nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi akabote okpamɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is having a good crop preservation system just as important as growing the food itself?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he hiaa tamɔ bɔ ni gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he hiaa ha lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ? Kɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ?

english: A good preservation system protects your hard work by preventing post-harvest losses, allowing you to safely store food to eat or sell long after the farming season ends.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe lɛ buɔ onitsumɔ ni wa lɛ he kɛtsɔ nibii ni baafite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ ni etsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ niyenii ni obaaye loo ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ toɔ shweshweeshwe be kakadaŋŋ beni okwaayeli be lɛ egbe naa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What should I do on my farm plot once I finish harvesting all my crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji migbe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ naa?

english: After harvesting, you need to prepare the plot again and wait for the next rainy season before buying new seeds to start a fresh planting cycle.
ga: Kɛ́ okpa nikpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, esa akɛ osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ ni omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli koni ohe dumɔwui heei ni okɛje dumɔwui hee shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their foliage burns easily. Plantains grow fast and produce large leaves that act as natural sunshades, protecting the young cocoa plants and keeping the soil cool while they get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo tsɔnei. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and rot during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, which is a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning extra tree branches lets sunlight and fresh air into your farm, which dries out the pods and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela, ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ krokomɛi ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for leafy growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure around the plant roots will help turn the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo kooloi ashishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ fata he lɛ Tse shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, especially nitrogen. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, restoring the soil's fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it a mistake for me to apply fertilizer to my field right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ mawo miŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainwater sweeps across the soil and washes the fertilizer away down the river before your crop's roots have time to drink it in. It is better to apply fertilizer when the ground is already damp after a mild rain.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii kɛyaa faa lɛ mli dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. The leaves use sunlight to manufacture food, which is then sent down underground to grow thick, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni atswa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛ feɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ amɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛdu sweet potato ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the ground around their crops with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi haa he ni amɛduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. The dry grass traps moisture in the soil so it doesn't dry out fast in the hot sun, keeps the ground cool, and stops weeds from popping up around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ enɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: How do I know which way to put cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ odu kɛ bɔ ni ooofee okɛ ŋmei ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: You must ensure the small growth buds on the cassava stem are pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the roots and shoots will struggle to emerge, leading to weak plants and small harvests.
ga: Osumɔɔ ni okwɛ koni hiŋmɛii bibii lɛ Yɛ ŋmei tso ko nɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baaná naagba akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices. Spraying the leaves with neem oil or soapy water helps destroy these tiny pests and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpata tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛɛmɛi ni tsiɔ baai heei adalɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plants do not get enough water. When stressed by heat and thirst, the plant drops its blossoms to save its own life rather than trying to grow fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ kumai ye lɛ Tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni odu aduawai

english: Why do my young cocoa plants die when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that dry out easily under direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates living umbrellas that keep the soil moist and protect the cocoa while it grows.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni ooodu yɛ masɛi Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu kookoo lɛ he be mli ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from intense heat, poor watering, or lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and rich in organic material helps the plant hold its flowers to form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. nu ni ehiii loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong, green leaves. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kompost loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛ, eŋɔli dalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is healthy enough for growing cassava and vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu ŋmei kɛ aduawai?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, feels soft and crumbly in your hand, and holds moisture without staying soaked like thick mud. If soil is too sandy or hard like rock, adding organic manure improves its quality.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. E nuɔ he kaa e ngɛ bɔdɔ nɛ e ngɛ tsɔe ngɛ nine mi. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli tamɔ sũ ni mli edɔ Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋã tsɔ loo ewa tamɔ tɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my tomato seeds too close together in the bed?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ saatso nɔ?

english: When tomatoes grow too close together, they fight each other for light, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin stems and small fruit. Giving plants extra space lets air flow freely, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Beni Tomatoi Daa Abɛŋkɛɔ He Tsɔɔ Tomatoi kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ aduawai bibii. He ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my planted cassava crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi miida oya fe ŋmei tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive wild plants that naturally steal water and soil nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives young cassava roots the space and nourishment they need to expand.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii bibii lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why are holes appearing in my cabbage leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ kaabe baa nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by insects like caterpillars feeding on the crop. Inspecting under the leaves early and using appropriate organic or safe chemical sprays prevents pests from destroying the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ bu yɛ baai amli. Ni oookwɛ baai lɛ ashishi mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni sa ni ji organic loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize as soon as the very first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell that dries out newly sprouted seeds. Waiting until the rainy season fully sets in ensures young seedlings get continuous water to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni haa dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ agbiɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná nu ni yaa nɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so quickly inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ oya yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if stored in hot, unventilated rooms or if bruised during digging. Storing undamaged yams in a cool, shady barn on raised wooden slatted racks keeps air circulating and stops rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli mli loo egbɔjɔ beni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Too atomo ni mli ewo muji yɛ shĩa ni mli ejɔ, ni shade yɔɔ mli yɛ adekai ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli ni ekpaa fitemɔ.

english: How can buying improved seed varieties help my harvest compared to reusing my old saved seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ ni miheɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mikpamɔ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui momo ni akɛto lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ he.

english: Improved seed varieties are specially developed to produce higher yields, resist local plant diseases, and tolerate dry conditions better than older saved seeds.
ga: Afee dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Helai ni tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ amɛhe ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi fe dumɔwui ni etsɛ ni ato lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow before the grain is even ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmaa lɛ shɛɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back their green color and keeps the crop healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal infection called black pod disease, which spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions. Clearing weeds under the trees and pruning excess branches lets sunlight and air flow through, drying out the trees and stopping the fungus.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishi kɛ tsei aniji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsiɔ ŋmeii anaa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without turning into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when they do not get steady water. High heat damages the flower's pollen, causing the plant to drop the blossoms instead of spending energy to grow tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu daa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu tomato.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce the energy needed to grow big tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant feed the root below.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ tso helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛyeɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce plenty of green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pea pods lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cowpea plants put all their energy into making leafy stems instead of flowers. Since cowpeas naturally gather their own nitrogen from the air, extra nitrogen fertilizer encourages leaf growth over bean production.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai ŋmeii amli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsina ŋmeii buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ woɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ moŋ fe ŋmeii ni afeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and hard even after growing in the field for a full year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe wa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ afi muu fɛɛ ekwɛ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, well-aerated soil to expand properly. If the soil is hard-packed, heavy with clay, or lacks key nutrients like potassium, the plant spends its energy just trying to survive rather than swelling its roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wa Shikpɔŋ ni tsii yɛ. loo niyenii mli nibii titrii tamɔ potassium ni bɛ lɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛkɛ ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants stay open with loose leaves instead of forming hard, tight heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ashiɔ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe kɛ baai ni etse amɛhe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee yitsei ni mli wa ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages form tight heads when they get cool soil conditions, consistent moisture, and steady feeding. Hot weather or irregular watering makes the outer leaves spread out loosely instead of wrapping tightly into a firm head.
ga: Kaabeji feɔ yitsei ni wa kɛji akɛ ekɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ. Ha hulutsoo be lɛ aya nɔ ni oha niyenii daa Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be lɛ haa kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo. Mohu ɔ, a fĩɔ lɛ wawɛɛ kɛ peeɔ yi nɛ da si.

english: When soil stays too wet for long periods, roots drown and begin to rot, or soil bacteria attack the stem's water channels. Even though water is present, the damaged roots can no longer carry it up to the plant, causing it to wilt.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛje shishi amɛgboi. Aloo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ moŋ Shi shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ atere amɛ kɛya tso lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ. ha egbi

english: Why are the leaf edges of my plantain trees curling up and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Brown, curling leaf edges on plantains usually mean the plant is losing water faster than its roots can absorb it, often due to dry soil or a lack of potassium. Plantains have huge leaves that need steady moisture and nutrients to stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miifite nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo potassium ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Plantains yɛ baai wuji ni biɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aha amɛ be fɛɛ be koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my seeds sprout quickly after rain while others in the same field fail to come up at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ? be mli ni dumɔwui krokomɛi Yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, eko kwraa kwɛɛɛ?

english: Seeds planted too deep struggle to push through the soil, while seeds planted too close to the surface can dry out in the sun or get eaten by birds. Uniform planting depth and light soil coverage ensure all seeds sprout evenly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ baaná naagba akɛ amɛaatsi kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo okpoi baanyɛ aye amɛ. Dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ ni tamɔ amɛhe kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tseee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ mi-kokoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand the strong sunshine in Ghana; fast-growing plantains provide necessary shade and maintain soil moisture, protecting the cocoa plants during their first two years.
ga: Cocoa tsei nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ naa. Dumɔwui ni miida oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Buu kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stick cuttings at an angle instead of pushing them straight down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni madu shi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle places the buds at the right depth for easy sprouting while allowing roots to expand outward near the soil surface, resulting in larger, easier-to-harvest tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu cassava niji yɛ 45 degree angle mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ashɛ he ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni akpamɔ waaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning purple?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ purple lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks phosphorus, an important nutrient that helps the crop build strong roots and grow properly early in the season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my maize leaves so quickly right after the first rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ fiteɔ mi-corn baai lɛ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths fly into fields on wind currents brought by early rains, laying hundreds of eggs on soft, green maize leaves as soon as the crop sprouts.
ga: Autumn caterpillar ŋmeii lɛ foɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔji amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ. Amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ ŋmeii baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot when the weather is very wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a mold that thrives in dark, damp weather; raindrops splash spores from the soil onto lower pods, spreading the rot quickly through the farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli edɔ mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli kɛyaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. Rot gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high during hot afternoon sun or when the soil dries out completely, as a way to save moisture and stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa Koni eye ebua ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehi shi

english: Curling and yellow leaves on tomato plants in Ghana are commonly caused by a virus spread by whiteflies, tiny white insects that multiply during warm, dry conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii eyɛŋ ni fɔɔ yɛ be mli ni edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and twisted even though the leaves look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni efite lɛ? Ani baai lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo?

english: Yam tubers grow twisted and short when the soil beneath the mound is packed too tightly or filled with stones, which physically stops the roots from expanding smoothly downwards.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ kukuji kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã shishigbɛ mlɛo.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds harvested from last season's hybrid maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mibuɔ dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ he ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid maize lose their vigor in the next generation, producing uneven plants and much lower yields compared to fresh certified hybrid seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa fe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odase lɛ.

english: How do I know my cassava is fully grown and ready for harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open from the expanding tubers below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca feɔ klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crops turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green. When nitrogen runs low, the plant moves what little it has from its old bottom leaves up to nourish the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli Kɛ́ nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ momo lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on a piece of land after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize eats a lot of soil nutrients. Crops like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally feeding and restoring the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa ehe hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: If I plant my cassava stalks very close together, will I harvest more tubers?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani makpa ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Planting too close actually reduces your yield. When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight each other underground for space, water, and soil food, resulting in many tiny, thin tubers instead of big, heavy ones.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aba shi. Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitsei bibii babaoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ yitsei wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground into the air and sun, allowing the plant to make maximum food which goes down to swell the big yam tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ, ni niyenii lɛ yaa shi ni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender stems and leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade from bigger plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them from harsh heat and keep the surrounding air humid while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ tsei bibii kɛ baai ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni ebu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli ahi shi yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crop help them survive dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry grass acts like a blanket over the dirt, known as mulch. It stops the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps the roots cool, and holds rain moisture in the ground much longer so your crops don't wilt.
ga: Hay tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulch. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ nugbɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ No hewɔ lɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbo.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot stems growing at the bottom of my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain stand lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: The main plantain stem needs a massive amount of food to produce a heavy bunch. If you leave too many suckers growing at its base, they steal water and nutrients from the main stem, leaving you with small, weak plantain bunches.
ga: Plantain tsei titrii lɛ biɔ niyenii babaoo koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii. Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa onáa plantain tso bibioo ko ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds slow down my crop growth even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa tsei lɛ daraaa fioo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that grow much faster than crops. They steal the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, effectively starving your plants even when water is available.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛjuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ moŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without forming any fruit during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and water stress make the plant panic and conserve water. When the plant gets too stressed by heat, it sheds its flowers because it feels it doesn't have enough water and energy to feed developing fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ haa tsei lɛ feɔ gbeyei ni amɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛ tsei miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni fa fe nine mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ejaakɛ amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛbɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaaha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why am I seeing tiny holes and powdery waste inside the leaf funnels of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa bibii lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: This is a clear sign of caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm. They hide deep inside the soft inner leaves (the whorl) during the hot day to feed safely away from sunlight and chemical sprays, leaving holey leaves as they grow.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ he okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai bibii lɛ amli baai (rings) lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni oye niyenii shweshweeshwe lɛ, ha hulu la kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ akashɛ he. Shi bu yɛ baai lɛ amli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are my traditional local crops like plantain and cocoyam better for my health than buying fast food from the town?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ tsei tamɔ plantain kɛ cocoa lɛ hi kɛha mihewalɛ fe niyenii ni ayeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Traditional Ghanaian staple crops are full of natural fiber, complex carbohydrates, and key vitamins that digest slowly. This helps maintain steady energy and protects your body against modern lifestyle illnesses like high blood pressure and diabetes.
ga: Ghana blema nibii ni aduɔ, ni eyi obɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli fibers. complex carbohydrates kɛ vitamins ni he hiaa ni shwieɔ shi blɛoo Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ogbɔmɔtso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ebuɔ ogbɔmɔtso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ shihilɛ mli helai tamɔ lá ni tsiimɔ kɛ sikli hela he.

english: What crops can I grow on my farm that will help protect men's prostate health as we get older?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baaye abua ni abu hii a-prostate hewalɛnamɔ he beni wɔdaraa lɛ?

english: Growing fresh tomatoes, leafy green vegetables like kontomire, and legumes provides powerful natural antioxidants such as lycopene and key minerals that support prostate health and protect body tissues.
ga: Tomato hee ni aduɔ, aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli tamɔ kontu, kɛ ŋmãa. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waaa tamɔ lycopene kɛ minerals ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa prostate hewalɛ ni ebuɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli fãji lɛ ahe lɛ haa.

english: Is there a leafy crop I can easily grow in my farm garden to help lower high blood pressure naturally?
ga: Ani tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ baai ni manyɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli mlɛo ni baaye abua ni lá ni tsiimɔ yaa hiɛ lɛ aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Leafy green vegetables like kontomire (cocoyam leaves) and spinach, as well as hibiscus (sobolo), are high in natural potassium and minerals that help relax blood vessels and lower high blood pressure when eaten regularly.
ga: Aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli tamɔ kontomire (kookoo baa) kɛ spinach, kɛ agbɛnɛ hibiscus (sobolo) lɛ yɛ potassium kɛ mineral babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ mli. Nɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni lá fãji lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe ni ehaa lá ni tsiimɔ yaa hiɛ lɛ baa shi kɛ́ aye lɛ daa.

english: Why is everyone encouraging farmers to grow orange-fleshed sweet potatoes instead of the common white ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ woɔ okwaafoi hewalɛ koni amɛdu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu sweet potatoes yɛŋ daa lɛ najiaŋ?

english: The orange color shows that the potato is packed with Beta-carotene, which your body turns into Vitamin A. This helps boost your immune system against illnesses and improves eyesight much better than white varieties.
ga: Orange tsɔɔ akɛ beta-carotene eyi ŋmɔtɔ mli obɔ, ni ogbɔmɔtso lɛ tsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ vitamin A. Ehaa ogbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nii ni gbeɔ helai lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa onaa nii jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ.

english: Will putting too many chemical sprays on my crops make the food unsafe for my family to eat?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baaha niyenii lɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha miweku lɛ ni amɛye?

english: Yes, using excessive chemical pesticides leaves harmful residues on the harvested crops. Eating these chemicals over time can strain your internal organs and lead to long-term health problems.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ shĩɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai nɛɛ tsu nii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ogbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ, ni ekɛ helai ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ aba.

english: How does using animal manure or compost improve the quality of the vegetables I grow?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha aduawai ni miduɔ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Compost feeds the soil naturally with slow-release nutrients, making your vegetables richer in vitamins, better tasting, and free from harmful chemical residues that cause body weakness.
ga: Kompost lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ejieɔ ehe kpo blɛoo lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa o-vegetables lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ vitamini, efeɔ fɛo, ni tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni haa gbɔmɔtso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ bɛ mli.

english: If my soil is weak and exhausted, will the food I harvest from it also make my family weak?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ Ani niyenii ni mikpaa lɛ baaha miweku lɛ hu agbɔjɔ?

english: Yes, crops get their nourishment directly from the soil. If the soil lacks key minerals, the harvested food will have very low nutritional value, leaving those who eat it exposed to malnutrition and tiredness.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii naa amɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ minerals ni he hiaa Niyenii ni akpaa lɛ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni baa shi kwraa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, mɛi ni yeɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii ni esaaa kɛ tɔlɛ kpeɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and dry up when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Just like human bodies weaken under severe heat and poor diet, maize plants lose their green color when they run out of water and nitrogen in the soil, shutting down growth to try and stay alive.
ga: Taakɛ adesa gbɔmɔtso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ niyenii ni esaaa shishi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Abele tsei lɛ ahe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu kɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa mɔ dalɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehi shi.

english: Which nutritious crops can I farm that do not require too much hard physical strain on my body?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli manyɛ matsu he nii ni mikɛ migbɔmɔtso lɛ tsuuu nii fe nine?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans are less demanding physically, fix their own nitrogen into the soil, and produce high-protein harvests that strengthen your body against sickness.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni sũ mli nitrogen lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ni afee nibii ni protein babaoo yɔɔ mli, ni baaha gbɔmɔtso lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛjɛ hela mli.

english: Why does my harvested cassava rot so quickly after I pull it out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a tough outer skin to protect them and continue to breathe rapidly after harvest. This causes rapid internal spoiling within two days unless processed into gari or flour quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bɛ kponɔgbɛ nɔ ko ni mli wa ni buɔ amɛhe ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛmuɔ oya kɛji akpa amɛ. Enɛ baaha emli lɛ agbo oya yɛ gbii enyɔ mli. ja afee lɛ oya ni afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ.

english: How does processing raw crops like coconut or cassava increase their value at the market?
ga: Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua ni eha jara aya hiɛ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Processing crops into dried, grated, or milled forms prevents fast spoilage and allows you to create high-demand food products that sell for much higher prices than fresh, raw produce.
ga: Nibii ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛfee nɔ ni egbi, ni akpɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni etsiɔ fitemɔ naa oya. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ ofeɔ niyenii ni ataoɔ waa ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa fe nibii heei ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I consider growing coconut palms on my farm alongside my main food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu ŋmei tsei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ niyenii titrii ni miduɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Coconut palms produce all year round once mature, providing rich oil and flesh that add high nutrition to local meals while giving your household an extra steady income stream.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmei tsei afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ. Ehaa fɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo ni kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo fataa maŋ lɛ mli niyenii ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa oshia lɛ naa shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow healthier when I plant beans between them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa waa kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans pull nitrogen directly from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as natural fertilizer that nourishes neighboring crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa

english: How do tall shade trees help protect my young crops during the hot dry season?
ga: Te tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade trees act like big umbrellas that block intense sunlight from burning delicate young plants while slowing down water evaporation from the soil.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji ni tsiɔ hulu ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekashã tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, causing the plant to pull stored nutrients out of its old leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛha tso hee ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: What causes my fruit trees to drop their blossoms before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ miigbee shi dani ewo yibii?

english: Trees drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or pest damage, as the plant attempts to save its remaining energy to survive.
ga: Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni nu hɔmɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: How many years will I wait for a coconut tree to start producing nuts after planting?
ga: Kɛ́ odu sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ ni ŋmei tso ko aje ŋmei tso lɛ shishi?

english: Dwarf coconut varieties can start bearing fruit within 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties usually take 6 to 8 years to yield their first harvest.
ga: Dwarf ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ fɔɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii.

english: Why do my stored grains get moldy so quickly after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains spoil when stored with high internal moisture; drying them thoroughly in the sun until they are completely hard stops mold and insects from destroying your harvest.
ga: Nibii fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa. Etsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite onibii.

english: How can I keep my harvested yams from rotting in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Storing yams off the ground in a shaded, well-ventilated yam barn keeps them dry and cool, preventing humidity from starting the decay process.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ sweet potato kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ sweet potato shĩa ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha amɛhe agbi ni amɛhe ajɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje fitemɔ nifeemɔ lɛ shishi.

english: What can I apply to my soil to help my crops develop rich, full fruit?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Adding well-rotted manure or potassium-rich fertilizers feeds soil microbes and supplies the nutrients crops need to build natural oils, sugars, and strong healthy fruits.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo potassium ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he lɛ haa sũ mli nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ niyenii ni ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛná adebɔɔ mli fɔji, sugars kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant shade crops like plantains alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ madu tso ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantain, yɛ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. Planting plantains alongside them provides essential shade, cools the soil, and helps retain soil moisture while the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba. ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Planting trees too close creates competition for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also blocks airflow, making it easier for fungal diseases to spread quickly from tree to tree.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ hu naa. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ baagbɛ ashwã.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm is being attacked by Akate bugs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ Akate kooloi miitutua mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You will notice dark spots or brown, burnt-looking patches on the young shoots, stems, and pods. The leaves will wilt and dry up, making the top of the tree look as if it were scorched by fire.
ga: Obaana ŋmeii ni tsuɔ loo shãa he okadii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ tsei bibii, amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi anɔ. Baai lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbi. Ehaa tsei lɛ ayiteŋ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni la miitso.

english: This rot is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, damp conditions. High humidity and rain droplets splash the fungus onto the pods, causing them to turn black and decay if not removed or treated.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ ashwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji ajieee amɛ loo atsaaa amɛ.

english: Why do some of the flowers on my cocoa trees dry up and fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed flowers if they lack nutrients, water, or proper insect pollination. High insect pests or poor soil health can cause even more flowers to drop early before pods can form.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji niyenii ni sa, nu loo ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ bɛ mli. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni fa babaoo loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo mra dani ŋmeii aba.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the extra shoots called chupons growing on my cocoa tree trunks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Chupons waste the tree's energy by drinking water and food meant for pod production. Removing them ensures the tree directs its nutrients toward producing healthy branches and pods.
ga: Chupon fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ ni akɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni enuɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛ niji kɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why should I clear weeds from around the base of my crops regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with your crops for water and soil nutrients. They also trap unwanted moisture around the base of the stems and provide hiding places for harmful farm pests.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ataooo lɛ hu amɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛhaa ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ náa he ko ni amɛhiɔ amɛhe.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs fertilizer to help my crops grow better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have yellowish leaves instead of healthy dark green ones, or produce small fruits, the soil is likely lacking vital nutrients and needs fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ najiaŋ. loo ewoɔ aduawai bibii Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why should I avoid spraying chemical medicine on my crops during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ he?

english: Spraying during hot sunlight causes the chemical to evaporate too quickly before it can work. The intense heat combined with the chemical can also scorch and burn the tender leaves of your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai lɛ shwie hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ dani amɛtsuɔ nii. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni akɛ tsofai fata he lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni ashã tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai.

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color clearly— green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting pods only when they turn yellow ensures high-quality seeds inside.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su yɛ faŋŋ mli. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuru loo purple lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ pɛ lɛ, no haa dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before they produce corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa baa lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize requires nitrogen to stay green and produce strong cobs, so adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the season helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot strips the soil of specific nutrients and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi bɛ. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which way I stick cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Nɔ ni he hiaa ji bɔ ni mafee madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the growing buds pointing upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the stems waste vital energy turning around underground, leading to delayed growth and small tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. This results in delayed growth and small tubers.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so I can get more crops on my small plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed well, resulting in healthier plants and bigger total harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often warms up the dry ground without soaking it deeply. Planting immediately can cause seeds to dry out or rot in the hot, damp soil before the main rainy season fully settles.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ nu shwieee nɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbi loo amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba naagbee.

english: Why do some extension officers advise planting hot peppers around a cabbage farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi komɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ yɛ kaaba ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Hot peppers have a strong scent and natural chemical compounds that repel many common insects. Planting them around your vegetables creates a natural border that keeps pests away without extra chemical sprays.
ga: Hot peppers yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa, ni adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni shwieɔ kooloi bibii babaoo ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ yɛ mli. Aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ Aduawai ahe lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli husu ko baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi ashwie nɔ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass around the roots of my crops during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi mashwã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves around crops, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from evaporating moisture from the soil. It keeps the roots cool and wet, helping plants survive dry spells longer.
ga: Spreading dry grass or leaves around crops is called mulching. It will help prevent the hot sun from evaporating moisture from the soil. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without making any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or irregular watering. When temperatures get too hot or the soil dries out completely, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy and water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why do I need to pinch off the small side shoots growing on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ shi lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ

english: Removing extra side branches, called suckers, stops the plant from wasting food on extra leaves. This allows the plant to focus its energy on growing larger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tso lɛ afite baa niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to grow green and healthy. It can also happen if heavy rain has flooded the soil and is suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi.

english: Which direction should I point a cassava stem cutting when pushing it into the ground?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ootsi kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ ni afo lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: Always plant the cassava stem with the small buds or nodes pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant it upside down, the sprouts will struggle to reach the surface, resulting in weak plants and very small cassava tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cassava tsei lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu ŋwɛi Dumɔwui lɛ baaná naagba ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ hu faaa kwraa.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden sticks next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb high to capture as much sunlight as possible. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground to prevent diseases and helps the plant produce energy to grow much larger tubers under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking woɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akabote mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ tsei wuji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extremely high heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kpe. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: It is safer to wait for two or three good rains so the soil gets deeply wet. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout, but if a dry spell follows immediately, the young seedlings will wither and die.
ga: It will be safer to wait for good rain. two or three times to deeply moisten the soil. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Be kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Tso bibioo lɛ baagbo ni ebaagbo.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts on a plot where I harvested maize last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the ground, leaving the soil weak. Groundnuts and beans are special because they take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring its strength for future crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. gbɔjɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Peanuts kɛ beans ji nɔ ko krɛdɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is making ragged holes inside the top leaf funnels of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni elaaje yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Those holes are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding deep inside the central leaves. You can control them early by putting a small pinch of clean dry sand, wood ash, or recommended neem leaf extract directly into the funnel.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ lɛ mra. Kɛji ooofee enɛ lɛ, okɛ ŋã ni mli tse ni egbi, tso mli sũ loo neem baa ni ajieɔ yi akɛ ajieɔ lɛ fioo ko awoɔ ŋã lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is it good to scrape all the dry leaves off the ground under my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni egbi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ?

english: No, leaving fallen leaves on the ground creates a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool and moist during hot days. Bare soil gets dried out quickly by the sun and washes away easily when heavy rains fall.
ga: Dabi, baai ni egbee shi lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ lɛ oya.

english: Can I put fresh poultry manure directly on my vegetable beds?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifã hee afata mi-vegetables saatsoi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh poultry manure is very strong and contains high levels of heat and ammonia that can burn plant roots. You should stack the manure in a heap and let it dry out and break down for several weeks before putting it near your crops.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi ni afee ehee lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ hulutsoo kɛ ammonia ni fa babaoo yɛ mli, ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. You should pile the manure into piles. Ha ni egbi ni efite otsii babaoo dani okɛma ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why are my pepper seedlings growing tall and thin instead of short and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛmiifee bibioo yɛ kuku ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔji lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Seedlings grow tall and skinny when they are not receiving enough light because they are stretching upward to find the sun. Moving your nursery bed to a brighter area with good sunlight will help them grow strong, thick stems.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa kɛji amɛnáaa la ni fa bɔ ni sa ejaakɛ esa akɛ amɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛna hulu la. Kɛ́ ajie gbekɛbii akwɛmɔ saatsoi lɛ kɛtee he ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná tsei ni wa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and turn brown when I plant them in an open field with direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade during their first two years because direct heat dries out their tender leaves. Planting fast-growing plantains alongside cocoa provides a natural leaf canopy that blocks harsh sunlight and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ agbi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli baai ni haa hulu ni naa wa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small shoots coming out from the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Extra ni jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ mi plantain lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Removing excess shoots—called suckers—ensures that all the water and plant nutrients go into one main stem, resulting in a healthier tree and a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii Enɛ baaha nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei fɛɛ amli lɛ afee ekome yɛ tso kome mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ plantains babaoo ni dara ni tsii lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning light green and yellow starting from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tip usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green foliage. Adding poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmãa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmɔŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Will growing cowpeas or groundnuts between my rows of maize reduce my maize yield?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaha miŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: No, legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts actually pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as natural fertilizer that helps your maize grow better without stealing its food.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ejuuu niyenii.

english: Why is my crop burning when I throw fresh chicken manure directly onto the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa kɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee shwie baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fresh poultry manure contains strong ammonia and salts that scorch soft plant tissues. Manure must be composted or worked into the soil around the base of the plant rather than dropped on leaves.
ga: Ammonia ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni shãa tsei lɛ amli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ yɛ kooloi afɔfɔi ni afee ehee lɛ amli. Esa akɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii loo akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli, moŋ fe ni aaashɛrɛ ashwie baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on tender young leaves hidden inside the plant funnel; spraying an organic extract like neem leaf water or recommended pesticide early on destroys them.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ baai bibii ni akɛtee tsei amli ŋmeii amli lɛ. Akɛ tsofai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsofai amli tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔɔ nɔ mra. lɛ baakpata amɛhiɛ

english: Why does covering the soil around my tomato plants with dry grass keep them from wilting in hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haaa amɛgboi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like an insulating cover that stops sunshine from evaporating soil water, keeping moisture near the roots and protecting them from heat.
ga: Dry mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe ni obu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why do my sweet potatoes rot when I plant them on flat land during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa beaŋ lɛ?

english: Flat land traps standing water around roots during heavy rains, drowning the plant. Creating raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu damɔ he. Shishifãi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso lɛ ni shwieɔ nu mli. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: How do I know my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting without uprooting the whole stem?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mijieee amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, the main stem turns woody, and the ground around the base of the plant begins to crack open from expanding tubers below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso titri lɛ tsɔɔ tso. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ miije shishi egbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ shishigbɛ yitso lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ mli.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? Kɛkɛ ni mikɛ tso lɛ wo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to produce energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking the vines holds leaves up into the sun and prevents fungal diseases caused by wet ground contact.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ amli baa lɛ naa.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the younger top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara, ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do people say planting cowpea alongside my maize helps the maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa ehe waa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans are legumes that capture free nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, acting like a natural food supply for crops planted near them.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why does my farm yield less rice each year if I keep planting it on the exact same piece of land without resting it?
