ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the soil over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does my local lowland rice stay healthy when covered in water, while my maize rots and dies in the same water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi maŋ lɛ mli flat rice lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ nu ha he lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-abele lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ yɛ nu lɛ nɔŋŋ mli.

english: Rice plants have special hollow tubes in their stems and roots that send air down to the roots even when submerged, whereas maize roots drown without open soil air.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ baa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli kɛ́ amɛbote nu mli po. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava crop stay green through the long dry season when my other crops wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi feɔ nakai lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ gboɔ?

english: Cassava drops its outer leaves to conserve moisture and relies on deep taproots to pull underground water up into its water-storing tubers.
ga: Cassava duɔ esɛɛ baai lɛ koni ekɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛgbalaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛyaa nu ni akɛtoɔ lɛ yitso lɛ he.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without forming peppers during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee pepper yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop its blossoms to save energy and water rather than spending resources on growing new fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii baatsu nii ni akɛdu aduawai heei

english: Why do my heavy rice stems fall over flat onto the mud right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ tsii waa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, minɔ lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji nɔ dani kpamɔ be lɛ shɛ?

english: This is called lodging, which happens when rice stems grow too tall and top-heavy due to high nitrogen levels or thick planting, making them weak against rain and wind.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ lodging, ni baa kɛji ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwere tsɔ ni amɛyiteŋ tsii yɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo loo dumɔwui ni fa babaoo hewɔ. Enɛ haa nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɔ etswaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ oya.

english: Why do weeds make my main crop produce tiny harvests if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔ titri lɛ yibiiwoo aba lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mijieee jwɛi lɛ mra hu?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for light, water, and soil nutrients, effectively starving your crop during its critical early development stage.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing holes through the middle leaves of my young corn plants at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the funnel of the maize plant during the hot day and emerge at night to feed on the tender young leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni ejeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni eye baai bibii.

english: Why does my harvested rice turn moldy and smell bad after I store it in bags inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni akɛwo kotokui amli yɛ tsu lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If harvested rice is not dried sufficiently before bagging, trapped moisture creates a humid environment that causes mold spores to multiply rapidly inside the bag.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ egbiko bɔ ni sa dani awoɔ kotoku mli lɛ Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ faa oya yɛ kotoku lɛ mli.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside leaves of my young maize plants before they even produce cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ dani amɛjeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli po lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides in the heart of maize plants. They feed on fresh leaves, which weakens the plant and stops it from growing healthy cobs if not managed early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe ewoɔ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai heei, ni no haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ shwereɔ waa kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the soil gets too dry. Without enough moisture and cool conditions, the plant cannot support turning flowers into heavy fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua kɛkɛ ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsake amɛhe ni amɛfee aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree leaves turn brown and burn when there is hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains around them to block strong heat and keep moisture in the air and soil while they grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ. Tsei loo plantains ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ. Bɔni afee ni akafee dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ.

english: What makes black spots spread across my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by excessive moisture and fungus during wet periods. Excess water sitting on the pods creates a perfect environment for the rot to grow and spread from pod to pod.
ga: Enɛ ji blackpod hela ni hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nu ni fa fe nine ni kpɛtɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ adara ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii krokomɛi amli.

english: Why does my land produce much smaller cassava roots now than it did a few years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fioo kwraa fe afii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the ground every time you harvest. Over time, continuous farming without adding manure, fertilizer, or letting the land rest exhausts the soil, leaving fewer nutrients for new crops to grow large roots.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa amɛ. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Enɛ haa niyenii ni haa tsei heei ni shishifãi wuji yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs daylight to make food. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun, improves airflow around the plant, and prevents leaf diseases, leading to bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛhoo. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ekɛtsiɔ baa helai anaa. Ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly in the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural survival trick where the plant rolls its leaves to expose less surface area to the hot sun, preventing water from escaping too quickly during the heat of the day.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa. Tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛha he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji koni nu akaje mli oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after the first rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants natively adapted to the local environment. Their seeds lie sleeping in the soil and are designed to sprout instantly and absorb available water and food faster than domesticated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛjɛ fɔmɔ mli amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli. Edumɔwui lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni afee lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii oya fe shia tsei.

english: Why is it better to buy certified maize seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Saved seeds from high-yield varieties often lose their strength and vigor in the next generation, producing uneven crops and smaller yields compared to freshly certified seed stock.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ahereɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ he.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps leaves off the hot ground, protects them from rot and ground pests, and ensures maximum sunlight reaches the plant so you get bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ahe. Ni ehaa hulu la babaoo shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe bɔ ni eeenyɛ bɔni afee ni oná sweet potatoes wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for healthy green leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost helps restore their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting beans together with my maize help my crop soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which can pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. This acts as natural food for your maize, improving soil fertility without extra fertilizer costs.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni baanyɛ agbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa o-corn lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni awo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nyɔmɔ kroko.

english: It is best to apply fertilizer about two to three weeks after planting, once the roots are established enough to drink up the nutrients. Always make sure the soil is moist so the fertilizer dissolves and does not burn the plant roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli aaafee otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ te shi bɔ ni sa lɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛnu niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli ni ekashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very wet to very dry. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and adding mulch helps keep the plants cool and saves the flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ nɔ ni edɔ waa kɛtee nɔ ni egbi waa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ mli ajɔ ni eye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water prevents air from reaching the roots, allowing water molds to attack them. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nu mli ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ atutua. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do small green caterpillars eat holes in the middle leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ bu yɛ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the tender central leaves of maize. Catching them early and applying organic neem extract or recommended sprays directly into the plant funnel stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tswaa ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ organic neem extract loo sprays ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsu nii lɛ haa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden early in the morning or in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because it gives plants the moisture they need to handle the hot afternoon sun. It also allows wet leaves to dry quickly during the day, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa tso lɛ náa nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ etsu hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ he nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa baa ni efɔ lɛ hu ni egbiɔ oya yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: Why do weeds slow down my crop growth even when rain falls regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa oya eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ?

english: Weeds act like greedy thieves, stealing the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your main crop needs to grow strong. Clearing weeds within the first month of planting leaves all the food and water for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi hiɛjoolɔi. Ejuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa tsei ni okɛ amɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛdara waa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ aba onibii amli.

english: If oil palm trees grow very well on my farm, does that mean the land is fertile enough for other crops?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mu tsei kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi?

english: Yes, lush wild oil palms usually indicate rich, fertile soil. However, palm trees have deep roots that can search for hidden underground water, so shallow-rooted crops like vegetables might still struggle if the topsoil dries out.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, mu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii, ni baa nii. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmei tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni baanyɛ ana nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni akɛtee. No hewɔ lɛ tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, tamɔ aduawai lɛ baanyɛ ana amanehulu lolo kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli gĩ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has deep underground water before spending money to drill a borehole?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mafite shika kɛfo nu bu?

english: You can look for natural plant signs. Areas where oil palm trees, bamboo, or large evergreen plants stay green throughout the long dry season usually indicate that the groundwater table is close to the surface.
ga: Obaanyɛ otao adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe okadii. Hei ni mu tsei, ŋmeii loo tsei wuji yɔɔ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt and turn yellow during dry weather even when the soil is rich in manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ sũ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ?

english: Nutrient-rich soil needs water to dissolve those nutrients so plant roots can absorb them. Without enough moisture, your crops cannot drink or feed, causing them to wilt and turn yellow from thirst and starvation.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he miihia nu koni ekɛjie nakai niyenii lɛ koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ faaa lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ anu nu loo amɛye niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kumai kɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ.

english: What happens to fruit trees like palm and cocoa when the soil is good but there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni baa tsei ni woɔ yibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ kookoo nɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi shi nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: When water is scarce, fruit trees enter survival mode. They will shed their flowers, drop young fruits early, or produce small, lightweight seeds to conserve the little energy and water they have left.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa Yibii tsei lɛ baabote wala shihilɛ mli. Amɛbaashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Shĩ aduawai bibii oya loo feemɔ dumɔwui bibii ni tsiimɔ waaa koni okɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ ato.

english: Why does my topsoil look dark and rich, but my maize still dries up after just a few days without rain?
ga: Why does my topsoil look dark and rich? Shi mi-ŋma lɛ mli egbi lolo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Dark soil shows high organic matter, which is great for plant food, but heat and direct sunlight can quickly evaporate surface moisture. Shallow crops like maize cannot reach lower water reserves like deep tree roots can.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli. ni sa kɛha tsei aniyenii Shi dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ atsɔ oya. Nibii ni aduɔ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ bɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛyaa nu jɛɛhei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tamɔ tsei shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: How do long dry spells affect the overall growth rate of my cash crops?
ga: Te hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ saa mi shika ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Water is the main ingredient plants use to turn sunlight into food. When water is scarce, the plant slows down its growth, stems stop thickening, and new leaf production stops until moisture returns.
ga: Nu ji nibii titri ni tsei kɛtsakeɔ hulu la amɛfeɔ niyenii. Kɛ nu faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ baadalɛ aya hiɛ fioo, amɛshishifãi lɛ baakpa ŋmɔlɔ, ni baai heei ni ajieɔ lɛ baakpa kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Is groundwater from a borehole good and safe for watering my farm crops?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni jɛɔ nu bu mli lɛ hi ni ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Yes, borehole water is usually clean and free from pests, weed seeds, or chemical runoff often found in rivers. It provides a reliable supply of fresh water to keep your crops healthy all year round.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ nubu mli lɛ mli tse ni tsɛŋemɔ helai, jwɛi dumɔwui, loo tsofai ni hoɔ ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ faai amli lɛ bɛ mli. Amɛhaa nu kpakpa jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi jogbaŋŋ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do some farms stay completely green during the dry season while neighboring farms dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji komɛi feɔ ŋmɔji kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli ŋmɔji lɛ ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Farms that stay green usually sit over underground water veins that deep tree roots can reach, or the farmers use groundwater wells and boreholes to irrigate their crops continuously.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji ni yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji lɛ taraa shikpɔŋ shishi nu paipii ni tsei shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ anɔ. Aloo okwaafoi kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nubui kɛ nubui tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu be fɛɛ be.

english: Can mature oil palms survive long dry seasons without artificial watering?
ga: Ani mu tso ni eda lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛji akɛ akɛ nu ni akɛfee lɛ haaa lɛ?

english: Mature oil palms are tough because their extensive root systems spread wide and deep underground to draw moisture, making them much more drought-resistant than short-term crops like maize or tomatoes.
ga: Mu tsei ni eda lɛ wa waa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi ni fa babaoo lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi koni ekɛgbala ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmãa loo tomato.

english: If there is no stream near my farm, what is the best way to secure water for dry season farming?
ga: Kɛji faa ko bɛ ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ? What is the best way to provide water for crops in the dry season?

english: The most reliable solution is to hire a drilling team to dig a borehole to tap into underground water. You can also cover your soil with dried grass or leaves (mulching) to trap soil moisture longer.
ga: Nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ fe fɛɛ ji ni aha mɛi ni tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ nu lɛ koni amɛfo bu ko ni amɛkɛpompɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai (mulch) hu aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong direct sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or shade crops like plantains to protect their tender leaves and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains amli koni amɛbu baai bibii ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, which is the main food it needs to build healthy green leaves and produce large ears of corn.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni akɛwo ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: What is causing the center of my young maize leaves to look chewed up with brown dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn leaf lɛ teŋgbɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ emli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the funnel of the plant during the day and eats the young, growing leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei amli ŋmeii amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni oye baai bibii ni miida lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain after a dry period is often followed by a hot dry spell. If you plant too early, the sprouted seeds will run out of water and die before the main rains settle in.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli nu baaje mli ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to push cassava stick cuttings into the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei nine lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems have small raised bumps called leaf nodes or eyes that point upwards toward the sky. Planting the stem with these nodes facing up ensures the leaves and shoots grow out properly above ground.
ga: Kasava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ leaf nodes loo buds ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ shishi ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ kwɛ ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do we have to heap the soil into mounds before planting yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔbua shikpɔŋ lɛ naa wɔfee gɔŋ dani wɔdu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow large deep underground and need soft, loose, and well-drained soil to expand freely without rotting in trapped water.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni amɛdara. ni ebiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Koni amɛshwere yɛ heyeli mli ni amɛgbooo yɛ nu ni amɔmɔ amɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut away the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots suck away water and plant food from the main mother plant. Removing all except one strong replacement shoot allows the main stem to produce larger and heavier bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome pɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off without producing fruit when the air gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no insects visiting to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from under the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do extension officers tell us that planting groundnuts makes the soil better for maize next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ, kɛ́ wɔdu ŋmei lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi kɛha afi ni baa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, leaving natural food behind for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to push cassava sticks into the soil when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni esa akɛ matsi ŋmei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small buds or 'eyes' on the cassava stem cutting. These eyes must always point upward toward the sky; planting them upside down makes it difficult for shoots to grow and significantly reduces your tuber yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmei’ ni yɔɔ yucca tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ hiŋmɛii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. ni eha tuber yibiiwoo lɛ ba shi waa.

english: Why do I need to build big soil mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ama gɔŋ agbo dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yams require loose, deep soil to expand into long, thick tubers. Creating high mounds gives the roots space to grow easily without hitting hard ground and prevents the tubers from rotting in flooded soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni mli tse. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa he ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛbaada ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and burning under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hulu lɛ etswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight because their tender leaves dry out and burn easily. Planting temporary shade plants like plantains nearby creates a canopy that protects young cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the tips downward in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛba shi yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips on maize are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires nitrogen to stay dark green and produce heavy cobs, so adding compost, poultry manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will fix this.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmãa ni tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi Ko ni amɛkɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds your maize crop and keeps the soil fertile without relying solely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha o-corn tsei lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from taking over your garden bed.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akaha obɔɔ mli saatsoi lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when soil temperatures get too hot or when the plant experiences sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light soil cover helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo be trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli fioo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tomatoi lɛ ahe ni amɛmaa shi shiŋŋ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the main plantain tree. Pruning away all but one or two strong shoots focuses the plant's energy into producing a larger, heavier bunch of fruit.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ tsei lɛ fɛɛ ahe, ja eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hewalɛ aya yibii wuji ni tsii ni ewoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil depletes the exact same nutrients every year and allows soil pests to build up in high numbers. Rotating maize with beans or cassava gives the soil time to recover and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abele ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ afite afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark powder inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ powda bibii ni tsuɔ waa lɛ. yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant during the day to feed on young leaves. Applying targeted natural remedies like neem seed extracts or safe insecticides early in the morning can stop them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem dumɔwu mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ leebi lɛ baanyɛ akpa enɛɛmɛi.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the main leaves start to turn yellow and drop off, which typically happens between 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ be mli ni baai titrii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Why do some cassava roots grow very large while others stay small and hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi komɛi dara nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni shishifãi komɛi ji bibii ni amɛhe wa lolo lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers grow large when the soil is loose and well-drained, giving the roots space to expand, whereas hard and compacted soil restricts root growth.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ ada.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Tubers rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots; planting on raised ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Tubers fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Dumɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ.

english: Why does my yield get smaller when I plant cassava on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ faaa kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to recover or replenish those nutrients naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ahaaa sũ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ loo ekɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: How can I tell if my land has good soil for planting cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ ŋmei?

english: Good cassava soil is crumbly, sandy-loam, and allows water to soak through easily without leaving standing puddles after a heavy rain.
ga: Cassava shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli tse ni ŋã yɔɔ mli. Nu tsɔɔ mli oya. Kaashi nu ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ.

english: Why do crops grow better on one side of my farm than on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome fe fã kroko lɛ?

english: Soil depth, organic matter, and shade levels vary across the farm, causing plants in richer, sunnier spots to grow stronger than those in depleted areas.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ he ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ daa waa fe tsei ni yɔɔ he ko ni mɛi bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Which direction should the buds point when I push cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔɔ kɛ́ amɛmiitsi ŋmei nine kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: The small growth buds on the stem cutting must always point upward toward the sky so the shoots can sprout quickly above the surface.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ tsei bibii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting cassava together with maize affect how both crops grow?
ga: Te ŋmãa ni akɛfataa ŋmãa he lɛ saa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested early, leaving sunlight and soil space for the slower-growing cassava to spread out later in the season.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɛ aha ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants drop off during hot, dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is the plant's natural defense mechanism to save water and keep its underground roots alive during dry spells.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbuɔ nu he ni ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly absorb water and nutrients faster than cultivated crops, taking advantage of the early rains.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small ears even when the leaves look green and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ toi bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: A bushy maize plant puts too much energy into leaves if plants are sown too close together or if there is too much nitrogen early on, leaving insufficient sunlight and nutrients for the ears to fill out properly.
ga: Abɛi tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaha amɛbaai lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo tsɔ kɛji akɛ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ nitrogen fa tsɔ yɛ shishijee bei lɛ amli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni toi lɛ baanyɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the plant reduces leaf surface area to prevent water from evaporating too quickly during severe midday heat.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu lɛ akafo oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop lower leaves when they don't get enough sunlight due to crowding or when moisture near the soil causes fungal infections, signaling a need for better spacing or pruning.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ hewɔ loo kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Etsɔɔ bɔ ni ehe hiaa ni afee gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ loo afolɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start going soft and bad just two days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bafee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni mikɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ tsu nii lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rapidly deteriorate once disconnected from soil water and nutrients, which is why they must be processed quickly into gari or flour to preserve their food value.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afee lɛ oya ni afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ koni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ akafite.

english: How can I tell the right time to harvest my yam so it stays fresh longer after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii? Enɛ ji koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yams are fully mature when the above-ground vines and leaves naturally turn yellow and dry up, indicating that the tuber has stored maximum food and developed a firm skin for storage.
ga: Sweet potatoes shɛɔ dalɛ he beni wain tso lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ eto niyenii babaoo ni amɛná hewolo ni wa kɛha nibii ni akɛtoɔ.

english: How do I know if my soil actually lacks food for crops before I spend money on fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa miduɔ nii lɛ bɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ? Dani obaafite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahemɔ mli?

english: Yellowing leaves, thin stems, and slow growth are clear signs of nutrient shortage, but testing soil with a local extension worker is the best way to buy only what your field truly needs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei bibii kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo ji okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa. Shi kɛ́ okɛ maŋ lɛ mli sũ lɛ mli nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ lɛ, no ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ ohé nɔ pɛ ni he hiaa oŋmɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Does clearing my field with heavy machinery damage the crops I plant afterward?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni tsii ni mikɛjieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy machinery compacts the topsoil, making it difficult for delicate crop roots to spread deep and preventing rainwater from sinking into the ground effectively.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã shɔŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ koni ekabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: How far apart should I plant plantain suckers so they don't fight each other for nutrients?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-plantain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkaye niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ?

english: Plantains require about three meters of space between plants so their large root systems can find food and their broad leaves do not block sunlight from neighboring stems.
ga: Plantains he miihia ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee aaafee mitai 3 bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ anyɛ ana niyenii ni baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ akatsi hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, natural fertilizing the soil for neighboring maize crops while giving you two harvests from one field.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do pests attack my vegetables even when I water them and the weather is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai miitutua mi aduawai lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hi moŋ?

english: Healthy and juicy crops attract pests precisely because they offer high nutrition, so crops require regular inspection and early pest protection regardless of good weather.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mli ewo nu lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ niyenii ni mli wa ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli daa ni abu he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe mra. ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpakpai yɔɔ ha lɛ he

english: My tomato leaves are turning brown and drying up like they are burnt; what is causing this to my crop?
ga: Mi tomato baai lɛ miitsɔ blɔfo ni amɛmiigbi tamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ. Mɛni kɛ enɛ miiba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: This is likely late blight, a fungal disease that attacks leaves and fruit during wet weather. It spreads quickly through tiny spores carried by wind and splashing rain.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ afee sɛɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa baai kɛ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii amli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswaa kɛyaa

english: Why does disease spread so much faster across my field during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Fungal spores and bacteria thrive in water and high moisture. Raindrops bounce off infected leaves and splash the disease onto healthy neighboring plants.
ga: Fungal kɛ bacteria tsɛŋemɔ helai shwereɔ yɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Some farmers in my village say spraying dissolved aspirin on sick plants cures blight; is this true and safe?
ga: Okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ kɛɔ akɛ, kɛ́ afɔ aspirin ni nu mli shwieɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsa late blight lɛ. Ani enɛ ji anɔkwale ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Aspirin is not a reliable or approved cure for blight. While it contains salicylic acid which can slightly trigger a plant's natural defense, using proper agricultural fungicides or resistant seeds is much safer and more effective.
ga: Aspirin jeee tsofa ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ loo ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ kɛha sɛɛ mli hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Eyɛ mli akɛ salicylic acid ni baanyɛ aha tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni tsiɔ ehe lɛ aya hiɛ fioo lɛ yɛ mli moŋ. Shi okwaayeli mli tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii loo dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I protect my vegetable farm from pests without buying expensive chemical sprays from the shop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabu mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shwapo lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can make natural sprays using crushed neem leaves or soapy water, and practice crop rotation or intercropping to naturally keep pests away.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ neem baai ni atswa loo nu ni akɛ samla ewo mli lɛ afee adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ loo tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ atsu nii koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if a chemical spray is safe for me to handle on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Check the color band on the bottle label—green and blue bands indicate lower toxicity, while yellow and red mean high danger. Regardless of the color, you should always wear protective clothing like gloves and a face cover when spraying.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kɔla ni yɔɔ tɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Bars eŋɔli kɛ bluu tsɔɔ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ faaa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔŋ kɛ etsuru tsɔɔ oshara ni mli wa waa. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni su lɛ ji Esa akɛ owo atadei ni buɔ mɔ he tamɔ glɔvs kɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa hiɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ oofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some agricultural products I buy after seeing farm adverts fail to work on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli nibii komɛi ni miheɔ beni mina ŋmɔ mli adafitswaa lɛ tsuuu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Adverts promote products generally without considering your specific soil type, crop variety, or local climate. Local agricultural extension officers can give tailored advice that fits your exact field conditions.
ga: Adafitswai woɔ nibii ahe hewalɛ babaoo ni esusuuu shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko, tsei srɔtoi, loo he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe. Kuu lɛ mli okwaayeli he nitsulɔi baanyɛ aha ŋaawoo ni sa kɛha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my crops need fertilizer or if my soil is already strong enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ momo?

english: If your crop leaves start turning pale yellow instead of rich dark green, or if the stalks remain thin and stunted, your soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo ni egbɔjɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: There are different types of fertilizers in the market; how do I choose the right one for my maize farm?
ga: Ayɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi babaoo yɛ jara nɔ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala nɔ ni sa kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Young crops need balanced nutrients like NPK (15-15-15) early on to build strong roots and leaves, while nitrogen-heavy fertilizers like Urea are applied later when the plants are growing tall rapidly.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia niyenii ni sa tamɔ NPK (15-15-15) mra. Bɔni afee ni afee shishifãi kɛ baai ni wa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛ mli beni tsei lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to local conditions, allowing them to steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: If my crops wilt during a hot dry spell, will they recover automatically once it rains again?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Ani tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: If the leaves only droop during the afternoon heat but stay green, rain will revive them. However, if the leaves and stems dry out completely and turn brown, the plant tissues are dead and cannot bounce back.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa shi amɛji eŋɔli lolo lɛ Nugbɔ baatswa ekoŋŋ, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji baai lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gĩ kwraa ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ gboiɔ ni anyɛɛɛ aku sɛɛ akɛba.

english: Can I put fresh chicken droppings directly on my crop roots right after cleaning the coop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee awo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ beni mijie tsina ŋmei lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is very strong and contains high amounts of ammonia that can burn and destroy your crop roots. You should dry or mix the droppings with crop leaves and let them rot into compost for a few weeks before applying them to your farm.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa waa ni ammonia babaoo yɛ mli ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite otsei lɛ ashishifãi. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbi loo okɛ tsei ahe baai afutu ni oha egbo ni etsɔ ŋmeii otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛwo oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What is the real difference between ordinary farm soil and manure for my plants?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ folo kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mi tsei lɛ ateŋ?

english: Ordinary soil holds the plant upright and retains water, while manure is decomposed animal waste or plant matter full of plant food (nutrients) that feeds the soil and helps your crops grow healthy yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli. Beni ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ lɛ, kooloi loo tsei amli jwɛi eyi kɛ tsei aniyenii (nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ) ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my crop leaves still turning yellow even after I applied chicken manure to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves can happen if the manure was applied fresh and burnt the roots, or if the soil is too waterlogged or too dry for the roots to absorb nutrients. Using well-matured manure and maintaining good soil moisture usually fixes this.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ aba kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ hee wo mli ni shishifãi lɛ shã. Aloo kɛji akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ loo egbi tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: How long does chicken manure stay active in the soil to feed my crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Decomposed chicken manure breaks down slowly and releases nutrients into the soil over 3 to 6 months, feeding your crops continuously through a full growing season.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo lɛ fiteɔ fiofio. ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 6, ni ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii be fɛɛ be yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What do extension officers mean by 'crop medicine', and when should I apply it to my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ tsɔɔ yɛ ‘tsei ahe tsofa’ he ni mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: Crop medicines are agricultural chemicals used to protect plants, such as insecticides for bugs, fungicides for plant diseases, and weedicides for weeds. It is best to spray early in the morning or late afternoon when insects are active and the intense sun won't dry up the medicine too quickly.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsaa tsei ahe ji okwaayeli tsofai ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe, tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii. Fungicide kɛha tsei ahe helai kɛ herbicide kɛha jwɛi Esa akɛ ashwie nɔ leebi loo shwane mli. Be nɛɛ ji be ni kooloi bibii tsuɔ nii. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haŋ tsofa lɛ agbi oya tsɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from a sickness or if they are just thirsty for rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiye hela loo nugbɔ he kumai miiye amɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Thirsty plants usually wilt in the hot afternoon heat and revive in the cool evening or after watering, while sick crops show dark spots, leaf curls, powdery marks, or rot that remain regardless of water.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ fɔɔ shwiemɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni ehiɛɔ shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi loo beni awo lɛ nu sɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ baajie ŋmeii diji, baai ni ebɔle amɛhe, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni eshwɛ ni nu kɔɔɔ he eko lɛ kpo.

english: Why do insects keep eating my crop leaves even after I sprayed medicine on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwieɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Insects may return if heavy rain washed the medicine off the leaves, if you used the wrong chemical for that specific pest, or if the dose was too weak. Always spray in dry weather and make sure the medicine matches the pest problem.
ga: Kplukai lɛ baanyɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie tsofa lɛ kɛjɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni ejaaa tsu nii kɛha nakai tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ, loo kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛhaa lɛ faaa tsɔ lɛ, shwie nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ. Ni kwɛmɔ akɛ tsofa lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ naagba lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Is crop medicine safe to spray on garden vegetables that my family plans to harvest and eat soon?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsofa lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaafɔse aduawai ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli ni miweku lɛ eto gbɛjianɔ akɛ amɛbaakpa ni amɛye etsɛŋ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, but you must respect the waiting period listed on the medicine container—often 3 to 14 days after spraying—to ensure the chemical breaks down fully before the food is harvested and eaten.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ obu mɛmɔ be ni aŋmala awo tsofa lɛ mli lɛ he. (Be pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 14 sɛɛ beni afɔse tsofai lɛ) koni ana akɛ tsofai lɛ efite kwraa dani akpa amɛ ni aye.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and leafy but produce small ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ abele toi bibii lɛ?

english: High nitrogen manure makes plants grow thick leaves and tall stems, but crops also need phosphorus and potassium to form big fruits and grain. Balanced feeding ensures both strong growth and heavy ears of corn.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa baai ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ. Shi fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium hu he miihia tsei koni amɛfee aduawai kɛ dumɔwui wuji. Niyenii ni ja haa ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ toi tsii.

english: Why do my crops wilt and dry up much faster during the dry Harmattan weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya kwraa yɛ Harmattan hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds carry very dry air that sucks water out of crop leaves faster than roots can draw moisture from dry soil. Covering the ground around your plants with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and saves water.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi waa ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hu sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow strong and green. Applying urea or NPK fertilizer, or mixing well-rotted animal manure into the soil, will help the leaves regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛfee eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ urea loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii loo akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ futu sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but legumes like beans and groundnuts can capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth. Rotating these crops naturally restores your soil's fertility so your next crop grows better.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ebaanyɛ emɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛku sɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni oootsake lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains or cassava next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ dumɔwui loo ŋmei yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn and die under strong, direct sunlight. Plantains or cassava grow quickly and provide wide leafy shade that protects the cocoa seedlings and keeps the soil moist during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains, loo cassava, daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to grow strong and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Groundnuts bloom above the ground, but the actual nuts grow inside the soil. After the flower is pollinated, the stem naturally bends down and buries itself so the groundnut pods can safely form and ripen underground.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shi nuts diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baakoto shi ni ebaafu ehe yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ni amɛshwereɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground to prevent diseases and allows the plant to direct its energy into growing large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akabote mli. ni ehaa tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground before it is time to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays soaked with too much water for long periods, especially in heavy clay or low-lying areas. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away easily.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ nu babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Titri lɛ, yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa loo hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of proper nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing balanced plant food helps the blossoms stay attached and develop into fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni ahaa tso lɛ niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the leaves and cobs of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mibaa kɛ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on tender maize leaves. Checking your field early and putting crushed neem leaves or approved control products directly into the central leaf funnel of the plant stops them from destroying your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii. Akwɛɔ hei ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mra ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa loo nɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akudɔ lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite onibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and bunching together at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the juices from the leaves and spread plant viruses. Spraying the plants with mild insecticidal soap or neem oil early on controls these pests and protects new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli ni egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli Kɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni waaa lɛ shwieɔ tsei anɔ. loo neem fɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Koni akɛkudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni abu shweremɔ hee he

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the essential shade and moisture cocoa seedlings need during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients away. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or manure helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛfite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is mostly caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies, or by viruses they spread. Spraying with neem oil or soap solution early on kills these insects and protects the new leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla baashwie nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni egbe nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebu baai heei ahe.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients and weakens the land. Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, restoring land fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam plants make food in their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight, which helps the plant send more energy down to grow large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ bulbs agboi akwɛ̃.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and shrivel up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet places. Pruning extra shade trees and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm and keeps pods dry.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni efɔ tsɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei krokomɛi ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni miduuu tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. Regular watering and placing dry grass around the plant base keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ Regular plant bases lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the stem base swells. You can carefully dig up one stand to check if the tubers are thick enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ baafu Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu shidaamɔhe kome he nii ni okwɛ kɛji yitso lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the roots of my plantains help them grow during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ mi plantain shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, acting like a blanket over the soil. It blocks the hot sun from drying out the earth, keeps soil cool, and slowly decays into rich organic fertilizer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni efite fiofio ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my garden eggs drop their leaves and rot at the stem when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai ni amɛgboɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Excess water sitting around the plant roots suffocates them and encourages root-rot fungi. Creating raised soil beds and small drainage gutters lets extra water flow away from the roots.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle Tse lɛ shishifãi ahe lɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ewoɔ fungal shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsũi ni awó nɔ kɛ nu homɔ gbɛi bibii ni afee lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Is it harmful to leave old, giant trees standing inside my farm among my crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ mashi tsei wuji ni damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Giant trees cast heavy shade that can reduce sunlight for crops like maize or young cocoa, and competing roots take away water and nutrients. Trimming back large branches or removing select non-beneficial trees helps your main crops get enough sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo be ni baanyɛ aha hulu la aba shi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo kookoo bibii. ni shishifãi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji wuji loo tsei ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ni ooojie lɛ, ebaaye ebua otso titri lɛ ni ená hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to prune the overgrown branches of my old cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ kookoo niji ni egbɔ ni eda fe nine lɛ?

english: Pruning overgrown branches opens the tree canopy to allow light and airflow. This keeps the farm less humid, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod disease and encourages healthy flower and pod growth.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni eda fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ mli lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Gbɛ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ faaa. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ naa ni ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni he wa lɛ daa.

english: If my cassava roots stay in the ground for years and grow very huge, can I still harvest and eat them?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo ni amɛdara waa. Ani manyɛ makpa ni maye lolo?

english: When cassava roots are left in the ground for too long, they become woody, fibrous, and lose their starch content. It is best to harvest cassava at maturity (usually 9 to 12 months) for the best eating and processing quality.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ bafeɔ tso, amɛhe feɔ ŋmeii ni amɛmli ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Esa akɛ akpa ŋmei beni edara kwraa (bei pii lɛ, eyeɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12) koni anyɛ ana niyeli kɛ nitsumɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: What can I do when my fruit trees produce more fruit than my family can eat so they don't just rot on the ground?
ga: Mɛni mifeɔ kɛ́ mitso lɛ wo yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni miweku lɛ baanyɛ aye? Bɔni afee ni amɛkagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: Excess fruit can be sold at local markets, shared with neighbors, or processed into dried fruits, juices, and jams to extend shelf life and prevent post-harvest loss.
ga: Abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ aduawai ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei. Jaa kɛ akutsoŋbii loo afee lɛ aduawai ni egbi, nu, kɛ jam koni ekɛha shihilɛ aya hiɛ ni ekɛtsi nibii ni baafite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my harvested plantains turn soft and rot so quickly before I can get them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally release ethylene gas as they ripen, which speeds up spoilage in hot weather. Harvesting them at the proper mature-green stage and storing them in cool, shaded, well-ventilated areas slows down ripening.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ jieɔ ethylene gas kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha efite oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kpamɔ yɛ be ni sa mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni okɛto he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu yɔɔ. Ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ blɛoo.

english: Why do my mangoes fall off the tree and get spoiled by maggots before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-mango lɛ gbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni ŋmeii fite lɛ dani minyɛ mifo lɛ?

english: Fruit flies lay eggs inside ripening mangoes, causing them to rot and drop early. Clearing dropped fruits from the ground and using simple pest traps in the tree canopy helps protect your harvest.
ga: Yibii amli ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii yɛ mango ni ekwɛ̃ mli. Ehaa mango lɛ fiteɔ ni egbeeɔ shi oya. Yibii ni egbee shi lɛ ni oooŋɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ atsu nii koni eye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: How can I stop my harvested yams from rotting while they are stored in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ koni amɛkafite be mli ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot when kept in hot, poorly ventilated places or when damaged during harvest. Storing unbruised yams in a raised, shaded, and well-ventilated yam barn protects them from excessive heat, dampness, and pests.
ga: Sweet potatoes baa fite kɛji akɛ akɛto hei ni edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. aloo kɛ́ efite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potatoes ni etseee lɛ to tsũ ko ni nɔ kwɔ, ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ, hulutsoo ni fa fe nine, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: My family left a piece of farmland untouched for years; how should I prepare it before planting crops again?
ga: Miweku lɛ shi ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa he. Dani obaadu ekoŋŋ lɛ, te esa akɛ osaa ohe oha tɛŋŋ?

english: Fallow land builds up healthy soil organic matter, but it also accumulates weeds and deep-rooted brush. Clearing unwanted bush, testing or amending the soil, and tilling properly will prepare a clean bed for your new crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ewo muji lɛ feɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ebuaa jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni shishifãi mli kwɔ lɛ hu anaa. Tsoi bibii ni ataooo lɛ ajiemɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ kaa loo tsakemɔ Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baasaa he ko ni he tse kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ.

english: How often do I need to visit and weed my farm so wild plants don't ruin my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mayasara miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ amli koni koo mli tsei akafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Young crops need regular weed control, especially during the first 6 to 8 weeks after planting. Visiting your farm weekly ensures aggressive wild weeds do not choke your crops or steal soil nutrients.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni akwɛ jwɛi anɔ daa. Titri lɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 6 kɛyashi 8 ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Otsi fɛɛ otsi saramɔ ni oooya oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni koo mli jwɛi ni baa lɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii loo amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I clear away dead and rotting plant materials from around my living crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei ni egboi ni miifite lɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɛ ka lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaving rotting crop debris in the field can attract pests and harbour plant diseases or fungi that spread to healthy growing crops. Clearing or composting old crop waste keeps your field healthy.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ekɛ tsei ahe helai loo ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aba. Nibii ni etsɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ahe jwɛi ni oootsi loo okɛwo mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔji lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I wait for the rainy season before I start planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ wɔmɛɔ kɛyashi nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ dani wɔjeɔ tsei adumɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Waiting only for the rains limits you to one or two harvests a year and leaves your crops vulnerable to sudden droughts. Using controlled watering or simple irrigation lets you plant early and harvest when crop prices are highest in the market.
ga: Nugbɔ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha okpa kpamɔ kome loo enyɔ pɛ yɛ afi mli. Ni ekɛ oŋmɔshi nibii woɔ oshara mli akɛ hɔmɔ baaba trukaa. Nu ni akudɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii mra ni okpaa be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara wa fe fɛɛ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ.

english: Can I still grow crops successfully during the dry season when there is no rain?
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ lolo?

english: Yes, crops can grow very well in the dry season as long as you have access to a nearby water source like a stream, borehole, or river to keep the soil moist.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei baanyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli, kɛji akɛ oyɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ faa, nubu loo faa, koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does controlled watering help my crops grow better than relying only on rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni akudɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe nugbɔ pɛ ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Controlled watering gives your crops a steady, continuous supply of water at the exact times they need it, which prevents soil drying out, reduces crop stress, and leads to faster, more uniform growth.
ga: Nu ni akudɔ lɛ haa otsei lɛ náa nu ni yaa nɔ, ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi. Ha tso lɛ nɔnyɛɛ aba shi ni ekɛ oyaiyeli kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa baa.

english: Is local Ghana rice a profitable crop for me to grow right now?
ga: Ani Ghana ŋmãa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he ni esa akɛ madu bianɛ?

english: Yes, local Ghana rice currently has very high market demand, meaning traders and consumers are actively buying it, making it a reliable crop for earning strong farm income.
ga: Hɛɛ, amrɔ nɛɛ jarayeli nibii babaoo miitao Ghana maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ jarayelɔi kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miisumɔ waa ni amɛhe ŋmãa. Enɛ haa efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛha okwaayeli mli shika ni mli wa ni anáa.

english: What kind of land setup do I need to start growing rice successfully?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ̃ ehe hiaa mi koni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: Rice grows best on low-lying, flat land that holds water well, located close to a water source so the soil can stay consistently wet or flooded during the growing stage.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu hiɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Eyɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe ko Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ loo nu atsɔ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why do rice plants require so much water compared to other crops like cassava or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in swampy or flooded conditions because wet soil helps them absorb nutrients quickly while naturally suffocating weeds that would otherwise compete with the rice.
