ga: Omɔ tsei daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ jwɛi loo nu afua shihilɛi amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ jwɛi ni baanyɛ ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ abɔ akaŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What does it mean for me to expand from family farming to commercial crop farming?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛha mi akɛ magbɛ mihe kɛjɛ weku okwaayeli mli kɛya jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ nɔ?

english: Commercial farming means producing large quantities of crops specifically to sell in big markets for profit, rather than just feeding your household, which requires reliable land and permanent water supply systems.
ga: Jarayeli okwaayeli tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni afeɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jarayeli hei wuji koni ana sɛɛnamɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha oshia lɛ niyenii kɛkɛ Enɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ nu gbɛjianɔtoo ni baahi shi daa.

english: How do irrigation dams help my crops during long hot spells?
ga: Te nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Irrigation dams store large amounts of water that can be piped or channeled directly to your farm fields, keeping crop roots hydrated even when temperatures are high and rainfall stops.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ toɔ nu babaoo ni abaanyɛ akɛ paipii amli loo akɛya oŋmɔji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa ni nugbɔ ekpa nɛmɔ po.

english: Can I start small-scale irrigation on my own farm before formal community dams are built?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabɔi nu shwiemɔ bibioo yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mama akutso lɛ mli nu ŋshɔnaa yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ?

english: Yes, you can start simple irrigation by using small water pumps or digging water channels from local streams to your fields, allowing you to increase yields right away.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oje shishi kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Abaanyɛ ana enɛ kɛtsɔ nu pɔmp bibioo ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo nu ni jɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli faa ko mli kɛyaa oŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa okɛ nibii ni otsuɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farm land has good potential for large-scale crop production?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hegbɛi kpakpai kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo akwɛmɔ?

english: Land has high potential if it is fertile, mostly flat, and situated near a reliable year-round water supply like a river or stream that can support continuous crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ yɛ nyɛmɔi babaoo kɛji akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Efã babaoo yɛ faŋŋ. ni eyɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ, tamɔ faa loo nugbɔshiimɔ. ni baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii aya nɔ aya hiɛ

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds around my young cocoa trees even before they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle mitso lɛ he lɛ? Cocoa tsei ji gbekɛbii dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi po.

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients, water, and sunlight away from young cocoa plants, which can stunt their growth or kill them before they ever produce pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha amɛdalɛ afee mlɛo loo egbe amɛ dani amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: What will happen to my young cocoa seedlings if I leave the farm alone for a couple of years right after planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi ŋmɔ lɛ mli afii fioo komɛi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If left unattended, aggressive weeds and bush growth will choke the cocoa seedlings, competing for soil nutrients and light, which will cause most of the young trees to die.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni baa lɛ baatsi kookoo dumɔwui lɛ anaa. Shikamɔ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ la. Enɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo agboi.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast on my farmland right after I clear the land and plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ beni mijie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Clearing the land exposes the soil to direct sunlight and rain, which stimulates dormant weed seeds in the soil to sprout and grow rapidly alongside your planted crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya yɛ tsei ni oduɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Is it safe for me to rest and wait once my cocoa and plantain suckers are in the ground?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafo mihe ni mamɛ beni mi-cacao kɛ plantain tsei lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: No, early-stage farm management requires continuous physical work, especially suppressing weed growth and monitoring plant health, to ensure your crops survive and yield well later on.
ga: Dabi, shishijee ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ daa. Titri lɛ, jwɛi adalɛ ni tsiɔ naa kɛ tsei lɛ ahewalɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do many cocoa farmers in Ghana plant plantains on the same land as their new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miidu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛkookoo tsei heei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and provide essential shade to protect young, fragile cocoa seedlings from direct sunlight, while also providing food and income while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Be nɛɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, okɛ niyenii kɛ shika haa yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How long do I have to wait after planting my cocoa before I can start harvesting the pods?
ga: Kɛ́ odu kookoo lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani onyɛ okpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Standard cocoa trees usually take about three to four years to start bearing fruit, though some improved hybrid varieties can begin producing within two to three years if properly cared for.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3-4 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi baabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ afii 2-3 mli moŋ, shi kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can plantain plants damage or steal nutrients from my young cocoa trees if I plant them together?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ afite loo amɛju niyenii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo he kome?

english: When spaced correctly, plantain plants help young cocoa trees by offering needed shade without stealing too many nutrients, but you must manage them so they do not over-shade or crowd the cocoa.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baaye abua kookoo tsei bibii lɛ kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛaaha amɛ ni amɛjuuu niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo lɛ nɔ. Shi esa akɛ okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni kookoo lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ loo ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are young cocoa trees more delicate and sensitive than fully grown cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo fe cacao tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow root systems and delicate leaves that easily dry out under direct sun, whereas mature cocoa trees have deep roots and a thick leaf canopy that can withstand harsher weather.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa lɛ anaa.

english: Why does establishing a cocoa farm require so much labor right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kookoo ŋmɔ ni ato lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Newly planted farms require constant manual weed control, shade management, and crop protection during the first few critical years, which takes regular and heavy physical work.
ga: Okwaafoi ni adu ehee lɛ he miihia ni akɛ niji akudɔ jwɛi. Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu ni yaa nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli. ni biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛwoo ni tsii be fɛɛ be

english: Who should I involve in helping me maintain my cocoa farm to keep up with all the work?
ga: Namɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mihe awo mli koni eye ebua ni kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ ahi shi yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Many farmers involve family members, energetic young men and women, or hired farm labor to share the heavy ongoing work of weeding, clearing, and caring for the young farm year-round.
ga: Okwaafoi babaoo kɛ amɛwekumɛi ji wekumɛi. Oblahii kɛ oblayei ni yɔɔ miishɛɛ Aloo amɛheɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi koni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo nitsumɔ ni wa ni yaa nɔ ni ji jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli saamɔ, kɛ ekwɛmɔ mli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and rolling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellowing and rolling leaves usually mean your maize is either stressed from a lack of water or being attacked by pests like fall armyworms. Checking under the leaves for tiny caterpillars or applying nitrogen fertilizer when the soil is moist can help save the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworm etutua lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ mli loo okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and woody even though the leaves above ground look very big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, cassava puts all its energy into growing big leaves instead of feeding the roots. Adding wood ash or potassium-rich manure helps the plant send food down to build bulky cassava roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli Yɛ shishifãi lɛ niyenii najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso mli sũ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii amaje shi koni efee ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off before they can grow into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Heavy rain or sudden heat causes stress that makes pepper plants shed their flowers to survive. Flowers also fall off if insects fail to pollinate them, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo latsaa ni naa wa trukaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa chili tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ baa. Fɔfɔi hu shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo amɛmli. aloo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Maize takes away a lot of food from the soil, leaving it weak. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull free nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, naturally fertilizing the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abele gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ha egbɔjɔ Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the cocoa pods on my trees turning black and rotting during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet weather when air cannot pass through the farm. Pruning extra branches lets sunlight and wind dry the trees, preventing the fungus from multiplying.
ga: Fɛ̃i ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i be mli lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ agbi lɛ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo.

english: Why should I trim off some of the leaves and side branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛhe niji lɛ?

english: Trimming side shoots forces the tomato plant to send all its water and food to the main fruits instead of waste it on useless leaves. This gives you bigger, healthier tomatoes that ripen faster.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ, ebaaha tomato tso lɛ atsɔɔ emli nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ kɛya aduawai titri lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ Enɛ baaha tomatoi lɛ afee wuji ni amɛná hewalɛ ni ebaaha amɛshwere oya.

english: Why does spear grass keep growing back on my farm even after I weed it thoroughly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ spear jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mifoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Spear grass has deep underground stems called rhizomes that stay alive even when you cut the top leaves. To stop it, you must dig up the underground roots entirely or spray a systemic herbicide that travels down to kill the root system.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes. Enɛ baahi shi kɛji ofo baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ po. Bɔni afee ni okpa lɛ Esa akɛ Ofo shishifãi lɛ amli kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni baafã gbɛ kɛya shi koni egbe shishifãi lɛ ashwie nɔ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants look wilted and dead in the afternoon sun but wake up again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo ni egbo yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi te shi ekoŋŋ leebi

english: In the hot sun, leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it from dry soil, causing temporary wilting to protect the plant. Adding mulch like dried grass around the stem keeps the soil cool and wet so the leaves stay firm.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu tsei ahe Mulching tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Baai lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting and shrinking when I store them in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living roots that start growing shoots when they feel heat and humidity in storage. Breaking off the new sprouts early and keeping the tubers on raised racks in a shaded, cool barn keeps them fresh and heavy for market.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni baabɔi shweremɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli. Akwɛ̃ɔ tsei heei mra ni akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ato shĩai ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛfee ehee ni amɛtsii kɛha jarayeli.

english: Why are tiny insects chewing through the wooden stakes I set up in my vegetable farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye tsei ni mikɛma mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Termites and wood-boring insects chew dead wood to clear paths, build nests, or gather material, not necessarily because the wood contains crop food. Using untreated dead wood in your field attracts these pests, so treating wooden stakes or using alternative props prevents insect infestations near your crops.
ga: Termites kɛ koolooi ni shwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ yeɔ tsei ni egboi koni amɛkɛjie gbɛi, amɛma ŋmeii, loo amɛbua nibii anaa. Jeee be fɛɛ be enɛ he hiaa ejaakɛ tsei aniyenii hu yɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni egboi ni atsako amɛhe lɛ tsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaagbala nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso ŋmɔji akwɛmɔ loo nibii krokomɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii Ebaaye ebua ni tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni bɛŋkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my maize stems have small holes in them with insects chewing inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ mli?

english: Stem borer caterpillars burrow into maize stalks to feed on the tender inner tissues where they are protected from heat and predators. Applying recommended treatments into the leaf whorl early in the season prevents these borers from weakening the stem.
ga: Stem borers lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei amli koni amɛye mligbɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Biɛ ji he ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsa lɛ tsu nii yɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why does my yam plant need a tall wooden stake to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb upward to spread their leaves toward sunlight for better growth. Lifting the leaves off the ground also protects them from soil-borne diseases and encourages the plant to direct its energy into growing big underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu la mli koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ekɛtsiɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ anaa, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ atsu nii kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off before producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani pepper yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients cause stress to the plant, making it drop its flowers to conserve energy. Regular watering and mulching around the base help keep the root area cool and retain blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii ni esaaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔ̃ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he daa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ hu hiɔ shi.

english: Dropping leaves is the cassava plant's natural way of saving water during dry weather. When the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue expanding its roots.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni ŋmei tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shishifãi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop turning purple?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ purple lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually indicate a lack of phosphorus in the soil or cold, waterlogged earth that prevents roots from absorbing food. Adding organic manure or appropriate fertilizer corrects this deficiency.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ ni mli ejɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa tɔmɔ nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while still attached to the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads in overly wet and shaded conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to allow sunlight and airflow through the farm helps keep the cocoa pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fuŋ ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over easily when a heavy wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support the heavy weight of mature fruit bunches during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a bamboo or wooden prop prevents the tree from breaking or uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo tso fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tso lɛ akumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Why do some of my cassava tubers taste bitter or turn hard after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi feɔ ŋmɔlɔ loo amɛhe wa yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants produce chemical compounds as a natural defense mechanism when stressed by heat, drought, or delayed harvesting. Harvesting at the right time and soaking or processing the roots properly removes the bitter taste and makes them safe to eat.
ga: Cassava tsei feɔ tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛji dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ loo ŋmaakpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ be ni sa mli ni akɛ shishifãi lɛ wo nu mli loo atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaajie ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ebaaha amɛfee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen nutrients, or that the soil is holding too much water, which prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Fast-growing plantain trees have broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crops produce small yields when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing all of them to remain weak and produce smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How can I tell if armyworms are eating my maize farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ parasaiti miiye mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Look for ragged holes in the leaves and dark green or brown waste inside the central top funnel of the plant. If armyworms are present, you will see small caterpillars hiding inside that central shoot.
ga: Taomɔ bu ni etse ehe yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ funnel lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ Obaana ŋmeii bibii. Akɛtee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal disease that thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches lets sunlight and air flow through, keeping pods dry and healthy.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ duŋ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when weather temperatures become too hot or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells followed by sudden heavy watering, which causes stress.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ naa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi waa Ni nu ni akɛhaa amɛ trukaa lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. ni kɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots turn soft and watery instead of firm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni akpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni nu yɔɔ mli moŋ fe ni eeefee nɔ ni wa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots turn watery if harvested immediately after heavy rainfall or if harvested too late in the season. Harvesting during drier periods gives you firm, starchy roots.
ga: Nu baahi cassava shishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo akpa yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli tsɔ. Nikpamɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi ni mli edɔ ni tamɔ powda aba.

english: Does leaving dead grass and cleared leaves on my farm soil help my crops?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni egboi kɛ baai ni ajie yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mashiɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving dried leaves and grass around your crops creates mulch. Mulch traps moisture in the dirt, prevents weeds from growing, and rots over time to enrich your soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ oshi baai kɛ jwɛi ni egboi yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Mulch mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkafite yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛwo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable garden in the heat of the afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu shwane loo leebi?

english: Early morning is best because water reaches the roots before the hot sun evaporates it. It also allows leaves to dry quickly, which stops fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ nu lɛ baashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha etsɔ la. Eyeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ hu ni egbiɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ kpaa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my yam vines even after the vines are tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso lɛ kɛlɛ moŋ

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to generate food and grow big tubers underground. Tall weeds shade the vines and steal water and nutrients from the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat and sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to protect them, the strong sun scorches their leaves and dries out the soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kɛha wala lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my yam tubers stay very small if I plant them too close to each other on the mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ bibii waa kɛji akɛ midu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When yams are planted too tightly together, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Giving them enough space allows each tuber room to expand and grow big.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii ni mli wa tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛaaha lɛ haa tsu fɛɛ tsu mli lɛɛɔ ni edaa.

english: Why is burning my bush after clearing the farm bad for my cassava crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi jwɛi ni mishãa beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛha mi-cassava tsei lɛ?

english: Burning destroys essential nutrients and beneficial organisms in the topsoil that plants feed on. It leaves the ground hard and dry, making it difficult for cassava roots to expand properly.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsei yeɔ niyenii lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni egbiɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows diseases specific to tomatoes to build up in the dirt. Rotating with crops like beans or maize refreshes the soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tomato helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ

english: Why is it unsafe for me to dry my harvested maize directly on the bare tarred road?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ebɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ magbi mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni asphalt yɔɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Drying maize on roads exposes it to dirt, fumes, lead from vehicle exhaust, and animal waste. Using clean tarpaulins or raised drying platforms keeps the grain safe and prevents dangerous toxins from forming.
ga: Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ gbɛjegbɛ nɔ lɛ haa muji, lasu, kɛ lead ni jɛɔ tsɔne mli lasu mli lɛ naa. kɛ kooloi amli jwɛi Kɛ́ akɛ tarp ni he tse loo nɔ ni awo nɔ ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni ehaa tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baabua amɛhe naa.

english: Why do my stored groundnuts develop a bitter taste and green powder after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts ni mikɛto lɛ mli ŋɔɔ ni etsɔɔ powda eŋɔli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: The green powder is a dangerous mold called aflatoxin that grows when nuts are stored while still damp. Properly drying the groundnuts before storing them keeps them safe to eat and prevents mold poison.
ga: Powda eŋɔli lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ oshara ni atsɛɔ lɛ aflatoxin. Enɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmeii jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛyeɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know when my oranges are ready for harvesting so they don't rot quickly on the way to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-orange lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo oya yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Harvest oranges when the peel begins changing from dark green to yellowish-green while remaining firm. Picking them too late makes them soft and easily bruised, causing them to rot rapidly during transport.
ga: Kpãa ŋmeii beni amɛhewolo lɛ tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛtee eŋɔli ni mli edɔ ni loo lɛ mli wa lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ loo lɛ shwie shi sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha loo lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ ni ebaatsɔ mlɛo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ebaagbo oya beni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ shwieɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer right against the stem burns the plant's skin and young roots. Spreading it a short distance away allows the roots to absorb the nutrients safely from the moist soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata tso lɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hewolo kɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ ashã. Egbɛɔ eshwaa he ko kuku Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why must I wait a few days after spraying my cabbage before harvesting it to sell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ gbii fioo komɛi beni mikɛ mi-cabbage lɛ afɔ shi dani makpa koni mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays need time to break down naturally under the sun. Harvesting too soon leaves pesticide residues on the leaves that can cause serious food poisoning to your buyers.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ heɔ be dani efiteɔ yɛ hulu la shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ haa tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwɛɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni baanyɛ aha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ aye niyenii ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and stop producing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa fɔmɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny pests like insects sucking the sap or spreading a plant virus. Catching and managing these insects early stops them from stunting the plant and ruining your harvest.
ga: Koolooi bibii, tamɔ koolooi ni nuɔ nu loo amɛgbɛɔ muawai amɛshwãa tsei anɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ooomɔ ni okwɛ nɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafee shwilafo ni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the soil runs out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green leaves. The maize plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃. Abɛi tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land every year make my harvest smaller each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ haa miŋmãa lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Maize draws the same specific nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting it continuously drains those nutrients completely and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in that soil.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Tsei ni yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ shwieɔ nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ kɛyaa. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants staying short and refusing to grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni ekpooɔ akɛ ebaada lɛ?

english: When soil is hard or lacks essential nutrients, plant roots cannot spread out to feed. Stunted growth happens because the roots are restricted and cannot gather enough food and water to build a strong stem and leaves.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ mli lɛ Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛyatao niyenii. Dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe naa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛbua niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni amɛfee tsei kɛ baai ni wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a field without any large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or taller forest trees to block the sun and keep the air cool and moist around them until their roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei kakadaji koni amɛtsi hulu lɛ naa ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli ajɔɔ. Ha efee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baa mli.

english: How do weeds actually hurt my crops if I leave them growing in the same farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miha amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Weeds act like aggressive neighbors that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from the soil, leaving your crop plants hungry, thirsty, and weak.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii, kumai yeɔ bo, ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my corn seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain in the early season is often a temporary rain followed by a dry spell. If seeds sprout during this dry period, the hot sun will dry out the weak young roots before the real rainy season starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ ji be kukuoo ko ni nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ hɔmɔ be nɛɛ mli Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ agbi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why do I get smaller crops if I plant many seeds very close together to save farm space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛbu ŋmɔ mli he lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their leaves block each other's sunlight and their roots fight for the same water and soil food. This competition leaves all the plants small and weak instead of strong and full of fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee hewalɛ ni eyi obɔ kɛ yibii

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground when the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can make clay soil waterlogged, filling up all the tiny air holes in the ground. Cassava roots need air to breathe, and without it, water mold attacks the tubers and causes them to rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ afee nu. Okɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ awo mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Ni kɛji akɛ ebɛ Nu mli ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Extreme heat or lack of steady water stresses the plant. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival rather than wasting energy on growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛwala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni okɛduɔ aduawai

english: Why are my bean plants drooping and wilting during the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil is usually caused by microscopic soil pests or fungal diseases that block the water-carrying tubes inside the stem, preventing water from reaching the upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsiɔ nu ni akɛyaa tsɔnei ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ baa. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe.

english: Why is maize the main crop used for making animal feed in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ji kooloi aniyenii titri yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Maize is rich in easily digestible carbohydrates, providing the high energy that poultry and livestock need to grow quickly and produce well.
ga: Carbohydrates ni shwieɔ mɔ mli oya lɛ fa babaoo yɛ ŋmãa mli. Ehaa hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ ni he hiaa kooloi kɛ kooloi koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: How many months does it take for a standard maize crop to mature after planting?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ ni ŋmãa ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ shɛɔ ŋmãa ni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most maize varieties grown in Ghana mature within 90 to 120 days (3 to 4 months), depending on the rain and the specific variety planted.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ gbii 90 kɛyashi 120 mli (nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4), ni enɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or heavy rain that has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: What causes my maize cobs to have missing grains instead of full rows?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii bɛ mli moŋ fe ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ?

english: Missing grains happen due to poor pollination, which is often caused by drought or extreme heat during the flowering stage when the silks are forming.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ jɛ pollination ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli, be mli ni siliki lɛ miifee lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: How can I keep insects like weevils from eating my harvested maize in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye ŋmãa ni akpa yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Drying the maize thoroughly until the grains are hard and storing them in sealed, airtight bags prevents weevils from surviving and multiplying.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa ni akɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkahi shi ni amɛshwere.

english: What is the best way to plant my maize to keep weeds from taking over the field?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ ŋmãa koni jwɛi akaye ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting in straight, evenly spaced rows allows the growing maize leaves to shade the ground quickly, which stops weeds from getting sunlight to grow.
ga: Aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja ni ato he gbɛjianɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Enɛ baabu jwɛi lɛ ahe koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Why does the price of imported farm inputs like fertilizer go up when the dollar rate rises?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli mli nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ajara yaa hiɛ beni shika ni ji dɔlai lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Because agrochemical companies buy these imported supplies using foreign currency, an increase in the dollar rate makes it more expensive for them to import, driving up local prices.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, agrochemical nitsumɔhei lɛ kɛ maŋsɛɛ shika heɔ nibii nɛɛ. Dɔlai ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa nibii ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ jara wa waa. Enɛ haa maŋ lɛ mli jara yaa hiɛ.

english: Are there other crops I can grow on my farm to replace some of the maize in my animal feed?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ ni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛto ŋmãa najiaŋ yɛ mikooloi aniyenii mli?

english: Crops like cassava and sorghum can be dried and processed to replace a portion of maize in feed while still giving animals energy.
ga: Abaanyɛ agbi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni atsu he nii koni akɛto ŋmãa ni yɔɔ kooloi aniyenii mli lɛ ekomɛi najiaŋ yɛ be mli ni ehaa kooloi lɛ hewalɛ lolo.

english: Why does the market price of maize jump so high during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa jara yaa ŋwɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, fewer farmers are harvesting, so the supply of fresh maize drops while demand stays high, causing prices to rise.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Okwaafoi kpaŋ nii fioo No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa hee ni akɛhaa lɛ eba shi yɛ be mli ni nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ fa lolo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji jara ni yaa hiɛ.

english: How can I improve my soil to get more maize harvest without buying expensive chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni manyɛ makpã ŋmãa babaoo ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: Adding animal manure, compost, or rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas returns natural nitrogen into the soil for free.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo ŋmei fata ŋmei tamɔ tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer around the base will help feed the soil and restore the plant's health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he Konii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does rainwater stay standing on top of my soil for days instead of sinking in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu damɔ shikpɔŋ gbii babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo lɛ?

english: Standing water means your soil has high clay content or has become too hard and compacted. Adding organic matter like dry grass, compost, or decayed leaves breaks up hard soil so water can drain properly without rotting plant roots.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ fa babaoo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ jwɛi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo baai ni fiteɔ fata he lɛ, ebaagbala sũ ni mli wa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni nu lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates living shade umbrellas that protect the seedlings from harsh sun until they are strong enough to grow outdoors.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Young cocoa lɛ masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ kpo nɔ.

english: Staking raises yam leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight to make food for the plant. Leaves left on the damp ground easily catch diseases and cannot gather enough light to build big tubers underground.
ga: Staking baajie sweet potato baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Baai ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ helai baa mɔ nɔ oya ni enyɛŋ ebua la ni fa bɔ ni sa naa ni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the center fold?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the fall armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center funnel of young maize plants. Catching them early and applying safe recommended insecticides or local remedies directly into the plant funnel stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji cutworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo maŋ lɛ mli tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ afee shweshweeshwe lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ awo tsei amli ŋmeii amli. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off instead of turning into fresh tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato hee lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or too much chemical nitrogen. Giving the plants consistent water at their roots and light shade during midday heat keeps the flowers healthy enough to form fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsofa ni ji nitrogen babaoo nɔ. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ nu daa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ hulutsoo yɛ shwane mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Should I leave all the small suckers growing around my main plantain stem, or cut some off?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii yɛ mi plantain tso titri lɛ he loo mafo ekomɛi?

english: You should trim away most suckers and leave only one or two strong ones. Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight for water and soil nutrients, which results in smaller, weaker bunches of plantains.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni oshi eko loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛwuu koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Why do weeds make my cassava plants stay thin and short even when there is good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ kuku kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cassava plants and steal sunlight, water, and food from the soil before the cassava roots can reach them. Clearing weeds early gives your crop full access to everything it needs to grow big roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmei tsei. ni ejuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ náa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi wuji lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are mature enough to dig up for harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa ni akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the plant reaches 9 to 12 months old and its bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off. You can test harvest by gently digging around one plant to check if the tubers are thick enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo beni tso lɛ eye nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 ni eshishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ oka okpamɔ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome he ni ooofo blɛoo koni ona kɛji ŋmeii lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same spot on my land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and lets maize pests build up in the ground. Rotating your farm with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients back into the dirt naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi baaje shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni oooha ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake oŋmɔ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means the crop is starving for nitrogen, an important nutrient it needs from the soil to stay green and build strong stalks.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛma tsei ni wa.

english: Why do people say planting beans together with my maize will help the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as natural fertilizer for nearby crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot completely drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests and diseases that target maize to build up in that soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ abɛi lɛ mli lɛ kwraa. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, pepper plants lose water from their leaves faster than their roots can take it up, so they temporarily curl or droop to protect themselves from drying out.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too high or water is inconsistent, which prevents the flower from pollinating properly to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a clear field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaf surfaces and shallow roots that burn and dry out quickly under direct sunshine; they require shade trees to protect them until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground when the rains are too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe; excessive water logging suffocates the roots and creates the wet conditions that fungi need to decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu babaoo ni ahiɛɔ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa ni ŋmei lɛ baafolɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my seeds very close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛkuu mli?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to compete with one another for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin plants with smaller produce.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa shi amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do weeds growing around my cassava actually hurt the crop if there is enough dirt for everything?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cassava lɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛji shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and actively steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your cassava, leaving the crop weak and reducing how much food it produces.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-cassava lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni niyenii ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why are there small ragged holes appearing inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni etse amɛhe lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes inside the center funnel of young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the funnel and eat the soft growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of your maize plant mean the soil is running low on nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to build strong stems and stay green, so the plant moves whatever little nitrogen it has left to its newest top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ o-corn tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma amɛshishifãi ni wa ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant groundnuts or beans before planting maize on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei loo ŋmei dani wɔdu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family. Their roots work with good soil bacteria to grab nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which acts like a free natural fertilizer for your next crop of maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans fata legume weku lɛ he. Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai kpakpai tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ lɛ awo sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight. Large trees act as natural sunshades that keep the soil cool and moist, protecting the fragile young cocoa leaves from getting scorched by the hot sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he.

english: Why shouldn't I spray water on my vegetable leaves in the middle of a hot sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ nu shwieɔ aduawai ahe baai anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli?

english: Water droplets on leaves during hot hours act like tiny magnifying glasses under the sun, which can burn the leaves. Warm, wet leaves also attract fungal diseases that can ruin your crop.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo yɛ hulu lɛ shishi, ni baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ. Baai ni mli edɔ ni efɔ lɛ hu gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ afite onibii lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb up so their leaves can spread out and get as much sunlight as possible to make food. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and diseases from damaging the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛhoo nii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei ni fiteɔ kɛ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I cut off the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajie midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them lets all the food go into the main tree so it can bear bigger and heavier bunches.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Nibii ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii lɛ fɛɛ yaa tso titri lɛ mli bɔni afee ni enyɛ eye ebua tso ni da ni tsii fe no lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. This sudden water or heat stress causes the plant to drop its blossoms to save its own life.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Nɛkɛ nu loo dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ haa tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem starts to crack upwards as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark powdery droppings in the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ powda bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ hoppers lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It crawls into the central shoot of the maize plant where it hides from the sun and eats the soft, developing leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Efoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli he ni ekɛ ehe teeɔ hulu la lɛ he ni eyeɔ baai bibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: What makes my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly like small cups?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap underneath the leaves. As they feed, they transfer viruses that cause the leaves to twist and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Amɛjieɔ helai ni fiteɔ baai ni tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa lɛ.

english: How can I store my harvested maize so it doesn't get spoiled by insects or mold before I am ready to sell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii akafite lɛ dani afee klalo akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Drying your maize properly until the grains are hard, and then storing them in airtight bags or cool, dry granaries keeps moisture and pests away so your harvest stays fresh for months.
ga: Gbimɔ o-corn lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi mli koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Bɔni afee ni onibii lɛ ahi shi ehee nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do crops like grains last for a long time in storage, but my fresh tomatoes spoil within a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmaa hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi mi-tomato hee lɛ fite yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Grains can be dried to remove almost all water, which stops mold and decay from growing, whereas fresh fruits like tomatoes contain lots of water and continue to age and break down quickly after picking.
ga: Abaanyɛ agbi ŋmaa koni ajie nu lɛ babaoo kɛjɛ mli. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aya hiɛ. Yɛ be mli ni aduawai heei tamɔ tomato mli nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni ebaagbɔ ni ebaafite oya kɛji akɛ ato he.

english: How do I know if my harvested grain is dry enough to put inside a storage house without rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmaa ni mikpa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni efiteee?

english: You can test your grain by biting it hard; if it cracks sharply without feeling chewy, or if salt doesn't stick to it when shaken in a dry jar, it is dry enough for long-term storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka odumɔwui lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ amɛ ni ooomɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efo oya ni enuuu he akɛ ashɛre lɛ Aloo kɛji ŋmei lɛ shwieee shi kɛji akɛ akpokpo yɛ tɔ ni egbi mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my stored grains lose weight and turn into dust over time when kept in regular sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ sũ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ́ akɛto daa kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils bore into the seeds to eat the nutritious inner part, leaving behind light, empty shells and insect waste, which destroys the weight and quality of your crop.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii shwieɔ dumɔwui amli koni amɛye niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni amɛshiɔ la, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko kɛ ŋmeii amli fãi. Enɛ fiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ kɛ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ.

english: Do I need to put chemical powders on my stored beans to keep tiny beetles away?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tsofa powda awo kɔfi ŋmeii ni ato lɛ anɔ koni ŋmeii bibii lɛ akabote mli?

english: Not necessarily; you can store your beans in triple-layer airtight bags (such as PICS bags) which naturally suffocate beetles and eggs by cutting off oxygen, keeping your food chemical-free and safe.
ga: nɔ ni he ehiaaa; Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmeii awo vacuum kotoku ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii etɛ mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku), ni no baaha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baafo mli lɛ nɔ. Ha oniyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni tsofai bɛ mli ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my storage building need cool airflow if the crops are already harvested and dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi nitoohe lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ?

english: Harvested crops are still living plant tissues that release heat and moisture into the air. Good air circulation removes this trapped heat and dampness so mold cannot grow on your produce.
ga: Tsei ni akpa lɛ ji tsei ahe fãji ni hiɛ ka lolo ni jieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ shwereee yɛ nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do market prices for crops drop so low right after harvest time, and how can storage help me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be sɛɛ lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi?

english: Prices drop because almost every farmer is harvesting and trying to sell at the same time, flooding the market. Storing your crop allows you to wait until supply drops and prices rise before selling.
ga: Jara baa shi ejaakɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ okwaafonyo fɛɛ okwaafonyo miikpa ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli, ni enɛ eha jara lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nu. Onibii ni okɛtoɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ omɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ baa shi ni amɛjara baaya hiɛ dani ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: How does storing my crops give me better control over the prices buyers offer me?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ haa minine shɛɔ jara ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛhaa mi lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: When you have safe storage, you are not forced to accept low offers out of fear that your crop will rot tomorrow. You gain the freedom to hold onto your produce until a buyer offers a fair price.
ga: Beni oyɛ he ko ni okɛtoɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Anyɛŋ onɔ ni okpɛlɛ nɔ ni baa shi nɔ yɛ gbeyeishemɔ akɛ onibii lɛ baafite wɔ lɛ hewɔ. Oyɛ heyeli ni okɛ onibii lɛ baahiɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni mɔ ko ni baahe lɛ baaha bo jara ni sa.

english: I hear about government community warehouses; how can keeping my produce there help my farm business?
ga: Minu nɔyeli akutso lɛ mli nitoohe lɛ he. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nibii ni mikɛtoɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ?

english: Government warehouses provide professional, large-scale storage that keeps your crops safe from pests and weather, sometimes providing you with storage certificates you can use to secure loans while waiting for better prices.
ga: Nɔyeli nitoohei lɛ yɛ hei wuji ni ŋaalɔi kɛ nibii toɔ ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he. Bei komɛi lɛ, nibii ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ he wolo ko baahi ni obaanyɛ okɛtsu nii ni okɛwo nyɔmɔ be mli ni omɛɛɔ jara ni hi fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: How do government buying programs or buffer stock systems work to protect my income?
ga: Te nɔyeli lɛ nibii ahe gbɛjianɔtoi loo shika ni akɛwoɔ nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii eha tɛŋŋ koni ebu mishika ni miná lɛ he?

english: Government buffer stock operations step in during heavy harvests to purchase crops directly from farmers at a stable, guaranteed minimum price, preventing market prices from crashing completely.
ga: Atsuɔ nɔyeli lɛ buffer stock nitsumɔi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ babaoo mli koni akɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ okwaafoi adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ jara ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ nɔ. Tsi jarayeli jara lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi kwraa.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I burn all the cleared bush on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji mishã tsei bibii fɛɛ ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu lɛ?

english: Burning kills beneficial soil organisms and burns away natural organic matter, leaving the topsoil dry, weak, and less able to hold water for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ, ni eshãa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli egbiɔ, egbɔjɔɔ, ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ nu kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell if the soil has enough moisture for me to start planting my seeds after the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: Dig down about the depth of your hand into the dirt; if the soil easily forms a ball in your fist without crumbling, it holds enough moisture for seeds to sprout safely.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aaafee bɔ ni onine lɛ mli kwɔ ha. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔ bɔɔlu yɛ otsitsi mli ni efoŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and moisture to protect young cocoa trees during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni akɛbu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do some extension officers advise covering the dirt around my crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi komɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ awo he ni ebɔle jɛmɛ lɛ he sũ lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, traps moisture in the soil on hot days, keeps root zones cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow starting from the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow strong. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, black rotten spots at the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɔɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, often caused by irregular watering during dry periods.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: What is causing tiny holes in the middle leaves of my young corn with small dirt-like grains inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Dumɔwu bibioo ko yɛ mi-baby corn leaf lɛ teŋ. Etamɔ muji yɛ emli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing center of the corn plant and eats the tender young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without turning into any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when temperatures get too high, when the soil gets too dry or waterlogged, or when there are not enough insects like bees around to pollinate them.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee pollination.

english: How do I know which way to put a cassava stem cutting into the ground when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole bɔ ni ooofee ofolɔ o-cassava tso lɛ ni okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small buds on the stem cutting and make sure they point upwards toward the sky, because planting stems upside down prevents healthy shoots from sprouting easily.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei bibii lɛ. yɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Ni okwɛ koni amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yitso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adara oya.

english: Why does planting groundnuts make the soil richer for the crop I plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I make a raised bed to plant in instead of just planting directly in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee saatso ni awo nɔ kɛha dumɔ moŋ fe ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Making a planting bed helps the crop produce plenty of leaves, whereas planting stems directly in plain ground will only give you a very small harvest.
ga: Dumɔ he ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ baai babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ko fioo pɛ aba.

english: If I want to harvest a lot of leafy greens to sell, what is the best way to plant them?
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni okpa aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ. Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ lɛ?

english: You should plant them in prepared beds, because beds encourage the plant to grow abundant leaves rather than just focus on stem growth.
ga: Esa akɛ odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni asaa he nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, saatsoi lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa tsei lɛ ahe tsei babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ baama tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ pɛ anɔ.

english: Will planting stem cuttings directly in my field give me a big leaf harvest?
ga: Ani tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha maná baai wuji?

english: No, planting stems directly will only give you a little bit of leaves. To get plenty of leaves, you need to prepare proper planting beds.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni ooodu tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha oná baai fioo ko pɛ. koni onine ashɛ baai babaoo nɔ Ehe miihia ni osaa dumɔhe ni sa.

english: Does changing the way I prepare my soil affect which part of the plant grows bigger?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakemɔ lɛ saa tso lɛ fãi ni daraa lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, planting in beds specifically boosts leaf production, while other planting methods may leave you with mostly stems and very few leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔ yɛ saatso nɔ tɛ̃ɛ haa baa shweremɔ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ be mli ni gbɛi krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii Ebaanyɛ eshi bo kɛ ŋmeii babaoo kɛ baai fioo ko pɛ.

english: I hear other farmers talking about 'po' and 'dentist'—are these different types of the same crop?
ga: Minu okwaafoi krokomɛi ni miiwie ‘Po’ kɛ ‘Dentist’ he. Ani tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ji enɛɛmɛi?

english: Yes, 'po' and 'dentist' are two different varieties of the same crop, and each variety can behave or serve a slightly different purpose.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ‘po’ kɛ ‘dentist’ ji tso kome mli henɔi srɔtoi enyɔ. Ni kooloi srɔtoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko baanyɛ ajie amɛhe kpo loo amɛtsu yiŋtoi srɔtoi fioo ahe nii.

english: How do I choose between the 'po' variety and the 'dentist' variety for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ‘po’ tso kɛ ‘dentist’ tso kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You should look at what each variety is meant to do; understanding the specific function of 'po' or 'dentist' will help you select the right one for your harvest goals.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ nɔ ni srɔtoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko feɔ. Kɛ́ onu nitsumɔi pɔtɛɛ ni ‘po’ loo ‘nyanyɔji’ tsuɔ lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ohala nitsumɔ ni sa kɛha otii ni okɛma ohiɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do different varieties of the same plant have different uses?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komekomei lɛ ahe sɛɛnamɔi srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Different varieties like 'po' and 'dentist' have specific characteristics—some might grow leaves better or serve a unique function, so it helps to know what each variety does best.
ga: Henɔi srɔtoi tamɔ ‘po’ kɛ ‘dentist’ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ su. Henɔi komɛi baanyɛ akwɛ baai jogbaŋŋ loo amɛtsu nitsumɔi krɛdɛɛi. No hewɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni aleɔ henɔ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I avoid getting confused when I see different crop varieties being grown in my community?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mihe kɛjɛ basabasafeemɔ he beni minaa ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You avoid confusion by learning the specific function of each variety, like 'po' or 'dentist', so you know exactly why a farmer is growing that particular type.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa futumɔ kɛtsɔ nitsumɔ pɔtɛɛ ni tso srɔtoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tsuɔ, tamɔ ‘po’ loo ‘nyanyɔji’ lɛ kasemɔ nɔ, koni ole nɔ tuuntu hewɔ ni okwaafoi lɛ duɔ nakai tso pɔtɛɛ lɛ.

english: My main goal is to harvest green leaves rather than stems, so how should I set up my field?
ga: Otii titri ni ma mihiɛ ji ni makpa baai eŋɔli moŋ fe ŋmeii. No hewɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ mato midumɔ he lɛ he gbɛjianɔ?

english: Focus on building planting beds, because using beds is designed to maximize leaf growth so you get plenty of harvest.
ga: Kɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama dumɔhei afeemɔ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, afee saatsoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ koni ebaaha baai lɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni oná ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Is there a big difference in harvest size if I focus on growing leaves instead of stems?
ga: Ani kpamɔ lɛ dalɛ baafee srɔto kwraa kɛji mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ma baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ŋmeii ni miida lɛ?

english: Yes, focusing on growing leaves in planting beds gives you a plentiful harvest, whereas focusing on stem planting yields very little produce.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ma tsei ahe tsei ni ooodu yɛ otsu lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha oná kpamɔ babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ jwɛŋmɔ ma dumɔwui ni akɛ tsei tsei duɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nɔ ko fioo pɛ baaba.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct heat from the sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and have wide leaves that create shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist so it can survive its early stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eshishijee fãi lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is an important plant nutrient. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to stick tall wood into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers. Lifting the vines up on tall sticks helps the leaves catch full sunlight to make food for the tuber underground, while also keeping the leaves off the damp wet dirt where diseases grow.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no ji nɔ ni kɛ helai srɔtoi baa.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully grown and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is time when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil right around the base of the stem starts to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Obaale beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: What is eating small holes in my young corn leaves and leaving dirt inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji yɛ tsei lɛ amli?
