english: That is likely the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides inside the growing point of the maize plant to eat soft leaves, and early treatment with recommended sprays or neem extracts is needed to protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ no ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ koni eye baai bibii. ni ehe miihia ni atsa lɛ mra. Kɛ neem spray loo tsofa ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni akɛbuɔ onibii ahe lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass is called mulching. It keeps the soil moist by stopping the sun from drying out the water, prevents weeds from growing, and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ hulu la ni ehaaa nu lɛ agbi lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why is it risky to sow my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the year is often followed by a hot dry spell before the main rains start. If your seeds germinate during that brief rain, the hot sun afterwards will dry out and kill the small seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ, No sɛɛ lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui bibii lɛ agboi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme hot weather, inconsistent watering, or lack of soil food. Keeping the soil evenly moist and avoiding extreme dryness helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same piece of farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the same specific nutrients out of the soil continuously and allows specialized soil pests to multiply. Swapping with crops like beans or groundnuts restores nutrients back into the dirt.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi krɛdɛɛi babaoo feɔ babaoo. Jarayeli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the young plants fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Giving each plant proper distance ensures every crop gets enough room and nourishment to produce a full harvest.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ sa lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there is too much direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn and dry out easily under harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby provides a protective cover that keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya ni egbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the land later in the season. Planting them together allows you to harvest two different crops from the same field without them competing for space at the same time.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Yɛ ŋmei gbɛfaŋ lɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli ni okɛ he ko akaŋ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants turn light yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abele tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize plants usually mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that heavy rainfall has waterlogged the soil and prevented the roots from taking up food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ abɛi tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni etsĩ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛye nii.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperature levels get too high or when there is severe water stress. It can also happen if insects like bees are not available to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛna nu he haomɔ ni naa wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii amli ŋmeii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically a reaction to tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices, or a sign that the plant has contracted a leaf-curl virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ feɔ. Aloo eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni haa tso lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ emɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava rot in the ground when heavy rains flood the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess water sits on the field for days, it smothers the roots, allowing rotting fungi and bacteria to quickly break down the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ta ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ, efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: How do I know if my soil is too weak to grow a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni ekɛ ŋmaa kpakpa baawo?

english: If your crops grow very slowly, look pale green instead of dark green, or produce small yields despite good rainfall, your soil has lost its nutrients and needs organic manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo waa lɛ Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. aloo ewoɔ yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efite ni ehe miihia humus loo organic fertilizer.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my maize field so quickly right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ oya nɛkɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths lay hundreds of eggs on young maize leaves right after the rains begin because the soft, fresh green shoots provide ideal food for their newly hatched caterpillars.
ga: Autumn caterpillar ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ ŋmeii baa bibii anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni efɔ ehee lɛ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the vines of my yam plants turning black and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: Blackened yam vines are a common sign of yam anthracnose, a fungal disease that spreads rapidly across leaves and stems in warm, humid weather after rain.
ga: Atomɔ wain tsei ni efee ediŋŋ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ atoohe anthracnose he. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ baai kɛ tsei ahe yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know when my underground cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves on the stem turn yellow and drop off, the base of the stem thickens, and cracks begin to form in the soil around the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni ŋmeii bɔi feemɔ yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli.

english: What is the pink or blue powder coated on the seeds I bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni ji powda ni yɔɔ pinki loo bluu ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nihɔɔlɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: That colored coating is a protective medicine made of fungicide and insecticide. It protects the seed from rotting in the damp soil and stops insects from eating it before it sprouts.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ ji tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii fee. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. ni etsĩɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Can I save leftover seeds from last year's harvest and plant them again this season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato ni madu amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Old seeds lose their strength over time, especially in hot weather. While they might still grow, they will yield much less crop compared to buying fresh, certified seeds or testing a few in wet cloth first to check if they germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui momo lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara lolo, shi kɛlɛ. Shi ebaaha yibiiwoo bibioo kwraa fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ. Aloo okɛ mama ni efɔ lɛ aka amɛ okwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ona kɛji amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the rains keep changing in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Instead of relying on specific calendar months, wait until the soil receives at least two solid days of rain. Dig down to palm-depth; if the soil is damp and sticks together slightly, it is safe to sow your seeds.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ kalanda nyɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ lɛ, Mɛɛ kɛyashi kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa gbii enyɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ onine mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ he lɛ Obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui shweshweeshwe.

english: Dropping leaves is a survival trick. The plant intentionally sheds its leaves to stop losing water during dry spells, storing its energy underground in the tubers until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji teemɔŋ sane ni haa mɔ hiɔ shi. Tsei tsɔɔ yiŋtoo ko nɔ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ akpa. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ yitso lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast with big leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the cocoa the shade and cool soil it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow even after I applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the plant lacks food, but if you already used fertilizer, heavy rain may have washed it away, or waterlogged soil is suffocating the roots so they cannot absorb the nutrients.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii. Shi kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii etsu nii momo Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo tsei lɛ. Aloo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. When it gets too hot, the pollen dries up and the flower gives up.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Kɛji edɔ tsɔ Pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ gboɔ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on my farm after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the ground. Groundnuts are special crops that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does spear grass keep growing back on my land even after I spray weedkiller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ spear jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ edaa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ eshwie shi po lɛ?

english: Spear grass has deep underground roots that store energy. Contact sprays only kill the green leaves on top, while systemic weedkillers travel down into the roots to kill the whole plant permanently.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ hewalɛ toɔ. Spray lɛ baagbe baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli koni eyagbe tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛya naanɔ.

english: How do I know my yam tubers are ready to harvest without digging them up first?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛtsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Look at the vines above ground. When the leaves turn yellow and dry up completely, it means the plant has finished growing and put all its energy down into the tuber.
ga: Kwɛmɔ wein tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ edara ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ewo bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when the sun gets too bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Beni hulu la lɛ kpɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. They need temporary shade plants like plantain or cassava grown beside them to protect their soft leaves from scorching until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava, ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, root space, and soil nutrients to grow. Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for food, leading to weak stems and small harvests.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa, shishifãi kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu yɛ amɛhe koni amɛye niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa, ni akpaa nii fioo.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to start planting my seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔwui adumɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ?

english: You should plant after the first few steady rains have soaked deep into the ground, usually around April. Planting too early in dry soil causes the seeds to dry out and die before they can sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ odu beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ bei fioo lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee April. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build healthy green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help them regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads during cool, wet weather. You can protect your farm by trimming overcrowding branches to let air flow through and removing infected pods immediately.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ ni ooofo mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ, ni ooojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow much slower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi tso titri lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, stealing water, sunlight, and plant food directly from the soil. Removing weeds gives your main crops all the nutrition they need to grow fast and strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni amɛduɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji ojie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ, obaaha tsei ni okwɛɔ amɛ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa tree if I want more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ cacao tso ni eda lɛ nɔ kɛji miitao ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes dead or useless branches so that sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts of the tree. This helps the tree direct its energy into producing large, healthy pods instead of feeding unwanted leaves.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha baai ni ataooo lɛ niyenii

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before tiny pods can even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ afee lɛ?

english: Trees shed their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by hot weather, dry soil, or sap-sucking insects. Providing good shade and protecting the trees from pests helps the flowers stay on and form cocoa pods.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kpakpa ha tso lɛ ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and droop during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan winds absorb water out of leaves and soil very fast. Plantains require lots of water to stay firm, so they droop to protect themselves when soil moisture becomes very low.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ oya. Nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛgbee shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Can I plant cassava in the same field where I am growing young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, cassava can provide useful temporary shade for young cocoa trees. However, keep enough distance between them so the cassava's large tuber roots do not steal water and food from the young cocoa tree.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei baanyɛ aha cacao tsei bibii lɛ aná be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, ha jɛkɛmɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi cacao tsei lɛ ateŋ bɔni afee ni cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi wuji lɛ akaju nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How do I know how many weeks my maize or cowpea crops need before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male otsii enyiɛ ni ebaahe ni ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa afee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ?

english: Fast-growing crops usually have a set maturity window, often around 12 to 16 weeks (3 to 4 months). Checking the crop's specific variety duration helps you plan your harvest time before the rainy season ends or dry weather sets in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni daa oya lɛ yɛ be ni ato kɛha amɛdalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ feɔ otsii 12 kɛyashi 16 (nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4). Kɛ́ okwɛ be ni tsei srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ komɛi yeɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni oto okpamɔ be lɛ he gbɛjianɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba naagbee loo hulutsoo be lɛ aba.

english: Why is it important for me to follow guidelines from crop researchers and extension officers on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni ŋmɔshi nibii amlitaolɔi kɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛhaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Agricultural researchers test seeds and farming methods under specific Ghanaian climate conditions. Following their tested guidelines helps reduce the risk of crop failure, controls pests, and improves your overall harvest yields.
ga: Okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi kaa dumɔwui kɛ okwaayeli gbɛi lɛ amɛkwɛɔ yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli. Nifeemɔi ni aka amɛ akwɛ lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafite lɛ baa shi. tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ ni oha onitsumɔ fɛɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What are the advantages of preparing my land early before the main rains begin?
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mra he Mɛni yɔɔ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ baa?

english: Early land preparation allows the soil to soak up the initial rains, helps clear weeds before they mature, and ensures your seeds are planted early enough to take full advantage of the entire rainy season.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ shishijee nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi lɛ dani amɛdaraa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni adu odumɔwui lɛ mra bɔ ni sa koni onyɛ oná nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do helper crops or companion plants support my main crops on the field?
ga: Te yelikɛbualɔ loo nanemɛi tsei baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii titri ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Helper crops, like planting beans alongside maize, capture essential nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, while also providing living ground cover to protect the main crop's roots from heat.
ga: Fiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii asɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe Emɔɔ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni wala yɔɔ nɔ ni buɔ tso titri lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: How can I tell that my crop has completed its life cycle and it is time to stop watering or clear the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ ewala be lɛ naagbee? Ni ani be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa nu shwiemɔ loo jɛmɛ shwiemɔ?

english: When crops reach maturity, their leaves naturally turn yellow and dry up, and seed heads harden. This indicates that the plant has finished transferring nutrients to the crop and water intake has naturally stopped.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ mli lɛ naa ni nu ni ekɛwoɔ mli lɛ ekpa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I start my seeds in a nursery bed before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A nursery provides a controlled environment with shade and carefully managed water. This gives young seedlings an early, protected start so they grow strong and survive better when transplanted into the harsh open field.
ga: Nursery lɛ haa shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ ni hulutsoo kɛ nu ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii jeɔ shishi mra ni ebuɔ amɛhe. Enɛ ji koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ awo ŋmɔji ni mli wa waa amli.

english: Why do short-duration crops that mature in 16 weeks suit some farming seasons better than long-term crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ otsii 16 mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha okwaayeli bei komɛi fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Short-duration crops complete their lifecycle quickly within a single short rainy season. This allows farmers to harvest rapidly, secure food or income quickly, and avoid late-season droughts.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ gbeɔ amɛwala shihilɛ naa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku kome pɛ mli. Ye obua okwaafoi ni amɛkpa oya Niyenii loo shika he shweshweeshwefeemɔ oya ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ he.

english: How does planting crops with different growth periods help my farm income throughout the year?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛɔ ni amɛdalɛ fãi srɔtoi yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ mli shika ni mináa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Mixing quick-maturing crops with longer-term crops provides continuous harvests. You receive quick income from short-term crops while waiting for main long-term harvests to mature.
ga: Tsei ni daa oya kɛ tsei ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa nii daa. Onáa shika oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Can planting cover crops make my weeding work easier during the growing season?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha efee mlɛo akɛ makwɛ mijwɛi lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yes, cover crops carpet the ground with dense foliage, blocking sunlight from reaching weed seeds and reducing the amount of manual weeding you need to perform.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Ni ehaa jwɛi ni okɛ oniji tsuɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: What happens to the soil once a crop finishes its fruiting cycle and dries up?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii ko gbe eyibiiwoo be lɛ naa ni egbi?

english: Once a crop finishes producing seeds and dries, it stops pulling nutrients from the soil. Leaving crop residue on the field helps return organic material to the soil as it decomposes.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbe dumɔwui awomɔ naa ni egbi. Ebaakpa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my crop yields much lower this year compared to last year even though I planted the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu yɛ afi nɛɛ mli lɛ baa shi kwraa fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ midu dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Crops depend heavily on rainfall timing, soil nutrients, and temperature. Small changes in when the rainy season starts or declines in soil fertility can significantly lower your total harvest compared to previous years.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ nugbɔ bei anɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulutsoo lɛ waa Tsakemɔi bibii ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ baanyɛ aha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi waa kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I clear all the trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava around them to keep the air cool and retain soil moisture while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni ebɔle amɛhe. koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ

english: What causes the leaves on my maize plants to start turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is running out of nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves stay green and form healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni eha toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Excessive water fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. This waterlogged environment creates ideal conditions for root rot fungi to attack and destroy the tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni nu eyi mli obɔ nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni efite amɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing holes in the inner leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the tender leaf whorl at the center of young maize plants. Treating them early prevents them from destroying the growing point of the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Tsamɔ ni afeɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I harvest more crop from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani minyɛŋ makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows individual plants to grow stronger and produce larger, healthier yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso fɛɛ tso adara ni ewo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next crop rather than draining the soil nutrients year after year.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, drought, or sudden heavy rains cause stress to the plant, leading it to drop its flowers to save energy for basic survival instead of making fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie fɔfɔii amɛshwie shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha shishijee wala moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds naturally have wild, aggressive root systems that absorb water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to grow quickly and shade out your young crop seedlings.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei. Enɛ baaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Ha amɛdara oya ni amɛha otso bibii lɛ dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant the seeds from the maize harvest I bought at the local market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ dumɔwui?

english: Market maize often comes from hybrid varieties whose saved seeds lose their strong yield qualities in the next generation. Buying certified fresh seeds ensures uniform growth and better disease resistance.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ jɛɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa srɔtoi ni dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ amɛ yibiiwoo su ni mli wa lɛ mli yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha amɛdara be fɛɛ be ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long does a young cocoa tree take from planting until it starts giving me pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tsei bibii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, while older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years to yield their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree keep standing and producing fruit year after year without dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ damɔ shi ni ewoɔ yibii afi fɛɛ afi ni egbooo lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a perennial tree crop with a deep root system. Once established, it can live and produce pods for 30 to 40 years or more if protected from extreme drought, pests, and diseases.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ni yeɔ daa ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji abɔ amɛ pɛ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi ni amɛwo pods afii 30 kɛyashi 40 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Kɛji akɛ abu he kɛjɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ahe.

english: How do I know when my cocoa tree is too old and needs to be cut down for a new one?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni afo lɛ?

english: When a tree's trunk becomes hollow, or it produces fewer than 10 to 15 pods per year even with fertilizer and good rain, it has passed its peak age and should be rehabilitated or replanted.
ga: Beni tso lɛ shishi mli ewo muji loo ewoɔ ŋmeii ni shɛɛɛ 10 kɛyashi 15 daa afi yɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Tso lɛ eshɛ afii ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he. ni esa akɛ aku sɛɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ loo adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it good to grow food crops like cassava and plantain inside my young cocoa farm?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ makwɛ niyenii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plantain provides temporary shade and moisture for young cocoa seedlings, but heavy crops like cassava should not be planted too close because their broad root systems compete for soil nutrients and shade young cocoa too much.
ga: Plantains haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli kɛ fɛ̃i. Shi esaaa akɛ aduɔ tsei ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ, ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo babaoo tsɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off side shoots and extra branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifo kookoo tso lɛ sɛɛ tsei kɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called chupons, steal food and water from the main tree without producing many pods. Pruning them helps the tree direct its energy into pod growth and improves airflow to prevent disease.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo baaa. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ kɛyaa pod lɛ mli, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni helai akamɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their leaves when the dry Harmattan weather starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ baai babaoo fite beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ je shishi yɛ Harmattan lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is the tree's natural defense mechanism during severe dry periods to reduce water loss from evaporation and keep its trunk and root system alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli. Bɔni afee ni nu ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi ni abu tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees flower heavily at certain months instead of making flowers all year round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli moŋ fe afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees respond to rainfall patterns. The onset of rains triggers flowering, while dry spells cause the tree to conserve energy and hold back on producing new flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ tsuɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he nii. Nugbɔ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ fɔfɔi, yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ haa tsei lɛ toɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ ni ehaaa amɛfee fɔfɔi heei.

english: Why are the pods on my tree turning black and soft before they get fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifee blɛoo dani amɛshwere kwraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, overly shaded farms. Clearing weeds and pruning thick tree branches allows sunlight in to stop the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei niji ni mli ewo wu lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la tsiɔ ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekabote mli.

english: How do I know if my farm soil needs fertilizer to help the cocoa trees make more pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni eye ebua cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: If cocoa leaves look pale or yellow during the growing season, or if healthy trees drop young pods before they grow big, the soil is low on essential nutrients like potassium and phosphorus.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ Aloo kɛji tso ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii dani amɛdaraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Can I eat any part of the cocoa pod for food, or is the crop only good for dried beans?
ga: Ani manyɛ maye kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fã ko akɛ niyenii? Aloo ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sa kɛha ŋmeii ni egbi pɛ?

english: While cocoa beans are sold for income, the sweet, white mucilage pulp surrounding fresh cocoa beans inside the pod is safe and delicious to eat as a sweet fruit snack while harvesting.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ kookoo ŋmeii koni akɛná shika moŋ, shi muji yɛŋ ni ŋɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Kookoo ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ pod lɛ mli lɛ hu yɛ shweshweeshwe ni ŋɔɔ ni ayeɔ akɛ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ ni akɛyeɔ nii yɛ be mli ni akpaa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like small babies that cannot handle harsh sun and dry winds. If they do not have shade trees or plantains nearby to block the sun, the dry air pulls all the moisture out of their leaves until they dry up and die.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ abifabii bibii. ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ naa Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulu la lɛ bɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi hulu la naa Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my corn plants rolling up like tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves roll up like a straw when the plant is thirsty to protect itself from losing water in the sun. Once the sun goes down or the plant receives rain, the leaves will unfold and lay flat again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ jwɛi kɛ́ kumai miiye tso lɛ koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni hulu lɛ shwieɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi loo tsei lɛ ná nugbɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and curling upward like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids hiding on the underside of the leaf. As these pests suck the sap out of the leaf, they damage it and cause it to grow twisted and wrinkled.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Amɛfiteɔ nii ni amɛhaa efoɔ ni efoɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting and turning dark just two days after I dig them up from the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi fitemɔ ni amɛfee duŋ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are like fresh wounds once pulled from the ground; they react quickly with the oxygen in the air as they try to heal. This natural chemical reaction causes the tuber to decay rapidly unless it is cooked, processed into gari, or kept submerged in water.
ga: Cassava shishifãi tamɔ pilamɔi heei ni ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ. Amɛtsuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ he nii oya beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsa lɛ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofafeemɔ nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya. ja ahoo Afee lɛ Gari loo akɛwo nu mli

english: Why do people tell me that planting cowpeas or groundnuts will make my soil better for next season's corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko miikɛɛ mi akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni midu lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground like natural fertilizer. When you harvest the legumes, that free plant food stays in the soil to feed the corn you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Beni okpaa ŋmãa lɛ Nakai tso niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I cut away the extra young shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi tsɔne titri lɛ eje kpo.

english: If you leave too many young shoots around one plantain stem, they behave like too many children sharing a small bowl of food. Removing most shoots and leaving only one or two leaves all the water and nutrients for the main tree so it can produce a large bunch.
ga: Kɛji oshi tsei bibii ni ebɔle ohe lɛ Tso kome fa tsɔ. Ebaafee enii tamɔ gbekɛbii babaoo ni miija niyenii yɛ tsɛnsi bibioo ko mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, eshiɔ nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni haa tso titri lɛ feɔ ŋmeii agbo.

english: Why are the yellow flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant feels stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. If the plant feels it doesn't have enough balanced food or water, it drops the flowers to save its own life.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ ebɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, Ebaashɛ fɔfɔi ashwie shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do I need to clear tall sticks for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves work like solar panels that need direct light to manufacture food for the big tuber growing underground. Lifting the vines up on stakes keeps the leaves away from the hot soil, reduces leaf rot, and allows them to catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Ebaai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei, ni ehe hiaa kane tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha tsɔnei wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baa lɛ mli fitemɔ he okadii lɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni enáa hulu la babaoo

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and pale green even when rain is falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm because their roots grow very fast and drink the water and soil food before your crops can reach it. Even with rain, your crops stay hungry and turn pale green because the weeds are stealing all the nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Akɛni amɛshishifãi lɛ daa oya hewɔ lɛ, amɛnuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ lolo ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ miiju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is there fine dirt that looks like sawdust inside the funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: That sawdust-like dirt is actually the waste left behind by caterpillars like the fall armyworm. The worm hides inside the center of the corn plant where it chews soft young leaves before they open up.
ga: Muji ni tamɔ ŋmei lɛ ji muji ni ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ shiɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Kpɔŋɔ lɛ kɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Ekɛ baai bibii shwieɔ shi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How do I know if new crop seeds brought into the country are safe to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui heei ni akɛba mimaŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Before new crop varieties are released to farmers, agricultural experts and regulatory authorities test them thoroughly to ensure they are safe for human consumption, safe for the soil, and suitable for local growing conditions.
ga: dani amɛjie tsei srɔtoi heei kpo amɛtsɔɔ okwaafoi Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nilelɔi kɛ nitsumɔhei ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kaa tsei srɔtoi nɛɛ amɛkwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛhe yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesai niyenii. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha shikpɔŋ ni ehi kɛha shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key plant food, or that the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to take up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aná niyenii kpakpai.

english: What is causing small holes in my corn leaves and dark waste inside the center stalk?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni nɔ ko diŋŋ ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows inside the growing tip of the corn plant and eats the leaves before they unfold.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Tubers rot underground mainly when the soil holds too much water without proper drainage, allowing fungal organisms in the soil to attack the root tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested hybrid corn to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Saving and replanting hybrid seeds will give you a much smaller yield because the high-yielding traits are only strong in the first generation and decline in the next.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui heei ni okɛtoɔ ni oduɔ lɛ baaha oná yibiiwoo bibioo kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, su ni haa yibii babaoo baa lɛ mli wa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ, ni ebaa shi yɛ yinɔi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: How does planting cowpeas between my maize rows help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants cover the soil to block weeds and naturally capture nitrogen from the air, which enriches the soil for the maize plants.
ga: Cowpea tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akaje mli ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jara wa kɛha ŋmãa tsei.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a light rain, and bury it a few inches into the soil near the plant stem so heavy rain won't sweep it off the field.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. ni ofu sũ lɛ 2-3 inch kɛbɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa akajie lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up tight during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense mechanism to trap moisture and reduce water loss through evaporation when the sun is very intense.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekɛba nu ni laajeɔ lɛ shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ kɛ́ hulu la lɛ tsoɔ waa.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients needed to set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha yibiiwoo ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving every individual plant weak and underdeveloped.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdarako jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yams need big soil mounds to grow big and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ato sweet potatoes lɛ he ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni efee agbo ni elɛɛmɔ waa lɛ?

english: Loose, raised soil mounds allow yam tubers to expand easily underground without hitting hard soil, while protecting the roots from drowning during heavy rains.
ga: Gɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewó nɔ lɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni enaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkabote nu mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I leave space between my maize plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to weak stalks and small, empty corn ears.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Cassava drops its leaves in dry weather to save water. The plant rests while keeping its root tubers alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli koni nu akafite. Tsei yaa wɔɔhe kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ni amɛhaa amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Hot sun makes leaves lose water faster than roots can pull it up from the soil. The plant wilts to protect itself from burning, but recovers when temperatures cool down.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei gboɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ la he. Shi ebaahi shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba shi.

english: Why are there small ragged holes in my young maize leaves that appear overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani no je kpo nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the green funnel of the maize stem during the day and feed on the leaves at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli, ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Heavy rains and high dampness spread a fungal disease called Black Pod, which quickly damages pods if trees do not get enough sunlight and airflow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods baa. Enɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ oya kɛji tso lɛ naaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant nutrient responsible for leaf growth and healthy green coloring.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso mli niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa kɛ eŋɔli su ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my farm make the next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, leaving behind natural fertilizer for the crops you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms dropping off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when the daytime heat is too high or when there are no small insects around to shake and pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ aduawai ni aduawai bɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii komɛi bɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe ni baakpokpo ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines grow plenty of leaves but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi bulbs bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant spend all its energy growing leafy vines above ground instead of sending food down to grow thick tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baaha tso lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛkwɛ wain tsei ni baai yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekwɛ̃ bulbs ni mli tse

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before any pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by prolonged dry spells, lack of soil nutrients, or poor insect pollination. Providing adequate shade and organic mulch helps the trees retain flowers and form pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni ehiii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli haa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni efeɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning brown at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies, or by water stress. Using protective neem sprays or insect barriers helps keep leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ nu mli haomɔ mli Neem spray loo kooloi ahe nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests of maize each year when I keep planting on the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi be mli ni miduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts vital nitrogen back into the earth naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rainy season gets very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles in the soil for too long without draining away, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps surplus rainwater drain so roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate stems and leaves that easily burn under full sun. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside them creates a protective umbrella until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni adu yɛ he kome lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he aba kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily right when the fruit bunch starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that struggle to support the heavy weight of full bunches during strong winds. Supporting the stems with sturdy bamboo or wooden stakes prevents the plants from snaping or falling.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfi jwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ muji ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni mli wa fĩ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo ekagbee shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce almost no fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai babaoo shi aduawai ko kwraa bɛ?

english: When plants get too much nitrogen but not enough phosphorus and potassium, they put all their energy into leaf growth instead of flowering. Using a balanced fertilizer encourages the plant to set plenty of fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen babaoo shi amɛnáaa phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my yam vines need to be lifted up on tall wooden stakes instead of growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akwɛɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows the leaves to capture maximum sunlight to feed the tuber underground, while keeping the leaves away from damp soil where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout even after I plant them right after the first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ po lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often a 'false rain' followed by intense heat that dries out the topsoil before seeds can root. Waiting until the rains become steady and consistent ensures the soil stays moist enough for seeds to germinate.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji ‘nugbɔ amale’, ni latsaa ni naa wa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ gĩɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa, ni ebaa daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my farmland is good enough for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Maize grows best in dark, soft soil that drains water easily after heavy rainfall. If water sits on top of your soil like a pond for days, maize roots will rot and the plants will not grow well.
ga: Abɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ tamɔ ŋshɔ mli gbii babaoo. Abɛi shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni tso lɛ edaŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing on cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried by tiny white flies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings is the best way to keep your plants healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Cassava Mosaic Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Yucca tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When maize plants are too close, they fight each other for food, water, and sunlight, leading to thin stems and small cobs. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food to produce big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa bibii. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: What makes my tomato leaves turn pale yellow even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu daa gbi po?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are missing important soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is holding too much water around the roots. Adding composted manure or fertilizer can give them the strength to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ sũ lɛ miihiɛ nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know it is the right time to sow my seeds when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Wait until the rains become steady and the ground stays moist for several days. Planting after just one light rain is risky because the soil can dry out quickly and destroy the germinating seeds before the next rainfall.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii babaoo. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni efiteɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why does allowing weeds to grow on my pepper farm reduce the amount of pepper I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ miha jwɛi shwere yɛ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa pepper ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight directly from your pepper plants. They also host harmful insects and plant sicknesses that can destroy your pepper flowers before they turn into fruits.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ o-pepper tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛji ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baanyɛ afite o-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai hu jɛɛhe.

english: Can I save some of the maize grains from my current harvest to plant next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You can, but saved seeds often produce weaker plants and smaller cobs in the next season. Buying certified seeds from a recognized agro-dealer gives you stronger plants that yield more food and resist diseases better.
ga: Obaanyɛ, shi dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fɔɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ awoɔ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko ni ale lɛ dɛŋ lɛ baaye abua bo ni oná tsei ni he wa. Ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly when the farm is too wet, damp, and dark. Clearing weeds and trimming overgrown tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry the farm and stop the disease.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ ŋmɔji amli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ehaa helai kpaa.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or beans on land where I harvested maize last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but beans and cowpeas put natural plant food called nitrogen back into the dirt. Planting beans refreshes the soil so future crops can grow strong without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ adara waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and curling up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees, heat burns their leaves and dries out the moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ, Dɔlɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai lɛ ni egbiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves stay green so the plant can photosynthesize and produce large ears.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ tsei nyɛɔ amɛfeɔ fotosintɛsis ni amɛfeɔ toi wuji.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting beans or cowpeas in the same field where I planted maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that gather nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. Planting them after heavy feeders like maize naturally restores soil fertility.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa du nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up wooden stakes instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines that need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food. Staking keeps leaves exposed to light and off damp soil, preventing leaf rot and encouraging large tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni shwereɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee amɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji lɛ daraa.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small suckers growing around my main plantain tree to stay?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ji nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Too many suckers steal water and soil nutrients from the main stem, resulting in small fruit bunches. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree produces a heavy, healthy harvest.
ga: Suckers babaoo tsɔ juɔ nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai bibii bibii. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ yibii ni tsii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too close together to try and fit more in my field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ koni mibɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This results in thin, weak plants that produce lower overall yields and catch diseases easily.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni no haa yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ lɛ baa shi, ni helai baa amɛnɔ oya.

english: How does cassava manage to stay alive and keep growing even when there is no rain for months?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei ahi shi ni ekwɛ̃ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko nyɔji babaoo moŋ?

english: Cassava drops its top leaves during dry spells to conserve water, while relying on its deep root system and underground food stores to stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu akafite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii ni amɛnáa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when heat gets too high or when water supply is uneven. Extreme heat dries out the flower's pollen, preventing it from forming a tomato.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be babaoo ba amɛnɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Etsiɔ tomatoi lɛ afeemɔ naa.

english: Why do I see ragged holes in my young maize leaves early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa pores yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by nocturnal pests like fall armyworms that feed on crop leaves at night or early morning while hiding inside the plant funnel during hot daytime hours.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbɛkɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ cutworms, ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa be mli ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei akutsei amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often a response to tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on leaf undersides, or a sign of a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ ji hetoo kɛha kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ thrips loo mites, ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ. Aloo eji hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi?

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow before the crop is even ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po afee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key food in the soil. It can also happen when the soil is too dry or completely flooded with water, preventing the roots from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia otso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ ni no hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: When rain stays trapped in heavy soil, the roots cannot breathe because there is no air left in the wet dirt. This causes soft fungal rots to grow and spoil the tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ko eshwɛɛɛ yɛ sũ ni efɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers without forming any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers if they lack water during the dry season, if the soil lacks proper plant food, or if pests like mirids damage the blossoms before pods can form.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji nu bɛ amɛmli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe niyenii ni sa loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ.

english: Will my crops produce a bigger yield if I pack many seeds very close together in the ground?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibii babaoo kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them out gives each crop enough room and energy to grow bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my soil produce fewer crops when I plant maize on the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and lets pests build up in the dirt. Switching crops, like planting beans after maize, restores nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni amɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ kɛ no sɛɛ lɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomatoes develop black, rotten spots at the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔi diji ni egboi yɔɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This problem, called blossom-end rot, is caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often made worse when soil goes back and forth between being too dry and too wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii kwraa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ yaa kɛbaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ tsɔ teŋ.

english: Does removing extra stems and leaves from my pepper plants help them grow bigger peppers?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mijie ŋmeii kɛ baai ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Yes, trimming weak or unnecessary branches helps the plant send its strength and food directly into growing larger, healthier peppers instead of wasting energy on useless leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ yaa ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why should I avoid applying fertilizer when heavy rain is falling on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni nugbɔ miinɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainwater will wash the fertilizer off the soil surface before the roots can swallow it, wasting your money and leaking the chemicals into nearby streams.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmiɔ. Eji shika ni afiteɔ kɛ tsofai ni hoɔ kɛyaa faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the soil around young plants with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ baai kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from the hot sun so water stays in the ground longer, while also stopping weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ akaye nɔ.

english: How do improved seed varieties from agricultural officers differ from the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli nitsulɔi adɛŋ lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ he?
