english: Improved seeds are specially selected and bred to resist common local crop diseases, survive drought better, and give you a higher yield than seeds saved from older crops.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akwɛɔ amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei momo amli lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up tightly into tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize leaves curl up, the plant is trying to protect itself from losing water to the hot sun. The rolled leaves trap moisture inside and reduce the leaf surface exposed to heat, which is a natural signal that your crop is under heat and water stress.
ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baafite amɛ lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Baai ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli ni ehaa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulutsoo baa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ shishi.

english: What crops can I plant that will not easily dry up and fail if the rains stop early?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ ni amɛgbiŋ oya ni amɛfite kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra?

english: Crops like cassava, cowpea, millet, and sorghum are very tough because they either have deep roots that search for underground water or leaves that store moisture, making them reliable crops during low rainfall seasons.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ cassava, cowpea, millet kɛ sorghum lɛ wa waa ejaakɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni taoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu loo baai ni toɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ tso ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the trees during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, dark environments. Heavy rains paired with thick shade from overhead trees trap moisture on the pods, allowing the fungus to spread quickly.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ duŋ yɔɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa ni jɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their blossoms before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani ewoɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by excessive heat, dry soil, or sudden weather changes. The plant drops its flowers to save energy so the main body of the plant can survive the harsh condition.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni fe nine, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ fã titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: This is often caused by root rot or bacterial wilt. When soil stays flooded or damp without good air flow, roots rot away and can no longer drink water or oxygen, causing the top of the plant to wither and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo muawai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ kɛbaa. Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛnu nu loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yiteŋ gbɔjɔɔ ni egboɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Nitrogen is the nutrient that gives leaves their deep green color and helps plants grow big and healthy, so the plant pulls remaining nitrogen from older leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ yɛ baai momoi amli lɛ koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my yam vines grow huge leafy stems but give me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji shi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen, the plant spends all its strength growing leafy vines above ground instead of storing starch and expanding the tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ No lɛ tso lɛ baaye ebe fɛɛ ni ekɛkwɛ wain tso ko nɔ ni ebaai lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e kɛ starch toɔ nɛ e haa nɛ tsɔwi ɔmɛ ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do so many pests start attacking my cowpea field as soon as the flowers appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi babaoo jeɔ shishi amɛtutuaa mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ je kpo pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and soft tissue that act like a magnet for insect pests like thrips and pod borers, which feed on the flowers to reproduce.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ nu mli nu kɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ magnɛt, ni egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers. ni yeɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛfɔ bii

english: Will planting groundnuts alongside my main cassava crop ruin the soil or help it?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua lɛ?

english: Planting groundnuts with cassava actually helps the soil. Groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground, which fertilizes the soil and feeds the cassava plant as it grows.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehaa ŋmei tsei lɛ niyenii be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How do I know beneath the ground that my cassava is fully grown and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava shows it is ready when the lowest leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open as the tubers expand underneath.
ga: Yuccas tsɔɔ akɛ amɛfee klalo beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and scorching during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates a protective canopy that reduces heat and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa hulutsoo baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning light yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Applying a balanced nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's life restores the green color and strengthens leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ni ja wo tso lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha tso lɛ baai lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: How does growing groundnuts or beans alongside my main crops improve my soil?
ga: Te ŋmei loo ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they enrich the soil with free nutrients for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What is eating tiny holes in the middle leaves of my maize plants and leaving brown powder inside?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu bibioo ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ni eshiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding deep inside the plant's funnel. Checking your farm early and using targeted organic extracts or approved control spray protects the leaves before major losses occur.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tsei lɛ atsɔnei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akwɛɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu tso lɛ yibii ahe dani nibii wuji ni baafite lɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds slow down my crops even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that aggressively steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all available nutrients go directly into growing your main plants.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ yaa onibii titri lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do I need to make big mounds of soil before planting yam seeds in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ agbo ko dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand easily underground. Large mounds break up hard soil, improve water drainage, and give the tubers room to grow long and wide.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi oya. Gɔji wuji gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa yitso he lɛ yaa hiɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa

english: Why did my cassava crop grow very tall stems but produce very small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ waa shi shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: Excessive leaf and stem growth happens when there is too much nitrogen relative to other soil nutrients, or when weak stem cuttings are used. Mature stem cuttings and balanced soil encourage the plant to send energy into growing underground tubers.
ga: Baai kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ fe nine lɛ baa kɛji akɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ mli niyenii krokomɛi ahe. aloo kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ mli tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ miitsu nii Tso lɛ mli tsei ni eda kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ yaa tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know that the rainy season is stable enough for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ yɛ shiŋŋ lolo bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ oje dumɔwui adumɔ shishi?

english: It is best to wait for two or three heavy, soaking rains that penetrate deep into the ground. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then wither if dry heat returns.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji latsaa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: When is the right time to put top-dressing fertilizer on my maize farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Top-dressing fertilizer is best applied about 4 to 6 weeks after planting, when the maize is knee-high. This provides a fresh nutrient boost right when the crop enters its fastest growing phase.
ga: Esa akɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋtayaa lɛ mli ŋtayaa yɛ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, beni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ tsitsi nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii heei fataa he kɛji tso lɛ bote eshishijee dalɛ mli pɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. Keeping moisture consistent around the roots and providing light shade during hot afternoons keeps the flowers healthy so fruit can set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa hulutsoo yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ mli waa bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ anyɛ atswa.

english: Young cocoa trees are tender and can easily burn under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean they lack nitrogen, which is essential plant food, or the soil has too much water. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps them regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ amɛmli. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛná amɛ su ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Holes in maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the crop's central funnel during the day and feed at night. Checking your farm early and using approved sprays or targeted ash/sand in the funnel can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni teɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli ni amɛyeɔ nii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo sũ/ŋã ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ cone lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and getting pale spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and pale spots on cassava are signs of Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies and infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers prevents this problem.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛhaa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds after the first rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adũ dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil may dry out again. Wait until the rain soaks deep into the soil—about the depth of your hand—and rains become consistent before planting.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ekoŋŋ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ—aaafee onine mlibotemɔ—ni nugbɔ lɛ anɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani odu.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa baadu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, acting as a natural food source for maize. Planting them together improves soil health and gives you two different crops from the same piece of land.
ga: Peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmãa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why are my harvested yams rotting so quickly in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto lɛ?

english: Yams rot fast if they were bruised during digging, exposed to direct hot sun, or kept in damp conditions. Storing uninjured yams on raised bamboo racks in a well-ventilated, shaded barn keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni pilaaa lɛ to ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmeii atoohe ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather gets too hot, when watering is irregular, or if the plant lacks nutrients. Watering regularly at the roots and mulching the soil keeps ground cool and helps fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ bɛ be fɛɛ be loo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ woɔ yibii.

english: Why does my piece of land yield less food every year even when I plant the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni midu yɛ nakai gbɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same plot every year drains specific soil nutrients without giving the earth time to recover. Rotating different crop types and letting the land rest restores its fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe koni ená ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive tough conditions, so they absorb water and soil food much quicker than domesticated crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing the nutrients your crops need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why should I change the crop I plant on my land every year instead of just planting maize every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu ŋmãa daa be lɛ

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests that love that crop to build up in your farm. Rotating maize with crops like cowpea puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be ni Seasons lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cowpeas tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients and leaves the ground weak. Groundnuts and other leguminous plants have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, making it fertile again for your next crop.
ga: Abele yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Peanuts kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ehaa ewoɔ yibii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I put fresh chicken manure directly around my young pepper plants?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee awo he fɛɛ he. Ani abaanyɛ adu mi-pepper tsei bibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, fresh chicken manure is very strong and produces heat that will burn young roots and kill your plants. You must dry or compost the chicken manure for a few weeks until it cools down before mixing it into the soil.
ga: Dabi, tsina fɔmɔ nii heei lɛ mli wa waa ni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni baashã shishifãi bibii ni baagbe otsei lɛ baa. Ebaabi ni okɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ agbi loo okɛwo mli otsii fioo komɛi kɛyashi ebaajɔ dani okɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally during dry spells to save water and withstand the heat. The plant is not dying; it is focusing its energy underground to keep the tuber roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni enyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ naa. Tso lɛ gbooo, ekɛ ehewalɛ miitsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni eha tuber shishifãi lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of big green leaves but very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or fresh manure, which tells the plant to grow green branches instead of flowers. Balancing the soil food encourages the plant to set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii heei babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ kɛɛ tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ niji eŋɔli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers before any peppers can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the air gets too hot or the plants don't get enough water. Extreme heat damages the flower pollen, so the plant sheds the blossom to save its energy.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start planting maize when the main rainy season begins?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ boteɔ mli lɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath may still be dry. Wait until you get two or three steady rains that wet the ground deep enough so your seeds won't dry up after sprouting.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa bɔ ni sa. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize get mouldy in the sack even after I dried it under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli beni migbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli po lɛ?

english: The outer surface of the maize kernel might feel dry, but moisture can still be trapped deep inside the seed. If you bag it too quickly, that hidden moisture comes out inside the sealed sack and creates mould.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmãa lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanu he akɛ egbi. Shi ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛwo mli oya tsɔ lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ joɔ foi kɛyaa kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How can I tell when my sweet potatoes are mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Watch the leaves—when the main vines start turning yellow and dry, dig out one potato and cut it open. If the juice inside dries quickly without turning dark, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ—beni wain tso titri lɛ jeɔ shishi etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ kome ni ofo mli. Kɛji nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ gĩ oya ni etsɔɔɔ duŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ eshɛ nikpamɔ.

english: What does it mean when my plantain leaves turn brown around the edges and curl up?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ mi plantain baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔle amɛhe ni amɛbɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Brown, curling leaves are a sign that the plantain tree is suffering from lack of water or strong heat. Putting dry grass or leaves around the stem base as mulch keeps the soil cool and retains water.
ga: Baai ni ekpɛtɛ, ni ji asasu ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu efo dumɔwui lɛ amli loo edɔ fe nine. Mulch kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I grow pepper on the exact same piece of farmland every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting pepper continuously in the same soil wears out specific nutrients and allows pests and diseases like bacterial wilt to build up in the ground, causing poorer yields every season.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaafite niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ helai tamɔ bacteria wilt buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi daa be.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to plant quick crops like vegetables before major farm projects start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii mra tamɔ aduawai dani okwaayeli nitsumɔi wuji aje shishi lɛ?

english: Quick-growing vegetables cover the soil to prevent weed buildup, provide fast income, and prepare the land's health before longer-term crops are established.
ga: Akɛ muji woɔ aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ anɔ koni jwɛi akabua amɛhe naa. Ha shika oya ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ dani odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why are my vegetables rejected for export even when they look healthy to me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpoo mi-vegetables lɛ koni akɛya maŋsɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni amɛhi kɛha mi moŋ?

english: International buyers test crops for invisible chemical residues and tiny pest damages. Even if produce looks fine on the outside, failing safety tests causes export rejections and country bans.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ jarayelɔi kaa dumɔwui amɛkwɛɔ kɛji tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni anaaa lɛ eshwɛ kɛ kooloi bibii ni efite. Eyɛ mli akɛ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kponɔgbɛ moŋ Shi shweshweeshwefeemɔ he kaai ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli lɛ eha akpoo nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ ni agu amɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli.

english: How long do I need to wait after spraying my pepper before harvesting it to sell?
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani abaanyɛ akpa ni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Every crop chemical has a mandatory waiting period listed on the bottle—usually 3 to 14 days—allowing chemicals to break down safely so the produce is safe for buyers to eat.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ yɛ be ni akɛbaamɛ ni aŋmala awo tɔ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ gbii 3 kɛyashi 14 dani tsofai lɛ fiteɔ shweshweeshwe bɔni afee ni mɔ ni heɔ lɛ lɛ aye nɔ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that carry plant viruses. Spraying neem oil or recommended organic treatments early controls these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni hiɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Akɛ Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ haa mra. Abaanyɛ akudɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ.

english: Extreme heat and erratic watering stress pepper plants, causing flowers to fall off prematurely. Keeping soil moist and providing light shade during hot dry spells helps fruit set.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Ehaa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he.

english: Why does my pepper plant have plenty of green leaves but very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pepper fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants put all energy into leaf growth instead of flowers. Switching to fertilizers richer in phosphorus and potassium encourages fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Kɛji akɛ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ baa shi.

english: Can I intercrop pepper with other vegetables like garden eggs on the same land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ aduawai krokomɛi, tamɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii atsu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, but you must space them far enough apart so they do not fight for sunlight and airflow, which can create humid conditions that trap fungal diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ oshi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ akabote mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ ni mɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba.

english: When is the best time of year to plant pepper to get the best market price in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmɔtɔ koni ana jara ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana?

english: Planting pepper toward the end of the major rains allows harvest during the dry season, when supply drops across the country and market prices rise.
ga: Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ maŋtsɛ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ anaagbee lɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ ji be ni nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ baa shi yɛ maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ, ni jarayeli jara hu yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my harvested peppers rot so quickly before I get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting peppers in the hot afternoon heat causes them to lose water and decay faster. Harvesting early in the morning and keeping produce cool preserves freshness longer.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ chili shwie shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ afite ni ebaafite oya. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ leebi ni oha onibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant too many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, leaving all of them weak, small, and low-yielding.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do we make big earth mounds before planting yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmaa gɔji wuji dani wɔduɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil to expand easily into large roots. Mounds provide soft soil for the tubers to grow and prevent standing water from rotting the crop.
ga: Sweet potato tubers he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse koni shishifãi wuji akwɛ̃ oya. Gɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa, ni ehaa nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why should I clear weeds from my farm while my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the nutrients, water, and light meant for your farm, which can stunt crop growth permanently if left unchecked early on.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ la kɛhaa oŋmɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei adalɛ naa kɛya naanɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ mra.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen in the soil, or that too much water around the roots is stopping them from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo nu yɛ he fɛɛ he Shishifãi babaoo nyɛɛɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer when the ground is moist instead of when it is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe be mli ni egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the crop roots can drink it in. Applying fertilizer on dry ground can burn the plant roots and waste the fertilizer into the air.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil, which causes the plant to protect itself by shedding flowers it cannot support with water.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ nu lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Curled and yellowing cassava leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies.
ga: Kasava baai ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes inside the centers of my young maize plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu ko ni etse ehe yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Holes in the center funnel of maize plants are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the tender new leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Why should I cut off the thin shoots growing straight up from the lower trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Those shoots, called water suckers, drink up the tree's water and food without producing cocoa pods, taking energy away from the pod-bearing branches.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu. Enuɔ tso lɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni ekɛfeee kookoo ŋmɔtɔ. ni ejieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei niji lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil is low on nitrogen, an essential food for crops. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn deep green and support strong crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ ni eha tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield less food when I plant maize on the same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the exact same spot every season continuously drains the same soil nutrients and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like beans or groundnuts naturally recharges the soil with nitrogen.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. Taakɛ eji lɛ, ekɛ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from intense, direct sunlight, which scorches their soft leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving large shade trees or planting plantains beside young cocoa creates a cooler, shaded environment that keeps the soil moist and protects the seedlings.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Enɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ ashã ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Cocoa tsei haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa shihilɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Yam plants make food through their leaves using sunlight to grow tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot, damp ground into full sunlight, which increases tuber size and prevents leaf rot diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ, ni amɛkɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyashi amɛbaaná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tuber lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Which direction should the buds face when I insert cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Beni okɛ ŋmei niji woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ okwɛ?

english: The small growth buds or nodes on the cassava stem should always point upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the shoots spend too much energy turning around, resulting in weak stems and poor tuber growth.
ga: ŋmeii bibii loo nodes Esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifã lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋwɛigbɛ Shoots lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo baatsu nii ni ekɛtsake. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni ŋmeii lɛ hu edaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait a few days after the very first rain of the season before planting my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ gbii fioo komɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani madu aduawai dumɔwui?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by intense sun that heats up the dry ground, which can bake and destroy newly planted seeds. Waiting for continuous, reliable rainfall ensures the soil stays consistently moist for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa ni haa hei ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ mɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain bunches grow small when I leave all the young shoots growing around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii waa beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too many young shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients. Pruning away excess suckers leaves the main tree with enough strength and nutrients to grow large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tsobii bibii loo tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tsei agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds on my farm cause my cassava roots to remain small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your cassava plants. Clearing weeds early ensures the cassava gets all the soil food it needs to swell into thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni etsɔ yitso ni mli wa ni mli wa

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience severe heat stress or irregular watering. Providing consistent soil moisture and mulching around the roots helps the plants keep their flowers so they can form healthy pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni awo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni aná pepper hetooi ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rotten before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Black, sunken spots at the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which occurs when roots cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, usually due to dry soil conditions. Watering tomatoes consistently keeps the calcium flowing evenly into the developing fruits.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi shihilɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha calcium lɛ aya aduawai lɛ amli be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do I have to buy new seeds from the store every season instead of just using seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ shwapo lɛ mli daa afi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ pɛ baatsu nii

english: Improved or hybrid seeds are specially bred to give high yields only in their first planting. If you harvest and replant those saved seeds, the natural science of the plant causes the second generation to lose its strength, leading to much smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ loo dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛji okpa nakai dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ni odu ekoŋŋ lɛ Adebɔɔ mli nilee ni kɔɔ tsei ahe lɛ baaha tsei ayinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ ahewalɛ aba shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why do my crops seem to produce smaller harvests every year when I keep replanting seeds from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miyaa nɔ miduɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds naturally deteriorate over generations because they mix traits with weaker plants nearby and pick up seed-borne diseases over time, causing their overall quality and yield to drop.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ yɛ yinɔi amli beni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ oya lɛ futuɔ amɛhe ni amɛbuaa helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ anaa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni hi kɛ nɔ ni anáa lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Is it compulsory to buy fresh certified seeds every year, or can I treat my saved seeds to make them yield just as well?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi? Aloo manyɛ makwɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ anɔ koni ewo yibii ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ?

english: Treating saved seeds with chemicals can protect them from insects in the soil, but it cannot restore the natural high-yielding power that is lost after the first harvest. Fresh certified seeds are needed for maximum yields.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai tsu dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahe nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Shi enyɛŋ ekɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni haa yibii babaoo ni elaaje yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli he miihia koni aná yibii babaoo.

english: How come the maize I plant from my saved harvest grows into plants of different heights and sizes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni midu kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ mli lɛ da ni etsɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ amɛdalɛi srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds lose their uniform traits after the first harvest. When you replant saved grains, the natural science of genetic breakdown causes some plants to grow tall, others short, and the cob sizes to become irregular.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ amɛsu kome lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Beni oduɔ dumɔwui heei ni ato lɛ Adebɔɔ mli nilee ni kɔɔ fɔmɔ nii ni fiteɔ lɛ he lɛ baaha tsei komɛi afee shɔŋŋ. Tsei komɛi yɛ kuku. ni cob lɛ dalɛ jeee nɔ ni sa

english: Why do seeds I dry and keep in my room lose their ability to sprout after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni migbiɔ ni mikɛtoɔ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds are living things that breathe. High heat and humidity in standard storage cause seeds to consume their stored energy quickly or attract invisible mold, which weakens or kills the tiny embryo inside.
ga: Dumɔwu ji nɔ ko ni hiɛ kã, ni muɔ. Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii oya loo egbalaa ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ. Enɛ baaha fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ afee bibioo. ni yɔɔ mli lɛ gboɔ loo egbɔjɔɔ

english: Why do my cassava plants give me smaller tubers when I keep using stem cuttings from old fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni miyaa nɔ mikɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Stem cuttings naturally collect invisible plant viruses and diseases over continuous seasons. Planting cuttings from very old fields transfers these sicknesses to the new crop, reducing tuber size.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni afo lɛ buaa helai ni anaaa kɛ tsei ahe helai anaa yɛ be ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ baaha helai nɛɛ aya ŋmɔshi nibii heei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso lɛ dalɛ ni baa shi.

english: What makes fresh store-bought seeds sprout faster and more evenly than the seeds I select by hand on my farm?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ daa fe dumɔwui ni mikɛ minine shwieɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought certified seeds undergo strict quality checks where only fully mature, disease-free, and strong seeds are selected and treated under controlled conditions to ensure uniform germination.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ shwapoi amli lɛ kwɛɔ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Amɛhalaa ni amɛtsaa dumɔwui ni eda, ni hela bɛ mli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni akudɔɔ mli koni amɛkwɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my crops start flowering early when the rainfall stops for just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi oya nɛkɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: When crops experience drought stress, their natural survival instinct forces them to produce flowers early to leave behind seeds before the plant dies, even if the plant is still too small.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ kpe Adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo nyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi mra. ni eshiɔ dumɔwui yɛ esɛɛ dani tso lɛ gboɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ ji bibioo tsɔ lolo po.

english: How can I test if the seeds I saved from last season are still alive and good for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni esa akɛ adu?

english: You can wrap 10 of your saved seeds in a damp cloth for a few days; if fewer than 8 sprout healthy roots, the seed batch has lost its natural strength and you should buy fresh seeds.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mama ni mli efɔ awo dumɔwui 10 ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ mli. kɛha gbii fioo komɛi Kɛji shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa fe 8 lɛ daraa lɛ, dumɔwui akuu lɛ hewalɛ baaje edɛŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui heei.

english: Why do modern seed varieties cost so much money compared to our traditional local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui lɛ jara wa waa kɛ akɛto wɔ maŋbii akusum dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Modern seeds require years of scientific research, field testing, and specialized breeding to make them resistant to diseases and droughts, which makes them cost more but offers much higher harvests.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui biɔ jeŋ nilee mli niiamlitaomɔ afii babaoo. Gbɛjianɔtoo mli kaa kɛ fɔmɔ pɔtɛɛ koni helai kɛ hɔmɔ anyɛ ashi. Enɛ haa amɛjara wa waa shi amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. Without shade trees or plantain plants to shield them, intense sun scorches their tender leaves, causing them to dry up and turn yellow to survive.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baaha amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why is my maize crop turning light green and yellow when the stalks are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ yɛ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for green growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen away, so adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back the dark green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei yeɔ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays in heavy soil without draining away. Excess water suffocates the roots and allows soil fungi to invade, causing tubers to rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ mli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa sũ mli ŋmeii boteɔ mli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baagboi.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants drop off without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. When the plant feels stressed, it drops blossoms to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Beni tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaawo fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? ni ekɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ma shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce energy to grow large tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the ground away from damp pests and diseases, giving them full access to sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la lɛ kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the young shoots to keep growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow creates competition for soil food and water. Pruning down extra suckers ensures the main plant gets enough energy to yield a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ekɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ tsei babaoo ni tsii.

english: What are the small caterpillars eating holes into the center leaves of my maize, and why do they spread so fast?
ga: Kplukai bibii miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ. Ni mɛni hewɔ amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya nɛkɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, pests that lay hundreds of eggs inside the central leaf funnel of maize plants. They multiply quickly because the adult moths can fly long distances between farms overnight.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni woɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. Amɛfɔɔ oya ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afã gbɛ kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ateŋ nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts between my crop seasons help my soil stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ be mli ni mikwɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they naturally enrich the soil with nitrogen for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden eggs curling upward and growing very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on sap and spread plant viruses. Controlling these small pests prevents them from stunting the plant's leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔyeli yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛtsiɔ amɛnaa koni amɛkatsi tsei ahe baai lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I dried and stored from last year fail to sprout when planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni migbi ni mikɛto nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their ability to sprout if stored in places with heat, humidity, or insect damage. Dampness causes stored seeds to weaken or mold long before they are planted in the farm.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto hei ni dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i, loo kooloi fiteɔ. Fɛ̃i haa dumɔwui ni ato lɛ feɔ blɛoo loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani aduɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and scorching in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hulu lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains around them acts as natural umbrellas, protecting the leaves and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Ebuɔ baai ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I remove the dark, rotted cocoa pods from my tree as soon as I see them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni miifite lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli kɛji mina lɛ pɛ?

english: Rotted pods carry black pod disease, which spreads rapidly through rain splashes to healthy pods; removing and safely disposing of infected pods keeps the fungal disease from destroying your whole crop.
ga: Pods ni egbo ji nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni okɛshwie shweshweeshwe lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii hela lɛ naa koni ekafite onibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small ragged holes and tiny caterpillars inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ekumɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii Eyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest; checking leaves early and applying recommended treatments directly into the central plant shoot prevents the caterpillars from killing the growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ; Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ amli mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbe he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my maize field yield less harvest when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize continuously pulls the same nutrients from the soil; rotating your land with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and stops pests from building up.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall stems with thick leaves but give me small, skinny tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ waa kɛ baai ni mli tse shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Staking spreads the leaves out so they catch more sunlight to make food for the plant, which directly leads to larger and heavier yam tubers.
ga: Staking gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa koni hulu la babaoo anyɛ afee niyenii aha tso lɛ. Enɛ kɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii baa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or uneven watering, which prevents proper pollination and fruit development.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination kɛ aduawai ni sa lɛ anaa.

english: Why are my green tomato plants suddenly wilting and dying during the hot afternoon even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that clogs the internal water pipes of the stem, blocking water from reaching the upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni sũ ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I cover the base of my crop plants with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai aha mi tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with organic mulch traps water in the soil, keeps root zone temperatures cool, and stops weeds from sprouting and stealing plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to apply chemical fertilizer right before a big rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ akɛ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours wash away topsoil and dissolve fertilizer away from plant roots into rivers and ditches, wasting your investment.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ shwieɔ faai kɛ ŋmeii amli. ni haa ofiteɔ shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to grow green leaves and food. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help your maize become strong and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ niyenii Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni o-ŋmei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔji.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on the land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops like groundnuts and beans gather natural plant food from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting them after maize heals the soil so your next crop grows better without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii buaa tsei aniyenii naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni ooodu yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce more pods when I leave large trees growing inside my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo kɛ́ mishi tsei wuji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Large trees shield delicate cocoa leaves from harsh sun and strong winds, keep the ground cool and damp, and drop leaves that rot down into rich natural fertilizer for your cocoa.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. kɛ baai ni fiteɔ ni eba shi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo kɛhaa o-cocoa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open on the farm right when they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they go from dry soil to sudden heavy water, such as after a sudden heavy rain. The inside of the fruit swells up faster than its skin can stretch, causing it to crack.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛji ejɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtee nu ni hoɔ trukaa, tamɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa trukaa lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli fũuɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he, ni no haa egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains fall for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on your farm without draining away, it drowns the roots, allowing decay and rot to set in quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ. Nu baaha shishifãi lɛ ashwie shi. Ha ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efite oya.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my yam mounds with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass traps moisture in the soil during hot days, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly decays into food that helps your yams grow bigger.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaye nɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-sweet potatoes lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are insects attacking my cabbage leaves much more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa cabbage baai yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Many harmful insects love warm, dry air and multiply much faster in the sun. During the rainy season, heavy rain naturally washes many of these insects and their eggs off the leaves.
ga: Koolooi babaoo ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ sumɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi. Ni amɛshwereɔ oya kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa kooloi bibii kɛ amɛwuji lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my stored cowpea grains get filled with tiny holes and powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ nibii bibii lɛ? Nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Small insects called weevils hatch from tiny eggs laid on the crop before harvest. If the seeds are not dried completely or protected in airtight containers, the insects hatch and eat the inside of the grains.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ moths lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ wɔji bibii amli. ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani akpaa Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa loo abuuu he yɛ tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli. Kplukai lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. The plant drops the flowers to save its own energy until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ miihao amɛ. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch high to search for sunlight instead of spending energy to produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao hulu la moŋ fe ni amɛaafite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the topsoil, so applying urea or NPK fertilizer helps the leaves recover their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ urea loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Does planting cowpeas on my farm help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, cowpeas belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and stores it in root nodules. When the plant roots decay in the soil, they release natural fertilizer that helps crops like maize grow better in the next season.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cowpeas fata legume weku lɛ he, ni no gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei shishifãi fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei tamɔ ŋmãa ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ kpo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing necessary shade and conserving soil moisture during the cocoa tree's first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden poles to climb on instead of spreading across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso ni esa akɛ ekwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture maximum sunlight for their leaves. When the leaves get full exposure to the sun, they generate more energy, which fuels the growth of larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ Ebaaha hewalɛ babaoo aba. ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ daa lɛ

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up tightly like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking plant juices from the undersides of leaves. Treating the plants early with an neem-based spray or recommended organic pesticide stops the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ tso mli nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛ neem fee ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akpa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for steady rains before planting my main maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu niyenii titri ni akɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ?

english: Planting right after the first brief rain can be risky because if a short dry spell follows, the soil will dry out and kill newly germinated seeds. Waiting for consistent rainfall ensures seeds have continuous moisture to grow strong.
ga: Aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kukuoo ko sɛɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ko nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi ni dumɔwui heei baanyɛ akwɛ̃. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni abaamɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: When too many shoots grow from the same plantain stem, they compete for nutrients and water. Removing excess shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, allowing the main stem to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Beni plantain tsei babaoo ni jɛ tso kome mli lɛ fa babaoo lɛ. Nakai tsei lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi, ni no baaha ŋmeii titri lɛ afee ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look thin and weak even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, root space, and sunlight from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get full access to soil nutrients so they can build thick stems and healthy leaves.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Koni tso lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli tse kɛ baai ni mli wa.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 and 12 months after planting. You can tell they are ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack open.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ amɛfee klalo kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience extreme heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during extremely hot afternoons helps the plant hold its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know which type of yam variety is best to plant if I want to sell quickly in Ghanaian markets?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male sweet potato henɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ makwɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ oya yɛ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Market preferences usually favor specific varieties like Pona because of its high consumer demand, white flesh, and dry texture, whereas other traditional local varieties might yield well but sell at lower prices.
ga: Jarayeli mli nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ komɛi tamɔ Pona yɛ amɛ nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ taoɔ babaoo, loo yɛŋ kɛ amɛhe ni egbi lɛ hewɔ, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ nibii kpakpai aba shi ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ.

english: Why should I consider buying modern improved crop seeds if my traditional local seeds have been growing for years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ Beaŋ Dumɔwui ni Atsake lɛ ahe lɛ he? Kɛji akɛ adu mi shishijee maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ afii babaoo ni eho nɛ

english: Traditional seeds are reliable and familiar, but improved seed varieties are specifically bred to give higher yields, resist common local pests, and withstand unpredictable rain patterns.
ga: Anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ kusum dumɔwui anɔ ni ale jogbaŋŋ. Shi afɔɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Eteɔ shi ewoɔ akutsoŋ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni eteɔ shi ewoɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ.

english: Can I plant any cut section of a harvested yam tuber to grow a new plant?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu sweet potato ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ mli ŋmeii koni mikɛkwɛ tsei heei?

english: The top cut (head) of the yam tuber sprouts the fastest and most reliably, though cured middle and tail pieces can also grow into healthy tubers if treated properly before planting.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni afo (yitso) ni yɔɔ sweet potato tuber lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe fɛɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Teŋgbɛ fãi kɛ tsitsii ni atsa lɛ po baanyɛ adara ni amɛfee bulbs ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu.

english: Does the source or quality of water I use for my crops really affect how my yams grow?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jɛɛhe loo bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ saa mi-sweet potatoes lɛ adalɛ he?

english: Yes, clean water free from heavy chemical pollutants or salt allows roots to absorb nutrients easily, whereas salty or contaminated water can stunt root growth and ruin soil quality.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni mli tse ni tsofai, nibii ni fiteɔ nii loo ŋmeii ni mli ewo muji bɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni mli edɔ loo nu ni mli ewo muji baanyɛ aha shishifãi ada ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii.

english: How can I tell if my yam plants are getting too much water in the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi sweet potato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When yam plants receive too much water, their lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the underground tubers begin to rot because the soil lacks air.
ga: Kɛji sweet potato tso lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Eshishi baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi. Ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ bɔi fitemɔ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do we build soil mounds or ridges before planting yams instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmaa gɔji loo ŋmeii dani wɔduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Building soil mounds loosens the earth so the yam tuber can expand deep underground while preventing excess rainwater from pooling and rotting the crop.
ga: Gɔŋ ni ooofee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ abua naa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What causes my crop leaves to turn yellow early in the rainy season, and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Early leaf yellowing often means the crop is missing key soil nutrients like nitrogen or is sitting in waterlogged soil; applying a small amount of fertilizer and improving farm drainage usually fixes it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ mra lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo eyɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ naagba lɛ he nii.

english: Is it good practice to grow small crops like maize or vegetables on the same farm alongside my yams?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ masɛi?

english: Yes, intercropping yams with short-season crops like beans or maize helps cover the bare soil, suppresses weeds, and provides food or income while waiting for the main yam harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potatoes ni akɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei duɔ. Ye obua ni aha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ, jwɛi kɛ niyenii loo shika aha be mli ni mɛɔ atomɔ ŋmaa titri lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yams from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yams are mature and ready to harvest when the leaves and vines naturally yellow and dry up completely, showing that the tuber has stopped growing and is fully formed.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eda ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ efee ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ yitso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni eda.

english: How should I store my harvested yams so they don't rot or spoil quickly?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ato koni amɛkafite loo amɛkafite oya?

english: Yams store best off the ground in a well-ventilated, shaded wooden barn where air circulates freely to keep tubers cool and dry, stopping them from rotting or sprouting early.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ sweet potato toɔ ŋmɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ mli. He ni kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli oya koni eha yitso lɛ mli ajɔ ni egbi. Enɛ baatsi enaa koni ekafite loo ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the essential food plants need to build green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or organic manure helps the leaves turn green so the plant can catch sunlight and make big corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la ni eha ŋmãa toi lɛ adara.

english: Why does my cassava drop its leaves during the dry season, and is my crop dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miigboi?

english: Your cassava is not dying; it naturally drops its leaves to save water when rain is scarce. It enters a resting phase while keeping its food energy stored safely inside the roots until the next rainy season begins.
ga: O cassava ɔ gbo we lolo. Ejɛɔ ebɔɔ su mli egbeeɔ shi koni ekɛhere nu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Botemɔ wɔɔhe be lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni okɛ niyenii hewalɛ toɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why did my maize seeds fail to sprout after I buried them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If seeds are planted too deep, they run out of energy before the young shoots can reach the top of the ground to find sunlight. Planting maize seeds shallowly, about two finger-joints deep, allows them to sprout quickly and safely.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ Hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ koni amɛyana hulu la. Abɛi dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ, aaafee nineshi 2 lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant cowpeas alongside my maize crop?
