ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ madu tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap natural nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the maize plant growing next to it. At the same time, the spreading leaves of the cowpeas cover the ground to stop weeds from growing and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii yɛ be kome too mli ni Cowpea baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I cut down all the large shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gĩi ni amɛgboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants act like human babies and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Leaving larger shade trees on your farm protects young cocoa plants from heat damage and keeps the surrounding air humid.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii feɔ amɛnii tamɔ adesai abifabii ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Kɛ́ oshi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa ni baafite amɛ lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when the plants experience extreme heat or dry soil. Giving your tomatoes consistent water at the roots and light shade during extremely hot periods keeps the flowers healthy enough to turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ́ aha tomato lɛ nu daa yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into small cups and staying stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? Ni egbɔjɔ lolo?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the plant's juices and spread viruses. Protecting your plants with neem oil spray or safe pest controls keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ bu otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and capture as much sunlight as possible to build large underground tubers. Staking also lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and rot.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni akɛtsi baa hela kɛ fitemɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when weeds are left growing around their roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni ashiɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with your crops by taking the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crops need to grow. Clearing weeds regularly ensures all available soil food goes directly to growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛtsɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ yaa otsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potato roots look small and thin even though the leaves on top look huge and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni dara ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer without enough potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of developing big tubers below. Balanced fertilizer helps the plant send food down into the roots.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ ebaa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii, moŋ fe ni eeefee bulbs agboi yɛ shishigbɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, a key food they need to grow strong. This often happens when heavy rains wash soil nutrients away or when the soil lacks organic matter, which can be fixed by adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the crop's life.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli ni akɛbaafata he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my cassava producing very tall stems with leaves but small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ waa shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from overly rich soil, it spends all its energy growing leaves and branches above ground instead of storing food in its roots below. Balancing the soil food and planting healthy stem cuttings helps the plant focus on growing bigger tubers.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo lɛ nɔ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai kɛ niji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa bulbs wuji ni yaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops burn and die when I apply fertilizer close to their stems during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain salts that need plenty of soil water to dissolve safely. When applied too close to stems during dry weather, the fertilizer draws water out of the plant's roots instead of feeding them, causing the plant to dry up and burn.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni biɔ shikpɔŋ nu babaoo koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Fertilizer lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Why does my maize crop yield less every year when I keep planting it on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi lɛ? Be mli ni miduɔ lɛ lolo yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planted continuously in the same place, maize consumes the exact same nutrients every season until the soil is completely empty. Rotating your land with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts refills the soil with nitrogen naturally and prevents pests from settling down.
ga: Aduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be. Okɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ awo mli daa be mli kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni akɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni etsĩ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo shishifãi.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves drop and dry out as soon as the dry harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji harmattan be ni egbi lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that lose water very fast under strong sun and hot winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a cool environment that traps moisture and shields cocoa leaves from direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya waa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni akwɛɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ baa.

english: How does leaving dry grass on top of my farm soil help my vegetables survive during hot periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that blocks the sun from baking the soil. It slows down water evaporation, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from springing up to steal water from your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ko ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni ehaa sũ lɛ shãaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ koni amɛju nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why do flowers keep falling off my tomato plants without turning into fruits during hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ otsi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and irregular watering stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers as a defense mechanism to save energy. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps the plant hold onto its blooms until fruits form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I harvest more food from my small plot of land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ makpa niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani manyɛ maná mi nɔ babaoo?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and very small harvests. Proper spacing gives each crop enough room to breathe and feed, giving you a bigger overall harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni akpaa nii fioo ko pɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛmuɔ ni eyeɔ nii. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii babaoo yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the extra shoots around my main plantain stem to grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he? Mi plantain tsei titri lɛ feɔ ekome kɛkwɛɔ.

english: Allowing too many shoots, or suckers, to grow around one plantain stem creates competition for food and water, leading to tiny bunches. Pruning back excess suckers so that only one or two strong ones remain with the parent tree keeps the plant healthy and bunches large.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso kome he Enɛ haa akaŋshii baa niyenii kɛ nu he. ni kɛ tso bibioo ko baa Afoɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhe wa ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are there small ragged holes appearing inside the center funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu bibii ni etse ehe lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes inside the center leaf roll are a classic sign of caterpillars like Fall Armyworm hiding inside the plant to feed on fresh growth. Finding these early allows you to protect the crop before the caterpillar destroys the growing tip where the maize head forms.
ga: Bu ni mli efo ni yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji ŋmei ko ni ale waa, tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni kɛ ehe ewo tso lɛ mli koni eye ŋmei heei ni eda lɛ. Nibii nɛɛ ni ooona mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni miida lɛ he ni ŋmãa yitsei lɛ feɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantain plants to shield them, the intense sun burns their leaves and dries out the soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baaha hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu ni he hiaa kɛha wala lɛ gĩɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of turning into fruits during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ aduawai najiaŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat makes tomato pollen sterile and stops flowers from getting fertilized. When a flower is not fertilized properly, the plant drops it to conserve water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato pollen lɛ feɔ nɔ ni bɛ fɔmɔ nii, ni ehaaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee fɔmɔ nii. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi ko fɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This yellowing is a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow, so when the soil runs low, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha baai ŋmɔji heei lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans between my rows of corn help my farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants drop leaves and roots decompose, that nitrogen enters the soil and feeds the corn growing nearby.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei lɛ shwie baai ni amɛshishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Nitrogen boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmãa ni adu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I avoid putting chemical fertilizer on my soil right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away the fertilizer before the plant roots can absorb it, which wastes your money and can contaminate nearby streams.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ shika ni ebaanyɛ efite faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot under the soil when the heavy rain season lasts too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits around the roots for many days, it suffocates them and allows underground rot organisms to attack the plant.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe gbii babaoo Ebaaha egbɔjɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ shishi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ atutua tso lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during high winds even when the plant looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy fruit at the top. When rain softens the ground, strong winds can easily push the heavy plant out of the soft soil unless you prop it up with wooden poles.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni tsii yɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ashɛre tsei ni tsii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nɔ oya. Ja okɛ tso ko tsu nii ni okɛfi sɛɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which target the soft center leaves of young corn plants. The adult moths lay eggs on the leaves, and the hungry caterpillars hatch to feed on the tender growth.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Akpɔlɔi ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ fɔɔ koni amɛye ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and getting small and crumpled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap out of new leaves, or by a virus carried by these insects that distorts plant growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai heei amli nu lɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ hiɛɔ ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto tall bamboo sticks instead of letting them grow along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need full sunlight to make the energy required for building large tubers underground. Staking gets the leaves off the wet ground, protecting them from mud and soil diseases while exposing them to sunlight.
ga: Hulu ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ muji kɛ shikpɔŋ helai ahe yɛ be mli ni okɛ amɛ woɔ hulu la mli lɛ.

english: Why do my heavy pepper branches keep snapping off when the plant gets full of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper niji ni tsii lɛ yaa nɔ efoɔ lɛ? Mɛɛ be tso lɛ eyi kɛ aduawai?

english: Pepper plants naturally produce heavy loads of fruit that their thin stems cannot hold alone. Tying the branches to sturdy wooden stakes or using support strings helps bear that weight so the stems do not bend or snap under a full harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ amɛtso bibii lɛ anɔ. Can’t keep it Fimɔ tso nine lɛ kɛya tso ni wa nɔ loo okɛ kpãa atsu nii ni okɛfi sɛɛ koni ekɛfi tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieee shi loo amɛkuuu kɛji akpa amɛ kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants fall over on the ground whenever it rains heavily in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants have weak, top-heavy structures and shallow roots that loosen when the soil becomes wet and muddy. Propping the plants upright with strong stakes keeps them standing tall even through heavy rain and wind.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, amɛhe wa, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ muji. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni wa ha otso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa po mli.

english: What simple materials can I use to prop up my pepper plants so they stay upright?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni he hiaa koni akɛfi pepper tso ko sɛɛ koni ehi shi jaŋŋ?

english: You can use local bamboo poles, strong sticks, or wooden stakes pushed into the soil near the base of the plant, then loosely secure the main stems to the stick using soft twine, raffia, or cloth string.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii tsei atsu nii. tso nine ni mli wa loo tso ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, fimɔ tso titri lɛ he jogbaŋŋ kɛya tso lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ kpã ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ji raffia loo mama kpã ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ

english: Why is it important to tie pepper plants with strings before they produce full fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ kpãa akpɛtɛ pepper tsei ahe dani amɛbafɔfɔi babaoo lɛ?

english: Securing plants early gives them a strong framework as they grow. When the heavy fruits eventually appear, the pre-tied strings immediately support the extra weight without causing sudden stress or damage to the growing plant.
ga: Kɛ́ akwɛ tsei anɔ mra lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kpãai ni akɛfiɔ momo lɛ fiɔ muji ni fa fe nine lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni ekɛ haomɔ loo fitemɔ baaa tso ni miida lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my pepper fruits turn soft and rot whenever they touch the damp soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper yibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil naturally carries tiny moisture-loving fungi and bacteria that cause soft rot. When fruits rest on wet dirt, these germs easily break through the skin, causing the pepper to decay quickly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ni haa efiteɔ. Kɛ́ aduawai lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ boteɔ hewolo lɛ mli oya. Ehaa pepper fiteɔ oya

english: How does lifting my crops off the ground protect them from crawling insects?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ahe?

english: Many crawling pests like caterpillars, beetles, and slugs live in the topsoil and feed on fruits lying on the dirt. Raising plants off the ground creates distance, making it much harder for these pests to reach and destroy your harvest.
ga: Kooloi babaoo ni shwereɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛyeɔ aduawai ni kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Tsei ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ baa. Enɛ haa ewaa kwraa kɛhaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akɛ amɛaashɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni amɛfite.

english: Why do vegetables spoil so much faster when they lie directly on wet farm mud?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai fiteɔ oya waa kɛ akɛwo ŋmɔ mli sũ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Mud traps moisture against the skin of the crop and prevents air from drying it out. This constant dampness creates the perfect environment for mold and decay to spread through the crop.
ga: Muji mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewolo mli ni ehaaa egbi. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: How does keeping pepper plants upright make my harvest look better for market buyers?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-pepper tsei lɛ ni mikɛbaakwɛ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Peppers grown off the ground stay clean, free of mud stains, and unblemished by ground rots. Clean, smooth, and undamaged peppers attract buyers quickly and sell for much higher prices at the market.
ga: Pepper ni adu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafee nɔ ni he tse. Ebɛ muji mli muji Ni ebɛ muji ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbo nɔ, ŋmɔtɔ ni he tse, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni efiteee lɛ gbalaa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ oya ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa yɛ jara nɔ.

english: How can I tell when my green peppers are fully mature and ready to be picked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-green chili lɛ edara ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: Green peppers are ready to harvest when they reach full size, feel firm and hard when squeezed gently, and display a glossy, deep green color before they begin to turn soft or change color.
ga: Chili eŋɔli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛshɛ amɛdalɛ he. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ amɔ lɛ fioo. ni ojie su ni kpɛɔ ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kpo dani eje shishi efee blɛoo loo etsake su.

english: Does lifting pepper branches off the ground help the leaves stay healthy and green?
ga: Ani kɛ́ owó pepper niji anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee eŋɔli?

english: Yes, holding branches upright allows good air movement and sunlight to reach every leaf, which dries up dampness and keeps the foliage green, healthy, and free from leaf diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji lɛ ni aaaha amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli ni hulu la shɛɔ baa fɛɛ baa he. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli, ehe wa ni baa helai bɛ mli.

english: Why does heavy rainfall make all my yams ready for harvest at the exact same time as other farmers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa mi-sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ be kome too mli lɛ? kɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi

english: Consistent and widespread rain provides uniform moisture across the region, which causes yam plants everywhere to mature at the same rate.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ haa hulutsoo be fɛɛ be baa kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato tsei lɛ fɛɛ daa yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ.

english: How does rain actually affect how big my yam tubers grow under the soil?
ga: Te nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ saa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rain softens the soil and helps nutrients flow into the roots, giving the yam plant the water it needs to expand and bulk up its tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni hoɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa sweet potato tso lɛ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa ni eha ŋmeii lɛ ayi afa.

english: Can too much rain harm my yams while they are still growing in the ground?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aye sweet potatoes awui be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, excessive rainfall can cause waterlogged soil, which starves root systems of oxygen, leads to fungal diseases, and causes tubers to rot.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee nu. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa Ni ebaanyɛ eha oyitso agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do yam prices drop so low in the market when we get plenty of rain during the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ jara baa shi nɛkɛ lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Good rains lead to a bumper harvest for every farmer, creating a surplus in the market where supply exceeds buyer demand, which naturally drives down prices.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmaa kpakpa baa okwaafoi fɛɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni fa fe nine baa jarayelihe lɛ he ni nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha nibii ajara aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it difficult to find a good buyer when everyone in my village harvests yams at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaana hɔlɔ kpakpa be mli ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are abundant everywhere, traders have many options and can demand lower prices because food is easily available from any nearby farm.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ he fɛɛ he lɛ Jarayelɔi baaná nibii babaoo ni amɛbaahala ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbi jara ni baa shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niyenii yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli oya.

english: Should I transport my yams to the market immediately after harvest or wait a while?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ sweet potato aya jara nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa lɛ loo esa akɛ mamɛ fioo?

english: If the market is flooded at peak harvest, waiting while properly storing your yams allows you to sell later when supply drops and prices go back up.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nu eyi jara lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Mɛmɔ be mli ni okɛ o-sweet potatoes lɛ eto jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha onyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ sɛɛ mli beni nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ ba shi ni jara lɛ ku esɛɛ eba shi lɛ.

english: Why do crops in different towns all flood the market at the same time after a good rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ maji srɔtoi anɔ lɛ baafee nu afua yɛ jara lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kpakpa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weather patterns usually affect entire regions, so crops across multiple towns experience the same growing conditions and reach maturity together.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi saa kpokpaa muu lɛ fɛɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ maji babaoo amli lɛ yɛ shihilɛ kome mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli.

english: What happens to yams if I leave them in wet soil too long after a heavy rain to avoid market price drops?
ga: Mɛni baa sweet potato nɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ koni jara akagbee shi?

english: Leaving mature yams in wet ground risks tuber rot and pest invasion; it is better to harvest them and store them in a well-ventilated structure.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi sweet potato ni eda yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tuber rot kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba. Esa akɛ akpa amɛ ni akɛto he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ.

english: Can I store my harvested yams safely to sell them when prices recover?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ato shweshweeshwe koni mahɔ̃ɔ kɛji jara lɛ tee hiɛ?

english: Yes, storing healthy, uninjured yams in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated yam barn prevents decay and keeps them fresh until market prices rise.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ sweet potato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni epilaaa lɛ ato sweet potato shĩa ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Ebaatsi fitemɔ naa ni ebaaha efee ehee kɛyashi jara nɔ jara lɛ baaya hiɛ.

english: If good rainfall causes crop prices to collapse everywhere, how can I protect my farm income?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ kpakpa ha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara ba shi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi okwaafonyo lɛ shika he?

english: Staggering your planting dates or growing a mix of different crops ensures you do not harvest everything at the same time as everyone else.
ga: Gbii ni akɛduɔ nii ni haa mɔ naa kpɛɔ ehe loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ haa okpaaa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli tamɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ.

english: Officer, why do my young maize leaves turn yellow when the plants are still very small?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ? Tso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa lolo?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually show that the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is its main food for growing green leaves. Giving the crop a small amount of nitrogen fertilizer early on helps it recover and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ daa lɛ. Ha otsei lɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fioo mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why does my cassava take up to a full year to yield, while my maize is ready in just three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ afi muu fɛɛ ni ekɛbaa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-abele lɛ efee klalo yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava stores its food underground in thick roots, which takes many months of steady growth to build up. Maize puts its energy into growing seeds above ground quickly before the plant dies, so it matures much faster.
ga: Cassava kɛ niyenii toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shishifãi ni mli tse amli. Enɛ biɔ nyɔji babaoo ni yaa nɔ daa dani abua naa. Abɛi kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ dumɔwui oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tso lɛ gboɔ. No hewɔ lɛ edaa oya kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over during heavy rains when the heavy bunches start to show?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli beni niji lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not dig deep into the earth; they spread out near the surface. When the soil becomes soft from rain and the fruit bunch gets heavy, the shallow roots cannot support the weight without wooden props.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ efooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Amɛgbɛ amɛshwã he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bafee blɛoo kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli ni aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ muji lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ he lɛ bɛ.

english: If I leave weeds to grow around my pepper plants for too long, will it stop them from fruiting?
ga: Kɛji oshi jwɛi yɛ Pepper tso lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ Ani ebaaha ewo yibii loo ebaaha ewooo yibii?

english: Yes, weeds act like fast thieves that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your pepper plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets the strength it needs to produce plenty of healthy peppers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-pepper tsei lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ babaoo aba.

english: Officer, why does my soil produce small harvests if I plant maize on the same piece of land every single year?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Maize removes the exact same nutrients from the soil season after season without giving anything back. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas helps return vital nitrogen into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli ni ekɛ nɔ ko haaa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ Haa nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upward and drying up during the hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, combined with heat stress. Keeping insects away and watering the root area regularly helps protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ fata he Kplukai ni tsiɔ amɛnaa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa shishifãi lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my garden egg flowers dropping to the ground instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miigbee shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant lacks enough water or nutrients, or when bees are not visiting to pollinate them. Consistent watering and avoiding harsh chemical sprays while flowers are open helps fruit set properly.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii baaa koni amɛbafee pollination. Nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ amli daa kɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods so the beans do not spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Cocoa pods are ready when their skin turns fully yellow or orange. Harvesting too early leaves the beans bitter and undeveloped, while leaving them too long causes the seeds inside to rot or germinate.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ hewolo lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni ashiɔ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so fast while I am waiting to transport them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya nɛkɛ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni akɛ amɛ aya jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they get bruised during digging, exposed to direct hot sun, or piled in unventilated spaces. Keeping them in a cool, shaded barn elevated off the bare ground protects them until transport arrives.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛhe fã beni amɛmiifo lɛ. hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ loo ato amɛhe yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ to ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli ni awo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛyashi be mli ni tsɔne ni akɛyaa jɛmɛ lɛ baashɛ.

english: Officer, why should I buy new certified seeds instead of just replanting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du wuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ ekohu.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid harvests lose their vigor and disease resistance in the next generation, producing uneven plants and smaller yields. Certified seeds are specially bred to give strong, uniform crops and bigger harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ekome ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. daa ni amɛfee babaoo

english: Which crop is easier for me to harvest on my farm between yam and cassava?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha mi akɛ makpa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ sweet potatoes kɛ cassava teŋ?

english: Cassava is much easier to harvest because its tubers lie closer to the surface and require less digging, whereas yam harvesting is physically demanding and requires deep, careful digging to avoid damaging the tubers.
ga: Cassava ŋmɔmɔ waaa kwraa ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni amɛheɔ be babaoo ni akɛfoɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmei ni akpaa lɛ biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ, ni ebiɔ ni akumɔ mli shɔŋŋ ni akwɛ jogbaŋŋ koni akafite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why does harvesting yam leave me so much more exhausted than harvesting cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpaa lɛ haa mihe jɔ̃ɔ mi fe ŋmeii ni akpaa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep underground within mounds, demanding intense physical labor and heavy digging to unearth them cleanly, while cassava roots are shallower and lighter to lift from the soil.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ gɔji amli. Enɛ biɔ nitsumɔ ni wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsa koni akɛtsa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ abaawo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I have limited farm labor or physical strength, should I plant cassava or yam?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ loo gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ babaoo hu? Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei?

english: You should focus more on cassava because it requires significantly less strenuous labor, especially when it comes time to dig up the mature roots.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmei nɔ babaoo ejaakɛ ebiɔ nitsumɔ fioo ko kwraa. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ be shɛ ni esa akɛ atsa shishifãi ni eda lɛ.

english: Why is digging up yams considered such hard work compared to other root crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ ŋmeii ni atsa lɛ akɛ eji nitsumɔ ni wa kɛ akɛto shishifãi krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Yams grow deep and are fragile, meaning you cannot rush the process; you must spend long hours carefully clearing soil around each tuber using heavy tools so they do not snap.
ga: Atomɔ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onyɛŋ okɛ oyaiyeli atsu nii. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo atsu nii ni okɛjie sũ ni bɔle bulb lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ nibii ni tsii anɔ koni ekakumɔ.

english: How does the work involved in farming cassava differ from farming yam?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro nitsumɔ ni kɔɔ ŋmei dumɔ he lɛ yɛ ŋmei dumɔ he?

english: While both crops require field preparation, yam requires much more intensive labor for making high mounds, staking vines, and heavy digging at harvest, whereas cassava is far less demanding to manage and harvest.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni tsei henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ biɔ he ni asaa he lɛ. Sweet potatoes biɔ nitsumɔ ni mli wa babaoo koni akɛma gɔji lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, Wein Tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso mli kɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsaa waa beni akpaa Cassava lɛ biɔ nibii babaoo ni esa akɛ atsu he nii ni akpa.

english: Can I rely on selling cassava to support my family and pay for my children's education?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ ŋmei ni mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ koni mikɛkwɛ miweku lɛ ni mikɛwo mibii lɛ askulyaa he nyɔmɔ?

english: Yes, cassava is a safe and dependable staple crop that provides a steady stream of income over time, helping many farming households cover essential family expenses like school fees.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. ni haa shika ni yaa nɔ yɛ be mli lɛ baa Eyeɔ ebuaa okwaayeli shiai babaoo ni amɛwoɔ weku lɛ shika ni he hiaa tamɔ skul nyɔmɔwoo.

english: Why do I only seem to have a small amount of money left over after selling my cassava harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni shika fioo pɛ eshwɛ mi beni mihɔ̃ɔ ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava prices per unit can be low, and costs for field labor or transport eat into earnings, so while it provides reliable earnings, the profit margin on each sale is usually small.
ga: Ekolɛ, ŋmei kome jara baa shi. Ni ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ loo gbɛfaa he nyɔmɔwoo yeɔ shika ni anáa lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ ekɛ shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ haa moŋ Shi bei pii lɛ, sɛɛnamɔ ni jɛɔ jarayeli fɛɛ jarayeli mli baa lɛ faaa.

english: Is it still worth planting cassava if the profit from selling it is small?
ga: Ani ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ lolo akɛ abaadu ŋmei kɛji akɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni jɛɔ jarayeli mli baa lɛ faaa?

english: Yes, because cassava is reliable, easy to grow, and stores well in the ground, ensuring you always have food for your home and a guaranteed, small surplus profit when you sell.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ ŋmei nɔ, edumɔ waaa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa onáa niyenii kɛha shia lɛ be fɛɛ be. Ni sɛɛnamɔ fioo ko ni fa fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni ama nɔ mi kɛji ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: If I plant both yam and cassava, will that help secure a better income for my household?
ga: Kɛji midu sweet potatoes kɛ cassava fɛɛ Ani ebaaye ebua mishiabii lɛ ni amɛná shika kpakpa?

english: Yes, growing both balances your risks; yam brings higher market value per tuber despite demanding hard work, while cassava offers low-labor stability and continuous sales to keep cash flowing.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okɛ oshara he akɔnɔ lɛ feɔ ekome. Sweet potatoes haa jarayeli jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe mɔ fɛɛ mɔ yɛ nitsumɔ ni wa ni he hiaa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei haa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ nitsumɔ fioo kɛ jarayeli ni yaa nɔ koni shika ahi shi.

english: Should I expect quick wealth from harvesting root crops like yam and cassava?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makpa shweremɔ oya gbɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni akpaa lɛ mli?

english: No, tuber farming usually yields modest, gradual earnings rather than huge sudden profits, but with consistent production, it reliably leaves you with enough money to care for your household.
ga: Dabi, tuber okwaayeli kɛ sɛɛnamɔi bibii ni baa fiofio baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona sɛɛnamɔ kpele trukaa Shi kɛ nibii ni afeɔ daa lɛ Enɛ baaha oná shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛkwɛ oshia lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani abele lɛ afee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen—an essential nutrient for green growth—or that excess water around the roots is preventing the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ loo nu ni fa fe nine yɛ he fɛɛ he Shishifãi lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye nii.

english: Why does my land yield smaller cassava tubers if I plant cassava in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmei shishifãi bibii kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the specific soil nutrients that crop needs to grow big, while allowing pests and diseases tailored to that plant to multiply in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara lɛ aba shi be fɛɛ be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for other crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil naturally for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miijie fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often fall off due to stress from prolonged heat, lack of soil moisture, or attacks by small insect pests like mirids, which prevent the flowers from setting fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ hewɔ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ mirids ni haaa fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: How do I know if my cassava is ready to harvest under the ground without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni akuuu ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots are generally mature when the lower leaves on the main stem naturally dry up and fall, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daa kɛji tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: Why are my pepper plants producing thick foliage and leaf growth but no flowers or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai ni mli tse kɛ baai ni shwereɔ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo ŋmeii bɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages the pepper plant to focus all its energy on leaf growth rather than making flowers and fruit; reduced nitrogen and adequate sunlight trigger flowering.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ pepper tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Nitrogen ni ayeɔ lɛ nɔ ni baa shi kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ haa fɔfɔi baa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often brought on by irregular watering during dry periods.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Yams are climbing vines that need support to lift their leaves into the sunlight, which allows the plant to make food efficiently and build large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Should I leave all the young suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he? Mi plantain lɛ shishitoo?

english: Leaving all suckers causes them to fight for light, water, and nutrients; cutting back all but one or two strong suckers helps the main plant direct its energy into producing a large bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛwuu koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ fɛɛ mli, ja tso lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ pɛ ekome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ awo yibii wuji amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell; planting too early causes seeds to sprout and then die from lack of water before the main rainy season settles in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgboiɔ yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ.

english: When bottom leaves turn yellow in a V-shape pattern, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant is moving whatever nitrogen it has left to the newer top leaves so it can keep growing, signaling that the soil needs compost or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ miitsi nitrogen fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛmiiya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni enyɛ eya nɔ eda. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young crop leaves with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle baai bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dried grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground, keeps the soil cool during hot sunny afternoons, and stops weed seeds from receiving sunlight to grow.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ fĩɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need as much sunlight as possible on their leaves. Staking the vines helps the leaves catch full sunlight, which allows the plant to produce enough energy to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni hulu la babaoo he hiaa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit cluster starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top. Without support, strong winds or the weight of the fruit can easily uproot the plant, so propping the stem with sturdy wooden or bamboo forks is necessary.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo tso yibii lɛ tsiimɔ baanyɛ ajie lɛ oya kɛji akɛ nɔ ko bɛ ni fiɔ esɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo tso yibii lɛ tsiimɔ he miihia. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ tso fɔk loo ŋmei tso ni wa awo tso lɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad to plant four or five maize seeds in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the growing plants to compete against each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. This results in weak, skinny stalks with small or missing maize cobs instead of healthy ones.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ haa tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ kɛ ŋmãa bibii loo ni elaaje lɛ baa yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantain plants grown right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and provide large leaves that shade the cocoa trees, keeping them cool and moist while their roots mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tso lɛ he jɔɔ. Ha cacao tso lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and stopping the fruits from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa aduawai lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus disrupts how fluids move inside the plant, causing leaves to twist and preventing normal fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Virus lɛ gbalaa nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do tiny green and black bugs gather on my cowpea plants as soon as flowers appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii diji lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ je kpo pɛ.

english: Insects like aphids are attracted to the sweet sap inside new flower buds and tender shoots. They suck this sap out, which weakens the plant and can cause the flowers to fall off before forming cowpea pods.
ga: Wuo ni anaa yɛ fɔfɔi heei kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii, tamɔ aphids. Amɛmuɔ mliki nɛɛ amɛyaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ebaanyɛ eha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo dani cowpea pods lɛ afee.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills the soil with excess water, oxygen cannot reach the roots. This waterlogged environment causes fungal diseases to attack the roots, turning the firm cassava roots into soft, rotten mush.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni nu eyi mli obɔ nɛɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi ni wa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni fiteɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or inconsistent watering. When stress levels are too high, the plant discards its flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni naa wa mli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Kɛji akɛ haomɔ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do you take soil samples from my field, and what will it tell me about my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nyɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni mɛni ebaakɛɛ mi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Collecting soil samples helps us test what nutrients your land is missing or has in excess. This tells us exactly what fertilizer or soil treatment your crops need so you do not waste money buying the wrong inputs.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wɔkwɛɔ lɛ haa wɔkaa kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa loo eshɛɛɛ he. Enɛ tsɔɔ wɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bɔni afee ni ehe akahi ni ofite shika kɛhe nibii ni ejaaa ni akɛfeɔ nibii lɛ.

english: If I bring a sick plant sample from my farm to your office, how does that help you find a cure?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ekomɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ba o-ɔfis lɛ. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ebaatsɔ eye ebua bo ni ona tsabaa?

english: By examining the infected plant sample under proper testing conditions, extension officers can identify the exact pest or fungus causing the disease. Once identified, we can give you the precise medicine or farming practice to save the rest of your field.
ga: Kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli nɔkwɛmɔnii ni akwɛɔ yɛ kaa shihilɛi ni sa shishi lɛ nɔ. Extension nitsulɔi lɛ baanyɛ ana tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɛ hela baa. Kɛji ayɔse wɔ lɛ Wɔbaanyɛ wɔha bo tsofa loo okwaayeli gbɛi ni ja ni baaha oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ akafite.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost early in the season restores their green color and leads to bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii wuji aba.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often fall off due to stress caused by intense heat, improper watering, or lack of nutrients in the soil. Mulching the soil to keep it moist and applying the right fertilizer helps the flowers stay on and develop into peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ haomɔ ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. nu ni esaaa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Mulching koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What causes the leaves of my tomato plants to curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil spray or recommended treatments keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and cannot survive direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects the young cocoa from burning until they grow stronger roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli waa.

english: How do I know if my land is well-prepared before I plant my cassava cuttings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ asaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmei?

english: Good cassava land needs soft, loose soil that allows roots to spread easily without water logging. Forming high mounds or ridges breaks up hard soil, giving the cassava roots space to expand into thick tubers.
ga: Kasava shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni nu shwieee nɔ. Gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni afeɔ lɛ haa sũ ni wa lɛ gbálaa. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛfeɔ yitsei ni mli tse.

english: Why do heavy weeds in my farm make my yam tubers turn out small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your yam plants. Without full access to these resources, the yam plant lacks the energy needed to build big, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ o-yam tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ Sweet potato tsei lɛ hu náaa nibii nɛɛ ahe gbɛ kwraa lɛ, amɛnaŋ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: When soil stays completely waterlogged, crop roots cannot breathe, causing the plants to wilt and leaves to turn yellow even though the ground is wet. Digging drainage channels around your field allows excess water to flow away safely.
ga: Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa Tso lɛ shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ ni oootsi lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: What happens to my crops if I apply fertilizer when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can safely absorb it. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil in scorching sun causes the concentrated salts to burn the roots, damaging your crops instead of feeding them.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ. Kpatamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha amɛ niyenii.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during heavy rainfall, so the roots can absorb the nutrients before water washes them away from the field.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai dani nu afɔ amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy growth that often gets washed out of the soil by heavy rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa enɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and wither under full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that scorch easily in direct heat, which is why they need partial shade from larger trees during their early years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ tsei wuji adɛŋ yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What causes small green caterpillars to eat holes in my maize leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: These are usually Fall Armyworms, which hatch from moth eggs on the leaves and feed aggressively on soft plant tissue during cooler night hours.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ tso lɛ baai amli ŋmeii amli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ waa yɛ gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without making any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot or when the plant suffers from lack of water, which prevents successful pollination and fruit formation.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ naa.

english: Why does planting my crops too close together lower my total harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete against each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak plants that produce smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baa.

english: Covering the soil with organic mulch keeps the ground cool, prevents water from evaporating too quickly, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Organic mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground if I leave them too long past harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ fe nikpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Mature cassava roots continue to take in excess water from wet soil, which attracts fungi and bacteria that cause root rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi ni eda lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmɔɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and soil diseases that feed on that crop to build up over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help improve the soil for my other crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo kɛha mi tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my harvested maize cobs start rotting and developing mold when I keep them inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛ́ mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize cobs carry natural moisture when harvested. If stored in an enclosed room without proper sunlight and fresh air, the trapped moisture creates heat, causing mold to grow and ruining the grain.
ga: Abɛi ŋmeii lɛ mli fũuɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akpa. Kɛji akɛ akɛto tsu ko ni aŋã mli ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Fɛ̃i ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii daa ni efiteɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the cassava I dug up a few days ago is still safe to sell for people to eat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei ni mifo gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe lolo ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ aha mɛi?

english: Fresh cassava spoils quickly after harvest. If you cut it open and see dark blue or brown streaks through the white flesh, or if it smells sour, it has started decaying and is no longer good for consumption.
ga: Cassava ŋmɔŋ fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa. Kɛji akɛ afo mli lɛ, abaanyɛ ana bluu loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ kɛtsɔ loo yɛŋ lɛ nɔ. loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ebɔi fitemɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to harvest my vegetables right after spraying them with insect medicine?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makpa aduawai amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: No, chemical sprays leave harmful residues on crops. You must wait a specific number of days—called the waiting period—so the chemical breaks down fully, making the crop safe for human consumption.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shĩɔ nibii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awui. Esa akɛ omɛ gbii pii. (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mɛmɔ be) koni tsofai lɛ afite kwraa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesai niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits turn soft and turn black at the bottom while still hanging on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato aduawai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition, called blossom end rot, happens when the soil lacks enough calcium or when the plant does not get steady water while the tomatoes are growing.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa kɛji akɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa nu ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be beni tomato lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow very big in one section of my farm but stay thin and small in another section?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miida babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli lɛ? Shi loloolo lɛ, eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ bibioo yɛ hei krokomɛi.

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand smoothly. Hard or rocky soil restricts tuber growth, while rich, soft soil allows the roots to swell into large, heavy yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haaa tuber lɛ ada. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii agboi ni tsii.

english: What causes my plantain bunches to ripen and go soft too quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains lɛ shwereɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya tsɔ dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ?

english: Plantains naturally give off a ripening gas called ethylene. High heat, direct sunlight, or bruising during harvest speeds up this process, making the fruit ripen much faster.
ga: Plantains jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ. aloo ni ooona fãji yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ baaha nitsumɔ lɛ aya oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ shwereɔ oya kwraa.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing big leaves but failing to form tight, round heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitsei ni mli wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbage requires cool conditions and balanced soil nutrients to form tight heads. Excessive heat or too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages leaf growth instead of solid head formation.
ga: Kaabaji he miihia kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni sa koni ekɛfee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Dɔlɛ babaoo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baawo baai lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee yitsei ni wa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Why do my dried cowpea beans get filled with tiny holes after I store them in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas ni egbi lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? He fɛɛ he beni mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Tiny insects called bruchid weevils lay eggs on the beans. The young insects hatch and eat their way out from inside the dried beans, leaving tiny holes behind.
ga: Kooloo bibioo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ bruchid moth lɛ fɔɔ ewuo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Kplukai bibii fɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. kɛtsɔ bu bibioo ko ni eshiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my garden egg flowers drop off the plant before they can turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the plant is stressed by severe drought, excessive heat, or insect attacks like thrips that damage the flower stem before pollination occurs.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa kpe. hulutsoo ni fe nine loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa mɔ, tamɔ thrips, ni fiteɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi dani pollination baa.

english: Why does my harvested cassava stay hard when I boil it instead of becoming soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ mli wa kɛji akɛ ahoo lɛ moŋ fe ni eeefee blɛoo lɛ?

english: Cassava can stay hard after cooking if it is harvested too early or too late, or if it suffered from water stress during growth. Harvesting at the right time (usually between 9 to 12 months) and maintaining good soil moisture helps roots cook until soft and tender.
ga: Cassava baanyɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ beni ahoo lɛ sɛɛ kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ mra tsɔ loo sɛɛ tsɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ enine shɛ nu nɔ haomɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ Nikpamɔ yɛ be ni sa mli (bei pii lɛ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ) kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛyashi amɛbaafee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I know for sure that my cassava is fully ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: You can tell cassava is ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack. You can also dig up one test plant to inspect the size and starchiness of the tubers before harvesting the whole farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ kaa tso kome hu atsu nii ni okwɛ bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ dara ha kɛ bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ ha dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Which cassava variety should I plant if I want tubers that cook quickly for eating instead of industrial processing?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmãa srɔtoi esa akɛ makwɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni maye ŋmãa ni shwereɔ oya moŋ fe ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ nitsumɔhei?

english: You should ask for improved 'sweet' cassava varieties from agricultural officers. These varieties have lower cyanide levels and high starch quality, allowing them to soften rapidly when boiled compared to high-starch varieties bred mainly for gari or starch processing.
ga: Esa akɛ obi ŋmãa henɔi ni ŋɔɔ ni atsake lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ adɛŋ. Nɛkɛ srɔtoi nɛɛ yɛ cyanide ni baa shi kɛ starch ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa efeɔ blɛoo oya kɛ́ ahoo. Akɛ enɛ toɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni afɔɔ amɛ titri kɛha ŋmeii ahe nitsumɔ loo nitsumɔ he lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots turn dark and spoil just a couple of days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli beni atsa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot quickly because once cut from the plant, oxygen enters the root and triggers rapid chemical breakdown. To keep them fresh longer, keep a short piece of stem attached to the root, avoid bruising them during harvest, or submerge clean roots in water or moist sawdust.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya ejaakɛ kɛ́ afo amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli pɛ lɛ, Oxygen boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa tsofai lɛ fiteɔ oya. Bɔni afee ni ehi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ Ha tso kuku lɛ akpɛtɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okapila amɛ yɛ nikpamɔ be mli. Aloo okɛ shishifãi ni he tse awo nu loo ŋmei ni mli efɔ mli.

english: What causes my cassava flour or gari to have a bitter taste, and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava ashikiŋsha loo gari lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ aaatsɔ atsĩ naa?

english: Bitterness comes from natural compounds called cyanogenic glucosides found in cassava. Soaking, fermenting, and properly pressing out the water from grated cassava before roasting or drying breaks down these compounds and removes the bitter taste safely.
ga: Nɔ ni haa ŋmɔlɔ lɛ jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ cyanogen glucosides ni anaa yɛ ŋmei mli lɛ mli. Akɛ ŋmei ni atsɔ mli lɛ woɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni ajieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ mli dani ashãa loo agbiɔ. Ebaagbala nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ amli ni ejie ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing lots of tall leaves but giving me very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa shi eshishifãi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ?

english: Excessive leaf growth with small roots happens when soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus. Balanced fertilization and loose, well-drained soil encourage the plant to send its energy down into expanding roots rather than stems.
ga: Baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine ni shishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo ni potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni ja kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ yaa shishifãi ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifã lɛ shishi.

english: Why is my cassava yield getting smaller every year even though I have farmed cassava on this same land for 25 years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mifeɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi lɛ? Ni mikɛ afii 25 edu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava continuously on the same land removes essential soil nutrients without giving the land time to recover. Rotating cassava with leguminous crops like cowpeas or applying organic manure restores nutrients to boost your yields again.
ga: Kasava ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa loo okɛ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ shikome ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Underground root rot is usually caused by waterlogged soil or fungal infections during heavy rains. Planting cassava on mounds or ridges in well-drained soil prevents water from standing around the roots and rotting them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa mɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa ni eha amɛgboi.

english: What is the best way to cut and plant cassava stems so they sprout strongly?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ ŋmei tsei ni aduɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Cut stems into 20–25 cm lengths from the middle, mature part of healthy plants. Plant them slanted at a 45-degree angle with the buds pointing upwards to ensure strong root development and quick sprouting.
ga: Kpãa tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fã ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛyashɛɔ 20–25 cm. Dumɔ yɛ 45 degree angle mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi koni shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ waa ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cassava plants curling, twisting, and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai bibii lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by small whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. Using disease-resistant stem varieties and removing infected young plants early stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔŋ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmei bibii loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ. Stem henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ akpa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. When nitrogen is low or washed away by rain, the plant cannot make enough green food (chlorophyll) to stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji nitrogen faaa loo nugbɔ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli (chlorophyll) ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha hewalɛnamɔ kpakpa.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi?

english: When the afternoon sun is very hot, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. The leaves droop to reduce their surface area in the sun to save water, and they usually bounce back once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Kɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi koni ekɛbu nu he. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?
