english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year without giving the ground time to recover. It also lets pests and diseases that feed on that specific crop build up in large numbers in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu akɛ kooloi kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of big green leaves but produce only tiny cassava roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miiya hiɛ waa nɛkɛ? Eyɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Shi eyɛ ŋmei shishifãi bibii. Yɛ shishi pɛ

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are shaded too much, the cassava puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leaves above ground instead of sending energy down to store in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tso lɛ ewo hulutsoo tsɔ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi ni ekɛto shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out suddenly, or when there are no insects around to shake and pollinate the blossoms. Without successful pollination or under extreme heat stress, the plant drops the flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ trukaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ he ni baakpokpo ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yeee omanye loo yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and getting tiny and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled, wrinkled pepper leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies are sucking juice from the underside of the leaves and spreading a virus that stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies he okadi. Amɛmiinu nu kɛmiijɛ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmiigbɛ helai ni tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the branch before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This blackening is called black pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, overly wet, and humid environments. It spreads quickly when cocoa trees are too crowded or shaded and rain bounces soil onto low pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ hela fɔŋ nɛɛ akɛ black pod hela. Fungi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ duŋ mli kɛ enɛ baa. Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ, ni ebaagbɛ eshwa oya kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ. Ni nugbɔ miinɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my maize stems fall over near the ground just as the corn starts forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ beni abele lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over (lodge) when root systems are weak or when stem borer insects eat away the inside of the lower stem, making the plant too weak to hold up the heavy corn ears against wind or rain.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi (ejeɔ kpo) kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo kɛ́ kooloi ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi ŋmãa toi ni tsii lɛ anaa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔshiimɔ he.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantain suckers beside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide canopy shade and moisture to shield the young cocoa seedlings during their critical first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is ready to be dug up from the ground without damaging the roots?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efiteee shishifãi lɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the plant reaches maturity age (usually 9–12 months depending on the variety), the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem starts to crack as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛji tso lɛ eda kwraa (bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9-12 ni damɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ). Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: How does clearing and leveling my land properly help my crops survive when the rains are low?
ga: Te mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Properly prepared and leveled land catches rainwater evenly and allows it to soak deep into the soil instead of running off, giving your crops a steady supply of moisture even during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ ni etse lɛ baamɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eha ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeejo foi. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ po.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and droop when my field gets flooded after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmɔji amli nu ho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water drowns the crop's roots by filling all the air spaces in the soil, which prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing essential soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ewoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Why do other farmers cover the ground around young crops with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi kɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi haa he ni tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the soil so it doesn't evaporate under the hot sun, keeps the soil cool, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that scorch easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates a protective cover that reduces heat and keeps the surrounding air humid.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ haa gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni haa dɔlɛ baa shi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I leave space between my maize plants instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small cobs. Giving them space allows each plant to get enough food to grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni ŋmeii lɛ hu yɛ bibii. He ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does clearing weeds early in the season help my crops grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your crops. Clearing them early ensures that all the soil nutrients go directly into growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ yaa odumɔi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are getting enough food from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy cassava plants have deep green leaves, thick stems, and steady growth. Small, pale, or yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is low in nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Kasava tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli diŋŋ, tsei ni mli wa, kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Baai bibii, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack the leaves of my maize right after the first heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-abɛi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The start of the rainy season creates warm, moist conditions that trigger pest eggs, like Fall Armyworms, to hatch quickly onto fresh green leaves. Checking your fields early helps you catch them before they spread.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo baa. Enɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ, fɔɔ oya yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ anɔ. Gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni omɔ lɛ dani egbɛ eshwa.

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests and diseases build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do seeds bought from an agriculture officer often produce better crops than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli he onukpai adɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai be fɛɛ be fe dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and tested to resist diseases, handle harsh weather better, and give uniform, higher yields compared to seeds saved from previous harvests.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana kɛji helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛhe. Enyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa he nii jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa ni nɔ kwɔ baa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know the right amount of water to mix with crop chemicals before spraying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nu ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ afutu mli dani mikɛshwie nɔ?

english: Mixing chemicals with too little water can burn your crop leaves, while using too much water weakens the mixture so it fails to kill pests. Always follow recommended mixing ratios or check with an extension officer so your crops stay healthy while being protected.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ fioo pɛ futu nu mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã. yɛ be mli ni nu babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛŋ egbe kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Nyiɛmɔ bɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ahaa lɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be. aloo bi mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ Koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni abu he

english: Why can buying unapproved chemicals at the market damage my cocoa crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ fiteɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Unapproved or fake chemicals often contain unknown, harsh ingredients that can scorch cocoa leaves, destroy delicate flowers, or leave harmful substances inside the beans that make them unsafe for sale.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ loo amalei lɛ amli nibii ni mli wa, ni aleee ni baanyɛ ashã kookoo baai lɛ yɛ mli. efiteɔ fɔfɔi ni waaa lɛ loo eshiɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni haaa ehi akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: How long should I wait after spraying pest chemicals before harvesting my crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie shi dani makpã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Crops need time to naturally absorb and break down chemicals after spraying. Waiting for the recommended period ensures the harvested food is clean and completely safe for human consumption.
ga: Be he miihia tsei koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛŋɔ tsofai lɛ ni amɛgbala mli beni afɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Be ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaamɛ lɛ haa niyenii ni akpa lɛ he tseɔ kwraa ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha adesa niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that lose moisture very quickly under hot direct sunlight. Without shade crops like plantains or shade trees acting as sun umbrellas, the intense heat scorches and kills the young plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ fiteɔ oya. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã ni ekpata tsei bibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before any pods start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they experience stress from drought, insect attacks, or poor soil nutrients, because the tree lacks the strength and resources to nourish young pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛ kɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ hɔmɔ, kooloi tutuamɔ, loo shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni faaa lɛ kpe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ nibii ni ekɛbaakwɛ ebii lɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow before the ears are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen in the soil. The plant takes whatever nutrients are left in its lower leaves and moves them up to feed new green leaves and growing ears.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ heɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ni ekɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni miida lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why does black pod disease spread so fast across my cocoa farm when heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Raindrops splash fungal spores from the soil and infected cocoa pods onto surrounding healthy pods. The moisture helps the fungal disease multiply quickly and spread from tree to tree.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ. Fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baa oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and small even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than regular crops and aggressively steal underground water, fertilizer, and sunlight, effectively starving your crops and stunting their growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei krokomɛi ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la waa. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ baa shi.

english: What happens to my cassava tubers if I plant the cuttings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsei ni afolɔ mli lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cassava cuttings are planted too close, their roots fight each other underground for space, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin, small roots instead of large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii, ni no haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ ŋmeii wuji najiaŋ.

english: Why do saved maize seeds from my last harvest produce smaller yields than fresh seed packets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwoɔ paketi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength and vigor in the next generation, producing weaker plants and smaller maize ears compared to certified seeds bought fresh each season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii baa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ ehee yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why are wild animals suddenly attacking my farm now, even though they left my crops alone during the first two years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi awuiyelɔi batutua miŋmɔ lɛ trukaa lɛ? Ni amɛshi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ pɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli?

english: Newly planted crops in their first one or two years generally do not attract animals because they are small and provide little food. As the crop grows and reaches three or four years, it matures, yields more food, and provides cover, which is when animals begin to take notice and visit the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei heei ni adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi kome loo afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbalaaa kooloi ejaakɛ amɛji bibii ni amɛhaa niyenii fioo. Kɛ tso lɛ da ni eye afii etɛ loo ejwɛ Ebaada. ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ wɔɔhe ni ji be ni kooloi srɔtoi je shishi amɛkadi ŋmɔ lɛ ni amɛsara.

english: Do farm animals and pests usually bother newly planted crops right away in their first year?
ga: Ani bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ mli kooloi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu ehee lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: No, when you plant a new crop, animals usually leave it alone for the first one or two years. It typically takes three to four years of crop growth before animals start becoming a real concern for the farmer.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ odu tso hee lɛ, kooloi sumɔɔ ni amɛshi lɛ pɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi loo afii enyɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani tsei lɛ daa dani kooloi jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ nɔ ni haoɔ okwaafoi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: How many years after planting a new crop should I expect animal pests to start invading my field?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni midu tso hee lɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baabɔi he ni miyɔɔ lɛ tutuamɔ?

english: For the first one or two years, animals rarely bother new crops. You should prepare for animal pests around the third or fourth year, as that is when plants become mature enough to attract wildlife.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi loo afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ kooloi gbaaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei anaa. Esa akɛ osaa ohe koni okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai atsu nii yɛ afi ni ji etɛ loo ejwɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ agbala koo mli kooloi.

english: Is it normal for animal pest problems on a farm to increase as the crops get older?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe naagbai lɛ baaya hiɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Yes, it is very common. Animals usually ignore young crops during their first two years, but as the farm reaches three or four years of growth, animal visits increase because the crops offer more food and shelter.
ga: Hɛɛ, eji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ waa. Koolooi sumɔɔ ni amɛku amɛhiɛ amɛshwie ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Shi beni ŋmɔ lɛ edara afii etɛ loo ejwɛ lɛ, Koolooi asaramɔi hu tee hiɛ waa ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa niyenii kɛ wɔɔhe babaoo.

english: Why do animal pests wait until a farm is three or four years old before they start feeding on the crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔ ko yeɔ afii etɛ loo ejwɛ dani amɛjeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ayeli shishi lɛ?

english: In the first one or two years, young crops do not have enough foliage, fruit, or roots to serve as a strong food source for animals. By the third or fourth year, the crops have developed enough to attract animals looking for food.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi loo afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Young ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ baai, aduawai, loo shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha kooloi lɛ aná niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ afi ni ji etɛ loo ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, aduɔ nibii bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ agbala kooloi ni taoɔ niyenii lɛ.

english: Why didn't I see any bush animals on my farm during my first year of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mana tsei bibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the first year or two after planting, a farm does not yet provide the heavy cover or abundant harvest that bush animals look for. Animals usually start visiting only after three or four years when the farm is well established.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi loo afii enyɔ ni adu sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ Okwaafoi lɛ bɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa loo babaoo ni koo mli kooloi taoɔ lɛ lolo. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi jeɔ saramɔ shishi yɛ afii etɛ loo ejwɛ sɛɛ pɛ beni ato ŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are pests attacking my neighbor's four-year-old farm while my one-year-old farm right next to it is untouched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai miitutua mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ ni eye afii ejwɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔ ni eye afi kome ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ bɛ mli kwraa lɛ?

english: Animals prefer older farms because plants that are three or four years old offer actual food and security. Young farms in their first year or two do not offer enough food yet, so animals pass them by.
ga: Koolooi sumɔɔ ŋmɔji ni etsɛ ejaakɛ tsei ni eye afii etɛ loo ejwɛ lɛ haa niyenii diɛŋtsɛ kɛ shweshweeshwe shihilɛ. Gbɛjegbɛi bibii ni yɔɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afi loo afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, no hewɔ lɛ kooloi lɛ yaa amɛhiɛ.

english: If animals haven't disturbed my farm for the past two years, does that mean my location is naturally safe from pests?
ga: Eji kooloi gbaaa miŋmɔ lɛ naa yɛ afii enyɔ ni eho lɛ mli kulɛ. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: Not necessarily. Animals usually leave crops alone for the first one or two years simply because the plants are young. Your farm may still attract animals once the crops reach three or four years of age.
ga: Jeee nakai kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi shiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amɛkomekomei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi loo afii enyɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ tsei lɛ darako lolo kɛkɛ. Ekolɛ oŋmɔ lɛ baagbala kooloi lolo kɛji tsei lɛ eye afii etɛ loo ejwɛ pɛ.

english: When is the right time for me to start putting up fencing or traps against destructive animals on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋtayaa loo tsɔne ni akɛtswaa kooloi ni egboi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shishi?

english: While basic care is needed from day one, destructive animals usually do not bother crops in the first two years. You should have your fencing or pest protection ready before the farm reaches its third or fourth year when animals start coming.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ shishijee kwɛmɔ nɔ kɛjɛ gbi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ gbaaa ŋmɔshi nibii anaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooofee gbogbo loo nɔ ko ni akɛbaagbe kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe klalo dani ŋmɔ lɛ abote afi ni ji etɛ loo ejwɛ lɛ mli beni kooloi lɛ baashɛ lɛ.

english: Does planting a new crop reset animal pest problems on my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagba ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, starting a new crop often gives you a break from animal pests for one or two years. It usually takes three to four years for animals to start targeting the new plants again.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, tso hee ni ooobɔi nitsumɔ lɛ baaha oye ohe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe afi loo afii enyɔ. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani kooloi jeɔ tsei lɛ ahiɛ amɛshwieɔ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upwards like small cups during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in intense heat to reduce water loss. By folding their leaves, they shield themselves from direct sunlight and retain moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛbuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my yellow maize leaves turn purple when the plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ miitsɔ purple be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ fioo kwraa lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking phosphorus or the soil is too cold and wet for the roots to absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ tso lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ ni edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings burn and die if I clear all the big trees before planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ dani midu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight. They require shade trees or fast-growing nurse crops like plantains to shelter them while their roots and canopy develop.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: When maize is planted too densely, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin stems with small or empty ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa babaoo tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni toi bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cassava turning yellow while the leaves at the top stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop lower leaves when they lack nitrogen or water. The plant automatically moves available nutrients from older leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ kɛji nitrogen loo nu faaa. Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo lɛ amli koni eye ebua dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my garden eggs get soft, dark spots at the bottom of the fruit before they fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni mli tse lɛ? Yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi dani ŋmeii lɛ adara kwraa?

english: This issue, known as blossom end rot, is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually triggered by irregular watering where the soil dries out completely between rains.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off without producing fruit when temperatures get too high, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tsei Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa tsei lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers start rotting underground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam rot underground is usually caused by excessive water sitting in the soil due to poor drainage, or by soil pests like nematodes creating tiny wounds that let fungus enter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato fitemɔ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes ni feɔ pilamɔi bibii lɛ anɔ. ni haa ŋmei lɛ boteɔ mli

english: Why does maize saved from my last harvest produce smaller yields than seed bought in a sealed bag?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni jɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ kotokui ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high yield in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits, resulting in lower yields when replanted.
ga: Akwɛɔ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil has lost its power to grow good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ dɔŋŋ?

english: Exhausted soil shows signs such as crop leaves turning light yellow, stunted plant growth, water sitting on the soil surface for too long, or weeds outgrowing your crops easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baatsɔɔ okadii tamɔ tsei ahe baai ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. dwarf plant growth Nu yɛ ni eshwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Aloo ewaaa akɛ jwɛi lɛ baakwɛ̃ fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect their underground tubers from drying out. Once the rains return, the plant naturally grows fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baaná baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants developing small ragged holes and looking chewed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Mɛi ni etse ni etamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the foliage. Inspecting the central funnel of the plant early allows for timely pest control before yields are damaged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmãa baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ yɛ be ni sa mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas or beans together in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, legumes like cowpeas or beans fix nitrogen from the air into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer to feed the maize crop and improve overall soil fertility.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa niyenii mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall with many leaves but produce almost no flowers or fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eshwɛ fioo ni fɔfɔi loo aduawai ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages plants to focus all their energy on stems and leaves rather than fruit. A balanced blend of nutrients containing phosphorus and potassium promotes flowering and fruit production.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai lɛ. Niyenii ni mli wa ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli ni akɛfutuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai baa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Leaving too many young shoots, or suckers, forces them to compete with the main plant for food and water. Removing extra suckers directs energy into producing larger, heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii fe nine. Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tsei ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ashi akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Tsofɔi ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ yaa tsoi wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ afeemɔ mli.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when they are not pollinated by insects, or when the tree experiences water stress or nutritional deficiencies. Maintaining adequate shade and soil moisture helps flowers set into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii eshɛɛɛ amɛhe. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ naa nu he haomɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ aná hulutsoo ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does lifting my yam vines off the ground with wooden stakes actually help tubers grow bigger?
ga: Ani mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni mikɛ tso tsoɔ nɔ lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, staking keeps yam leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to make food. This extra food flows down to build larger, healthier yam tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking jieɔ sweet potato baa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Niyenii ni fata he nɛɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow back much faster than my crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly absorb water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing vital resources from your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛgbala nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop during the hottest part of the afternoon even if the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water through evaporation faster than the roots can draw it up, causing temporary wilting. As the air cools in the late afternoon, the leaves naturally bounce back.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ Baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cabbage seeds very close together in a seedbed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kaabii dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crowding plants forces them to fight for sunlight, air, and root space, leading to thin, weak seedlings. Proper spacing ensures each plant grows strong, full heads.
ga: Tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛwu amɛha hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ahe he. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa waa ni eyiɔ obɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning light green and yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛkwɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. A clear sign above ground is when the lower leaves of the plant naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem with leaves mostly at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ji be mli ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Tso lɛ yitso lɛ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni eyɛ baai babaoo yɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nutrients from the soil, but beans and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing the field for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks and small harvests compared to crops planted with proper spacing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ akɛto tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to cover the dry soil around our crops with dead leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle wɔŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dead plant material, called mulching, works like a blanket. It traps moisture in the ground so water doesn't dry up fast under the hot sun, keeps the roots cool, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu lɛ gĩii oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do my crops grow much stronger if I plant immediately after the first heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli wa waa kɛji akɛ midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first major rain washes down a high amount of natural nitrogen into the dry soil, giving seeds an extra nutrient boost and helping young roots grow deep before any short dry spells arrive.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen babaoo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa niyenii kpakpai krokomɛi. ni ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ dani hulutsoo be kuku ko baa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy that feeds the tuber underground. Raising the vines on sticks keeps the leaves in the sun and off the damp soil where fungal diseases can rot them.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Wein tso lɛ ni akwɛɔ yɛ tsei aniji anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ, ni amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ afite yɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the central funnel leaves of my young maize plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ cone baa lɛ mli

english: This is typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm that hide inside the central funnel of the plant. Spraying early with neem water or recommended treatments prevents them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Aloo, gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsaa lɛ baaye abua ni akafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering. When soil moisture goes from very dry to very wet, the plant cannot move calcium from the soil into the fruit properly, causing the bottom to turn black.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛbaa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli. Tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛya aduawai lɛ amli. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to intense sun. Without shade crops like plantains or shade trees to cover them, harsh sunlight burns their leaves and stunts their growth.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni fa babaoo baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: How does keeping permanent shade trees on my farm help my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni hiɔ shi daa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mikoo tsei lɛ?

english: Permanent shade trees shield mature cocoa from extreme heat, reduce wind damage, and keep the soil moist during long dry spells, helping trees stay productive for longer.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ buɔ kookoo ni eda lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, dark, soft, and well-draining so water does not sit on top, while containing plenty of rotted leaves that feed the root system.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ nu kɛ ehe kpaaa ŋwɛi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, baai ni fiteɔ babaoo yɛ ni haa shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ.

english: How does clearing weeds around the base of my cocoa trees help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with cocoa trees for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Clearing them ensures your cocoa gets all the food and water available.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ebaaha o-cocoa lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Pruning opens up the canopy so air and light can reach inside the tree, reducing humidity that causes diseases and allowing the tree to put energy into pod production.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la ashɛ tso lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni kɛ hela baa lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and dry up before they fully grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is usually black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in overly wet and shaded conditions. Keeping the farm clear of overgrown foliage helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ ni baai ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: What causes the small flowers on my cocoa trees to fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ bibii? Yɛ mi kookoo tso ni gbeeɔ shi ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Flowers fall off due to stress from drought, extreme heat, poor soil nutrition, or lack of tiny pollinating insects called midges.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ hɔmɔ mli baa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai. loo kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollin lɛ ni bɛ lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wilt and drop leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds carry very dry air that quickly strips water from plant leaves, while dry soil prevents young roots from pulling up replacement water.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi waa mli, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ, etsĩɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkajie nu ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield a lot of pods one year and very few the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli, ni afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: A heavy harvest drains the tree's stored food reserves. If the tree does not receive enough nutrients and water, it produces fewer pods the next year to recover.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni tsii haa tso lɛ niyenii ni eto lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baawo ŋmeii fioo yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli koni ekɛtsa ehe.

english: Why do my cocoa pods take longer to ripen during very rainy and cloudy months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛshwereɔ yɛ nugbɔ kɛ atatu nyɔji amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods rely on consistent sunlight and warm temperatures to mature; heavy cloud cover and constant rain slow down their natural ripening process.
ga: Cocoa pods biɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ be fɛɛ be dani ekwɛ̃. Atatu ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi.

english: What are capsids, and why are they damaging my cocoa leaves and pods?
ga: Mɛni ji kapsid? Ni mɛni hewɔ ofiteɔ mi-kookoo baai kɛ mi-pod lɛ?

english: Capsids (locally known as Akate) are small insects that feed on young cocoa shoots and pods. They pierce the plant tissue to suck sap, leaving toxic damage that causes shoots to dry up and black spots to form on pods, greatly reducing your harvest.
ga: Capsids (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ agates) ji kooloi bibii ni yeɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Amɛfoɔ tso mli fãji amli koni amɛnu nu lɛ. Eshiɔ nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ŋmeii diji baa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa nikpamɔ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why are the top leaves and young shoots of my cocoa trees drying up and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi bibii lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This dieback usually happens when capsid pests feed on the tender young branches. Their feeding cuts off the flow of nutrients and water, causing the tips of the branches to dry out as if burnt by sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbele nɛɛ baa kɛji akɛ capsid tsɛŋemɔ helai ye tsei niji bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Amɛ niyenii lɛ tsiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Ha niji lɛ anaagbee lɛ agbi tamɔ nɔ ni hulu lɛ eshã amɛ.

english: Why do pests seem to attack my cocoa trees more when new leaves start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ beni baai heei jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pests like capsids prefer young, tender green shoots and leaves because they are soft and easy to feed on. When your trees produce fresh growth flushes, insects gather to feed on the fresh sap.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ baai ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ mlɛo. Beni otsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ, kooloi baabua amɛhe naa koni amɛye nu hee lɛ.

english: What causes small black, dry spots to form on my green cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii baa? Egbi yɛ mi-cocoa pod eŋɔli lɛ nɔ

english: These dark spots are feeding marks left by pests like capsids. When the bugs bite into young pods to suck juices, the skin dies in those spots, which can stunt pod growth or cause premature rotting.
ga: Nɛkɛ hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ nɛɛ ji okadii ni kooloi bibii, tamɔ capsids, shĩɔ, kɛ́ kooloi bibii ŋmɔ ŋmeii bibii koni amɛnu nu lɛ. Hewolo lɛ baagbo yɛ nakai be lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ pod lɛ dalɛ naa loo ekɛ fitemɔ aba oya.

english: How do I know if a pest control chemical like Akate Global is safe to spray on my cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Akate Global lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ mi-kokoo lɛ nɔ?

english: Approved cocoa chemicals are scientifically tested by agricultural authorities to ensure they target dangerous pests without killing beneficial insects, harming the tree, or damaging the cocoa beans.
ga: Okwaayeli nitsumɔhei eka tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kookoo mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ amɛkwɛ yɛ jeŋ nilee mli koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛtutua kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛgbeee kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, amɛyeee tsei awui loo amɛfiteee kookoo ŋmeii.

english: How does a pest spray actually protect my cocoa farm from insects?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ abu mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe?

english: Insecticides work by killing target pests on contact or when the pests attempt to eat sprayed leaves. This stops the bugs from reproducing and spreading across your farm, allowing healthy green leaves to grow back.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni akɛtaoɔ lɛ lɛ gbemɔ nɔ kɛji akɛ eshɛ he loo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ bɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eye baai ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi kooloi bibii lɛ anaa ni amɛkafɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. ni ehaa baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ daa ekoŋŋ

english: How can I tell if the spray I used against cocoa pests is working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cocoa pest spray lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: You will know it is working when fresh shoots start growing clear without dark, burned-looking spots, and you see fewer damaged pods and active insects on your trees.
ga: Obaale akɛ etsu nii beni tsei heei je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmeii diji ni tamɔ nɔ ni ehiii kɛjɛ la mli lɛ bɛ mli lɛ. Ni obaana pods kɛ kooloi bibii ni tsuɔ nii fioo yɛ otsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it important to buy pest chemicals endorsed by the Ghana Cocoa Board?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ahe tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni Ghana Cocoa Board lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ amɛji tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ?

english: The Ghana Cocoa Board tests chemicals to make sure they effectively kill local pests and do not leave dangerous chemical residue in your cocoa beans, protecting your income and bean quality for export.
ga: Ghana Cocoa Board lɛ kaa tsofai lɛ amɛkwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni eshiii tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ okɔɔŋtso lɛ mli. Buu oshika kɛ bean quality he kɛha maŋsɛɛ ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ.

english: How can I get government-supported pest control inputs for my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe saji ni nɔyeli lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ kɛha mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You can connect with your local extension officer or visit a recognized Cocoa Board distribution center, where approved crop protection materials are shared or recommended directly to farmers.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyana okpokpaa lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ lɛ. aloo yaa Cocoa Board lɛ mlijaa he ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ ni akɛ nibii ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ jaa loo ajieɔ yi ahaa okwaafoi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Can using the wrong spray on my cocoa trees affect the price I get for my beans?
ga: Ani tsofa ni ejaaa ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi-kookoo lɛ nɔ lɛ baaná jara ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ kookoo lɛ he lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, using unapproved or generic chemicals can leave harmful chemical residues or strange odors in the beans. This can cause international buyers to reject your harvest or lower the quality grade of your cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ loo ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashi tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo ŋmɔlɔi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ. yɛ kɔfi ŋmeii amli Enɛ baanyɛ aha majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ akpoo okpamɔ lɛ loo amɛba okɔɔŋtso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow after heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash away essential nutrients like nitrogen from the topsoil into deep water channels. Additionally, when soil becomes waterlogged, the roots cannot breathe to absorb nutrients, causing the leaves to lose their green color.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya nu gbɛi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli. Kɛfata he lɛ, kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu koni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. ni haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot when rainwater stands on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ta miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When rainwater collects on the land and cannot drain away quickly, it drowns the roots, causing fungal infections and rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nu lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eho oya lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Is natural rainwater better for my crops than pumping water from a local river?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ nu kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi fe nu ni mikɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli faa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater is naturally soft and absorbs small amounts of nitrogen from the air, which acts as a free boost for plants. River water can sometimes carry toxic chemicals from mining activities or thick mud that smothers small plant roots.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni haa tsei lɛ yeɔ ehe nɔ Bei komɛi lɛ, tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni jɛɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi amli loo sũ ni mli edɔ ni haa tsei bibii ashishifãi ahe lɛ baanyɛ ahi Faa mli nu lɛ mli.

english: Why are my vegetable leaves scorching and dying after I water them with river water near a mining area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ni bɛŋkɛ he ni atsuɔ shika tsuru lɛ yɛ lɛ ha amɛ lɛ?

english: Water sources contaminated by mining runoff often contain harsh chemicals and heavy metals. When crops absorb this polluted water, it damages their internal systems, causing the leaf edges to burn and dry out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni mli wa kɛ dade ni tsii yɔɔ nu jɛɛhei ni nu ni jɛɔ ŋtayaai amli lɛ efite lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei ŋɔ nu ni mli ewo muji nɛɛ, Ebaafite emli gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ shãa ni egbiɔ.

english: Why is the rich top layer of my farm soil washing away into the streams every time it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa faa lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: When soil is left bare without trees or cover crops, heavy raindrops hit the earth with force, loosening the dirt and sweeping the most fertile topsoil away into nearby water bodies.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ Nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ nii fe fɛɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu gbɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my land become hard like concrete after the rainy season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When soil lacks organic matter like decayed leaves or manure, heavy rains pack the dirt particles tightly together. Once the sun dries it out, the soil bakes hard, making it difficult for crop roots to spread.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ loo kooloi afɔfɔi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa muji bibii lɛ kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ hulu lɛ gbi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa ewaa kɛhaa tso shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the hot sun if I don't plant shade trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli kɛji miduuu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that cannot handle full sunlight or extreme heat. Shade plants act like umbrellas, shielding them from burning heat and preserving moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ atsu hulutsoo be fɛɛ loo latsaa ni naa wa he nii. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely high, heat stress damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing fertilization so the plant sheds its flowers to save energy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ Heat stress fiteɔ pollen ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Bɔni afee ni akɛ hewalɛ akafite lɛ, tsei gbalaa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ba lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with aggressive root systems naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to suck up water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei yɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni miida.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with very small ears when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ toi bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their leaves compete for sunlight and their roots fight for the same soil moisture and nutrients, leaving each plant with too little energy to produce large fruits or ears.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baawu koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa hewalɛ fioo tsɔ ni ekɛwoɔ yibii loo toi wuji.

english: Is the way I plant local maize the same method I should use for other maize varieties?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni mitsɔɔ nɔ miduɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa lɛ ji gbɛ ni esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ midu ŋmãa srɔtoi krokomɛi?

english: Yes, the basic planting process—such as seed depth, soil preparation, and general care—is the same for almost all maize varieties, whether local or introduced.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishijee dumɔ gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ dumɔwui lɛ amlibotemɔ, shikpɔŋ saamɔ kɛ kwɛmɔ fɛɛ fata he. Nakai eji yɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ ŋmãa srɔtoi fɛɛ he. Kɛji eji maŋ lɛ mli loo ajieɔ yi

english: Can I use the same planting steps for both white maize and yellow maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ dumɔ gbɛjianɔtoo kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛha ŋmãa yɛŋ kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, white and yellow maize have the exact same planting requirements, including planting depth, row setup, and watering needs.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa yɛŋ kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ yɛ taomɔ nii ni kɔɔ amɛdalɛ he lɛ nɔŋŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji dumɔwui lɛ amlibotemɔ, ŋwɛi ŋtayaai, kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ he hiamɔ nii.

english: How deep should I plant my maize seeds in the soil?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni eshɛ ha tɛŋŋ?

english: Maize seeds should generally be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep so they stay moist enough to germinate while remaining safe from birds and heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5 koni eha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkwɛ̃. Ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ okpoi kɛ dɔlɛ he.

english: How do I know if the maize seeds available in our market are local varieties?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ wɔjarayelihe lɛ ji maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa srɔtoi?

english: Local seeds are usually traditional varieties grown and saved by farmers in your community over generations, adapted specifically to your local soil and climate.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akutsoŋ dumɔwui ji kusum mli dumɔwui srɔtoi ni okwaafoi ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ edu ni amɛkwɛ nɔ kɛjɛ yinɔi babaoo mli. Amɛfee amɛhe pɔtɛɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Can I save and plant seeds directly from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ato ni madu?

english: Yes, planting seeds saved from your last harvest is standard practice for local maize varieties, though certified seed varieties may need to be bought fresh each season.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ adumɔ ji nifeemɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ kɛha maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa henɔi lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ ehe baahia ni ahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ehee yɛ be fɛɛ mli moŋ.

english: Why is local maize commonly recommended for planting in our community?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa yɛ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Local maize is well-suited to the local climate and soil conditions, and farmers can easily re-use seeds from their own harvest using familiar planting methods.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ni okwaafoi baanyɛ amɛkɛ dumɔwui ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkpa lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni amɛle ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛduɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I prepare my land differently depending on the variety of corn I want to grow?
ga: Ani esa akɛ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni misumɔɔ ni madu lɛ naa?

english: No, land preparation like clearing weeds and tilling the soil follows the same process regardless of which maize variety you decide to plant.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ he saamɔ tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ biɔ gbɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni ŋmãa srɔtoi ni okpɛɔ oyiŋ akɛ obaadu lɛ ji lɛ,.

english: Do different types of maize need different spacing between planting holes?
ga: Ani ŋmãa henɔ fɛɛ henɔ biɔ ni srɔtofeemɔ ahi ŋmãa bui ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Most maize varieties follow standard spacing rules, though checking specific variety recommendations helps prevent plants from crowding each other out.
ga: Abɛi babaoo nyiɛɔ gbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa henɔi pɔtɛɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ mlikwɛmɔ baaye abua ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ akabɔle amɛhe moŋ.

english: Does local maize need fertilizer just like high-yielding seed varieties?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ he miihia tamɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: While local maize can grow in native soil, applying proper fertilizer will still help increase your yield just as it does for other varieties.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ abaanyɛ adu maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ, shi kɛ akɛ ŋmãa ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ tamɔ ŋmãa srɔtoi krokomɛi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do extension officers encourage following standard planting steps for all maize fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ hewalɛ akɛ anyiɛ ŋmãa dumɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ sɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Standard planting steps ensure proper seed-to-soil contact and optimal spacing, giving every seed the best chance to sprout evenly regardless of the variety.
ga: Dumɔ gbɛjianɔtoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ lɛ haa dumɔwui kɛ sũ lɛ kpaa gbee jogbaŋŋ kɛ gbɛ ni sa. Enɛ haa dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu naa hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni ekɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ ekɔɔɔ he eko henɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Can I use a water pump machine to water my crops during the dry season, or should I just wait for the rain?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu pɔmp aha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli? Aloo esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Using a water pump machine to irrigate your crops during dry spells keeps plants alive and ensures you get at least a partial harvest, rather than risking total crop failure while waiting for unpredictable rains.
ga: Nu pɔmp ni okɛbaatsu nii ni okɛshwie oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa kɛ hoo lɛ, onine shɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni baafite lɛ amli be mli ni ooomɛ nugbɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ.

english: How often should I run a water pump on my vegetable farm when the rains stop?
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matswa nu pɔmp ni yɔɔ mi aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Most vegetables need light, consistent watering every 1 to 2 days during hot dry periods to keep the topsoil moist without flooding the roots.
ga: Aduawai babaoo biɔ ni afɔ amɛ nu daa gbi 1 kɛyashi 2 yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu akawo shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt during dry hot weather even when I give them a little water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu fioo moŋ?

english: In hot weather, surface water evaporates very quickly before reaching deep roots; crops need steady, deep watering early in the morning or late evening so moisture stays in the soil longer.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya waa dani eshɛɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe. Ehe miihia ni awo tsei lɛ nu ni mli kwɔ be fɛɛ be leebi loo gbɛkɛ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Will I harvest as much crop using pump irrigation in the dry season as I do during the main rainy season?
ga: Ani mikɛ nu pɔmp baakpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli tamɔ bɔ ni mifeɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry season pump irrigation might produce a slightly smaller harvest than a good rainy season, but it allows you to sell produce when market prices are highest due to low crop supply.
ga: Nu ni akɛ pɔmp shwieɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi fioo fe nugbɔshiimɔ be kpakpa mli. Shi ebaaye ebua bo ni ohɔ̃ɔ onibii lɛ be mli ni jara lɛ nɔ jara wa fe fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do farmers in places like Akomadan focus so much on growing tomatoes and vegetables all year round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ hei tamɔ Akomadan lɛ maa tomato kɛ aduawai adumɔ nɔ mi waa nɛkɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Farmers in Akomadan use continuous watering and soil management to grow vegetables year-round, taking advantage of steady market demand for fresh produce even during dry months.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Akomadan lɛ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ aduawai afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Ekɛ jarayeli nibii heei ni ataoɔ daa lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli po.

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly due to heat stress and a lack of water; keeping the soil consistently moist during dry spells helps the flowers stay on the plant and form healthy fruits.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji dɔlɛ haomɔ kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my crops if the rain delays for several weeks after I plant?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ otsii komɛi yɛ be mli ni midu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Delayed rains cause seeds to germinate poorly and young plants to stunt or dry up, which is why having an alternative water source or pump helps save your investment.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni nu jɛɛhe loo pɔmp ni oyɔɔ sɛɛfimɔ baanyɛ aha okɛ shika akafite yɛ oshika ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland is suitable for pump irrigation?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha pɔmpi ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ?

english: Suitable land for pump irrigation must be close to a reliable water source like a stream, river, or well, and should be relatively flat so water flows smoothly to all crops.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha pɔmpi ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ abɛŋkɛ he ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, tamɔ faa, faa loo ŋshɔ, ni esa akɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it difficult to get my harvested crops from the farm to the market when bad weather hits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaaná ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛya jara nɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: Unpaved farm roads easily become muddy or damaged during bad weather, making vehicle transport difficult and causing perishable crops like vegetables to spoil before reaching buyers.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli ni atswako amɛhe lɛ feɔ muji loo amɛfiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli. Enɛ haa tsɔne ni akɛyaa he fɛɛ he lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa. ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ oya, tamɔ aduawai lɛ fiteɔ dani eshɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: Who can I talk to in my district when my crops are dying and I do not know how to fix it?
ga: Namɔ manyɛ mikɛ lɛ awie yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ beni miŋmɔshi nibii miigboi ni mileee bɔ ni mafee masaa lɛ?

english: You can reach out to local agricultural extension officers or district officers who offer free guidance on crop diseases, proper watering methods, and best farming practices.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyana okpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ loo kpokpaa nɔkwɛlɔ ni baanyɛ aha bo ŋaa ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ tsei ahe helai ahe lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ ashwieɔ nu kɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ

english: Why are the green leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen fertilizer or getting soaked in waterlogged soil, which stops the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo amɛwo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the hot afternoon heat even when the ground is not completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko kwraa moŋ?

english: Under strong sunlight, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up, so they temporarily wilt to conserve moisture until the sun cools down.
ga: yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kukuoo ko kɛyashi hulu lɛ baaha ehe ajɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani amɛyibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when the weather becomes too hot, when watering is uneven, or when there are no bees around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii

english: What is eating small holes in my crop leaves during the night?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ?

english: Night-feeding insects like armyworm caterpillars hatch from eggs laid on the underside of leaves and feed on soft leaf tissue while hiding from the hot sun during the day.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli fãji be mli ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ gbi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains leave excess water trapped around roots, which suffocates the cassava tubers and lets soil fungi invade and rot the crop before harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛhaa amɛboteɔ mli ni amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: Why do my newly sprouted tomato seedlings suddenly collapse and die at the base of the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiigboi yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by damp soil fungi that attack delicate seedling stems at ground level when the soil stays too wet and lacks direct airflow.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni tutuaa dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lolo ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Why did my crops turn brown and die after I applied fertilizer directly around the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains strong salts that draw water out of green stems and delicate roots, burning the plant if placed too close to the main stem.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli lɛ yɔɔ mli. Ebaashã tso lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he tsɔ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts after harvesting maize from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii beni mikpa ŋmãa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, renewing the earth's fertility naturally for heavy feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jeŋ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ nibii ni akɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ kɛha kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my crops grow bigger yield when I leave clear space between each plant instead of planting many close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo beni mishiɔ gbɛ babaoo yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu tsei babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: Proper spacing gives every single plant its own share of sunlight, air, root space, and soil nutrients without fighting neighbor plants.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa enáa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehulu, kɔɔyɔɔ, eshishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awuu.

english: How do weeds actually slow down the growth of my main crops if I don't clear them?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ aha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji mijieee amɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal vital groundwater, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients away from your crops while harboring destructive field pests.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eji he ko ni ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so quickly if I leave the baskets sitting in the hot sun at the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi tsɛnsi lɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High temperatures speed up the ripening and internal breakdown of harvested tomatoes. When left in the direct sun, heat builds up inside the basket, causing the fruits to soften, lose water, and rot rapidly. Keeping harvested tomatoes under cool shade extends their freshness.
ga: He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ baaha tomato ni akpa lɛ akwɛ̃ oya. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ baabua ehe naa yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ blɛoo, nu sɛɛ foɔ, ni egboɔ oya. Tomato ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo.

english: What happens if I store my harvested maize in a hot shed without proper air flowing through it?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ mi-abele ni akpa lɛ to tsũ ko ni mli edɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli?

english: High temperatures combined with trapped air create a warm environment where mold and grain pests like weevils multiply quickly. Overheated maize will spoil, lose its market quality, and can become unsafe for consumption.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ fataa he lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli dɔɔ. he ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ oya lɛ Abele ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baafite. Efiteɔ jarayeli su ni ebaanyɛ efee nɔ ni bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha niyeli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn dark and spoil just a few days after I dig them out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ ni mikɛfo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots are very sensitive to heat and air exposure. High outdoor temperatures cause rapid internal breakdown and decay within 48 hours, so cassava must be kept cool or processed immediately after harvest.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he waa. Kponɔgbɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ kɛ mligbɛ fitemɔ baa oya yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ akwɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo atsu he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my stored yams rot faster when I leave them on the hot ground instead of placing them in a raised yam barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mishi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛaawo sweet potatoes ŋmɔ ko ni awó nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The bare ground absorbs and holds intense heat from the sun, which bakes the yams and creates warm conditions that promote rot. A raised yam barn allows cool air to circulate around the tubers, keeping them at a lower temperature and preventing spoilage.
ga: He ni agbele naa lɛ shwieɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ. Enɛ baaha sweet potato lɛ ashã ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni woɔ fitemɔ he hewalɛ aba. Sweet potato ŋmɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ bɔleɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe, ni ehaa amɛhe jɔɔ ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants roll up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In extreme heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. Curling and drooping is the plant's natural way of reducing the leaf area exposed to the hot sun to conserve water until temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Curling kɛ drooping ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛi ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbaa baa he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and dry during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and high heat. Without shade trees like plantains to protect them, the strong heat scorches the leaves and causes the young plant to dry out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni buɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my cucumber plants stop producing flowers when the weather becomes extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kukumba tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?
