english: Extreme heat causes severe stress, forcing the plant to use all its energy just to stay alive. When temperatures get too high, the plant drops its blossoms or stops flowering to prevent trying to grow fruit it cannot support.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa baa. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi loo ebaakpa fɔfɔi fɔmɔ koni ekɛtsi enaa koni ekabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo yibii ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ.

english: Why are white, dry spots appearing on the side of my sweet peppers facing the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni egbi jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-bell peppers lɛ afã ni kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ lɛ?

english: This is known as sunscald, which occurs when high temperatures and intense direct sunlight physically burn the crop's skin. Ensuring the plant has enough healthy leaf cover helps shade the fruit from heat damage.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ shãa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ hewolo lɛ shã. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni tso lɛ aná baai ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaabu aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why is it bad to harvest my leafy vegetables like spinach or garden egg leaves in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ abaakpa aduawai ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ spinach loo eggplant yɛ abɔɔ mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Vegetables harvested during the hottest time of day suffer heat shock and lose moisture instantly. Harvesting early in the morning when the crops are full of cool morning moisture keeps them crisp and fresh for much longer.
ga: Aduawai ni akpaa yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ naa hulutsoo trukaa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ leebi be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi kɛ leebi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi ehee ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does soil in my crop beds dry out and crack so quickly during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ midumɔ saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight and high temperatures cause water in the topsoil to evaporate rapidly. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) blocks the heat, keeping the soil cool and moist for the roots.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya. Mulching around Kɛ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ latsaa he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top ones are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen. When the plant does not get enough food from the soil, it steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ejuɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops dry up and die if I put chemical fertilizer right against the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fertilizers are concentrated mineral salts that draw moisture out of tender plant roots if touched directly, burning them. Placing fertilizer a few inches away from the stem allows the roots to safely drink dissolved nutrients from the damp soil.
ga: Fertilizers ji mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli ni eshãa amɛ kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo ko pɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nuɔ niyenii ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I plant them in a clear, open field without big plants around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that dry out quickly under direct, intense sunlight. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby to act as natural umbrellas until their root systems grow deep enough to survive harsh heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta Kɛyashi eshishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa.

english: How do I tell which direction to push a cassava stem cutting into the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni esa akɛ matsi ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds on the stem cutting and make sure they point upward toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down forces the new shoots to curve awkwardly to find light, which weakens the plant and reduces tuber growth.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei bibii lɛ. yɛ tsei ni afolɔ abɛŋkɛ kpaakpa lɛ anɔ Ni okwɛ koni amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Yucca tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa ŋmeii heei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ gbeyei nɔ kɛyaa la lɛ he. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aba shi.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground and give my yam vines long wooden sticks to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie he ko ni mikɛ niji kakadaji lɛ atsake lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread high in the air to capture maximum sunlight for making energy. If the vines crawl on the hot soil, they easily catch fungal diseases and cannot make enough food to produce large tubers underneath.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni enyɛ eŋɔ hulu la lɛ koni ená hewalɛ babaoo. Kɛji wain tsei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ewaaa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ yeɔ amɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji yɛ amɛshishi.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes dry or sterile, preventing the flowers from getting fertilized. Because the flower cannot form seeds, the plant sheds it to conserve water and energy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ mli egbi loo ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo fɔmɔ mli Enɛ ji akɛ fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui. Tsei jieɔ nu koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves around the roots of my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ashwie miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry plant materials, known as mulching, acts like a shield against the sun. It stops water in the soil from evaporating quickly, keeps the roots cool, and prevents hard crusts from forming on top of the earth.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ gãimlibii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmeii ni wa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding deep inside the central funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, commonly known as Fall Armyworms, prefer feeding on the soft, tender young leaves inside the leaf funnel. That central pocket protects them from harsh rain, burning sun, and natural predators while they eat.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni afɔɔ amɛ tsɛmɔ akɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Kotoku ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu ni tsoɔ waa, kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my harvests get smaller if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize pulls the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and leaves behind specific pests that survive in that ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores nitrogen to the soil and starves out soil-dwelling pests.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hiɔ shi yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ekomɛi. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ejie tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster after a rain than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native species naturally adapted to survive harsh local conditions and aggressively steal water and light. Cultivated farm crops have been bred for taste and yield rather than wild survival, making them slower to compete without human help.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni jɛ koo lɛ mli ni atsake lɛ koni ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli, ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu kɛ la. Akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ koni amɛná ŋmɔlɔ kɛ yibiiwoo moŋ fe ni amɛaahi shi yɛ koo lɛ mli. Enɛ haa akaŋshii ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo ni adesa yelikɛbuamɔ bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade during their first two years because direct sunlight scorches their young leaves. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides immediate shade and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ ashã. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground whenever we get heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them and cannot drain away. Planting cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain off, keeping the roots safe from rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden stakes to climb on instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ni akɛkwɔɔ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to catch direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking the vines holds the leaves up into the light and keeps them clean from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tseɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe tseɔ kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow starting from the tips during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which maize relies on to make green leaves and grow strong. Applying compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa aha ebaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce very small bunches even when the soil looks rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ?

english: When a plantain plant produces too many young shoots (suckers) at its base, those suckers steal nutrients from the main stem. Removing most suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures full-sized fruit bunches.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ. Nakai tsei lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha aduawai ni fa babaoo aba.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist through regular watering and mulching helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ fe nine loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to chew holes into the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide deep inside the funnel of young maize plants. Treating the center leaves early with recommended organic mixtures like dry sand/ash or approved spray prevents crop loss.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa tamɔ ŋã/ashwishwɛ ni egbi loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite.

english: Why does covering the soil with dry grass around my crops help them during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo he ni ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that stops water from evaporating in the sun, keeps plant roots cool, and decomposes into rich organic plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛhaa nu lɛ koni ekatsɔ hulutsoo be mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa

english: Can I grow medicinal plants like Neem or Moringa alongside my main crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsofa tsei tamɔ neem loo moringa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ masɛi?

english: Yes, planting trees like Moringa or Neem along farm edges provides shade, natural organic fertilizer from fallen leaves, and leaves that can naturally repel field pests without hurting food crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei tamɔ moringa loo neem ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba. Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛɔ baai ni egbee shi kɛ baai ni baanyɛ ashwie kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeee niyenii tsei lɛ awui.

english: How can I easily check if my farmland soil is healthy before I spend money planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani mafite shika kɛdu nii?

english: A simple way is to check the soil texture and color: dark, crumbly soil that holds together gently when squeezed but crumbles easily—and contains earthworms—indicates fertile soil ready for crops.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsɔɔ nɔ afeɔ enɛ ji ni akwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ su ha: shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ, ni egbɛ eshwa ni ekɛ ehe ebɔ he fioo. Kɛ́ ashɛre lɛ, ebaakumɔ oya. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse, ni esa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can cocoa crops be used for anything else besides making sweet chocolate?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ kookoo tso lɛ afee nɔ kroko fe tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ feemɔ?

english: Yes, cocoa is rich in antioxidants and healthy fats, which are processed into products like dark cocoa drinks, soaps, cosmetics, and health remedies.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛ fɔ ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fa babaoo yɛ kookoo mli. ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ nibii srɔtoi tamɔ kookoo ni mli edɔ ni anuɔ, samla, tsofai ni akɛsaa gbɔmɔtso he, kɛ tsofai ni haa mɔ he waa.

english: Why is there so much focus on processing our cocoa beans right here in Ghana instead of shipping them raw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ jwɛŋmɔ ema wɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe nitsumɔ nɔ yɛ Ghana biɛ moŋ fe ni akɛbaamaje amɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Processing cocoa locally converts raw beans into high-value products like cocoa butter and powder, which creates local jobs, keeps more profits in Ghana, and increases demand for farmers' crops.
ga: Akutsoŋ kookoo nitsumɔ tsakeɔ ŋmeii ni ahoko lɛ nibii ni jara wa waa tamɔ kookoo bɔta kɛ pauda. ni haa maŋ lɛ mli nitsumɔi baa Ha sɛɛnamɔ babaoo ahi Ghana mli ni okwaafoi aŋmɔshi nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ

english: How does local factory processing of crops benefit a small scale farmer like me?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli nitsumɔhei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi lɛ?

english: When crops are processed locally, it creates a steady local buyer market, reduces dependence on foreign prices, and allows farmers to easily access locally made crop products like organic cocoa waste fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atsu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli Ebaaha maŋ lɛ mli jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ aba. Akɛ hiɛnɔkamɔ ni yɔɔ maŋsɛɛ jara nɔ lɛ aba shi ni aha okwaafoi lɛ aná nibii ni aduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli tamɔ organic cocoa fertilizer.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting before my new cocoa trees start bearing pods?
ga: Kɛ́ midu migbe naa lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani kookoo tsei heei lɛ aje shishi amɛwo ŋmeii?

english: With modern hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana, trees usually begin producing pods within 2 to 3 years, compared to older varieties that took 4 to 5 years.
ga: Kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid cocoa henɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ Bei pii lɛ tsei jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni akɛtoɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 he kɛha cocoa henɔi ni eda lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed leaves during dry weather to save water; keeping permanent shade trees on your farm helps protect cocoa leaves from harsh sun and extreme heat.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to trim and prune my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or unproductive branches, allowing airflow and sunlight to reach the inner tree, which prevents diseases and helps the plant focus its energy on growing larger cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo ni wooo yibii lɛ ajieɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa mɔ nɔ, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I recognize if my cocoa crop is infected with the cocoa swollen shoot virus?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ etsɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ amli?

english: Infected trees show swollen branches or roots, red leaf veins, and misshapen pods; early removal of infected trees is necessary to stop the virus from spreading to healthy parts of your farm.
ga: Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ niji loo shishifãi ni efuu, baai lɛ amli fãji tsuji, kɛ ŋmeii ni efite lɛ kpo. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra Ehe miihia ni akpa helai ni baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: What kind of nutrients do my cocoa crops need to grow big, healthy pods?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiaa mi-kokoo tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa?

english: Cocoa plants need balanced soil with plenty of potassium and phosphorus, especially during pod formation, to help the beans inside grow full and healthy.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni ja ni potassium kɛ phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ be mli ni afee pods lɛ. Koni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why must I ferment my harvested cocoa beans under plantain leaves before drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-cocoa yibii ni mikpa lɛ woɔ plantain baai ashishi dani mikɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fermentation kills the bean seed inside, removes natural bitterness, and creates the rich chocolate flavor and dark color that buyers look for when buying quality cocoa.
ga: Fɛ̃i gbeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa tsokolate ni mli edɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ kɛ́ amɛheɔ kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Is it safe to clear all shade trees from my cocoa farm so my crops get maximum sunlight?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ majie tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Enɛ ji koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni manyɛ.

english: No, cocoa crops perform best under light shade because full sunlight can stress the trees, shorten their lifespan, and make them more vulnerable to drought and pests.
ga: Dabi, kookoo tsei tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. ehaa amɛwala be baa shi ni ehaa hɔmɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui waa.

english: Can I use the same cassava variety from my farm to make both gari and fufu?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ afee gari kɛ fufu fɛɛ?

english: No, different cassava varieties have different properties. Varieties meant for making gari usually have higher starch content and less moisture, while varieties for eating as boiled fufu need to be softer, less fibrous, and easier to pound.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei srɔtoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ nibii srɔtoi. Srɔtoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ kari lɛ fɔɔ starch ni fa babaoo yɛ mli, ni ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ srɔtoi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ ayeɔ akɛ fofu ni ahoo lɛ afee mlɛo fe tsutsu lɛ. Eyɛ fiber fioo. ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ aaatswa

english: Why do some cassava roots work better for making industrial starch than for home cooking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi komɛi hi kɛha nitsumɔhei amli ŋmei feemɔ fe ni akɛhooɔ nii yɛ shia lɛ?

english: Cassava varieties bred for industrial starch contain very high concentrations of starch and dry matter, whereas cooking varieties are selected for taste, texture, and quick cooking times.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni akwɛɔ koni akɛfee nitsumɔhei amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nibii ni egbi babaoo waa. yɛ be mli ni ahalaa cassava henɔi yɛ amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ, amɛhefɛo kɛ be ni akɛhooɔ oya lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does my cassava turn out too watery when I try to process it into gari?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ mli nu fa babaoo kɛ́ mibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni matsu he nii lɛ?

english: Different cassava varieties behave differently after harvest. If the cassava is too watery, you might be planting a cooking variety meant for pounding into fufu rather than a dry processing variety meant for gari.
ga: Cassava henɔi srɔtoi Amɛfeɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji ŋmei lɛ mli nu fa tsɔ Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni akɛfeɔ fufu. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeedu tsei ni egbi ni akɛtsuɔ nii ahaa Gary lɛ

english: Why do different cassava roots behave differently when cooked or processed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ kɛ́ ahoo amɛ loo atsu he nii lɛ?

english: Cassava roots contain varying amounts of starch, water, and fibers depending on the specific variety. These internal traits determine whether a tuber boils smoothly for fufu, ferments well for gari, or extracts efficiently for starch.
ga: Starch, nu, kɛ fiber srɔtoi yɛ cassava shishifãi amli. Edamɔ tso pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ Nɛkɛ mligbɛ sui nɛɛ tsɔɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ shãa jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa fufu, amɛshãa jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa gari, loo amɛjieɔ ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe to feed my farm animals the same crop varieties that my family eats?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maha kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii ni miweku lɛ yeɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: While animals can eat some human food crops, certain crop varieties are grown specifically for livestock because they provide better nutrients for animal growth or contain traits that make them unsuitable or unpalatable for human meals.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi baanyɛ aye adesai aniyenii moŋ. Shi aduɔ tsei komɛi pɔtɛɛ ahaa kooloi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa kooloi adalɛ. aloo eyɛ sui ni haa esaaa loo ehiii kɛha adesa niyenii.

english: Why are some crops planted specifically for livestock instead of human consumption?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ tsei komɛi pɔtɛɛ ahaa kooloi moŋ fe ni adesai yeɔ lɛ?

english: Certain crop varieties produce high leaf foliage or specific nutrient balances that farm animals need to build meat and milk, making them ideal for fodder rather than human cooking.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi woɔ baai kakadaji loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa ŋmɔ mli kooloi koni amɛkɛfee loo kɛ mliki yɛ mli. Enɛ haa ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi aniyenii fe adesai aniyenii.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer talks about 'modified' or improved crop varieties?
ga: Kɛji akɛ shweremɔ he nitsulɔi lɛ wie tsei srɔtoi ni ‘atsake’ loo ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe lɛ, Mɛni etsɔɔ?

english: Modified or improved varieties are crops that plant breeders have developed to have specific traits, such as growing faster, resisting diseases, giving higher yields, or fitting a specific market use like industrial processing.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni atsake loo afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji tsei ni tsei akwɛlɔi efee koni amɛná sui pɔtɛɛ komɛi tamɔ amɛdalɛ oya, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe, kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo. loo nɔ ni sa akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ jarayeli he pɔtɛɛ ko, tamɔ nitsumɔhei ni feɔ nibii

english: Will modified crop varieties grow differently from the traditional ones I usually plant?
ga: Ani tso henɔ ni atsake lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe shishijee tso ni mikwɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, improved varieties often grow faster, yield more tubers, or resist common pests better, but they might require specific management or be intended for direct supply to processors rather than traditional kitchen use.
ga: Hɛɛ, srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ lɛ fɔɔ daa oya. Ehaa ŋmeii babaoo baa loo enyɛɔ eshiɔ ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ Shi ekolɛ amɛbaabi nitsumɔ krɛdɛɛ ko loo afee koni akɛha mɛi ni feɔ nibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe bɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ blema beaŋ.

english: How do I decide which cassava variety to plant before clearing my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni esa akɛ madu dani majie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should choose based on your end goal. If you plan to sell to a processing factory, plant high-starch industrial varieties; if you want to sell in the local food market, choose varieties suited for gari or fufu.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala yɛ oti ni ma ohiɛ yɛ naagbee lɛ naa. Kɛji oto gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaahɔ̃ɔ oha nitsumɔhe ko ni feɔ nibii lɛ Dumɔ nitsumɔhei srɔtoi ni starch babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛji oosumɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli niyenii ajarayelihe lɛ Halamɔ henɔ ni sa Gari loo Fufu.

english: Can industrial starch cassava varieties also be sold in the local food market for meals?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ahɔɔ nitsumɔhei ni akɛ ŋmei fee lɛ mli ŋmei yɛ maŋ lɛ mli niyenii jarayelihe lɛ akɛ niyenii?

english: While you can sell them, industrial starch varieties may not cook well or taste good for traditional dishes like fufu, so local food buyers might reject them in favor of traditional cooking varieties.
ga: Kɛji obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ po Shi ekolɛ nitsumɔhei amli ŋmeii lɛ hoɔɔɔ nii jogbaŋŋ loo amɛhe ŋɔɔ yɛ blema niyenii tamɔ fufu mli, no hewɔ lɛ mɛi ni heɔ niyenii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ akpoo amɛ ni amɛye abua blema niyenii.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots coming from the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni jɛɔ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Plantains share nutrients from the soil through their root system. Leaving too many shoots (suckers) forces the main plant to compete for food and water, resulting in smaller bunches. Keeping only one main plant and one or two young shoots ensures bigger plantain yields.
ga: Tsei bibii jaa niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Suckers (shoots) babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ baaha tso titri lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei niji lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ okwɛ tso titri kome pɛ kɛ eshishifãi bibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha plantain lɛ awo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing tips on lower maize leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. As the maize grows fast, it moves nitrogen from older leaves to feed the new top leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛji ŋmãa miida oya Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose many of their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ baai babaoo fite yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry, windy weather as a natural defense mechanism to conserve water. With fewer leaves, the tree loses less moisture to the hot air, helping it survive until the rain returns.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Beni baai lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ baafite ŋmɔtɔ fioo kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam plants produce bigger tubers when I give them wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji beni mihaa amɛ tso ni amɛkwɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need sunshine to produce energy for underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward sunlight, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the plant to build larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ he. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni eye ebua tsei ni amɛwo sweet potatoes wuji.

english: Tomato flowers fall off, or 'drop,' when temperatures get too high or when plants experience erratic watering. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the blossom, preventing fruit development and causing the flower to dry up and drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ‘egbeeɔ shi’ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ ahaaa tsei lɛ nu yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. etsĩɔ aduawai lɛ anaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my plot make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with natural soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop season ends, that trapped nitrogen remains in the soil to nourish the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eya nɔ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the underside of young leaves, or by viruses transmitted by these insects. The feeding damages the leaf tissue, causing it to shrink and twist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Niyenii fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. ni haa egbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ

english: Why am I finding small caterpillars eating deep inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni miiye nii kɛmiiya mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer hiding inside the moist, soft central leaves (the funnel) of maize. This location protects them from direct sunlight and predators while they feed on the growing heart of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli efɔ (cones) lɛ amli. He nɛɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe beni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is mature and ready for harvesting when the tubers are under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants signal maturity when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, usually 9 to 12 months after planting. You can also gently dig near the base of one plant to inspect the size and firmness of the root tubers before full harvest.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ blɛoo hu atsu nii yɛ tso kome shishigbɛ koni okwɛ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ dara ha kɛ bɔ ni amɛhe wa ha dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ kwraa.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering bare soil with dry grass (mulching) acts as a protective shield against the scorching sun. It stops moisture from evaporating quickly out of the ground, keeps root zones cool, inhibits weeds, and breaks down over time to enrich the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) haa nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni efiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Fast-growing plantain trees act as natural umbrellas, providing shade, keeping the air cool, and holding moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand the heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai, ni amɛhaa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulutsoo lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves, especially starting from the lower part of the plant, usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants use to build healthy green leaves and grow tall.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, titri lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ hei lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛfeɔ baai ni wa, eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small even when the plants grow very tall with lots of leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ? He ni sweet potato tsei lɛ daa waa ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much leafy food or is planted too close to other crops, it puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of sending starch down to build big underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha ŋmei niyenii ni baa babaoo yɔɔ mli loo ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi tsɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu ŋmɔtɔ kɛba shi koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔi wuji.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight to make food. Keeping leaves off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and helps produce larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkafiteɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔi wuji baa.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the daytime weather gets too hot, when soil moisture changes suddenly from wet to very dry, or when tiny insects attack the flowers, stopping fruit from setting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli egbi waa lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi, ni no haa aduawai lɛ shwieee shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and making the plant stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni eha tso lɛ miikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies transmitting viral sicknesses to the plant, or by extreme heat stress during dry weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is enough soil in the farm for all of them?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni manyɛ makwɛ amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive thief plants that drink up the ground water, steal the soil nutrients, and block sunlight away from your main crops, leaving them weak and small.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔ tso ko ni yɔɔ basabasa ni nuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Ju niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni oha hulu la ni jɛ otsei titrii lɛ amli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔ ni efeɔ bibioo.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds after the first rain comes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu tsei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell that can dry out and kill new seeds. It is safer to wait until the rain falls consistently over a few days and the topsoil stays wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaya nɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer on my crops so it does not waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛkafite?

english: Fertilizer works best when crops are actively growing with developed roots and when the soil is slightly moist. Applying fertilizer on dry soil burns the roots, and applying it right before heavy rain washes it away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei miida jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshishifãi edara, kɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baashã shishifãi lɛ. Ni okɛwo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aho shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why does planting the same crop on the same piece of land every season make my harvest drop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows specific crop diseases and insects to live permanently in that field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe helai kɛ kooloi komɛi hiɔ nakai he lɛ daa

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees drying up and turning brown during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight and hot winds because their roots are shallow. They need plantain trees or shade trees planted nearby to shield them from the heat and keep the surrounding air cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Amɛmiitao dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛtsi dɔlɛ naa ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown dust in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest caterpillar that hides inside the growing tip (funnel) of the maize. Early treatment with recommended sprays or neem extract into the central funnel is needed to save the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ lɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli (channels) lɛ mli. Ebiɔ ni atsa lɛ mra. Kɛ spray loo neem mli nu ni akɛwoɔ centre cone lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus ko ni whiteflies bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi susuɔ akɛ eji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa lɛ adumɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed new growth, showing that it needs fertilizer like Urea or NPK.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK awo mli.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to sow my maize seeds after the first rain of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: One short rain is not enough because the heat below the surface will dry out and burn the seeds. You should wait until the rain wets the soil down to the depth of your hand before sowing.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kuku kome pɛ faaa ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛshã. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ nine mli dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why do I need to clear tall sticks to support my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ koni mikɛfi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking raises the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch full sunlight to make food for the growing tuber. It also prevents fungal diseases that easily spread on wet leaves lying on soil.
ga: Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni ekɛ hulu ni fa aha niyenii aha bulbs ni miida lɛ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ baai ni efɔ ni kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu naa.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Mulching around the roots with dry grass and keeping the soil moist helps hold the blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts under the ground are mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the main leaves start turning yellow and dry. You can pull up two sample plants and check if the insides of the pods have dark, brown veins rather than white, wet shells.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo beni baai titrii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ ogbala tsei enyɔ ni ji nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ nɔ ni okwɛ kɛji fãji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ amli. Yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli efɔ yɛŋ najiaŋ?

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant cowpea or beans in the same farm after my maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpea and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they naturally enrich the soil with nutrients that the next crop needs to grow well.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my tomato plants suddenly wilting and dying within days even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt or root rot fungi living in the wet soil that block water pipes inside the stem. Rotating your tomatoes with maize or cassava helps clean the soil of these hidden bacteria.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nɛkɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ ahe sũ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Look for the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, or carefully dig up one mound to check the size of the roots; cassava typically matures between 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Taomɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, loo ŋmɔ blɛoo ni okwɛ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ dara ha. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Can I leave cassava in the ground if I am not ready to sell or eat it right away?
ga: Kɛji efeee klalo akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ loo ayeɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Ani abaanyɛ ashɛrɛ ŋmei ashwie shikpɔŋ?

english: Yes, cassava can safely stay underground for several months after maturing as a form of natural storage, but leaving it past 18 months can make the roots woody and less suitable for eating.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ sɛɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛtoɔ. Shi kɛ́ ashi nɔ ni fe nyɔji 18 lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ afee tsei ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain trees turning yellow and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nutrients like potassium, or the plant is suffering from drought or a fungal disease. Adding animal manure or fertilizer around the base helps keep the leaves healthy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ potassium, loo akɛ tso lɛ miikpe hɔmɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baabɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ mli waa.

english: How can I prevent my yams from rotting in the ground before harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi sweet potatoes lɛ anaa koni ekafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa?

english: Yam rot is usually caused by water sitting around the tubers or pests in the soil. You can prevent this by building high mounds or ridges so rain drains away easily.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni damɔ amɛhe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato ni egbo baa. Tubers loo pests ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni oootswa koni nugbɔ lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli oya lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my plantain tree to snap and fall over before the fruit is ripe?
ga: Mɛni haa mi dumɔwui lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily because they have shallow roots that can be weakened by heavy wind or soil pests. Supporting heavy trees with bamboo poles helps hold them upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo sũ mli kooloi baanyɛ agbɔjɔ. Tsei ni tsii ni akɛ ŋmei tsei fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why do my yam plants need wooden stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch direct sunlight, which helps the plant create more energy to grow large, healthy tubers underground instead of letting leaves rot on damp soil.
ga: Staking Wo sweet potato baa lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ ohe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo baa koni ekɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha baai lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ,.

english: How many suckers should I leave around one plantain stem to get big bunches?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi ŋmeii enyiɛ koni maná ŋmeii agbo?

english: It is best to leave only two or three strong suckers per plantain stem. Leaving too many suckers forces the main plant to share food and water, which results in smaller bunches.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ plantain tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ehe bahia ni tso titri lɛ aja niyenii kɛ nu. ni haa niji bibii baa

english: Is it good practice to plant cassava and plantain together on the same plot?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmei kɛ plantain yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava and plantain together works well because plantains provide gentle shade while cassava roots draw food from deeper underground, as long as you give them enough space.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ he kome lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmei lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni mli jɔ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Shii abɔ ni obaaha lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Which way should I put cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, te esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: You should plant cassava cuttings with the growth buds pointing upward toward the sky, inserted either straight up or at a slant, so the shoots can grow above ground easily.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava niji lɛ adu ni cassava ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛtsɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo tsɔne ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: If I cannot visit my farm every day, how can I stop weeds from taking over my crops?
ga: Kɛji minyɛɛɛ maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dried leaves or grass, called mulching, blocks sunlight to weed seeds and keeps moisture in the soil while you are away.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ aha onibii ahe. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu lɛ naa kɛjɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli be mli ni obɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby protects young cocoa from harsh heat until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale green and yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the tip inward when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the primary nutrient crops need to build strong green leaves and grow tall.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha tsei lɛ miihao. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes in the ground for my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei awo shikpɔŋ kɛha mi sweet potato tsei lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight. Elevating the leaves on stakes keeps them off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and giving the plant maximum energy to build large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ tsei wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When maize seeds are planted too closely, the plants compete with each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. As a result, they grow thin and weak, producing tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛhe tsɔi ni amɛgbɔjɔ. ni kɛ cob bibioo loo efolo baa

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant too early, tender seeds will germinate and quickly dry up before consistent rains return to keep the soil moist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster than most cultivated crops and aggressively drink the water and eat the nutrients in your soil, effectively starving your main crop of what it needs to develop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ. ni okɛ hiɛdɔɔ anu nu ni oye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, otso titri lɛ hɔmɔ baaye lɛ koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my plants with dry grass or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or straw creates a protective layer that traps water in the ground, prevents weeds from popping up, and keeps crop roots cool under hot sun.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaje kpo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves drop off leaving a bare stem, and the top leaves begin to turn yellow. You can also carefully dig around one plant to check if the tuber size is suitable.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ gbee shi, ni eshi shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ. ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli hu. tso kome jogbaŋŋ koni ekwɛ kɛji yitso lɛ dalɛ sa loo esaaa

english: Holes in the center leaves of young maize are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the funnel of the plant during the day and feeding on tender leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ ehe ewoɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni eyeɔ tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified maize seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist common diseases, withstand drought, and produce much higher yields. Saved seeds lose their strength over generations, leading to weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do the seeds I bought from the agro-chemical shop have a bright pink or red powder on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihe yɛ agrochemical shwapo lɛ mli lɛ mli powda ni mli tse loo tsuru yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: That colorful powder is a protective chemical treatment applied to seeds to prevent soil insects, birds, and fungal diseases from destroying them before they can sprout.
ga: Powda ni yɔɔ sui srɔtoi lɛ ji tsofa ko ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe koni sũ mli kooloi bibii, okpoi, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How deep into the soil should I push my corn seeds when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Corn seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep. If planted too deep, the young shoot will exhaust its energy before reaching sunlight, and if planted too shallow, heat and birds will destroy it.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimita 3 kɛyashi 5. Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, Young shoots lɛ hewalɛ baaho dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. ni kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ Dɔlɛ kɛ okpoi baafite nine lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, often because heavy rains washed them away. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, bei pii lɛ, ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo amɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ daa ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating ragged holes into the leaves of my maize plants, and how do I protect them?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni elaaje ni yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛnaa?

english: Ragged holes are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central funnel of the plant. Applying recommended pest treatments early in the morning or evening when caterpillars feed will control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji ni ekumɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ niyenii lɛ, ebaaye amɛnɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to start planting my maize immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rainfall becomes consistent. The first rain is often followed by a dry spell, which can dry up the soil and kill newly sprouted seeds.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa. Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni efite dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why should I place chemical fertilizer a few centimeters away from the plant instead of right against the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimita fioo ko pɛ moŋ fe ni mabɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that can burn tender stems and roots if touched directly. Placing it a short distance away allows roots to absorb it safely through the soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã ŋmeii bibii kɛ shishifãi kɛji amɛkɛ amɛhe kpe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛtsɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do some of my harvested corn cobs have missing kernels and empty spaces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii kɛ he ko ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Missing kernels happen when severe dry weather or heat occurs during the flowering stage, preventing the tassels from successfully pollinating all the silk threads on the ear.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji hulutsoo loo latsaa ni naa wa ba yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ akafee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ toi lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my young maize make the crop stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-baby corn lɛ miiha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with young crops for light, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures all soil nourishment goes directly into your crop's growth.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Ekwɛɔ koni shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ aya ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why did my maize crops dry up and die after I sprayed weedkiller on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Not all weedkillers are safe for crops. Non-selective weedkillers kill all green plants, including maize, whereas selective weedkillers only destroy target weeds without harming the crop.
ga: Tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ baagbe tsei eŋɔli fɛɛ. Abele fata he. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa lɛ kpataaa jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ ahiɛ ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need to be pruned when cutting off branches feels like I am destroying the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ? Kɛ́ oofolɔ tso lɛ, enuɔ he tamɔ nɔ ni ofite tso lɛ.

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or overcrowded branches so the tree can direct its water and nutrients to growing healthy, high-quality pods instead of wasting energy on excess leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi, helai, loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii afee ŋmeii ni wa ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: What are those fast-growing shoots coming out near the root base of my cocoa trees, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ mafo mli?

english: Those shoots are called chupons or suckers. They drain water and plant food away from the main fruiting branches without producing good yields, so removing them helps the main tree stay strong.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ akɛ chupons loo suckers. Amɛshwieɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii yɛ he ko ni kɛ tsei niji titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai. No hewɔ lɛ, niji ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tso titri lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce so many flowers, but only a few of them turn into actual fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfeɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii.

english: Flowers must be pollinated by small insects carrying pollen from flower to flower before a fruit can form. If there are not enough pollinators around, unpollinated flowers simply dry up and drop off.
ga: Esa akɛ koolooi bibii ni hiɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ faaa lɛ faaa lɛ Fɔfɔi ni fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: What is hand pollination, and how does doing it help my crop produce more yield?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Hand pollination means using a small brush or tool to transfer pollen directly between flowers yourself. This guarantees that more flowers get fertilized and grow into healthy pods, especially when natural insects are scarce.
ga: Nine nɔ pollination tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ brɔsh loo dɛŋdade bibioo ko tsuɔ nii. Kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛ pollen lɛ aya fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ baaná fɔmɔ nii ni amɛbaadara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii faaa.

english: Are all the tiny insects crawling around my crop flowers harmful pests that I need to spray?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ yɛ mifɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ fɛɛ ji kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara ni ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofa ashwie nɔ?

english: No, many small insects like midges and bees are friendly pollinators. They carry pollen between flowers, which is necessary for your crops to set fruit and yield pods.
ga: Dabi, kooloi bibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ naanyobɔɔ mli. Amɛhiɛɔ pollen yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ he miihia koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii ni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal disease that thrives in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Opening up the tree canopy through pruning allows sunlight and air to dry the pods and stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ pods diji baa. Kɛ́ agbele tso lɛ shishi kɛtsɔ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my crop flowers drop off when the overhead tree canopy gets too thick and dark?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi beni ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ amɛyiteŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ duŋ lɛ?

english: Crops need a balanced amount of sunlight to make food for flower development. Excessively dark shade increases humidity and fungus risks while starving the flowers of the light needed to stay attached.
ga: Hulu la ni sa he miihia tsei koni amɛná niyenii kɛha fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ. Shade babaoo haa oshara ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he lɛ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ hɔmɔ ye La Fɔfɔ lɛ koni ehi shi.

english: How do weeds growing around the base of my crops prevent my pods from growing bigger?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mitso lɛ shishitoo lɛ aha mi ŋmeii lɛ akafee agbo?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crop's roots for groundwater, fertilizer, and soil nutrients, leaving your crop starved of the food it needs to build large, heavy pods.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ náaa niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are my crops growing smaller leaves and yielding less fruit after many years of farming the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ baa bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo beni mikɛ afii babaoo etsu nii yɛ he kome lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous farming drains essential nutrients from the soil over time. Without adding compost or organic fertilizer, the soil becomes too weak to support healthy crop growth and high yields.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee gbɔjɔmɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ adalɛ.

english: If land close to my farm has been heavily dug up for mining, why do my crops nearby start struggling to grow?
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni ajieɔ shika tsuru kɛjɛɔ mli babaoo kɛha shika tsuru ŋmɔ lɛ Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Heavy digging damages the natural underground water table and washes away healthy topsoil, leaving nearby land too dry and infertile for crop roots to absorb enough water and nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ babaoo baafite. ni efɔseɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa hei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I plant them in an open field without any tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that get burnt easily by strong sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees protects them from direct heat and keeps moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting at the tip often mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps the leaves turn deep green again so the plant can grow heavy maize cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmãa ni tsii.

english: Cassava drops leaves to save water when the weather gets dry and hot. It is not dead; it goes into a resting state to protect its underground tubers until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ. Egbooo, ebaaya hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli koni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo tsei kɛha sweet potato wain tsei koni makwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows the leaves to catch more sunlight and prevents soil-borne diseases from touching the leaves. More sunlight on the leaves helps the vine build larger, healthier yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ baashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Hulu la babaoo ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni ewoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium or irregular watering while the tomato is growing. Giving your plants steady water and adding calcium-rich lime or eggshell dust to the soil prevents the fruit bottoms from blackening.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni tomato lɛ miida lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ ni okɛ lime loo ŋshɔŋlooi ahe sũ ni calcium eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahe sũ lɛ naa koni ekafee ediŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight little balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bɔɔlu bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves. Sprays made from neem oil or soap water can help clear these pests so new leaves can open normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ saamɔ fee lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. koni baai heei lɛ agbele bɔ ni sa

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce flowers above the ground but the nuts grow under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shi ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After the yellow groundnut flower is pollinated, it sends out a long stalk called a peg. This peg bends downward and pushes itself into the soil, where the actual groundnut pod forms safely away from surface heat.
ga: Beni afee ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi ni ji yellow lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ, Ebaana tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg ni baajɛ mli aba. Nɛkɛ ŋmei nɛɛ baakoto shi ni ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. he ni bean pods lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ he ni kɛ dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ.

english: When too many shoots grow around the main stem, they steal food and water from the parent plant. Removing extra shoots—leaving only two or three—ensures the main stem gets enough nutrients to produce a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii komɛi miida yɛ tso wulu lɛ he tsɔ lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efee tsei niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrink during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet, humid shade. Trimming dense branches to let air and sunlight into the farm and removing infected pods helps keep the healthy pods safe.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shĩa mli hei ni efɔ, ni edɔ waa lɛ kɛbaa. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni pods ni mli wa lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it bad for me to water my cabbage crops during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli nu ni mikɛhaa cabbage tsei lɛ ehiii kɛhaaa mi lɛ?

english: Watering under hot afternoon heat causes most of the water to evaporate before roots can absorb it, and hot water drops on leaves can scorch them. Watering early in the morning allows plants to drink fully before the heat begins.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ shwane mli la ni tsoɔ lɛ tsu nii kɛshwie nu lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ nuɔ nu dani hulutsoo be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: If my farmland stays covered in water during the rainy season, can I still grow any crops on it?
ga: Kɛji mi okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ Ani manyɛ madu tsei yɛ nakai he lɛ?

english: Yes, water-loving crops like rice, taro (cocoyam), and sugarcane thrive in waterlogged soil. However, crops like maize and cassava will rot if their roots remain submerged in standing water for too long.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni sumɔɔ nu tamɔ ŋmãa, taro (kookoo) kɛ ŋmãa shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa baafite kɛji akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ wo nu ni damɔ shi mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Is low-lying, swampy land good for farming, or should I look for higher ground?
ga: Ani shikpɔji ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ hiɛ lɛ hi kɛha okwaayeli loo esa akɛ matao hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ?

english: Swampy land can be extremely fertile because rain washes rich organic matter into low areas. While it requires drainage work or water-tolerant crops in the wet season, it provides excellent moisture for growing crops during dry periods.
ga: Swamp hei lɛ baanyɛ afee hei ni baa nii waa ejaakɛ nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo lɛ amli kɛyaa hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ esa akɛ tsei ni tsɔɔ nu mli loo tsei ni nyɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi moŋ. Shi ehaa tsei ni miida lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do vegetables grow better near valley bottoms during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ shishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Valley bottoms naturally collect and store groundwater from surrounding hills. During the dry season when rain stops, this stored moisture stays in the soil, allowing vegetables to keep growing without dying from heat.
ga: Jɔɔ lɛ shishi lɛ buaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni jɛ gɔji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ amli lɛ anaa ni ekɛtoɔ. Yɛ fɛ̃i be mli beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ Nɛkɛ nu ni abua naa nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa aduawai kwɛ̃ɔ ni hulutsoo lɛ gbooo.

english: How do I know if the soil on my land holds too much water for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: If rainwater sits on top of the soil for several days without sinking in, or if walking on it leaves deep mud holes, the soil holds too much water. Maize needs well-drained soil so air can reach its roots.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni eboteee mli, Aloo kɛji onyiɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa sũ bu ni mli kwɔ baa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miihiɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia ŋmãa koni kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up the tiny air spaces in the soil, suffocating the plant's roots. When roots cannot breathe, they stop taking up plant nutrients from the ground, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu lɛ, ebaakpa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ namɔ Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Can I plant peppers and tomatoes on land that floods whenever heavy rain falls?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ nɔ?
