english: No, tomatoes and peppers are very sensitive to wet roots. Standing water causes root rot quickly and creates conditions for deadly soil bacteria to attack and wilt the plants.
ga: Dabi, tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nuɔ shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ ahe waa. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ oya ni ehaa shihilɛi baa koni sũ mli helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atutua tso lɛ ni eha egbo.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn soft and rotten in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays soaked in water for too long. Stagnant soil water cuts off oxygen to the tubers and attracts harmful soil fungi that break down and destroy the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa bulb lɛ mli lɛ, ni egbalaa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers build high dirt mounds before planting crops like cassava and yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi maa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔlɔ dani amɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei?

english: Building high mounds lifts the root system above standing water in wet fields. This protects the growing tubers from rotting while giving them loose, aerated soil to expand into large crops.
ga: Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyaa nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli edɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baabu bulbs ni miida lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwereɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: How do digging small channels or ditches across my field help my crops grow better?
ga: Gbɛ bibioo ko ni mifoɔ Aloo te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni nu ni tsɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Ditches create clear pathways for excess water to drain away from your crops' root zones. This prevents waterlogging during heavy downpours while keeping the soil underneath safely moist.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ ko feɔ gbɛ ni mli ka shi faŋŋ kɛhaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ejɛ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni nu akabote mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa be mli, yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli ewoɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: If wild grass decays under standing water on my land, does that make the soil rich for crops later?
ga: Kɛji koo mli jwɛi lɛ fite yɛ nu ni ekã shi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shishi Ani ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi kɛha sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, as grass rots in water, it breaks down into natural organic manure. Once you drain the excess water, this rotted plant material enriches the soil with nutrients that help future crops grow well.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, beni jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. Efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Beni okɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Tso nibii ni fiteɔ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii ni baaye abua tsei ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field without tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and heat, which scorches their leaves and dries out their roots. They require shade trees or fast-growing plantains around them to block strong sunlight and retain soil moisture until their root systems mature.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baadara.

english: Why do I need to push tall wooden stakes into the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ mawo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural vines that need plenty of sunlight to produce large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, allowing the leaves to trap sunlight efficiently while preventing leaves from rotting due to soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli wain tsei ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of the lower leaves on maize usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow strong, and when the soil runs out, the plant moves the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ. Ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ etee Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa shweremɔ hee mli.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikpa ŋmãa?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas can take nitrogen from the air and feed it back into the soil through their roots. Planting them restores soil fertility naturally for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark black and rot right on the branch during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and humid weather. Rainfall splashes the fungal spores onto the pods, and dense foliage keeps the pods wet, causing them to turn black and decay.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shihilɛi amli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Ni baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa etsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ.

english: This condition is Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies or by planting stems from infected plants. The virus damages the chlorophyll in the leaves, preventing the plant from making food and reducing tuber yield.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli ŋmeii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Virus lɛ fiteɔ klorofil ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii ni ehaa tuber yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark waste inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ ni eshiɔ ŋmãa diŋ ko yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The worm hides deep inside the leaf funnel of the maize plant during the day to feed on soft new leaves, leaving behind chewed leaves and sawdust-like waste.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Eshiɔ baai ni ashɛre kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off the plant without forming any tomatoes when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: High temperatures stress the tomato plant and cause the pollen inside the blossoms to become sterile. When flowers cannot be fertilized properly due to heat, the plant drops them to conserve water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni bɛ fɔmɔ kotoku. Beni fɔfɔi ko nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ yɛ latsaa hewɔ lɛ Tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why are my cassava tubers soft, smelly, and rotting inside the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo, amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains cause water to collect in the soil without draining, the roots get suffocated from lack of oxygen and are attacked by soil fungi, causing root rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu buaa ehe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa lɛ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over from the root when a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ eshishifãi amli oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that stay near the surface, especially if tiny soil pests like nematodes or root weevils have damaged them. Mound soil high around the base of the stem and support heavy bunches with wooden poles to prevent them from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fite amɛ. Okɛ muji lɛ ato ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛbɔle he. Akɛ tsei fiɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ tsei niji ni tsii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough room and food to grow strong stalks and produce big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under the harsh sun. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and protecting the soil moisture during the heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo ŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse. ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ hulutsoo be mli

english: How do I know if the first rain of the season is enough for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: One rain is not enough because the dry soil underneath is still warm and thirsty. Wait until you get a few strong rains that wet the ground deep enough so the germinating seeds do not dry out and die.
ga: Nugbɔ kome pɛ kɛkɛ faaa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni kumai miiye lɛ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa bɔ ni sa. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Does it matter which direction I turn my cassava stick when pushing it into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ ootsi ŋmei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmei lɛ atsɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down makes the plant waste energy and grow tiny roots. Always make sure the small leaf buds on the stem are pointing upward toward the sky before planting.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛɔ shishifãi bibii. Kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani odu

english: Covering the ground with dead leaves or grass acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and stops water from drying up fast in the sun, keeping your crops hydrated between rains.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaaa nu lɛ agbi oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly and look weak when weeds are growing near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ be mli ni jwɛi yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they steal the soil food, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds early allows your crops to consume all the food in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛjuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa onibii lɛ yeɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my growing maize turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, a key plant nutrient. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant pulls food from its older bottom leaves to feed the young green leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri lɛ Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni eda ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are tiny holes suddenly appearing in the middle of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu bibioo ko je kpo trukaa yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like fall armyworms eating the tender leaves. Checking your farm early lets you catch and treat them before they destroy the growing heart of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa bibii lɛ amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ amɛ ni otsaa amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Giving them steady water and partial shade during hot weather keeps the flowers on the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my maize is ready to be harvested from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the leaves wrapped around the cob turn dry and brown, and the grains become hard when pressed with your thumbnail. Leaving them too long in the field attracts insects and rot.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai ni bɔleɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ tsɔne bibioo ko nyɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oshi yɛ shia lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaagbala kooloi bibii kɛba ni ebaaha egbo.

english: Can I use slightly salty water from my deep well to irrigate my vegetable crop, or will it ruin them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni ŋmei yɔɔ mli fioo ni jɛ nu bu ko ni mli kwɔ mli lɛ awo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu? Aloo ebaakpata nakai tsei lɛ ahiɛ?

english: Most crops can still grow with mildly salty water if your soil drains water easily. While sensitive plants like peppers might grow a bit slower, rainfall during the wet season will help wash the excess salt deeper into the ground away from the roots.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo hu baanyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛ nu ni mli edɔ fioo kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ oya. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ adara blɛoo fioo moŋ, shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato leaves look burnt at the tips even though I water them every day from my borehole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã yɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi kɛjɛɔ nubu ko mli moŋ?

english: When underground water contains minerals or mild salts from deep rock layers, watering too frequently can cause salt to build up near the roots. This makes it hard for the plant to drink water, causing the leaf tips to dry out and look burnt.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli eyi kɛ minerals loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni jɛ tɛi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu shii abɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmei abua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaanu nu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã.

english: Which food crops in Ghana can handle water that has a bit of salt in it?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ atsu nu ni ŋmei fioo yɔɔ mli lɛ he nii?

english: Crops like coconut, oil palm, cassava, and certain cabbage varieties are quite tough and can tolerate mildly salty underground water better than sensitive crops like cocoa, beans, or pepper.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii, mu, ŋmeii kɛ kaabii komɛi wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli edɔ fioo lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ fe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ kookoo, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii.

english: How does water pulled from deep underground differ from rainwater for my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ nugbɔ nu ni akɛhaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he?

english: Rainwater is pure and soft, while water pulled from deep underground layers has passed through minerals and rocks. Deep water often contains extra minerals or mild salts that stay in the soil after the water dries.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tɛi kɛ tɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli nibii krokomɛi loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo fataa he. ni baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nu lɛ egbi sɛɛ.

english: How can I check if the water from my new well is hurting my crop soil over time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji nu ni jɛɔ mi-po hee lɛ mli lɛ miifite mitso lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Watch out for a thin white or grey crust forming on top of the soil after watering dries up, or check if the soil surface feels unusually hard and sticky. These are signs that salts or minerals from underground water are settling in the top layer.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. ni feɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nu lɛ egbi sɛɛ Aloo kwɛmɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nuɔ he akɛ ewa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii loo minerals ni jɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli lɛ miiho yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow crooked and short instead of growing long into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kuku yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ kakadaŋŋ kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soil is made of different layers. If your field has a hard, gravelly, or rocky layer close to the surface, the yam tuber cannot push through it and is forced to bend or grow sideways.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ fãi srɔtoi. Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii ni wa, ŋmeii, loo tɛi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ Anyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ amli. ni anyɛɔ enɔ koni ekoto loo eda yɛ afã

english: Why do crops planted in low valley lands stay green during the dry season while those on hilltops dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ lɛ?

english: Valley lands sit closer to the natural underground water layer. As the surface soil dries, deep plant roots in lowlands can still reach the damp underground layers that hold water year-round.
ga: Shikpɔji ni yɔɔ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ he kpaakpa. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ Tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ yɛ hegbɛ lolo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋshɔ ni mli efɔ ni toɔ nu afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do mature cocoa trees survive dry spells while newly planted seedlings die so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui heei ni adu lɛ gboiɔ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings only have short roots stuck in the dry top layer of soil. Mature trees have developed long taproots that reach deep down into moist soil layers where water stays hidden.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi kakadaji ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni nu yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plow deeply before planting deep-rooted crops like cassava or sweet potatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani miduɔ tsei ni shishifãi mli kwɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei?

english: Plowing breaks up the compacted upper layers of the earth, making it easier for root crops to penetrate deeper layers where soil moisture is retained longer during hot days.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ akɛ amɛaabote ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do some of my crops wilt even when the soil surface looks wet after watering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ yɛ nu sɛɛ moŋ?

english: If water cannot soak past a heavy clay layer below the surface, it gets trapped around the roots. This chokes the roots of air, causing the plant to wilt even though there is plenty of water around it.
ga: Kɛji nu nyɛɛɛ abote shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ, no lɛ Nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ he fɛɛ he moŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow better when water drips slowly at their roots rather than being poured over the whole field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu hoɔ blɛoo kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofɔse yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water drips directly at the roots, the plant receives a steady supply of water right where it drinks, without losing water to evaporation in the hot sun. Keeping water off the leaves also prevents fungal diseases from spreading across your crop.
ga: Kɛ nu hoɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ Tso lɛ naa nu ni fa daa yɛ he ni enuɔ nu yɛ lɛ. Ni nu ni jɛɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ efooo. Nu lɛ ni oootsi kɛjɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa onibii fɛɛ amli.

english: Is underground water from a borehole safe and healthy for watering my vegetables during the dry season?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni jɛɔ nubui amli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni ehi kɛha aduawai ni akɛhaa amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Yes, borehole water is usually clean and excellent for crops during dry periods. However, in some areas, underground water contains high levels of minerals or salt, so it is good to watch if a white crust forms on your soil, which means the water needs to be mixed with rainwater or tested.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ nubui amli lɛ mli tse ni ehi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Shi kɛlɛ, yɛ hei komɛi lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ loo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi akɛ oookwɛ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ko ba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ nu lɛ afutu nugbɔ nu loo aka lɛ akwɛ.

english: How does using pipes to supply water directly to my farm change the way my crops grow compared to waiting for rain?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ paipii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni haa nu tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa lɛ kɛ akɛto nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he mɛmɔ he?

english: Piped water allows you to give your crops consistent moisture year-round. This prevents the plants from experiencing dry spells that stunt their growth, leading to faster maturity, higher yields, and the ability to harvest during off-seasons when market prices are higher.
ga: Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaná be ni hɔmɔ baa ni haaa eda lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ oya. Nibii ni anáa babaoo kɛ nyɛmɔ ni ayɔɔ ni akɛkpaa nii yɛ be mli ni jarayeli nibii jara wa lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and droop in the middle of the afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Under intense afternoon heat, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. Curling leaves is the plant's natural way of reducing its surface area exposed to the sun to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ shishi lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Leaf curling ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa ehiɛ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he.

english: Why do my crop flowers fall off without producing any fruits when the ground gets too dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ lɛ?

english: Flowering requires a lot of energy and water from the plant. When soil becomes very dry, the crop senses danger and sheds its flowers to save water and keep itself alive, which reduces your final harvest.
ga: Fɔfɔi biɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nuɔ oshara he ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha amɛhi wala mli. Enɛ baaha onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off when I give them plenty of water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛ nu babaoo ha lɛ daa gbi lɛ?

english: Too much water fills all the air spaces in the soil and starves the plant roots of oxygen. When roots drown, they rot and can no longer absorb plant food, causing the leaves to turn yellow and drop as if the plant were starving.
ga: Nu babaoo haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ bote nu mli lɛ Ebaagboi ni enyɛŋ eŋɔ tsei aniyenii dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi tamɔ nɔ ni hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ.

english: Why does the soil around my young crops turn hard like rock after I water it heavily with a hose?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ wa tamɔ tɛ beni mikɛ hose lɛ ewo nu babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy streams of water break down small soil particles and wash them together into a tight layer that hardens when the sun cooks it. Gentle watering methods, like drip pipes, protect soil structure so roots can easily push through and breathe.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ waa lɛ gbálaa sũ mli nibii bibii amli ni ekɛ amɛ feɔ ekome ni efeɔ sũ ni mli edɔ ni kɛ́ ahoo yɛ hulu la mli lɛ, ewaa. Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ afɔɔ nu blɛoo, tamɔ hoses ni hoɔ nu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ abote mli ni amɛmu mlɛo.

english: Will my maize produce bigger cobs if I water it heavily once a week or lightly every day?
ga: Ani mi-ŋmãa lɛ baawo toi wuji kɛji mikɛ nu shwie nɔ babaoo shikome yɛ otsi mli loo mikɛ nu shwie nɔ fioo daa gbi?

english: Crops prefer steady, moderate moisture rather than flooding followed by extreme dryness. Light, regular watering keeps the root zone consistently moist, helping the plant absorb soil nutrients smoothly without shocking the roots.
ga: Tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fioo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ po, moŋ fe nu ni shwieɔ shi ni ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa, daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhaaa amɛshishifãi lɛ afee shoo.

english: Why should I place dried grass around my crop stems when watering my field in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo he? Tsei ashishifãi kɛji oowo ŋmɔji amli nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like an umbrella over the soil. It blocks the harsh sun from evaporating the water you put in, keeping the soil cool and moist for your crop's roots much longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Etsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni okɛwo mli lɛ la. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How deep down does water need to soak in the soil for my crops to actually benefit from it?
ga: Te esa akɛ nu lɛ mli akwɔ tɛŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana he sɛɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Water needs to reach where the active feeding roots live, which is usually between 15 to 30 centimeters underground. If water only wets the top layer of dirt, the roots will stay near the surface and dry out quickly under the heat.
ga: Esa akɛ nu lɛ ayashɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji sɛntimita 15 kɛyashi 30 yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji nu shwieɔ muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ nɔ lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ la lɛ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to stay green and grow strong. This often happens in worn-out soil or after heavy rains wash nutrients away from the root area.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Amɛji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite nɔ loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are there small holes and dark brown dirt inside the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli.

english: This is caused by a pest called Fall Armyworm. The caterpillars hide in the center of the maize plant, eating the tender leaves and leaving behind their waste, which looks like small piles of wet dirt.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ. Ye baai bibii lɛ ni oshi jwɛi ni tamɔ muji bibioo ko ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and getting light green and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Your cassava likely has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is a plant sickness spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. It prevents the leaves from making food properly, which stops the tubers underground from growing large.
ga: Ekolɛ o-kasa lɛ yɛ kasa mosaic hela. Enɛ ji tso hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni ekahoo jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when planted under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like baby seedlings that cannot survive strong heat. Without shade trees or plantain plants to give them cover, the strong sun burns their soft leaves and dries out their roots before they can grow deep.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii tamɔ dumɔwui bibii ni nyɛɛɛ adamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baaha nɔ lɛ bɛ Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã ebaa bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and thin when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa beni midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to grow strong stems and healthy leaves.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni wa.

english: Why is it good to plant beans or groundnuts on my farm after I harvest my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops like beans and groundnuts take good air from the atmosphere and fix it into the soil as plant food. Planting them restores the natural nutrients that maize took away, making your soil rich again for the next season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa baa. Akɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii kɛha tsei. Dumɔ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni ŋmãa jieɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines produce larger tubers when I train them to grow up sticks or stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ bulbs wuji beni mitsɔseɔ lɛ koni eda ni etsɔ tso loo kolum lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tubers growing under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight and stay away from damp dirt diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni eshɛ amɛbaa lɛ he koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ helai ahe

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off without turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil switches suddenly from very dry to very wet. Sudden weather changes stress the plant, causing it to drop its blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli lɛ haoɔ tsei. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plant leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it up from the soil. The leaves temporarily droop to protect the plant from losing too much moisture, and they usually stand up straight again in the cool evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni tso lɛ akafite ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. ni bei pii lɛ, edamɔ shi jaŋŋ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling into cups and refusing to spread wide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni amɛkpoo akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã lɛ?

english: Curling in pepper leaves is often caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips hiding underneath the leaf. They drink the sap from the young leaf, causing it to twist, wrinkle, and stop normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛnuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ, ni no haa amɛtsiɔ amɛhe, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpaa amɛdalɛ ni sa.

english: How can I stop a crop sickness from spreading across my entire farm once it starts on a few plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsei ahe hela ko naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛji akɛ eshɛ tsei fioo komɛi pɛ ahe?

english: Crop diseases spread easily through wind, water droplets, farm tools, or infected soil. Removing and burning sick plants immediately, cleaning your farm tools, and planting disease-resistant crop varieties will stop the sickness from destroying your entire farm.
ga: Tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nu mli nui, kɛ okwaayeli nibii anɔ. loo shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ nɔ Jiemɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni oshã amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tsumɔ oŋmɔ mli nibii ahe ni odu tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ Ebaatsi hela naa koni ekafite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap and carrying plant viruses. Controlling these insects early using organic sprays like neem oil or recommended insecticides keeps the leaves healthy and open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛgbele.

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal sickness called Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet, shaded conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and air, along with removing infected pods early, protects the remaining cocoa.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Tso niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. Agbɛnɛ hu, jiemɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning light yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an important nutrient in the soil, or the ground is overly waterlogged. Applying compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli Aloo sũ lɛ mli nu fa tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant cassava on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific plant food from the soil and allows pests and sicknesses that target that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating cassava with legumes like cowpeas restores nutrients and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli niyenii komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and weak even if I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds act as aggressive thieves on your farm, stealing water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Dropping leaves is a cassava plant's natural self-defense against extreme heat and drought. By shedding leaves, the plant conserves water in its stems and roots to stay alive until the rain returns.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛtsɔ baai ni eshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu hiɔ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to plant stakes or tall sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ tso kakadaŋŋ loo tso nine koni mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can trap direct sunlight, which the plant uses to make food. When yam leaves get maximum sunlight, the plant produces much bigger tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ, ni tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛye niyenii. Be mli ni sweet potato baai lɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ baawo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni dara kwraa.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings burn and die when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have tender stems and shallow roots that dry out quickly under fierce sunlight. Providing temporary shade using plantain leaves or shade trees protects them until their root systems grow deeper.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni akɛ plantain baai loo hulutsoo tsei tsuɔ nii lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Why are insects damaging my harvested maize inside the storage room even when I harvested them clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi-ŋma ni mikpa yɛ nitoohe lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikpa lɛ ni ehe tse moŋ

english: Insects like grain weevils lay microscopic eggs on crops while they are still in the field, or they hide in uncleaned storage bags. Drying your grain thoroughly until it is completely hard and using airtight storage containers kills the pests and prevents damage.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. loo ni akɛteeɔ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni he tseee amli Dumɔwui lɛ ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa kɛ nibii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: How do I know when my cassava crops are fully mature and ready to be harvested from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell they are ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open as the tubers expand underground.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ amɛfee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay very thin and small even after spending a full year in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii waa yɛ be mli ni mikɛ afi ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Small tubers usually happen when the soil is too hard and compacted for roots to expand, or when the soil lacks potassium. Overcrowding plants or letting weeds compete for nutrients can also prevent cassava tubers from growing large.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bulb bibii baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe kɛyashɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã. aloo be mli ni potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi loo ni aŋmɛɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛye niyenii he akaŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara.

english: Why do some cassava tubers turn out very sticky and stretchy when cooked, while others turn out dry and crumbly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi komɛi wa ni amɛhe wa waa kɛji ahoo lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu egbi ni amɛhe ejɔ?

english: The stickiness comes from high starch content, which depends on the cassava variety, soil nutrients, and the age of the plant at harvest. Varieties bred for high starch produce a gummy, elastic texture, whereas mature table-eating varieties tend to boil dry and soft.
ga: Nɔ ni haa ewaa lɛ jɛɔ starch ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. ni damɔ ŋmei henɔi lɛ amli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ afii ni tsei lɛ eye beni akpaa lɛ nɔ Henɔi srɔtoi ni akwɛɔ koni ŋmei babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmei ni wa ni ehiɛɔ shi lɛ baa. Yɛ be mli ni ayeɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni eda lɛ yɛ okpɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ahooɔ amɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ bɔdɔɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava stems from any farm, or do different cassava types perform differently in the soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei tsei kɛjɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli, aloo ŋmei henɔi srɔtoi tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ?

english: Different cassava varieties have different qualities; some are bred specifically for high starch yields (good for processing into flour or starch), while others are softer for direct boiling. Choosing improved, disease-free stems from extension officers ensures better yield and field survival.
ga: Cassava henɔi srɔtoi yɛ sui srɔtoi Akwɛ henɔi komɛi pɔtɛɛ koni amɛha ŋmei ni fa babaoo aba. Ekomɛi yɛ bɔdɔɔ (ehi kɛha nitsumɔ ni akɛfeɔ ashikishaŋ loo ashikishaŋ), yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛha dãafeemɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ahala tsei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai bɛ mli kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi adɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha yibii kpakpai aba ni ehi shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava plant produce so many leafy stems on top but very few tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to put all their energy into growing tall stems and thick leaves instead of developing underground roots. Balanced fertilization with potassium encourages the plant to store energy in the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai ni mli tse. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, potassium ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: What happens to my cassava tubers if heavy rains cause water to sit on my farm for a long time?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Cassava roots cannot survive in waterlogged soil because standing water starves the roots of oxygen. If water sits on the farm for several days, the tubers will rot in the ground before you can harvest them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ naa lɛ. Kɛji nu tee nɔ ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo Bulbs lɛ baagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why do my freshly harvested cassava tubers start developing dark blue or black streaks inside after just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ bluu loo ediŋŋ yɛ mli yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots spoil quickly after harvest because exposure to air causes a natural chemical breakdown called post-harvest physiological deterioration. To prevent this, process tubers into starch, gari, or flour within 48 hours, or keep harvested roots covered in damp sand.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni fiteɔ ni ale lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ baa. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ enɛ naa lɛ, Ha ŋmeii lɛ afee ashikishaŋ, gari, loo ashikishaŋ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli, loo okɛ ŋã ni mli efɔ aha shishifãi ni akpa lɛ ahe.

english: Why is cassava starch so good for making stretchy doughs compared to maize flour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tapioca starch lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ feemɔ kɛ akɛto ŋmãa starch he lɛ?

english: Cassava starch contains carbohydrate molecules that bind strongly with hot water to create a smooth, flexible, and elastic gel. Maize flour has a different starch structure that breaks easily, producing a firmer and less stretchy paste.
ga: Tapioca starch lɛ ji carbohydrate molecules ni kɛ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ kpaa gbee waa koni efee gel ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nyɛɔ efoɔ, ni enyɛɔ efoɔ. Abɛi mli ŋmei yɛ ŋmei gbɛjianɔtoo sɔrɔto ko ni fiteɔ oya. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli waa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi.

english: Can I grow cassava together with maize on the same piece of land without them damaging each other?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛfiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, cassava and maize grow well together because maize matures quickly in about 3 months, while cassava grows slowly in its early stage. After harvesting the maize, the cassava takes over the field and gets full sunlight to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛkwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmei daa oya yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. Beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baaha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni ebaaná hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛyashi ebaakwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cassava plants curling up and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai bibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or by planting infected stem cuttings. Planting certified disease-resistant varieties prevents this disease from spreading.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ adu tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ hela lɛ ahe odaseyeli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela nɛɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, a major food crop plants need to grow. It can also happen when heavy rain leaves too much water in the soil, which prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni esa akɛ akwɛ̃ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shi nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant plantain trees alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees often fall over when the fruit bunch starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ yaa nɔ egbeeɔ shi beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that do not go deep into the ground. When a heavy bunch of plantains forms at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wind or the weight of the fruit to pull the root system out of the soil. Farmers use strong forked wooden poles to prop up the stem.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni plantains babaoo feɔ yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná muji yɛ eŋwɛi fã lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo tso yibii lɛ tsiimɔ baagbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okwaafoi kɛ tsei ni akɛ fɔji ni wa tsuɔ nii kɛfiɔ tsei lɛ akui lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why should I plant cassava using stem cuttings instead of using the seeds from the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ atsu nii yɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Stem cuttings grow much faster and produce an exact copy of a high-yielding mother plant. Planting true seeds takes a very long time to germinate, and the resulting tubers are often small and unpredictable in size and taste.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni afolɔ lɛ daa oya kwraa ni ewoɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ henɔi pɛpɛɛpɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, dumɔwui adumɔ heɔ be kakadaŋŋ waa dani ekwɛ̃ɔ. Ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ji bibii ni amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛhe ŋɔɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to erect tall wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the open air to catch plenty of sunlight, which the plant turns into energy to swell the tuber underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground, protecting the plant from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã he ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tso lɛ tsakeɔ enɛ efeɔ hewalɛ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper flowers usually drop when the plant experiences stress, such as extremely high heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why are the fresh leaves on my tomato plants curling up and crinkling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids that suck the sap out of young leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects. It can also happen when the weather is extremely hot and dry as the plant tries to conserve moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he lɛ.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition results in tall, thin, weak stems that easily fall over and yield very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni gbeeɔ shi oya ni amɛwoɔ tsei bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my main crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain after a dry period is often followed by several weeks of heat before the continuous rainy season starts. If seeds sprout right after the first rain, the young seedlings will wither and die from drought during the dry gap that follows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ, otsii babaoo mli latsaa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yaa nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagboi yɛ hɔmɔ mli yɛ hɔmɔ be ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why will the grafted mango tree seedling I bought bear fruit much faster than one I sprout from a mango seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso ni akɛwo mli ni mihe lɛ woɔ yibii oya kwraa fe mango tso ni mikɛ dumɔwui du lɛ?

english: A grafted tree uses a branch taken from a mature, fruit-bearing adult tree attached to a young root stem. Because the top part comes from an adult tree, it begins producing flowers and fruit in two to three years, whereas a seed must grow through a long juvenile phase of five to seven years.
ga: Tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛ niji ni ajie kɛjɛ tso ni eda ni woɔ yibii ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ shishifãi bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ jɛɔ tso ko ni eda mli. Ebaabɔi fɔfɔii ni ewo yibii yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ adara yɛ oblahiiaŋ ŋmɔnɔ be ni heɔ aaafee afii enumɔ kɛyashi kpawo lɛ mli.

english: Why do the foreign seeds I buy start giving smaller yields after a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Improved or hybrid seeds are bred for maximum performance in their first planting. If you continuously re-use seeds from those plants over multiple years, their genetic strength breaks down, causing crop yield and size to naturally decline.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ loo ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he lɛ koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kɛ okɛ nakai tsei lɛ amli dumɔwui tsu nii ekoŋŋ be fɛɛ be yɛ afii babaoo mli lɛ, Amɛfɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo kɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Can I save seeds from my current harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You can save traditional local seeds, but saving seeds from foreign hybrid crops usually results in weaker plants and smaller harvests because hybrid traits do not pass down strongly to the next generation.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ maŋ lɛ mli kusum dumɔwui lɛ ato he. Shi bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, akɛ sui ni ji hybrid lɛ haaa yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli waa.

english: Are local Ghanaian seed varieties better than foreign imported ones for long-term farming?
ga: Ani Ghana maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba kɛha be kakadaŋŋ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Local traditional crops are hardy and can be replanted for many years without losing their character, whereas foreign hybrids yield heavily in the early years but lose their quality and vigor after four or five years.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ wa ni abaanyɛ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ afii babaoo ni amɛhefɛo lɛ sɛɛ efooo. yɛ be mli ni maŋsɛɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsofa kroko lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Shi ehilɛ kɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ afii ejwɛ loo enumɔ sɛɛ.

english: How long can I keep harvesting from the same crop before I need to buy fresh planting material?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makpa nii kɛjɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli dani ehe baahia ni mahe nibii heei ni akɛduɔ nii?

english: Most high-yielding hybrid crops produce their best harvest for about three to five years. After this period, crop yield and quality drop significantly, meaning you need to replace them with fresh, certified planting material.
ga: Tsei ni akɛfee tsofa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ateŋ babaoo woɔ yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ aaafee afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa kɛ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ baa shi waa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ nibii heei ni akɛduɔ nii ni aŋmala he odaseyeli awo mli lɛ ato najiaŋ.

english: Why do some new crop varieties give huge fruits early on but smaller ones in later years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi heei komɛi woɔ yibii wuji mra shi amɛwoɔ yibii bibii yɛ sɛɛ mli afii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: New improved varieties put intense energy into early fruiting, which quickly uses up both the plant's reserves and the soil's nutrients. Without heavy feeding and eventual stock replacement, the fruit size drops as the plant ages.
ga: Henɔi heei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ heɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛha yibiiwoo mra. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ tsei ni ato kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii oya. Kɛji akɛ niyenii babaoo haaa kɛ naagbee lɛ, atsakeɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ dalɛ baa shi be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: How do I know when my farm's crop quality is starting to permanently decline?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ ebɔi fitemɔ kɛmiiya naanɔ?

english: You will notice smaller harvest weights, changing fruit shapes or colors, increased vulnerability to pests, and plants taking longer to recover after harvesting compared to their first few years.
ga: Obaayɔse akɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ faaa. Tsakemɔi ni baa aduawai lɛ ahe loo amɛhe su mli lɛ ha tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe oya Ni tsei lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ kɛ akɛto klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ahe.

english: What causes crop quality to reduce after four or five years on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ afii ejwɛ loo enumɔ sɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Quality drops due to a combination of seed degeneration in hybrid plants, essential soil nutrients getting used up by continuous harvesting, and pests or diseases building up in the soil over time.
ga: Nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi yɛ dumɔwui ni fiteɔ yɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa daa lɛ nɔ. kɛ kooloi loo helai ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I prevent my crops from losing their harvest quality as the years go by?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmaakpamɔ kpakpa yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: You can maintain strong harvests by practicing crop rotation, feeding the soil with manure or fertilizer, and replacing your main crop stock with fresh, high-quality seeds every few years.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ni okɛ dumɔwui heei ni hi jogbaŋŋ atsake onibii ni oduɔ lɛ daa afii fioo komɛi.

english: Does adding fertilizer fix crops that have lost their quality after five years?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii kwraa yɛ afii enumɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer improves soil nutrients and helps plants grow, but if the crop quality is dropping due to aged hybrid seed stock, fertilizer alone cannot restore the original genetic quality, and new plants will be needed.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ mlihilɛ ba shi yɛ dumɔwui ni etsɛ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ni abua naa lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ nyɛŋ aha shishijee fɔmɔ su lɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Ni ebaabi tsei heei.

english: Why do foreign seed suppliers tell farmers that crop quality will drop after a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui ahe nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ okwaafoi lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafite yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Suppliers inform farmers because hybrid crops are designed to produce heavily for a limited lifespan, so they want farmers to plan ahead to replace old stock and keep farm production high.
ga: Mɛi ni kɛ nibii baa lɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ leɔ ejaakɛ afee tsei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ wala be fioo mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmiisumɔ ni okwaafoi lɛ ato gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ koni amɛtsake ŋmɔ mli nibii ni etsɛ lɛ ni amɛha ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I cut down all the big shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mifo tso agbo ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat. High sunlight burns their young leaves and dries out soil moisture, so keeping shade trees protects them until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo be ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the stalk usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to stay green and healthy, so yellowing is a sign that the plant needs fertilizer or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, su ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my crop wither and dry up if I pour fertilizer directly against the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts. When placed right against the stem, it draws moisture out of the plant roots and burns them. You should always apply fertilizer in a ring a small distance away from the stem.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli ni eshãa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ring lɛ mli ni okɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo.

english: Why is it good for my soil to plant groundnuts or beans on the land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ akɛ madu shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients, but crops like groundnuts and beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them restores natural fertility to your land for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo, shi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in the fresh middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai heei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of maize plants. Catching them early and applying approved treatments prevents them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off instead of turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or insect damage. Keeping the soil regularly watered and healthy helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa ni ehi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yam leaves need sunlight to produce energy that builds big roots under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the earth so the leaves can catch maximum sunlight and produce larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa shishifãi wuji baa shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo ni amɛwo sweet potatoes wuji.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to plant for a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso ni hi fe fɛɛ ni madu koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Use the middle section of mature, disease-free cassava stems about the thickness of a human thumb. Avoid the soft green tops or very dry bottoms, as middle cuttings sprout the strongest leaves and roots.
ga: Kɛ ŋmei tso ni eda, ni hela bɛ mli ni mli wa tamɔ gbɔmɔ waŋshi lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ atsu nii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso nine ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baakwɛ baai kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa fe fɛɛ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetables with dry grass instead of leaving it bare?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables lɛ he lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, shields the soil from hot sunshine. This keeps the earth moist for longer, stops soil from washing away during heavy rain, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why is it dangerous to sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by many hot dry days before the regular rains start. If seeds sprout during this dry gap, the young plants will dry up and die from lack of moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli egbi lɛ amli Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate roots and thin leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby shelters the cocoa from intense heat and keeps moisture in the soil until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ tsei bibii, yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize is starving for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant leaf growth. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient deeper into the soil where young roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei ahe baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii nɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my land produce better yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This leaves natural fertilizer in the soil that feeds the maize plants and improves soil fertility.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stem cuttings upside down in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava buds naturally sprout upwards. If you plant the stem upside down, the shoots must bend around to reach the surface, which wastes the plant's energy and results in weak stems and very small tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ Esa akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ abɔle ehe koni eshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ hewalɛ afite. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yitsei bibii waa

english: Why should I prune away extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces them to compete with the main plantain tree for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree gets enough food to grow a large bunch.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ abɔi akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ŋmei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ ŋmei agbo.

english: What is causing small holes and sawdust-like droppings inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides in the growing center of the maize plant and eats the tender new leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off the plant before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, dry weather, or sudden water changes. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo nu mli tsakemɔi trukaa Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Lifting the vines with stakes helps the leaves catch as much sunlight as possible while keeping them off the hot, damp ground. More sunlight helps the leaves produce energy to grow larger underground yam tubers.
ga: Wein tso lɛ ni akɛ tso woɔ nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ ni ebɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool and moist by slowing down evaporation. It also stops weeds from growing and taking nutrients away from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni ejie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and stunted even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than most crops and aggressively steal nutrients and fertilizer from the soil. Even with plenty of rain, your crops become weak because the weeds are consuming their food supply.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii hu bɛ hewalɛ ejaakɛ jwɛi yeɔ amɛ niyenii jɛɛhe lɛ.

english: Why should I buy new certified maize seeds every year instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase daa afi lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je ngma kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ to.

english: Reusing saved seeds from hybrid varieties leads to weaker plants and much lower yields in the second generation. Buying certified seeds each season ensures uniform crop growth, better disease resistance, and maximum grain yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi kwraa yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ada daa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ helai nyɛɔ eshiɔ ni ehaa dumɔwui ni fa fe fɛɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient, or that heavy rains have waterlogged the soil. Applying fertilizer like NPK or urea at the right time restores their green color and keeps them growing fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewoɔ nu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Why are small caterpillars creating holes in my corn leaves early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miifee bu yɛ mi-abɛi lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the tender leaf whorls of young maize. Scouting your field early and spraying recommended control agents before they reach the plant's growing point protects your crop from severe damage.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ahe baai bibii. Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛbuɔ tso lɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ okɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ shi dani tso lɛ adalɛ ashɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ fitemɔ ni mli wa he.

english: Why do my corn stalks grow thin and fall over easily when I plant too many seeds together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo he kome lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing helps it develop thick, strong stalks and deep roots that resist wind damage.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eshishifãi lɛ mli tse, ni eyɛ hewalɛ, kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni teɔ shi woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why are the tips of my harvested corn cobs missing grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Incomplete grain filling happens when drought, heat, or poor soil fertility prevents proper pollination while the plant is flowering. Proper soil management and planting at the right time ensure all cob silks get pollinated.
ga: Dumɔwui ni eyimɔ eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa kɛji hɔmɔ, dɔlɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ ba. Enɛ haaa pollination ni sa aba be mli ni tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ dumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaha cob silkworms lɛ fɛɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough water for me to start planting my maize seeds after the early rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli shishijee lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up if the rain pauses. Wait until the rain moistens the soil at least hand-deep and consistent rainy days have settled in before sowing.
