ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kukuoo ko. Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛ hoo lɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni yaa nɔ daa, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why is it better to apply fertilizer to my corn in two stages rather than all at once when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ mli yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ lɛ hi fe ni mikɛwoɔ mli fɛɛ shikome beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Maize needs nutrients at different times—first to build leaves and roots, and later to form ears. Applying fertilizer in two split doses prevents heavy rains from washing all the nutrients away before the plant can use them.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia ŋmãa yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ji ni afee baai kɛ shishifãi. ni sɛɛ mli lɛ koni akɛfee toi Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: How do improved maize seed varieties survive dry spells better than traditional local seeds?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmãa dumɔwui ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe akutsoŋbii akusum dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Improved maize seeds are bred to grow deeper root systems quickly and flower earlier, allowing them to tap deep soil moisture and form grains before severe drought conditions destroy the crop.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ oya ni amɛwo fɔfɔi oya. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ egbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni ekɛ dumɔwui woɔ dani hɔmɔ ni naa wa fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young corn plants stop growing whenever weeds cover the farm floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ beni jwɛi ha ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than maize and steal sunlight, water, and fertilizer away from your crop's roots. Clearing weeds within the first four weeks gives your young corn the space and nutrients it needs to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmãa kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha obi lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why does my harvested corn rot or catch insects when I store it in sacks shortly after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ loo eyɛ kooloi amli kɛ́ mikɛwo kotokui amli beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested corn grains contain high moisture, which creates heat and invites mold and grain weevils. Drying your corn thoroughly in the sun until the grains are hard protects them during storage.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ baa ni efɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii nine. Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ abele lɛ he yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I plant them in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under intense heat. They need living shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or cassava to trap moisture and protect them from direct sun during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo yucca amli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi amɛhe ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantains on the same land where I am growing new cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko miikɛɛ mi akɛ midu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu kookoo hee nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce large, broad leaves that shade delicate young cocoa seedlings. They also provide food and income for your household while you wait for the cocoa trees to mature.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Amɛhaa oshiabii lɛ niyenii kɛ shika hu yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build leaves. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the new growth at the top, leaving the old bottom leaves starving.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Ha shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop season ends, those roots decay and release free nitrogen into the soil to feed your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nakai shishifãi lɛ baafite ni amɛjie nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot under the ground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Excess rain saturates the earth and removes air pockets, causing waterlogging that rots the tubers and allows fungi to attack the plant.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ ni ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui kɛjɛɔ mli. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa tso lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off without producing any pepper fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely hot or the soil gets dry, pepper plants drop their flowers to conserve water and energy. Keeping the soil moist around the base helps the plant retain its blooms.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the fruit bunches start growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ mli tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the top of the soil. As the heavy bunch matures, the plant becomes top-heavy and can be pulled over by gravity or wind unless supported with a sturdy wooden stake.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji akɛ kuu lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tsei lɛ hu tsii ni hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ agbala amɛ kɛba. ja tsei ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for the underground tubers. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground, exposing it to full light and reducing leaf fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Na la ni fa babaoo ni oha fungal helai ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ aba shi

english: Why shouldn't I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests and diseases multiply in the ground. Rotating crops starves out pests and balances soil health.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be fɛɛ be, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tightly and stop the plant from growing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that feed on leaf sap and spread viruses, or by severe heat stress. Protecting plants from early insect bites keeps the foliage healthy enough to bear fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe yɛ shishijee mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ ahe waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually indicates a nitrogen deficiency. The maize plant moves available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the younger top leaves and growing ears. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps keep the whole plant green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Abele tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baa bibii, ŋwɛi baa kɛ baai ni miida lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni otsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are small worms chewing holes inside the central leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the central funnel (whorl) of young maize. They eat the tender leaves, which weakens the plant's ability to capture sunlight and make food. Applying recommended treatments directly into the plant's center early on stops them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi (rings) lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni no haaa tso lɛ anyɛ emɔmɔ hulu la ni efee niyenii. Ni akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ baatsu nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ akafite onibii.

english: Why does my lowland rice yield much better when the field is flooded with standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai babaoo yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ?

english: Lowland rice thrives in standing water because water smothers competing weeds and makes nutrients in the soil easier for the roots to absorb. It also regulates soil temperature and prevents the root system from drying out during hot spells.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli ejaakɛ nu lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwereɔ oya. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ hu yaa hiɛ, ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ agbi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava plant have thick green leaves above ground but produces very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava focuses its energy on leaf growth instead of tuber development when the soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded too close together. Spacing your plants properly and avoiding excessive nitrogen lets the plant send energy downward to swell the roots.
ga: Cassava kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe tuber lɛ shweremɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ akudɔ hewalɛ kɛya shi koni eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do I need to erect tall stakes for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct sun exposure to manufacture food for the heavy underground tuber. Staking lifts the leaves into the air and sunlight, improves airflow to reduce fungal diseases, and results in much larger tubers at harvest time.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛba tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ shi. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown or black and rotting right on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, humid, and overly shady conditions. Pruning excess branches on your shade trees and harvesting ripe pods quickly lowers moisture in the canopy and prevents the rot from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ, ni mli edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ yɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni akpaa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa shi oya, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do some shoots on my plantain tree grow into strong plants while others remain weak and produce small bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ ekomɛi miida ni amɛmiitsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii komɛi bɛ hewalɛ lolo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: Plantain produces different types of shoots (suckers). 'Sword suckers' have narrow, blade-like leaves and strong roots that produce large bunches, while 'water suckers' have broad leaves early on and weak roots. Choosing only sword suckers for planting ensures healthy, heavy-bearing trees.
ga: Plantains woɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi (ŋmeii). ‘Sword shoot’ lɛ yɛ baai ni mli tseee ni tamɔ dade kɛ shishifãi ni wa ni feɔ panicles agboi, yɛ be mli ni ‘water shoot’ lɛ yɛ mra be mli baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ. Klante ŋmeii pɛ ni ahalaa koni akɛdu lɛ haa tso lɛ mli waa ni etsiiɔ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Providing consistent watering and mulching the base of the plant helps keep the soil cool and moist, encouraging flowers to stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Wo fɔfɔii lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ he ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upward and looking stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies, which can transmit viruses, or by physical stress like irregular watering and intense heat. Controlling sucking insects early and maintaining steady watering helps protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ashwã lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ nu ni akɛhaaa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa mli. Kplukai ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my groundnut plant drop thin stalks down into the ground after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiho eshishifãi bibii lɛ beni ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants flower above ground, but after pollination, they grow specialized stems called 'pegs' that push into the soil. The actual groundnut pods form and mature under the dirt, which is why loose, well-drained soil is necessary for pegs to enter easily.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ Amɛyɛ tsei krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bean pods lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ana shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni pins abote mli mlɛo lɛ.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant stem varieties helps keep your cassava healthy and green.
ga: Kasava lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela kɛbaa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Tso lɛ tso henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ eyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni o-cassava lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni efeɔ eŋɔli.

english: What causes dark black spots to spread rapidly across my cocoa pods after rain?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads easily in cool, wet weather. Pruning extra shade tree branches lets sunlight into your farm to dry the pods and prevent the fungus from growing.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ mli kɛbaa. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni oookpa lɛ haa hulu la boteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni eha ŋmeii lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Why is the base of my pepper plant's stem turning black and rotting right above the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is stem rot, which happens when the soil stays too wet and fungal diseases attack the root area. Raising your planting beds helps excess water drain away so the stems stay dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji stem rot hela. Enɛ baa mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lolo ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Dumɔhe lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Tso lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves bend downward and turn brown even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: This is often Fusarium wilt, a soil disease that blocks water from moving inside the stem. Removing infected plants completely and using clean plantain suckers prevents the disease from attacking your next crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fusarium wilt, ni ji hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni haaa nu aya tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ kwraa ni okɛ plantain tsei ni he tse tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ akatutua oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop all their flowers without growing any pods during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers during hot, dry spells to save water and survive heat stress. Providing shade trees like plantains or Gliricidia keeps the farm cool so the cocoa trees can retain their flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ, ni egbiɔ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains loo glicidia yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni cacao tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my orange trees shed most of their small green fruits before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ miiho eyibii bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ? Bei pii lɛ dani amɛba?

english: Citrus trees drop young fruits when they experience sudden water stress or pest attacks. Keeping the soil around the tree covered with mulch holds in moisture and stops the fruits from falling.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji amɛkɛ nu mli haomɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai kpe trukaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli, ni ebaatsi yibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why are my maize plants staying short with light green leaves even though I weed the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ baa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Light green and short maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nutrients like nitrogen. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer gives the plants the energy they need to grow tall and dark green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmãa kuku lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams grow small and twisted when the soil is hard or rocky, which blocks the tuber from expanding. Building soft, tall soil mounds gives the yam plenty of room to stretch downwards as it grows.
ga: Sweet potatoes bafeɔ bibii ni efiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo tɛi yɛ nɔ. ni tsiɔ tuber lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa. Gɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kɛlɛ ni afee lɛ haa sweet potato lɛ naa hegbɛ babaoo ni ekɛ ehe shwieɔ shi beni edaa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if caterpillars are hiding inside my maize plants before they eat the crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei lɛ amli dani amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Look closely at the center leaves for small ragged holes and sticky droppings that look like sawdust. Finding these early signs of Fall Armyworm allows you to apply treatments before the pest destroys the growing tip.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ jogbaŋŋ. Taomɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi ni tamɔ ŋmeii. Fall Armyworm he okadii ni tsɔɔ mra lɛ ni ooona lɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa dani tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ kpataa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Will planting cowpea together with my maize help or hurt my maize crop?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu lɛ baaye abua loo ebaaye mi-ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: Planting cowpea with maize helps your crop because cowpeas feed the soil with nitrogen, which maize loves. The cowpea leaves also cover the ground, keeping the soil moist and stopping weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ejaakɛ ŋmãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nitrogen, ni ŋmãa sumɔɔ waa lɛ. Cowpea baai lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo. Enɛ haa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the topsoil. Leaving a few tall trees or planting plantains beside young cocoa creates a canopy that protects them from harsh heat until they are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi tsei kakadaji fioo komɛi loo ooodu tsei bibii yɛ amɛmasɛi. Kɛyashi tso lɛ daa lɛ, cacao tso lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants as they start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi beni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up to catch sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground to prevent diseases and allows the plant to make enough food to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Atomɔ tso lɛ miikwɔ wain tso ko ni esa akɛ ewo ebaa nɔ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akabote mli. ni ehaa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulb agboi akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves turn green so the plant can produce full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli koni eha tso lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do people say that planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants harvest and decay, that nitrogen stays in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer, and feeds whatever crop you plant there next.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpa tsei ni amɛgboi Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebaaya nɔ ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni oduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: How can I stop the soil on my vegetable farm from drying out so fast during the hot sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dried grass or leaves—called mulching—blocks direct sunlight from reaching the soil. This traps moisture in the earth and keeps crop roots cool.
ga: He ni ebɔle ohe lɛ nɔ ni oooha Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi akpã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Ehaaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Which way should I point cassava stem cuttings when pushing them into the soil?
ga: Te esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei nine lɛ atsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava stems must be planted with the small buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots struggle to reach the surface, leading to weak plants and very poor tuber growth.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cassava tsei kɛ fɔfɔi bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji okɛ tsei shwie shi lɛ Tsobii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni tuberous lɛ hu daaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I allow all the small sucker shoots to keep growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha ŋmeii bibii lɛ akwɛ̃? shweremɔ ni bɔle Ani mi plantain tso titri lɛ?

english: No, you should cut away most suckers and leave only one or two strong ones. If too many suckers grow at once, they steal nutrients and water from the main stem, resulting in small plantain bunches.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be kome mli Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii.

english: What is making small ragged holes in the central leaves of my young maize crops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ?

english: These holes are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed deep inside the center whorl of young maize plants. Catching them early and applying organic sprays like neem leaf extract or recommended insecticides can save the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ahere ŋmɔshi nibii ayiwala.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat or a lack of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulched helps the plant hold onto its blooms so they can develop into fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni awo nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe koni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Is it safe to plant maize and cassava together on the same piece of land at the same time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, leaving the slow-growing cassava behind to use the remaining field space.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ ni eshiɔ yɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ atsu nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if the spray medicine I bought is damaging my crops instead of protecting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ shi ni mihe lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni eeebu amɛhe?

english: If your crop leaves show scorched edges, yellow spots, or twisted growth a few days after spraying, the chemical was likely applied at too strong a dose, sprayed in direct heat, or was the wrong chemical for that plant.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛi ni eshã Ayɛ ŋwɛigbɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo shweremɔ ni ejaaa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni afɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ekolɛ akɛ tsofai ni mli wa tsɔ tsu nii. Heat spraying tɛ̃ɛ Aloo eji tsofa ni ejaaa kɛha nakai tso lɛ?

english: Why does a weed-killing chemical destroy grass in my farm but leave my cassava unharmed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ miigbe jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shi migbeee mi-cassava lɛ?

english: Selective weed killers are made to attack only specific plant leaves like narrow grass leaves, while leaving broad-leaf crops like cassava safe because the crop can naturally break down the chemical inside itself.
ga: Afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahala koni akɛtutua tsei komɛi ahe baai pɛ, tamɔ jwɛi ŋmeii bibii, yɛ be mli ni ashiɔ tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ, tamɔ yucca lɛ, ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei baanyɛ akumɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: When soil lacks nitrogen, the corn plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up first.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen lɛ Abele tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni amɛkɛye ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with lush leaves, but the roots underneath stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or too much shade, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top stems and leaves instead of storing energy as starch in the tuber roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ shweremɔ mli yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, akɛ hewalɛ toɔ akɛ starch yɛ tuber shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look limp during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: On hot days, leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink from the soil. Curling up reduces the leaf area exposed to the hot sun, helping the plant hold onto moisture until the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛwo ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden heavy rainfall, which prevents proper pollination from occurring.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Enɛ haaa pollination aba.

english: Why do caterpillars hide deep inside the funnel of my young maize plants during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ atsɔnei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworm hide in the central funnel of the maize plant during the day to stay cool and protect themselves from birds, feeding on the tender inner leaves when night comes.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ okpoi ahe. Kɛtsɔ mligbɛ baai bibii lɛ ni ayeɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does black pod disease spread so fast across my cocoa trees when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ oya beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, humid shade. Raindrops bounce off the soil and splash fungal spores onto low-hanging cocoa pods, quickly spreading the disease.
ga: Fuŋs ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ kɛ pods diji baa. Nugbɔshiimɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ fungal spores shwieɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. ni ehaa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small yields when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight each other for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block each other from sunlight, resulting in weak, crowded plants.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛmli eyi.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants get scorched easily by the harsh tropical sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and have large leaves that provide quick shade and cool humidity, protecting the young cocoa trees until they are strong enough to survive on their own.
ga: Hulu ni naa wa waa lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa mra be mli hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees often fall over during strong rainstorms just when the fruit bunches grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli lɛ? Beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ tso agbo mli pɛ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Propping the main trunk with sturdy bamboo poles or branched wooden stakes gives the tree extra balance so high winds cannot pull it down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ kɛ ŋmei tso ni wa loo tso ni akɛ niji yɔɔ mli lɛ to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná shiŋŋ babaoo. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akagbala tsei lɛ kɛba shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of tiny holes and covered in greenish powder inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni powda eŋɔli ko yɛ ni ha koni lɛ nɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the tender leaves inside the plant funnel. The powder is caterpillar waste. Spraying approved neem-based treatments or recommended insecticides into the center funnel early in the morning helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Pauda lɛ ji ŋmeii amli nu. Kɛ́ akɛ neem tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves. Spraying the plants with soapy water, wood ash solution, or mild insecticides gets rid of these insects and stops new leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ tso ashwishwɛ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni waaa lɛ ashwie tsei anɔ Enɛ baagbe kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaatsi baai heei ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning light yellow in a V-shape and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ V su mli ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay dark green and grow well. Applying top-dressing fertilizers like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will restore essential nutrients to your soil.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ŋmãa afee eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi tamɔ NPK loo ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers under the ground are small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to put all their energy into growing stems and leaves instead of roots. Avoiding heavy nitrogen fertilizer late in the season allows the plant to send stored food downward into forming big roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ najiaŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsuɔ niyenii ni ato lɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi wuji.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting a crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize removes a lot of nutrients from the dirt, leaving the soil tired. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas can take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, naturally enriching the soil for the next crop cycle.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ he ajɔ Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotten before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by irregular watering and a lack of calcium in the plant as the fruit develops. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and adding wood ash or lime to the soil helps prevent the fruit tips from turning black.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli beni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akatsɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before growing into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ cacao ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they experience water stress during dry spells, insect damage, or lack of soil nutrients like potassium. Maintaining good shade trees, preserving soil moisture, and controlling sap-sucking insects help flowers turn into full pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna nu he haomɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli, kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ haa anáa hɔnɔ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to tall wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the food that feeds the growing yam tuber underground. Staking lifts the vines into the light, keeps leaves dry, and prevents soil-borne diseases from rotting the stems.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa la lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ ni ehaaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akafite ŋmeii lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without tall crops around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct hot sunlight and harsh dry winds. They need temporary shade from fast-growing crops like plantains to protect their tender leaves until they grow strong enough to withstand the full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛkɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize leaves start turning yellow from the bottom of the plant going up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green and healthy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee eŋɔli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce a lot of big leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai wuji waa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas make too many leaves and fewer pods when the soil has too much nitrogen or if they do not get enough sunlight. Using fertilizers higher in phosphorus encourages the plant to produce flowers and pods instead of just leafy growth.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ baai babaoo tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Mohu ɔ, e ji tsohi nɛ a ngɛ wae ɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots remain thin and small even after a full year in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii lolo yɛ be mli ni mikɛ afi muu fɛɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot swell if the soil is packed too tightly or lacks potassium. Planting in loose, well-drained soil gives the roots room to expand and store food easily.
ga: Kasava shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɔjɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shishifã lɛ mli gbɛ lɛ mli waa ni ekɛ niyenii toɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground before I dig them up for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifoɔ amɛ koni makpa lɛ?

english: Yams rot underground when water collects around the roots without draining away properly, or when tiny soil pests attack the tubers. Planting yams on high mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain off easily.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. shishifãi ni nu bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tutua ŋmeii lɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up into little cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? ni okpa dalɛ

english: Pepper leaves curl when tiny insects like aphids or thrips suck the sap from under the leaves and spread plant viruses. Spraying neem leaf water or recommended pest treatments keeps these insects away.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips nu nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ mli ni amɛgbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem baa mli nu loo gbɛi krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the branch during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning dense branches lets sunlight and fresh air reach the trees to dry out damp pods.
ga: Fungi hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ kookoo diji baa. Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ he koni eha tso lɛ mli tsei ni mli efɔ lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out suddenly, or when the plant lacks moisture. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ trukaa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my watermelons turn soft and black while they are growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ shishi feɔ blɛoo ni eyɛ ediŋŋ be mli ni edaa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This issue, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the fruit develop firm bottoms.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ koni amɛshishi afee shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains before the bunches are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that cannot support heavy fruit bunches when strong winds blow through wet, softened soil. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden poles or bamboos prevents the tree from collapsing.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ. Abaanyɛ ana kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for healthy leaf growth. Adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the base of the plants will help them regain their green color and produce bigger ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ ni wa Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ awo he fɛɛ he. Tso lɛ shishi baaye abua tso lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why are my pepper plants staying very short and stunted even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Stunted growth often happens when the soil is too hard for the roots to spread out and find nutrients. Loosening the soil around your plants and mixing in well-rotted manure will help the roots grow deeper and support bigger plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛna niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ futu mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni eye ebua tso ni da lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture the cocoa saplings need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha kookoo tso lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves have tiny holes all over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii bibii yɛ amɛhe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by small pests like caterpillars feeding on the crop. Spraying your plants with a natural neem leaf extract or an approved mild pesticide will help keep these insects away.
ga: Small holes in cabbage leaves are often caused by small pests such as caterpillars that feed on the crop. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni waaa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu he kɛjɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why do my yam leaves turn brown and dry up long before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Vines drying up early is usually caused by leaf spot diseases or intense heat from the bare ground. Staking your yam vines high off the soil gives them better airflow and keeps the leaves cool and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ wain tso lɛ gbiɔ oya ji leaf spot hela loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ mli jɔɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ

english: Why are my cowpea pods curling up and covered in tiny black insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii diji ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: Those tiny black insects are aphids that suck juice from the plant, causing the pods to deform. You can spray them with mild soapy water or neem oil to clear them off without harming the crop.
ga: ŋmeii diji bibii Nomɛi ji ŋmeii ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. ha pod lɛ afite Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ afɔ nɔ. loo neem fɔ ni akɛbaafɔ he ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays pooled around them for too long. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away so the roots stay dry enough to thrive.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching around the plant stems helps protect the flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ he ko ni edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ Tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛkatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my watermelons cracking open on the field right before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Watermelons burst open when they get a sudden heavy rush of water after a dry period. Watering your farm evenly throughout the growing season prevents the fruit inside from expanding faster than its skin can stretch.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji akɛ aha amɛ nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ ashwã oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my groundnut plants have plenty of green leaves but very few pods under the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi pods fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts need soft, loose soil so the flowering pegs can easily push underground to form pods. If the soil is too hard or lacks calcium, adding wood ash and loosening the dirt around the base will help more pods develop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia ŋmeii. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ ashɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ shishi oya koni amɛfee ŋmeii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo calcium bɛ mli Tso sũ ni akɛfataa he kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ adara babaoo.

english: How can I tell if a crop sickness on my land is caused by a fungus or a bacterium?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa?

english: Fungal diseases usually look like dry brown patches, powdery spots, or fuzzy molds on leaves. Bacterial diseases often cause wet, slimy rots, dark watery spots, or a foul smell on the plant stems and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai jeɔ kpo akɛ ŋmeii ni egbi, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Powder spots loo mold ni bɛ faŋŋ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ nu ni egbo, ni efɔ, ni eyɛ ediŋŋ baa. Aloo ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo ko yɛ tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops getting covered in a white powdery dust?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ yɛŋ ehà baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: That white powder is a common fungal infection called powdery mildew. The fungus lives on the leaf surface and steals nutrients from your crop, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and drop early.
ga: Nakai powda yɛŋ lɛ ji hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Fungi lɛ hiɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni ejuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why are my crop leaves suddenly wilting during the middle of the day even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt. Bacteria enter the roots from the soil and block the tiny tubes inside the stem, stopping water from reaching the leaves even if the soil has plenty of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, muawai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Muawai boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ tsɔnei bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa, ni no haaa nu ayashɛ baai lɛ ahe kɛji akɛ sũ lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu po.

english: Can crop diseases spread from my neighbor's farm to my own field?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛya mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ mli?

english: Yes, fungal spores can travel long distances on the wind, while bacteria can spread through flowing rainwater runoff, insects moving between fields, or shared tools.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya he ko shɔŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛtsɔ ahum nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kplukai ni nyiɛɔ ŋmɔji ateŋ loo nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni ajaa

english: Can using the same cutlass across different crops spread sickness on my farm?
ga: Dagger kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi anɔ Ani hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cutting a sick plant leaves infected sap, bacteria, or spores on your cutlass blade. When you cut a healthy crop next, you can introduce those disease germs directly into the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baaha nu ni mli ewo muji, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahi otsɔji lɛ anɔ. Be kroko kɛ́ obaafo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Obaanyɛ okɛ nakai helai lɛ amli helai lɛ awo tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: If I see a few plants getting sick on my land, should I pull them out or wait for them to recover?
ga: Kɛji mina tsei fioo komɛi ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ani Esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ he loo mamɛ ni etsa?

english: It is best to uproot infected plants immediately and safely dispose of them away from your field. Leaving sick plants gives fungi and bacteria time to multiply and infect the rest of your healthy crops.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooogbala tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ojie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ náa be koni amɛshwere ni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ hela.

english: Why do my crops get far more rot and spot diseases during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ ni helai babaoo yeɔ amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fungi and bacteria thrive in wet conditions and warm weather. Heavy rain drops also splash soil-dwelling bacteria and fungal spores up onto the healthy lower leaves of your crops.
ga: Fungi kɛ bacteria yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu shwieɔ helai ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do crops in one part of my land grow healthy while crops in another part of the same field turn yellow and rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã kome nɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ fã kroko nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Soil conditions vary across a field. Certain patches may hold too much water or contain high concentrations of soil-borne fungi or bacteria that attack roots in that specific area.
ga: Esoro shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Ekolɛ hei komɛi yɛ nu babaoo loo ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni tutuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nakai he pɔtɛɛ lɛ.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check for crop health issues?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛnamɔ he naagbai?

english: You should walk through your field at least twice a week. Spotting early signs of fungal or bacterial infection allows you to treat or isolate the problem before it turns into a major loss.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ otsɔ oyale mli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Kɛ́ ona mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa lɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa loo otsiɔ naagba lɛ naa dani ebafeɔ nɔ ni elaaje waa.

english: What should I do when a strange, serious sickness starts spreading fast across my crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni gbeɔ mɔ bɔi gbɛfaŋnɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ amli?

english: You should immediately inform your local agricultural extension officer. They can visit your field to identify whether the issue is bacterial or fungal and escalate severe outbreaks to district officers for additional guidance.
ga: Esa akɛ atswa akutso lɛ mli okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ adafi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛyasara onitsumɔhe nine lɛ koni amɛkwɛ kɛji naagba lɛ ji bacteria loo fungus. ni ekɛ hela lɛ tee kpokpaa nɔ onukpai lɛ aŋɔɔ koni amɛwo lɛ ŋaa krokomɛi.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into straws during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to reduce their surface area, which slows down water loss when the sun is strong. It is the crop's natural defense mechanism to conserve water until temperatures drop.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi. Enɛ baaha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛ́ hulu la lɛ mli wa. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni ekɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashi dɔlɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its lower leaves during drought to reduce the amount of water it needs to survive. Once regular water or rainfall returns, the plant will shoot out fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava shĩɔ eshishigbɛ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛba nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi lɛ shi. Kɛ nu loo nugbɔ nɛ daa Tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants stay very small and produce tiny flowers prematurely when rainfall is low?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraaa ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi bibii mra be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo lɛ?

english: When crops face extreme heat or water shortage early in life, stress triggers them to flower quickly as an emergency effort to produce seeds before the plant completely dries up.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa kpe yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli mra lɛ, Haomɔ baaha tsei lɛ afɔlɔ oya. Enɛ ji mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ oya koni akɛ dumɔwui aba dani tsei lɛ agbi kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die if I clear away all the big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, full sunlight and excessive heat. Shade trees act as a natural shelter, keeping the air cool and soil moist so the delicate seedlings can establish healthy roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shweshweeshwe shihilɛhe. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing tall and weak instead of short and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ kukuji kɛ ŋmɔji najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together or hidden under dense shade, they stretch upward searching for light, making their stems thin and fragile.
ga: Kɛ tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo amɛtee amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ Tso lɛ baajie ehe kɛya ŋwɛi koni eyatao la. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why are all the flowers falling off my pepper plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or water stress. The plant aborts the flowers to save its strength for keeping its main stem and roots alive.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu mli haomɔ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do my yam plants know when it is time to start swelling and forming tubers under the soil?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni sweet potato tsei leɔ be ni esa akɛ amɛje shishi amɛfuu ni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii?

english: Yam plants react to changes in daylight hours and rain patterns, shifting their energy from growing vines above ground to storing food in underground tubers for the dry season.
ga: Sweet potato tsei hereɔ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi amli. Amɛtsakeɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ wain tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa niyenii ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛha hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable crops during the early morning or in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning gives the soil time to soak up moisture before the hot afternoon sun evaporates it, allowing crop roots to drink deeply and stay hydrated through the day.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shwieɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu waa ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale yellow when heavy rains leave water standing on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu hiɔ miŋmɔji lɛ amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Too much standing water drowns plant roots by cutting off oxygen in the soil. Without oxygen, roots cannot breathe or absorb the nutrients required to keep leaves dark green.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa tsei shishifãi shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable roots with dry grass keep them alive longer between rainfalls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-vegetable shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) protects the soil from direct heat, slowing down water evaporation and keeping the root zone cooler and moist for a longer time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. Adding well-decomposed animal manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer like urea gives the maize the food it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ nii waa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ nitrogen fee tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Staking holds the yam leaves up high where they can capture maximum sunlight to produce food for the tuber. It also keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which protects the plant from soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi yɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaatsiɔ baai anaa koni ekashwɛ yɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my cocoa trees when they are already growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-kookoo niji lɛ ekomɛi? Akɛ eedara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Pruning removes excess branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts of the tree. Good airflow prevents humidity build-up, which causes black pod disease, and allows the tree to focus its energy on producing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. ni ji black pod hela lɛ baa ni ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa cocoa pods wuji ni amɛfeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before they can grow into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from excessive heat, dry soil, or insect attacks like thrips. Keeping the soil consistently moist during dry hot days and managing garden pests helps the flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni fe nine, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutua amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni etsɔɔ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is eating holes into the middle leaves of my young corn plants, and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ yeli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant to feed, but early application of recommended neem extract solutions or specific insecticides can clear them out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Shi kɛ akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi yɛ shishijee mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie amɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantains alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ madu kookoo tsei ni kookoo dumɔwui heei yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under the harsh sun. Fast-growing plantains produce large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas to protect the cocoa trees during their first few years while giving you plantains to sell or eat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni buɔ cacao tso lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eŋmɛɔ bo gbɛ ni ohɔ̃ɔ loo oyeɔ plantains hu.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots under the ground are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare main stem, and the ground around the base of the plant starts to crack. You can carefully dig around one stem to inspect the tuber size before harvesting the full field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Shi tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ ni ehi shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa tso lɛ he kɛkwɛ bɔ ni bulb lɛ da ha dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my pepper plants help them stay healthy during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ haa amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the dirt from direct heat. It slows down water evaporation, keeps the root zone cool, and prevents weeds from growing and competing with your crop for water.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akatswa nu he akaŋ.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to sprout when I bury them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry limited food energy inside them to sprout and reach the surface. If buried too deep, the young shoot runs out of energy before reaching light and air, causing the seedling to die under the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, oblahii kɛ oblayei lɛ ahewalɛ baaho dani amɛshɛ la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen, a vital food for growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach, or the soil itself may be exhausted from continuous farming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ yɛ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: What causes black spots to spread across my cocoa pods and turn them dark and rotten?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛfeɔ diŋ ni amɛfiteɔ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, overly shaded conditions. Clearing excess shade, pruning low branches, and removing affected pods stops moisture from trapping the fungal spores.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Ni ajieɔ shade ni fa fe nine lɛ low pruning kɛ pods ni ena naagbai lɛ ajiemɔ Ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ kpaaa koni ekamɔ mold spores lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without growing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi shi ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Trees drop flowers when they are under stress from heat, severe dry spells, or a lack of soil nutrients. Providing moderate shade and maintaining soil moisture gives the tree the strength it needs to nourish flowers into full cocoa pods.
ga: Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyɔɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ shishi. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shade ni sa ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛkwɛɔ fɔfɔi ni efeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my crops growing smaller and weaker every season even though I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibii ni miigbɔjɔ daa be mli eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same soil year after year drains specific nutrients needed for healthy growth. Rotating your crops or adding organic manure restores soil fertility so plants can grow strong again.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa amɛnáa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsake loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside leaf funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the center of maize plants to feed on soft new leaves. Catching them early and applying targeted sprays or natural remedies like ash or neem liquid protects the crop before major damage occurs.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ he loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ sũ loo neem nu atsu nii. Ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die suddenly even when the soil around them is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden collapse is caused by soil-borne bacteria or fungi blocking the water tubes inside the stem. Because water cannot travel up the stem, the plant dries out and dies even if water is present in the soil.
ga: Nɛkɛ shwiemɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu nyɛŋ ayashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Tso lɛ gbiɔ ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting under the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water pools around them in heavy or flat soils, depriving the roots of oxygen. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away freely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: How can I know the right time to plant my crops now that rainfall patterns are changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nugbɔshiimɔi tsake?

english: Rather than relying strictly on fixed traditional months, wait until the soil gets a deep, soak-in rain for two or three consecutive days. This ensures there is enough moisture trapped in the root zone for young seeds to sprout safely.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaye kusum nyɔji ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni ekɛwo nu mli gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe koni dumɔwui bibii lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dried leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ ni baai egbi kɛ jwɛi?

english: Covering the ground with dried vegetation, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool, retains moisture during dry days, suppresses weed growth, and eventually rots to feed the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ koni ebatsɔ niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli
