english: Why is it better to mix animal manure into the soil rather than leaving it on top of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaafutu ŋmɔshi nibii awo sũ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni aaashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mixing manure directly into the soil places nutrients right where plant roots can absorb them easily. Leaving manure exposed on top lets the sun burn off useful nitrogen and allows rain to wash away the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa he ko ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ oya. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shãa nitrogen ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa nugbɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Can I plant cassava on the same piece of land where I already have plantains growing?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miyɔɔ plantains momo lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can grow cassava and plantains together on the same plot. Cassava grows well in the open spaces between plantain trees, allowing you to harvest two different crops from the same land without wasting space.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei afee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ dumɔwui ateŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome ni ofiteee he ko.

english: Is it possible to grow food crops like plantains inside my young cocoa farm?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu niyenii tamɔ plantains yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting plantains in a young cocoa farm is a common practice. The broad leaves of the plantain trees provide shade that protects young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight while giving you food to harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Dumɔwui lɛ ahe baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa niyenii kɛha okpamɔ lɛ.

english: Will planting different types of crops close together make them fight each other for food in the soil?
ga: Ani tsei srɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha amɛwuu yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: If you leave enough space between your crops, they will not fight. Different crops feed at different soil depths, so proper spacing allows them to grow together peacefully.
ga: Kɛji oshi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ Amɛwuuŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi baaye nii yɛ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ aŋmɛɔ tsei nɛɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃ yɛ toiŋjɔlɛ mli.

english: Why is it so dangerous to leave weeds growing around my young cassava and plantain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-cassava kɛ plantain tsei lɛ yɛ oshara waa diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from your crops. If you let weeds take over, your crops will stay small, become weak, and yield very little food.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji oha jwɛi lɛ ye nɔ lɛ, Oŋmɔshinii lɛ baafee bibioo, egbɔjɔ ni ekɛ niyenii fioo ko pɛ baaha.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds from my farm so my plants can grow well?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni tsei lɛ aya nɔ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: You should clear weeds regularly during the early months of planting. Once your crops grow tall and their leaves cover the ground, they will naturally block sunlight and prevent new weeds from growing quickly.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni okɛdu lɛ mli. Beni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛbaai lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Amɛbaatsi hulu la naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaatsi jwɛi heei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Can heavy weeds cause my plantain trees to produce very small bunches of plantain?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni tsii lɛ baanyɛ aha mi plantains lɛ awo plantains bibii bibii waa?

english: Yes, heavy weeds steal the vital soil nutrients that plantain trees need to build strong stems and produce large, full bunches of fruit.
ga: No ji anɔkwale akɛ, jwɛi ni tsii lɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni plantains he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni amɛwo aduawai wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my crops are sick with a plant disease instead of just lacking water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ahe hela miipiŋ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe nu ni miiho kɛkɛ?

english: A sick plant often shows signs like dark spots on leaves, rotting stems, white powders under leaves, or strange yellow patterns that do not go away even after it rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ okadii tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ akpo. Powda yɛŋ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi. aloo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ Ni sɛɛ efooo kɛji nugbɔ enɛ po.

english: What should I do immediately if I notice a disease on a few leaves of my crop?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina hela yɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ ekomɛi anɔ?

english: You should carefully cut off the infected leaves or remove the sick plant entirely from the farm and destroy it so the sickness does not spread to your healthy crops.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo ojie tsei fɛɛ ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What simple things can I do to prevent diseases from breaking out on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi hela naa koni ekaba yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Keep your farm clean by pruning extra branches for good air movement, clearing weeds, removing rotten pods, and making sure water does not collect at the base of your trees.
ga: Ha oŋmɔ lɛ mli atse kɛtsɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ni oookpa koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ, jwɛi ni ooojie, kɛ ŋmeii ni egboi ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni nu akabua ehe naa yɛ otsei lɛ ashishi.

english: Why do the leaves of my young crops turn yellow and stop growing early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the plant's roots are damaged by a soil disease, pests are attacking it, or weeds are stealing all the nutrients from the soil.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ efite tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Pest tutuamɔ ko yɛ. Aloo jwɛi miiju niyenii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: How do I know the exact time my cocoa pods are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods change color when they are ready—usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange depending on the variety. Harvesting them too early means the beans won't be fully developed, while waiting too long can cause the seeds inside to germinate or rot.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛfee klalo. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. loo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli Edamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛmɔ be kakadaŋŋ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi.

english: Does plucking cocoa pods by twisting them with my hands hurt the tree's future yield?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmɔji ni akɛ niji gbalaa lɛ baaná wɔsɛɛ be mli nibii ni afeɔ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: Yes, pulling or twisting pods by hand damages the bark cushion on the trunk where flowers grow. Always cut the pod stem cleanly with a sharp hook or cutlass so the flowering spot remains healthy to produce new pods next season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ oniji gbala loo otsɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni mli wa afo ŋmei lɛ shishifã lɛ mli koni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ koni ekɛ ŋmei heei aba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees growing very tall with many leaves but not producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ebɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees get too much shade or high-nitrogen soil without enough sunlight, they focus all their energy on growing tall and bushy instead of flowering. Lightly pruning upper shade branches allows sunlight in, which signals the tree to start producing pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo loo shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ, Yɛ fɔfɔi ni amɛaawo lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ anɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ fioo koni hulu la abote mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ okadi akɛ ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their flowers before they turn into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop flowers when they suffer from water stress during dry spells or lack essential soil nutrients. Keeping the soil covered with organic mulch and protecting the flowers from insect pests helps more flowers turn into healthy young pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nu he haomɔ kpe amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ organic mulch tsuɔ he nii kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛfeɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do cocoa trees planted too close together give a smaller harvest than trees planted with wide spaces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni da lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close, their branches block sunlight from reaching the lower trunk where flowers need light to bloom. Overcrowded roots also fight over the same soil nutrients, leaving every tree underfed and producing fewer pods.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso niji tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. ni fɔfɔii lɛ he hiaa la koni amɛfɔlɔ Shishifãi ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ.

english: Why are some of my full-grown cocoa pods turning black and dry on the tree before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ekomɛi feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in wet, humid shade. Clearing bush around the trees, pruning branches to let wind blow through, and removing infected pods quickly keeps the disease from destroying the rest of your harvest.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shĩa mli hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ajieɔ tsei bibii ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, afoɔ tsei aniji koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Ni kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akafite onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa pods if I let weeds grow tall around the stems of my trees?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji miha jwɛi shwere kɛbɔle amɛhe? tso shishi

english: Tall weeds steal water and nutrients away from the cocoa roots, causing the beans inside the pods to remain light and small. Weeds also trap moisture around the tree trunk, creating a damp home for pests and fungal rot to destroy your crop.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi amli. Enɛ haa kɔfe yibii ni yɔɔ pod lɛ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni efeɔ bibioo. Jwɛi hu mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. tso shishi Enɛ haa he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ koni amɛfite onibii.

english: Can I grow cassava together with my young cocoa trees on the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ cocoa tsei afee ekome kɛdu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Cassava grows very strong roots that steal water and heavy soil food away from young cocoa roots, which can stunt the cocoa. Plantains are a better choice to plant with young cocoa because their wide leaves give gentle shade without choking the cocoa roots.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa waa. ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii amli Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo lɛ afee bibioo. Plantain ji tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo tsei bibii ni aduɔ lɛ ejaakɛ ebaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo blɛoo ni ekɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwieee shi.

english: Will applying fertilizer make my cocoa trees yield pods continuously throughout the whole year?
ga: Ani cacao tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaya nɔ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer strengthens the tree and increases total pod numbers, but cocoa trees still naturally produce pods in major and minor seasonal cycles linked to rainfall. Fertilizer helps the tree yield heavily during these seasons rather than fruiting non-stop.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ mli waa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ. Shi cacao tsei yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ shishijee kɛ sɛɛ mli be mli nibii ni kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ yɔɔ tsakpaa lɛ amli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ nɛkɛ bei nɛɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii daa lɛ

english: How does heavy shade from large forest trees affect the growth of my cocoa crops?
ga: Te hulutsoo ni mli wa ni jɛɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ saa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While young cocoa trees need heavy shade to protect their soft leaves from burning, adult trees need filtered sunlight to produce heavy pods. Too much thick shade keeps the farm damp and dark, which slows pod growth and encourages plant diseases.
ga: Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo ni mli wa koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. Tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni atsɔ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii. Shade babaoo baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee duŋ. Enɛ haa pod lɛ dalɛ baa shi ni ewoɔ tsei ahe helai ahe hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is no longer producing enough pods to be worth keeping?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛto be kakadaŋŋ?

english: When a cocoa tree's output drops to around 30 or 40 pods, it shows that the tree is no longer yielding well and will not give you much profit, meaning it may need improvement or removal.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tso ko yibiiwoo ba shi kɛyashɛ aaafee 30 loo 40 lɛ, cacao tso lɛ wooo yibii dɔŋŋ, ni sɛɛnamɔ babaoo hu baaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ ehe baahia ni asaa loo ajie kɛya he kroko.

english: What yield numbers should I look out for to know if a cocoa tree is performing poorly?
ga: Mɛɛ yibiiwoo yibɔi esa akɛ makwɛ koni mana kɛji mi-kokoo tsei lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: If a tree is only producing around 30 to 40 pods, that is a sign of poor yield, indicating that the tree lacks good genetics or health to yield higher.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii aaafee 30 kɛyashi 40 pɛ lɛ, no lɛ ekolɛ no ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ekpaaa nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ fɔmɔ su kpakpa loo hewalɛ kpakpa ni baaha ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers come to inspect how our cocoa trees are standing on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ baa koni amɛbakwɛ wɔ kokoo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkwɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ha lɛ?

english: Officers assess the farm to evaluate the condition and stability of the trees, helping farmers determine which ones need support and which low-yielding ones should be removed.
ga: Okwaafoi akwɛlɔi koni amɛkwɛ bɔ ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi amɛhaa lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛleɔ tsei ni he hiaa yelikɛbuamɔ. Ni esa akɛ ajie tsei fɛɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo lɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why would I need to prop up my cocoa trees with wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei afi kookoo tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Using poles as physical supports helps weak or heavily laden trees stay upright so they can be managed and improved rather than collapsing.
ga: Gbɔmɔtsoŋ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei asɛɛ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo jatsu ni tsii amɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ. Koni enyɛ ekwɛ nɔ ni eya hiɛ moŋ fe ni eeegbee shi

english: What steps can I take to support cocoa trees that are struggling to stand upright?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni maye mabua ni mafi cacao tso ni enaa naagba yɛ edamɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can cut strong support poles and place them under the leaning or weak branches to keep the tree standing stably while you try to improve its production.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofolɔ sɛɛfimɔ tsei ni wa ni okɛwo tsei niji ni shwieɔ shi loo ni bɛ hewalɛ shishi koni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ yɛ be mli ni otsuɔ nii koni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ.

english: What happens if I do not put support poles under my weak cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni baaba kɛji akɛ mikɛ tso lɛ wooo kookoo tso ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ shishi?

english: Trees that are weak and left unsupported will fail to stand well, making them impossible to maintain, which eventually leads to them needing to be uprooted.
ga: Tso ni he waaa ni nɔ ko bɛ ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ nyɛŋ adamɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. ni haaa efee nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ekɛ amɛshishijee baa.

english: What should I do with a cocoa tree that refuses to yield well even after care?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kookoo tso ni kpooɔ akɛ ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni mikwɛ enɔ po lɛ?

english: If a cocoa tree consistently produces poor yields and does not improve with support, the best step is to uproot it to make room for better-yielding trees.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cacao tso lɛ wooo yibii ni ehiii be fɛɛ be ni eyaaa hiɛ kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni ajie shishifãi lɛ koni aha gbɛ aha tso ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Can a low-yielding cocoa tree be restored before deciding to remove it completely?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ asaa kookoo tsei ni woɔ yibii fioo lɛ dani akpɛ yiŋ akɛ abaajie amɛ kwraa?

english: Yes, you can first attempt to improve the tree's health and support it with poles, but if it still fails to yield well, uprooting becomes necessary.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oka klɛŋklɛŋ ni oha otso lɛ aya hiɛ ni oye obua lɛ. Shi kɛji tso lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai lolo Ehe miihia ni ajie kɛjɛ shishi.

english: How do I decide whether to keep or uproot an old cocoa tree on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ mahã kookoo tsei momo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi loo mafo amɛshishi?

english: You assess its pod output; if it produces low numbers like 30 or 40 pods and cannot be improved even with structural supports, it should be uprooted.
ga: Okwɛɔ nɔ ni jɛɔ pod lɛ mli baa lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ afee pods fioo ko, tamɔ pods 30 loo 40, ni anyɛɛɛ afee hiɛyaa kɛ tsɔnei ni fiɔ sɛɛ po. Esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shishi.

english: Why is uprooting low-yielding trees recommended for my farm's success?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ ajie tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ koni miŋmɔ lɛ aye omanye lɛ?

english: Keeping trees that yield very little wastes space and labor; uprooting bad yielders allows you to clear the farm for high-yielding crops that increase your harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei ni haa gbɛ kɛ nitsumɔ fioo ko pɛ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii ni ehiii lɛ ni oootsi lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ ojie oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them provides living shade and keeps the air humid so the young trees can survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni eye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii Mine yɛ bu ko ni akɛtee tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that feeds on the young leaves inside the maize funnel. Treating the center of the plant early with recommended control measures stops them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei ŋmeii amli lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ mra. Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ amɛ lɛ baatsi amɛnaa dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes in the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni mi sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ.

english: Yam is a vine plant that produces its edible tuber underground. Lifting the leaves up on stakes exposes them to maximum sunlight, which helps the plant produce more food to feed and grow a larger tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni woɔ ŋmeii ni ayeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo ni ekɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why does my maize yield get smaller every year when I keep planting it on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen and nutrients from the soil. Planting it continuously in the same spot empties the soil's natural strength, which is why rotating crops or adding manure is needed to rebuild fertility.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Yɛ yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni atsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young suckers sprouting around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: If too many suckers grow around one stem, they compete for water and nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves just two or three strong stems, ensuring the main plant develops large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ tso kome he. Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ baajɛ mli aba. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná kuu agbo ni tsii.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the leaf sap and spreading viruses. Managing these pests early stops the curling and helps the plant produce normal flowers and fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baa mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without setting any fruit during the dry, hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High temperatures and dry soil cause stress to tomato plants, making them drop their flowers to conserve energy. Keeping the soil consistently moist and using mulch around the base keeps the root zone cool.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa tomato shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn hard and woody if I leave them in the ground too long after the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When cassava stays in the ground past full maturity, the roots lose starch content and build up thick fibers. Harvesting at the right time prevents the tubers from becoming tough or rotting when rains return.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi ebaada kwraa. Shishifãi lɛ laajeɔ starch ni amɛfeɔ fibers ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛkafite kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on a plot before planting maize there next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani midu ŋmãa yɛ jɛmɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When the legume crop is done, that extra nitrogen stays in the soil as natural food for the next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ agbe ŋmãa tsei lɛ anaa Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops immediately after the first rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are native to the land and sit dormant in the soil, ready to sprout at the slightest moisture. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing water and nutrients while your crop seeds are still trying to germinate.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni amɛwɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Efee klalo akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ be mli ni odumɔwui lɛ miitao amɛkwɛ̃ lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow flowers and pods directly on the main trunk instead of on thin branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe niji bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally display a behavior called cauliflory, where flowers grow on the thick, strong wood of the main trunk and heavy branches so the tree can safely support the heavy weight of mature pods.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ kɔlifloa lɛ kpo. He ni fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni tsii lɛ anɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii ni edara kwraa lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do many of the small, tiny green cocoa pods on my tree turn brown and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Mɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi dani amɛdara lɛ.

english: This natural crop behavior is called cherelle wilt. The tree purposely thins out surplus young pods that it doesn't have enough nutrients, water, or energy to fully mature.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ tso adebɔɔ mli subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eyeɔ eshishifãi bibii lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛkaná niyenii, nu, loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaadara ni amɛdara.

english: Why should I cut off the fresh green shoots that keep growing from the bottom of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These shoots, called suckers or chupons, waste the tree's water and nutrients on fast stem growth rather than directing that energy into producing pods on the main tree.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo chupon. Ebaaha tso lɛ mli nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afite kɛtsɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ oya lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ jamɛ a he wami ɔ kɛ fɔ tso ngua a nɔ nɛ o maa pee pods ɔ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and burn when there are no shade trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally prefer partial shade because direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves, overheats the surface roots, and dries out the moisture needed for healthy growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ sumɔɔ hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ. Ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ baa lɛ hiɛ lɛ mli dɔɔ tsɔ. ni egbiɔ nu ni he hiaa kɛha gbɔmɔtso lɛ dalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and slender with thin stems when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete for sunlight and stretch rapidly upward to reach light, spending energy on height rather than developing thick stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe oya kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná la. Ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa moŋ ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods start turning black and rotting right after the heavy rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ diŋ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates high humidity and splashes soil water onto pods, spreading a microscopic fungus that causes black pod disease, which thrives in cool, damp conditions.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa ni ekɛ sũ mli nu shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei bibioo ko ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa. ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and curl during the hot afternoon even when the soil was moist in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi moŋ?

english: In extreme heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can absorb it from the soil. Curling leaves is the plant's way of reducing its surface area to save water.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbaa ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer right inside the soil.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsake lɛ tɛ̃ɛ amɛfee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops stay green longer during dry weather when I spread dry leaves around their base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni migbɛɔ baai ni egbi mishwaa amɛshishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with organic mulch creates a protective blanket that shields the ground from the sun, keeps soil temperatures cool, and stops moisture from evaporating quickly.
ga: Organic mulching lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akaho oya

english: Where is the best spot around a tree trunk to apply fertilizer so the roots can absorb it quickly?
ga: Mɛni ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ? Tso shishi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ oya?

english: Fertilizer should be spread underneath the outer edge of the leaf canopy (the dripline), because that is where the tree's fine feeder roots are concentrated and ready to absorb nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋwɛitsu lɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi (drip line) ejaakɛ biɛ ji he ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds and hot sun drain moisture from the plant very quickly. Cocoa trees shed leaves to protect themselves from losing water, but providing shade trees like plantain or shade trees keeps the root soil moist and protects young cocoa.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli oya. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ amɛhe lɛ he. Shi hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni akɛhaa Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build green leaves. The plant takes nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but yield very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are planted too close together, the cassava spends all its energy growing leaves and stems toward sunlight instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei baato niyenii yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ enɔ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on all their leaves to make the starch that grows big tubers. Staking lifts leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the leaves to catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni oha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni ooonyɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baawo mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps the maize grow bigger without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛku sɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like an umbrella for the soil. It traps soil moisture, keeps the roots cool during hot days, and stops weeds from stealing plant food.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni ehaaa jwɛi akaju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli

english: What is causing holes in the leaves of my young maize plants with little green grains inside the center stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn plants lɛ baai ni dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baa? Eyɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the growing center (funnel) of the maize plant during the day and feeds on tender leaves before they unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ dalɛ mli shɔŋŋ (cone) yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same spot where I harvested tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he ni mifo mi-tomato lɛ yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same crop family and suffer from the same pests and soil diseases. Planting them in the same spot season after season allows pests and fungus to multiply in the soil and attack the new crop.
ga: Tomato kɛ pepper yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyɔɔ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kome. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and drop off without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely hot or when the plant suffers from sudden dry spells. High heat prevents the flowers from pollinating, so the plant sheds them to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ mli egbi trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why didn't my maize seeds grow out of the ground after I buried them deep during planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mifu amɛ shɔŋŋ yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too deep, they run out of stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil before reaching the surface sunlight, causing them to rot or die underground.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ tsɔ Hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ dani eshɛ hulu la lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What happens to my crops if water stays on my farm for a long time after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: If standing water sits on your farmland for about three months, your crops will suffocate and die because prolonged flooding prevents their roots from getting the air they need.
ga: Kɛji nu ehi oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi ejaakɛ nu afua ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: How can I protect my farm from holding too much stagnant water during the rainy season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ ŋmɔji anaa koni amɛkato nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Building basic drainage canals or water channels allows excess rainwater to flow away from your field, helping your crops thrive instead of drowning in sitting water.
ga: Shishijee nu tsɔne loo nu gbɛ ni ooofee lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli. Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara moŋ fe ni ooobote nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Why are my crops dying in low-lying parts of my field where rainwater collects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii miigboi yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ lɛ?

english: Water pools easily in low areas and blocks oxygen from reaching the soil. When crops remain submerged for months without drainage, their roots rot and the plants perish.
ga: Efoɔ nu mli oya yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Beni aduɔ nii yɛ nu shishi nyɔji babaoo ni nu bɛ mli. Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tso lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What simple construction work can I do on my farmland to stop crop loss from flooding?
ga: Manyɛ matsu tsumaa nitsumɔ fɛɛ tsumaa nitsumɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ nu afua mli lɛ.

english: Digging small canals or drainage pathways across your land creates an exit for floodwater, preventing stagnant water from staying around your crop roots.
ga: Faa bibioo ko ni ooofo Loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ baaha ana tsabaa kɛha nu afua. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsi ehe kɛjɛ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Do crop roots actually need to breathe air to stay alive?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni tsei shishifãi lɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛhi shi?

english: Yes, crops need oxygen around their roots to breathe just like people do. When deep water covers the ground for months, it cuts off air and kills the plant.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia oxygen ni ebɔle amɛhe. Shishifãi ni akɛmuɔ tamɔ bɔ ni adesai he hiaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. beni nu ni mli kwɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo lɛ Ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ni ekpata tsei ahiɛ.

english: How long can my crops stay in flooded water before they completely die?
ga: Be enyiɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baanyɛ ahi nu afua mli dani amɛgboi kwraa?

english: While crops can endure wet conditions for short periods, standing water that remains on your land for about three months will kill most crops.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋmɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ anaa yɛ be kukuoo mli moŋ, Shi nu ni baahi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ lɛ baagbe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Will digging small channels across my land actually help my crops grow better?
ga: Gbɛ bibioo ko ni afoɔ Ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, digging water channels prevents standing water from sitting on your soil for months, giving your crops the oxygen-rich environment they need to thrive.
ga: Hɛɛ, nubu ni oootsa lɛ baatsi nu naa koni ekata oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo. Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa shihilɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ mli ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Why do I sometimes see foam on top of standing water in large government plantations?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ minaa ŋmeii yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo ni yɔɔ nɔyeli abɔɔ agbo lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The foamy surface comes from specialized government interventions and treatments that introduce air into standing water, allowing crops on those plantations to continue breathing.
ga: Foamy surface lɛ jɛɔ nɔyeli lɛ nifeemɔi kɛ tsamɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛbaa nu ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nakai ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ amu.

english: Is there a water treatment I can use as a small-scale farmer to keep submerged crops alive?
ga: Ani nu mli tsamɔ ko yɛ ni manyɛ mikɛtsu nii akɛ okwaafonyo bibioo koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ ahi shi?

english: Treatments that make standing water foamy and breathable are expensive government-level resources. For small-scale farmers, building drainage canals to drain the water is the best solution.
ga: Tsofai ni haa nu ni ekã shi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa mɔ muɔ lɛ ji nɔyeli nibii ni jara wa waa. Kɛha okwaafoi bibii Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ mli lɛ maa ji tsabaa ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: How do large commercial plantations keep their crops alive in flooded fields compared to small farmers?
ga: Te ŋmɔji wuji ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ haa amɛŋmɔshi nibii hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli eha tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto okwaafoi bibii ahe?

english: Government plantations use special resource interventions to make standing water foamy so crops can breathe, while small-scale farmers must rely on digging canals to drain water away.
ga: Nɔyeli ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nibii krɛdɛɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii anyɛ amu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, esa akɛ okwaafoi bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ faai ni amɛfoɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛjie nu lɛ kɛya.

english: Why is it important for me to write down the exact date I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋma gbi pɔtɛɛ ni midu miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miwo shi lɛ?

english: Crops do not talk or remind us when they are mature. Keeping written records of your planting dates helps you accurately predict harvest time, schedule fertilizer application properly, and prepare for pest control before problems happen.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ewieee loo ebɔɔɔ wɔ kɔkɔ kɛ́ amɛdara kwraa. Kɛ́ oŋmala gbii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ ahe saji awo wolo nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni otsɔɔ nikpamɔ be lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ be ni sa kɛha fɔmɔ nii. ni osaa ohe kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ dani naagbai aba.

english: How does keeping track of how much fertilizer I use help my farm make more money?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ abɔ ni mikwɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ená shika babaoo lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Tracking your expenses and fertilizer amounts helps you calculate your exact profit after harvest. It shows you whether applying a certain amount of fertilizer actually increased your crop yield enough to justify the cost.
ga: Ni oookwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nyɔmɔwoo kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni obuɔ sɛɛnamɔi pɔtɛɛ ni obaaná yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Etsɔɔ bo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo mli lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ bɔ ni sa ni baaha shika ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ afee nɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting maize after the first rains fall?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath may still be too dry. Wait until the rain becomes steady over a few days so the soil holds enough moisture for the seeds to germinate without dying.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lolo. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ ji koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbooo.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take longer to yield fruit if I plant them near the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛji midu amɛ yɛ be ni hulutsoo be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains need constant moisture to build strong roots. If planted at the beginning of a dry spell, the young plant goes dormant to survive, which delays its growth and pushes back your harvest date by several months.
ga: Ehe miihia ni plantains lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa be fɛɛ be koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ baaya wɔɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi ni ehaa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: How will I know when my yam tubers are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Because yams grow underground, you must watch the leaves. When the yam vine and leaves naturally turn yellow and dry up, it is the plant's signal that it has finished feeding the tuber and it is time to harvest.
ga: Akɛni sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ baai lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ sweet potato wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ Enɛ ji okadi kɛha tso lɛ akɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii ni be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛdara ni amɛwo aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they face environmental stress, such as extreme heat, uneven watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Giving them balanced water and shade during peak heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ kpe. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ni akɛhaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves on purpose during dry spells to reduce water loss and protect their underground roots. As long as the stem remains green, the plant will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baahi shi akɛ eŋɔli lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: How can I tell if pests are attacking my cocoa trees before the pods get ruined?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui miitutua mi cacao tsei lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ afite?

english: Since trees cannot speak, you must look for early visual signs like yellowing leaves, small holes in the bark, or dark spots on young pods. Checking your farm regularly helps you spot these attacks early.
ga: Ejaakɛ tsei nyɛɛɛ awie. Obaasumɔ ni otao okadii ni anaa mra tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, buji bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yibii amli, loo hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ yibii bibii lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona tutuamɔi nɛɛ mra.

english: Why do fall armyworms suddenly attack my corn field early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay their eggs on young, tender corn leaves right as the farming season starts. The eggs hatch quickly, so inspecting the undersides of leaves early in the plant's life helps you catch them before they spread.
ga: Katerpillar ŋmei lɛ woɔ ewui yɛ ŋmãa baa bibii anɔ yɛ ŋmãa be lɛ shishijee mli. Wɔɔji lɛ baafo oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi yɛ ogbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ amɛ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why should I change where I plant my maize and cowpeas every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake he ni miduɔ mi-ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa yɛ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot every year allows pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with cowpeas starves maize pests and allows the cowpeas to add natural nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ cowpeas tsakeɔ lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ abele lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa cowpea lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and die when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because their leaf roots and skin are delicate. Tall trees shield young cocoa from harsh direct sunlight and keep the surrounding air and soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi, baai kɛ amɛhewolo lɛ waaa. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or severe weather changes like the Harmattan. It is the tree's natural way of saving water and energy to stay alive.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa tamɔ harmattan lɛ, eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Yellow maize leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Adding proper fertilizer or decaying plant manure provides the food maize needs to stay dark green and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná su ni mli kwɔ ni he hiaa lɛ, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii wuji aba.

english: Check the central leaves of your maize plants for small ragged holes and dark, sawdust-like waste. If present, tiny caterpillars are inside the funnels of the plants feeding on the growing tips.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli kɛji bu bibioo ko yɛ mli. Ani egbɛ eshwa ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ? Kɛ nakai ni lɛ, ani ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or gets excess rain early on, the plant focuses all its energy on growing top leaves rather than storing food underground in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo nugbɔ enɛ babaoo mra. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ adalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot fast if they get cut during harvest, get exposed to heat, or lack fresh air. Keeping them bruised-free on raised, well-ventilated racks in the shade keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli, akɛwo la mli, loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ tsɔne ni awo nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-vegetables lɛ ni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turn black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot and happens when tomato roots cannot absorb enough calcium. Irregular watering or sudden dry spells usually block the plant from pulling calcium from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato shishifãi nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli be fɛɛ be loo hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and wrinkling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant juices, or from a plant virus carried by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kɛ nakai kooloi lɛ baa lɛ amli

english: Why does my land yield less food every year when I keep planting maize on the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts the exact same soil nutrients every season. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns natural nitrogen and restores soil health.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afee ekome daa be. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaha adebɔɔ mli nitrogen aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I keep my crops from drying out quickly during the dry Harmattan weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi oya yɛ Harmattan hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the bare soil around your crop roots with dried grass or leaves (mulching) traps moisture in the ground and shields the soil from dry winds and high sun.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni ooobɔle ohe lɛ Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo otsei lɛ ashishi (mulching) lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbiɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tip down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed animal manure helps the leaves turn green again and supports crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why does my cassava farm produce huge bushy stems and leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ tsei agboi kɛ baai shi shikpɔŋ shishi tsei bibii waa lɛ?

english: When cassava soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, the plant puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of roots. Using balanced soil nutrients and avoiding excess nitrogen helps the plant direct food down into the tubers.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmei shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ajie nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii aya bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop yields keep reducing every year if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and soil diseases to build up. Rotating your crop with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil fertility and stops pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nibii.

english: The first rain often only wets the surface layer of the soil, and a long dry spell often follows. If you plant too early, the seeds might sprout and then dry up and die; waiting for steady rains ensures deep soil moisture for survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nuɔ pɛ. ni bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mɛmɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ehi shi.

english: How does spreading dry grass or palm fronds on the soil around my vegetables help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi loo ŋmei tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-vegetables lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, known as mulching, stops weeds from taking over, traps moisture in the ground so you water less, and keeps the soil cool during hot sunny days.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi akaye nɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ewo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist during hot periods helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he. aloo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce enough energy to grow large tubers. Lifting the vines off the ground also prevents soil-borne fungal diseases from rotting the foliage.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulbs agboi lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ ajie wein tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ efiteɔ baai lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ plantains yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide immediate broad shade and cool air, protecting the delicate cocoa plants until they grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni miida oya lɛ haa hulutsoo babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ebuɔ kookoo tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulu lɛ naa.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or beans together with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the corn. Their broad leaves also cover the ground, suppressing weeds and conserving moisture.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa. Baai ni mli kwɔlɔ hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ ni oha hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi.

english: What causes ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small dirt-like powder inside the central whorl?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ muji? Yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the plant to feed on young leaves. Early application of approved organic or chemical sprays into the leaf funnel helps control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ momo lɛ wo tso lɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Do I need to leave big trees on my farm to shade my cocoa plants?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mashi tsei wuji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛha kookoo tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yes, young cocoa trees naturally thrive under canopy shade because direct, harsh sunlight can scorch their delicate leaves and dry out the soil too quickly.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋwɛitsu ko shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ.

english: Should I plant shade trees around my coconut palms to protect them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ he koni mabu he?

english: No, coconut palms need full, direct sunlight throughout the day to grow strong and produce good fruit, so they do not require shade trees.
ga: Dabi, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he hiaa ŋmei tsei yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsei atsu nii koni akɛha hɔnɔ.

english: How do I know if my crops need full sunlight or shade?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hulu loo hulutsoo be fɛɛ he miihia miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Crops like coconuts, cassava, and maize require open sunlight to produce properly, while shade-loving crops like cocoa and ginger need partial shade to prevent heat stress.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ ŋmei biɔ hulu la ni mli tse koni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo tamɔ kookoo kɛ ŋmei he hiaa hulutsoo fioo koni amɛtsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa.

english: Can I plant cocoa trees and coconut trees together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu kokoo tsei kɛ ŋmei tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: It is difficult because coconut trees need full sun while cocoa trees need shade, so you must carefully space them so the coconut trees do not block light unevenly or compete for soil nutrients.
ga: Enɛ wa ejaakɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo he hiaa ŋmei tsei. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, hɔɔŋ he miihia kookoo tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ amɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii tsei lɛ akafee hulutsoo ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee loo amɛkatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is it safe to grow short crops like cassava or vegetables under my coconut trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ mi ŋmei tso lɛ shishi?

english: Yes, while coconuts do not need shade above them, you can grow short crops between young coconut palms to make good use of the empty land without harming the trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii biɔ ni hulutsoo ahi amɛhe moŋ. Shi obaanyɛ odu be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii hu yɛ ŋmeii bibii ateŋ. Koni akɛ he ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni afiteee tsei lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting plantains next to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tso bibioo?

english: Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as temporary umbrellas, providing essential shade to young cocoa seedlings during their vulnerable first couple of years.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ be kukuoo mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni amɛgbɔjɔ lɛ amli.

english: Should I cut down every single tree on my land before I start planting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani mabɔi dumɔ?

english: Not always; if you are planting cocoa, keeping selected native trees provides helpful shade, whereas full clearing is usually done only for crops that need direct sun like coconuts.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be; Kɛji oodu kookoo Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni ahala lɛ akwɛmɔ baaha oná hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hulu la he hiaa amɛ tɛ̃ɛ, tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kwraa lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings drying up and turning brown in the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings do not have strong roots yet and suffer when exposed to direct sunlight, which causes their leaves to burn and dry out.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni wa lolo, ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why are my coconut trees growing very tall but producing very few coconuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ kɛlɛ shi ekɛ ŋmei fioo pɛ woɔ lɛ?

english: Coconut trees often produce few fruits if they are planted under tall forest trees or heavy shade, as they need maximum sunlight to bear heavy fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ koo mli tsei kakadaji ashishi loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ejaakɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia lɛ dani ewo yibii ni tsii.

english: Do shade trees help keep moisture in the soil during the dry season?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, shade trees block direct sun from hitting the ground, which reduces soil evaporation and drops fallen leaves that rot into organic fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei tsiɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi ni nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ amli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛhaa onibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant the food it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: What causes small worms to eat holes in my cabbage leaves early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Yeɔ bu yɛ mi kaabaji baai lɛ amli leebi?

english: Those worms are caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid by butterflies and moths. They chew on leaves to grow, but you can protect your cabbage by picking them off by hand or spraying the plants with a natural neem leaf mixture.
ga: Amɛji ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwuji amli. Amɛyeɔ baai koni amɛdara. Shi obaanyɛ obu cabbage he kɛtsɔ onine ni oookɛfo mli loo ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem baa ni akɛfutuɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but produce small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi shishifãi fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much shade or too much nitrogen, it spends all its energy growing branches and leaves instead of roots. Cassava needs full sunlight and balanced soil to store food in big underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei ná hulutsoo babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai amli yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Hulu ni fa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ja he miihia Cassava koni ekɛ niyenii ato eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ amli.

english: Why didn't the seeds I saved from my last tomato harvest produce good fruit this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee tomato ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from store-bought or hybrid tomatoes often lose their strength in the second generation, leading to weak plants. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures you get strong plants that produce plenty of good fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ tomatoi ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ haa onine shɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii kpakpai babaoo nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants curl their leaves and droop in the afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miibɔle amɛbaai lɛ ahe ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can drink it, so the plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out. They usually recover by evening when the weather cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. Bei pii lɛ, elaajeɔ gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant groundnuts on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting groundnuts in the same spot every year allows soil pests and diseases that attack groundnuts to build up in the dirt. Rotating your farm with crops like maize or sorghum helps clean the soil and keeps your crops healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake oŋmɔ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ ni ehaa onibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I pinch off the extra small branches growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji bibii lɛ? Extra ni miida yɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Removing those small extra shoots, called suckers, directs the plant's water and food straight into making bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasting energy on useless extra leaves.
ga: Nibii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ Atsɛɔ no akɛ sucking out. Enɛ baatsɔɔ nu kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛya tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ feemɔ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai krokomɛi ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my garden egg plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding compost helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves in your farm because their roots steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops all the food and space they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha onibii lɛ niyenii kɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do some farmers cover the ground around their crops with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi haa he ni amɛduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like an umbrella for the soil. It blocks the hot sun from drying out the ground, helping the soil stay wet and cool for a longer time.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni edɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under full sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, shielding young cocoa from excessive sun heat and keeping the soil moist so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he. Ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft rot in the ground when heavy rains fall in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave water standing in the farm, the roots get suffocated from lack of air, allowing fungal diseases to rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu tsiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afite yɛ ŋmeii ahe helai ahewɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during small storms even when they have big bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum bibii amli lɛ? Kɛji jwɛi agbo ko yɛ po

english: Plantain trees fall over easily when pests like tiny worms or stem borers attack their underground roots and stems, weakening the plant's hold on the soil so it cannot support heavy bunches.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutua shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ he ni ekɛkpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baa shi, no hewɔ lɛ enyɛŋ ekwɛ tsei bibii ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the middle tip backwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ naa kɛyaa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips in a V-shape usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key food crop plants need to stay green and build strong stems.
ga: Shishijee ŋmɔŋ ni baa yɛ baai lɛ anaa yɛ V su mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛma amɛshishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but the flowers drop off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ekɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi ni edaaa ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when high heat or dry weather dries up the pollen inside the blossom, preventing the flower from fertilizing and turning into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ ha fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ gĩ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkabote gbalashihilɛ mli ni amɛkawo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking juice from under the leaves and transferring plant viruses that distort growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛ tso mli helai ni fiteɔ dalɛ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why is it better for me to spray chemical pest medicine early in the morning rather than in the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ leebi moŋ fe shwane hulu lɛ?

english: Spraying in the early morning works best because winds are calm so chemicals stay on target, leaf pores are open to absorb the treatment, and heat won't dry up the medicine too fast.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. No hewɔ lɛ tsofai lɛ ji nɔ ni sa. Pores lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ tsofa lɛ. Ni latsaa lɛ haŋ tsofa lɛ agbi oya tsɔ.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same spot on my farm three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ he?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains all the specific nutrients maize needs and gives maize-specific pests a permanent home to build up and attack your future harvests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abɛi lɛ. Ni ehaa ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ kooloi lɛ naa shia ni baahi shi daa ni amɛto owɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ ni amɛtutua amɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, leaving free natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ahaa dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I not spread fertilizer on my farm right before a big rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ anɔ?

english: A heavy downpour will wash away the loose fertilizer granules before the plant roots can soak them up, wasting your money and labor.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ amɛ. Ehaa shika kɛ nitsumɔ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the green leaves on my maize crops turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Leaves turn yellow starting from the tip when the soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves and grow big. Applying well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and strength.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ naa kɛji nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.
