english: Why do my crops produce very small yields when I put many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo fata bu kome he lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants fight each other for the same limited water, sunlight, and soil food, causing all of them to stay small and weak.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly during the dry season even when I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa leebi moŋ?

english: In extreme heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it, so they naturally slow down their growth to save energy and protect themselves from drying out.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny invisible insects like mites or aphids sucking the sap out of young leaves, or from a plant virus carried by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii kɛ baai lɛ shwiemɔ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei ahe nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli loo kɛjɛɔ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die during the afternoon even when the soil around them is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a tiny organism in the soil that enters the plant's roots and blocks the inner tubes that transport water up to the stem and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji nɔ ko bibioo ko ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni boteɔ tsei ashishifãi amli ni etsĩɔ mligbɛ tsɔnei ni kɛ nu yaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do tiny insects eat the flower buds off my cowpea plants before they can bloom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye mi-cowpea tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Insects like flower thrips attack soft new flower buds because they are sweet and full of juice; spraying organic neem oil as soon as buds appear protects them so flowers can form pods.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ fɔfɔii a-thrips lɛ tutuaa fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ejaakɛ amɛmli ŋɔɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Organic neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ je kpo pɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu amɛhe koni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground before it is time to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when rain water sits around them for too long in heavy soil, creating a wet environment where destructive soil fungi multiply and attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ. creating a wet environment Biɛ ji he ni ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baashwere ni ebaatutua ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop all their blossoms without making any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by hot sun, dry soil, or sap-sucking pests like capsids; keeping protective shade trees and controlling pests helps the flowers turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulu la ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Tso lɛ nɔ hulutsoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni etsɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever a heavy wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that can be destroyed beneath the ground by microscopic worms called nematodes or plantain weevil grubs, weakening the tree's grip on the dirt.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo plantain beetles lɛ baanyɛ afite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa bɔ ni tso lɛ kpɛtɛɔ lɛ he waaa.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to tall wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for the tubers growing under the ground, and lifting the leaves onto poles keeps them in the sun and away from damp soil rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Ni kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la ni amɛgbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. During the dry Harmattan season, hot sun and dry air drain water from the leaves faster than the roots can drink, causing the leaves to scorch and yellow if they don't have shade.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Yɛ Harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ mli Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ hoɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ.

english: Why do so many flowers drop off my cocoa trees without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: A cocoa tree naturally produces thousands more flowers than it can support. If the tree is short on water, soil nutrients, or sunlight, it sheds extra flowers to save its strength for the pods it can actually feed.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ nɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo hulu la lɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi krokomɛi ni baaha hewalɛ ahi shi kɛha ŋmeii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ.

english: If I cut off branches from my cocoa tree, won't I lose cocoa pods?
ga: Kɛ mifo kookoo nine lɛ Ani kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ laajeŋ?

english: Pruning actually increases your harvest. When you trim unnecessary branches, air and sunlight flow through the tree, which prevents damp diseases like black pod and directs food straight to healthy pod-bearing stems.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsei lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la baatsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai ni mli ewo fɔ tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ anaa ni ekɛ niyenii yaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the stem as soon as the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet conditions. Rainwater carries fungal spores onto the pods, and if the air around the tree stays humid and damp, the fungus multiplies quickly inside the pod.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. Nugbɔ nu kɛ fungal spores yaa pods lɛ amli. Ni kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ he lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lolo. Fuji lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya yɛ pod lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop growing whenever weeds cover the farm floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ kpaa kwɛ̃mɔ be fɛɛ be ni jwɛi baaha ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that drink up the moisture and food in the soil before your cocoa roots can reach them. They also trap cold air near the soil, slowing down root growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani kookoo shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he. Emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ hu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ daa blɛoo

english: Why does my cocoa tree shed many of its old leaves just before it flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiho baai momo lɛ dani ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Dropping old leaves is a natural way for the cocoa tree to save energy. It discards worn-out leaves so it can focus its food and water on producing fresh leaves, new flowers, and strong pods.
ga: Baai momoi ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni cacao tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he. Ekɛ baai ni efite lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama niyenii kɛ nu nɔ koni ekɛ baai heei, fɔfɔi heei kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why are my cocoa leaves pale green instead of dark green even when it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ ji eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ?

english: Pale green leaves usually mean the tree lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Rain gives the tree water, but without proper plant food in the dirt, the leaves cannot make their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ nuɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ tso niyenii ni sa bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ.

english: Why do straight shoots keep sprouting up around the bottom trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni ja kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi koko tso lɛ

english: These shoots, called chupons, grow when the tree senses stress or wants to renew itself. However, they steal food from the main trunk and branches where pods grow, so removing them keeps the tree productive.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ daa kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli loo ehe miihia ni eda ehee. Shi kɛlɛ, amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ niji ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why do plantain plants help my newly planted cocoa trees survive better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tsei ni midu ehee lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plantains grow broad leaves very quickly that act like natural umbrellas over young cocoa. Their stems also store a lot of water in the ground, keeping the soil cool and damp for young cocoa roots.
ga: Plantains lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei bibii anɔ lɛ oya. Tso lɛ hu toɔ nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛha kookoo shishifãi bibii.

english: Why do pods growing on the outer edges of my cocoa trees look smaller than the ones inside the canopy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ asɛɛgbɛ lɛ feɔ bibii fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pods exposed to direct outdoor sun can get overheated and dry out faster. Pods growing under the protective canopy stay cooler and get a steady supply of tree food, allowing them to grow larger.
ga: Pods ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ baanyɛ adɔ fe nine ni egbi oya. Tso lɛ haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ shishi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa amɛ niyenii daa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow from the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow fast. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or compost when the soil is moist helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Cowpeas and beans are special plants that pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This feeds your maize naturally, improves soil health, and gives you two different crops from the same piece of land.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha o-corn lɛ aye nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ aba kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Fertilizer works best when the crop is young and growing fast—usually two to three weeks after sprouting—and when the soil is moist. Applying it on wet soil allows the plant roots to drink up the nutrients immediately.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei lɛ darako ni amɛmiida oya—bei pii lɛ, otsii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ—kɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ nuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack of soil nutrients, or insect attacks from pests like mirids. Keeping enough shade trees and protecting young flowers from pests helps them grow into full cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen lɛ tutuamɔ. Kɛ́ aha fɔfɔi bibii lɛ hulutsoo ni sa ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and stopping growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by heat stress or a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Keeping the ground around plants covered with mulch and controlling whiteflies keeps the foliage healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ loo hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ kwɛ he ni tso lɛ bɔle lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni akudɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes into my young maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Botemɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni oshi muji ni tsuɔ yɛ mli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center of young maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended biological or chemical treatments saves the growing point of the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava tubers rot when water collects around their roots for too long, causing fungal decay. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed underground by microscopic pests called nematodes or stem borers. Planting clean, healthy suckers and staking bearing plants with bamboo poles keeps them upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ baanyɛ afite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Bamboo tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni aduɔ kɛ tsei ni akɛ bamboo tsei woɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi ja.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes next to my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato wain tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off the wet ground, preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi tsei ahe helai ni ji fungal leaf lɛ anaa.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow so slowly during the first few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak and must compete with aggressive weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early in the first four weeks allows your crops to establish strong roots and grow fast.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ ashi akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdara oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is an essential plant food. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the nutrients they need to grow strong and turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ hewalɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava leaves to curl up and develop yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies and by using stems from sick plants. You can protect your farm by planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ashishifãi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I plant my pepper seedlings far apart instead of close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu pepper dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ fe bɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in small peppers. Spacing them properly lets air flow freely through the crop, which reduces diseases and allows the plants to bear larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli oya. Enɛ haa helai baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high or when the soil gets too dry. Watering your plants regularly and providing light shade during very hot periods helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Nu ni oooha tso lɛ daa ni oha lɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it better to clear my farmland without burning the leftover grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni ashãaa jwɛi kɛ baai ni eshwɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable nutrients in the topsoil and kills beneficial soil creatures like earthworms. Leaving cleared grass to decompose naturally turns it into organic fertilizer that keeps the soil rich and moist for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. ni efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ jwɛi ni he tse lɛ gbɛ ni efite yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees droop and dry up so quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and very large leaves that lose water rapidly under hot sun. Covering the soil around the base of the plant with dry leaves or straw (mulching) keeps the soil cool and retains water longer.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni dara waa ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulching) shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize, or will the cowpeas ruin the maize crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina ŋmãa? Aloo ani tsina ŋmeii baafite ŋmãa tsei?

english: Planting cowpeas with maize is actually beneficial. Cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds your maize while providing you with an additional harvest.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ. Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa oŋmei lɛ niyenii kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fataa he.

english: How do I know if the ragged holes in my young maize leaves are caused by fall armyworm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ fall worms ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ ba?

english: Fall armyworm leaves ragged, torn holes in the central leaves of young maize, often leaving behind a yellowish powder that looks like wet sawdust. Checking your farm early lets you treat the plants before the caterpillars destroy the central growing tip.
ga: Autumn cutworm lɛ haa bu yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ. Okwaafoi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaha onyɛ otsa tso lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ afite ŋmeii ni miida yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my sweet potatoes under the ground are ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Sweet potatoes are usually ready when the leaves start turning yellow and dying back. You can also dig up one tuber and cut it; if it is mature, the white sap inside will dry quickly without turning black.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato lɛ efee klalo akɛ ayeɔ kɛ́ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi. Obaanyɛ okɛ bulb hu atsu nii ni ofo mli. Kɛji ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, nu yɛŋ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baagbi oya ni etsɔŋ ediŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that suck up water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds within the first three to four weeks after planting ensures your crops get all the water and soil nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for leafy growth. When nitrogen is scarce, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Beni nitrogen faaa lɛ Tsei yeɔ baa momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing tall with huge leaves, but the roots underground are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: This happens when soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. High nitrogen forces the cassava plant to put all its energy into growing stems and leaves above ground rather than swelling the tubers below.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha yitso lɛ shishi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die as soon as the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji fɛ̃i be lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight and heat. They require temporary shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to hold soil moisture and block intense sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he hulutsoo.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates sharply. Extreme heat stresses the flower, preventing pollination and causing the plant to drop the flower entirely.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha fɔfɔi lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Tsiɔ pollination naa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling up tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or by a viral infection spread by insects, which damages the leaf tissues as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my vegetables turn black and rot before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ ashishi miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which occurs when a plant cannot absorb enough calcium. It is commonly triggered by uneven watering during hot spells, which stops calcium from moving into the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ. Enɛ haaa calcium aya aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of creeping on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yams are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch direct sunlight, which helps them make energy to swell their underground tubers. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ ebɔɔ hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops must fight each other for limited water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This competition causes them to stretch tall and weak instead of growing thick and strong.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ awuu koni amɛná nu fioo, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily blow down and fall over during heavy winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally have shallow root systems holding up heavy tops. Microscopic worms called nematodes or root-boring insects often eat away these shallow roots, weakening the anchor and causing the plant to collapse.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni fiɔ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo root borers lɛ yeɔ nɛkɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɛɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have natural beneficial bacteria in their root nodules that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil food. When the crop leaves rot into the soil, this natural nitrogen feeds whatever you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ naa bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni tso baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ baaha niyenii aha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: What is the best crop for me to start planting as a new farmer in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji tso ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔ akɛ okwaafonyo hee yɛ Ghana?

english: Staple grains like maize and rice are great starting crops because they have strong local demand, grow relatively fast in a few months, and help you build foundational farming skills before moving to long-term tree crops.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ji shishijee ŋmãa kpakpa yɛ bɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ hewɔ. Edaa oya kwraa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa shishijee okwaayeli he ŋaa dani oyaa be kakadaŋŋ mli dumɔ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my farmland is ready for planting after clearing the bush?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ beni ajie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Your land is ready when large tree stumps, roots, and stubborn weeds are removed, and the topsoil has been loosened so young seeds can easily sprout and push roots into the ground.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛji ajie tsei wuji, shishifãi, kɛ jwɛi ni wa lɛ. Ni ajieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui bibii akwɛ̃ ni amɛtsi amɛshishifãi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: How does clearing and burning the bush affect the crops I plant afterward?
ga: Te jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Burning bush leaves behind ash, which gives your soil a quick temporary nutrient boost for early crops, but doing it repeatedly destroys long-term organic matter and helpful soil insects needed for future farming.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashã lɛ shĩɔ sũ. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa oya yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Shi enɛ ni afeɔ shii abɔ lɛ Ebaakpata nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni he hiaa kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for leaf growth, or that the soil is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai

english: Why does maize grow very tall in some parts of my field but stay short in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi shi ehiɔ shi kuku yɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Soil richness and moisture vary across a field. Areas with deeper soil, better water holding capacity, or higher organic matter produce taller, healthier maize plants than poorer patches.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulutsoo lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ Toɔ nu ni hi loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo lɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ afee shɔŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ fe hei ni shihilɛi gboi yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do rice plants need so much water compared to maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa tsei kɛ akɛto ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in very wet or flooded soils, which prevents weeds from crowding them out and keeps their shallow root systems constantly supplied with moisture.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ loo nu eyi nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi akabote mli, ni ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ akabote mli. Fɛ̃i yɛ jɛmɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my young crops so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ oya?

english: Young crops have small roots and easily lose the fight against weeds for sunshine, water, and soil food, so clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to everything they need to grow.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi lɛ mlɛo koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some crops produce food in a few months while others take years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi woɔ niyenii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ afii babaoo lɛ?

english: Short-season crops like grains focus their energy entirely on rapid flower and seed growth, whereas tree crops like citrus or cocoa must build strong woody trunks and deep roots before they can support fruit.
ga: Be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmaa kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui adalɛ oya nɔ. Esa akɛ tsei tamɔ citrus loo cocoa lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua aduawai.

english: Why are my maize plants falling over right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miigbee shi dani kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over, or lodge, when strong winds push them down because their roots are shallow, their stems have been weakened by insect borers, or they received too much fertilizer early on.
ga: Abele gbeeɔ shi loo ehiɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ yɛ eshishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ hewɔ. Tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ahewɔ. loo enine shɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ mra

english: Why are the grains on my rice heads turning empty or brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa yitso lɛ nɔ lɛ efee efolo loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Empty or discolored rice grains happen when small insect pests suck the liquid out of the young developing grains, or when fungal diseases infect the plant during flowering.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko loo amɛhe su etsake lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii ni yeɔ nu lɛ miinu nu kɛjɛ omɔ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli. aloo beni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: What will happen to my crops if all the big trees on my farm are cut down?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji afolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Removing all trees exposes your crops to harsh direct sunlight and severe heat, which can dry out the plants, burn young leaves, and reduce crop yields.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie tsei lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa aba oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ eha tsei agbi, eshã baai bibii, ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii aba shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning brown and yellow after the surrounding trees were cleared?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni ebɔle mihe lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ beni ajie tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crops adapted to filtered light experience sunshock when shade is suddenly removed. Strong sunlight breaks down the green chlorophyll in the leaves, turning them yellow or brown.
ga: Tsei ni etsake amɛhe amɛwo la ni ajieɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulu la baakpe kɛji ajie shade trukaa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ klorofil eŋɔli ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Efee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do some of my crops need shade trees while others perform better in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi ahe hiaa tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Crops like young cocoa and plantains are sensitive to high heat and water loss, so shade protects them. Other crops like maize and cassava need direct energy from full sunlight to produce grains and tubers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo bibii kɛ plantains bibii nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he waa. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei nɛɛ ahe. Tsei krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa, biɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo dumɔwui kɛ ŋmãa.

english: Can I plant food crops directly under large shade trees on my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Large trees compete with crops for water, sunlight, and nutrients. While light shade is good for some crops, planting directly under heavy tree canopies usually stunts crop growth due to lack of light.
ga: Tsei wuji kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii, eyɛ mli akɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse lɛ hi kɛha tsei komɛi moŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa yɛ la ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does my farmland lose all its topsoil whenever heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Tree roots and fallen leaves act as a protective cover that holds the soil together. Without trees, heavy rain washes away the fertile topsoil where your crops get their nutrients.
ga: Tso shishifãi kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome. Kɛji tsei bɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ, he ni ŋmɔshi nibii naa amɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up so fast during the dry season without shade trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Shade trees reduce ground temperatures and slow down evaporation. Without them, direct heat bakes the earth and causes moisture in the soil to evaporate rapidly.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ baa shi ni ehaa la ni hoɔ oya lɛ baa shi. Kɛ amɛbɛ Dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ atsɔ oya.

english: Why are my crops growing poorly after the land was cleared with heavy machines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛ tsɔnei ni tsii efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy machinery squashes and compacts the earth, making it hard for crop roots to spread, breathe, and absorb water. It also scrapes away the rich surface soil.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii miimiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛha tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã, amɛmu, ni amɛmɔmɔ nu. Ejieɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ hu.

english: Is burning trees and bush on my land before planting harmful to my future crops?
ga: Ani tsei kɛ tsei bibii ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ lɛ yeɔ wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awui?

english: Burning destroys organic matter and kills helpful soil organisms that decompose plant material into plant food, leading to weaker soil fertility over time.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni gbálaa tsei amli nibii amli kɛfeɔ tsei niyenii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do tall trees around my farm stop strong winds from destroying my plantain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ kwɔlɔ nɛkɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔ lɛ tsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekafite dumɔwui ni midu lɛ.

english: Tall trees act as natural windbreaks. They slow down strong gusts of wind so that heavy, shallow-rooted crops like plantains do not snap or get blown over.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ he tsɔne. Amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni tsei ni shishifãi ni tsii ni mli ekɔɔɔ tamɔ plantain lɛ akakumɔ loo akatswa amɛ kɛya.

english: How do trees on my farmland help keep the soil cooler during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tree canopies block direct solar radiation, while tree roots pull cool water from deep underground and release moisture into the surrounding air, creating a cooler microclimate for nearby crops.
ga: Tso lɛ yiteŋ tsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei shishifãi gbalaa nu ni mli ejɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli ejɔ baa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a canopy that protects seedlings from sunburn and keeps the soil moist while root systems develop.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo bibii ewo mli lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I remove some of the small sucker shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: When too many suckers grow around a single plantain tree, they steal water, light, and nutrients from the main stem. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only the strongest ones, ensuring the main stem produces a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe Dumɔwu kome pɛ lɛ, ebaaju nu, la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ awo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy green growth, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its green color and form healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout properly if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The season's first rain often only wet the surface soil, leaving lower layers dry. If a dry spell follows, germinated seeds dry out and die, which is why waiting for regular, steady rainfall ensures enough soil moisture for seeds to establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔ̃ɔ pɛ. Ha shishigbɛ fã lɛ agbi. Kɛji hɔmɔ nifeemɔ ko nyiɛ sɛɛ Beni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ pɛ lɛ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, ni baa daa lɛ mɛmɔ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Does it matter which direction the leaf buds point when I plant cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Ani ehe hiaa beni aduɔ ŋmei ni afolɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down forces new shoots to turn themselves around underground, wasting energy and leading to weaker foliage and smaller root tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Tso lɛ tsei ni miida ni tsɔɔ shishi lɛ haa tsei heei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni efiteɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai bibii kɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to feed the tuber growing under the soil. Lifting the vines off the ground on tall stakes maximizes sunlight exposure and prevents leaf rot caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni eye ebua bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu la lɛ aba babaoo. ni atsĩ baa ni sũ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers before any tomatoes start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miishwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani tomatoi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or irregular watering. Consistent watering during hot periods cools the plant down and allows the flowers to successfully pollinate and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl upward and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking leaf sap and spreading viruses. Controlling insect pests early keeps the leaves flat so they can continue growing and producing peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ Mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my groundnuts produce healthy green leaves above ground but very few nuts under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts need loose, soft soil so the flower pegs can bend down and push underground to form nuts. Hard or compacted soil prevents pegs from entering the ground, forcing the plant to spend all its energy on leaf growth instead.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia ŋmeii. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni anyɛ abɔle fɔfɔi lɛ ashishi ni ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee ŋmei. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ moŋ.

english: How does growing cowpeas or beans on my field improve the soil for my next crop of maize?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally captures nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil. When the legume crop finishes, that leftover nitrogen remains in the soil as natural fertilizer for nutrient-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa agbe naa lɛ Nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa kɛha tsei ni he hiaa lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Can I plant cocoa and rubber together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu kookoo kɛ rɔba yɛ he kome?

english: While both grow well in forest zones, rubber trees grow very tall and develop deep roots that can compete with cocoa for water and nutrients. If you plant them together, you must space them very wide so the rubber shade does not block all the sunlight from the cocoa.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛ fɛɛ amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni tsei yɔɔ lɛ moŋ, Shi rɔbɔt tsei daa waa ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ amɛkɛ kookoo abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛji okɛ amɛ wo he kome Ehe miihia ni okɛ amɛ ahi he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ waa. Bɔni afee ni rɔba tsɔne lɛ akatsi hulu la fɛɛ ni jɛɔ kookoo lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Can I plant food crops like plantain while waiting for my young tree crops to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains be mli ni mimɛɔ ni midumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Yes, intercropping young cash crops with food crops like plantain or cocoyam is beneficial. The food crops provide food and early income for your family while giving temporary shade to the young trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaadu shika ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantain loo cocoa. Dumɔ niyenii ni okɛ niyenii kɛ shishijee shika aha oweku lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ hu náa hɔnɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: How many years after planting cocoa do I have to wait before harvesting the pods?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko du kookoo sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ emɛ dani ekpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties recommended in Ghana usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome ni akɛba Ghana lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: How long does a rubber tree take before it is ready for harvesting latex?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani rɔbɔt tso ko feɔ klalo ni ekɛbaakpa e-latex lɛ?

english: Rubber trees require a long waiting period. It takes about 6 to 7 years of growth before the trees become mature enough to tap for latex.
ga: Rɔba tsei biɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani amɛmɛ. Eheɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani tso lɛ daa dani enyɛɔ etswaa nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my rubber tree is thick enough to start tapping?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-gum tso lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi gbee?

english: A rubber tree is ready for tapping when the trunk circumference measures at least 50 centimeters at a height of 1 meter from the ground level.
ga: Rɔba tsei efee klalo kɛha gbee kɛji akɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ shɛɔ sɛntimitai 50 kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mita 1.

english: Why is it important for me to talk to an agricultural extension officer before planting tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko agba sane dani madu tsei?

english: Extension officers help you test your soil, select improved crop varieties, and teach you correct tree spacing, which prevents costly mistakes before you invest your money.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi lɛ baaye abua bo ni oka shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ. Halamɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni etsɔɔ bo bɔ ni ooofee osaa bɔ ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni otsiɔ tɔmɔi ni jara wa waa lɛ anaa dani okɛ oshika lɛ woɔ mli.

english: Does rubber grow well in every part of Ghana?
ga: Ani rɔba kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kpokpai fɛɛ anɔ?

english: No, rubber needs regions with high annual rainfall and deep, well-drained soil, which is why it thrives mainly in the Western, Central, and Eastern regions of Ghana.
ga: Dabi, Yang biɔ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa daa afi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ hewɔ ni rɔba kwɛ̃ɔ titri yɛ Ghana anaigbɛ, teŋgbɛ kɛ bokagbɛ kpokpai lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: What main costs should I plan for when starting a new tree crop farm?
ga: Mɛɛ shika titri esa akɛ mato he gbɛjianɔ kɛji mije tso ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: You need to budget for land clearing, buying certified seedlings from approved nurseries, labor for digging holes and planting, and fertilizer or weed control for the first few years.
ga: Esa akɛ oná shika he gbɛjianɔtoo kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ. Hemɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ. Nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo kɛha bu ni atsa kɛ tsei adumɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die during the harsh dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn under full sun; they need shade plants like plantain to cover them during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu lɛ shãa kwraa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I measure exact distances between trees instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu he pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper tree spacing ensures that each plant receives enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients, preventing diseases from spreading easily and improving overall yield.
ga: Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsi helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo lɛ naa ni oha nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow leaves, or when too much standing water is preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. aloo be mli ni nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu.

english: How do I know if my land is ready for me to start planting cassava?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu ŋmei?

english: Your soil is ready when it is moist but not muddy, loose enough for roots to spread easily, and cleared of big weeds that would steal light and nutrients from the young plants.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ edɔ shi ebɛ muji. Eha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo bɔ ni sa. ni ojie jwɛi wuji ni juɔ la kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ.

english: Why does harvesting crops on the same piece of land year after year make the harvest smaller each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akpaa daa afi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ akpaa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Crops pull specific nutrients out of the earth as they grow. If you plant the same crop repeatedly without giving the soil fertilizer or rest, the soil loses those nutrients and cannot feed new plants properly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo okɛ hejɔɔmɔ wooo mli lɛ Sũ lɛ laajeɔ nakai niyenii lɛ ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua tsei heei jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the middle leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the soft inner leaves of maize. They feed on the plant's growing point, which slows down growth unless you treat them early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Amɛyeɔ nii yɛ hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ, ni no baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ja otsa amɛ mra.

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot inside the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni ha mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifo amɛ?

english: Yam rot is caused by tiny worms called nematodes or microscopic fungi in the soil that enter the tuber through small scratches, especially when the soil stays too wet for long periods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ baa ji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli kɛboteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli, titri lɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep falling off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa blossoms fall off when the tree does not get enough water or nutrients, or when tiny insects called midges are not present to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ náaa nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ Nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ baa koni ebawo fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves drop and look sleepy during the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni ewɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from losing too much moisture, but recovers when the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tso lɛ baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni efiteɔ lɛ he. Shi ebaahi shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli bawo wu.

english: How does heavy rainfall right after flowering hurt my pepper harvest?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔi asɛɛ lɛ saa mi-pepper kpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Hard rain washes away pollen from the pepper blossoms and can physically knock the flowers off the plant before fruit can form, leading to fewer peppers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ pollen ni jɛɔ pepper fɔfɔi amli lɛ he. Ni ebaanyɛ eha fɔfɔii ajɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai aba. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, chili ŋmɔtɔi fioo pɛ baaba.

english: Why do extension officers suggest planting cowpeas or beans alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas pull natural plant food from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow next to crops like maize, they leave that extra food in the soil for the maize to use.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ekwɛ̃ yɛ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ Amɛshiɔ nakai niyenii ni fa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmãa lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my plantain suckers too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plantain trees are planted too close together, their wide leaves block the sunlight from each other, and their roots fight for the same water and soil food, resulting in smaller bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso lɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei krokomɛi anɔ lɛ naa. Ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ sũ henɔ kome mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ bibioo

english: Why should I sort my corn seeds and plant them one by one instead of throwing a handful in each hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ amli ni madu amɛ komekomei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Sorting seeds ensures only healthy, damage-free seeds go into the ground. Planting them individually prevents crowding, allowing each seedling to get enough space, sunlight, and soil nutrients to produce large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui amlihalamɔ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni efiteee pɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tso kome yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaatsi mɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa gbɛ, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I test a sample of my corn seeds before planting to know if they will actually sprout in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi makwɛ dani madu koni mana kɛji amɛbaakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Take a sample of 100 seeds and place them on a wet cloth or moist soil for a few days. The number of seeds that sprout gives you the germination rate; if 85 or more sprout, your seed batch is healthy and ready for planting.
ga: Bua dumɔwui 100 he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ naa ni okɛwo mama ni mli efɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi. Dumɔwui ayibɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ haa onáa bɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amɛhaa lɛ. Kɛji tsei 85 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu.

english: Why are the corn seeds I bought from the dealer covered in a bright pink or blue color?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mihe kɛjɛ jarayelɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ ji pinki loo bluu ni kpɛɔ lɛ?

english: The bright color is a protective chemical coating applied to commercial seeds. It prevents soil insects, harmful fungi, and birds from destroying the seed before it has a chance to sprout.
ga: Su ni kpɛɔ lɛ ji tsofa ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni akɛwoɔ jarayeli dumɔwui anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anaa Fung ni yɔɔ oshara Kɛ okpoi fiteɔ dumɔwui dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How does using a planting board with fixed holes help me get a better yield from my maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni bu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni minine shɛɔ ŋmãa kpakpa nɔ?

english: A planting board ensures every seed is placed at the exact same distance and depth. Equal spacing stops plants from competing with one another for water and nutrients, leading to uniform growth across the farm.
ga: Dumɔwui ahe diski lɛ haa akwɛɔ koni akɛ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ awo he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ kɛ mlibotemɔ kome. Gbɛjegbɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ baatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkaye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: How deep into the soil should I place my corn seed when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Plant corn seeds about 3 to 5 centimeters deep, which is roughly the length of your thumb knuckle. If planted too shallow, the seed can dry out or be eaten by birds; if planted too deep, it runs out of energy before reaching the surface.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5, ni ji aaafee ŋmãa lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmãa lɛ. Kɛji adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ agbi loo okpoi aye. Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, hewalɛ baaho dani eshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ.

english: What should I do if two maize seeds sprout right next to each other in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii enyɔ kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Gently remove the weaker seedling and leave the stronger one. This process, called thinning, prevents the two plants from stealing food and water from each other, resulting in a healthier overall harvest.
ga: Jiemɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ blɛoo ni oshi nɔ ni he wa lɛ. Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ tsɔne ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Enɛ ji koni tsei enyɔ lɛ akaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young corn plants curl up into thin tubes during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn plants curl their leaves inward as a natural defense mechanism to shield themselves from direct sunlight and reduce water loss through evaporation during hot, dry periods.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni amɛkɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eha nu ni laajeɔ yɛ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young corn turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that the plant is lacking nitrogen, a vital nutrient for growth, or that the soil is waterlogged and suffocating the roots. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli su lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to remove weeds around my corn very early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni maná mi-abele kɛjɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Young corn grows slowly in its first few weeks, while weeds grow very fast. Removing weeds early ensures they do not steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your corn needs to establish strong roots.
ga: Abɛi bibii daa fiofio yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli. Yɛ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa o-ŋmãa lɛ koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my young corn after planting?
ga: Kɛji adu lɛ, ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata gbekɛbii abele lɛ he beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Apply the first round of fertilizer about 10 to 14 days after the seeds sprout, and a second round when the corn reaches knee height. This timing gives the crop energy right when it is growing its leaves and forming cobs.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mli aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. kɛ kpokpaa ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ beni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe Be nɛɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ be mli ni ebaakwɛ baai ni ebatsɔ ŋmãa pɛ.

english: How long should I wait to harvest my crops after spraying them with chemicals?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Every crop chemical has a mandatory waiting period, known as the withdrawal period. You must wait a specific number of days after spraying before harvesting so the chemical breaks down safely, ensuring the food is non-toxic for consumers.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ yɛ mɛmɔ be ni ale lɛ akɛ jiemɔ be. Esa akɛ omɛ gbii pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ tsofai lɛ ni okɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani okpa tsofai lɛ koni amɛfite shweshweeshwe. Ha oná nɔmimaa akɛ niyenii lɛ efeŋ nɔ ni gbeɔ mɛi ni yeɔ lɛ.

english: Will putting extra chemical medicine on my sick crops make them recover faster?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai babaoo fata mitso ni hela mɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ aya nɔ oya?

english: No, applying more than the recommended dose can burn the crop's leaves and damage the root system. Always use the specified measurement so the plant recovers safely without toxicity.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ni fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ baai lɛ ni efite shishifãi lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ susumɔi ni atsɔɔ lɛ atsu nii koni tso lɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akafite lɛ.

english: Should I spray crop medicine as soon as I notice pests eating my leaves?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ tsei anɔ kɛji mina kooloi ni yeɔ mibaai lɛ pɛ?

english: Yes, treating pest damage early prevents loss in overall yield, but you must first identify the correct pest to ensure you apply the right chemical treatment.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ akafite. Shi esa akɛ oyɔse tsɛŋemɔ hela ni sa lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ okɛ tsofai ni sa miitsu nii.

english: How can I tell if the chemical or fertilizer I applied to my crops is actually working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ miitsu nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: If the treatment is effective, within a week or two you will see healthy green shoots, active leaf growth, and a reduction in insect damage or disease spots.
ga: Kɛji tsofafeemɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ mli Obaana ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa. baai lɛ miidara ni kooloi ni fiteɔ loo helai ahe tsɔi lɛ miiba shi.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and failing to reach their expected height?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni miisumɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves and stunted growth indicate nutrient deficiency, especially nitrogen. Supplying the proper fertilizer restores leaf color and allows the plant to resume normal growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa. titri lɛ nitrogen Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is my cassava crop producing smaller yields than the expected maximum target?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ faaa fe yibiiwoo ni fe fɛɛ ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Crops cannot reach their maximum yield capacity if they lack adequate soil nutrients, proper water, or correct plant spacing, causing the plant to produce smaller roots.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ awo yibii babaoo kɛji niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. nu ni sa loo tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ shishifãi bibii.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves inward to lessen surface exposure to intense heat and prevent precious water from evaporating too fast.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni hulutsoo ni naa wa waa aba shi, ni nu ni jara wa lɛ akafo oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall and thin without producing fruit under shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes require full sunlight to manufacture energy for flowering and fruiting. Under tree shade, the plant stretches upward searching for light, spending all its energy on stem growth instead of fruit.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia tomatoi koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo. tsei ashishi Tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei ahe yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my garden egg plants falling off without turning into vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma lɛ?

english: Crops drop their flowers when stressed by water shortage or extreme heat. The plant intentionally sheds flowers to preserve energy and water needed to keep the rest of the plant alive.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu ni faaa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛfeɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu ni he hiaa koni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi lɛ he.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farmland make my next maize crop grow so well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa mi-ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, naturally enriching the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves are tender and easily damaged by direct sun. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains next to young cocoa provides living shade that keeps the plants cool and moist while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Nurse tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe jɔɔ be mli ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward to protect themselves from intense heat and reduce water loss. It is a natural defense mechanism to save moisture until temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛha nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing tall with lots of leaves, but the tubers under the ground are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, cassava puts all its energy into growing green foliage above ground rather than storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baawo baai eŋɔli ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why are the lower branches of my oil palm trees turning yellow and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing of older palm leaves usually signals a lack of potassium or water in the soil. The tree naturally steals nutrients from its older, lower fronds to nourish the fresh, growing leaves at the crown.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni egbɔ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium loo nu bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why did my mature plantain tree tip over after a light wind when the stem was healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko sɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo moŋ?

english: Plantain trees can look healthy on top while microscopic worms called nematodes damage their roots underground. Weakened roots cannot anchor the heavy stem into the soil, causing the entire plant to collapse.
ga: Dumɔwui baanyɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fiteɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ tso ni wa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbee shi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the growing center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, a destructive pest that lays eggs on green maize leaves. The larvae hide deep inside the central whorl of the plant, feeding on new leaves before they fully expand.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baa eŋɔli nɔ. Lalabii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ baai heei ni ayeɔ dani amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa kwraa lɛ nɔ.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the growing fruit. It commonly occurs when soil moisture fluctuates between extremely dry and wet spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi waa kɛ be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ teŋ.

english: Why are the flower buds dropping off my pepper plants before making fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Without stable soil moisture and moderate temperatures, the plant cannot support fruit growth and drops its flowers to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ kpe. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ hulutsoo ni sa bɛ. Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwie shi koni ehi shi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and dry up while still attached to the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, dark foliage. Pruning extra shade branches to let air and sunlight through reduces humidity around the pods and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ, ni mli efɔ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofo tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni eha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ aba shi. pods lɛ ni etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why is it important for me to weed around my young yam vines before the main rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Atomɔ tsei dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa?

english: Weeds grow much faster than yam vines and consume the initial rainwater and soil nutrients first. Clearing weeds early ensures that the yam plant gets all the sunlight and feeding it needs to build big tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ni amɛyeɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii klɛŋklɛŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha sweet potato tsei lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and scorching in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshã yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted around them to act as natural umbrellas until their roots grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ. koni etsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaa kɛyashi eshishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa

english: Why do my maize plants stay thin and produce tiny cobs when I plant several seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ko lɛ, midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots compete for the same small pocket of water, food, and sunlight in the soil. Giving each seed its own space allows the plant to grow thick stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tsitsi ni mli tse kɛ tsitsi agbo.

english: Why do weeds slow down my crop growth even after I have added fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that drink water and eat soil nutrients faster than your crops. If you do not clear weeds first, they will consume the fertilizer meant to nourish your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni nuɔ nu ni eyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, Amɛbaaye ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni ekɛha onibii titrii lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise planting cowpeas or beans in the same farm with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow green and healthy, so growing them together naturally feeds the soil.
