ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall sticks to climb on instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɔɔ ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. When the leaves get plenty of sun, the plant produces more energy to build large tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ baajie hewalɛ babaoo kpo ni ekɛfee bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress or dry soil. When the soil lacks moisture during hot periods, the plant sheds its flowers to conserve water and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ latsaa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi hewɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why should I wait after the very first rain of the year before sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: The first rain after a long dry spell is often followed by several hot days without rain. If you plant immediately, the dry soil will scorch the newly sprouting seeds before the reliable rainy season fully starts.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ Bei pii lɛ, gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ waa ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baashã dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi kwraa.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stem cutting to ensure it sprouts well in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select the thick, hard middle portion of a mature, healthy cassava stem. The soft top tips dry out too quickly, while the very bottom part of the stem is too woody and takes longer to sprout shoots.
ga: Halamɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni mli tse ni wa ni miida ni ehe wa lɛ. Tso bibioo lɛ naagbee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ. yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ ji tso tsɔ ni eheɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Which plantain sucker is the best one for me to transplant to my new farm plot?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi akɛ mikɛbaaya miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Look for 'sword suckers', which have narrow, blade-like leaves and a broad bulb at the base. They have more stored energy and grow into stronger plantain trees than suckers with wide, flat leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword bud’, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ ŋmei kɛ bulb ni mli kwɔ yɛ shishigbɛ. Amɛyɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛto ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ dumɔwui ni he wa fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and turning light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a sign of a virus usually carried and spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus weakens the leaves so they cannot trap sun energy properly, which stops the tomato plant from producing good fruit.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji hela ko ni bei pii lɛ ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Virus lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛto hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii kpakpai.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is short on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or when the soil stays waterlogged for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ loo kɛ́ nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, naturally restoring your soil's fertility for the next season.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Taakɛ eji lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small flowers before pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Dani pods lɛ baafee?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by a lack of water, poor soil nutrients, or insect attacks. It can also happen if there are not enough tiny insects called midges around to transfer pollen between the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Niyenii ni ehiii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny without bearing good fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛwooo yibii ni amɛfeɔ shwiili kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food. They stretch upward as fast as possible to reach the sun instead of spending energy on growing thick stems and big fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out in full sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get more sunlight, which helps the plant grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni eha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la babaoo aba. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kwɛɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves drop down and wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out, and it will recover as the air cools down in the evening.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. ni ebaahe ejɔ lɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and developing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from making food properly, which causes small tubers and poor harvest yields.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ ji mɛi ni hiɛɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa ŋmeii bibii ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why am I advised to trim off some of the lower leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Trimming lower leaves removes old foliage that consumes energy without producing food. It also allows fresh air to blow through the plant, keeping the stems dry and stopping diseases from spreading.
ga: Kɛ́ afo shishigbɛ baai lɛ, ejieɔ baai momo ni yeɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ebɔɔɔ lɛ. Eha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ agbi ni ehaaa hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops mature much faster than mine even though we planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tsei lɛ daa oya fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu amɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Your neighbor is likely using certified improved or hybrid seeds designed to mature early and resist dry conditions. Traditional seeds saved from previous harvests often take longer to grow and yield fruits.
ga: Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ loo dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli ni afee koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli lɛ miitsu nii. Bei pii lɛ, kusum dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: The first rain of the year is often a false start followed by a long dry spell. If your seeds germinate after that first rain, the young sprouts will dry up and die in the hot soil before the main rains actually return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ ji amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ aku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside young cocoa protects them from harsh heat and helps hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafee dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa, ni ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Too many shoots compete with the main plantain stem for food and water, which leads to small bunches. Leaving only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main tree gets enough energy to produce big fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. ni haa tsei bibii kwɛ̃ɔ Kɛ́ ashi tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need for leaf growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni baai lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: What is eating the soft inner leaves of my young maize plants and leaving holes?
ga: Mɛni ye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai bibii lɛ ni eshi bu?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on the center shoot of young maize. Spraying approved natural neem remedies or targeted insecticides early in the morning helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long in heavy or poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away easily and keeps the roots dry.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Etsɛ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ oya, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can trap direct sunlight. When the leaves receive enough light, they generate the food needed to grow large, healthy tubers underneath the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ŋmeii wuji ni he wa lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of insect pollinators. Giving the plants consistent water during dry spells helps the blossoms turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ faaa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei anɔ nu daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant sap, or by viruses spread by whiteflies. Managing insects early protects the new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Mra be mli ŋmeii akwɛmɔ Ebaaye abua ni ebu baai heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil while the crop is actively growing. Applying it on dry ground causes plant burn, and applying it right before heavy rain washes the nutrients away.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ. Ni kɛ akɛtsu nii dani nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ hoɔ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. Mulching keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, stops soil moisture from drying up quickly, and suppresses weed growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsi shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa

english: Why should I switch to planting my maize in neat straight lines instead of scattering the seeds the way my family has always done?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake kɛya ŋmãa dumɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã tamɔ bɔ ni miweku lɛ feɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures each maize seed gets enough space, sunlight, and soil nutrients to grow strong, while also making it much easier for you to weed, fertilize, and harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Extension officer, people are rushing to buy hybrid cassava stems, but what actually makes them better than our local stems?
ga: Nɔyaa he nitsulɔ Mɛi kɛ oyaiyeli tee koni amɛyahe hybrid cassava. Shi mɛni haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi fe wɔ maŋ lɛ mli srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Hybrid cassava stems are bred to withstand common pests and diseases like Cassava Mosaic Virus, and they produce much higher yields of larger tubers in a shorter growing period.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmei tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ ŋmei mosaic hela. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni dara kwraa yɛ be kukuoo mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: If I switch from using green manure to chemical fertilizers, will it spoil my farmland over time?
ga: Kɛji mitsake kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli kɛtee tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli Ani miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the plant quickly, but using only chemical fertilizer without organic matter can harm soil health over time; using a balanced mix of both preserves soil quality while boosting yield.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya. Shi tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ nɔ awui yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ futu mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ehaa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ.

english: How many days after planting my maize should I expect to see the sprouts coming out of the dirt?
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmãa lɛ, gbii enyiɛ mli esa akɛ okpa gbɛ akɛ ebaaje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: In good, moist soil, maize seeds usually sprout within 4 to 7 days after planting.
ga: Yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii 4 kɛyashi 7 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: I transplanted my tomato seedlings three days ago, but their leaves are drooping; did I ruin them?
ga: Midu tomato dumɔwui gbii etɛ ni eho nɛ. Shi amɛbaai lɛ gbee shi. Ani mikpata amɛhiɛ?

english: Transplanted seedlings often droop for the first few days due to transplant shock while their roots adjust to new soil; with gentle watering and protection from harsh sun, they will bounce back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo lɛ amli yɛ dumɔwui ni adu lɛ ahe gbeyeishemɔ hewɔ beni amɛshishifãi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ afɔ amɛ nu blɛoo ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ, amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers instead of turning them into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as sudden hot spells, inconsistent watering, or a lack of key nutrients in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ hulutsoo trukaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli nibii titrii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why are the leaves on my young cassava plants turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellow and curling leaves are a sign of insect attack, usually whiteflies, or a viral disease; removing affected leaves early prevents it from spreading to the rest of the farm.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ebatutua amɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji whitefly loo hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli. Baai ni ena hela lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ hei krokomɛi.

english: If I put too much fertilizer on my crops, will it burn and destroy my farm?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ Ani ebaashã ni efite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, excessive fertilizer places too much salt near the roots, which draws water out of the plant and causes the leaves to burn and dry up.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaha ŋmei abɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tsɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni ehaa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines keep creeping on the hot soil and turning brown instead of growing long and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ miiho kɛmiitsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up toward sunlight; leaving them on the hot ground causes the leaves to burn and exposes them to soil diseases.
ga: Tso tso he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ashã ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ helai aba.

english: How many days do I need to wait after spraying weedkiller before it is safe to plant my seeds?
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ eshwie shi lɛ, gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooodu dumɔwui?

english: You typically need to wait between 7 to 14 days after applying standard weedkiller so the chemical breaks down in the soil and does not kill your new crop seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehe baahia ni omɛ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 beni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha tsofai lɛ agbala yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfiteee odumɔwui heei lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die so easily if I plant them in full sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like newborn babies—their root systems are still small and fragile. Direct sunlight dries out their tender leaves and soil quickly before the roots are strong enough to pull up enough water, causing the seedling to scorch and die.
ga: Kakao tso bibioo tamɔ abifao ni afɔ lɛ ehee. Shishifã lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya dani shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashã ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do young crop seedlings get destroyed by insects much more easily than older, bigger plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaaa kwraa akɛ kooloi bibii baafite dumɔwui bibii fe tsei ni eda ni dara lɛ?

english: Young plants are still developing their natural toughness and outer defense layers. Their soft, juicy leaves are easy for pests to chew, whereas mature plants have tougher leaves and stems that insects find harder to destroy.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ miifee amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ kɛ kponɔgbɛ hebuu fã lɛ lolo. Amɛbaai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ waaa kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Shi tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ baai kɛ shishifãi ni wa waa ni ewa akɛ kooloi baakpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Why do my young maize plants turn pale yellow after heavy rains fall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away nitrogen—the main nutrient that makes leaves green—deep into the soil. Because young maize plants have short roots, they cannot reach the buried nutrients until their root system grows deeper.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai feɔ eŋɔli lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi yɔɔ kuku. No hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ ana niyenii ni afu lɛ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ mli.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer when my crop is still small rather than waiting until it starts flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo tso lɛ mli nu be mli ni eji gbekɛ lolo moŋ fe ni mamɛ ni ebɔi fɔfɔi?

english: Applying fertilizer early gives the young plant the building blocks it needs to develop strong roots and sturdy stems. A plant needs a solid body structure early on so it can support heavy fruits or grains later.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Ehaa tsei bibii lɛ náa shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Tsei he miihia gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa mra. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni enyɛ eye ebua aduawai loo dumɔwui ni tsii sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my young cassava plants early instead of waiting until they grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Cassava tsei bibii mra Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni eya ŋwɛi?

english: Young cassava plants have small leaves that cannot block sunlight from reaching the ground, allowing weeds to grow fast and steal light, water, and nutrients. Once cassava grows tall, its canopy shades out the ground and naturally slows down weed growth.
ga: Cassava tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii. ni nyɛŋ atsĩ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei da lɛ Eshishifã lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I put dry grass or straw around the base of my young vegetable plants during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi abɔle mitsei bibii lɛ ashishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around young plants with dry leaves or straw acts like a blanket. It protects weak, shallow roots from hot weather and keeps moisture in the ground longer so the small plant does not dry out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔni afee ni tsei bibii akagbi

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt and droop right after I move them from the nursery into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings damages their fine root hairs, making it hard for them to suck up water immediately. Exposing them to direct field sun right away causes water to leave the leaves faster than the damaged roots can replace it.
ga: Kɛ́ otsi dumɔwui lɛ, ebaafite shishifãi lɛ ahe yitsɔi bibii lɛ. Ehaa ewaa akɛ aaaŋɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nu ashi baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi ni efite lɛ baanyɛ atsake lɛ.

english: Why do my young pepper plants drop their leaves when the weather suddenly becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso bibioo lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ? Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa?

english: Dropping leaves is a young plant's way of saving its own life during extreme heat. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces the amount of water it loses through evaporation while its small root system is still struggling.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahereɔ tsei bibii awala yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baaha nu ni laajeɔ kɛyaa la mli lɛ nɔ aba shi yɛ be mli ni shishifã bibioo lɛ Ekɛ naagbai miikpe lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my young maize stalks fall over easily when strong winds blow early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ ŋmãa be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young maize plants initially grow upwards faster than their roots grow sideways. Until the plant forms support roots near the base of the stem, piling soil around the base helps keep it standing upright during storms.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, abɛi tsei bibii lɛ daa oya fe shishifãi ni daa yɛ afã. Kɛyashi tso lɛ baafi shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ. heaping dirt around Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers seem to sit in the soil for weeks without growing new leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛtara shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ otsii babaoo ni baa hee ko ejeee kpo lɛ?

english: After planting, a plantain sucker spends its energy underground establishing new roots first. Once the root foundation is strong enough to absorb water and food, the plant will rapidly sprout new leaves above ground.
ga: Beni adu Plantain suckers lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ shishi hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ shishifãi heei klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ́ shishitoo lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops look yellow after heavy rains wash through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away essential nutrients in the topsoil—a process called leaching. Without these nutrients, especially nitrogen, crop leaves turn yellow because they lack the food needed to stay green and healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaching. Kɛji niyenii nɛɛ bɛ titri lɛ nitrogen Tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Can I plant fresh cocoa trees on land where deep soil has been dug up and moved around?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ kookoo tsei heei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akumɔ mli shɔŋŋ ni ajie kɛtee he kroko lɛ nɔ?

english: Disturbed or excavated land loses its fertile topsoil layer. Cocoa seedlings will struggle to grow there unless you replenish the organic matter and soil nutrients using compost or manure before planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni agbala mli loo atsa lɛ baafite eshikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni baa nii lɛ. Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ jɛmɛ. Ja okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ dani odu.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is naturally good for cocoa growing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha adebɔɔ mli kookoo dumɔ?

english: Good cocoa soil is dark, crumbly, deep enough for roots to spread, and holds moisture without staying waterlogged. Soil that is too sandy dries out too quickly, and heavy clay locks up roots.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ mli bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu bɛ mli Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ tsɔ lɛ baagbi oya tsɔ. ni shikpɔŋ sũ ni mli tse lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Is it good for me to plant my cocoa right at the edge of a stream?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu kookoo yɛ faa ko naa?

english: While cocoa trees need moisture, planting directly on the edge of a stream can drown the roots during high water levels. Waterlogged soil rots the roots and prevents them from breathing air.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia kookoo tsei moŋ, shi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ faa ko naa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ be mli ni nu lɛ fa babaoo lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaaa amɛmu kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Will using muddy or dirty water from a stream harm my cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani nu ni mli ewo muji loo muji ni jɛ faa mli lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ awui?

english: Heavy mud and pollutants in water can clog the fine roots of young plants, making it difficult for them to drink water and absorb nutrients, which can stunt their growth or kill them.
ga: Muji ni tsii kɛ nu mli mujiwoo baanyɛ atsĩ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ anaa, ni eha ewa aha amɛ akɛ amɛaanu nu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛdalɛ naa loo egbe amɛ.

english: What happens to my crop's roots if chemicals contaminate the farm's nearby water source?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji tsofai fite ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu jɛɛhe ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical toxins burn delicate root tips and prevent the plant from taking up food. Over time, this causes the leaves to dry up and drop off, leading to tree death.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ shãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaye nii. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji tso lɛ gbele.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when there are no bigger shade trees near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct, intense sunlight. Larger shade trees act as a natural shelter, protecting young cocoa from leaf scorch and soil drying out.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shweshweeshwe shihilɛhe. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ baai ni eshã kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ahe.

english: How many years must I wait for a new cocoa tree to produce its first pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani cacao tso hee ko ajie eklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: With good care, modern hybrid cocoa trees usually begin bearing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older varieties can take 4 to 5 years.
ga: kɛ hiɛdɔɔ kpakpa Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cacao tsei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu amɛ, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahe afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Why do weeds make my young cocoa trees grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal sunlight, water, and soil food from young seedlings. Clearing weeds around the base of the plant gives the seedling full access to the nourishment it needs.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kɛ hiɛdɔɔ juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Shishitoo lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to prune branches on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni afolɔ yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ he hiaa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches and leaves, allowing air and sunlight to pass through the tree crown. This reduces humidity that breeds black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more fruit.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji kɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ ayiteŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my harvested maize grains light in weight instead of heavy and full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he waaa moŋ fe ni eeetsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grains become light when the plants do not get enough water or nutrients, especially nitrogen, during the grain-filling stage, or if pests damaged the leaves while the crop was forming.
ga: Abɛi mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen Yɛ be mli ni awoɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during cool, rainy weather. Removing infected pods immediately and clearing nearby weeds helps stop the disease from spreading and improves pod quality.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni ajie jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I prevent my dried cocoa beans from getting moldy during the rainy season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Mold grows when beans retain too much moisture. You must dry your beans thoroughly on raised bamboo mats, turn them frequently, and cover them quickly whenever rain approaches to keep the quality high.
ga: Mold daa kɛji akɛ ŋmeii hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Esa akɛ ogbi kɔfi yibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ dumɔwui lɛ shii abɔ. Ni oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ, okɛ tsɔne lɛ naa koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani etsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from heat stress, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which causes the plant to focus on growing green leaves instead of producing peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hewɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with weak stalks and smaller, lighter ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and dry up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean your cassava plants lack essential nutrients, are infected by cassava mosaic virus, or are suffering from prolonged dry weather, which prevents the roots from growing big and heavy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ o-cassava tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa. Cassava mosaic virus hela loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ edaaa ni amɛhe feɔ tsiimɔ.

english: Why should I keep clearing weeds around my crops even after they have grown tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Tsa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi lɛ ekwɛ̃ moŋ.

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and space from your crops at every stage of growth. Keeping the ground clear ensures your crops stay healthy and produce full, heavy yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ he ko kɛjɛɔ onibii amli yɛ amɛdalɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ ni tsii.

english: What makes my garden eggs and tomato leaves curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa abɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids that suck the plant's sap and spread viruses. Controlling these pests early helps the plant stay strong and yield good fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs fertilizer to produce better crop yields?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: If your crops grow slowly, look pale or yellowish instead of deep green, or yield small and light produce, your soil is running low on nutrients and needs manure or commercial fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo lɛ Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ loo ewoɔ yibii fioo ni mli tse Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Which crops can a young farmer plant to get good quality harvest within just three months?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii okwaafonyo oblanyo ko baanyɛ adɔ koni ewo yibii kpakpai yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli?

english: Short-season crops like vegetables (tomatoes, pepper, okra) and legumes (cowpeas) mature within 60 to 90 days, allowing quick harvests and regular income if given proper care.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ aduawai (tomato, peppers, okra) kɛ legumes (tsina ŋmei) lɛ shwereɔ yɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 mli, ni no haa anyɛɔ akpaa oya ni anáa shika daa kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow before the crop even starts making grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po jeɔ dumɔwui awomɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to stay green and produce energy. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer early gives the crop the food it needs to build healthy grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant grain on the same piece of land every year, why do my harvests keep getting smaller?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ mi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ miiba shi fioo lɛ?

english: Crops consume specific nutrients from the soil every season. Planting the same crop continuously without resting the land or adding fertilizer drains the soil, resulting in lower grain yields each year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii daa be. Kɛ́ ookwɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmaa ni anáa lɛ baa shi daa afi.

english: Why do people say planting beans or groundnuts before my grain crop makes the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei dani midumɔwui lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that can pull nitrogen out of the air and fix it into the soil. When you plant grain crops after them, the grain crops feed on this left-behind nutrient and grow much better.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmaa tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ baaye nɛkɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ nɛɛ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: How do liquid fertilizers sprayed on leaves help my crops grow better than solid fertilizer in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves have tiny openings that can absorb liquid nutrients quickly, especially during dry times when roots struggle to take up food from dry soil. It gives the plant a fast boost when forming grains.
ga: Baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni mli ewo muji oya Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ be mli ni shishifãi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya kɛ́ amɛwo dumɔwui.

english: Will I get more grain harvest if I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Ani makpa dumɔwui babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: No, planting seeds too close together causes plants to compete with each other for light, water, and nutrients. Giving them proper space allows each plant to grow strong and yield bigger grain heads.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhe abɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edaa waa ni ewoɔ dumɔwui ayitsei wuji.

english: Can I save some of the grain I harvest this season to plant as seed for next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni mikpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ato koni mikɛdu akɛ afi ni baa lɛ dumɔwui?

english: While you can, saved grain from hybrid varieties will produce weaker plants with smaller yields. Buying certified seeds each season ensures strong plants that consistently yield high amounts of grain.
ga: Kɛji obaanyɛ po Shi dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ hybrids mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛnáa dumɔwui babaoo be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do weeds steal so much yield from my young grain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiju nibii babaoo ni jɛɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young grain plants and take away the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your crop needs. Removing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the nourishment required for a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛheɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my crop growing very tall with big leaves but not producing any grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen causes plants to focus on growing tall and leafy instead of making flowers and seeds. Crops need balanced nutrients, including phosphorus and potassium, to switch their energy into forming grain.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa amɛdalɛ ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. Fosfɔs kɛ potasium fata he Koni etsɔ hewalɛ nɔ etsɔ dumɔwui

english: Why do my crops dry up so fast during a short dry period even when it rained recently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli nɛkɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ moŋ?

english: Soil with low organic matter cannot hold onto rainwater for long. Adding compost or dry organic materials helps the soil act like a sponge, retaining moisture for roots even during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔji ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli faaa yɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ahi nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni egbi fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars keep destroying the green center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yaa nɔ amɛfiteɔ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are pests like the fall armyworm that feed on the growing point of young grain crops. Checking plants early and using recommended controls protects the leaves so the plant can grow and produce grains.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ dumɔwui bibii ni miida lɛ. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe koni tsei lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛwo dumɔwui.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and dying before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: This usually happens because the plants lack nitrogen in the soil or are not getting enough water. Nitrogen moves from older lower leaves to feed new growth at the top, so applying fertilizer like NPK or compost early helps keep the whole plant healthy and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Nitrogen lɛ fãa kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli mra. Ebaaye ebua ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee eŋɔli.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow well without me adding any artificial fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ efataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means they have special roots that trap nitrogen gas directly from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil, naturally feeding themselves and enriching the field.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ. ni etsake lɛ efee niyenii kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni enaa kɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni akɛfataa ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the plant grows very tall with lots of leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ be mli ni yucca tso lɛ daa waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo po lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or shade, it puts all its energy into growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of storing energy underground. Planting in full sunlight with balanced soil nutrients encourages bigger root tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen loo shade babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baawo tsei kakadaji ni miida kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, Dumɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja yɔɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, poor watering, or lack of pollination. When temperatures get too high or soil moisture fluctuates wildly, plant stress causes the blossoms to fall before fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. nu ni ehiii loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ fa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa. Tsei ahe haomɔ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ woɔ.

english: Why do I need to make high soil mounds before planting seed yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni owó shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii adu lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow straight down and need loose, soft earth to expand properly. High mounds create a deep bed of soft soil that allows the tubers to grow long and thick without hitting hard, compact ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa ni amɛhiɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni haa bulb lɛ daa ni etsɛɔ ni etswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Can I plant peppers and tomatoes right next to each other on the same plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: It is better not to plant them together because they belong to the same plant family and share the same pests and diseases, like bacterial wilt. Planting them side-by-side allows diseases to spread much faster across your entire farm.
ga: Esaaa akɛ aduɔ amɛ yɛ he kome ejaakɛ amɛjɛ weku kome mli ni amɛyɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai tamɔ bacteria wilt. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet weather and thick shade. Pruning cocoa trees and clearing weeds allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm, stopping the fungus from growing.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kookoo tsei lɛ ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni egbiɔ. ni ekpaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and turn pale even when I plant good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal food, sunlight, and water away from your crops. When weeds crowd your farm, they choke crop roots and prevent them from getting the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ jwɛi eyi oŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ Etsiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi anaa ni ehaaa amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: I want to expand my farm, but I lack physical strength for heavy daily labor. Which crops are easier to manage?
ga: Miisumɔ ni magbala miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shi mibɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ kɛha daa gbi nitsumɔ lɛ. Mɛɛ tsei ahe nitsumɔ waaa?

english: Tree crops and perennials like plantain, cashew, or oil palm require heavy work mainly during land clearing and planting. Once established, they demand much less daily physical labor compared to vegetables, making them easier to manage over large areas.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei kɛ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ plantains kɛ cashew nuts Loo oil palms lɛ atsu nii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛji ato amɛ shishi lɛ Amɛbiɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ fioo ko kwraa daa gbi kɛ akɛto aduawai ahe. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaakwɛ nɔ yɛ hei wuji.

english: If I save maize seeds from my current harvest to plant next season, why will they yield less than store-bought certified seeds?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli lɛ to koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ amɛwoɔ yibii ni faaa fe dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields only in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those high-performing traits in the next generation, resulting in weaker plants and smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know which maize seed variety is best for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmãa dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Different maize varieties are bred for specific conditions, such as short rain seasons, disease resistance, or market preference. Choosing the right variety depends on your local weather patterns and what buyers in your area want to purchase.
ga: Afɔ ŋmãa henɔi srɔtoi yɛ shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli, tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku, helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai. loo jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ Srɔtoi ni sa ni oooha lɛ damɔ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the difference between buying certified seeds from researchers and using seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ niiamlitaolɔ ko dɛŋ ni miheɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ teŋ?

english: Research-backed seeds are specially developed by scientists to yield more food, grow uniformly, and resist pests. Seeds saved from your previous harvest often lose these improved traits over time, leading to smaller yields and uneven growth.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi efee dumɔwui ni niiamlitaomɔ fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni niyenii aba babaoo. shweremɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ bɔ ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Bei pii lɛ Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant a newly released crop variety from research, will it require special care compared to local seeds?
ga: Kɛji midu tsei heei ni ajie kɛjɛ niiamlitaomɔ mli lɛ Ani ebaabi kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ahe?

english: New research varieties are usually bred to be hardier and faster-growing than local seeds. While they follow the same basic farming practices, following proper spacing and management helps them reach their full yield potential.
ga: Nibii amlitaomɔ henɔi heei Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ amɛ koni amɛhe wa ni amɛdara oya fe maŋbii dumɔwui. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛnyiɛɔ okwaayeli nifeemɔi titrii lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ moŋ, shi kɛ́ amɛnyiɛ sɛɛgbɛ ni sa kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛshɛ amɛ yibiiwoo he nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do some crop varieties mature faster than others, and how does that help me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi shwereɔ oya fe ekrokomɛi lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ enɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi?

english: Early-maturing crop varieties are bred to complete their life cycle quickly (such as in 60 to 77 days). This helps you harvest food fast during lean seasons and allows the crop to mature before short rains dry up.
ga: Afɔ̃ɔ tsei srɔtoi ni daa mra koni amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ naa oya (ni ji yɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 77 mli). Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii oya yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ. ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ dani nugbɔshiimɔi kukuji lɛ anɛ.

english: What kind of crops should I plant if the rainy season in my district is very short?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ, mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ madu?

english: You should plant short-duration crop varieties that take under 80 days to mature. These quick-growing crops finish producing grain before the dry spell sets in, reducing the risk of crop failure.
ga: Esa akɛ odu srɔtoi ni heɔ be kukuoo ni heɔ gbii 80 kɛyaa dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Nɛkɛ tsei ni shwereɔ oya nɛɛ gbeɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ afeemɔ naa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ. Enɛ haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafite lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell how many days my maize will take before it is ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbii enyiɛ mi-ŋma lɛ baahe dani eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Every seed variety has an estimated maturity time provided by plant breeders, usually measured from the day of planting. Checking seed labels or asking an extension officer gives you the exact timeframe to plan your harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi fɛɛ yɛ be ni miihe ashɛ be ni tso lɛ kwɛlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ. Bei pii lɛ, asusuɔ enɛ he kɛjɛɔ gbi ni adu lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe wolo lɛ loo obi mɔ ko ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ, ebaaha bo be pɔtɛɛ ni okɛto okpamɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Does the color of the maize grain affect how well I can sell it in Ghanaian markets?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ahe su lɛ saa bɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ ahaa yɛ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ he?

english: Yes, local market demand often depends on grain color. In most Ghanaian markets, white maize is preferred for local foods like banku and kenkey, while yellow maize is often preferred for livestock feed.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ taoɔ lɛ damɔ ŋmaa lɛ su nɔ. yɛ Ghana jarayeli hei babaoo lɛ, mɛi sumɔɔ abele yɛŋ kɛha maŋ lɛ mli niyenii tamɔ Banku kɛ Kenkey, yɛ be mli ni akɛ abele ŋmɔŋ tsuɔ nii akɛ kooloi aniyenii.

english: Is white maize different from yellow maize in terms of how it grows?
ga: Ani esoro ŋmãa yɛŋ kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ yɛ bɔ ni edaa lɛ he?

english: White and yellow maize generally grow in similar ways, but they serve different culinary and nutritional purposes. White maize dominates food markets, while yellow maize contains extra Vitamin A and is popular for poultry feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa yɛŋ kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ daa yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Shi amɛyɛ niyenii kɛ niyenii kpakpa he yiŋtoi srɔtoi. Abɛi yɛŋ yeɔ niyenii jarayeli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ mli vitamin A fa babaoo titri, ni mɛi sumɔɔ waa akɛ niyenii ni akɛyeɔ kooloi.

english: Why do agriculture officers give specific official names to crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai kɛ gbɛi ni sa haa dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Official names are given to distinct crop varieties created by researchers so farmers can easily identify their specific benefits, such as fast maturity, grain color, or pest resistance, when buying seeds.
ga: Gbɛi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli kɛha tsei srɔtoi ni niiamlitaolɔi fee. Bɔni afee ni okwaafoi lɛ anyɛ ana sɛɛnamɔi pɔtɛɛ ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ oya, tamɔ bɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ eda ha kɛ bɔ ni ehiɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ Beni aheɔ dumɔwui

english: Why are there so many different types of maize seeds available to buy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui srɔtoi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Plant breeders create multiple maize varieties so farmers in different ecological zones—such as dry savannas or rainy forest zones—can select the exact seed that thrives in their environment.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmãa srɔtoi babaoo. kɛha okwaafoi ni yɔɔ shihilɛhei srɔtoi tamɔ ŋmɔji ni egbi loo kooi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛhala dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ ni baashwere yɛ amɛshihilɛhe lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is the main food they need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients away or clog the soil with too much water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hole niyenii mli nibii loo nu babaoo tsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field help my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei loo ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are special plants that take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants harvest and decay, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil, acting like natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa tsei ni amɛgboi Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I remove the extra small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them leaves only one or two strong stems, which helps the main tree grow larger stems and bigger bunches of plantains.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii ni fata he lɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baashi, ni no yeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ tsei wuji kɛ plantains akui wuji.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to catch maximum sunlight, which gives the plant energy to build big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the wet ground so they do not rot or catch diseases easily.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni baai lɛ akafite loo helai akamɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce small harvests even if I planted good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; they drink the water, eat the soil nutrients, and block the sunlight that your crops need to grow big. Because the crops are forced to fight for these resources, they end up weak and produce less.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. amɛnuɔ nu Yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, anyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛwu amɛha nibii nɛɛ. Amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seeds when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: It is best to plant after the soil has received two or three steady, heavy rains so that the ground is wet deep down, not just on top. Planting too early after one light rain can cause the seeds to sprout and then dry up if hot, dry days return.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni naa wa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa. Jeee ŋwɛi pɛ Dumɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji akɛ aku sɛɛ akɛba yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave the soil flooded with water for days, the roots cannot breathe, allowing rot-causing germs in the soil to quickly attack and destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Enɛ haa helai ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ oya ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field with no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and thin roots that cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and intense heat. Without shade plants like plantains or trees to protect them, the sun dries them out faster than their small roots can draw water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo. ni nyɛŋ adamɔ hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni buɔ he lɛ bɛ Hulu la baagbi oya fe shishifãi bibii. ni baanyɛ agbala nu

english: Why does my mango tree drop most of its small fruits before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango shwieɔ aduawai bibii lɛ? Bei pii lɛ dani amɛdara?

english: Mango trees often produce more tiny fruits than they can feed. If the tree lacks water or nutrients, or is stressed by hot weather during flowering, it naturally drops the extra small fruits to save enough energy for the rest of the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei woɔ yibii bibii tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii loo eyɛ haomɔ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ Tso lɛ baajie aduawai bibii. Nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa haa tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and dry up even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho trukaa ni amɛmiigbi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting despite daily watering is usually caused by soil-borne diseases or overwatering, which rots the plant's tiny root hairs. When the roots rot or get blocked by disease, they can no longer draw water up to the stem and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa loo nu ni akɛhaa fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa trukaa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa gbi lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ egbo loo hela etsĩ amɛnaa. Amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala nu kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: Bottom leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the young leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen (often from excess manure or fertilizer) but lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing heavy leaves and stems above ground instead of expanding its root tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ (bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli) shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites that suck juices from the underside of young leaves, or by a plant virus carried by whiteflies. The damaged leaves wrinkle and distort as they try to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ji whiteflies lɛ ahe nibii ni baa lɛ amli Baai ni efite lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rain and strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots near the surface. If tiny pests like nematodes or root weevils attack and weaken these roots, or if the soil gets soaked soft, the heavy weight of the fruit bunch easily pulls the roots out of the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo root weevils tutua ni amɛgbɔjɔ shishifãi nɛɛ, Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ Yibii akui ni tsii lɛ baajie amɛshifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear away all the big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie cacao tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct hot sun and strong winds. Big trees provide vital shade and hold moisture in the air, creating a cool microclimate that protects young cocoa seedlings until they grow mature and tough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa, ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like straws during the middle of hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves inward on hot days as a self-defense mechanism. By rolling up, the plant reduces the amount of leaf area exposed to direct sun, which cuts down on water loss through evaporation.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe. Kɛji okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ Tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ahe ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ baaha nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting green shoots inside the barn even before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ po baa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have a natural internal timer known as dormancy. After resting for a few months after harvest, the tuber naturally breaks dormancy and uses its stored moisture and nutrients to push out new shoots, seeking light and soil to grow.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli be he ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Beni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Tubers lɛ fiteɔ wɔɔhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei heei kɛjeɔ kpo Taomɔ la kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baakwɛ̃.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly when temperatures get too high or when plants suffer from water stress. Extreme heat damages pollen, preventing fertilization, so the plant sheds the unproductive flowers to conserve moisture.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni wooo yibii lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do groundnut flowers grow above ground on the stems, but the actual nuts grow under the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei ashishi, shi ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, the flower stalk elongates into a stem called a peg. This peg grows downwards and pushes itself deep into the soil, where the nut safely develops away from sun damage and pests.
ga: Beni atswa ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifã lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋtayaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg. Nɛkɛ pin nɛɛ baagbee shi ni ekɛ ehe baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe, ni hulu ni fiteɔ nii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ he jɛkɛ.

english: Why do the blossom ends of my young watermelons turn black and rot before the fruit can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee ni amɛmiifite dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular— dry soil prevents the plant's roots from absorbing available calcium and delivering it to the fruit.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ calcium ni yɔɔ lɛ ni amɛkɛyashɛ aduawai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the seedlings cool and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baadara ni ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the rest of the plant is still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food green plants need to grow. The plant takes whatever nitrogen it has left and sends it to the newer top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei eŋɔli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Tso lɛ heɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ekɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Ha shishigbɛ baai lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same patch of land every single farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ? Dumɔ be

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and gives soil pests a permanent place to live. Changing crops allows the soil to rebuild its strength and disrupts pest life cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ. ni efoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot in the ground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain sits in the soil without draining away, it drowns the roots and creates the perfect environment for destructive fungi to cause rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmeii baanyɛ afite ni amɛgboi lɛ baa.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves on the soil around my vegetable plants during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ashwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? Mi aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Dry grass acts like a blanket over the soil, stopping the hot sun from drying out the earth quickly. This keeps water in the soil longer so your vegetables stay hydrated with less watering.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, o-vegetables lɛ hiɔ shi ni nu fioo pɛ okɛwoɔ mli.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce small bunches when I leave all the shoots growing around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii ni miida yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ

english: All those extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main trunk for water and plant food. Removing most of the suckers forces all the energy into the main tree so it produces large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi fɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ tsei niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie sucker lɛ mli babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛbote tso titri lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ewoɔ yibii ni tsii ni dara.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plant without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. The plant drops the flowers to save its strength to survive the bad conditions.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ amɛhewalɛ mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why does trimming away some side branches of my pepper plants help them yield more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-pepper tsei lɛ asɛɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Trimming removes weak branches that waste plant energy without producing fruit. It allows light and air to reach the rest of the plant, directing food straight into growing big, healthy peppers.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni fiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii lɛ. Enɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he, ni ekɛ niyenii majeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni miida ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are weeds harmful to my crops even after I have already applied fertilizer to the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ sũ lɛ ewo mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast growers with strong roots that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. If you don't clear them, the weeds eat the crop's food first.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ Jwɛi lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do armyworms hide inside the center of my young maize plant leaves instead of eating on the outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaye nii yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: The central funnel of a young maize plant contains the softest, newest leaves for worms to chew easily, and it shields them from direct sunlight, heavy rain, and natural predators.
ga: Abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli baa bibii ni ji ehee fe fɛɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aye lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly like pencils during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ pensil yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: When afternoon heat becomes intense, maize leaves roll up to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun. This is a natural defense mechanism that stops water from evaporating too quickly so the plant can survive until the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, latsaa lɛ mli wa waa. Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ la oya tsɔ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Can I use treated tap water from the city to water my vegetable garden, or will it damage my plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ maŋ lɛ mli nu ni asaa lɛ awo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu? Aloo ebaaha tso lɛ afite?

english: Treated tap water is safe for crops in small amounts, but rainwater or river water is much better. Tap water contains small amounts of added chemicals like chlorine, while natural water carries rich dissolved minerals that feed your plants.
