ga: Nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ pɔmpi mli ni asaa lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ fioo mli. Shi nugbɔ nu loo faa mli nu hi kwraa fe no. Tap nu lɛ yɛ tsofai fioo komɛi ni akɛfataa he tamɔ chlorine, yɛ be mli ni adebɔɔ mli nu lɛ yɛ minerals babaoo ni mli edɔ ni haa otsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni yibii bɛ mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: High temperatures make tomato pollen dry or sticky, which stops flowers from being fertilized. When pollination fails, the plant sheds the unused flowers to save its water and energy for survival until cooler weather returns.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato pollen lɛ agbi loo efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni ekawo fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛtsuuu nii koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: If I rent a plot of land that was used for growing cassava for three years, why won't my new pepper crop grow well without fertilizer?
ga: Kɛji miha shikpɔŋ kɛha ŋmei dumɔ afii etɛ Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei hee lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛji ŋmei bɛ mli?

english: Cassava is a heavy feeder that pulls large amounts of nutrients out of the earth over time. After several harvests, the soil is left hungry and empty, so sensitive crops like pepper need animal manure or compost to rebuild soil fertility.
ga: Cassava ji niyenii ni tsii ni jieɔ niyenii mli nibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔi babaoo sɛɛ lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ biɔ kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do crops planted near the riverbank grow faster and look greener than the ones on my higher dry land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ faai ahe lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli fe mi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ egbi ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ nɔ tsei lɛ?

english: Riverbank soils stay naturally moist and gather rich topsoil that washes down from higher land during rains. This constant supply of water and washed-in plant nutrients allows crops along the river to grow much faster.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ faa lɛ naa lɛ hiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, ni ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ naa. Nu ni yaa nɔ kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ faa lɛ naa lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya kwraa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow from the tip inward in a V shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaagbee mli kɛmiiya mli yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: A yellow V shape on older leaves is a clear sign that the plant is missing nitrogen. Heavy downpours often wash nitrogen deep past the root level, causing the plant to pull stored energy from its lower leaves to feed the upper growing leaves.
ga: V-shapes ni yɔɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen lɛ mli kɛyaa shɔŋŋ fe shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbalaa hewalɛ ni ato kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛya ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cowpea and groundnut crops leave the soil richer for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea kɛ peanut tsei lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaadu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that partner with beneficial organisms in the soil. These organisms trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on the roots, leaving natural plant food behind in the dirt after harvest.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ekome. Nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi bibii amli, ni amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight without burning. Planting them under fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects them from harsh heat and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛshãaa. Tsei nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ hulutsoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How is my cassava able to stay alive and produce tubers even during months when there is no rain at all?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cassava lɛ ahi shi ni ewo ŋmeii yɛ nyɔji po amli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ kwraa lɛ?

english: Cassava stores water and food reserves inside its thick underground roots during wet weather. When the dry season comes, it can shed its leaves and survive on its underground storage until the rain returns.
ga: Cassava kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ eshishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be baa lɛ. Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba lɛ Ebaajie baai lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do strong winds easily push over my plantain trees right after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa kɛtsɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ amli mlɛo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that spread horizontally near the top of the soil rather than deep down. When heavy rain turns topsoil into soft mud, the shallow roots lose their grip, allowing wind to blow the heavy plant over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋwɛigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ, moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ amɛhe. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atswa tsei lɛ ashwie shi.

english: Why do tomato prices drop so sharply in Ghana during certain months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato jara baa shi waa yɛ Ghana yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes are highly perishable and mature at the same time for many farmers in a region. Because tomatoes rot within days after harvest, farmers rush to sell them all at once, creating a sudden market surplus that forces prices down.
ga: Tomatoi fiteɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ be kome mli kɛha okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ akpa tomato lɛ, egboɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Okwaafoi kɛ oyaiyeli hɔ̃ɔ amɛ tomatoi lɛ fɛɛ shikome. Enɛ haa jarayeli mli nibii ni fa fe nine baa trukaa ni haa nibii ajara baa shi.

english: Why is planting onions targeted for an end-of-year harvest considered very profitable?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ kɛ yiŋtoo akɛ abaakpa nii yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ akɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he waa lɛ?

english: Demand for vegetables spikes significantly during the end-of-year festive period (Christmas and New Year) in Ghana, while onion supply often tightens, allowing farmers who harvest at this time to command much higher prices.
ga: Nibii ni ataoɔ yɛ aduawai ahe lɛ yaa hiɛ waa yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbijurɔyelii lɛ amli. (Blonya kɛ Afi Hee) yɛ Ghana, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛhaa lɛ faaa kwraa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, okwaafoi ni kpaa nii yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ jara ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ.

english: How can I protect my farm business from total loss if the market price of my vegetables crashes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ he koni ekafite kwraa kɛji mi-aduawai lɛ jara ba shi?

english: You can practice staggered planting—planting small portions of your field every few weeks instead of all at once—so that your entire harvest does not hit the market during a single price crash.
ga: Obaanyɛ okase dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ fã bibioo ko ni ooodu yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ daa otsii enyɔ nɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu fɛɛ shikome Bɔni afee ni onibii fɛɛ akabote jara nɔ yɛ jara ni baa shi kome mli.

english: Why do tomato farmers lose more money during a market glut than maize or grain farmers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato okwaafoi lɛ laajeɔ shika babaoo yɛ jarayeli mli nibii babaoo mli fe ŋmãa loo ŋmaa okwaafoi lɛ?

english: Grains can be dried and stored in a barn for months while waiting for market prices to recover, whereas fresh tomatoes must be sold within days of harvesting regardless of how low the price is.
ga: Abaanyɛ agbi ŋmaa ni akɛto ŋmɔji amli nyɔji babaoo, ni amɛmɛ ni jara lɛ aya hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, esa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ tomato hee yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ kɛjɛ be mli ni akpa lɛ. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni jara lɛ baa shi ha

english: Can I hold onto my harvested tomatoes in a regular room for a month to wait for market prices to go up?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ ato tsu ko ni yɔɔ daa lɛ mli nyɔŋ kome koni mamɛ ni jara lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: No, fresh tomatoes contain high water content and thin skins, causing them to soft-rot within a few days without industrial refrigeration, unlike hardier crops that can be stored at room temperature.
ga: Dabi, tomato ŋmɔŋ mli nu babaoo yɛ mli, ni ehewolo hu yɛ mlɛo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛji akɛ nitsumɔhei ni akɛwoɔ friji mli lɛ bɛ mli. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ tsei ni wa ni abaanyɛ akɛto ŋwɛi fɛ̃i mli lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to dry onions in the shade after harvesting before selling them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔgbi onions yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni wɔkpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ dani wɔhɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Drying (or curing) onions hardens their outer skin and closes the neck, which stops bacteria and fungi from entering the bulb, allowing them to stay fresh for weeks or months while you look for good buyers.
ga: Sabalai ni agbiɔ (loo etsaa) lɛ haa hewolo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ mli waa ni ehaa tsitsi lɛ naa. Enɛ haaa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii abote tuber lɛ mli. Ha o-onions lɛ ahi shi otsii loo nyɔji babaoo be mli ni otaoɔ mɔ kpakpa ni baahe lɛ.

english: Is it safer for a beginner farmer like me to grow onions or tomatoes if I am worried about post-harvest losses?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha okwaafonyo hee tamɔ mi akɛ ebaadu sabolai loo tomato? Ni kɛji akɛ mihao yɛ nibii ni baafite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ hu?

english: Onions are generally safer because they have a longer shelf life after harvesting, giving you time to negotiate sales, whereas tomatoes spoil quickly and force you to accept whatever price buyers offer immediately.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sabolai yɛ shweshweeshwe ejaakɛ ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onáa be ni okɛsusuɔ jarayeli lɛ he. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tomato fiteɔ oya ni enyɛɔ onɔ ni okpɛlɛɔ jara ni mɔ ni heɔ lɛ lɛ kɛhaa lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes crack or split open on the plant right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miigba loo amɛmiijara yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they receive a sudden heavy watering or rain after a dry period; the inside of the fruit fills with water rapidly and expands faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Tomatoi baatswa kɛji amɛná nu ni naa wa trukaa loo nugbɔ nɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Nu yiɔ aduawai lɛ amli oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are my onion plants producing tall green leaves but very small bulbs underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi bulbs bibii waa yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the onion plant to put all its energy into leaf growth rather than shifting energy down into building a thick, healthy bulb.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni miida lɛ ahe. Mohu ɔ, a jeɔ he wami ɔ kɛ yaa sisi konɛ a pee yihi nɛ a mi wa nɛ a he wa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any small tomatoes when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato bibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat (above 35°C) damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing pollination and forcing the plant to drop the flowers to conserve moisture and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa (ni fe 35°C) fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Tsi pollination naa ni onyɛ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie fɔfɔi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he

english: If I plant cocoa trees today, how many years will they keep producing pods for my family to inherit?
ga: Kɛji midu kookoo tso ŋmɛnɛ Afii enyiɛ kroko amɛbaawo pods ni weku lɛ baatsɔ nɔ?

english: Cocoa trees can remain productive for 30 to 40 years or even longer if well cared for. This makes cocoa a long-term investment that can support your family across generations.
ga: Cacao tsei baanyɛ awo yibii afii 30 kɛyashi 40 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa kookoo feɔ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ aye abua oweku lɛ kɛjɛ yinɔ kome mli kɛya yinɔ kroko mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when there are no big forest trees left around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ? Be mli ni kooi wuji komɛi eshwɛɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocoa naturally grows under forest canopies. Without shade, strong direct sunlight stresses the tree, dries out the soil moisture, and damages the leaves, making it harder for the tree to survive and produce pods.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo bɛ Strong, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbiɔ. ni efiteɔ baai lɛ Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tso lɛ akɛ eeehi shi ni efee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their young flowers before they can grow into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii babaoo dani eda ni etsɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed. Dropping some flowers is the tree's natural way of managing its energy, but excessive flower drop can also mean the tree lacks water or soil nutrients.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Fɔfɔi ni ashiɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ tso hewalɛ nɔ. Shi fɔfɔi babaoo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hu baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it necessary for me to cut off some branches from my cocoa trees when I want them to produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi lɛ? Be ni miisumɔ ni ekwɛ̃ pods babaoo

english: Pruning removes weak, unnecessary, or diseased branches so sunlight and air can reach the middle of the tree. This prevents fungal diseases and directs the tree's energy into growing healthy pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni he ehiaaa, loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii ahe helai anaa ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai babaoo baafata he.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, and dark conditions. Removing infected pods and clearing tall weeds helps air flow through the farm and reduces moisture where the fungus spreads.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ hei ni ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if the soil in my cocoa farm is tired and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When soil loses its fertility, crop leaves turn pale green or yellow, growth slows down, and fruit pods remain small or drop early. Pale leaves and weak tree canopy are clear signs that the soil needs additional nutrients.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwereɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo ni aduawai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ ji okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia niyenii krokomɛi.

english: Is it good practice to plant food crops like plantain or cassava alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu niyenii nibii tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe?

english: Planting plantains with young cocoa is very beneficial because the plantain leaves provide temporary shade and moisture. However, avoid cassava directly next to cocoa, as its roots spread aggressively and suck out too much soil moisture.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi yɛ plantains ni akɛ cocoa tsei bibii duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ baai lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛmuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo.

english: Why do tall weeds in my cocoa farm make my crop yield drop so low?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa baa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your cocoa trees. They also trap moisture around tree trunks, creating a moist environment where crop diseases thrive.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-cacao tsei lɛ mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ hu. tso shishi Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsei ahe helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How do I protect my cocoa trees from dying when the dry harmattan wind starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbo kɛ́ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ je shishi?

english: Covering the base of your trees with dry leaves or plant waste (mulching) keeps soil moisture from evaporating, while maintaining shade trees breaks the harsh winds and lowers stress on the cocoa canopy.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo tso lɛ mli nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi (mulching) ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei lɛ ni oooha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa nɔnyɛɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How long must I care for a new cocoa seedling before I can harvest my first pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ ehe baahia ni makwɛ mi-kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ anɔ dani manyɛ makpa mi-koko dumɔwui klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years to produce their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛshɛɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the root area or drowns the roots so they cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa baai ni wa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ahe loo eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi kɛyashɛ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my granular fertilizer right before a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ granular fertilizer fataaa he amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall will wash the fertilizer off the top of the farm or push it too deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach it, effectively wasting your money and effort.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fitemɔ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in thin, weak stalks and tiny cobs, leading to a smaller overall harvest than if you spaced them properly.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi fe kɛji okɛ amɛ to he ko jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava produce big stem branches and lots of leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ niji wuji kɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems instead of storing energy down in the roots to form large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or sudden dry spells stress the tomato plant, forcing it to drop its flowers to save water and stay alive rather than spending energy growing fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Anyɛɔ mɔ nɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdu aduawai.

english: Why do my plant leaves curl up and roll inward when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which helps prevent precious moisture from evaporating out of the leaves.
ga: Baai ni akpɛ́ɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ ni jara wa lɛ ajɛ baai lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants twisting and curling up tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids, which carry viruses that corrupt the plant's normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni hela ko ni fiteɔ tsei ahe baai ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and cool conditions. Overgrown shade trees and unpruned branches trap moisture around the pods, allowing the fungus to bloom.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hei ni mli ejɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ tsei niji ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ mɔɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops look weak and stunted so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ miifee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are naturally tougher than food crops, meaning they aggressively steal sunlight, drinking water, and soil food before your planted crops have a chance to take them in.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe niyenii tsei. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ hulu la, nu ni anuɔ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani otsei lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe woɔ mli.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass or maize husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Ani okɛ jwɛi loo ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ baaye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Covering the soil—called mulching—acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating in the heat, prevents weed growth, and eventually breaks down into natural soil food.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ edɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellow, curled leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: Why do my maize stalks stay short and turn purple instead of growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ purple moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ lɛ?

english: Purple and stunted maize stalks mean the plant is lacking phosphorus, an essential soil nutrient. Applying the right NPK fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the roots grow strong and restores normal growth.
ga: Abɛi tsei ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ ni eha amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds before the main rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui dani nugbɔ anɛ?

english: Planting should happen immediately after the first continuous, heavy rains begin—usually around March or April depending on your region—so seeds get enough moisture to sprout without drying out in false early rains.
ga: Esa akɛ adu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee March loo April. Edamɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ baaná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa lɛ nɛ leebi.

english: Why does the soil on my farm turn hard like rock after it rains and dries in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛsaa yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Soil gets hard when it lacks organic matter like compost or dead leaves. Adding organic manure keeps the soil loose and spongy, allowing water to soak in better and roots to spread easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egboi bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly even after I clear my farm with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ dade shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing with a cutlass cuts weeds at the surface but leaves the roots alive underneath. Planting cover crops like cowpeas or leaving dry leaves on the ground as mulch blocks sunlight and stops weeds from coming back fast.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ shwie shi lɛ, efoɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ shi eshiɔ shishifãi lɛ yɛ shishi lolo. Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ loo baai ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ oya.

english: Why is it good to plant maize and cassava together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting maize and cassava together makes efficient use of your farm. Maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving the land free for the slower-growing cassava to expand and mature later.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmãa ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ haa oŋmɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi he ko koni yucca ni daa blɛoo lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni eda sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before they can produce any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani manyɛ mawo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when watering is inconsistent. Covering the soil around the plants with dry grass keeps the roots cool and moist, helping the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i. Ye obua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee aduawai

english: Why is my harvested maize rotting and getting full of insects inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ miifite ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ kooloi bibii lɛ?

english: Insects and mold attack maize when it is put into storage while still damp. Drying your corn thoroughly in the sun until the kernels are completely hard before storing them in airtight bags prevents spoilage.
ga: Kplukai kɛ ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmãa kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe be mli ni edɔ lolo. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulu mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa dani okɛwo vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over. Rotating different crops, such as planting groundnuts or beans after maize, helps restock essential nutrients in the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads in overly damp and shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let sunlight and air flow through the farm stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Is it better for me to plant all my maize seeds on the same day, or should I spread the planting across a few weeks?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ? Aloo esa akɛ magbɛ dumɔwu lɛ mashwã otsii fioo komɛi amli?

english: Spreading your planting over a few weeks, known as staggered planting, protects you from losing your entire crop if a sudden dry spell hits at a critical growth stage. It also allows you to harvest and sell your yield over a longer period rather than all at once.
ga: Ale he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ ni oooha otsii fioo komɛi hu aya hiɛ lɛ akɛ dumɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ. Ebuɔ ohe koni onibii fɛɛ akafite kɛji hɔmɔ ba trukaa yɛ be mli ni shweremɔ he hiaa waa lɛ. Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ hu ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohɔ̃ɔ fɛɛ shikome lɛ

english: Why do my cassava plants grow so tall and thin when I plant them very close to my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: When cassava and maize are planted too close together, they fight for available sunlight. The cassava stretches unnaturally tall to get above the maize leaves, which drains its energy away from growing big roots underground.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Kasava lɛ tsei lɛ shwereɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baajie hewalɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi wuji ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure early in the growth period restores the healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara waa Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing plenty of flowers, but the flowers dry up and drop off without forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. When the weather gets extremely hot and dry, the plant sheds its flowers to save water for its own survival until growing conditions improve.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tuber growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and catching soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni eshɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahe koni ekɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛkafiteɔ ni amɛkaheɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees shed most of their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shedding leaves is a natural survival mechanism for cocoa trees during dry weather to reduce moisture loss through the leaf surface. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young trees from harsh dry winds and reduces leaf drop.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni cacao tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ he ni ehaa baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden egg plants curling up like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves. As they drink the plant's juices, they cause the leaves to distort and twist, which slows down the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Beni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ Amɛbaahã baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: How does planting cowpeas help improve the soil for the next crop I want to plant?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni misumɔɔ ni madu lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant dies and rots, this stored nitrogen releases into the dirt, acting as a free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo ni egbo. Ajieɔ nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my main plantain stem die after producing only one bunch of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain tso titri lɛ gboɔ beni ekɛ plantain kuu kome pɛ wo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed by nature to flower and produce fruit only once in its life cycle. Once harvested, the main stem naturally dies back so its remaining energy can feed the young shoots (suckers) sprouting around its base.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Kɛji akpa Tso titri lɛ baagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ aha ŋmeii bibii (ŋmei) ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ.

english: How can my cassava crop survive long heatwaves when my maize crop wilts and dies?
ga: Te mi-cassava tsei lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli? Beni mi-ŋma lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava has a special survival system where it can stop growing and drop its leaves during severe dry weather to save water, safely storing energy in its underground roots until the rains return to revive it.
ga: Cassava yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo krɛdɛɛ ko ni ekɛhiɔ shi. Ebaanyɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ baai ashwie shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa lɛ mli. koni ekɛ nu akafite Ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut down my cocoa trees when they start showing swollen shoots instead of giving me medicine to spray them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ beni amɛbɔi shwiemɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha mi tsofa lɛ?

english: The Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus disease lives inside the plant's sap system where chemical sprays cannot reach. Cutting down and burning infected trees is the only proven way to prevent the virus from spreading through insects to the rest of your healthy cocoa farm.
ga: Cocoa swollen virus hela lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli, ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni ashãa lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni ana he odaseyeli ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ kooloi bibii anɔ egbɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. ni ji kookoo ŋmɔji ni hi kɛha ohewalɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft roots and delicate leaves that burn quickly in full sunlight. They need temporary shade plants like plantains planted around them to block the harsh sun and keep the soil moist while their roots grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why should I trim extra branches and shoots off my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ ni majie kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Removing unwanted branches and shoots prevents the tree from wasting energy on leaves instead of pods. It also allows sunlight and air to move through the tree, which prevents damp conditions that cause black pod disease.
ga: Niji kɛ ŋmeii ni ataooo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai anɔ moŋ fe ŋmeii. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when it rains too heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the field for too long, the soil gets waterlogged and suffocates the roots, causing them to rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ashiɔ nu ni ehiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baatsɔ nu ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni ebaaha amɛgboi.

english: Why do the tiny fruits on my crops fall off the stems before growing into full vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ berry lɛ No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ aduawai ni eyi obɔ?

english: Fruit drop often happens when a plant experiences stress, such as sudden drought, extreme heat, or damage from sucking pests. Ensuring steady water supply and checking for insects can help the plant hold its fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔi, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nɔ ni jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ nu lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa be fɛɛ be kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very few leaves when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ baai fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Plants need sunlight to make their own food. When they are shaded by big trees, they stretch upward searching for light, using up their energy to grow tall rather than growing thick stems and healthy leaves.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii. Beni amɛyɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛtaoɔ la. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a he wa.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition results in weak plants, small yields, and easy spread of diseases between touching leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Ehaa yibii fioo pɛ ni egbɛɔ hela eshwaa oya kɛji akɛ eta baai ahe

english: How does covering the ground around my crops with dry grass stop them from drying out?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ehà he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts like a blanket. It shades the dirt from the hot sun, keeps the soil cool, and prevents moisture from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ebuɔ muji kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid putting fertilizer on my field when the ground is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Crop roots can only drink up fertilizer when it is dissolved in water. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the roots and waste your money because the plant cannot absorb it until rain falls.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ atsɔ nu mli pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni efite shika ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Lower leaves turn yellow when the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for growth. It can also happen when the soil is too wet or during dry spells, which prevents the plant from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha dalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ loo yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil turn hard like a rock during the dry season, making my crops wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛsaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ? Mahã midumɔ nii lɛ agbi?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic material like compost or decayed leaves, which act like a sponge to trap moisture and keep soil soft. Without organic matter, direct sunlight bakes the soil particles tightly together.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni ekɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ko bɛ ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ afee ekome jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that lose moisture very fast under intense heat. They need shade crops, like plantains, to act as living umbrellas and cool them down until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni amɛha amɛhe ajɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why do my cassava stems and roots rot in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long because roots need air to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen, encouraging soil fungi to attack and decay the plant roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ni amɛha tsei shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay very small when I plant the stems close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cassava ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete fiercely for the limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight available, leaving insufficient energy for any individual plant to develop large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa tsei aŋkroaŋkroi baanyɛ afee bulbs wuji lɛ faaa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my pepper crops after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-pepper tsei lɛ beni mijie jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally built to survive tough conditions, allowing their roots to steal water, sunlight, and soil food faster than domestic crops, which need more care to establish.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni adebɔɔ fee koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe shia tsei, ni biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my tomato plants without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get extremely high or when water is scarce. The plant sheds flowers to save water and keep itself alive during stressful weather.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Tso nɛɛ woɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha ehi wala mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni haoɔ mɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do I find small holes in my maize leaves shortly after the seeds sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai amli beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ

english: Small holes in tender leaves are usually caused by early insect pests, like the fall armyworm, feeding on the leaves while hiding in the moist center of the growing maize shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ mra, tamɔ asraafoi atsɛŋemɔ helai ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Eyeɔ baai kɛtsɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ teŋ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout even after I water the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ nu ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep where air cannot reach them, if the soil is soaked continuously without air, or if the seeds were old or damaged by pests before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite amɛ dani adu.

english: Why do my stored yams start producing green shoots while sitting in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃mɔ be mli ni mita mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living plant roots that naturally go dormant after harvest. When exposed to heat and humidity in storage, the yam detects natural signals telling it that it is time to sprout and grow into a new plant.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tso shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni bɛ nitsumɔ. Adebɔɔ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Kɛji akɛ akɛwo hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i mli yɛ nitoohe lɛ Sweet potatoes naa adebɔɔ mli okadii ni tsɔɔ amɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tsei heei.

english: Can I dig up the small suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree to plant a new farm?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii. ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani abaanyɛ akɛ plantain tsei lɛ atsu nii ni akɛdu ŋmɔ hee?

english: Yes, those young suckers are natural offspring of the main tree. You can carefully separate a healthy sucker with strong roots from the mother plant and transplant it to start a brand new plantain tree.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nakai abifabii lɛ ji tso titri lɛ adebɔɔ mli seshibii. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ agbala ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni shishifãi ni wa yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. ni aduɔ koni akɛje dumɔwui heei ashishi

english: Should I leave all the young shoots growing around my plantain tree, or should I remove some?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii komɛi ni miida yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ loo esa akɛ majie amɛteŋ ekomɛi?

english: It is best to prune away extra shoots and leave only two or three strong ones at different stages of growth. If you leave too many suckers, they will fight with the main tree for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to smaller plantains.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2-3 pɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Amɛkɛ tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: How do I know if a plantain sucker is healthy enough to be planted in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sucker dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look for a sucker with a broad, firm base and narrow, sword-like leaves. These 'sword suckers' have strong vigor and will grow into healthy, high-yielding trees faster than shoots with thin stems and broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ klante. Nɛkɛ ‘bamboo ŋmeii’ nɛɛ wa ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni he wa, ni woɔ yibii babaoo oya fe ŋmeii ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear all weeds and trash around the base of my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ojie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, midumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ he miihia.

english: Clearing the base gives the young crop a clean space free from weeds that steal fertilizers and water. A tidy area around the stem also prevents pests and diseases from hiding near the plant's sensitive root system.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ naa he ko ni he tse ni jwɛi ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu bɛ mli. He ni yɔɔ fɛo ni bɔleɔ Stems lɛ he lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai akatee amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers when starting my field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu plantain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mije okwaayeli shishi?

english: You should plant them about 3 meters (around 10 feet) apart. This spacing gives each plantain tree enough room to spread its large leaves, catch sunlight, and grow suckers without shading out neighboring plants.
ga: Esa akɛ odu amɛ aaafee mitai 3 (aaafee ninetalɔi 10) kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ jɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbai wuji lɛ eshwaa, ni enáa hulu la, ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni etsĩii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do some shoots on the same plantain stem grow fast while others wait to grow later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ dumɔwu kome nɔ lɛ daa oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi mɛɔ koni amɛda sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is natural plant hierarchy. The mother tree directs most of its nutrients to the first shoot so it can mature first. Once that shoot grows big, the next shoot behind it receives more energy and begins to grow rapidly.
ga: Enɛ ji tsei adebɔɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoo. Tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kudɔɔ niyenii ni eyɔɔ mli lɛ babaoo kɛyaa klɛŋklɛŋ tso lɛ nɔ koni enyɛ eda klɛŋklɛŋ. Beni tso lɛ da lɛ Mfoniri ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ baaná hewalɛ babaoo ni ebɔi dalɛ oya.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow very slowly during certain months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo waa yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Crops naturally slow down their growth during dry or cold seasons to conserve water and energy. Once the rains return and temperatures warm up, the crops resume fast growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi yɛ fɛ̃i be loo fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ oya.

english: Why does it take so many months after planting before my plantain trees produce fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ nyɔji babaoo yɛ mi-plantains lɛ adumɔ sɛɛ dani ewoɔ aduawai babaoo lɛ?

english: Plantains need time to build a strong root network and produce enough large leaves to store sunlight energy. Only after establishing a solid structure can the plant support the heavy weight of a fruit bunch.
ga: Be he miihia plantains koni amɛma shishifãi ni mli wa ni amɛwo baai ni dara bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ hulu la hewalɛ baato. Beni afee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ pɛ kɛkɛ ni tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my neighbor's plantain trees yield fruits earlier than mine even though we planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo plantain lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu lɛ yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Differences in soil fertility, water availability, sucker quality, and field maintenance can cause plants to mature at different speeds. Soil with more organic matter and moisture helps plants yield faster.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli Nu ni yɔɔ, nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ adara yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya.

english: How many years can I keep harvesting plantains from the same original stand?
ga: Afii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa plantains kɛjɛ shidaamɔhe kome nɔ?

english: With good farm management, clearing of old stems, and proper sucker selection, a plantain stand can continuously produce new shoots and fruits for 3 to 5 years or even longer.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa nɔ Ajieɔ tsei akutsei momoi kɛ ŋmeii ni sa lɛ ahalamɔ Dumɔwui adumɔwui baanyɛ aya nɔ amɛwo ŋmeii heei kɛ yibii afii 3 kɛyashi 5 loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: Why are some of my plantain bunches producing very small fruits while others on the same farm grow very big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii bibii waa lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kui komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ dara waa.

english: Plantain fruit size depends heavily on how much food and water the plant receives. If too many young shoots grow around one tree, or if the soil lacks nutrients, the plant distributes its energy thinly, leading to smaller plantains.
ga: Bɔ ni plantain tso lɛ yibii lɛ da ha lɛ damɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ waa. Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ tso kome he loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ Tsei lɛ baagbɛ amɛ hewalɛ lɛ eko amɛshwã. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do so many small shoots keep growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ. Mi dumɔwui titri lɛ shishitoo

english: These shoots are called suckers, which are the plant's natural way of reproducing. Leaving all of them to grow forces them to compete with the main tree for light and nutrients, which reduces your crop yield.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii, ni ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ efɔɔ bii. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛdara lɛ, ebaanyɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛkɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi.

english: What causes the leaves of my plantain trees to turn yellow and dry up before the fruit matures?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi plantain baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani yibii lɛ baa?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for key nutrients like nitrogen, suffering from a fungal disease like Black Sigatoka, or struggling to get enough water during hot spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiye niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko tamɔ black sigatoka miiye lɛ. aloo ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni ená nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the fruit bunches start getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ mli tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the ground. When heavy bunches form, strong winds can pull the roots right out of the wet soil unless you support the stem with a wooden prop.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ yɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ja okɛ tso ko tsu nii ni okɛfi tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers when starting a new field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu plantain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he tɛŋŋ beni mijeɔ tso hee shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers should be spaced about 3 meters by 2 meters apart. This gives their broad leaves enough room to capture sunlight without shading each other out or competing for underground water.
ga: Esa akɛ plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 2, ni eha baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔ hulu lɛ ni amɛhaaa amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛkaye shikpɔŋ shishi nu he akaŋ.

english: Can I grow plantains alongside other crops like maize or cocoa on the same land?
ga: Mibaanyɛ makwɛ plantains kɛfata ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmãa loo kookoo he. Ani ebaanyɛ ehi he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, plantains are great for intercropping. Their broad leaves provide necessary shade for young cocoa seedlings, and growing fast crops like maize between young plantain rows helps make good use of the space while plantains mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ. Ni kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ ŋmãa bibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akɛ he ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How do my plantain crops handle long dry seasons without rain?
ga: Te mi dumɔwui lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛkpee nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ naa?

english: Plantain stems store a lot of water, but prolonged drought slows down growth and shrinks bunch size. Covering the soil around the base with dry leaves or mulch helps trap soil moisture during dry periods.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo. Shi hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha panicle lɛ dalɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: What simple organic materials can I put in the soil to help my plantains produce heavier bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ mlɛo manyɛ mikɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni eye ebua mi plantains lɛ ni amɛwo jwɛi ni tsii?

english: Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or decayed crop leaves into the planting hole provides rich organic nutrients that feed the shallow roots and encourage thick stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsei ahe baai ni egboi fata dumɔ bu lɛ he lɛ, ehaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ náa niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo. ni ewoɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji ahe hewalɛ.

english: How do I tell when a plantain bunch is mature enough to be cut down for sale?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni plantains lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ afolɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: A plantain bunch is mature when the individual fruits lose their sharp side ridges and become round and plump, even while the skin is still completely green.
ga: Plantains kuu ko shɛɔ dalɛ he beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko fiteɔ esɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. ni ebatsɔ kokroo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji akɛ hewolo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo po.

english: Why do my plantains ripen and turn yellow so quickly after I cut them and put them in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ oya nɛkɛ beni mifolɔ amɛ ni mikɛwo kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Once cut, plantains naturally release a gas that speeds up ripening. Packing them tightly in enclosed bags traps heat and this gas, causing the fruits to soften much faster than if kept in cool, airy shade.
ga: Kɛ́ afo lɛ, plantains lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa ekwɛ̃ɔ oya. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ blɛoo oya fe kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ ni jɛmɛ ejɔ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to wash my cutlass and boots with soap before moving to another farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛkɛ samla afɔ amɛ ŋmeii kɛ amɛ bɔɔtui ahe dani amɛya ŋmɔ kroko mli lɛ?

english: Disease germs and tiny pests from sick crops stick to dirt on your cutlass, shoes, and clothes. Washing them off prevents you from accidentally carrying hidden crop sicknesses into healthy fields.
ga: Muawai bibii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ kpɛtɛɔ muji ni yɔɔ o-daggers, o-shɔji, kɛ otadei lɛ ahe lɛ he. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaatsi bo gbɛ koni okakɛ tsei ahe helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ aba ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ oshara mli.

english: If I plant clean, healthy yam seeds right next to my neighbor's old yam field, will my yams still stay healthy?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmeii dumɔwui ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmeii ŋmɔ momo lɛ masɛi lɛ, Ani mi ŋmeii lɛ baaná hewalɛ lolo?

english: Not necessarily. Insects, wind, rain splash, and people walking between fields can easily carry diseases from your neighbor's sick plants onto your clean crops. It is best to keep clean fields separated from older or sick farms.
ga: Dabi, kooloi bibii, kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ gbɔmɛi ni nyiɛɔ ŋmɔji ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ ajie helai kɛjɛ okutsoŋbii tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya oŋmɔshi nibii ni he tse lɛ amli oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaagbala ŋmɔji ni mli tse kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni egbɔ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why should I restrict visitors or farm animals from freely walking through my yam field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi saralɔi loo ŋmɔ mli kooloi anaa koni amɛkatsɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli amɛye amɛhe?

english: People and livestock pick up mud containing microscopic crop diseases and pest eggs on their feet. When they walk through your field, they drop these germs into your soil, which can infect your healthy yams.
ga: Mɛi kɛ kooloi holeɔ klon ni tsei ahe helai bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni jɛɔ nane mli baa lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ amɛnyiɛ oŋmɔji amli lɛ Amɛshiɔ nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ atswa o-sweet potato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ he hela.

english: Why are agricultural officers plucking and planting small vine leaves instead of planting whole yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi jieɔ wain tsei ahe baai bibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmeii muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Plucking healthy vine cuttings is a fast way to multiply clean seed material. Instead of burying a whole tuber that you could eat or sell, a single healthy plant can yield many vine cuttings that grow into brand-new, disease-free seed yams.
ga: Wein tso niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ oya ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ dumɔwui ashwãa. Mohu ɔ, mo pu bulb muu nɛ o ma nyɛ maa ye loo o jua. Tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ awo wain tso niji babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni hela bɛ mli.

english: Can a small piece of a yam tuber or a tiny vine cutting really grow into a full-sized yam?
ga: Ani sweet potato tuber bibioo ko loo wain tso bibioo ko ni afo lɛ baanyɛ ada ni etsɔ sweet potato ni da waa?

english: Yes. As long as the small tuber piece or vine cutting is healthy and disease-free, it has all the genetic instructions to sprout roots, feed on soil nutrients, and produce a large, healthy tuber by harvest time.
ga: Hɛɛ. Shii abɔ ni ŋmeii bibii loo wain tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ amɛhe lɛ. Eyɛ fɔmɔ su mli gbɛtsɔɔmɔi fɛɛ ni baaha shishifãi akwɛ̃. Ye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni owo ŋmeii wuji ni wa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli

english: Why do my stored yams keep rotting in the barn even when the tubers looked fine during harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miifite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli moŋ?

english: Rotting is often caused by invisible fungal or bacterial diseases that infected the crop while it was still in the soil. Using certified disease-free seed yams and keeping your storage barn cool and well-ventilated prevents these hidden rots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni anaaa ni gbeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes ni hela bɛ mli ni awo he odaseyeli akɛtsu nii, ni oha otsu lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu abote mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ anaa.

english: How can I tell if the seed yams I buy from the local market carry disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ yɛ hela?

english: Diseased seed yams often have subtle signs like soft spots, cracks, strange dark rings inside, or dry rot under the skin. Buying certified clean seeds from trusted sources ensures you are not paying for hidden sickness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ naa okadii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ŋmeii, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ emli, loo ŋmeii ni egbi yɛ hewolo lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni he tse ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli ni ooohe kɛjɛ he ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni owooo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ.

english: How do I know that these lab-cleaned seed yams will give me a better harvest than my traditional big seed tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni atsuu he yɛ laboratorii mli nɛɛ baawo yibii ni hi fe mi kusum dumɔwui agboi lɛ ayitsei lɛ?

english: Traditional tubers often carry invisible viruses that drain the plant's strength over generations. Lab-cleaned seed yams have had those hidden viruses removed, allowing the plant to grow with full vigor and produce bigger, healthier tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni anaaa ni fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli lɛ yɛ blema bulbs amli. Sweet potatoes ni atsuu he yɛ laboratori lɛ jieɔ nakai helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa kɛyashɛɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my young yam plants to curl up and turn yellow early in the season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato bibii lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are usually symptoms of a plant virus spread by insects or infected seed tubers. The disease prevents the leaves from making food, which weakens the whole plant and shrinks your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso mli helai ni kooloi loo dumɔwui ayitsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Hela nɛɛ haa baai lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛfee niyenii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha onibii ni obaawo lɛ aba shi.

english: Where do yam diseases come from if I don't see any insects eating my crops?
ga: Nɛgbɛ sweet potato hela lɛ jɛɔ kɛji minaaa kooloi ni yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Many crop diseases are caused by microscopic fungi, bacteria, or viruses. They live inside infected seed tubers or remain hidden in the soil from previous seasons, causing damage without any visible insects present.
ga: Tsei helai babaoo jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii, muawai loo muawai amli. Amɛhiɔ dumɔwui ayitsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli loo amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ mli. Ekɛ fitemɔ baa ni kooloi bibii ni anaaa bɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the ground is waterlogged and drowning the roots. Adding the right fertilizer or draining standing water helps the plant make food again and turn green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ miiho. Nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli loo nu ni hoɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aná niyenii ekoŋŋ ni ehi shi eŋɔli.

english: In extreme afternoon heat, tomato leaves lose moisture through evaporation faster than the roots can suck up water from the soil. The plant droops to protect itself from drying out, but it usually recovers once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my bean plants producing a lot of flowers but failing to grow any actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ekwɛɛɛ anɔkwa ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Too much heat or an imbalance of fertilizer—like too much nitrogen—causes bean plants to focus only on growing leaves or drop their flowers before fruits can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ babaoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, tamɔ nitrogen babaoo. Ha bean tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ pɛ ni ebaakwɛ nɔ loo ejie fɔfɔi lɛ dani aduawai lɛ aba.

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot and turn black when rain stays on the farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When excess water fills all the tiny spaces in the soil for days, it cuts off air to the roots, causing them to suffocate, rot, and die.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine eyi shikpɔŋ bibioo ko mli obɔ gbii babaoo Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa mɔ shwieɔ mumɔ, fitemɔ kɛ gbele.

english: Why do tiny insects attack my pepper plants more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-pepper tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Hot and dry weather allows many small pests, like aphids and mites, to reproduce much faster. Heavy rains during the wet season naturally wash these insects off the leaves and destroy their breeding spots.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ kɛ kooloi bibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baa. Gbalamɔ oya Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ haa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni efiteɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli he ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods turn black because of a fast-spreading fungal disease that thrives in high humidity and damp shade. It can also happen naturally if the tree does not have enough food or water to support all its growing pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni shwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ hewɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba yɛ adebɔɔ naa hu kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni miida lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What happens to my cassava tubers underground if I plant the stems too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji midu shishifãi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots fight each other for limited sunlight, space, and soil nutrients. This causes the plant to grow tall and leafy, but produces very small and thin tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, he ko ni yɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa ni ewoɔ baai babaoo. Shi yitso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa ni eyɛ mlɛo.

english: How do weeds actually harm my yam crop when they are growing in the same field?
ga: Te jwɛi ji oshara kɛha mi sweet potato tsei lɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm. They aggressively steal the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your yam needs to grow, while also serving as hiding places for harmful insects and plant diseases.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛkɛ ekãa juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa o-sweet potato lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii hu akɛ shĩa kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off the extra little branches growing at the bottom of my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafo tsei niji bibii lɛ? Jiemɔ shweremɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ tomato tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Those extra bottom branches, called suckers, consume the plant's energy to grow useless leaves. Removing them directs all the plant's food and energy into making bigger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni fa lɛ akɛ suckers. Kɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni okɛwo baai ni he ehiaaa. Tomato ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa tomato ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni anáa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have a special ability to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant harvested and rots, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free natural food for the next crop.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa tsei ni amɛgboi Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start planting my maize when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje ŋmãa dumɔ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ be lɛ bashɛ?

english: You should plant after the soil receives two or three steady rains and is moist down to your mid-finger depth, rather than planting immediately after the very first light rain.
ga: Esa akɛ odu nii yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni edɔ kɛyashɛ inchi teŋgbɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and skinny without producing big ears when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni toi wuji bɛ amɛhe lɛ, kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why does my crop look like it is yellowing or stopping growth after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛkpaa shweremɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Applying too much fertilizer at once or placing it directly against the stem burns the plant roots and stalls growth. Fertilizer should always be placed a few centimeters away from the plant stem in moist soil.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ shishi shikome loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni ebaaha ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai fioo komɛi.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even when I plant maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains the soil of specific nutrients. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally restores nitrogen and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen aba ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I pay to use a mechanical seed planter, or is planting my seeds by hand just as good?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo nyɔmɔ koni mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ atsu nii? Aloo ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ oniji baadu nii nakai nɔŋŋ?

english: A mechanical planter places seeds at equal depth and consistent spacing across your field, which leads to uniform germination, healthier plants, and major time savings compared to hand planting.
ga: Mɛi ni kɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ he ko ni mli kwɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtoɔ he kome yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Tsei yɛ hewalɛ Ni ekɛ be babaoo baa shi kɛ akɛto nine ni akɛduɔ lɛ he.

english: How can using an electric or solar water pump help my farm during the dry season?
