ga: Te nu pɔmp ni akɛ srawa hewalɛ loo hulu tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Electric or solar pumps draw water efficiently from wells, dams, or rivers to irrigate your fields, allowing you to grow crops and generate income year-round instead of relying only on rainfall.
ga: La loo hulu pɔmpii gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ nubu, faa, loo faa mli jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛshwie oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ nu. Ehaa oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni onáa shika yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ nugbɔshiimɔ pɛ nɔ lɛ

english: I hear about modern Western farming methods, but how do I know which ones will actually work on my land?
ga: Minu ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ anaigbɛ okwaayeli gbɛi ahe. Shi te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni baatsu nii diɛŋtsɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Not all foreign practices fit tropical soils. Focus first on basic proven techniques—like soil testing, proper row planting, and timely weeding—before investing in expensive modern equipment.
ga: Maŋsɛɛ nifeemɔi esaaa shikpɔji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ anɔ. Kɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama shishijee ŋaai ni ana he odaseyeli nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ kaa kɛ dumɔwui ni sa. kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa lɛ Dani akɛ shika awo ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii ni jara wa amli

english: What is the difference between chemical fertilizers and manure for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Chemical fertilizers give plants a fast, direct boost of specific nutrients like nitrogen, while animal manure improves the long-term soil structure and helps the ground hold moisture better.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, tɛ̃ɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii yaa hiɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ

english: Why should I buy certified hybrid maize seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa ni ji hybrid dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields and resist local pests and droughts, whereas saved seeds lose their strength over generations and produce smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odase lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni eha yibiiwoo babaoo ni ekɛte shi ewo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hɔmɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: What key steps can I take to make sure my maize field produces enough food to feed my family and sell to the market?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa manyɛ mafee koni mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ awo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahã miweku lɛ niyenii ni mahɔ̃ɔ kɛya jara nɔ?

english: To maximize yield, use quality seed varieties, keep the field completely weed-free during the first four weeks, apply fertilizer at the recommended stages, and control pests early.
ga: Bɔni afee ni nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ Okɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ atsu nii. Ha he ni jwɛi akafee lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ naa. ni akudɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Big trees act as natural umbrellas that shade the tender seedlings, reduce heat, and keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ hulutsoo baa, ehaa dɔlɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves, showing that it needs nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛya baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Atsɔɔ akɛ enɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ NPK loo urea.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil when we get too much continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni wɔnáa nugbɔ babaoo ni yaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water stays in the soil for too long without draining, it chokes the roots and encourages soil fungus to rot the tubers, which is why planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa ni ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting long wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifiteɔ be kɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ? Koni eha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground to capture more light and prevents soil-borne diseases from spoiling the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni emɔ la babaoo ni ekɛtsi helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa koni ekafite.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of pollination. Gentle wind or insects are needed to shake the flowers so pollen moves inside the flower to form a tomato fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Ehe miihia ni akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ loo kooloi ni tswaa lɛ atsu nii. koni ekɛwo fɔfɔii amli Koni eha pollen lɛ aya fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi ebaatsɔ tomato aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that hide under the leaves to suck out the sap. Spraying with organic neem oil or safe insecticides removes these insects so new leaves can grow flat and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛmu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ. Enɛ baaha baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut down some of the young suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Too many young suckers compete with the main plant for water, nutrients, and space. Removing extra suckers and keeping only two or three ensures all food goes into producing large, heavy bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, kɛ he ko he. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛto enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii muu lɛ fɛɛ afee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow a lot of green leaves but fail to produce many pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewooo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Applying too much chemical nitrogen fertilizer makes cowpeas put all their energy into leaf growth instead of flowers and pods, or tiny insects called thrips destroyed the blossoms before pods could develop.
ga: Tsofai ni ji nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii ni Ale amɛ akɛ thrips lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, amɛfiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Why does paddy rice need to stand in water, unlike crops like corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ŋmãa adamɔ nu mli ni esoro lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice roots can survive in shallow standing water, which smothers competing weeds that would otherwise choke the crop, while ensuring the rice plant has a constant supply of water to grow properly.
ga: Omɔ shishifãi baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli. Enɛ jieɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛyaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, kwɛmɔ ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ aná nu jɛɛhe ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to apply chemical fertilizer on my field right after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baafata miŋmɔji lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainwater flushes loose fertilizer off the topsoil into gutters and streams before plant roots can absorb it, wasting your money and failing to feed the crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji shika ni afiteɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is missing nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. This often happens when the soil is poor or when heavy rains wash fertilizer away from the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii jeɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer directly against the main stem of my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ mitso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem causes 'chemical burn,' which damages the delicate plant skin and roots. It is best to place fertilizer in a small ring or pocket a few centimeters away from the stem so the roots can safely reach for it.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha ‘Chemical burns’ aba ni efiteɔ tsei lɛ ahewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ amɛshishifãi Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋmeii bibii amli. loo yɛ kotoku mli ni kɛ tsɔne lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai fioo komɛi. koni anyɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe

english: How can I tell if Fall Armyworms are attacking my maize field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ Fall Armyworms miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Look inside the top leaf funnel (whorl) of young maize plants. If you see ragged holes in the leaves, saw-dust like waste inside the center, and small striped caterpillars hiding there, Fall Armyworms are present.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmã tso bibioo ko baa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ (rings) lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ona buji ni etsilɛ yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ. ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ehiɛ jɛmɛ, Fall Armyworms yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot before they are ready to be picked?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning excess tree branches and weeding your farm allows sunlight and air to dry out the pods and prevent the rot.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ duŋ shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ jwɛi shwie oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I wait until the rains are steady before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba shi dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Planting after just one early rain is risky because a dry spell might follow and kill the sprouting seeds. Waiting for steady rains ensures the soil maintains enough moisture for seedlings to grow strong roots.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ leebi nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be baanyɛ aba ni dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baanyɛ agbo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why is it better to buy certified seeds instead of using seeds from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to yield high harvests and fight off local diseases. Replanting saved seeds from high-yield crops often leads to weaker plants and much lower yields in the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛkɛ maŋ lɛ mli helai awuu. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo amli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and thin even though the leafy tops look very big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the plant puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground rather than swelling its tubers underground. Cassava needs loose, well-drained soil to build big tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tsei yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni mli tse lɛ he miihia cassava koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive shade. Regular watering and making sure plants get enough sunlight will help flowers convert into healthy fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo hulutsoo babaoo. Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ nɔmimaa akɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do weeds reduce my crop yield if I leave them growing in the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ aha miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ aba shi kɛji miha amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing food away from your main crops, allowing them to grow bigger and produce more.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Ha amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get full of small holes and turn into powder during storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ebafeɔ powda yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Storage pests like grain weevils burrow into harvested grains to feed and lay eggs. Properly drying your grain until it is hard and using airtight storage bags or containers keeps insects out and prevents crop loss.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe tamɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmaa ni akpa lɛ mli kɛhaa niyenii ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui. Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okɛ kotokui loo tsɛnsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ atsu nii koni kooloi akabote mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite.

english: Is it better for me to clear new land far out in the bush or keep farming on the land near my house?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ majie shikpɔŋ hee yɛ koo lɛ mli loo maya nɔ matsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ mishia lɛ nɔ?

english: Land deep in the bush usually has richer soil because it has rested for years, giving higher yields. Land near your house is easier to visit and protect every day, but its soil often needs extra manure or fertilizer because it has been used for a long time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ yɛ sũ ni jara wa waa ejaakɛ ehi shi afii babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa babaoo Shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ oshia lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo akɛ oooyasara ni obu he daa gbi. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he ejaakɛ akɛtsu nii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit hidden in the soil for a long time and are naturally adapted to sprout immediately when sunlight and rain hit cleared ground. Your crops need a bit more time to settle in, so early weeding gives them a fair chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe teeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ pɛ. Be fioo ko he miihia onibii lɛ koni amɛtsake amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa ni amɛdara.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off during the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during long dry spells as a natural survival trick to save water. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing its underground tubers.
ga: Cassava baagbee shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni akɛbaahere nu. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young tomato plants wilt in the afternoon sun even when the soil still has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Strong afternoon heat makes water evaporate from tomato leaves faster than the roots can drink it up. Putting dry grass or straw around the stem as mulch keeps the soil cool and helps the plant stay upright.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ tomato baai amli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Mulch kɛtsɔ jwɛi loo jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. tso lɛ shishi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme sun, irregular watering, or a lack of plant food in the soil. Giving them consistent moisture and compost helps the flowers turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haoɔ amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my yam seeds very close to each other to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When yams are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and food under the ground, and their leaves fight for sunlight. This leaves you with many small, thin tubers instead of big, heavy ones.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni eshishifãi lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ Enɛ baaha oná yitso bibioo ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ yitso agbo ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Why should I plant legumes like cowpeas on the same land as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa, tamɔ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Cowpeas act like natural soil builders by trapping nitrogen gas from the air and putting it into the ground. This feeds the maize plants nearby, making the soil richer without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ tsumalɔi kɛtsɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ aná niyenii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why is my maize growing short and pale yellow while my neighbor's maize on the same field is tall and dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ feɔ kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn pale yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build strong stems and green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or compost around the base will restore its dark green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo lɛ ni akɛaabɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaha eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my seeds when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to wait until the ground gets two or three heavy, steady rains that soak deep into the dirt. Sowing after just one light rain can burn the seeds if a dry hot week follows before the main rains settle in.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashã kɛji otsi ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa.

english: Why do small holes in my cabbage leaves slow down the growth of the whole plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ anɔ lɛ miiha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Leaves act like the plant's kitchen, using sunlight to make food for growth. When insects eat holes in the leaves, the plant cannot make enough food, which stops the cabbage head from forming properly.
ga: Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tso lɛ ŋtayaai. Kɛtsɔ hulu la ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛfee niyenii kɛha dalɛ nɔ. Kɛji kooloi ye buji ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haaa cabbage yitsei lɛ afee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my full-grown maize plants suddenly break and fall over just before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni edara lɛ fãa trukaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This usually happens because hidden pests, like stalk borers, chew through the inside of the stalk. As the plant gets heavy with mature cobs, the hollowed-out stem becomes too weak to support the weight and snaps.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ stem borers lɛ, shwieɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eshishifãi ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ baagbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua muji ni efoɔ.

english: What causes small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside my maize stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ni muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: That material is left behind by stalk borer caterpillars. They hatch on the leaves, tunnel into the stem, and eat the plant from the inside out, leaving small entry holes and waste behind.
ga: Nibii ni stem borers lɛ shiɔ yɛ sɛɛ. Amɛ fɔɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. afoɔ awoɔ tso lɛ mli ni eyeɔ tsei kɛjɛɔ emli kɛyaa kpo Eshiɔ bu bibii kɛ jwɛi yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my maize look green and healthy at first, but then fails to produce any cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Shi ekɛ cob baaa kwraa?

english: Insects inside the stalk can eat the internal tissues that carry water and food. Even if the outside stays green for a while, the plant loses the strength and nutrients needed to build cobs.
ga: Kplukai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye mligbɛ fãji ni hiɛ nu kɛ niyenii lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, kponɔgbɛ lɛ tee nɔ efee eŋɔli be fioo. Tso lɛ hu baafite ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmei lɛ.

english: How can I tell if there are insects eating inside my maize stems before the plant falls down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli dani amɛgbee shi?

english: Look for small pinholes on young leaves, tiny piles of waste in the leaf joints, or central leaves that dry up and turn brown while the rest of the plant stays green.
ga: Taomɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli, gunk bibii ni abua naa yɛ baai lɛ ahe, loo baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni baai krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ egbi. Tsei lɛ yɛ eŋɔli lolo.

english: How do I choose the right chemical to kill insects that live deep inside maize stalks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsofai ni sa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni hiɔ ŋmãa tsei amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: You need a systemic insecticide or specific worm-control chemical that penetrates the plant tissues or reaches inside the leaf whorl, because ordinary surface sprays cannot touch pests hiding inside the stem.
ga: Ohe miihia ni oná tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he ni baabote tso lɛ mli loo eshɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ata kooloi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: When is the best time to spray my maize to protect it from stem-eating worms?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ ŋmãa nɔ koni akatsi ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa?

english: Spray early when the crop is young, usually a few weeks after sprouting. Once the worms chew their way deep inside the stem, standard sprays can no longer reach or kill them.
ga: Spray kɛjɛ mra. Beni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ shwie tso lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ, Standard sprays lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe loo egbe amɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: Is it safe to pour pesticide directly into the center funnel of young maize leaves?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaafɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ awo ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, applying recommended granular or liquid treatments into the central funnel (whorl) is an effective method because young stalk borers gather there before tunneling into the stem.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofafeemɔ ni ji granular loo nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ŋta (ring) lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni mɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, stem borers bibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ jɛmɛ dani amɛboteɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Should I burn or bury old maize stalks after I finish harvesting?
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ, ani esa akɛ ashã ŋmãa tsei momo loo afu?

english: Yes, clearing, burning, or burying old stalks is helpful because stalk borers survive inside dry stalks over the dry season and will attack your new crop when rains return.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsei momo ni ajieɔ, ashãa, loo afuɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsei ni egbo lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ tsei ni egbi lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Ni ebaatutua onibii heei lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: If I see one or two broken maize plants in my farm, will the problem spread to the rest of the field?
ga: Kɛ mina ŋmãa tso kome loo enyɔ ni ekumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Naagba lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa hei krokomɛi. Ani ejɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, if one plant has stalk borers, it means adult moths are likely laying eggs across your field, so neighboring plants are at high risk of being attacked as well.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji tso ko yɛ stem borers Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ hu yɛ oshara waa akɛ abaatutua amɛ.

english: Can planting other crops together with maize help keep stem-eating caterpillars away?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa?

english: Yes, intercropping maize with plants like beans or specific trap grasses can distract or repel stem borers, reducing the damage to your main maize crop naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa loo jwɛi krɛdɛɛ ni akɛduɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie jwɛŋmɔ loo eshwie stem borers. Enɛ haa nɔ ni fiteɔ o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do people recommend planting plantains next to young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and provide broad leaves that create essential shade and moisture, helping young cocoa trees survive their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi mra.

english: What happens if I plant my crops too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting crops too close makes them compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leads to weak, thin plants and a much smaller harvest. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to thrive.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛhe waaa, kɛ ŋmaa bibioo kwraa baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda.

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to keep your farm healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛbaa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow poorly even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal valuable soil nutrients, water, and sunlight before your main crops can absorb them. Clearing weeds early gives your main crops full access to what they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jara wa, nu kɛ hulu la dani ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otso titri lɛ naa nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ fɛɛ koni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: How do I know if my maize crop needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your maize leaves start turning light green or yellow starting from the leaf tip and moving down the center, your soil lacks nitrogen and needs fertilizer like NPK or Urea.
ga: Kɛji o-corn baa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea awo mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same patch of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas helps fix nitrogen naturally back into the soil.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha sũ mli niyenii komɛi afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ bii. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits crack open before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ mli gbalaa dani manyɛ mafolɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack when watering is uneven—like a dry period followed by heavy rainfall. The inside of the tomato grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing it to burst open.
ga: Tomato mli fãa kɛji akɛ afɔ lɛ nu be fɛɛ be—tamɔ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Yam vines need to climb to expose as many leaves as possible to sunlight. This sunlight helps the plant manufacture food, which travels down to swell the underground tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛha hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Hulu la nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ

english: Can I just save seeds from my last maize harvest to plant for the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Saving seeds from hybrid crop varieties often leads to lower yields and weaker plants in the next harvest. Buying certified seeds ensures strong growth and better protection against diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha amɛdara waa ni amɛbu amɛhe jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: Why do my stored maize grains get small holes and white powder inside the bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni powda yɛŋ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by grain weevils eating the stored maize. Properly drying your grain to low moisture levels and using approved storage chemicals or airtight bags protects your harvest from weevils.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ. Nibii ni agbiɔ yɛ ŋmaa mli jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ baa shi Ni tsofai ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo vacuum bags ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to stay green and build strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔŋ mli ni amɛma tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts or beans in my farm before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When they die, that food stays in the soil and feeds the maize you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ebuaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ egbo lɛ, ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmãa ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices from the leaf undersides, or by a virus carried by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits too long in the soil without draining away. Excess standing water chokes the roots and allows fungal diseases to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Nu ni ekã shi fe nine lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field with no trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that dry out and burn in harsh, direct sunlight. They require temporary shade from taller plants like plantains to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni amɛshãa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to clear the weeds around my crops even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po.

english: Weeds act like thief plants that steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients faster than your crops can reach them, leaving your main crop weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aná. Enɛ haa otso titri lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Yam leaves need to capture as much sunlight as possible to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where they would otherwise rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfee hewalɛ ni akɛbaakwɛ bulbs lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that sit close to the soil surface. When heavy bunches of fruit grow at the top, the tree becomes top-heavy and needs wooden props to stay upright during storms.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ aduawai babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ anɔ tsii ni amɛbiɔ yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of forming fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences water stress from receiving too much or too little water.
ga: Tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ kɛjɛ nu babaoo loo fioo mli.

english: How do I know if the soil is ready for planting right after the first rain falls?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting after only one light rain is risky because the soil deeper down is still dry. You should wait until the soil stays moist a few inches down for a few consecutive days so seeds don't dry out after germinating.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Shikome pɛ oshara baa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli egbi lolo. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ aaafee 2-3 inches gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is its main food for growing leaves. When food is short in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to the new leaves at the top, leaving the old ones to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ daa. Kɛ niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha baai momoi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil still has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mibɛ amɛ lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: During very hot afternoons, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. The leaves fold or droop to reduce their surface area facing the hot sun so they don't dry out, and they usually bounce back in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe loo amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛha ŋwɛi ni kwɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ aba shi koni amɛkagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing plenty of green leaves but dropping all their flowers without making fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: If you give tomato plants too much nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy making big green leaves instead of fruit. Extreme hot weather or dry soil can also cause the plant to drop flowers to save its own life.
ga: Kɛji oha o-tomato tsei lɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ aha tso ko afɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long, suffocating the roots so they cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm land before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny bacteria on their roots that take food from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that stored food stays in the soil to help feed your next maize crop for free.
ga: Muawai bibii yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii amli. Yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Beni okpaa Niyenii ni ato lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua ni ejie o-ŋmãa niyenii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my young crop seedlings early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ midumɔwui bibii lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that grow faster than young crops, so they quickly steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your plants. Clearing them early ensures your crops get all the food they need to start strong.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni daa oya fe tsei bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the wind blows hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miitswa waa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep into the soil, and when the fruit bunch grows big and heavy, it pulls the plant off balance. Propping the tree with a strong, branched wooden stick holds the heavy weight and keeps it standing.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Ni kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ da ni egbɔjɔ Ebaaha tso lɛ akafee nɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei kɛ tsei niji ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsɔne ni tsii lɛ ni ebaaha edamɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to capture light, which the plant uses to manufacture food for the tuber underground. Staking keeps leaves off the hot ground, preventing disease and helping tubers grow bigger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ la lɛ. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa yitso lɛ ni edaa.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's hybrid harvest produce smaller crops than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi ni ji hybrid kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii bibii fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specially bred from two different parent plants to give a single high yield. The seeds produced by that crop lose those special power combinations, leading to uneven and smaller harvests.
ga: Akɛ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii kome ni nɔ kwɔ. Dumɔwui ni tsei woɔ lɛ laajeɔ nakai hewalɛ krɛdɛɛi ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nikpamɔ lɛ baaa be fɛɛ be, ni eshɛɛɛ he.

english: Why do young cocoa trees burn and die if I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very soft and sensitive, so strong direct sunlight dries out their leaves and burns them. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving larger trees overhead creates a canopy that protects the cocoa while it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛhe waaa. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni eshã baai lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei wuji ni ashiɔ yɛ yiteŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he beni edaa lɛ baa.

english: What is cocoa pollination, and why is it important for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji kookoo mli ŋmɔtɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Pollination is the process where pollen is moved within or between cocoa flowers so they can produce pods. Without pollination, the flowers will simply drop off, and your trees will not grow any cocoa pods.
ga: Pollination ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ pollen yaa kookoo fɔfɔi amli loo amɛteŋ koni anyɛ afee pods. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi. Ni otso lɛ kwɛŋ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english: How can I manually help my cocoa flowers turn into pods if natural pollination is low?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee pods kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli pollination lɛ faaa?

english: You can perform hand pollination by using a small brush or forceps to gently pick pollen from a open cocoa flower and transfer it to another flower's female part. This guarantees fertilization and increases the number of pods on your tree.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ onine awo fɔfɔii amli pollen kɛtsɔ brɔsh bibioo loo pliers ni okɛbaatsu nii blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ pollen ni yɔɔ kookoo fɔfɔi ni agbele lɛ mli lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsi kɛya fɔfɔi kroko ni ji yoo lɛ fã lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa fɔmɔ nii baa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ otso lɛ nɔ lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do so many flowers fall off my cocoa trees without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when they fail to get pollinated by insects, or when the tree is under stress from a lack of water, bad weather, or poor soil nutrients. Helping with pollination and proper farm care prevents flower drop.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ pollinators lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ miihao yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii loo niyenii ni ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Eyeɔ ebuaa yɛ pollination mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do sudden changes in weather or rainfall affect my cocoa trees' flowering?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ saa cacao tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees usually flower after a brief dry spell followed by rain. However, severe drought dries up flowers before they open, while excessive rain can wash away pollen and reduce insect activity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be kukuoo ko ni nugbɔ nɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, hɔmɔ ni naa wa baaha fɔfɔi lɛ agbi dani amɛba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ajie pollen lɛ ni eha kooloi anitsumɔ aba shi.

english: Which insects help pollinate my cocoa flowers, and how can I encourage them on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ kooloi bibii yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛwoɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo amɛhiɛ nyam yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Tiny insects called midges are the main cocoa pollinators. You can encourage them by keeping damp leaf litter and decaying plant material under the cocoa trees, which provides a safe breeding environment for them.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ ji mɛi titri ni haa kookoo mli ŋmɔtɔ baa. Obaanyɛ owo amɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ baai ni mli efɔ kɛ tsei amli nibii ni fiteɔ ni oookɛto cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛfɔɔ bii.

english: Will spraying insecticides for pests kill the beneficial bugs that help my cocoa form pods?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ashwie nɔ koni mikɛgbe kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa mi-kookoo lɛ ni efeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yes, heavy chemical spraying during peak flowering can kill beneficial midges. It is best to spray carefully, target only pest-infested parts, or spray outside the main flowering periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Okɛ ohiɛ afɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ lɛ pɛ nɔ. loo okɛshwie fɔfɔii afeemɔ be titri lɛ kponɔ

english: How does keeping shade trees on my farm affect cocoa flower production?
ga: Te shading ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa kookoo fɔfɔii afeemɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Moderate shade protects young cocoa flowers from drying out under strong sunshine and maintains humidity, which helps pollinating insects survive and keeps flowers healthy long enough to get pollinated.
ga: Shade ni sa buɔ kookoo fɔfɔi bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa mli ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ ahe waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwie fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to assist my cocoa trees for a heavy harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ maye mabua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛshɛ ŋmaa babaoo he?

english: The best time is at the start of the rainy season when the cocoa trees show abundant fresh flowering cushions along their trunks and main branches.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee. Enɛ ji be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi heei yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji wuji lɛ anɔ.

english: What basic farm care can I do to make sure my cocoa trees yield a great harvest this year?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee ŋmɔ mli saamɔ manyɛ mafee koni mi-cacao tsei lɛ awo yibii kpakpai afi nɛɛ?

english: Keep your farm weeded, prune dead or unnecessary branches to let in light, keep leaf litter on the ground for beneficial insects, and assist with hand pollination during peak flower blooms.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo tsei niji ni he ehiaaa koni ekɛ la aba. Shi baa jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ koni egbala kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kɛ nine mli pollination yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli

english: Does pruning branches from my cocoa trees prevent them from producing cocoa pods?
ga: Ani mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ ni afoɔ lɛ miitsi enaa koni ekafee kookoo ŋmeii?

english: No, proper pruning helps the tree direct its energy into producing pods rather than excess leaves. It also improves airflow and sunlight around the trunk where cocoa flowers grow.
ga: Dabi, tso lɛ ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la ni bɔleɔ he lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. Tso ni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ hu.

english: Why are the center leaves of my oil palm trees turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: This is often caused by palm weevil larvae (grubs) that burrow deep into the crown and eat the soft inner stem tissue. As they consume the heart of the tree, the central young fronds lose access to nutrients and dry out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji palm weevil larvae (beetles) ni buɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli fã ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Beni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, baai bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: What are those big white fat worms I find inside my dying palm trees, and do they hurt the tree?
ga: ŋmeii wuji ni mli ewo fɔ yɛŋ Mɛni ji nakai nɔ ni mina yɛ ŋmei tso ko ni miigbo lɛ mli? Ni ani amɛyeɔ tsei awui?

english: Those are palm weevil larvae (known locally as akokono). They hatch from eggs laid by adult beetles and feed aggressively on the soft inner heart of the tree, which eventually destroys the palm.
ga: Amɛji tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ŋmeii. (Maŋbii lɛ tsɛɔ lɛ Akokono.) Amɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ amli ŋmeii amli amɛfɔ̃ɔ. ni eyeɔ nii waa yɛ tso lɛ tsui ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaafite tso lɛ.

english: Is it true that the white grubs found inside decaying palm trunks can be eaten or sold?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ abaanyɛ aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni anaa yɛ tɛŋ tsei ni egboi anɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, palm weevil larvae are a nutritious food source rich in protein and healthy fats. Many people harvest and sell them in local Ghanaian markets, though their presence in a live tree means the crop is heavily damaged.
ga: Hɛɛ, palm weevil ŋmeii lɛ ji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ protein kɛ fɔ ni haa mɔ he waa. Mɛi babaoo kpaa amɛ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ Ghana maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei lɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli po ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii waa.

english: How do adult beetles get their worms inside a thick, solid tree trunk?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ladybug ni eda lɛ aná ŋmeii yɛ tso ni mli tse ni wa lɛ mli?

english: Adult weevils are attracted to cuts, pruning wounds, or soft tissue on the palm tree. They lay their eggs inside these entry points, and once the larvae hatch, they chew their way deep into the soft stem.
ga: Wevils ni eda lɛ sumɔɔ pilamɔi. pruning loo soft tissue ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ Amɛfɔɔ bii yɛ nɛkɛ hei ni akɛboteɔ mli nɛɛ amli. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ.

english: If the top part of my tree is damaged by pests, should I cut it off?
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai efite tso lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ?

english: Cutting off infected parts helps stop pests from spreading to healthy stems or neighboring plants. However, if the main growing tip at the center of a palm tree is completely eaten, the tree cannot recover and should be removed.
ga: Kɛ́ ofo fã ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ loo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Shi, kɛji akɛ aye ŋmei titri ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ kwraa lɛ, Tso lɛ he ejɔɔɔ lɛ ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ.

english: Why do some insect pests prefer eating the inside of plant stems instead of the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi komɛi sumɔɔ ni amɛye tso lɛ mli fã lɛ moŋ fe baai lɛ?

english: The inside of a stem or trunk contains soft, moist tissues packed with sugars and nutrients. Boring inside also protects the larvae from hot weather, heavy rain, and predators like birds.
ga: Faji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli efɔ ni sugars kɛ niyenii mli nibii yɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hu buɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi tamɔ okpoi ahe.

english: How can I tell if pests are eating my tree from the inside before the leaves fall off?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai miiye mi tsei lɛ kɛmiijɛ mli dani baai lɛ shwieɔ shi?

english: You can check for small holes in the stem leaking brownish sap, chewed plant fibers pushed out of small cracks, or a sweet, fermented smell coming from the trunk.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ buji bibii lɛ amli. Yɛ tso lɛ mli ni hoɔ nu ni ji brown lɛ. Anyɛɔ tsei ahe tsɔi ni ashɛreɔ lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo niyenii ni edɔ ni ŋɔɔ ko jɛɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: What can I do to prevent stem-boring pests from entering my crop in the first place?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akabote miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ nɔ?

english: Avoid making unnecessary cuts or deep wounds on your trees during maintenance, clean up farm debris, and promptly treat or cover any fresh cuts to prevent adult beetles from laying eggs.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni he ehiaaa loo pilamɔi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ he. Tsumɔ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi lɛ ahe Ni otsa loo oha pilamɔi heei ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ladybugs akawo ŋmeii.

english: Can insects breeding inside a dead tree spread to my healthy crops nearby?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni fɔɔ yɛ tsei ni egboi amli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli?

english: Yes, as larvae mature inside dead or decaying stems, they turn into winged adult beetles that fly to nearby healthy trees to lay new eggs. Clearing dead trees helps protect your living crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ tsei ni egboi loo ni miifite lɛ amli. Amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fiji ni foɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛyawo ŋmeii heei. Tsei ni egboi lɛ ni ooojie lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some farmers intentionally cut down old palm trees to let them rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi jɛɔ amɛtsui mli amɛfoɔ tɛŋ tsei ni egbɔjɔ koni amɛha amɛgboi lɛ?

english: Farmers sometimes fell old or unproductive palm trees intentionally to attract palm weevils, allowing them to harvest the valuable white grubs (akokono) for food or extra income.
ga: Bei komɛi lɛ, okwaafoi foɔ ŋmei tsei ni egbɔ loo ni wooo yibii lɛ yɛ yiŋtoo ko hewɔ koni amɛkɛgbala ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛkpaa ŋmeii yɛŋ (agokono) ni jara wa lɛ koni amɛná niyenii loo amɛná shika kroko.

english: What basic secrets can help me get a much higher harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Mɛni ji shishijee teemɔŋ saji komɛi ni baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: High yields come from doing the basics right: using certified seeds, spacing plants properly so they get enough light and food, and feeding the soil with compost or fertilizer at the right time.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo jɛɔ shishijee nibii ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fata he lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ koni eha la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa aba. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I make sure my harvested crops meet the high standards buyers want at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mikpamɔ lɛ kɛ shishitoo mlai ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ biɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ kpãa gbee?

english: Buyers want clean, fully mature crops without pest damage. You achieve this by protecting crops from pests early, harvesting at the right maturity stage, and drying grains or tubers properly before selling.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miitao ŋmɔshi nibii ni he tse ni eda ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli. Obaanyɛ onine ashɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooobu he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe mra lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akpaa yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛdara lɛ ni amɛgbi dumɔwui loo ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani amɛhɔ̃ɔ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I harvest more crops from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani minyɛŋ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak plants and small yields compared to crops planted with proper spacing.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni baaha yibii fioo pɛ kɛ akɛto tsei ni adu yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for plant nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is sitting too long around the roots and preventing the plant from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye oŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu eta shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni eha tso lɛ miigbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look dead in the hot afternoon sun even if they look fine in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni gboi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi kɛlɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ leebi.

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. Drooping is their natural way of folding leaves to save water until the cool evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ baai lɛ amli koni akɛto nu he kɛyashi gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and gives specific pests and soil diseases a permanent home to multiply.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ naa shia ni amɛfɔɔ daa.

english: When is the best time to feed fertilizer to my crops so I do not waste my money?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Bɔni afee ni mikafite shika?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and the crop is actively growing—usually a few weeks after shoots appear and during flowering—so roots can drink it in before rain washes it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ŋmeii lɛ eje kpo kɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ ji koni shishifãi lɛ anu dani nugbɔ lɛ aho lɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops so quickly if I leave them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive wild plants that grow faster than farm crops, stealing the water, fertilizer, and sunlight your crops need to stay strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants need wooden stakes to hold them off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ he hiaa ni akɛ tso awo mli koni ekɛhiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants grow heavy with fruit and fall over easily. Lifting them with stakes keeps leaves and fruit off wet soil, preventing rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ daa kɛ yibii ni tsii ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya. Kɛ́ owó tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai kɛ aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: How can I spot pest problems early on my farm before insects destroy my whole crop?
ga: Mayoo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mra. Dani kooloi bibii baafite miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ?

english: Walk through your farm every few days and look under leaves and inside young shoots for tiny eggs, hole bites, or insects, allowing you to stop them before they spread.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbii fioo ni okwɛ baai kɛ tsei bibii ashishi kɛji ŋmeii bibii, ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii yɛ mli koni onyɛ okpa amɛ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Can I safely farm mangoes or other crops on land that was previously used for galamsey (illegal mining)?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu mango loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛ galamsey tsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe? (shika tsuru tsamɔ ni mla eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ)

english: Land used for mining often has disturbed topsoil and toxic chemicals like mercury. Before planting, the soil needs time to recover, deep plowing, heavy organic compost, and soil testing to ensure crops do not absorb harmful chemicals.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ tsofai fɔji tamɔ mercury lɛ gbalaa shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsaa shika tsuru lɛ naa. Dani abaadu nii lɛ, ehe miihia ni sũ lɛ aná be dani ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nitsumɔ ni mli kwɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii. kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa koni ana akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eŋɔɔɔ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui.

english: Yes, intercropping with short-term crops like maize or legumes while mango trees are small helps maximize your farm space and food supply. However, once the mango trees grow large and create heavy shade, lower crops will not get enough sunlight.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmãa baa. Yɛ be mli ni mango tsei lɛ ji bibii lɛ, amɛbaaye abua ni oŋmɔ lɛ mli he kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ. Shi kɛ́ mango tso lɛ da ni ekɛ hulutsoo be ni tsii ha lɛ, Understory tsei lɛ naaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my mango tree produce plenty of flowers, but very few of them turn into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi fioo pɛ woɔ yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy flower drop usually happens because of high winds, insect damage, fungal diseases, or lack of water. Protecting the blooms from pests and ensuring adequate moisture during flowering helps more flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, tsɛŋemɔ helai, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ abu fɔfɔi ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe, ni anáa hulutsoo ni sa yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my mango tree leaves turn brown and drop off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mango trees drop leaves during severe dry spells as a survival mechanism to conserve internal water. Deep watering around the tree base and mulching with dry leaves helps keep the soil moist and leaves green.
ga: Mango tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ he. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ kɛ baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do mango trees bear fruit only once a year instead of all year round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango woɔ yibii shikome yɛ afi mli moŋ fe afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Mango trees require specific environmental triggers, such as a dry spell followed by rain, to induce flowering. Their internal hormonal cycle naturally restricts them to one or two main production seasons per year.
ga: Mango tsei biɔ shihilɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli tamɔ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ. koni ekɛwo fɔfɔii amli hewalɛ Amɛmli tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ haa amɛfeɔ nii yɛ be titri kome loo enyɔ mli yɛ afi mli.

english: How long will a newly planted grafted mango tree take to start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango ni adu ehee lɛ woɔ yibii?

english: Grafted mango trees usually start producing fruit within 3 to 4 years after planting, whereas trees grown directly from mango seeds can take 7 to 10 years to fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli beni adu amɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni mango tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 7 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my mango fruits dropping off the branches long before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-mango lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ dani edaa lɛ?

english: Young fruits fall off when the tree lacks sufficient nutrients or water to support all of them, or when fruit flies lay eggs inside them. Regular watering and managing pests early keeps the fruit attached until harvest.
ga: Yibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo kɛ́ aduawai amli ŋmeii woɔ amɛwui yɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ mra Enɛ baaha aduawai lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why do some mangoes stay very tiny while a few on the same branch grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei komɛi daraaa nakai lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ tso nine kome nɔ lɛ dara waa lɛ?

english: When a branch holds too many young mangoes, they compete for the tree's food. Removing some of the smallest, overcrowded fruits early allows the remaining mangoes to grow large and healthy.
ga: Kɛji tso nine kome ŋmɔ mango babaoo Ebaatswa akaŋ koni ená niyenii kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Ajieɔ aduawai bibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ mra Enɛ baaha mango ni eshwɛ lɛ afee wuji ni amɛhe wa.

english: What causes black spots on the skin of my mangoes while they are still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mango hewolo nɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black spots are commonly caused by anthracnose, a fungal disease that spreads in wet or humid weather. Pruning branches to allow airflow and using proper fungal sprays prevents the spots from ruining the fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, anthracnose ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli, ni akɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do some of my harvested mangoes dry up and rot internally instead of ripening nicely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni mikpaa lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Mangoes dry out or rot inside if they were infected by fungi during development or exposed to extreme heat right after harvest. Storing harvested fruit in a cool, shaded area prevents rapid moisture loss and rotting.
ga: Mango lɛ baagbi loo ebaagbo yɛ emli kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ba enɔ yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ loo ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo ni naa wa mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akaje mli ni efite oya.

english: Why should I plant my yams before planting other crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu sweet potato dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmei?

english: Yams require a full, long season with plenty of deep soil moisture to grow heavy tubers, so putting them in the ground first gives them the extra time they need before other crops start competing for nutrients.
ga: Sweet potatoes biɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni tsii akwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa be babaoo dani tsei krokomɛi jeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ he akaŋshii shishi.

english: Is it a good idea for me to plant cassava right after my yams are planted?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmei kɛji adu ŋmei amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, cassava is a tough and hardy crop that can thrive even after yams have taken early soil nutrients, allowing you to make the most out of your field space throughout the growing season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa, ni wa ni baanyɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ ná niyenii mli hewalɛ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mra po, ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmei lɛ shweremɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do farmers usually plant maize near the very end of their crop planting sequence?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ naagbee lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows much faster than heavy tuber crops like yams and cassava. Delaying maize planting prevents its tall leaves from blocking sunlight from the slower-growing root crops early on.
ga: Abele daa oya fe shishifãi ni tsii tamɔ sweet potatoes kɛ cassava. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ baai kakadaji anaa koni amɛkatsi hulu la ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni daa blɛoo lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Can I plant groundnuts and maize together in the same season after my root crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ be kome mli beni midu bulb lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, groundnuts and maize complement each other well because groundnuts mature quickly and put nitrogen back into the soil, which helps feed the nutrient-hungry maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei feɔ ekome jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmei daa oya ni ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ lɛ ni enáa niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Which months of the year are typically best for me to start planting my crops in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: In regions with two rainy seasons, the main planting period usually begins around March to April with the major rains, followed by a second shorter window around August to September.
ga: Yɛ kpokpai ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ bei enyɔ mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ March kɛyashiɔ April. kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji be kuku ni ji enyɔ ni miihe ashɛ August kɛyashi September.

english: What does it mean for my farm if my region only gets one rainy season instead of two?
ga: Mɛni ebaatsɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ yɛ enyɔ najiaŋ?

english: In a single-season area, you have only one continuous period of rainfall per year, which means you must carefully time your planting sequence so all your crops can mature before the dry weather sets in.
ga: yɛ be kome mli kpokpaa nɔ Oyɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ ni yaa nɔ yɛ afi mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ oto be ni okɛbaadu nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ ada dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba.

english: What happens to my planting schedule if the rainy season starts late in September?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi yɛ September naagbee gbɛ?

english: Late rains shorten your crops' total growing time, forcing you to adjust your schedule and choose crops or crop varieties that mature quickly so they do not dry up before harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ baaha dumɔ be fɛɛ afee kuku. Enɛ nyɛɔ onɔ ni otsakeɔ be ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ mli ni ohala ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛkagbi dani akpa.

english: How should I adapt my farming plan if the early March-April rains fail completely?
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ March-April shishijee gbɛ lɛ, te ooofee tɛŋŋ otsake gbɛjianɔi ni oto lɛ?

english: If early rains fail, you should focus your efforts on the late-season window around August and September, planting quick-growing crops that can make the best use of the limited remaining rainfall.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ mra Esa akɛ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama be lɛ naagbee gbɛ, aaafee August kɛ September. Amɛdu tsei ni daa oya ni baanyɛ amɛkɛ nugbɔ fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava take so much longer to mature than my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ fe mi-ŋmã lɛ?

english: Cassava is a root crop that spends many months building up thick underground tubers, whereas maize is a grain crop designed by nature to grow tall and produce food in just a few short months.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli tse. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, abele ji ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni adebɔɔ fee koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo niyenii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli.

english: How do groundnuts behave in the soil compared to heavy root crops like yams?
ga: Te ŋmeii feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ akɛto tsei ni shishifãi tsii tamɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ ahe?

english: Groundnuts grow shallowly and rapidly compared to yams, fixing their own nitrogen in the soil, which leaves the earth richer for surrounding or follow-up crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ to ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ahe lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daaa fioo ni amɛdaraa oya. Amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛsaa amɛ nitrogen lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle he loo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and die when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect their leaves from direct heat and strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa provides a living canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo fioo ko koni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni hiɛ ka ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the rest of the plant is green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build healthy green leaves. Feeding the soil with compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant maintain strong foliage for better yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ tso lɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when the heavy rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long without draining. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping oxygen around the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajo foi. ni ehiɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Why does my soil give me smaller maize harvests when I plant it on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil drains the specific nutrients maize relies on and allows soil pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and resets the land naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ ajɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba bɔ ni eyɔɔ tsutsu lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather becomes too hot and dry, or when they don't receive enough steady water. Mulching the base of the plant with dry grass holds moisture in the soil and lowers soil temperature.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni anáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i baa shi.

english: Curled, small pepper leaves are caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves. Checking under leaves early and spraying neem oil or recommended organic treatments stops these insects from damaging the growth.
ga: pepper baai bibii Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ baa. Akwɛ baai lɛ ashishi mra ni akɛ neem fɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ afɔ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite shweremɔ lɛ.

english: Planting crops too close forces them to compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants with small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop strong stems and larger fruits.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai ahe akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.
