He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy winds right before the fruit is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches, making them top-heavy and easy for wind to push over. Propping up the fruiting stems with sturdy wooden or bamboo stakes holds the plant steady until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ jwɛi ni mli tse. Enɛ haa efeɔ tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɔ ewoɔ lɛ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa damɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and weak even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. Clearing weeds during the first few weeks of growth ensures your crops consume all the nutrients meant for them.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves towards the sun so they can manufacture food for the plant. Elevating the leaves on stakes allows maximum light exposure, which directly feeds the underground yam tuber.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa la lɛ jeɔ kpo babaoo. ni baaha shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ

english: Leaves turn yellow at the bottom when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the crop the energy it needs to stay healthy.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering bare soil with dry plant material, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the sun from drying out the earth too fast, keeps soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your plot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ tsei ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ haa nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ehaa hulu lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water in heavy soil fills up all the air spaces, starving the cassava roots of oxygen and causing fungi to multiply. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rain to drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ ni tsii mli lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ shwereɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually a sign that tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or aphids are feeding under the leaves. Sprinkling neem water or insecticidal soap gets rid of these pests so new leaves can grow flat and clear.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ ŋmɔtɔ, tamɔ thrips loo aphids, miiye ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ ohe. Bɔni afee ni baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks water channels inside the stem. Rotating your tomatoes with non-related crops like maize or cassava starves out the disease over time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ tsakpaa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa baadu Ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ ayaje mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they face stress from dry weather, poor soil nutrition, or insect attacks. Ensuring enough shade trees, maintaining good soil moisture, and managing sap-sucking insects helps flowers turn into full pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli haomɔ mli. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Kwɛmɔ akɛ tsei ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha hulutsoo aba Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa. Ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and plant food from the main mother tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the mother tree to use its full strength to yield a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ ŋmei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant room to stretch its leaves and roots, resulting in stronger stems and larger harvests.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni ekɛbaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waa ni amɛkpaa nii babaoo.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunshine to manufacture food for the growing tuber under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, exposing the leaves to full sunlight while reducing leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa baa helai baa shi.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant seeds right after the very first small rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a hot, dry spell that bakes the ground. If you plant too quickly, the tender seedlings will dry up and die before the regular, reliable rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ baa.

english: What is liquid fertilizer, and how does it help my crops grow better than solid fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni ji nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa?

english: Liquid fertilizer is a nutrient liquid that can be sprayed onto plant leaves or soil. Because it is already dissolved in water, crops absorb it much faster than solid fertilizer, giving plants quick nourishment to grow strong.
ga: Nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii ji nu mli niyenii ni abaanyɛ afɔse ashwie tsei ahe baai loo shikpɔŋ nɔ. Ejaakɛ etsɔ nu mli momo. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ lɛ oya kwraa fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa. Ehaa tsei lɛ naa niyenii oya koni tsei lɛ adara ni amɛhe wa.

english: How long does it take for my crops to show improvement after I apply liquid fertilizer?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ beni mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ewo mli sɛɛ?

english: Because liquid fertilizer is absorbed directly through the leaves and roots, plants usually show greener leaves and faster growth within just a few days to a week after application.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsɔɔ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ bei pii lɛ tsei jieɔ baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ oya kpo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi kɛyashi otsi kome pɛ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛwo mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Will putting too much fertilizer on my crops make them grow twice as fast?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃ oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, applying too much fertilizer can burn plant roots and cause the leaves to dry up. Crops need just the right amount to grow healthy without getting stressed or damaged.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni eha baai lɛ agbi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe miihia bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni haomɔ loo nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee amɛ.

english: Can my crops absorb water and food through their leaves, or do they only feed through their roots?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ? Aloo amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ pɛ nɔ amɛyeɔ nii?

english: Crops can absorb nutrients through tiny pores on their leaves as well as through their roots. Spraying liquid fertilizer directly on the leaves helps feed weak or stressed plants very quickly.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmeii bibii amli aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. yɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ Nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni egbɔjɔ loo amɛmiihao lɛ oya.

english: Why do my crops wither so quickly during dry weather even when I put fertilizer in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa shi lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Plants need water to dissolve fertilizer in the soil so their roots can drink it up. Without moisture, solid fertilizer cannot feed the plant, and dry conditions cause leaves to lose water faster than roots can draw it in.
ga: Nu he miihia tsei koni amɛkɛjie ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa nyɛŋ aha tsei niyenii. Ni shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: How does liquid fertilizer help my plants survive hot and dry periods in Ghana?
ga: Te nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Liquid fertilizer provides essential nutrients together with moisture. This combination helps plants stay hydrated and healthy even when rainfall is light.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ŋmɔtɔ. Nɛkɛ nibii ni akɛfee ekome nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ fioo po.

english: How can I tell if my crops are hungry for extra nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni amɛná niyenii krokomɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ?

english: When crops lack nutrients, their leaves often turn pale green or yellow, growth slows down, and stems become weak. Feeding them fertilizer helps restore their deep green color and strength.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. shweremɔ blɛoo kɛ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ Kɛ́ awo amɛ fɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛnáa amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my crops turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When crops run out of essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, they take nutrients from their older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛhaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray liquid fertilizer on my crops in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Spraying during hot afternoons causes the liquid to evaporate before leaves absorb it, and hot sunshine on wet leaves can scorch and burn the tender plant foliage.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani baai lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: What is the best time of day to apply liquid spray to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baatsu nii?

english: The best time to spray crops is early in the morning or late in the afternoon when temperatures are cooler. This allows plants enough time to absorb the liquid nutrients without the sun drying them up too fast.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ ji leebi loo shwane mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaŋɔ niyenii ni ji nu lɛ ni hulu lɛ haaa egbi oya tsɔ.

english: Why should I keep large trees in my cocoa farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ tsei wuji anɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Shade trees protect young cocoa trees from harsh sunlight, keep the soil cool and moist, and drop leaves that rot into rich natural fertilizer.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. ni ehaa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa.

english: Will big shade trees steal water and nutrients away from my cocoa plants?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli?

english: Not if you use the right types of trees. Approved shade trees have deep roots that pull water from deep underground, so they do not compete with the shallow roots of cocoa plants.
ga: Jeee kɛji akɛ okɛ tso ni sa tsu nii. Tsei ni yɔɔ shade ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, enyɛŋ ekɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ ashi akaŋ.

english: Are all wild trees good to leave on my farm, or can some of them harm my crops?
ga: Koo tso fɛɛ tso sa akɛ ashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Aloo amɛteŋ ekomɛi baanyɛ aye midumɔ nii lɛ awui?

english: Some wild trees carry pests or diseases that attack cocoa, while others block too much light. It is best to keep approved trees like Terminalia or Newbouldia that help crops grow safely.
ga: Koo mli tsei komɛi yɛ kooloi loo helai ni fiteɔ kookoo. yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi tsiɔ la babaoo naa Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohiɛ tsei ni awo he odaseyeli, tamɔ Terminalia loo Newbouldia, ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdaraa shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: How do shade trees help my crops survive the hot dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Shade trees act like big umbrellas that lower the temperature on your farm and reduce evaporation, keeping moisture trapped in the soil longer during dry spells.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Without shade from trees or nurse crops like plantains, the sun cooks the leaves and dries out the roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei loo tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ bɛ hulutsoo be lɛ, hulu la baahoo baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: How do fallen tree leaves help improve the soil for my crops?
ga: Te baai ni egbee shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: When leaves fall and decay on the farm floor, they turn into natural compost that feeds the soil, improves moisture retention, and provides free nutrients to your crops.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ bafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa onibii lɛ.

english: How do tall trees protect my farm during heavy windstorms?
ga: Te tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ buɔ miŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Tall trees act as windbreaks that slow down violent gusts, preventing wind from snapping young cocoa stems or blowing off flowers before pods can form.
ga: Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa blɛoo. Tsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekafo kookoo niji bibii lɛ loo ekafo fɔfɔii lɛ dani ŋmɔtɔi aba.

english: Why is Cocobod encouraging cocoa farmers to plant specific shade trees on their land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Cocobod woɔ kookoo okwaafoi hewalɛ koni amɛdu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ pɛ yɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Research by Cocobod shows that cocoa trees grown under proper shade trees live longer, produce steadily for more years, and resist disease better than cocoa exposed to full sun.
ga: Nibii amlitaomɔ ni Cocobod fee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, kookoo tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni sa shishi lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Afee lɛ be fɛɛ be afii babaoo ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai jogbaŋŋ fe kookoo ni hulu la ni naa wa shɛɔ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm is getting too much shade or too little shade?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ miiná hulutsoo babaoo loo eshɛɛɛ hulutsoo fioo tsɔ?

english: If there is too much shade, cocoa trees produce few flowers and leaves stay damp, which causes black pod disease. If there is too little shade, leaves turn yellow and burn in the hot sun.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ Cocoa tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛ baai fioo hewɔ lɛ ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni kɛ black pod hela baa Kɛji hulutsoo be fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ shãa amɛ.

english: Can growing crops under tree shade really help me get better yields over time?
ga: Ani tsei ni miduɔ yɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi diɛŋtsɛ ni minine shɛɔ yibii kpakpai anɔ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Yes, proper tree shade reduces heat stress on crops, keeping the plants healthy and strong so they continue producing high yields for decades without wearing out the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe ŋmɔlɔ ni sa haa dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ baa shi. Ehaa tsei náa hewalɛ ni amɛhe wa No hewɔ lɛ, amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni amɛfiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How many years does it take for a newly planted cocoa tree to start producing fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii?

english: Traditional cocoa trees usually take between 3 to 5 years to bear their first pods, while newer hybrid varieties can start producing pods in about 2 to 3 years if given proper care and water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema cacao tsei lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛfeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ. yɛ be mli ni hybrid henɔi heei Ebaabɔi pods feemɔ yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni awo lɛ nu.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when exposed to strong sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have very delicate leaves that burn easily in full sun. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted around them to protect them until they grow strong enough to withstand direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: What causes cocoa flowers to drop off the tree without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers often fall off if the weather is too dry, if there are no tiny insects (midges) around to pollinate them, or if the tree lacks nutrients like potassium during its flowering stage.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee shi kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kplukai bibii (ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ) bɛ he ni amɛbaafee pollination, loo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ potassium yɛ fɔfɔi be mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is missing essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the roots are rotting from too much trapped water in the soil.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miifite kɛjɛ nu babaoo ni emɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop plants grow very fast in the beginning and then suddenly stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ da oya yɛ shishijee mli, ni no sɛɛ lɛ ekpa dalɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: Plants often stall when their roots run out of space or nutrients in the topsoil, or when hidden soil pests start attacking their root system underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ yaa wɔɔ kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ he loo niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛtutuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: What causes crop leaves to curl up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni haa tso baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mealybugs sucking the juice from the leaves, or by the plant curling its leaves to save water during extreme heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mealybugs ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if a crop disease is starting to spread on my farm before it ruins the whole harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso hela ko miibɔi gbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ekpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ?

english: Look out for early signs like small black or brown spots on leaves, leaves wilting during cool mornings, or strange white powders on stems. Checking under leaves once a week helps catch diseases early.
ga: Taomɔ mra be mli okadii, tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii diji loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso. Aloo powda yɛŋ ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ana hela mra.

english: Why do my crops dry up during the dry season while my neighbor's crops remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Crops stay green during dry spells if they have deeper roots, or if the soil is covered with dead leaves and grass (mulching) to trap moisture and protect the roots from heat.
ga: Tsei baahi shi eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli kɛji amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi (mulch) ehà shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli ni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he.

english: Does growing the same crop on the same piece of land every year weaken the crop's yield?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi?

english: Yes, planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to multiply, causing future yields to drop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii ni abaafee wɔsɛɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the stems of my young crops falling over and rotting at ground level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a fungal condition called damping-off, which happens when the soil is too wet, cold, or packed too tightly around young stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening, ni baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ, edɔ tsɔ, loo ebɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and dying during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants do not have deep root systems yet and cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. They need partial shade from food crops like plantain or cassava to retain moisture and protect their delicate leaves from burning.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lolo, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava mli. Koni hulutsoo ahi shi ni ebu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, overly shaded, or high-humidity conditions, especially when weeds around the base of the tree trap excess moisture.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ. Shade babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ tsɔ. aloo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ mɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for healthy leaf development and good cob formation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai ni wa kɛ ŋmeii kpakpai afeemɔ.

english: Why do I see small caterpillars eating inside the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni miiye mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common crop pest that feeds on the growing centers of maize, which damages the plant's ability to sprout leaves and leaves large holes if not managed early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji baa kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why are the cassava stems growing very tall and leafy, but the tubers underground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or receives excessive water early on, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing energy underground in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ mra. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ebaa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeekɛto shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes twisting, curling up, and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebɔle ehe, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hei komɛi lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection transmitted by small whiteflies that prevents the plant from producing normal food and limits root growth.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ afee niyenii bɔ ni sa, ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ ada.

english: Planting the same crop year after year strips the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up permanently in the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: How does planting cowpea or groundnuts on my farm help my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpea and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root nodules, naturally enriching the soil with fresh fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii heei kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off without fruiting when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil needed for blossom retention.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔi lɛ mli.

english: Why do plantain suckers take much longer to bear fruit when planted late into the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Plantains require continuous moisture during their early root growth phase; planting them late exposes them to dry weather too early, delaying their development cycle.
ga: Plantains he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ shishijee be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ. Dumɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baaha shihilɛi lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ shweremɔ be lɛ mli.

english: What actually makes a seed sprout and come to life once I bury it in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwu ko kwɛ̃ɔ ni ebaa wala mli kɛ́ mitɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need three main things to 'wake up' and germinate: moisture, warmth from the soil, and air. Water softens the outer seed coat and triggers the baby plant inside to send roots down for stability and shoots up toward the sun.
ga: Nibii etɛ he miihia dumɔwui koni ‘amɛte shi’ ni amɛkwɛ̃: ŋmɔtɔ, dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Nu lɛ haa dumɔwu lɛ kponɔgbɛ tsɔne lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ewoɔ dumɔwu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni eshishifãi lɛ aya shi shiŋŋ ni eda kɛya hulu lɛ he.

english: Do my young seedlings need fertilizer as soon as they pop out of the ground?
ga: Ani mi dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ?

english: No, newly germinated seedlings do not need fertilizer immediately. They feed on energy stored inside the seed itself during their first few days. You should wait until they grow a few true leaves and strong roots before applying light fertilizer or manure.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui heei ahe ehiaaa ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Amɛyeɔ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo lɛ amli. Esa akɛ omɛ ni amɛná baai diɛŋtsɛ fioo komɛi kɛ shishifãi ni wa dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni waaa awo mli.

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant fail to sprout while others right next to them come up fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if they are buried too deep, if the soil is too dry or flooded, or if soil pests eat them. Using high-quality certified seeds and planting them at the correct depth ensures more even sprouting across your field.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. loo kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ. Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ odaseyeli tsu nii ni okɛdu yɛ he ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How exactly do my crops drink water from the ground?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops 'drink' through tiny, microscopic hairs on their underground roots. These root hairs act like small drinking straws, sucking up soil moisture along with dissolved nutrients and pumping them up through the stem to the leaves.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ‘nuɔ’ kɛtsɔɔ yitsɔi bibii waa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ shishifãi ahe yitsɔi nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ jwɛi bibii ni akɛnuɔ nii. Ekɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ fataa niyenii ni mli ewo muji lɛ he. Kɛkɛ ni atsɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it better for me to pour water directly on the soil around the plant roots or spray water over all the leaves?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo mafɔ nu yɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: It is always best to apply water directly to the soil around the roots. Plants cannot 'drink' water through their leaves, and keeping leaves constantly wet can attract fungal diseases and molds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be akɛ ooofɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ nu. Tsei nyɛŋ ‘anu’ nu kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni kɛ́ aha baai lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbala ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii helai.

english: How can I tell if my young crops are getting too much water or not enough to drink?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi dumɔwui lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛnuuu nu?

english: If plants do not get enough water, their leaves will curl up, look limp, and turn brown. If they get too much water, the soil stays soggy, the roots starve for air, and the leaves will turn pale yellow and drop off.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ naaa nu bɔ ni sa lɛ, baai lɛ baakpokpo, ebaafee tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ, ni ebaatsɔ asarasu. Kɛji nu babaoo ba enɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ, ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: How do plants eat the fertilizer or manure that I spread on my farm?
ga: Te tsei feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants cannot eat solid food directly. Fertilizer and manure must first dissolve in soil water. Once dissolved, the plant roots absorb the nutrient-rich water and carry food throughout the plant so it can grow strong.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ aye niyenii ni wa tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kooloi ashishifãi awo shikpɔŋ nu lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛji etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ Tso shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛ niyenii yaa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I mix manure into my land before planting or put it around the crops after they sprout?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu loo mikɛfata he yɛ he fɛɛ he? Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ kwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ?

english: Mixing well-rotted manure into the soil a few weeks before planting is ideal because it enriches the ground and helps hold water. You can also add smaller amounts around growing crops later to give them an extra boost.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo sũ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi dani adu lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Obaanyɛ okɛ nibii bibii hu afata he kɛbɔle he. Obaanyɛ odu tsei yɛ sɛɛ mli koni oha amɛ hewalɛi krɛdɛɛi.

english: Why do some cassava plants on my farm grow huge tubers while others stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa lolo lɛ?

english: Plants compete with each other for space, sunlight, water, and nutrients. If crops are planted too close together, or if weeds steal their food, some plants will starve and stay small while stronger ones dominate.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Aloo kɛji jwɛi ju niyenii Hɔmɔ baaye tsei komɛi ni amɛbaafee bibii, shi tsei ni he wa lɛ baaye he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do improved crop varieties produce larger fruits than the traditional seeds saved from my old harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii wuji fe shishijee dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mikpamɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are specially bred to use water and soil nutrients more efficiently and resist common pests. This allows the plant to put more energy into growing bigger tubers, grains, or fruits compared to older seeds.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ bulbs wuji, ŋmaa, loo aduawai. Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni egbɔ lɛ ahe

english: How do I know how many cocoa trees I am supposed to plant on one acre of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kookoo tsei enyiɛ esa akɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ?

english: Spacing cocoa trees properly at about 3 meters by 3 meters allows roughly 435 trees per acre, which gives each plant enough space for roots to spread and leaves to capture sunlight without crowding each other.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei ateŋ lɛ ji aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3, ni ehaa aaafee tsei 435 yɛ acre kome mli. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni baai lɛ hu anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la lɛ ni amɛtsiii amɛhe.

english: What does climate-smart farming mean for my cocoa farm when the rains no longer fall as expected?
ga: Mɛni okwaayeli ni kɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he lɛ tsɔɔ kɛha mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ dɔŋŋ taakɛ akpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Climate-smart farming means using practical techniques like planting shade trees, keeping soil covered with mulch, and planting drought-tolerant crop varieties so your farm stays productive even when weather patterns change.
ga: Okwaayeli ni kɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he lɛ tsɔɔ ŋaai ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii tamɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ adumɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ adumɔ Koni oŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsake po.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight; without temporary shade crops like plantains to shelter them, the sun scorches their leaves and dries out their roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains akɛ wɔɔhe bɛ lɛ, Hulu lɛ hu shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ.

english: Why do cocoa farms in neighboring areas like Ivory Coast often produce more pods than my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ Ivory Coast lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Higher cocoa production usually comes from using high-yielding hybrid seeds, practicing regular pruning, applying the right fertilizer at the correct time, and keeping the farm free from dense weeds and diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni anáa babaoo lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi daa Nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli ni aha jwɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ helai akafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I leave fallen leaves on the ground under my trees instead of sweeping them away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi moŋ fe ni mafolɔ amɛ?

english: Leaving fallen leaves creates a natural blanket over the soil that holds moisture, protects roots from hot weather, and gradually breaks down into natural nutrients that feed your crops.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebuɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa onibii lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to let my cocoa trees grow as tall and bushy as they want?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mahã mi-cacao tsei lɛ adara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji bɔ ni amɛsumɔɔ lɛ?

english: Overgrown cocoa trees waste energy growing unnecessary branches instead of pods, and their thick canopy blocks airflow and sunlight, which creates a wet environment where pod diseases easily spread.
ga: Cacao tso ni eda fe nine lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ amli yɛ ŋmeii lɛ najiaŋ. ni ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni pod helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mli oya.

english: Can I continue growing cassava inside my farm after my cocoa trees have grown big?
ga: Ani manyɛ maya nɔ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni kookoo tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: Mature cocoa trees create a dense canopy that blocks sunlight, which cassava needs to grow tubers, and the heavy roots of mature cocoa will compete strongly with cassava for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni edara lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. ni ŋmei he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii Ni ŋmei ni eda lɛ shishifãi ni wa lɛ kɛ ŋmei yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but most of them fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani amɛteŋ babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they lack sufficient water or nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny beneficial insects (midges) to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land has good soil for planting cocoa before I clear it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ kookoo dani mafo mli?

english: Good cocoa soil is dark, crumbly, deep enough for long roots to grow, and retains moisture well without holding standing water after heavy rains.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ mli bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi kakadaji akwɛ̃. Ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛɛɛ nu mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly wet conditions and spreads through splashing rainwater when the farm canopy is too dense.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine lɛ mli. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli ewo wu tsɔ.

english: How do I know if fertilizer will actually help my crops or if it is a waste of money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ loo eji shika fitemɔ?

english: Fertilizer feeds the plant by restoring missing nutrients to tired soil. If your land has been farmed for many seasons without rest, using the right fertilizer restores nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus so your crops can yield much more.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii kɛtsɔ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ ni ekɛbaa shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ atsu oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii bei babaoo ni hejɔɔmɔ bɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus aba ekoŋŋ. Koni oha onibii awo yibii babaoo

english: Why does my maize turn yellow even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Maize turns yellow when nitrogen is missing or washed away by heavy rains. Fertilizer must be applied when the soil is moist and buried slightly so the plant roots can swallow the food before rain carries it off.
ga: Abɛi feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen lɛ laaje loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho kɛtee. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ami niyenii lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ afɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to fertilizer if I spread it on dry ground when rain does not fall?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer left on top of dry dirt evaporates into the air or blows away, losing its power. For fertilizer to work as a good investment, it must dissolve in damp soil so crop roots can drink it in.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ashiɔ yɛ muji ni egbi nɔ lɛ baatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo ebaatswa, ni no baaha ehe awa. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ afee nɔ ni he baaba sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, esa akɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Is buying commercial chemical fertilizer better than just using animal manure on my farm?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ hemɔ hi fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Both are helpful in different ways. Manure improves the soft texture and water-holding power of your soil over time, while chemical fertilizer provides fast, concentrated food for quick crop growth.
ga: Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ gbɛ̀i srɔtoi anɔ. Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ bɔ ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni mli wa ni yaa oya kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ oya lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing large green leaves but no fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ebɛ yibii lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants focus all their energy on leaf growth instead of flowers. Switching to a fertilizer rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages plants to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing heavy yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, ground water, and soil food. Proper spacing allows each plant to get enough sunlight and soil space to build strong stalks and large fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tsei ahe tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my main crops whenever I put fertilizer on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal nutrients before your crops can reach them. You should always clear weeds before applying fertilizer so your crops get all the food you paid for.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ dani onibii lɛ baashɛ. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ be fɛɛ be dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni owo he nyɔmɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and wilt during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink from the ground. Putting dry leaves or straw as mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mulching kɛ baai loo jwɛi ni akɛbɔleɔ he. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties protects your farm from this problem.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmei mli Ekɛ ŋmei mosaic hela ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛbaa ŋmei henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ naagba nɛɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting quickly after I take them out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rot happens when small cuts from harvest tools allow dirt germs to enter the tuber. Storing undamaged yams in a cool, airy barn off the bare ground prevents spoilage.
ga: Rot baa kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni afo lɛ ba. Kɛjɛ nibii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ amli lɛ, helai ni he tseee baanyɛ abote ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes ni efiteee lɛ to ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli mli yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the large shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ hulutsoo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily scorched by direct daylight. Leaving mature shade trees creates a cool microclimate and retains moisture in the soil, protecting the cocoa plants while their root systems develop.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ fioo, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebuɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my mature oil palm trees produce plenty of flowers but fail to grow heavy fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei ni eda lɛ ekomɛi woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi amɛwooo aduawai akui wuji lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees rely on beneficial insects like small pollinators or wind to transfer pollen from male to female flowers. If pollinators are absent or the tree lacks vital soil nutrients, the female flowers drop off without producing oil palm bunches.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ kooloi bibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa loo kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ. Koni ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei amli. Kɛji akɛ kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ bɛ loo tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Fɔfɔi yei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee oil palm panicles.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without producing any tomatoes during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato pollen to dry out and become sterile. When the flower cannot be fertilized, the plant sheds the blossom to conserve its water and energy for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato mli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Beni anyɛɛɛ afɔ fɔfɔi ko nɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ato koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape along the middle line?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ teŋgbɛ line lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the main vein of maize leaves indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy growth, so applying organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy green foliage.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ fãji titrii lɛ ahe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do groundnut plants help make the soil better for the next crop I plant on the same plot?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tso ko aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants form a relationship with helpful soil bacteria that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the roots. When the plant leaves and roots decay after harvest, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanut tsei kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ wekukpaa. Beni tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages cassava to spend all its energy growing foliage above ground. Without balanced nutrients like potassium, the plant neglects storing starch in its root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmei hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium bɛ lɛ, tsei kuɔ amɛhiɛ amɛshwieɔ nɔ akɛ amɛbaato starch yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of just trailing across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking holds yam leaves up high so they can catch direct sunlight to produce energy for heavy tuber growth, while keeping the leaves clean and clear of ground diseases.
ga: Ni akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ baawo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs agboi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ ahe atse ni helai akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do armyworms hide deep inside the central funnel of my maize plants during the day and only feed at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ nii gbɛkɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide inside the cool, moist leaf funnel during daylight hours to protect themselves from intense heat and predators like birds. They emerge during the cooler night hours when it is safer to feed on leaves.
ga: Asraafoi akuu lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai ni mli ejɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ tamɔ okpoi ahe. Amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ waa lɛ amli. Enɛ ji be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ ayeɔ baai lɛ.

english: Why do my crops give me smaller harvests when I plant them very close together to fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ miŋmɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for limited water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block each other's sunlight. Proper spacing gives every plant enough space, light, and food to grow big fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ, la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that suck up nutrients and soil moisture faster than crops can. They steal the food your crops need to stay strong, leaving the crops hungry even if water is available.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni tsei baanyɛ afee. Amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa onibii koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ moŋ.

english: Why should I plant plantains in the same field with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that shade the cocoa, keeping the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ ahe waaa waa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa kookoo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Heavy rains often wash this nutrient out of the topsoil, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help bring the green color back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ akwɛ amɛ ŋmɔji kɛ baai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can tell cassava is mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the main stem becomes thick and woody. You can also carefully clear away soil near the base of one plant to check if the root has grown broad and firm.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ yucca ko eda kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso titri lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tso. Obaanyɛ ojie sũ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ hu koni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛma shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do small caterpillars suddenly show up and eat the whorl inside my young maize plants after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jieɔ amɛhe kpo trukaa ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms that hatch from eggs laid by moths when warm, rainy weather arrives. They gather in the central funnel of young maize because the hidden stem tissue inside is soft, sweet, and protected from dry heat.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall armyworms ni fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ ba. abua naa yɛ ŋmãa bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋɔɔ, ni ebuɔ he koni la ni tsoɔ lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do I need to clear land and use tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji akwɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to generate food that travels down to swell the tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up off the damp ground, giving them full sun exposure and keeping them free from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why are my pepper blossoms falling off the plant without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off when the heat is too intense, when watering is uneven, or when the soil lacks phosphorus. Keeping the soil evenly damp with compost or mulch helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so they can turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwie shi pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni enyɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do extension officers encourage me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-extension agent lɛ woɔ mi hewalɛ koni madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they feed natural nutrients into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for your maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛhaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-corn tsei lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: When too many shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they compete for the same food, water, and sunlight, resulting in thin plants and small bunches. Leaving only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main plant gets enough nourishment to produce a large bunch.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ kui bibii. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii 1 loo 2 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ehiɛɛɛ shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee niji agboi.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling upward and growing very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny, invisible sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Applying natural sprays like neem oil or wood ash water helps deter these sap-sucking pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai ashishi loo helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ Adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi tamɔ neem fɔ loo tso mli ashwishwɛ nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi nɛkɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why is it better to build planting mounds across a slope instead of straight down the hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ama gɔŋ ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ moŋ fe ni oootsɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Making ridges across a slope acts as a barrier against heavy rain runoff, preventing topsoil and fertilizers from washing away down the hill. This holds water in the soil longer so crop roots can drink.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ ko ni afeɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkaho gɔŋ lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and crisp during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate intense, direct sunlight. During dry periods, sunlight scorches the leaves and evaporates soil moisture rapidly, which is why planting shade trees like plantains alongside cocoa is essential.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Hulu la shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Nɔ ni haa ehe hiaa ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for green growth. The plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to nourish the newer growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Curled pepper leaves are often caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or thrips hiding on the underside of leaves. As they suck out sap, they distort leaf growth and can transfer plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Beni amɛmuɔ mliki lɛ Amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tsei ahe helai amɛshwã.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms falling off the stem instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly between bone dry and overly wet. Stress causes the plant to drop blossoms to save its own energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa yɛ wu ni egbi kɛ nɔ ni efɔ fe nine lɛ teŋ. Haomɔ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he.

english: How do I know which way to point a cassava stem cutting when sticking it into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole bɔ ni afoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Look closely at the small raised nodes or growth buds on the stem. Make sure these buds point upwards toward the sky before planting so the shoot can grow straight up without wasting energy.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii ni awó nɔ loo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani odu. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ ada tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛfiteee hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight. Elevating the leaves off the damp ground exposes them to more sun for better tuber growth and reduces fungal diseases caused by wet soil contact.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo koni bulb lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni akɛkpeɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ aba shi

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ajie lɛ

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow around one mother plantain creates competition for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, resulting in larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he Dumɔwu kome pɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantain tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does planting groundnuts make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei dumɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnuts are harvested, that extra nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my oil palm tree produce flowers but fail to grow any palm bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei yɛ fɔfɔi shi amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Oil palms rely on tiny insects like weevils to carry pollen from male flowers to female flowers. If these insects are absent or if the palm is experiencing severe drought stress, the female flowers dry up without making fruit.
ga: Mu tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii anɔ koni amɛkɛ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii lɛ amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ bɛ loo tso lɛ naa hɔmɔ he haomɔ ni naa wa lɛ, Fɔfɔi yei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why do wild weeds spring up faster than my crops right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally adapted to survive harsh soils and react instantly to moisture. They germinate quickly to grab sunlight and soil nutrients before planted crop seeds fully break out of their shells.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ ni amɛtsuɔ he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ba. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛŋɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani dumɔwui ni adu lɛ jeɔ amɛhe kwraa kɛjɛɔ amɛmli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have large leaves that provide living shade, acting like umbrellas to keep the soil moist and cool while the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and thin when I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too tightly together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in crowded plants that stay small and yield very little food.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui lɛ babaoo tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is running low on basic plant food, especially nitrogen. The plant moves the little nourishment it has left from the older bottom leaves to the top to stay alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii, titri lɛ nitrogen. Tsei tsiɔ niyenii bibii ni eshwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why is it bad for me to keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the field, making future harvests smaller.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi kɛ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaa lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Excess water sitting in the soil pushes out the air that roots need to breathe, causing the tubers to drown and allowing soft-rot fungi to attack them underground.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni esa akɛ shishifãi lɛ amu lɛ kɛyaa. Okɛ ŋmeii lɛ awo nu mli ni oha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ atutua amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do people tell me to spread dry grass and leaves around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ashwie he fɛɛ he lɛ? Mi ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from growing easily.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsĩɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ oya

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop to the ground before they can turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a sudden lack of nutrients, as the plant tries to save water and energy by abandoning new growth.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pepper tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ shweremɔ hee ni amɛshiɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers suggest I pinch off small side shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? kɛjɛ tomato tso lɛ mli

english: Removing extra shoots forces the plant to send its energy and water into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasting resources on useless leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni daraa lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite nibii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why do small caterpillars like to hide inside the leafy funnels of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛtee amɛhe amɛwo mi-baby corn lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: The central funnel of a young maize plant is soft, moist, and tender, offering caterpillars protection from birds while providing a continuous supply of young leaves to eat.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋshɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ blɛoo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ okpoi ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ baai bibii haa koni aye be fɛɛ be.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant the seeds from my harvest of hybrid maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni maduɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strong qualities in the next generation, leading to mixed plant sizes, lower yields, and weaker resistance to local pests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛsui ni mli wa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ futuɔ, yibiiwoo baa shi, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ko ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas together with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa?

english: Yes, cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This natural process feeds the soil and helps your maize grow better without wearing out the land as quickly.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmã lɛ ni edaa jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee oya.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the field. Switching to crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa saplings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect their soft leaves from harsh, direct sunlight. Leaving some large shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa keeps the ground cool and moist until the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks next to my yam vines as they start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso nine kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Sweet potato wain tso be mli ni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ?

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need sunlight to make food for their tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, which stops diseases from spreading and helps the tubers grow bigger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haaa hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã, ni eyeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy soil during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the tubers remain dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi ni amɛgbi ni amɛhe awa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot and dry or when the plant doesn't get steady water. Heat stress causes the plant to drop its flowers to save water and stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu daa Heat stress haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: How do I know the right time to start sowing seeds at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔwui adumɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to wait until rains become steady and thoroughly wet the soil—usually after two or three strong rains—rather than planting after the very first rain, which might be followed by a long dry spell that kills fresh seeds.
