ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shi ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afɔ shi jogbaŋŋ—bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ—fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ekolɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni baafite dumɔwui heei baanyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ.

english: What makes the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that suck sap from young leaves and pass viruses to the plant. Spraying the crop early with organic neem oil or recommended treatments keeps these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ tsofa ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ mli nu lɛ ni ekɛ hela lɛ yaa tso lɛ nɔ Okɛ tsofa ni ji organic neem fɔ loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko atsu nii obaanyɛ oye obua ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow aggressively and steal sunlight, soil water, and nutrients that were meant for your crops. Clearing weeds during the early weeks of planting gives your crops the space and food they need to develop properly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, sũ mli nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ otsi klɛŋklɛŋ ni okɛduɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that easily burn under direct sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them creates a living umbrella that gives the cocoa seedlings the shade and moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass or cocoa pod husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Akɛ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Covering the soil, which is called mulching, acts like a blanket. It traps moisture so you water less, stops sunlight from letting weeds grow, and keeps heavy rain from washing away your rich topsoil.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Emɔɔ nu mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu fioo pɛ awo mli. Ehaa hulu la lɛ haaa jwɛi akwɛ̃. ni otsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ oshikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable garden early in the morning or in the middle of the hot day?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo shwane mli yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the water before the sun causes it to evaporate. Watering during the hot afternoon wastes water and can stress the plants.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani hulu lɛ haa etsɔɔ la. Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaafite nu, ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ aná haomɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow instead of stay dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient that helps plants grow green and leafy. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help them regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers plant groundnuts between rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts spread out over the ground to block weeds and keep the soil cool. More importantly, groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow bigger.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akabote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ, Peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ feɔ agbo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and giving the plants enough water helps the flowers stay attached and produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni oha tsei lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo tomato.

english: How do I choose the best part of a cassava stem to plant in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei lɛ fãi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should choose the middle part of a stem from a healthy, mature plant that is 8 to 12 months old. Make sure the stem piece has at least 4 to 6 strong raised nodes (buds), as these are where the new roots and leaves will sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala tso lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ kɛjɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, tso lɛ fã lɛ aná ŋmeii (shishifãi) ​​ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 4 kɛyashi 6, ejaakɛ biɛ ji he ni shishifãi kɛ baai heei baakwɛ̃ yɛ.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and allowing them to get maximum sun.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsi helai anaa ni oye obua ni oná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni ooonyɛ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants so quickly?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe oya nɛkɛ?

english: These holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the leaves at the center of the plant during the day and eat at night. Checking your farm early and using recommended treatments early prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ baai amli yɛ shwane mli ni amɛyeɔ nii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaatsi ŋmɔji anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can sprinkling clean wood ash from my kitchen fire on vegetable leaves protect them from pests?
ga: Ani tso sũ ni mli tse ni jɛɔ shĩa la mli ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai ahe baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa?

english: Yes, dry wood ash irritates the soft bodies of crawling insects like caterpillars and aphids, preventing them from eating the leaves. However, you need to reapply it after it rains.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso mli sũ ni egbi lɛ haa kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ agbɔmɔtsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli fuɔ. Enɛ haaa amɛye baai lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okɛwo mli ekoŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ.

english: What actually causes mold or white powdery stuff to grow on my harvested grains?
ga: Mɛni miiha ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ miije kpo yɛ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ anɔ?

english: Mold is caused by microscopic organisms called fungi. They are tiny living things you cannot see with your bare eyes, and they grow on crops when conditions are warm and wet.
ga: Nibii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ fungi kɛ fungi baa. Amɛji bɔɔ nii bibii. ni okɛ ohiɛ nyɛŋ ana Ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ.

english: Are there tiny organisms on my farm that can spoil my produce without me seeing them?
ga: Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ jɛmɛ. Ani nibii komɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii ni minaaa?

english: Yes, there are invisible microorganisms called fungi. Even though you cannot see them, they can live on your crops and produce harmful chemical toxins.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nibii bibii ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ amɛ fungi lɛ yɛ. Kɛji akɛ onyɛɛɛ ona amɛ po. Shi amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni amɛfee tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yɔɔ gbeyei.

english: What are aflatoxins, and how do they get onto my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji aflatoksin? Ni te fee tɛŋŋ ni ebote miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Aflatoxins are dangerous chemicals produced by tiny, invisible microorganisms called fungi. They form on crops when the harvested produce is exposed to high heat and moisture.
ga: Aflatoxin ji tsofa ko ni yɔɔ oshara ni nibii bibii ni anaaa amɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ fungi lɛ feɔ. Amɛfeɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ shɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa he.

english: Can my harvested crops contain hidden poisons even if I do not see any insects on them?
ga: Ani tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ tsei ni mikpa lɛ amli? Eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi moŋ.

english: Yes, crops can carry invisible chemicals called aflatoxins. These are produced by tiny fungi that you cannot see with your eyes, especially if the grains were left in damp and warm conditions.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ahiɛ tsofai ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ amɛ aflatoxins lɛ. Fungi bibii ji mɛi ni feɔ enɛɛmɛi. ni onyɛɛɛ okɛ ohiŋmɛii ana Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmaa lɛ yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni edɔ.

english: Why does heat and wetness make my stored maize and groundnuts spoil faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo haa mi-ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ oya lɛ?

english: Heat and moisture are the two main conditions that invisible fungi need to grow and produce dangerous chemicals called aflatoxins on your crops.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ji shihilɛi titrii enyɔ ni he hiaa ni ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ adara ni amɛfee tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni atsɛɔ amɛ aflatoxins lɛ yɛ onibii amli.

english: Why does moisture cause my harvested crops to become unsafe to eat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulutsoo be lɛ haaa mikpamɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ lɛ?

english: Moisture, especially when combined with heat, allows tiny unseen fungi to multiply and produce dangerous chemicals known as aflatoxins that poison the food.
ga: Fɛ̃i, titri lɛ kɛ akɛ dɔlɛ fata he lɛ baaha ŋmeii bibii ni Anaaa lɛ aba, amɛshwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara ni atsɛɔ amɛ aflatoxins ni yeɔ niyenii awui.

english: How do warm weather and rain work together to damage my harvested produce?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ feɔ ekome kɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: The combination of heat and wetness creates the exact conditions needed for invisible fungi to grow and produce harmful toxins like aflatoxins on your produce.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛfee ekome lɛ haa shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa koni ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ adara ni ekɛ tsofai fɔji tamɔ aflatoxin ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ aba.

english: Why is it important for me to cover my harvested crops when leaving them outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mishi yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering your crops protects them from moisture and extreme heat. Without heat and moisture, the invisible fungi cannot produce dangerous aflatoxin chemicals.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko ha onibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛji hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i bɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee tsofa ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ji aflatoxin lɛ.

english: How does keeping my harvested grains covered protect them from dangerous chemicals?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mikpamɔ lɛ ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe?

english: Keeping crops covered stops heat and moisture from building up on them, which prevents invisible fungi from producing harmful toxins called aflatoxins.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko. Enɛ haaa ŋmei ni anaaa lɛ lɛ afee tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni atsɛɔ lɛ aflatoxins lɛ.

english: What simple step can I take to stop invisible fungi from poisoning my stored crops?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo Koni matsi ŋmei ko ni anaaa lɛ naa koni ekafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ?

english: You must keep your crops covered and protected from moisture and excess heat, because fungi need heat and moisture to produce dangerous aflatoxin chemicals.
ga: Esa akɛ obu onibii ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛ dɔlɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo he miihia ŋmei koni enyɛ efee tsofa ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ji aflatoxin lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my maize seeds in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting maize with proper spacing—about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between plants—ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ ni aaafee sɛntimitai 75 yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ kɛ sɛntimitai 40 yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋmãa agboi ni mli wa aba.

english: What will happen to my cassava if I plant the cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If cassava cuttings are planted too close together, their underground roots compete for nutrients and space, resulting in thin, small tubers instead of large, heavy yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ he ko ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Why are my vegetable seedlings turning yellow and staying thin after sprouting densely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibioo yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When too many seeds germinate in one small spot, they choke each other out for light and nutrients. Removing the extra, weaker shoots gives the remaining plants the space they need to grow strong and green.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he bibioo kome lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ dumɔwui aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ yɛ la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ kɛ nɔ ni fa babaoo lɛ, ehaa tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ náa he ko ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, offering the necessary shade and moisture cocoa seedlings need during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I trim some of the leaves off my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Trimming lower leaves improves airflow around the plant to prevent fungal diseases and directs the plant's energy into growing bigger fruits rather than unnecessary leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ. Tsei ni akɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni akɛ tsei ahewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛwo aduawai wuji Yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: If I have a small piece of land, will I get a larger harvest if I crowd more crops into it?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he?

english: Crowding crops reduces overall harvest because overcrowded plants produce weak yields or fail to bear fruit. Giving fewer plants adequate space yields a heavier, higher-quality total harvest.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ baa shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo loo amɛwooo yibii. Kɛ akɛ tsei ni he ko bɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ ha lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni tsii, ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up into tight tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during peak heat as a natural defense to trap moisture and prevent water loss through evaporation when the sun is hottest.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekɛtsi nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do groundnut and carrot crops need loose, tilled soil to produce well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hiaa ŋmei kɛ karɔt tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Crops that form their food underground require soft, loose soil so their roots and pods can expand freely without struggling against hard, compacted dirt.
ga: Tsei ni feɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse. No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã amɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkɛ muji ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ebɔko.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings become tall and weak when left in the nursery bed for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When pepper seedlings sit too long in a crowded nursery bed, they stretch rapidly upward searching for sunlight, making their stems thin and fragile instead of thick and sturdy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui lɛ ta shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ saatsoi ni eyi obɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe oya koni amɛyatao hulu la. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: How can I tell if my yam plants are not getting enough food from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: If yam leaves turn pale yellow instead of dark green or if the vines stop growing vigorously during the rainy season, the soil lacks vital nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ Aloo kɛji wain tso lɛ kpa dalɛ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of a maize plant mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow, so when the soil runs low, the plant takes nitrogen from its older lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin with small ears when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛtoi bibii yɔɔ mli beni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and food from the soil. Giving each seed enough space allows the plant to build a thick, strong stem and grow larger ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná tsitsi ni mli wa, ni wa kɛ toii wuji.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to soaked too quickly. Water your tomatoes regularly and provide light shade during extreme heat to help the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Okɛ nu awo otomatoi lɛ amli daa ni oha amɛ hulutsoo bei amli koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo aduawai.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunshine and heat. Leaving a few large shade trees or planting plantains beside young cocoa keeps the soil cool and protects the fragile leaves from scorching until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaatsi baai ni waaa lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the dirt before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in the ground when rain water sits on top of the soil and cannot drain away. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps extra water drain off so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ efo kɛya. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting shoots inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally start growing shoots when they sense heat and humidity in the air, signaling to the tuber that it is time to grow a new vine. Keeping your yam barn cool, dark, and well-ventilated slows down sprouting.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baaje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i lɛ mli pɛ. Enɛ haa bulb lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu wain tsei heei. Kɛ́ oha o-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔ, efee duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bote mli lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ fioo.

english: Why should I wait for rain before puting fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ nugbɔ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Chemical fertilizer needs water from rain or moist soil to dissolve so crop roots can drink it in. Putting fertilizer on dry soil under bright sun will waste your money because the heat can burn the plants or cause the fertilizer to vanish into the air.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia nu ni jɛɔ nugbɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli koni etsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi lɛ ji shika fitemɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ laaje.

english: Groundnut plants pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally feeds the soil. When planted alongside maize, groundnuts shade the ground to keep moisture in while feeding the maize crop.
ga: Peanut tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli, he ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa Peanuts lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ haa lɛ.

english: What are these small caterpillars eating deep inside the leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ ni yeɔ yɛ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which love to hide and feed inside the central funnel of young corn plants. Catching them early and applying recommended natural sprays like neem extract directly into the central funnel helps protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛye nii yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa, tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ tsu nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛya ŋwɛi gbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Curling and twisted pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves. Spraying early with mild insecticidal soap or neem oil keeps these pests away and keeps the foliage flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ baashwie nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and keep the soil moist while cocoa trees mature during their first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Planting seeds too close forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to thin, weak stalks and small or empty corn cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How do I know if my soil is soft enough to plant cassava stems?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ bɔdɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akwɛ ŋmei tsei?

english: Cassava roots need loose, well-drained soil to expand properly. If you can easily push a pointed wooden stick about a foot deep into the ground after rain, the soil is soft enough.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji obaanyɛ otsi tso ni mli wa Aaafee ninetalɔi 1 kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee bɔdɔɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam leaves curl up and droop in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl in intense heat to close their pores and trap moisture inside so the plant doesn't dry out. If the leaves uncurl and look fresh again by evening, the plant is managing the heat naturally.
ga: Ha oyitsɔi lɛ abɔle ehe kɛ la ni naa wa koni eŋa ŋmeii lɛ ni emɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Koni tso lɛ akagbi Kɛji baai lɛ ebɔko ni efee ehee ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ. Tsei lɛ baakwɛ dɔlɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my sweet potato vines producing huge leaves but tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When sweet potatoes get too much nitrogen in the soil, they direct all their energy into growing leafy green vines above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛji sweet potatoes ná nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdu wain tsei eŋɔli ni baai yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Early morning is best because plants drink the water before the heat sets in, and excess water on the leaves dries quickly in the morning sun, preventing mold and fungal growth.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei nuɔ nu dani hulutsoo be lɛ jeɔ shishi, ni nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baagbi oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ leebi lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off unpollinated when the weather gets too hot, when watering is uneven, or when there are no bees around to shake the pollen inside the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni pollination bɛ mli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly during rainy, humid weather, especially in shady farms with poor airflow between trees.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods lɛ kɛ black pods baa, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants have sticky white webs and spots under them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ tsɔji yɛŋ ni shwieɔ shi kɛ tsɔji ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: Sticky white spots are caused by small insects called mealybugs or green mites that suck the sap from cassava leaves, causing the leaves to dry up and stunted plant growth.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii bibii kɛbaa lɛ Atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs loo green mites ni nuɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmei baa mli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbiɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: How many weeks after the first fertilizer application should I apply Urea to my rice crop?
ga: Otsii enyiɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwo mli lɛ sɛɛ esa akɛ mikɛ urea awo mi ŋmɔji lɛ amli?

english: You should apply Urea fertilizer about three to four weeks after the first application. This timing gives the rice plants the right nitrogen boost just when they need it to grow strong stems and leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ urea awo mli aaafee otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ni okɛwo mli lɛ sɛɛ. Be nɛɛ baaye abua ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ aná nitrogen ni sa yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ lɛ koni amɛha ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put Urea fertilizer too close to the base of my rice plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ urea fataa he ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi tsɔ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the plant stem can scorch or burn the tender stems and roots. Spreading it slightly away from the plant allows the roots to absorb the nutrients safely without damaging the crop.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã loo eshã tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ agbɛ ashwã fioo kɛjɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What does Urea fertilizer actually do to help my rice crops grow?
ga: Mɛni urea baanyɛ afee ni eye ebua mi ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Urea is rich in nitrogen, which acts as fuel for crop growth. It helps rice plants grow greener, stronger, and produce more grains, leading to a plentiful harvest.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo yɛ urea mli, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ tsofa ni haa tsei daa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni amɛdaraa, amɛhe wa ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ babaoo.

english: How should I physically spread Urea on my rice field so it works best?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafɔse urea yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ koni nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba?

english: You should broadcast or scatter the Urea evenly across the field between the plant rows, making sure not to drop thick piles directly on the plant stems.
ga: Esa akɛ ogbɛ urea lɛ oshwã loo oja mli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ Kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okaha ŋmei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ akagbee tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Should I remove weeds from my field before I apply Urea fertilizer to my rice?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔji amli dani mikɛ urea awo ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you must clear all weeds first. If you apply Urea while weeds are still present, the weeds will steal the expensive fertilizer away from your rice plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni ojie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ okɛ urea tsu nii be mli ni jwɛi yɛ lolo lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaju ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛjɛ o-rice tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important to go back and double-check my rice field after I finish weeding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ayasara ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ beni ajie jwɛi lɛ?

english: It is easy to miss hidden or small weeds during the first pass. Checking again ensures no weeds are left behind to multiply and steal nutrients from your growing rice.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ oookpa jwɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo bibii yɛ shishijee mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ mli shii enyɔ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ko kwraa eshwɛɛɛ ni ebaashwere ni eju niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ o-rice ni okwɛɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do weeds inside my rice farm affect my final harvest?
ga: Te ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli jwɛi lɛ saa mi naagbee ŋmaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your rice for water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Clearing them completely allows the rice plants to access all available nutrients, resulting in a much bigger yield.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ o-rice lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni yaa hiɛ.

english: What farm practices help ensure that my rice field gives me a high yield?
ga: Mɛɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi yeɔ ebuaa koni yibii babaoo aba mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli?

english: Keeping the field clean of weeds, applying Urea fertilizer at the correct time (about 3-4 weeks after the first treatment), and spreading it carefully will help your rice grow thick and yield abundantly.
ga: Ha ŋmɔji lɛ amli atse kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe. Kɛ́ okɛ urea wo ohe yɛ be ni sa mli (aaafee otsii 3-4 yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ tsofafeemɔ lɛ sɛɛ) ni okɛgbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-rice lɛ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: How do I know if my rice field is growing properly after applying fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A healthy rice crop will grow vigorously, turn a deep green color, and produce abundant grains after proper weeding and timely fertilizer application.
ga: Omɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ daa waa. Eji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa. ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ jwɛi ni ajie amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can I harvest my rice as soon as the grain heads appear?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmãa kɛji ŋmãa lɛ je kpo pɛ?

english: No, rice needs time after flowering and grain development to mature fully. Caring for the crop through proper nutrient timing ensures the rice grains become heavy and ready for a plentiful harvest.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa heɔ be yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmaa lɛ shweremɔ sɛɛ dani ekwɛɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ niyenii ni sa ha onibii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmaa lɛ afee nɔ ni tsii ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide essential shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa plants mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to leave space between my pepper plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ gbɛ yɛ pepper tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing prevents plants from competing for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also allows air to circulate between the plants, which reduces the risk of fungal diseases.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Eha kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ tsei ateŋ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yam tubers when I plant on the same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ sweet potato ŋmeii bibii beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Crops remove specific nutrients from the dirt as they grow. Planting the same crop on the same piece of land repeatedly exhausts those specific nutrients, leading to weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa hu baa shi.

english: How does adding dried animal manure help my crops grow better than plain dirt?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts as food for both the plants and the soil. It releases essential nutrients like nitrogen slowly over time and helps the soil hold onto water during dry periods.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ. Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, inconsistent watering, or lack of pollination. When the plant is stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be ni sa mli loo pollination ni bɛ Kɛji tsei lɛ miihao Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ ni ekɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess water fills all the small spaces in the soil, drowning the roots and allowing rot-causing fungi to multiply quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ he bibioo fɛɛ he bibioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ feɔ babaoo oya.

english: Why do my cowpea plants yield better during the light rain season than during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas prefer moderate water and lots of sunshine. Heavy rains wash away their flowers, promote leaf diseases, and rot the pods before they can mature.
ga: Cowpeas sumɔɔ nu ni mli tse kɛ hulu la babaoo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ baa helai baa ni ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: How do simple weeds hurt my crops if they are just plants growing in the field?
ga: Te jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your main crop needs to grow big. They can also hide harmful insects and diseases that spread directly to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otso titri lɛ koni etsɔ agbo lɛ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hu ato.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and why is it dangerous for my harvest?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ anɔ Ni mɛni hewɔ eyeɔ mikpamɔ lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Small holes are usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the leaves. If they destroy the growing central leaves, the maize plant cannot make energy to produce ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baai lɛ kɛji amɛfite baai ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa. Abɛi nyɛŋ ajie hewalɛ ni baaha afee toi lɛ kpo.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of planting maize seeds saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local diseases, handle heat better, and produce uniform, high yields. Saved seeds lose these strong traits over time, resulting in weaker crops.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ dɔlɛ ni ehaa yibii babaoo baa be fɛɛ be Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I start growing a mango tree from the seed inside the fruit I just ate?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maje mango tso shishi kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ aduawai ni miye amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: To plant a mango seed, remove the soft fruit pulp, carefully open the hard outer shell to remove the kernel inside, and plant that kernel in a seedling pot or bag with moist, fertile soil.
ga: yɛ mango dumɔwui adumɔ mli Jiemɔ aduawai lɛ loo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Gbelemɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ blɛoo koni ojie dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni odu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ tsɛnsii loo dumɔwui kotokui amli ni shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni mli edɔ yɔɔ nɔ.

english: Why does it take so long for a mango seed to shoot up out of the soil after I plant it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mango dumɔwui jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Mango seeds have a thick protective kernel that needs time and steady moisture to break open, so it takes several weeks to germinate and push its first green stem above the ground.
ga: Mango dumɔwui yɛ ŋmei ni buɔ mɔ he ni heɔ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa dani egbɛɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, eheɔ otsii babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ekɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ tso ni ji eŋɔli lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How long should my young mango plant stay in the nursery before I move it to my main farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mi mango tsei lɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: A mango seedling typically needs about four months in the nursery to grow strong stems and enough healthy leaves before it is ready to be transplanted to your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango dumɔwui lɛ he hiaa aaafee nyɔji ejwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaawo amɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What will happen if I leave my tree seedling in the nursery bag for too long and it grows very big?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi mi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ grow bag lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni amɛdara waa?

english: If a seedling stays in the nursery too long, its roots will become trapped and coiled at the bottom of the bag, making it difficult for the tree to absorb nutrients and grow properly once you plant it in the ground.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ehi ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Eshishifãi lɛ ŋmɛɔ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ kotoku lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tso lɛ akɛ ebaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ kɛji odu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Why do the roots of my seedlings break when I try to dig them up for transplanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fãa kɛ mibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni mafo amɛ koni mikɛwo he kroko lɛ?

english: Young roots grow deep and spread into the soil to hunt for water; when you uproot the plant forcefully, those tender root tips snap off because they are tightly held by the earth.
ga: Shishifãi bibii lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛyatao nu. Kɛ́ okɛ hewalɛ jie tso ko shishifãi lɛ Nakai shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ejaakɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shiŋŋ.

english: What happens to a young crop when its roots break while I am moving it into the ground?
ga: Mɛni baa tsei bibii anɔ kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ fã be mli ni mikɛ amɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Broken roots prevent the seedling from taking up water and food immediately, which causes the plant to go into shock, wilt, and grow slowly until new roots develop.
ga: Shishifãi ni ekumɔ lɛ baatsi dumɔwu lɛ naa koni ekaná nu kɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yaa shoofeemɔ mli, egboɔ ni edaa fiofio. kɛyashi shishifãi heei baaje kpo

english: How can I dig up my young trees to plant them without destroying their roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo tso bibioo ko mli koni madu ni mifiteee shishifãi lɛ?

english: Water the soil well before digging so it softens, and dig a wide circle around the plant stem so you can lift the seedling together with a ball of soil protecting its roots.
ga: Okɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani otsa koni efee blɛoo. ni otsa kooloo ni mli kwɔ obɔle tso lɛ he bɔni afee ni onyɛ owó dumɔwu lɛ nɔ kɛfata shikpɔŋ kuku ko he koni obu eshishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves of my young trees droop and dry up immediately after I plant them in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock, caused by damaged roots that cannot supply enough water to the leaves under the hot sun; providing temporary shade and watering regularly helps them recover.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shishifãi ni efite ni nyɛɛɛ aha baai lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhe awa amɛ.

english: Will the mango tree I grow from a seed give me the exact same sweet fruit as the parent tree I took it from?
ga: Ani mango tso ni mikɛ dumɔwui kwɛɔ lɛ baawo yibii ni ŋɔɔ tamɔ fɔlɔ tso ni mijie kɛjɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Trees grown directly from seed often yield different, smaller, or less sweet fruits than the parent tree; grafting a known sweet branch onto a seedling is the best way to get exact fruit quality.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ woɔ yibii ni yɔɔ srɔto, bibioo, loo ni ŋɔɔ fioo fe fɔlɔ tso lɛ. Ni akɛ tsei ni ale ni ŋɔɔ lɛ baawo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How large will a full-grown mango tree get once it matures in my field?
ga: Te mango tso ni eda lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ kɛ́ eda yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A mature mango tree grows into a very large tree with a wide leafy crown and deep roots, requiring plenty of space—usually 10 meters away from other trees—so it does not block light or crowd other crops.
ga: Mango tso ni eda lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ tso agbo waa. Eyɛ baai ayitsei ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. He ko babaoo he miihia lɛ—bei pii lɛ, ekɛ tsei krokomɛi teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 10—no hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ hulutsoo loo etsĩii ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi anaa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen or the soil is too waterlogged. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving soil drainage helps the leaves regain their green color so the plant can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea tsu nii, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee eŋɔli koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before they can grow into full fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, or when the soil gets too dry or lacks essential nutrients like calcium. Providing shade during intense heat and keeping the soil damp helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium bɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha fɔfɔi lɛ hulutsoo be mli ni edɔ waa, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies that transmit viruses. Spraying neem oil or suitable insecticides controls these pests and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ ŋmeii tamɔ thrips, thrips, loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ baakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaatsi baai heei ni baa lɛ anaa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, preventing leaf rot and increasing tuber size.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni eha niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni ehaa yitso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground if I don't harvest them on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mikpaaa amɛ yɛ be naa lɛ?

english: Mature cassava tubers stop growing actively and become very starch-heavy. Heavy rains or waterlogging encourage soil fungi to attack these mature roots, causing them to decay if left too long in wet soil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni starch babaoo yɔɔ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa shishifãi ni eda lɛ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their tiny young pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo dani edaraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed excess young pods—a condition called cherelle wilt—when the tree does not have enough water, shade, or nutrients to support all the pods at the same time.
ga: Cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Beni tso ko bɛ nu, hulutsoo, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua eshishifãi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves dry up and burn when I place dry fertilizer right at the base of the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated salts that draw water directly out of plant stems and roots when placed in direct contact, causing the plant tissue to burn. Fertilizer should always be applied a few inches away from the stem in moist soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, egbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ shãa. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi.

english: Why does my land yield less maize every year when I plant it on the same plot without rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi lɛ? Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni akpaaa?

english: Maize draws heavy amounts of specific nutrients like nitrogen from the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly on the same plot empties the soil's nutrient reserves unless you rotate with crops like beans or add manure and fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii tsake loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my crops while they are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and easily lose the fight for survival against weeds, which steal vital soil water, sunlight, and nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures young crops get all the resources needed to establish strong roots.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛyeɔ kunim yɛ ta ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ jwɛi lɛ mli oya. Enɛ fiteɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ naa nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why does weed spray kill the broad-leaved weeds on my farm but leave my maize crop alive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shi ehaa mi-ŋmã lɛ hiɔ shi lɛ?

english: Selective herbicides are chemically formulated to target specific plant leaf structures and root systems—like broadleaf weeds—while leaving grass-family crops like maize unharmed when applied correctly.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa lɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛkwɛ tsei ahe baai kɛ shishifãi, tamɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni eshiɔ jwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I hurry and use a sharp cutlass carelessly when opening my coconuts?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mifee oya ni mikɛ kakla ni naa wa tsu nii? Ani okɛ hiɛdɔɔ gbeleɔ ŋmei ko?

english: Rushing with a sharp tool can easily crack the inner shell incorrectly, causing the sweet coconut water to spill out and spoil the meat, while also risking severe cut injuries to your hands.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ tsu nii oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli agbala yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ oya. Enɛ haa ŋmei nu ni ŋɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ ŋmei lɛ mli nu lɛ. Oshara hu yɛ akɛ nine lɛ baapila waa.

english: How can I separate coconut husks from the shell without damaging the fruit inside?

english: What is the safest way to peel my coconuts without injuring myself on the farm?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni oyeee ohe awui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The safest method is using a mounted coconut husking stake, which allows you to leverage your body weight to remove the husk rather than swinging a sharp blade near your hands.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ji ni akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ owóɔ ogbɔmɔtso lɛ nɔ koni ojie ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsi tsɔne ni mli wa ni bɛŋkɛ onine lɛ

english: Why do I need to scrape off the leftover fiber from my coconuts after removing the heavy husk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijieɔ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii amli beni mijie ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Scraping the leftover fiber leaves the shell smooth and clean, which makes it easier to locate the natural soft spot for quick opening and prevents dirt from accumulating.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔji ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha tsitsi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe atse. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaana adebɔɔ mli hei ni egbɔjɔ kɛha gbelemɔ oya, ni ehaaa muji aba.

english: Is there a specific technique to make mature coconuts split open quickly and neatly?
ga: Ani gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajaa ŋmeii momoi amli oya ni afee lɛ fɛfɛo?

english: Yes, after scraping the bottom clean, striking the coconut firmly along its natural central seam line will cause it to split open neatly into two equal halves without shattering.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni ajie shishigbɛ lɛ he tse sɛɛ lɛ, kɛ́ otswa ŋmei lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ mli teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ, ebaakumɔ ŋmei lɛ mli enyɔ ni yeɔ egbɔ. afee ekome pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akumɔɔɔ

english: Why do some of my coconuts take so much extra force to open compared to others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokooi lɛ ekomɛi biɔ hewalɛ babaoo dani agbele kɛ akɛto ekrokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Coconuts with thick, uncleaned outer fibers absorb the force of your blow; cleaning the fiber off first ensures the full impact hits the hard shell directly so it cracks open easily.
ga: Kokooi, kɛ amɛ kponɔgbɛ tsɔji ni mli tse ni he tseee lɛ baajie oshoofeemɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ atsumɔ tsɔji lɛ ahe klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni tswaa lɛ baatswa tsɔji ni wa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Does cleaning and removing the fiber from my coconuts help me get a better price at the market?
ga: Ani ŋmei mli ŋmeii ni oootsumɔ ni ojie lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni onáa jara kpakpa yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Yes, market buyers pay higher prices for clean, fiber-free coconuts because they look fresh, are easier for consumers to open, and take up less transport space.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni he tse ni fiber bɛ mli lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ babaoo. Ejaakɛ ŋmei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ehee Eyɛ mlɛo kɛha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ akɛ amɛaagbele. ni eheɔ he ko fioo kɛha gbɛfaa

english: Why do my coconuts spoil quickly after I clean them in a rush for buyers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko lɛ fite oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ oyaiyeli tsu he nii miha mɔ ni heɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When you rush, you can cause micro-cracks in the hard shell that let in air and dirt, causing the coconut water inside to ferment and rot the flesh before reaching the buyer.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ oyaiyeli fee oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ amli lɛ mli agbala ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ muji boteɔ mli, ni enɛ haa ŋmeii nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni loo lɛ fiteɔ dani eshɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: Why should I remove all the hairy fiber left on the coconut shell before storing them in my shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie yitsɔi tsɔji ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei lɛ mli dani mikɛto mi ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The loose, hairy fiber traps moisture from the air, creating a humid environment that attracts mold, fungal rot, and tiny insects while in storage.
ga: Yitsɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni gbalaa ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii beni akɛtoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my stored coconuts lose their water even when I haven't cut them open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ nu fiteɔ lɛ? Ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli?

english: Rough handling or forced cutting during harvest creates invisible cracks in the shell where fiber was ripped away, allowing the water inside to slowly evaporate over time.
ga: Nitsumɔ ni mli wa loo ni anyɛɔ afoɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ baa ŋmeii lɛ amli he ni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ lɛ. Ha nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Beni be hoɔ lɛ

english: What is the difference between buying certified seeds and using saved seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ teŋ?

english: Certified seeds are specially tested and treated to ensure high germination rates, strong disease resistance, and uniform crop growth, whereas saved seeds often lose vigor and can carry hidden diseases into the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ ni atsuɔ he nii koni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ hela ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ tsei ni yaa hiɛ daa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ aya be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my vegetable seeds fail to sprout even after I plant them in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds can fail to germinate if the soil is waterlogged and lacks oxygen, if they are buried too deep for sunlight to signal growth, or if the seeds were already old and damaged before planting.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, hulu la lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ eda. aloo kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ ni efite dani adu

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and turn yellow when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that burn easily under full sunlight; they require shade plants like plantains to create a cooler, moist environment while they establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛfee shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛtoɔ amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, inconsistent watering, or a lack of essential nutrients like phosphorus in the soil during the flowering stage.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔi be mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn stalks are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency, meaning the plant is pulling nutrients from its older leaves to feed new growth because the soil lacks enough fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miigbala niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛmiijɛ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I tell if my crop's leaves are damaged by insect pests or infected by a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai efite mitso lɛ baai lɛ loo tso hela ko emɔ amɛ?

english: Insect damage typically leaves visible holes, chewed leaf edges, or visible bugs, whereas plant diseases usually cause discolored spots, wilting, powdery coatings, or rotting without clear bite marks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa buji ni anaa lɛ shwieɔ shi. chewed leaf edges loo visible insects Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsakeɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ he lɛ baa.

english: If I plant my cassava stems closer together, will I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which usually results in many small, poor-quality tubers instead of a high yield of large ones.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa yitsei bibii babaoo ni ehiii kwraa baa. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso agbo nɛ e woɔ yiblii fuu.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from around my crops while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni madu miŋmɔshi nii lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will quickly steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your plants, permanently stunting their development if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛha otsei lɛ. Enɛ baatsi dalɛ naa kwraa kɛji ajieee lɛ mra.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing and restoring the ground after heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akuɔ sɛɛ akɛbaa yɛ niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack from the expanding roots underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi ni mli elɛɛ yɛ eshishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open field without tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh direct sunlight because sunlight burns their tender leaves and quickly dries out soil moisture. Plantain trees or shade trees act as living umbrellas, keeping young cocoa cool and moist during its early growth.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Enɛ ji akɛ, hulu la lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya. Plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔ ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ.

english: Why should I space my maize seeds carefully instead of planting many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ama shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, du dumɔwuhi fuu nɛ a bɛŋkɛ a he ngɛ bu kake mi.

english: Planting seeds too close together causes the maize plants to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow thick stalks and produce larger, healthier cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes my cassava leaves to curl up with yellow patches, and how can I stop it from spreading?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ mli ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã?

english: Leaf curling with yellow patches is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried and spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and uprooting infected plants early stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmɔŋ baa. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does adding well-rotted chicken manure make my vegetables grow greener and faster than planting in plain dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo fata he lɛ, ehaa mi-aduawai lɛ shwereɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛkwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chicken manure contains essential plant nutrients, especially nitrogen, which helps leaves grow big and dark green. It also improves the soil's structure so it can hold onto water and feed the plants continuously.
ga: Niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei yɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii hu yaa hiɛ koni enyɛ ehiɛ nu mli ni eye ebua tsei daa.

english: How does the dry Harmattan season harm my crops, and what simple thing can I do to protect them?
ga: Te Harmattan Be ni Egbiɔ lɛ Yeɔ Miŋmɔshi Nibii Awui ehaa Te? Ni mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ ahe

english: The dry Harmattan winds suck moisture out of plant leaves and soil very quickly. Spreading dried grass or leaves on top of the soil around your crops (mulching) acts as a blanket that traps moisture and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ oya. Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni okɛaawo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle onibii ahe lɛ nɔ (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ mɔɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts growing under the soil are fully mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves turn yellow and begin to drop. You can pull up one plant to check; if the inside of the pods has dark brown markings and the seeds fill the shell completely, it is time to harvest.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ ogbala tso kome kɛya ŋwɛi koni okwɛ mli. Kɛji pod lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ eyi lɛ, be eshɛɛ ni abaakpa.

english: Is it helpful for my soil if I plant cowpeas or beans in the same field where I grow my maize?
ga: Ani ebaaye ebua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, leguminous plants like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil. This feeds the neighboring maize plants and leaves the soil richer for the next season.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers start to rot underground when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Too much water fills up all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and allowing rot-causing fungi to thrive. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ daa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any tomatoes actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to extreme heat, inconsistent watering, or pest attacks, which stress the plant and prevent pollination. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during extremely hot days helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the first rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and can sleep in the soil for months waiting for water. When rain falls, weeds germinate instantly and steal soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops, which is why clearing weeds early gives your crops a fair chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmɛ nu nyɔji babaoo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli oya fe tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Cocoa trees need deep, fertile soil that drains water well and receives steady rainfall. If your soil is sandy, shallow, or stays flooded after heavy rains, cocoa will struggle to grow and produce fruit.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni nu baanyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋã, ekɔɔɔ, loo nu eyi mli obɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Cocoa dumɔ wa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Can I plant food crops like plantains and cassava alongside my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains kɛ cassava yɛ kookoo tsei ahe?

english: Yes, planting crops like plantains is recommended because their big leaves shade young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight, while also giving you food and income before the cocoa matures.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ adu tsei tamɔ plantains ejaakɛ amɛbaai wuji lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, amɛhaa niyenii kɛ shika dani kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why am I spending so much money on my farm but getting very little financial return?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifiteɔ shika babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shi shika fioo pɛ minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Low returns usually happen when money is spent on inputs like fertilizer or spray at the wrong time, or when old trees produce low yields; applying inputs at the right time and replacing unprofitable trees helps lower costs and boost earnings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sɛɛnamɔi ni baa shi baa kɛji akɛ afite shika yɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be ni esaaa mli. aloo be mli ni tsei momoi woɔ yibii fioo Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ tsei ni sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he lɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔ baaha shika ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ aba shi ni eha shika ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees taking so long to start producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties can take 3 to 5 years to bear fruit, while improved hybrid varieties start producing in about 2 to 3 years. Lack of shade, poor weed control, or nutrient-poor soil can also delay production.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi amli kookoo henɔi lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwo yibii. Yɛ be mli ni hybrid cocoa henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje nitsumɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli lɛ, hulutsoo ni bɛ, jwɛi ni akudɔɔɔ jogbaŋŋ Loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli nibii bɛ mli lɛ hu baanyɛ aha nitsumɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: When is the right time to uproot old crop trees and start over?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie tsei momoi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aje ehee shishi?

english: When trees reach 25 to 30 years old, or if they suffer from incurable diseases like Swollen Shoot, their pod yield drops permanently. Uprooting and replanting with fresh hybrid seedlings is the best way to make the land profitable again.
ga: Kɛ tsei ye afii 25 kɛyashi 30, loo hela ko ni anyɛɛɛ atsa tamɔ ŋmeii ni efu lɛ ye amɛ lɛ, amɛ ŋmeii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa. Dumɔwui heei ni akɛ tsofa kroko ebɔ he lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us not to cut down all the big trees when clearing land for cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkafo tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛ́ wɔmiijie shikpɔŋ ni wɔkɛbaadu kookoo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow under larger forest trees. Keeping selective shade trees shields cocoa from intense sun heat, preserves soil moisture during the dry season, and prevents leaf burning.
ga: Cocoa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ashishi. Tsei pɔtɛɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni ebu kookoo he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni otsi baai ni shãa lɛ naa

english: Why do I need to cut off healthy branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can circulate freely. This reduces moisture that causes black pod disease and encourages the tree to focus its energy on growing cocoa pods rather than extra leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ ama cocoa pods ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe baai ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani akpaa?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in wet, humid weather. Regularly clearing weeds, pruning branches, and spraying approved fungicides keep humidity down and protect the pods.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. weeding tree pruning Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi ni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ efo mli?

english: If your crop leaves start turning yellow, trees look stunted, or flower production drops significantly, the soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen and potassium and needs organic matter or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ. loo fɔfɔii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe miihia ni amɛná nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest cocoa pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvesting when their skin color fully changes—usually turning bright yellow for green pods, or orange for reddish-purple pods. Harvesting only ripe pods ensures high bean quality and better weight.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhewolo nɔ su etsake kwraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebafeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse. loo akutu kɛha magenta ŋmeii Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsii hu aya hiɛ.

english: How can I keep my harvested vegetables fresh for a few days without a refrigerator?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ ahi shi gbii fioo komɛi ni friji bɛ mli?

english: You can keep harvested vegetables fresh by storing them in a cool, shaded area on damp jute sacks or using a simple charcoal cooling box. Keeping them out of direct sunlight slows down water loss and rot.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha aduawai ni akpa lɛ ahi shi ehee kɛtsɔ amɛ ni oookɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi yɛ jute kotoku ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ cooler adeka ni akɛ ŋmei tsuɔ nii daa lɛ atsu nii. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fiteɔ kɛ fitemɔ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil and soften so quickly after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya kɛji mikpa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and release heat after harvest. If left in direct sunlight or stacked too high in deep baskets, heat builds up rapidly, causing them to bruise, soften, and rot.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kpo beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ loo ato he ko ni nɔ kwɔ tsɔ yɛ tsɛnsi ni mli kwɔ mli lɛ, Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa oya, ni no haa egbɔjɔɔ, efeɔ blɛoo, ni egboɔ.

english: How can I prevent my harvested yams from sprouting and getting soft in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efee blɛoo kɛji akɛ akɛto?

english: Store yams in a well-ventilated traditional yam barn raised off the ground, away from sunlight. Periodically inspect them and gently break off any new sprouts to help the tubers stay firm.
ga: Kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ato blema ŋmɔtɔ shĩa ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. ni awó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni kɛ hulu la teŋ jɛkɛ Kwɛmɔ amɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli kɛ blɛoo. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei heei koni eye ebua ni bulb lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Can I leave my cassava roots unharvested in the soil to keep them fresh longer?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmei shishifãi ni akpaaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Yes, keeping cassava unharvested in the ground keeps it fresh, but leaving it too long past full maturity causes the roots to become hard, woody, and lose their rich starch content.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei to ni akpaaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi kɛ́ ashi lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ, amɛfee tamɔ tsei, ni amɛmli starch babaoo lɛ baaje mli.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my bananas so they don't get soft before reaching the market?
