ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa banana? Koni bananai lɛ akafee blɛoo dani amɛyashɛ jara nɔ?

english: Bananas are ready for harvest when the sharp ridges on the green fruit become rounded and full. Harvesting them while firm and green allows them to travel to the market safely before they ripen.
ga: Banana lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso yibii eŋɔli lɛ nɔ lɛ efee kokroo ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ be mli ni amɛji ehee ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfãa gbɛ shweshweeshwe kɛyaa jara nɔ dani amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why do my pawpaws become soft and rot on the tree before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-paw paws lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛshwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: This usually happens due to fruit fly infestation or fungal diseases infecting the fruit early in its development, or from extreme heat and dry spells during the ripening stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ aduawai amli ŋmei loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ aduawai lɛ amli mra be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ hewɔ. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ mli

english: How long does it usually take for harvested green tomatoes to naturally soften and turn red?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani tomato eŋɔli ni akpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa efeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Green tomatoes typically take 7 to 14 days to ripen at cool room temperature, depending on how warm the area is and how close the fruit was to maturity when picked.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato eŋɔli heɔ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 dani eshɛɔ yɛ friji mli. E da bɔ nɛ he nɛ a ngɛ ɔ mi dɔ ha a nɔ. Ni kɛ́ ajie lɛ, te ebɛŋkɛɔ shweremɔ he eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Which crops from my farm are best and safest to process into food for feeding young babies?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni abaanyɛ afee niyenii ni akɛhaa gbekɛbii bibii?

english: Orange-fleshed sweet potatoes, yellow maize, and soybeans are ideal crops because they are rich in essential vitamins, energy, and protein, making them nutritious and soft enough for infant porridge.
ga: Orange loo ni ji sweet potato yellow corn Kɛ soy ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ eyɛ vitamini, hewalɛ kɛ protein ni he hiaa waa. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni eyɛ blɛoo bɔ ni sa kɛha gbekɛbii niyenii.

english: How should I store ground maize flour so it stays good for feeding my family over time?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ ŋmãa ato koni ehe aba sɛɛnamɔ lolo aha miweku lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Make sure the grain is thoroughly dried before milling, then store the flour in airtight containers off the bare floor in a cool, dark room to prevent moisture absorption and mold growth.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ ŋmaa lɛ egbi kwraa dani okɛshwie. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ powda lɛ awo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli ewo duŋ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ akabote mli ni ŋmɔtɔ akatsɔ mli.

english: Does harvesting my maize early affect how long the grain will keep after harvest?
ga: Abele ni akpaa mra Ani enaa be ni esa akɛ akɛto dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, harvesting maize too early when moisture levels are high makes the grain prone to mold, fungal poison, and insect attack during storage unless it is thoroughly dried right away.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akpaa mra tsɔ beni hulutsoo be lɛ fa lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmei, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gbeyei, kɛ kooloi bibii tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Ja egbi kwraa amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting young cocoa trees while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: How can I tell when my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready to pick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods change color as they mature. Pods that start green will turn bright yellow, while pods that start dark red or purple will turn orange-yellow, showing that the seeds inside are fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Pods ni jeɔ shishi kɛ eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Pods ni jeɔ shishi akɛ tsuru loo purple ni mli edɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet conditions and heavy shade. Removing infected pods quickly and trimming tree branches helps air flow through the farm to prevent it from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya kɛ ŋmeii ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why must I ferment my cocoa beans under plantain leaves before drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ plantain baai lɛ ashishi dani mikɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fermentation heats up the beans to stop them from sprouting, removes the sour sticky pulp, and creates the rich chocolate flavor and dark color that cocoa buyers look for.
ga: Fɛ̃i haa dumɔwui lɛ mli dɔɔ koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Jiemɔ loo ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛjɛ ohe. ni ekɛ tsokolate ni mli edɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing out from the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Those extra shoots, called chupons, steal food and water from the main tree. Removing them allows the cocoa tree to send all its energy into growing healthy flowers and pods.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ehaa cacao tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ amli.

english: When is the right time for me to sow my maize seeds during the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli?

english: Maize should be planted right after the first steady rains begin, usually between March and April in southern Ghana, so the young plants get enough water to build strong roots.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ je shishi. Bei pii lɛ, efeɔ yɛ March kɛ April teŋ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi ni wa aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and curling up tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies and spread when infected stems are used for planting. Using disease-resistant stem varieties prevents this problem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Amɛji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii yɛji ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɛji adu ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Fɔlɔ tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to support my growing yam vines with tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato wain tso ni miida lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the ground on tall stakes helps them catch more sun, resulting in bigger yam tubers under the soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei kakadaji wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is weak and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crop leaves turn pale green or yellow, growth stays small and stunted, or your harvest gets smaller every year, your soil is running low on essential nutrients.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ batsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ Dalɛ ji bibioo ni egbɔjɔ. Aloo ani okpamɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi? Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crops more than older trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ awui fe tsei ni edara lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, shallow roots and struggle to compete with fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives young plants the best start.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni mli ekɔɔɔ. ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains spoil so fast when I keep them in ordinary sacks during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto kotokui folo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize grains absorb moisture from humid air during rainy weather, which allows mold and insects to thrive. Storing completely dried grains in airtight, sealed bags keeps moisture and air out, protecting your crop from spoiling.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii shwereɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi kwraa lɛ wo kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ akabote mli. Buu onibii ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly if I leave them lying on the wet ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested yams absorb water from damp ground, making them easy targets for fungal rot. Storing them on raised bamboo racks or in a shaded, well-ventilated yam barn keeps water away and allows them to last much longer.
ga: Atomɔ ni akpa lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni ŋmei kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ ashɛ he oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ amɛ ato ŋmei shĩa ko ni awo nɔ loo yɛ shĩa ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Ebaabu ehe kɛjɛ nu he, ni ebaahi shi be babaoo.

english: Why do heavy rains destroy my tomato seedlings when I plant them directly in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ gbeɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy raindrops break soft stems, wash away root soil, and spread fungal diseases. Protecting young seedlings under a simple palm frond shade shelter or greenhouse net shields them from harsh rainfall until they grow strong.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni egbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai eshwaa. Kɛ́ abu dumɔwui bibii ahe yɛ ŋmei tso loo ŋtayaa ni akɛwoɔ ŋtayaa mli lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: How can I keep my stored vegetable seeds safe from wet weather so they sprout well next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ aduawai dumɔwui ni ato lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Seeds lose their ability to sprout if they touch water or damp air. Dried seeds should be sealed inside airtight containers or glass jars kept in a cool, dark place to keep water out completely.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ amɛbote nu loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ mli. Esa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ awo tsɛnsi loo glase tsinsii ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni duŋ ewo mli koni nu lɛ fɛɛ akaje kpo.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I remove all the shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie kookoo tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight or excessive heat. Tall shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the air cool and preserving soil moisture so the young cocoa plants can survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa loo dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ adara.

english: Why does black pod disease spread so fast on my cocoa farm during cold, rainy months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya yɛ nyɔji ni fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: The fungus that causes black pod disease thrives in high humidity and spreads through rain splashes. Pruning dense branches lets sunlight and air into the farm, helping cocoa pods dry quickly after it rains.
ga: Fuji ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli. Nibii ni afolɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants turn yellow and rot when water sits on my farmland after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu hi he ni miduɔ yɛ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need oxygen to live, and standing water suffocates them while inviting root rot fungi. Planting on raised soil ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away from the stem and roots.
ga: Pepper shishifãi he miihia oxygen koni amɛhi shi. Ni nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni efɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ nine. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu babaoo hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer away before the crop roots have a chance to take it in. Applying fertilizer when the soil is damp—but not during heavy rain—ensures the plant absorbs the nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ—shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ—baaha tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants drop off during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a survival trick to reduce water loss. The plant remains alive underground and will quickly sprout new leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tso lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni ebaakwɛ baai heei oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing fruit during hot, dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil stress tomato plants, causing blossoms to drop to conserve moisture. Covering the soil with dried grass mulch keeps the ground cool and moist, helping plants hold onto flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haoɔ tomato tsei. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe.

english: How do I know if my land's soil is good enough to plant cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ kookoo tsei?

english: Good cocoa soil needs to be deep, rich, and well-draining so water does not sit around the roots. If water gathers and stays in pools after rain, or if the soil is too rocky, cocoa roots will rot or fail to grow properly.
ga: Kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa mli kwɔ, ewoɔ nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Koni nu akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe Kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi nubu lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛi babaoo yɛ Cocoa shishifãi lɛ baagboi loo amɛdaraŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees very close together so I can fit more on my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛhi ŋwɛi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting trees too close creates fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to smaller harvests. Giving each cocoa tree proper spacing allows it to grow full branches and produce many pods.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni haa yibiiwoo baa shi Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha cacao tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ niji ni eyi obɔ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and drying up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under hot, direct sunlight because their roots and leaves are delicate. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a giant umbrella, protecting them until they grow mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ waaa. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa wulu ko ni buɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the healthy branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Pruning removes overgrown and crowded branches so air can blow through and sunlight can reach all parts of the tree. This prevents dampness that causes diseases and directs the tree's energy into producing bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ajieɔ tsei niji ni edara fe nine ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Ni hulu la baanyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ ji koni akɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ hela baa lɛ naa, ni akɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmɔtɔi wuji.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, damp weather. Clearing weeds and trimming lower branches helps sunlight dry out the moisture on the farm, which stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli. Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbiɔ. Enɛ baaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do many of my cocoa flowers drop off the trunk without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but they only turn into pods if tiny insects called midges pollinate them. Leaving leaf litter on the ground provides a moist environment for these good insects to live and pollinate your flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi ebafeɔ pod kɛji kooloi bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Kɛ́ ashi baai amli jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa koni kooloi kpakpai anyɛ ashwere. Enɛɛmɛi baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to grow food crops like plantain and cassava on the same farm as my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ niyenii tamɔ plantains kɛ cassava yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Yes, planting food crops alongside young cocoa provides shade and early food or income while waiting for cocoa to yield. However, keep heavy feeders like cassava a bit away from seedlings so they do not steal all the soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha aná hulutsoo kɛ niyenii loo shika yɛ shishijee mli yɛ be mli ni mɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ awo yibii lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ akɛ niyenii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmei, awo he ko ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo. Bɔni afee ni akaju niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How does the dry Harmattan season affect my young crops, and how can I protect them?
ga: Te Harmattan hɔmɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ ahe?

english: The harsh Harmattan wind dries out the moisture in both the air and soil, causing crops to wilt. Covering the soil around the base of your plants with dry leaves or straw (mulching) helps trap moisture and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbiɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baagbi. Mulching around Kɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) awo tso lɛ shishi koni eye ebua ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni eha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why is it bad if I harvest cocoa pods that are still slightly green or not fully yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikpa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ fioo lolo loo amɛjeee ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Under-ripe cocoa pods do not have fully sweet beans inside, which prevents proper fermentation after harvesting. This results in flat, bitter cocoa beans that buyers will reject or pay less for.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni edako lɛ bɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ ni ŋɔɔ yɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa naa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa anáa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ baakpoo loo amɛbaawo nyɔmɔ fioo.

english: What should I do to keep my soil fertile as I clear more land to make my farm bigger?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni mijieɔ shikpɔŋ babaoo koni miŋmɔ lɛ afee agbo lɛ?

english: As a farm grows larger, soil nutrients get used up much faster by the crops. Adding compost, livestock manure, or the right chemical fertilizers restores essential nutrients into the ground so large harvests can continue year after year.
ga: Beni ŋmɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii lɛ oya kwraa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ falɛ ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni nibii babaoo ni afee lɛ aya nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do my crops need fertilizer even when I plant them in good soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ moŋ?

english: Soil loses its natural nutrients over time as crops grow and absorb them. Fertilizer acts like food for the soil, replacing lost nutrients so your crops can grow big, stay healthy, and produce a higher yield.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛheɔ amɛ lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Niyenii ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔ Koni onibii lɛ adara lɛ ná hewalɛ kpakpa ni owo yibii babaoo

english: Why shouldn't I pour fertilizer directly at the base of my plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the tender bark and roots. It is best to place it a few inches away in a small ring or trench where the spreading roots can safely drink it in.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛwo ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko loo ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko mli. Shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni anuɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow before they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, an important food element in the soil, or that too much water is sitting around the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or clearing excess water helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha sũ lɛ mli su lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after I put fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong wild roots that steal water and fertilizer faster than cultivated crops. You should always clear all weeds from your farm before applying fertilizer so your crops get the food instead.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni onyɛ okɛ niyenii aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ.

english: Why do insects keep destroying my crops even after I spray them with pest killer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛfiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ moŋ?

english: Insects may survive if the chemical was mixed with too much water, if rain washed it away right after spraying, or if you used the wrong chemical for that specific type of insect.
ga: Kplukai baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa babaoo futu nu mli. Nugbɔ shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ ashwie nɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni ejaaa tsu nii kɛha nakai kooloo lɛ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to spray chemicals on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because insects are most active then, there is less wind to blow the spray away, and the hot sun will not evaporate the chemical before it works.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kooloi bibii lɛ tsuɔ nii waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ ni tswaa spray lɛ kɛyaa. Ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haŋ tsofai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ dani amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will using too much pest chemical damage my land and future crops?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, using too many chemicals can burn crop leaves, kill good soil organisms like earthworms, and cause insects to build up resistance, making pests harder to kill in the future.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ baai ashã. Egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii kpakpai, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni ehaa kooloi bibii feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ hela lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ abaagbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ wɔsɛɛ.

english: What is a government fertilizer subsidy, and how does it help a small farmer like me?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔyeli yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛhaa kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi?

english: A subsidy means the government pays part of the total cost of the fertilizer so it can be sold to you at a cheaper price, helping you afford the inputs needed to grow more food.
ga: Yelikɛbuamɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nɔyeli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fã ko koni enyɛ ehɔ̃ɔ eha bo yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ. Enɛ haa onáa nibii ni he hiaa koni onyɛ odu niyenii babaoo.

english: Should I follow crop advice given by local chemical sellers or check with an extension officer first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ŋaawoi ni jɛ tsofa-feemɔ jarayelɔ ni yɔɔ mimaŋ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ loo makwɛ mi-extension agent lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: While chemical sellers know their products, some may try to sell you expensive items you do not need. It is always safest to consult an official Agricultural Extension Officer for neutral, reliable advice.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsofai ahe nitsulɔi lɛ le amɛnibii lɛ po, Shi ekolɛ mɛi komɛi baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ bo nibii ni jara wa ni he ehiaaa bo. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe be fɛɛ be akɛ oooya okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ŋɔɔ koni eha bo ŋaawoo ni tsɔɔɔ mɔ yiŋ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: Why do some farmers in my village receive subsidized farm inputs while others miss out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ nine shɛɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe yelikɛbuamɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi hu shɛɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Input supplies are often limited or delayed due to transportation issues. Registering early with your local district agriculture office or farmer group ensures your name is included on the official distribution lists.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ faaa loo esɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ gbɛfaa he saji ahewɔ. Kɛji okɛ ohe wo kpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe loo okwaafoi akuu lɛ mli dani okɛ ogbɛi awo nibii ni ajaa lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects the delicate leaves from scorching and helps retain soil moisture during their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaabu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom of the stalk usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to grow strong and green, so applying nitrogen fertilizer or compost helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize in the exact same spot on my farm season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same soil drains specific nutrients and allows pests and diseases that feed on maize to build up in the ground, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Cassava roots need well-draining soil to breathe. When heavy rains leave the soil soaked for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, which encourages fungal rots to develop underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yam vines naturally search for sunlight by climbing upwards. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread, allowing the plant to catch maximum sunlight and grow bigger tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei taoɔ hulu la kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛkwɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ egbɛ eshwa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni ehaa bulb lɛ feɔ wuji.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing flowers that just dry up and drop off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ni gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates sharply. Extreme heat prevents successful pollination, causing the plant to shed flowers to conserve its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa tsiɔ pollination naa. Ha tsei afee fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and growing very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips feeding on sap and spreading plant viruses, or by severe heat stress during dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting cowpeas before maize make the maize grow so much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When maize is planted after cowpeas, it uses that stored nitrogen as natural plant food.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen gas mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ tsina ŋmãa sɛɛ Ekɛ nitrogen ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii.

english: Why is it wasteful to spread dry fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji fitemɔ akɛ magbɛ ŋmeii ni egbi ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainwater washes the fertilizer away from the plant's root zone before roots can absorb it. Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil during light rain or normal conditions.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli. loo yɛ shihilɛi ni yaa nɔ daa mli

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Too many young shoots compete with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning them down to just one or two shoots ensures the parent plant can produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ woɔ plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do experienced farmers put plantain suckers on the same field where they plant new cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui woɔ shikpɔji ni amɛduɔ kookoo hee yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas. They protect delicate young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight and conserve soil moisture, while giving the farmer food and quick income before the cocoa starts bearing fruit.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa okwaafoi lɛ niyenii ni ehaa amɛnáa shika oya dani kookoo lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and dry up during the sunny dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow root systems and fragile leaves that cannot handle direct, intense heat. Without temporary shade crops like plantain or shade trees, high temperatures cause the plants to lose water faster than their roots can drink it, leading to wilting.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni waaa ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei lɛ, hulutsoo ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential food it needs to stay healthy and make green chlorophyll. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha hewalɛ kpakpa kɛ klorofil eŋɔli feemɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the blossom flowers on my tomato plants drop off before producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when plants experience extreme heat stress, dry spells, or irregular watering. This environmental stress prevents successful pollination, so the plant drops the flower instead of forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Nɛkɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my crops to stay small even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that aggressively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Even with good rain, the crops cannot get enough food to grow full size because weeds are consuming it first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ oya ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Dumɔwui nyɛŋ ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛkɛ ni amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe. Ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ baaye lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood waterlogged soil, oxygen gets cut off from the roots, allowing fungal rots to thrive and destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Afoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ daa ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer right before a massive rainstorm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ wulu ko baa lɛ?

english: Heavy, pouring rain washes topsoil and fertilizer away into rivers and roadside drains before crop roots can absorb it, wasting your investment and leaving crops hungry.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa faai kɛ gbɛjegbɛi ahe nubui amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Efiteɔ oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii.

english: Why do I get smaller maize harvests every year when I plant on the exact same piece of land without a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaaa ŋmãa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ he kome ni mikpaaa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the topsoil. Rotating with leguminous crops like cowpea or beans helps naturally rebuild soil nutrients for better future yields.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ be fɛɛ be. Legume ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cowpeas loo beans ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ama ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ená yibii kpakpai wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do I see large, ragged holes in the central leaves of my young maize stalks early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji agboi ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes inside the leaves are typical signs of pest attacks, such as Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the funnel of young corn stalks and eat tender leaves during warm weather.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ agbɛi amli ni eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I saved from last year's harvest fail to sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their ability to germinate if stored with high moisture, attacked by hidden weevils, or if they were hybrid seeds whose second-generation offspring do not perform as well as the parent plant.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ tutuaa Aloo kɛji eji dumɔwu ni akɛfee ekome ni yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ seshibii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do some of the cocoa pods on my trees turn black and rot before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ekomɛi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani akpa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp and cool conditions. Removing infected pods early helps prevent the disease from spreading to the healthy pods on your trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela akagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ otso lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes tiny insects to gather on my young cocoa pods and make them dry up?
ga: Nɔ ni haa kooloo bibioo ko bua mi kokoo bibii lɛ anaa ni egbi amɛ.

english: These are usually pests known as mirids or capsids that suck the sap out of young pods and branches. Treating the trees early stops them from killing the pods before they mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids loo capsids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsei niji bibii amli lɛ. Tsei ahe nitsumɔ mra Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛdara kwraa.

english: Is it safe to leave broken cocoa pod husks in piles near my trees after harvest?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mashi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekumɔ lɛ yɛ ŋtayaa ko mli yɛ mitsei lɛ ahe yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: No, leaving rotten husks near living trees creates a breeding ground for fungi and pests that can attack your next crop. It is better to compost them away from the farm or bury them.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa ni egbo ni ajieɔ lɛ Yɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahe lɛ eji he ni ŋmãa kɛ kooloi ni baanyɛ atutua oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ loo ooofu lɛ.

english: Why do I need shade trees planted on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees, especially young ones, get stressed and burned under harsh direct sunlight. Shade trees protect them from intense heat and help keep moisture in the soil during dry weather.
ga: Cocoa tsei, titri lɛ tsei bibii lɛ, haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛshãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why is it important to trim unnecessary branches and shoots from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ kookoo tsei aniji kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni he ehiaaa lɛ?

english: Extra branches and unwanted shoots steal food and water away from the trunk. Trimming them lets air and sunlight reach the tree, which keeps the tree healthy and helps it produce more pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii ni ataooo lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli waa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How do weeds growing around my cocoa trees affect my final harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te mi cacao tsei lɛ saa mi naagbee ŋmaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crop for water, nutrients, and space. Keeping the ground around your trees clear ensures all the soil nutrients go straight into making your cocoa trees strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, niyenii, kɛ he ko. Kɛ́ oha he ni otsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa koni eha o-cacao tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod is ripe enough to pick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie?

english: Unripe pods are usually green or dark red, but mature pods turn bright yellow or orange. Tapping the pod can also tell you if it is ready—ripe pods sound hollow because the seeds have separated from the outer shell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni edako lɛ ji eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ. Shi ŋmeii ni eda lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Kɛ́ otswa pod lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ bo hu kɛji pod lɛ efee klalo. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baatswa tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbala kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning pale yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are often a sign that the tree lacks key soil nutrients like nitrogen. Adding suitable fertilizer gives the tree the strength it needs to make fresh green leaves and support growing pods.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ fɔmɔ nii wo tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ anɔ, ni eye ebua tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage naturally turn into pods. Factors like high heat, lack of water, or bad weather can cause even more flowers to fall before forming fruit.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ baatsɔ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔ pods. Nibii tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli, loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is the tree's natural defence to save water during long dry periods. Covering the soil around the base with dry leaves or mulch helps trap soil moisture and protects the tree roots.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ tsei ahe koni amɛbu nu he yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ shwie shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if a new crop variety brought into Northern Ghana will perform well on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni akɛba Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: New crop varieties released by agricultural extension services are tested across different ecological zones in Ghana. Varieties recommended for the North are specifically bred to tolerate higher heat and shorter rainy seasons, ensuring better yields despite dry conditions.
ga: Aka ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ jie lɛ kpo lɛ akwɛ yɛ eko-zone srɔtoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ amli. Akwɛ tsei srɔtoi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo naa. Koni aná yibii kpakpai yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do some new seed varieties mature so much faster than the traditional seeds my family has saved over the years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni miweku lɛ kɛto daa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are bred to shorten their growth cycle. Early-maturing crops allow you to harvest before dry spells set in and help you escape late-season pest attacks.
ga: Atsakeɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛha be ni amɛdaraa lɛ afee kuku. Nibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa dani hɔmɔ baa, ni ehereɔ bo kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Can I grow the exact same crop varieties in the North that farmers plant in the southern forest regions of Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni okwaafoi duɔ yɛ kooi ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ kooyigbɛ?

english: Not always. Southern Ghana experiences two rainy seasons with higher humidity, while the North has a single rainy season and drier weather. Crops designed for the North need greater drought tolerance than those grown in the forest zones.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Ghana wuoyigbɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei enyɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Yɛ be mli ni kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi fe tsutsu lɛ. Esa akɛ tsei ni afee aha kooyigbɛ kpokpai lɛ anyɛ akpee hɔmɔ naa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ kooi amli lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away. Applying balanced fertilizer or well-decomposed manure will restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop seedlings wilt and die during short dry spells in the middle of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ amli dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow root systems that cannot reach deep soil water. Placing dry grass or mulch around the base of your plants keeps the soil cool and retains moisture during dry stretches.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ nu he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any fruit begins to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Blossom drop happens when temperatures get too high or water supply is irregular. Consistent watering and providing light shade during peak afternoon heat helps plants keep their blossoms and set fruit.
ga: Blossom ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa be ni mli wa lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yibii amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves but small, thin roots when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ́ akpa lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages the plant to put all its energy into growing leaves instead of roots. Using balanced soil nutrients containing phosphorus and potassium helps cassava build larger tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ awo baai ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe shishifãi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does planting cowpea or groundnut in my field make my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpea pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you rotate them with maize, they leave behind natural soil food that boosts your next crop's growth.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ okɛ ŋmãa tsake lɛ Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaha oŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted seeds right after the early rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui ni midu beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds stay alive in dry soil for months and are adapted to germinate immediately with the slightest moisture. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing light, water, and nutrients from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baahi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ nyɔji babaoo. ni atsakeɔ lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together causes plants to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow thick stalks and produce bigger harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Is it bad if my farm soil has a lot of sand mixed inside it?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ŋã babaoo yɛ mli?

english: Not at all. A good balance of fertile soil and sand is actually helpful because sand improves water drainage and air movement, which prevents root rot and allows your crops to grow strong.
ga: Jee nakai kraa. Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ kɛ ŋã ni akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋã haa nu hoɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow better when the soil is light rather than heavy and sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waaa moŋ fe ni eeefee nɔ ni tsii ni wa lɛ?

english: Looser soil containing sand allows plant roots to spread out easily and breathe, helping the crops absorb nutrients faster and flourish compared to hard, compacted clay soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ, ni etse ehe lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛmuɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ niyenii kpakpai oya ni amɛshwereɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni mli edɔ he.

english: Can mixing sand into heavy clay soil help my plants grow better?
ga: Ani ŋã ni mikɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, loosening heavy soil with sand improves its drainage and texture, making it easier for plant roots to extend deeper and access the water and nutrients they need to grow well.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni akɛ ŋã gbalaa mli lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How long does it usually take for newly planted crops to mature and flourish on a new farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ dani tsei ni adu ehee lɛ daa ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Depending on the crop and soil quality, it typically takes between one to two years—often around 15 to 18 months—for long-term crops to fully establish themselves and produce a good yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee afi kome kɛyashi afii enyɔ. (bei pii lɛ nyɔji 15 kɛyashi 18) koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ adara ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai. Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hi ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my young plants taking more than a year to show strong growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ heɔ nɔ ni fe afi dani ejieɔ dalɛ ni mli wa kpo lɛ?

english: Many crops spend their first year building a strong root system underground. Once the roots are settled in good soil, you will see the plant flourish heavily in its second year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ babaoo kɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ toɔ shishifãi ni mli wa shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ adu shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ Obaana tsei lɛ adaa waa yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: If I plant my farm today, when should I start expecting to see green, healthy foliage and broad growth?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmɔ ŋmɛnɛ Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mabɔi gbɛkpamɔ akɛ mana baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ dalɛ ni mli kwɔ?

english: On well-drained, fertile land, you can expect crops to start visibly flourishing and producing full foliage between 12 to 17 months after planting.
ga: Yɛ hei ni nu hoɔ yɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ lɛ anɔ. Obaanyɛ okpa gbɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabɔi shweremɔ ni kadiɔ mɔ ni ebaawo tsei ahe tsei babaoo yɛ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 17 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What main signs show that my crops have settled well into the soil after one year?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii titrii ni tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi kome sɛɛ?

english: After about a year to 15 months, settled crops will display vigorous green growth, strong main stems, and rapid leaf production, showing that their roots have adapted to the soil.
ga: Yɛ aaafee afi kɛyashi nyɔji 15 sɛɛ lɛ, tsei ni ehi shi lɛ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kpo. strong main trunk kɛ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ oya Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ etsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my new land is suitable for growing crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Good crop soil is rich in nutrients but also has enough sandy texture so it stays moist without holding too much excess water, giving plants the right conditions to thrive over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ tsei lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Shi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehiɔ shi ni nu babaoo ehiɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa shihilɛ ni sa koni amɛdara yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does rainwater standing on my farmland slow down the growth of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu ni damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil starves roots of oxygen, causing crop growth to stall. Having soil with sufficient sand content allows excess water to drain away so plants can grow without interruption.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ kpa dalɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ tsei baanyɛ adara ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ.

english: Does the condition of my soil affect how many years my crop will take to produce a harvest?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ saa afii enyiɛ ni eheɔ dani akpaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he?

english: Yes, poor or heavy waterlogged soil delays crop development, whereas rich, well-drained soil with good sand content helps plants reach full maturity and production within 1 to 2 years.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni ehiii loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aya hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ŋã kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ ashɛ shweremɔ ni yeɔ emuu ni ewo yibii yɛ afii 1 kɛyashi 2 mli.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer leaves and husks turn dry and brown, the silks turn black, and the kernels become hard enough that your fingernail cannot easily dent them.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ kɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Siliki lɛ tsɔɔ ediŋŋ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaŋ otsitsii lɛ atsɔ mlɛo.

english: Why is it bad to leave mature crops in the field for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Leaving ripe crops in the field exposes them to heavy rain, pests, birds, and mold, which lowers the quality of the produce and reduces the amount you can sell.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaagbala nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, okpoi kɛ ŋmeii, ni no baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaaha nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ hu aba shi.

english: Why does removing weeds early in the season help my crops yield more?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and plant food in the soil. Clearing them early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops as soon as the main rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Planting early gives seeds the steady moisture they need to germinate and build strong root systems before any unpredictable dry spells occur later in the season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni he hiaa amɛ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa. Dani hɔmɔ be ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baaba sɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is short on soil nutrients like nitrogen, suffering from drought, or infected by diseases like cassava mosaic virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni hɔmɔ miipiŋ lɛ. loo hela ko tamɔ cassava mosaic hela lɛ emɔ lɛ

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when stressed by extreme weather heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients, saving energy instead of producing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi moŋ ni ekɛ yibii baa.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in cool, wet weather and destroys the cocoa beans if infected pods are not removed promptly.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ mli. ni efiteɔ kookoo ŋmeii kɛji ajieee ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow much better when I mix animal manure into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure, helps the ground retain water during dry days, and slowly releases vital food that crops need for healthy growth.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpo fiofio.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and crooked in hard soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow by pushing expanding roots into the ground. If the soil is hard or compacted, the tuber cannot expand freely, resulting in small and misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi ni mli lɛɛɔ lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ Yitso lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã ehe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni efite.

english: Why should I avoid planting the same crop on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases that attack that specific plant to build up in the soil.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa nakai tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava plants naturally shed their leaves during dry periods like the harmattan to conserve water and protect their roots underground. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh new leaves and resume growing.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli, tamɔ Harmattan, koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flower stems down into the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miitsi efɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei lɛ kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts have a unique way of growing where the plant blooms above ground, but once pollinated, the stems bend down and push into the soil so the nuts can safely grow underground.
ga: Peanuts yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ. he ni tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shi kɛ́ ashɛre pollin lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it better for me to water my crops early in the morning rather than in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ nu leebi moŋ fe shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the roots to absorb moisture before the midday heat causes water to evaporate. It also prevents wet leaves from burning in strong sunlight or developing fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa amɛshwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ baai ni efɔ lɛ hu naa koni ekashã kɛji hulu la ni naa wa loo ŋmeii helai shɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, rotten patches on the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli edɔ ni egbo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Dark rotten spots at the bottom of tomatoes are called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often caused by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady prevents this problem.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ?

english: Yellow and curled maize leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, pest attacks like armyworms, or water stress. Adding organic compost or appropriate fertilizer early can help the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms loo nu mli haomɔ Organic compost loo fertilizer ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli mra lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms before forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani efee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat, insufficient water, or poor soil nutrients. Supplying steady water and using grass mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni naa wa mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my young crops regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ ji daa?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your young crops and can hide harmful insects. Clearing weeds gives your crops the space and food they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii bibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ oshara ato. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to plant vegetables like garden eggs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ aduawai, tamɔ ŋmeii, yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy soil feels rich, dark, and crumbles easily in your hand without forming a hard brick. It should absorb water easily without leaving long-lasting puddles on the surface.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ nii, eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni efiteɔ yɛ nine mli ni ekɛ brikii ni wa efeee. Esa akɛ eŋɔ nu oya ni eshiŋ nu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Storing damp maize creates mold and attracts grain insects that ruin the crop and produce harmful toxins. Proper drying ensures the grain stays safe to eat and sell for many months.
ga: Abele ni mli efɔ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbalaa ŋmaa mli ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛjieɔ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why should I process my fresh cassava into gari instead of selling it right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee ŋmei hee ni mafee Gari moŋ fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Fresh cassava roots spoil within two to three days after harvest, forcing you to sell quickly at low prices. Processing cassava into gari extends its shelf life for months and allows you to sell it for higher profit.
ga: Cassava shishifãi heei lɛ baafite yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ oya kɛ jara ni baa shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsu nii ni efee gari lɛ, ehaa ehiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo. ni eye ebua bo ni ohɔ̃ɔ koni ona sɛɛnamɔ babaoo

english: Why do my crops wither so quickly under the sun these days even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔi lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛnɔ moŋ?

english: Rising temperatures cause water to evaporate from plant leaves much faster than roots can draw moisture from the ground. When the sun is extremely hot, the plant loses water faster than it can drink, causing it to wilt to protect itself.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa nu shwieɔ tsei lɛ ahe oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛnu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ gboɔ koni ebu ehe.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn roll up into tight tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism against extreme heat. By curling up, the leaf exposes less surface area to the burning sun, which reduces water loss and helps the plant survive until the air cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ, baai lɛ haaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ashɛ amɛhe fioo. Enɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli woɔ la.

english: Very high temperatures damage the pollen inside the flowers, preventing fertilization. When a plant senses that conditions are too dry and hot to support fruit growth, it drops its flowers to save its strength.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ni etsĩ fɔmɔ naa Kɛ́ tsei nu he akɛ shihilɛi lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua aduawai lɛ adalɛ, Tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ehiɛ ehewalɛ mli.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize now that the rainy season keeps changing?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa? Ejaakɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be?

english: Because rainfall has become unpredictable, planting strictly by traditional calendar months no longer works. It is safer to wait until the soil gets deep moisture from two or three continuous heavy rains before sowing.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ ebafee nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ kusum kalanda nyɔŋ lɛ naa Strictly no hewɔ lɛ etsuuu nii dɔŋŋ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa dani odu nii.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It blocks direct sunlight from hitting the ground, keeping the soil cool and trapping water underneath so your crop roots stay hydrated.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Etsiɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ nu yɛ shishi bɔni afee ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Which food crops can I plant that will still produce food if the dry season lasts longer than usual?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu ni baaha niyenii aba lolo kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Crops with deep root systems or naturally low water needs, such as cassava, cowpea, millet, and sorghum, can endure long periods without rain far better than shallow-rooted crops like maize.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ loo nu ni he ehiaaa tsɔ, tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ ŋmei baanyɛ adamɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Why should I buy fast-maturing seed varieties instead of using the seeds saved from my old harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra yɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mikpamɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Fast-maturing seeds are bred to grow and produce food in a shorter period. This allows you to harvest your crops before a short rainy season suddenly ends or severe dry weather sets in.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo niyenii yɛ be kukuoo mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa onibii lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ baa naagbee trukaa loo nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ baa.

english: How does growing beans together with my maize protect my farm against bad weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe?

english: Beans cover the ground to shade the soil and retain moisture, while also taking nitrogen from the air to naturally feed the soil. Planting both ensures that if weather damages the maize, you still harvest the beans.
ga: Mulch beans koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli baa koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ye ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaahi shi. Obaanyɛ okpa ŋmeii lolo.

english: Why am I seeing strange new insects destroying my crops that I never saw on my farm years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi heei ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni miifite miŋmɔshi nibii ni minako yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Warmer weather and changing rain patterns create new environments that allow strange insects to multiply rapidly and migrate into areas that used to be too cool for them to live in.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni tsakeɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ hee ko baa ni haa kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ ayi faa oya ni amɛfãa kɛyaa hei ni tsutsu lɛ edɔ waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why is my piece of land giving me less food today than it produced ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ haaa mi niyenii fioo fe bɔ ni ewo afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Higher temperatures and heavy unpredictable rains wash away topsoil and break down soil nutrients faster. Farming the same soil continuously under these harsher conditions drains its fertility.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ oya. Kɛ́ aya nɔ atsu shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he nii yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyɔɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Keeping shade trees or planting plantains around them creates a protective cover that traps moisture and shields the seedlings until they grow strong enough to bear direct sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Tsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing much fewer pods now that they are around 20 years old?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo fioo beni eye aaafee afii 20 lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 15 to 20 years, their productivity naturally drops because the wood hardens, roots reach deeper depleted soil, and pest damage accumulates. Older farms need regular pruning, organic soil feeding, or gradual replanting with new high-yielding varieties to restore harvest levels.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tsei lɛ ye fe afii 15 kɛyashi 20 lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni tso lɛ mli waɔ lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. kɛ nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni abua naa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔji ni egbɔ lɛ ahe miihia ni afolɔ amɛ daa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli. aloo fiofio lɛ, okɛ ŋmeii heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ adu ekoŋŋ koni ekɛha ŋmaa lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the new top growth, which can be fixed by applying nitrogen fertilizer or compost around the base.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Tsei yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Abaanyɛ asaa enɛ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields when I plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets specific soil pests multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the ground and breaks the pest cycle naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi komɛi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow faster and choke my crops right after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts as food for all plants in the soil, not just your crops. If weeds are not cleared before or immediately after fertilizing, their fast-growing roots will steal the nutrients intended for your crops.
