ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Jeee oŋmɔshi nibii pɛ. Kɛji ajieee jwɛi lɛ dani awo mli loo beni awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, Amɛshishifãi ni daa oya lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa onibii lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to germinate if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season usually only wet the top surface of hot soil and is often followed by dry days. Planting too early causes seeds to scorch and dry out; waiting for consistent major rains ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ashã ni amɛgbi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ mɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if I do not harvest them before the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: When heavy rains soak the ground for long periods, water fills all the air spaces in the soil. Without air, the cassava roots suffocate and soil fungi quickly invade, causing the roots to rot underwater.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, sũ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ be kplaŋŋ. Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ mli oya. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nu shishi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily once the bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ aniji je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the top layer of soil while carrying heavy weight at the top. Supporting the main stem with a branched wooden pole (prop) prevents wind and heavy fruit weight from uprooting the stem.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ he, ni amɛhe wa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso (tso) ni niji yɔɔ mli lɛ fi tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkajie lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without forming any actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo anɔkwa tomato ko pɛŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when the air gets too hot, when watering is irregular, or when the plant lacks essential minerals like phosphorus. Consistent watering and shielding plants from extreme afternoon heat helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa Aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ minerals ni he hiaa tamɔ phosphorus lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do some of my cut yam pieces rot in the ground before they even shoot out leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mifo lɛ ekomɛi miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ baai po lɛ?

english: Cutting yam tubers creates open wounds that allow rot-causing germs in the soil to enter easily. Coating the cut sides with dry wood ash or fungicide and letting them dry in the shade before planting seals the cut and protects it from rotting.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa pilamɔi ni agbeleɔ naa ni haa helai ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli mlɛo. Okɛ tso sũ ni egbi loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii awo he ni afo lɛ he ni oha egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani odu koni ekɛtsi he ni afo lɛ naa ni ekafite.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen away from the roots, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted manure helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with bushy leaves but yield very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa ni kɛlɛ waa, ni efee ŋmɔji shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots. Using fertilizers rich in potassium helps the plant feed and swell the tubers instead of just growing tall.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni eyeɔ nii ni ekwɛɔ bulbs. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ shɔŋŋ kɛkɛ lɛ

english: How does planting groundnuts on my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni midu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means they have tiny organisms in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into plant food in the soil. When you harvest the groundnuts, that trapped nitrogen stays in the ground to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bɔɔ nii bibii yɔɔ mli. yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli Beni okpaa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big trees from my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to hot, direct sunlight and lose water quickly. Leaving or planting shade trees like plantain or forest trees creates a cool environment that protects the young cocoa leaves from burning until the plant is mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he waa, ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Shikpɔŋhosomɔ tsei tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same water and soil nutrients, resulting in small plantain bunches. Removing extra suckers leaves only two or three strong shoots, giving you much larger bunches at harvest.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ One plantain Plantains baawuu koni ená nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, plantains lɛ baaná ŋmeii bibii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ baashi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛji akpa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce energy for heavy tubers. Keeping the leaves off the hot ground also prevents fungal diseases that happen when wet leaves touch the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha amɛ bulbs ni tsii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa kɛji baai ni efɔ lɛ ta shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ naa.

english: Why should I start my tomato seeds in a nursery bed instead of planting them directly in the big farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ

english: Tomato seeds are very small and produce delicate sprouts that can easily get washed away by rain, eaten by insects, or dried out by the sun. A nursery lets you protect and water the tiny plants carefully until they are strong enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nugbɔ baanyɛ ahoo amɛ oya, koolooi baanyɛ aye amɛ, loo amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. He ni akwɛɔ tsei lɛ yɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe ni ohaa amɛ nu. jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi tso lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my vegetable crops on the farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔ mli aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Early morning is best because the soil can soak up the water before the hot sun turns it to steam. Watering at night keeps the leaves wet for too long in the dark, which attracts mold and leaf diseases.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ atsɔ lasu. Nu ni oooha amɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ duŋ mli. ni gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ foliar helai

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes into the central leaves of my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the growing center of young maize to feed on tender leaves. Checking your farm early and applying localized treatments into the central leaf funnel kills the caterpillars before they destroy the crop's growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni kɛ tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ baagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: Why do my pepper crops get sick with leaf diseases when I plant them on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ yeɔ foliar hela beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ saatso kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Pests and soil diseases that feed specifically on pepper plants stay in the soil after harvest. If you plant pepper in the same place every year, those diseases multiply; rotating with crops like maize or cassava starves out the pepper diseases.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ pepper tsei tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome daa afi Helai nɛɛ baafa babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmãa hela naa

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants turn yellow when they are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni eyɛ kuku waa lolo?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. This often happens when the soil is poor or when heavy rains wash the fertilizer out of the soil before the roots can feed on it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ yeɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with lots of leaves but giving me very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or are planted too close together, they spend all their energy growing stems and leaves instead of roots. Giving them proper spacing and using soil balanced in potassium helps the tubers grow large.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ashishi kɛ baai yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bulb lɛ ni edaraa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without producing any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miijie fɔfɔi ni amɛjieee cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from severe heat, long dry spells, or damage from sap-sucking pests like mirids. Maintaining moderate shade trees in the farm keeps the moisture around the blossoms so they can develop into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa miimɔ amɛ. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen lɛ efite. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be ni sa ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i ni ebɔle he lɛ hiɔ shi. fɔfɔii lɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ

english: How do I know if the very first rainfall of the season is enough for me to sow my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛdu midumɔwui lɛ?

english: One rain shower is usually not enough because the deep soil underneath remains dry. You should dig down into the soil to check that the wetness goes deep—about the length of your hand—otherwise your seeds may germinate and quickly wither when the sun returns.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ faaa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ mli egbi lolo. Esa akɛ otsa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ona bɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli kwɔ ha—aaafee onine lɛ kɛlɛ—aloo odumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni amɛgbo kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why does planting groundnuts alongside my maize make my field produce better crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to a plant family that traps nitrogen gas from the air and converts it into plant food within the soil. This naturally enriches the earth and leaves nutrients behind for crops like maize to feed on.
ga: Peanuts fata tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ he ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eshiɔ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa yeɔ nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ kɔɔpoi bibii amli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies that suck the sap from under the leaves and pass on plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from twisting and stunting the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. No shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli ni ekɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ yaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso lɛ ni amɛkafee nɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes turn dark and rotten before the fruit turns red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishigbɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani aduawai lɛ feɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It typically happens when soil moisture fluctuates wildly between very dry and soaked, which blocks the plant from drawing calcium up from the roots.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ baa be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli egbi waa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ agbala calcium kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: How do I keep insects from destroying my harvested maize while it is kept in the storage room?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa lɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ niitoohe lɛ?

english: Insects thrive on moisture and heat. To protect stored maize, make sure the grains are dried thoroughly until they crack sharply between your teeth, and store them raised off the floor in air-tight bags or cool, well-ventilated granaries.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ hulutsoo kɛ dɔlɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni abu ŋmãa ni ato lɛ he Kwɛmɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛbaagbala yɛ onyanyɔji ateŋ. ni okɛ amɛ awo kotoku loo ŋmɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my seed yams start sprouting in the storage barn long before the planting season reaches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be saŋŋ dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams wake up from dormancy and start sprouting early if the storage barn is warm and humid. Storing seed yams on raised wooden racks in a shaded, cool, and airy place keeps them asleep until you are ready to plant.
ga: Sweet potatoes teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔ mli ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji shĩa lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ to tso ni awo nɔ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwɔ kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaadu amɛ.

english: Why does my harvested grain spoil faster when stored in plastic sacks straight from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto plastic kotokui amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain carries internal moisture and continues to breathe. When locked in plastic sacks without proper drying, heat builds up inside, creating moisture that rots the grain and causes mold to grow quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ gbalaa nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛmuɔ. Kɛji akɛ awo plastic kotoku mli ni egbiko jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Dɔlɛ baabua ehe naa yɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni haa ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ oya.

english: How long does it usually take after planting for leafy crops to grow thick and healthy?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ dani tso lɛ baakwɛ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mli wa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most leafy crops take about one to two months after planting to establish strong roots and grow dense, healthy leaves across your farm plot.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji kome kɛyashi nyɔji enyɔ yɛ amɛdumɔ sɛɛ koni amɛto shishifãi ni wa ni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young crops seem to grow slowly during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ miida blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During the first month, crops focus their energy underground on building strong roots. Once the roots are settled, you will see rapid, lush leaf growth over the next month.
ga: yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli wa Obaana tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ni miida oya yɛ nyɔŋ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Can I put snails directly onto a freshly cleared plot of land without planting crops first?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii awo shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ nɔ ni miduuu tsei klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: No, snails require shade, food, and moisture to survive. You must plant crops first and allow them to grow for one to two months so they create a safe environment before introducing snails.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii, niyenii, kɛ nu he miihia amɛ koni amɛhi shi. Esa akɛ odu tso lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ni oha eda nyɔji kome kɛyashi enyɔ koni ekɛfee shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe dani okɛ ŋmeii lɛ aba.

english: Why must I wait one or two months after planting crops before introducing snails to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nyɔŋ kome loo enyɔ beni midu ŋmɔshi nibii dani mikɛ ŋmeii aba miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waiting one to two months allows the plants to grow tall and bushy enough to provide cool shade and plenty of leaf growth so the snails do not destroy young, fragile seedlings.
ga: Kɛ́ omɛ nyɔji kome kɛyashi enyɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ adara ni efee ŋmɔji bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ kɛ tsei ahe tsei babaoo baaha. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii efiteee dumɔwui bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: What happens to crop plants if I put animals like snails into the field too early?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra tsɔ?

english: If introduced too early, snails will eat and trample the tender young sprouts before they have a chance to establish roots, killing the crops before they can fully grow.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ kpo mra tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii yeɔ ni amɛnyiɛɔ tsei bibii anɔ dani amɛnáa hegbɛ amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni amɛgbeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani amɛdaraa.

english: How do I know that my crop field is ready for me to bring in snails?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ ekɛ ŋmeii baaba?

english: Your field is ready when the crops have grown thick, beautiful, green foliage—usually after one to two months—creating a cool canopy that covers the ground.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ baai ni mli tse, ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji—bei pii lɛ, yɛ nyɔji kome kɛyashi enyɔ sɛɛ—ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do growing leafy crops help keep snails healthy during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ahe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Broad-leafed crops act as natural umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and humid while protecting delicate farm animals like snails from harsh sunshine and drying out.
ga: Broadleaf tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni he yɔɔ oya, tamɔ ŋmeii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ he.

english: What kind of crops should I plant if I want to feed and shelter snails on my plot?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu kɛji miisumɔ ni mahã ŋmeii niyenii ni amɛhi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Fast-growing crops with large, edible leaves—such as cocoyam, plantain, or leafy vegetables—are ideal because they grow well within one to two months and offer both shelter and fresh food.
ga: Tsei ni daa oya ni amɛbaai wuji ni ayeɔ, tamɔ kookoo, plantains, loo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nyɔŋ kome kɛyashi enyɔ mli. ni eyɛ wɔɔhe kɛ niyenii hee fɛɛ

english: Do crops grown in a snail pen only provide shade, or do they serve other purposes?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii atsu mli lɛ haa hulutsoo pɛ loo amɛtsuɔ yiŋtoo kroko he nii?

english: Crops serve a double purpose: their leafy tops shade the ground to hold moisture, and their fresh leaves serve as a natural food source for the snails.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ yiŋtoi enyɔ ahe nii: Amɛbaai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni amɛbaai heei lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmeii.

english: Is it possible for crops and small farm livestock like snails to grow together on the same plot without destroying each other?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ bibioo ko tamɔ Snail mli lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛfiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, as long as you give the crops a head start of one to two months to grow strong, the plants and snails will thrive together in a balanced farm system.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaha nyɔji kome kɛyashi enyɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei kɛ ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli yɛ ŋmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni ja mli.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully ready to harvest so it does not spoil before buyers arrive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he kwraa kɛha kpamɔ? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo dani mɔ ni heɔ lɛ baashɛ?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and the silks at the tip become dark brown. If you press your fingernail into a kernel and it leaves a firm mark without spurting milky liquid, the crop has matured and is dry enough for transport and sale.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni egbi lɛ. ni siliki ni yɔɔ naagbee lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ onineshi tsɔne lɛ mii dumɔwu lɛ mli ni oshi okadi ko ni ojieee nu ni tamɔ mliki lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛya ni ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my harvested green plantains turn yellow and ripen so fast before traders can pick them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain eŋɔli ni mikpa lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ oya dani jarayelɔ lɛ baŋɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally produce a gas called ethylene when harvested, which speeds up ripening. Leaving harvested bunches in direct sunlight or crammed into unventilated bags traps heat and this gas, causing the entire batch to ripen rapidly within a few days.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa plantains lɛ, ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekwɛ̃ oya. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ loo akɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaamɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers instead of producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden hot spells without enough soil moisture, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium. High heat causes the plant to protect itself by shedding flowers it cannot feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ fãa amɛhe kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots, making them sensitive to harsh sunlight and water loss. Without protective shade crops like plantains around them, excessive sunlight burns the leaves and causes the tree to drop them to save moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains bɛ he lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha tso lɛ agbo bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why are my cassava roots remaining small and thin even after being in the soil for many months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo lolo yɛ be mli ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to expand when the soil is too tightly packed or lacks sufficient nutrients like potassium. Hard soil physically stops the tubers from swelling, while overcrowded planting forces stems to compete for light rather than storing food underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa tamɔ potassium bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni wa baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafuu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my yam tubers crack open in the ground before I dig them up for sale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani atsaa koni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers crack when heavy rain follows a dry spell. The sudden intake of water causes the inner flesh of the yam to grow faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to split open.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli. Nu ni anuɔ trukaa lɛ ha sweet potato lɛ mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do my tomatoes get soft and rot so quickly during transport to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya kɛ́ akɛmiiya jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot quickly when harvested fully ripe or packed tightly into rigid wooden crates. The pressure at the bottom squashes the lower fruits, and small skin tears allow bacteria and fungi present in warm air to multiply rapidly.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa loo akɛwo tso adekai amli jogbaŋŋ. Nɔnyɛɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ miimiɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Ni yaafo fioo Enɛ baaha helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Why are my garden egg leaves curling up and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in garden eggs is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies on the undersides of leaves, or by a viral infection they spread. These pests suck the plant's sap, starving the leaves of nutrients needed to stay green and flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amli amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ náaa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow after heavy rains fall on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away mobile nutrients like nitrogen from the root zone down into deeper soil layers. Excessive water also fills up air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots so they cannot absorb water or food properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hu eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu nu loo niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over when the fruit bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots, so when the heavy fruit bunch forms, the weight pulls the plant down. Poor soil structure, nematode pests damaging roots, or strong winds easily uproot top-heavy plantain trees that are not propped up with wooden sticks.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aduawai akuu ko ni tsii ba lɛ, Muji lɛ baagbala tso lɛ kɛba shi. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ehiii Nematode tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. Aloo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie tsei ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni tsei fioo ko pɛ fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishi oya.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight and high heat. Shade trees or plantain plants shield the young cocoa leaves from scorching sun and help keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to endure direct heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei loo plantains ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing of the bottom leaves usually shows that your soil lacks nitrogen. The maize plant moves the remaining nitrogen from its older lower leaves up to feed the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark waste inside the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ jwɛi ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the center leaves of the maize plant during the day, chewing through the leaves and leaving droppings behind.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Okɛ baai lɛ atsu nii ni oshi ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but producing small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? shi eyɛ yitso bibioo Shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava plants focus all their energy on growing tall stems and leaves instead of storing food down in the roots to form thick tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni kwɔlɔ ni miida lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee tso ɔmɛ a mi mi wa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛfeee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to high temperatures, lack of water, or poor pollination. When the plant experiences heat stress, it sheds its blossoms to survive rather than trying to feed growing fruits.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ji hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii. Kɛ tsei kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kpe Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ehi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for developing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them off the damp soil where rot and fungal diseases spread easily.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ akwɛmɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ, he ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ.

english: If I harvest all my crops at the end of the season, how do I select the best seeds to save for next year's planting?
ga: Kɛji mikpa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛto kɛha afi ni baa lɛ dumɔ?

english: Select seeds only from your healthiest, strongest plants that showed no disease symptoms and gave high yields. Clean the seeds carefully and store them in dry, airtight containers with wood ash to protect them from insects.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui pɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni he wa fe fɛɛ ni ejieee hela he okadi ko kpo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli. Tsumɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ. Ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni tso sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli koni kooloi akabote mli.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and weak when I put four or five seeds in one planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole makes the young plants compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Planting fewer seeds with correct spacing allows every plant to get enough food to grow thick, strong stalks.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui fioo ni aduɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni eshishifãi ni mli wa ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly droop and wilt during the afternoon even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil is usually a sign of root rot or bacterial wilt. Microbes in the soil attack the roots, blocking them from drawing up water to the rest of the plant despite the soil being wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji shishifãi ni egbo loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ he okadi. Nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛgbala nu kɛya tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Wild weeds are naturally adapted to quickly absorb the first rain and nutrients from the soil before cultivated crop seeds fully sprout. Early weeding prevents these aggressive plants from stealing food from your young crops.
ga: Kooloi amli jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Dani dumɔwui ni adu lɛ baakwɛ̃ kwraa Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or that the roots are sitting in too much water. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. Aloo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛfeee nakai moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During intense afternoon heat, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. Curling their leaves is the plant's natural way of reducing water loss, and they will bounce back when the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tomato tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa nu ni efiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa sɛɛ kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing yellowish patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck plant juices. Planting healthy stem cuttings from strong plants helps keep your farm free from this sickness.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Whiteflies bibii ni nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni hela nɛɛ akafee oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why do dark black spots appear on my tomato leaves and fruits whenever heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛ aduawai anɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes soil onto leaves and creates wet conditions where fungal sicknesses thrive. The excess moisture allows fungus to grow quickly on the leaves and fruits, causing dark rot spots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa sũ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ aba. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa oya yɛ baai kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ, ni ekɛ ŋmeii diji baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no taller plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigboi yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Taller plants like plantains act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and protecting the soil from losing moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo ni mli tse lɛ hulutsoo. ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as severe heat, dry soil, or lack of plant food. Keeping the soil consistently moist and well-fed gives the plant enough energy to turn flowers into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsei niyenii ni bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni eyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ fɔfɔii ni etsɔ aduawai.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves above ground but very small roots beneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their growth energy into lush leaves instead of growing tubers under the ground. Balancing your fertilizer encourages the plant to store food in the roots.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛhaa lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ etso lɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, Balancing fertilizer yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ niyenii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my crops growing much shorter and weaker this year on the exact same field I used last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida kuku ni amɛgbɔjɔ waa afi nɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mikɛtsu nii nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Crops pull food out of the soil every season. Growing the same crop on the same land continuously drains the soil's strength, so changing crops or planting legumes like cowpeas helps rebuild soil nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aba shi be fɛɛ be. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ loo aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to look thin and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal water, light, and soil food away from your crops. When weeds grow close to your crops, your plants go hungry and cannot grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye otso lɛ ni enyɛŋ eda waa.

english: Why do tiny insects start attacking my cowpea pods as soon as they form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ mi-cowpea pods lɛ tutuamɔ shishi kɛji amɛfee pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Growing cowpea pods produce sweet juices that attract pests like pod borers looking for food. Checking your field frequently allows you to catch and control these pests before they damage your harvest.
ga: Cowpea pods ni aduɔ lɛ haa nectar ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ pod borers ni taoɔ niyenii lɛ baa. He ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ shii abɔ Ehaa onyɛɔ omɔɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni oyeɔ nɔ dani amɛfiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too full of water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea when the soil is damp will help the leaves turn green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farm yield fewer crops every year even though I clear and burn the weeds every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi ni mishãa lɛ daa afi moŋ.

english: Burning cleared weeds destroys organic matter and beneficial micro-organisms in the soil. Over time, crops remove nutrients without replacement, so you need to practice crop rotation or add compost and fertilizer to restore soil life.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛtooo najiaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsake loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a field without any high trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct heat and heavy sunshine. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain or cassava beside them creates shade that protects the young cocoa leaves while they establish deep roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Is it really necessary to support my yam vines with tall sticks, or can I let them spread on the ground?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni akɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ afi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ? Aloo obaanyɛ oha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and keeps them away from damp ground diseases. This extra sunlight enables the plant to make more food and produce much larger yam tubers.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛtsi helai anaa yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ hulu la ni fa nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo ni amɛwoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara kwraa.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, dark conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let sunlight and air reach the pods helps prevent the dampness that causes the rot.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji krokomɛi amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ akahã ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: What is eating small holes inside the growing center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ adalɛ he lɛ mli?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant to feed on tender leaves. Spraying an approved pesticide directly into the central leaf funnel early in the morning or late evening targets them effectively.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatswa lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling up and turning small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves. Spraying a light soapy water mixture or suitable insecticide gets rid of the insects so clean leaves can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu fioo ni akɛ samla loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ koni baai ni he tse lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before setting any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and spreading dry leaves around the base as mulch keeps the roots cool and preserves fruit buds.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: How do I know which plantain shoots to cut away and which ones to leave growing around the main stem?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male plantain tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni esa akɛ mafo kɛ nɔ ni esa akɛ maha amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he?

english: Leave only one strong sucker with narrow, sword-like leaves to replace the parent plant after harvest, and cut away the rest with wide leaves. This prevents multiple stems from fighting over soil food and water.
ga: Tso lɛ tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ klante ji nɔ ni eshwɛ ni baaye tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ najiaŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. ni okɛ baa ni mli kwɔ afo nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni tsei babaoo akawuu yɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up without harvesting too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo ni mikɛkpaaa mra tsɔ?

english: Most local cassava varieties are ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, along with cracks forming in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ babaoo efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ŋmeii ni baa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains around young cocoa protects them from scorched leaves and keeps moisture in the soil so the roots can survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo plantains ni adu yɛ Young cocoa he lɛ buɔ cacao tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ baai ni shãa lɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves near the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green and build strong leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground when left in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water during heavy rains fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the cassava roots and allowing water-loving fungal diseases to enter and rot the tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ abote mli ni ekɛ tuber rot aba.

english: How does planting cover crops like leguminous plants help my farm if I cannot eat or sell them?
ga: Te cover crops tamɔ legumes ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛji minyɛɛɛ maye loo mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Cover crops carpet the ground to block sunlight from weeds, keep heavy rain from washing away your topsoil, and feed nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Ha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu lɛ akashɛ jwɛi ahe. Tsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni ekwɛɛɛ pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as intense dry heat, sudden drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, causing the plant to drop blossoms to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ latsaa ni mli egbi. hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: What causes the leaves inside the center of my young maize plants to look like they have holes eaten through them overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ fee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ bu yɛ mli nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This hole pattern is typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which hide deep inside the growing funnel of the plant during the day and feed heavily during cool hours.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu nɛɛ baa. ni amɛtao niyenii waa yɛ gbɛkɛ mli

english: Why do the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turn dark and rotten while the rest of the fruit looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi miifee ediŋŋ ni efite yɛ be mli ni eshwɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Dark, sunken bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, which usually happens when soil moisture swings rapidly between too dry and too wet.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato shikpɔŋ ni efee ediŋŋ lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ nɔ ni edɔ tsɔ teŋ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the damp ground to capture maximum sunlight for making energy, which directly helps the plant grow larger tubers underground while preventing leaf rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I cut away small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water, food, and light from the main plantain tree, which results in smaller bunches and weaker stems if they are not pruned down.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei krokomɛi juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa kɛji akɛ afolɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to throw chemical fertilizer onto dry soil around my crops during a hot week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ yɛ oshara mli.

english: Chemical fertilizer needs soil water to dissolve safely; on dry soil, the concentrated salts pull moisture out of the roots, burning the plant and causing it to wither.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli, ni ehaa tsei lɛ shãa ni ehaa amɛgboɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same piece of farmland every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests to multiply. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baajɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ

english: When crops are crowded, they compete heavily for sunlight, water, and food. They stretch upward rapidly searching for light, which makes their stems thin and fragile instead of growing strong roots and fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya koni amɛtao la. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. yɛ shishifãi kɛ yibii ni mli wa najiaŋ

english: Why do my yam vines produce plenty of bushy leaves above ground but yield very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai akui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi bulbs bibii waa yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to focus all their energy on growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots to build large tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama tsei ahe tsei ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ sisi a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: How do I know when my cassava is mature enough to harvest from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the main stem will begin to crack as the tubers swell underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaayɔse akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the young cocoa pods on my trees turn black and dry up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excessive shade and wet conditions. Trimming extra tree branches to let light in and quickly removing infected pods stops the fungus from spreading to healthy cocoa.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nine kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji krokomɛi koni la abote mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants turn yellow and curl up tightly during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpãa shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny insects called whiteflies that spread viruses between plants, or by heat stress. Keeping the field weed-free, watering at the base, and removing sickly plants early protects the healthy crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tsei ateŋ loo kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli Ha ŋmɔji amli jwɛi akafee nɔ ko, nu yɛ shishigbɛ ni ojie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni eha amɛhe awa.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds around my young cowpea plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Mi cowpea bibii lɛ duɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Young crops cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures the young crop gets all the food it needs and removes hiding places for crop-damaging pests.
ga: Tsei bibii nyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei bibii lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ. ni ajie hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ.

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism maize uses to save water. By rolling up, the plant reduces the leaf area exposed to the hot sun, stopping moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛji okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baaha he ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when the weather gets too hot, when water is scarce, or when there is too much fertilizer. Maintaining steady soil moisture helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu faaa loo be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds rot in the seedbed instead of sprouting after I sow them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ dumɔwui ashishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when planted too deep in heavy, waterlogged soil where air cannot reach them. Planting seeds near the surface in loose, well-drained soil gives them the warmth and air needed to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli tsɔ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: I thought plants love water, so why does too much rain ruin my vegetable crops?
ga: Misusuɔ akɛ tsei sumɔɔ nu. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ miifite mi-aduawai lɛ?

english: While plants need water to grow, heavy rain fills up all the air spaces in the soil, effectively drowning the roots. Without air, roots cannot breathe or absorb nutrients, causing vegetables to yellow, rot, and die.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu he miihia tsei koni amɛdara moŋ, Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ boteɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my open-field vegetables yellowing and rotting after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess rain on open land washes away soil nutrients and leaves root systems waterlogged. It also creates a wet environment where fungal diseases spread quickly across leaves and stems.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine yɛ hei ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ baaho niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ebaaha nu aba shishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ hu baa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: If I plant my vegetables inside a greenhouse, will heavy rains outside still affect them?
ga: Kɛji odu aduawai yɛ ŋmɔ mli Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shia kponɔ lɛ baaná aduawai anɔ hewalɛ lolo?

english: Yes, even inside a greenhouse, continuous heavy rain causes high humidity and reduces available sunlight. High moisture in the air can still trigger mold and plant diseases inside the structure.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ ŋmɔ mli po. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ hu kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo baa ni ehaa hulu la ni yɔɔ lɛ baa shi. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ awo ŋmeii kɛ tsei ahe helai ni yɔɔ tsũ lɛ mli lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: What will happen to my vegetable crops if the dry season sets in and I do not have water to spray on them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be eba ni mibɛ nu ni mikɛbaashwie nɔ?

english: Without rain or an irrigation system, the hot sun rapidly dries out the soil. Your vegetables will wilt, stop growing, and can suffer severe or total damage very quickly.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ loo nu shwiemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ko bɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. O-vegetables lɛ baagboi, ebaakpa shweremɔ, ni ebaanyɛ efite waa loo efite kwraa oya.

english: Why is it risky to start farming vegetables without setting up an irrigation system first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaaje aduawai adumɔ shishi ni atooo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Vegetables rely on steady soil moisture to survive. If the rains unexpectedly stop and you cannot irrigate, your entire crop can be ruined before you get a chance to harvest.
ga: Aduawai damɔ sũ mli fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ nɔ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa ni onyɛɛɛ okɛ nu awo mli. Onibii fɛɛ baanyɛ afite dani oná hegbɛ ni okpa.

english: How long can my vegetable crops survive once the dry season begins if I have no irrigation?
ga: Be enyiɛ mi aduawai lɛ baahi shi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi kɛji mibɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ?

english: Vegetable crops are very sensitive to dry weather; without irrigation, intense dry heat can ruin your crops in just two to three months, or even less.
ga: Aduawai tsei lɛ nuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi he waa. Kɛji nu shwieee nɔ Dɔlɛ ni mli egbi waa lɛ baanyɛ afite onibii yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ mli loo nɔ ni shɛɛɛ nakai po mli.

english: How fast can a short dry spell destroy my farm if it stops raining suddenly?
ga: Te hɔmɔ ni baa be kukuoo mli lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔ lɛ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Damage from a dry spell can happen in a very short timeframe. Soil loses moisture fast in the heat, and within just a couple of months without water, vulnerable crops can fail completely.
ga: Nɔ ni jɛɔ majik ni egbi mli baa lɛ baanyɛ aba yɛ be kukuoo mli kwraa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ni yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli ni nu bɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ hu baanyɛ afite kwraa.

english: Does growing crops in a greenhouse guarantee that bad weather will never hurt my harvest?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii lɛ enaŋ nibii ni mifeɔ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: A greenhouse offers protection from direct rain drops and strong wind, but extreme weather like prolonged dry heat or high humidity during heavy rains can still cause damage if heat and moisture aren't properly managed.
ga: Greenhouses buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Shi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa waa, tamɔ hulutsoo be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo hulutsoo be ni mli wa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli, Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite nii hu kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do vegetables seem to get damaged by bad weather much faster than tree crops like cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa lɛ fiteɔ aduawai oya fe tsei tamɔ kookoo lɛ?

english: Vegetables have soft stems and shallow root systems that store very little water. Because of this structure, both flooding from heavy rains and short droughts of two to three months impact them almost immediately.
ga: Aduawai yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nu fioo pɛ hiɛɔ. Kɛtsɔ nɛkɛ gbɛjianɔtoo nɛɛ nɔ lɛ Nu afua ni jɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hɔmɔ ni ba nyɔji fioo komɛi amli lɛ fɛɛ ná nɔ ko ni miihe ashɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What damage occurs to my open farmland when a heavy storm hits my vegetable bed?
ga: Mɛni fiteɔ miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ ni agbele naa lɛ nɔ kɛ́ ahum ni naa wa ko tswa mi aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy storms hit open land directly, packing down the topsoil, washing away valuable nutrients, and leaving standing pools of water that cause crop roots to rot.
ga: Ahum ni naa wa tswaa hei ni agbele naa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ekɛ niyenii ni jara wa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni eshiɔ nu ŋshɔi ni ekã shi ni haa tsei shishifãi fiteɔ.

english: How can I tell if old seeds I stored from last season are still alive and good to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui momo ni mikɛto yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni esa akɛ adu?

english: You can test seed vitality using a simple germination test by wrapping 10 seeds in a damp cloth for a few days. If most of them sprout, your seeds are alive and strong enough to produce healthy crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shweremɔ kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo aka bɔ ni odumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi amɛha lɛ okwɛ. Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni oookɛwo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii 2-3 lɛ nɔ lɛ, kɛji amɛteŋ babaoo kwɛ̃ Odumɔwui lɛ baahi shi lolo ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant my maize in straight lines with measured spacing instead of just scattering the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni asusu gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui kɛkɛ

english: Planting in measured rows gives each crop equal space to draw sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors, while making farm maintenance much easier.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni asusu he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbala hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔ mli saamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: What makes improved seed varieties from agricultural officers better than the traditional seeds I save myself?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui ni atsake kɛjɛ okwaayeli nitsulɔi adɛŋ lɛ hi fe blema dumɔwui ni mi diɛŋtsɛ miyeɔ mibuaa mihe lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are developed through scientific research to naturally withstand local pests, survive dry spells better, and yield more produce in a shorter time.
ga: Atsɔ jeŋ nilee mli niiamlitaomɔ nɔ afee dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Ehi shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo yɛ be kukuoo mli

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn pale yellow even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ miinɛ bɔ ni sa?

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant lacks nutrient energy in the soil, like nitrogen. Rain gives moisture, but compost or fertilizer provides the food energy crops need to stay green and healthy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii hewalɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to burn dry bushes and stalks on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã tsei bibii kɛ tsei ni egbi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu nii lɛ?

english: Burning kills the natural soil life and destroys organic matter that keeps your soil rich, moist, and fertile for growing crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings stop growing tall for a few weeks after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ekpaa shweremɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni mikɛ amɛ ewo he kroko lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The plant temporarily pauses top growth to focus its energy on building strong roots deep in the soil. Once the root system is established, vertical leaf growth continues.
ga: Tsei kpaa amɛdalɛ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ ama shishifãi ni wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ ato shishi lɛ, Vertical leaf lɛ dalɛ baaya nɔ.

english: Why are my farm vegetables growing very tall and thin with few leaves under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo, ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ yɔɔ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Crops stretch upward when searching for light. If shaded by larger trees, they waste energy growing weak tall stems toward the sun instead of thick, leafy leaves.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ beni amɛtaoɔ la lɛ. Kɛji oyɛ tso agbo ko shishi Amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ baai najiaŋ

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of key minerals causes stress, forcing the plant to shed flowers to conserve its energy for basic survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo shika tsuru ni he hiaa ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛha shishijee wala.

english: How does crop disease spread from one sick plant to healthy ones across my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Diseases spread through tiny microscopic spores carried by wind, splashing rainwater, infected farming tools, or insects moving between plants.
ga: Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa lɛ anɔ. nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi Okwaayeli nibii loo kooloi bibii ni nyiɛɔ tsei ateŋ ni hela emɔ amɛ

english: How should I safely store unused seeds and farm chemicals so they do not spoil before next season?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ ato shweshweeshwe koni amɛkafite dani be ni baa lɛ aba?

english: Store them off the ground in sealed containers placed in a dry, cool, and dark room to shield them from moisture, heat, and air degradation.
ga: Akɛto shikpɔŋ yɛ tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ naa mli ni akɛwo tsu ko ni mli egbi, ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ, dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ akafite.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, keeps the ground cool and traps moisture so your plants do not dry out quickly, while also stopping weeds from taking over.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ akagbi oya, yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa hu koni jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for food, specifically nitrogen, or that too much water is drowning their roots and stopping them from taking up nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen Loo nu babaoo haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛná niyenii kpakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and growing very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice out of the leaves and spreading plant sicknesses, which stops the plant from growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ kɛ tso helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haaa tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before any tomatoes grow on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as severe sun heat, lack of water, or soil that lacks essential nutrients like calcium.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the trees during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal sickness called Black Pod disease, which spreads rapidly in warm, damp weather when water stays trapped on the pods and branches.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛ́ nu tsɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting under the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpaa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil holds too much water without draining, allowing ground fungi to attack the wet roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni ekɛjieee nu. Enɛ haa ŋmei ni atswa lɛ tutuaa shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I leave space between my maize seeds instead of planting many close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu babaoo? Ha dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin stems and small harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni akpaaa nii babaoo.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize removes goodness from the soil, but beans put vital food back into the earth through their roots, keeping your soil healthy for the next farming season.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Mohu ɔ, ngmlɛfia ɔmɛ ngɔɔ niyenii nɛ he hia kɛ baa zugba a mi kɛ guɔ a sisije ɔmɛ a nɔ. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha okwaayeli be ni baa lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops so it does not go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛkafite?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil during periods of active plant growth, not during dry spells or heavy downpours that wash the fertilizer away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miida waa lɛ. Jeee yɛ hɔmɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my maize crop is mature enough and completely ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmã lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn dry and brown, and the grains become hard enough that you cannot dent them easily with your fingernail.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ atsɔ otsitsii lɛ anɔ atsɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do the leaves on my grain crop turn yellow and dry up just before harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani akpa lɛ?

english: This is a natural process where the mature plant stops feeding its leaves and directs all its remaining energy and nutrients straight into ripening the seeds.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei ni eda lɛ kpaɔ amɛbaai lɛ niyenii ni amɛtsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are some crop plants on my farm ready for harvest while others on the same field are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi Ayɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lolo.

english: Uneven crop maturity usually happens when seeds are planted at different depths, soil moisture is unequal across the field, or mixed-quality seeds were used.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei adalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jeee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. loo okɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni efutu atsu nii
