english: Will using a harvesting machine damage my crop compared to harvesting by hand?
ga: Ani ŋmaakpamɔ tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmaakpamɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ lɛ he?

english: A harvesting machine will not damage your crop as long as the plants are fully mature and dry; it actually harvests faster and reduces grain loss on the field.
ga: Nikpalɔ lɛ fiteŋ onibii lɛ, be fɛɛ be ni tsei lɛ edara ni amɛgbi lɛ. Kpamɔ oya ni oha dumɔwui ni laajeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my crops fall flat on the ground right before harvest when there is strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani akpaa be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Crops fall over, or lodge, when their stems are weakened by overcrowding, poor soil nutrients, or heavy grain heads that the stalks can no longer support during windy weather.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛjeɔ kpo kɛji tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo dumɔwui lɛ amli tsii waa akɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ amɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I harvest my grains early in the morning when there is dew on the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikpaa dumɔwui lɛ leebi be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting wet crops introduces extra moisture that makes the grains rot quickly in storage and can cause harvesting tools or machinery to clog easily.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kroko baa, ni no haa ŋmaa fiteɔ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ eha nibii loo tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ atsĩ mlɛo

english: What happens to my grain crop if I leave it on the field too long after it has ripened?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving ripe crops on the field causes grains to dry out excessively, shatter onto the ground, get eaten by birds and insects, or rot if unexpected rain falls.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmaa lɛ agbi tsɔ. Egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni okpoi kɛ kooloi ye lɛ. loo egbo kɛji nugbɔ nɛ trukaa.

english: Why do my rice grains drop off the stalk by themselves before I even get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ dani akpaa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Rice grains shatter and fall easily when the crop is over-ripe and extremely dry, making the stem holding the grain brittle.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ fãa oya ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ omɔ tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni amɛgbi waa. Enɛ haa tso ni hiɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my harvested grains start feeling hot when I heap them together in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ jeɔ shishi edɔɔ kɛ́ abua naa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Harvested grains release moisture and heat as they settle; if stacked without proper drying, trapped moisture creates heat which breeds mold and destroys the crop.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ be mli ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ato he ni egbiko jogbaŋŋ lɛ, nu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crop plants produce very small grain heads when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ naa dumɔwui ayitsei bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight fiercely for limited water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving less energy for the plant to build large grain heads.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ waa koni amɛná nu fioo, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaafee dumɔwui ayitsei wuji.

english: Does it matter which direction I point a cassava stem cutting when planting it in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ ofo ŋmei niji lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the node buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the leaves struggle to sprout upward and the roots produce very small, poor tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaawa akɛ ebaakwɛ̃. Ni shishifãi lɛ baajie ŋmeii bibii ni ehiii kwraa kpo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Giving each plant enough space allows it to grow strong stalks and produce larger, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha nu. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ehe awa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build healthy leaves. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives the crop the nitrogen it needs to turn dark green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná nitrogen ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nutrients from the ground, but leguminous crops like groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting groundnuts restores the fertility of your land naturally for the next season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmãa, tamɔ ŋmãa, jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil receives two or three steady, heavy rains that soak deep into the earth before planting. Planting right after the very first light rain is risky because if the rain stops for a few days, the heat will dry out and kill the germinating seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa ni baa shi shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ dani okɛdu. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyɛ oshara. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo lɛ, latsaa lɛ mli egbi ni ebaanyɛ egbe dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetables with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, called mulching, keeps the hot sun from evaporating soil water quickly. It keeps the roots cool, retains soil moisture longer, and eventually rots into rich manure.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ akafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmei

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when they are exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that dry out quickly under strong, direct sun. Planting shade crops like plantains or bananas alongside cocoa creates living umbrellas that shield the young cocoa until their root systems are mature enough to handle full heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo banana kɛ kookoo lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants as they begin to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi beni ebɔi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need tall sticks to lift their leaves high off the ground toward sunlight. When yam leaves get plenty of sunlight, they make more food for the plant, resulting in bigger yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛná tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ. Kɛji sweet potato baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaafee niyenii babaoo aha tsei lɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that nests in the funnels of maize leaves to eat the tender growing parts. Applying approved treatments early in the morning or late afternoon when the caterpillars come out to feed protects the crop from major damage.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni feɔ amɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii leebi loo shwane mli Kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ je kpo koni amɛbaye nii lɛ, amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa kɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ ni mli wa he.

english: Is it bad for my soil if I burn all the bush and dry leaves on my farm before planting?
ga: Ani ebaana shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo kɛji mishã tsei bibii kɛ baai ni egboi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani midu?

english: Burning clears land quickly, but the intense heat kills beneficial living organisms in the topsoil and burns away natural organic matter. Clearing without fire allows leaves to decay into natural manure that keeps your soil fertile and moist.
ga: La ni ashãa lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa gbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni eshãa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni la bɛ mli lɛ, ebaa lɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect them from intense direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects their delicate leaves from burning and helps retain moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo be fioo ko koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi

english: What is causing these small caterpillars to eat the leaves inside the central whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that attacks young maize. Early detection and applying recommended organic or chemical sprays into the leaf funnel during late afternoon helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fɔɔ baa ni tutuaa ŋmãa bibii lɛ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ anaa mra kɛ nitsumɔ. kɛyaa baai lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli koni eye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and giving plants enough space for airflow helps them produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ muji ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni aha tso lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know which part of a cassava stem is best to cut and plant for a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni esa akɛ mafo ni madu koni maná ŋmaa ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Use mature, healthy stems from the middle section of a harvested plant, avoiding the soft green top or woody base. Cut pieces with 3 to 5 growth nodes and plant them with the buds pointing upwards.
ga: Kɛ tsei ni eda ni mli wa ni jɛ tso ni akpa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ atsu nii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe. Kpɔ̃ɔ fã ko ni 3 kɛyashi 5 yɔɔ mli ni odu ni ŋmei lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi.

english: Wait until the rainy season fully sets in after two or three deep, soaking rains, rather than planting right after the very first light shower, which can cause seeds to germinate and then dry out.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa ni haa nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight rows with fixed spacing instead of scattering seeds by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niji baadu dumɔwui lɛ

english: Planting in rows gives each plant its own space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without crowding. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much faster and easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa ehe gbɛ, hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, kɛ nikpamɔ hu yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning light green or yellow even though there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen-based fertilizer will help restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which naturally absorbs nitrogen from the air and enriches the soil. Rotating them with maize restores soil fertility naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii. Kɛ akɛ ŋmã tsu nii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: How can I keep the soil around my plantain stems wet during the hot Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground around the base of your plantains with dry leaves, grass, or cocoa husks creates a mulch layer. This shield keeps the soil cool, traps moisture, and slows down water evaporation.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo kookoo ŋmeii ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii. Nɛkɛ tsɔne nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow smaller and produce less yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with your crops for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. Removing weeds during the first few weeks after planting ensures your crops get the food they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down makes it hard for roots to grow and reduces your yield. Always make sure the tiny growth buds on the stem point upward toward the sky before burying the stick.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei ni ooodu ni okɛ ohiɛ afɔ shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ehaa onibii ni onáa lɛ baa shi. Kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ ŋmeii lɛ afee bibii. yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani afu tso lɛ

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is even ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ po feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea early in the growing season keeps the leaves green and helps the ears grow big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eye ebua toi lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Is it safe for me to mix different fertilizers together in one bag to save time when applying them?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baafutu yɛ kotoku kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite yɛ nitsumɔ mli?

english: Not all fertilizers can be mixed ahead of time. Some chemicals react with each other, causing the mixture to clump into hard rocks or lose valuable nutrients into the air as gas before reaching your plants.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ afutu mli kɛtsɔ hiɛ. Tsofai komɛi kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ tɛi ni wa loo niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ laajeɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ dani eshɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe.

english: How does growing beans or cowpeas help make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer factory for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Muawai bibii yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpeas mli. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔhe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my yam crop after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yam plants need fertilizer most when their leaves start spreading out and roots are actively feeding, usually one to two months after sprouting. Applying fertilizer before the plant sprouts wastes money because there are no roots to absorb it.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii fe fɛɛ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa ni ahaa shishifãi lɛ niyenii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji kome kɛyashi enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Shika ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ ji shika fitemɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi ni baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences heavy stress from severe heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing shade during very hot weeks helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ ni naa wa kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen babaoo mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eyɛ hulutsoo yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What causes the leaves of my tomato plants to curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips transmitting a virus. Spraying your field early with organic options like neem oil helps protect plants from insect damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ tomato mli lɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli mra Kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem fɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe.

english: How can I keep tiny bugs from eating my harvested maize while it is stored in bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa? Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aye ŋmãa ni akpa be mli ni eyɔɔ kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Make sure your maize is completely dry before bagging, keep bags elevated off damp floors on wooden pallets, and use sealed hermetic storage bags that cut off oxygen so pests cannot survive inside.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ egbi kwraa dani okɛwo kotoku mli. Too kotokui ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ. Ni okɛ kotokui ni akɛ nibii toɔ mli ni atsĩ naa, ni ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seed bags every season instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ kotokui daa be mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid harvests lose their strength in the next generation, producing smaller crops and lower yields. Fresh certified seeds guarantee strong growth and high resistance to diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ maa dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ mi.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting enough water or if I am giving them too much?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo mikɛ nu babaoo miiha amɛ?

english: Crops show clear signs through their leaves and roots. Dry, crisp, or curling leaves mean the plant is thirsty, while yellowing leaves and soft, rotting stems usually mean the roots are drowning in too much water.
ga: Tsei jieɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi anɔ. Baai ni egbi, ni mli edɔ, loo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye tso lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egbo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ ebote nu babaoo mli tsɔ.

english: Maize leaves roll up during extreme heat as a natural defense to trap moisture and prevent water from evaporating into the air. Once the air cools down in the evening, the leaves unroll again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛtsi nu naa koni ekaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Baai lɛ shwie shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that create living shade to protect the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my maize in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures every plant gets equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients. It also makes it much easier to clear weeds, apply fertilizer, and walk through your farm without stepping on crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Agbɛnɛ hu, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ oootsi jwɛi, ooowo ŋmɔshi nibii amli, ni onyiɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ onaji akashwieee ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods to rest and save water inside its stem and roots. Even though the plant looks dead above ground, the cassava tubers underneath remain healthy and will sprout new leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ nu ahi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa lolo ni amɛbaakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Why do heavy rains cause the flowers on my cowpeas to fall off before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash away pollen from open flowers and prevent insects like bees from pollinating them. Excess water can also stress the plant, causing it to drop delicate blossoms early.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi ni agbele mli lɛ amli lɛ. ni etsĩ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkawo nakai fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii Nu babaoo baanyɛ aha tso lɛ ahao. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant is running out of food nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. The tomato plant moves nutrients from its oldest bottom leaves up to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tomato tsei lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the crop experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollination. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting shade trees nearby can help the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after the first rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are native to the soil, so their seeds are always ready to wake up and absorb water instantly. Crops are domesticated and take longer to establish roots before they can grow quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaate shi ni amɛŋɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Akwɛɔ tsei yɛ shia mli ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi dani amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and wrinkle when small green insects gather underneath them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: Small insects like aphids hide under leaves to suck out the liquid food juice inside the plant. As they feed, they cause the leaf to lose shape, wrinkle, and curl tightly inward.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ aphids lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ashishi koni amɛmu niyenii ni ji nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Beni ayeɔ nii lɛ, baai lɛ fiteɔ amɛhe, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyaa mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the ground stays too wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during heavy rains usually mean the roots are trapped in waterlogged soil and cannot take up nitrogen, or that nutrients have been washed away deeper into the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ emɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli, ni enyɛŋ ejie nitrogen. aloo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with big leaves but gives me small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ yitsei bibii lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes the cassava plant to spend its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantain yɛ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sun. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act like living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade it needs during its first years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo bibioo lɛ ni enáa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, which crawl into the funnel of young maize plants to feed on the soft growing leaves before the plant produces maize ears.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall armyworms ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ dani tsei lɛ awo ŋmãa toi.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow and curling up tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Curled yellow leaves on cassava are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whitefly insects.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle ŋmɔtɔ he lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ

english: Why do my groundnuts grow well even when I do not add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii po fataaa he lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that can pull nitrogen gas directly from the air using tiny nodules on their roots, feeding themselves naturally.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmei ko ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛye ehe niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I cover my garden soil with dry grass instead of burning it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo mibɔɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã lɛ?

english: Leaving dry grass on top of the soil keeps the ground cool, holds in moisture after watering, and slowly breaks down into natural food for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nu ni okɛwo mli lɛ sɛɛ, ni fiofio lɛ, ejara mli efee adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl inward during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during hot weather to shade themselves and stop water from evaporating too quickly from the plant.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds sprout much faster than my crop seeds after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have hardy natural seeds sleeping in the soil that respond instantly to moisture, growing fast to compete with your planted crops for sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ ba lɛ, amɛtsuɔ he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni edaa oya koni ekɛ hulu la ni adu lɛ yɛ mli lɛ aye akaŋ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when the fruit bunches grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi beni aduawai lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are short and shallow, making the heavy top part of the plant easy to push over in strong winds unless you support the stem with wooden poles.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ yɛ kuku ni amɛhe ekɔɔɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yiteŋ ni tsii lɛ feɔ mlɛo akɛ aaatsi kɛya nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Ja okɛ tso fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa plants keep dying when I plant them in a clear, sunny open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade to protect them from scorching heat and rapid water loss. Planting shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa creates a canopy that protects young cocoa until they are mature and tough enough to withstand sunlight.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nu ni fiteɔ oya lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu la lɛ naa.

english: Why should I plant maize and cassava together in the same farm instead of planting only maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa kɛkɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava takes up to a year to mature. Planting them together allows you to harvest food quickly from the maize while the cassava slowly expands to fill the space.
ga: Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei heɔ afi dani eshɛɔ ŋmei he. Hefatalɔi adumɔ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa mli oya. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ Egbɛɔ eshwaa fiofio kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eyiɔ he lɛ mli obɔ

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers like Urea or well-decomposed manure gives the plants the strength to stay green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: How do I know if my soil is loose enough to grow good cassava or yam tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei kpakpa loo ŋmei kpakpa?

english: Tuber crops need soft, well-drained soil so the roots can expand easily under the ground. If you can easily push a sharp stick deep into the soil after a rain without hitting hard rocks or clay, the soil is suitable for forming large tubers.
ga: Tubers biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi mlɛo. Kɛji akɛ obaanyɛ otsi tso ni mli wa awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ oya ni okɛ tɛi ni wa loo shikpɔŋ sũ etswaaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha bulb agboi akwɛmɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes twisting, curling, and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebɔle ehe, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hei komɛi lɛ?

english: Curled, yellow-patterned leaves on cassava are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting improved, disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers prevents this problem.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle yucca he lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ duɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to suddenly turn black and dry up on the stem?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ trukaa ni egbi yɛ tso lɛ shishi?

english: Cocoa pods turn black due to Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in wet, dark, and damp conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let sunlight reach the farm and removing affected pods early stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, duŋ, kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ ahe ni afolɔ babaoo koni hulu la ashɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni ena naagbai lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my pepper leaves look small and crinkled, and why is the plant refusing to grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ bibii ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ pepper tso lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crinkled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips feeding on the plant's sap and passing viruses to it. Spraying early with appropriate organic or chemical insecticides protects the leaves so the plant can grow tall and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛhaa helai baa. Organic loo tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ adara ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms keep falling off the plant without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or drought. Giving your tomatoes consistent water at the root level during dry spells helps the flowers stay on the plant and develop into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tomato nɔ nu daa yɛ shishifã lɛ he yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I tell that my plantain bunch is full and ready to be harvested while it is still green?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain tso lɛ eyi obɔ ni esa akɛ akpa be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: A plantain bunch is ready to harvest when the individual fingers become plump and round, and the sharp ridges on their green skin start to smooth out. You do not need to wait for the skin to turn yellow.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni nineshi nine lɛ eko fɛɛ eko egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ eŋɔli lɛ nɔ lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehe ehiaaa ni omɛ ni ohewolo lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily whenever a mild rainstorm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo be fɛɛ be ni wɔbaaná nugbɔ bibioo ko lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its root support is weak or when the stalks are weakened by stem borer pests. Heaping extra soil around the base of the stalks (earthing up) when the plant is knee-high gives it strong support against wind.
ga: Abɛi gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ shishifã lɛ sɛɛfimɔ lɛ gbɔjɔ loo kɛ́ ŋmei lɛ gbɔjɔ yɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ ŋmei lɛ ahewɔ. Shikpɔŋ kroko ni akɛbaabɔle tso lɛ shishi (shikpɔŋ nɔ) beni tso lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hebuu kpakpa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green. It can also happen if heavy rains flood the soil and prevent the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs maximum sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and allowing the leaves to catch full sunlight.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ebaatsi helai anaa, ni ebaaha baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the ground cool and traps moisture so you water less often. It also stops heavy rains from washing away the good topsoil.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni onyɛ okɛ nu awo mli shii abɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed, often by extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks by tiny insects. When stressed, the plant saves its strength by dropping flowers instead of feeding growing peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be Loo kooloi bibii tutuaa mɔ kɛji akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli. Tsei lɛ hiɛɔ hewalɛ mli kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp weather. Too much shade and lack of airflow around the trees help water sit on the pods, allowing the fungus to spread easily.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ kɛ fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Shade babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ ehe lɛ ni bɛ Tso lɛ haa nu lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curled, yellow cassava leaves are a classic sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. The virus weakens the plant, preventing it from producing large roots.
ga: Kasava baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Virus lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa shishifãi wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do people advise planting plantain suckers next to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and cool soil they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow small and thin when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough nourishment to grow thick and healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack as the tubers swell up beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ daa yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why does my maize crop dry up so quickly if a short dry spell happens when it is flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ be kukuoo ko yɛ ni egbiɔ beni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Flowering is the time maize needs the most water because it is making the grains. A lack of water at this exact moment causes severe stress, causing the leaves to dry up and reducing the corn yield.
ga: Fɔfɔii ji be ni nu he hiaa ŋmãa fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ no haa dumɔwui lɛ daa. Nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa. Ehaa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why are certified seeds from Cocobod better than saving seeds from my own harvested cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Cocobod kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli lɛ hi fe mi diɛŋtsɛ mi kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from your own harvest often lose their strength over generations and can carry hidden diseases. Certified seeds from Cocobod are specially bred in laboratories to resist diseases like Black Pod and yield much higher harvests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ okpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ aba. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ Cocobod he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ yɛ laboratori lɛ mli koni ekɛ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ akpee naa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I plant sprout quickly while others rot in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ni miduɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi fiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are old, damaged by insects, or infected with fungus. Quality treated seeds have a protective coating that prevents soil insects and rot from destroying the seed before it can germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji amɛgbɔ, kooloi efite amɛ, loo amɛyɛ ŋmei. Dumɔwui ni atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ he koni sũ mli kooloi kɛ ŋmeii akafite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does plowing my farmland with a tractor make my crops grow better than just clearing the bush with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ trakta tsuɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Plowing breaks up hard, compacted soil deep down, making it much easier for crop roots to push deep into the earth to find water and nutrients. It also buries weeds and mixes organic matter into the root zone.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ baatsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii. Amɛfuɔ jwɛi hu ni amɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli futuɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants produce tiny ears when I plant them close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ toi bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every single plant enough breathing room and food to produce big, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni ekɛmuɔ nii kɛ niyenii ni haa etoi lɛ feɔ agbo ni ehe wa.

english: Why is it dangerous to plant my bean seeds too deep down in the earth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu mi-beans lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ?

english: A seed only has a small amount of stored energy inside it. If planted too deep, the young shoot exhausts all its energy trying to push through the heavy soil and dies before reaching the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato yɛ amɛmli. Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ baafite hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ mli ni amɛgboi dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves on my corn turn yellow even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to stay green and grow. Heavy rains can actually wash nitrogen deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and tender leaves that lose water rapidly under direct sunlight and dry winds. They need temporary shade, like plantain trees planted next to them, to shield them until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao hɔɔŋ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ gãimlibii kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ aya mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the branches without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack of soil nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny insects in the farm to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava so the tubers do not spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Bɔni afee ni akafite yitso lɛ

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, typically around 9 to 12 months after planting. Leaving tubers in the ground too long makes them tough, woody, and watery.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi yitso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etamɔ tso ni nu hu yɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my main crops after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitso titri lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions and quickly claim open sunlight and rain. Main crops grow slower early on because they put their energy into building strong roots and fruits rather than wild aggressive growth.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛbiɔ hulu kɛ nugbɔ oya. Tso titri lɛ daa blɛoo fe tsutsu lɛ mra. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ shishifãi kɛ aduawai ni mli wa. Mohu ɔ, e daa wawɛɛ ngɛ nga a mi.

english: Why is my mango tree growing tall and leafy, but it refuses to bear any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ daa ni ewoɔ baai shi ekpooɔ akɛ ebaawo yibii lɛ?

english: A mango tree might put all its energy into leaves if there is too much nitrogen in the soil or if it receives heavy water right when it should be flowering. Mango trees often need a short dry period to trigger flower production before setting fruit.
ga: Mango tso baanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ awo ebaai lɛ amli kɛji akɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ beni esa akɛ ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei biɔ be kuku ni amɛgbi koni amɛwo fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii.

english: How many years does a newly planted mango seedling usually take before I start seeing fruit?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango dumɔwu ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibii kpojiemɔ shishi?

english: Grafted mango trees usually start bearing fruit within 3 to 4 years, whereas trees grown directly from a mango seed can take anywhere from 5 to 8 years to produce their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni mango tsei ni akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ mango dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé he fɛɛ he kɛjɛ afii 5 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛwo amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii.

english: Why should I clear and plow my land before the major rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni atsu nii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Preparing land early allows the soil to absorb initial rainwater easily, loosens hard ground for young roots to penetrate, and clears weeds so your crops do not have to fight them for food and water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ shishijee nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo. Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli koni shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ abote mli. ni ojie jwɛi lɛ koni ehe akahia ni onibii lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu.

english: How can I tell if my soil is rich enough to grow vegetables without adding extra fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fataaa he?

english: Dark, crumbly soil that holds moisture well and has earthworms is usually fertile. If crops grow with pale yellow leaves or remain short and thin, the soil is likely missing key nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni bei pii lɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ da kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ehi shi kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Is it better to water my crops heavily once a week or lightly every day?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu babaoo shikome yɛ otsi mli loo fioo daa gbi?

english: Deep watering once or twice a week is usually better than light daily watering because it encourages roots to grow deep into the ground, making the crop stronger and more resistant to dry spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni mli kwɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ hi fe nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fioo daa gbi ejaakɛ eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow and fall off during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much water fills up the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. When roots cannot breathe, they stop absorbing plant food, causing the leaves to yellow and drop.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Ekpaa niyenii ni jɛ tsei amli lɛ ŋmɔmɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from harsh heat and reduce the amount of water escaping into the air. It is a natural defense to save moisture until temperatures cool down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛha nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni akɛbaakwɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: What causes the flowers on my tomato plants to drop off before forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni miiha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai jeɔ kpo?

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer can stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers before pollination happens.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani pollination baa.

english: Why do I need to leave wide spaces between my cassava stems when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi he ko ni da yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ oodu lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that each cassava plant gets enough sunlight for its leaves and ample room under the soil for its roots to expand into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ yucca tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni yucca tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ebaai lɛ. Ni he ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my plantain plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Older bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and die as the plant grows and shifts energy to new top leaves. However, if many leaves turn yellow rapidly, it can indicate a lack of soil nutrients or poor water flow.
ga: Baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋwɛi baa heei anɔ lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai babaoo batsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ, Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I make my pineapples grow bigger and taste sweeter?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-pineapple lɛ adara ni efee fɛo?

english: Pineapples gain their sweetness from getting full sunlight and taking up nutrients like potassium from rich soil. Unlike some fruits, pineapples stop sweetening once harvested, so they must be left to mature fully on the plant before picking.
ga: Pineapple naa eŋɔɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛ niyenii tamɔ potassium ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii amli lɛ mli. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ aduawai komɛi lɛ, kɛ́ akpa pineapple lɛ, ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aŋmɛ pineapple lɛ gbɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto.

english: Why do some crop varieties produce much higher yields in Ghana than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ Ghana fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Ghana's warm tropical climate and rainy seasons favor crops that are naturally adapted to high sunlight and warm soils, allowing well-suited crops to convert sunlight into food much faster.
ga: Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni sa lɛ tsakeɔ hulu la lɛ amɛfeɔ niyenii oya.

english: What causes my soil to lose its power to grow good crops after a few harvests?
ga: Mɛni haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ ŋmaa fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Crops pull food nutrients out of the earth every season to grow. If you do not replace those nutrients using manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil becomes hungry and exhausted over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeee nakai niyenii lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same soil nutrients every year and allows specific pests and soil diseases to build up in that field.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ

english: How does adding animal manure help my soil stay healthy for future years?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ afii babaoo ni baa lɛ?

english: Manure acts like food for the living organism inside the soil, improving its ability to hold rainwater during dry spells and slowly releasing essential nutrients to plants.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ehaa nyɛmɔ ni akɛtoɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ fiofio.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up and drop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is very hot, plants lose water quickly through their leaves. Curling up is a defense mechanism to reduce leaf exposure and conserve moisture until the heat passes.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Curling ji gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛbaa ni ekɛ baai lɛ akabɔ he, ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni latsaa lɛ hoɔ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing larger when rain stops for just two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ enɛ otsii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpa kwɛ̃mɔ?

english: Water acts as the transport system that carries plant nutrients from the soil into the roots. Without water, the plant goes into survival mode and pauses growth to conserve energy.
ga: Nu tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo ni kɛ tsei niyenii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, tsei yaa wala mli ni amɛkpaa amɛdalɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops mostly when fruits begin to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: As plants form fruits, they concentrate natural sugars and proteins in those areas, emitting sweet scents that attract insects looking for high-energy food.
ga: Kɛ tsei wo yibii Amɛhaa adebɔɔ mli sugars kɛ proteins lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ nakai hei lɛ. Ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni gbalaa kooloi bibii ni miitao niyenii ni haa hewalɛ babaoo lɛ.

english: Is it good practice to plant legumes like beans together with my main crops?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu ŋmãa, tamɔ ŋmãa, kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ?

english: Yes, beans and other legumes take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the surrounding soil for nearby crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi. Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my harvested crop to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many improved high-yielding seed varieties lose their special traits in the next generation, producing weaker plants with smaller yields if you reuse the harvested seed.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi babaoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni atsake amɛ lɛ baafite amɛsui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Ebaaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ tsu nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put a large number of seeds into a single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When you put too many seeds in one hole, the seedlings are forced to fight each other for the limited water and food in that spot. Weak seedlings will starve and die, while the survivors will grow tall and skinny instead of strong and full of fruit.
ga: Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ Abaanyɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛwu amɛha nu kɛ niyenii fioo yɛ nakai he lɛ. Dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛgboi. Shi mɛi ni hiɛ ka lɛ daraa ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ yibii.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Overcrowding creates harsh competition among crops. Only the biggest and strongest plants will pull enough water and nutrients to grow properly, while smaller nearby crops get left behind and fail to produce a good harvest.
ga: Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa akaŋshii ni naa wa baa ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ. Tsei ni dara fe fɛɛ ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baagbala nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ashiɔ amɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: How do I know the right number of seeds to put in one spot for crops like maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male dumɔwui ayibɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ madu tso ko tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome?

english: Planting 2 to 3 seeds per hole is usually best. Putting high numbers like 10 or 15 seeds in one spot creates severe overcrowding, forcing crops to exhaust the soil water quickly and struggle to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ bu kome mli. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo, tamɔ 10 loo 15 wo he kome lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli ayi obɔ waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ oya ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛhi shi.

english: How does overcrowding harm my crops during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When too many crops share the same space, they rapidly drink up all the available moisture in the soil. Once the water runs out, the plants become exhausted and stressed, causing weaker plants to dry up and die completely.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ he kome tsu nii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Kɛ́ nu lɛ ho lɛ, tsei lɛ ahe feɔ shoo ni amɛhaoɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kwraa.

english: If I apply fertilizer to an overcrowded farm, will all the plants benefit equally?
ga: Kɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata ŋmɔ ko ni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ he lɛ Ani tsei fɛɛ baaná he sɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: No, the larger and stronger plants with bigger roots will grab most of the fertilizer first. The weaker plants won't get enough to drink or eat, so they will remain small even though you added fertilizer.
ga: Dabi, tsei wuji ni he wa ni shishifãi wuji yɔɔ mli lɛ baamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ. Tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ nuuŋ nu loo amɛyeŋ nii bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbaakã he ahi shi bibii kɛji okɛ amɛ wo amɛmli po.

english: How do deep roots help my crops stay alive when rain is scarce?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ hiɔ shi beni nugbɔ baaa lɛ?

english: Crops with strong, deep roots can reach underground water pockets that shallow-rooted plants cannot. This allows them to keep drinking and stay green for a long time during dry periods.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ ayashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu jɛɛhei ni tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ayashɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to clear out weak seedlings from my farm after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Thinning out weak seedlings leaves more water, sunlight, and food for the remaining strong plants. This removes competition so the surviving crops can grow big and stay healthy for a long time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii baa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa akaŋshii baa shi bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some crops in my field grow much faster and taller than others planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛkwɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Some seeds naturally sprout with stronger vigor than others. These strong plants pull water and nutrients out of the soil more aggressively, leaving less resources for the weaker plants around them.
ga: Dumɔwui komɛi baakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛhe wa fe ekrokomɛi. Nɛkɛ tsei ni wa nɛɛ baajie nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa nibii fioo pɛ ashiɔ ahaa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops so quickly if I don't clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ oya nɛkɛ kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally very tough and aggressive. They rapidly drink up the soil moisture and steal food meant for your crops, causing your crops to get tired, weak, and stunt in growth.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, jwɛi lɛ wa waa ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Amɛmuɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui, amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some strong crops keep bearing fruit for years while others die off quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni wa lɛ woɔ yibii afii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Strong perennial crops establish deep, powerful root systems that secure constant water and nutrients. Once established, they survive environmental stress and remain productive over many seasons.
ga: Nɛkɛ tso ni wa ni yeɔ afii babaoo nɛɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ekɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ahi shi daa. Kɛ ato amɛ shishi lɛ Amɛyeɔ shihilɛ mli haomɔi anɔ kunim ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ bei babaoo mli.

english: Yam plants naturally reach up toward direct sunlight. Giving the vines tall wooden poles to climb helps their leaves spread out wide to catch sunshine, which gives the plant the energy it needs to grow a big tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ aha wain tso lɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekwɔ lɛ, ehaa ebaai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni emɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young green cocoa pods turn completely black and shrink while still on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni egbɔjɔɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This blackening is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions. The fungus attacks the skin of the pod and rots the seeds inside before they can ripen.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ duŋ nɛɛ baa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Fuji lɛ tutuaa pod lɛ hewolo ni ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young corn plants suddenly filled with tiny holes and torn edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ efo?

english: Torn leaves and holes on young corn usually mean Fall Armyworm caterpillars are feeding inside the growing top of the plant. They lay eggs on the leaves and eat the soft inner parts during the night.
ga: Baai kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ miiye nii yɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli. Amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ ni amɛyeɔ hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and droop in the middle of the afternoon even if I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Ani okɛ nu ewo mli momo?

english: When the sun is very hot, tomato plants lose water into the hot air faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. Curling their leaves helps them save moisture, and they usually stand back up once the evening air cools down.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ni amɛfɔɔ shidaamɔ kɛji gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: When maize plants run out of nitrogen in the soil, they move whatever food they have left from their old bottom leaves up to the young growing leaves at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa baa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm to improve the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have microscopic organisms in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it directly into the ground. When the leaves and roots break down, they leave natural fertilizer in the soil for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nibii bibii waa yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest if the tubers are hidden under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: As cassava matures, the plant stops growing new main stems, and the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off. You can also dig gently near the base of one plant to check if the root tubers have grown thick.
ga: Kɛji cassava kwɛ̃ lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii titrii heei ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaagbee shi. Obaanyɛ okɛ blɛoo hu atsu nii. Ebɛŋkɛ tso ko shishi koni okwɛ kɛji shishifã lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my plantain stem shoot out smaller stems around its base, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ niji bibii ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, ni esa akɛ mafo amɛ?

english: The small shoots around the main plantain trunk are called suckers, which are the plant's way of reproducing. It is best to cut away most of them so the mother plant puts all its energy and soil nutrients into producing one large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei bibii ni bɔle plantain wulu lɛ tso lɛ he lɛ akɛ tsei. ni ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afɔɔ tsei lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaafo fã agbo ko mli koni tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ewo yibii agbo kome ni tsii.

english: Why does my maize crop grow powdery flower tassels at the very top before the corn cobs show up on the sides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ni tamɔ powder yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ esɛɛgbɛ lɛ?

english: The top tassel produces yellow pollen dust that gets carried by the wind to fertilize the silks on the growing cobs below. Without this pollen blowing down from the top tassels, kernels will not form inside the corn cob.
ga: Tassels ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ jieɔ pollen sũ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa koni ekɛ siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ awo mli. Kɛji akɛ pollen ko bɛ ni foɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, Dumɔwui efeee ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Can I feed my freshly harvested corn directly to my pigs, or do I need to prepare it first?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha tsinai ŋmãa ni akpa ehee lɛ tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo esa akɛ masaa he dã?

english: While pigs can eat raw corn, drying and cracking or grinding the grains helps the pigs digest the food much better, allowing them to gain more weight from the same amount of feed.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsinai baanyɛ aye ŋmãa ni ahoo moŋ, Shi ŋmãa lɛ ni akumɔ loo agbɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsinabii lɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ niyenii lɛ jogbaŋŋ kwraa. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛtsɔ niyenii ni amɛyeɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: What crops can I grow on my farm to provide the best nutritional benefit for feeding livestock?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii ni hi fe fɛɛ aha mikooloi lɛ?

english: Maize provides high energy for growth, but combining it with leguminous crops like cowpea or groundnut vines provides protein, creating a balanced diet for healthy animals.
ga: Abɛi haa hewalɛ babaoo kɛha dalɛ. Shi kɛ akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmãa fata he lɛ, ehaa protein, ni ehaa kooloi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni ja.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food corn needs to grow strong green leaves and big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why does my maize produce smaller cobs when I plant it on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same spot exhausts specific nutrients from the soil; rotating your farm with beans or cassava gives the land time to recover.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmei tsake oŋmɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my corn help the corn grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are natural fertilizer makers that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the corn roots next to them.
ga: Cowpeas ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa ŋmãa shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do market buyers pay higher prices for some maize varieties than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi ahe nyɔmɔ babaoo fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Buyers prefer varieties with larger grains, lower moisture, and good starch quality because they yield more flour and store longer without breaking down.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ srɔtoi ni dumɔwui wuji yɔɔ mli lɛ. hulutsoo be ni baa shi kɛ ashikishaŋ kpakpa Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa ashikishaŋ babaoo baa, ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ ni ekuuu.

english: How do I know which crop will bring the most benefit to sell at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he fe fɛɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Focus on crops that have strong local demand, store well without quick spoilage, and provide clear nutritional or processing benefits that buyers actively look for.
ga: Gbalamɔ ojwɛŋmɔ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni maŋbii lɛ taoɔ babaoo lɛ anɔ Too jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee oya. ni ekɛ niyenii loo nitsumɔ mli sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ waa lɛ aha.

english: What causes my harvested corn to develop white or black powder inside the storage sack?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ feɔ powda yɛŋ loo ediŋŋ yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: That powder comes from mold, which grows when corn is stored before it is completely dry; grains must be dried until they crack cleanly between your teeth before bagging.
ga: Pauda lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei ko mli. Ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ ajie ŋmãa dani egbi kwraa. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmaa lɛ kɛyashi ebaakumɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ onyanyɔji ateŋ dani akɛwo kotoku mli.

english: Why do some harvested crops spoil in a few days while dry grains last for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nikpamɔi komɛi fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ hiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Crops like tomatoes have high water content that attracts decay, whereas dry grains have very low moisture, putting fungal growth and bacteria on hold.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tomato yɛ nu babaoo ni gbalaa ŋmeii kɛbaa. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ mli nu faaa kwraa lɛ. Ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ adalɛ kpaa.

english: How can I protect my stored maize from weevils without buying expensive chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa?

english: Drying the maize thoroughly under the sun and storing it in airtight hermetic bags (like PICS bags) suffocates insects naturally by cutting off their oxygen.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛto vacuum kotokui amli (tamɔ PICS kotokui) lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ amɛ oxygen ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ ni ebaafo mli lɛ nɔ.
