english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Is it helpful for me to plant groundnuts on the same plot as my maize crop?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei lɛ baaye abua mi?

english: Yes, groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow strong, so planting them together improves your soil fertility naturally.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda waa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall with big green leaves but refuse to produce fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen-based fertilizer encourages the plant to put all its energy into growing branches and leaves instead of flowers. Tomatoes need phosphorus and potassium to form flowers and heavy fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama tsei niji kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Tomato he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni enyɛ ewo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cassava plants turning yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods as a self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss and protect their roots. Once the rains return, fresh green leaves will sprout back.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Baai eŋɔli heei baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small holes appearing on my maize leaves shortly after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ?

english: Holes are usually caused by pests like stemborers or fall armyworms that feed on tender leaves. Spotting this early lets you treat the crop with recommended spray treatments before the growing tip is destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ stem borers loo cutworms ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa. Enɛ kadimɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe nii dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do black spots appear on my cocoa pods when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excess humidity and heavy rain create damp conditions that spread fungal diseases like black pod. Clearing surrounding weeds and pruning extra branches helps air flow through the farm and keeps pods dry.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ eshwaa. Ha jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Ni tsei niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in high temperatures reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing the plant from losing too much water. Mulching around the base keeps the roots cooler and moist.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ he yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi. Tsi tsei anaa koni amɛkafite nu babaoo tsɔ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cocoa seedlings very close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Crowded trees compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing allows every tree to get enough air and light, producing more pods overall.
ga: Tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la ni sa. Enɛ haa pods babaoo baa fɛɛ.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yam plants signal maturity above ground when the leaves turn yellow and the vines dry out completely, showing that the plant has transferred all its stored energy into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni wain tso lɛ egbi kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ etee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil and develop mold inside my storeroom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ miifite ni miifee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain retains internal moisture after harvest. If you store it before drying it thoroughly under the sun, trapped dampness creates an ideal environment for mold and insects to multiply.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa hiɛɔ emli nu yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛto dani egbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli lɛ, Trapped moisture lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni baanyɛ afɔ.

english: How deep should I plant my corn seeds so they germinate well?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Corn seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep. If planted too shallow, birds might eat them or the soil will dry out fast, but if planted too deep, the young shoots won't have enough energy to break through the surface.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimita 3 kɛyashi 5. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, Okpoi baanyɛ aye amɛ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, sũ lɛ baagbi oya. Shi kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, Young shoots lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I not put three or four maize seeds in the same hole when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ woɔ bu kome mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Planting too many seeds in one hole forces the growing plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to thin stalks and small cobs. Planting one or two seeds per hole gives each plant enough space to grow big cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmei agbo ko akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing corn turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your corn lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source for crop growth. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea when the corn is knee-high helps the leaves stay green and produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ daraa Ni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea wo mli beni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves with sawdust-like dirt inside the shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn baa ni muji tamɔ ŋmei yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: This is damage from the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides in the central leaf funnel of the corn plant. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening targets the worms when they come out to feed.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ. Tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baatswa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛje kpo amɛmiitao niyenii lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers plant rice seeds in a small nursery first before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ? Dani obaafã kɛyadu nii yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Nursing rice seedlings first allows you to care for young plants in a controlled area and transplant only the strongest ones into the field. This gives the crop a head start against weeds and results in an even stand and better yield.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ŋmãa dumɔwui ni oookwɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ he ko ni akudɔɔ, ni okɛ tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ jwɛi anɔ kunim, ni ehaa ehe gbɛi jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why does rice need standing water in the field compared to corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ he hiaa ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: While rice roots can grow in moist soil, keeping a thin layer of water on the field smothers weeds that compete for nutrients and creates a steady temperature that helps the rice plant absorb fertilizer easily.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa shishifãi baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ moŋ, shi nu fioo ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ lɛ kɛyaa, ni ehaa hulutsoo be ni yaa nɔ daa ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ni amɛŋɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ mlɛo.

english: How can I tell when my rice crop is fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready for harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains on the plant turn golden-yellow, and the grains at the bottom of the stalk feel hard rather than soft or milky when squeezed.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. Ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee blɛoo loo amɛfee tamɔ mliki kɛji akɛ amɛmimɔ amɛ.

english: How do I know if my harvested corn is dry enough to put into bags for storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo kotoku mli kɛha nibii ni akɛtoɔ?

english: You can test maize by pressing a grain with your thumbnail or biting it; if it makes a sharp cracking sound and leaves no dent, or if salt mixed with a handful of grains in a dry jar stays dry, the maize is ready for storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka ŋmãa okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa ko ni okɛ otsitsi bibioo lɛ baanyɛ nɔ loo kɛtsɔ ŋmãa ni okɛbaamɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ gbee ko ni tswaa ni ŋmeii komɛi bɛ mli Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmaa ni akɛ nine efutu mli yɛ tsɛnsi mli lɛ ehi shi ni egbi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni akɛtoɔ.

english: What can I do to keep weevils from eating my stored maize grain?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni ŋmeii akaye ŋmãa ni ato lɛ?

english: To stop weevils, ensure the corn is thoroughly dried, clean the storage area completely before packing, and use airtight hermetic bags or approved grain protection dust to prevent insects from breeding.
ga: Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akpa lɛ, kwɛmɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi kwraa. Tsumɔ he ni akɛ nibii lɛ toɔ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ dani okɛwo mli. Ni okɛ vacuum bag loo dumɔwui ahe nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii koni kooloi akafɔ.

english: Why does my stored rice turn moldy even when I keep the room closed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? Ni miŋa tsu lɛ?

english: Rice turns moldy if it is bagged before drying completely or if the bags are placed directly on a cold concrete floor. Stacking bags on wooden pallets and ensuring proper grain drying prevents moisture buildup.
ga: Omɔ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ kotoku lɛ fɔ kɔnkrit shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ kotokui wo tsei anɔ ni oha dumɔwui lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Yellowing leaves often mean your cocoa plants are getting too much harsh, direct sunlight or lack sufficient water and nutrients. Providing temporary shade, like planting plantain alongside them, keeps the soil moist and protects young leaves from burning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-cocoa tso lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ. aloo nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ Ehaa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛgbɛ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa baai bibii lɛ ashã.

english: Why should I keep some big trees standing in my cocoa farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi moŋ fe ni mafo amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Large shade trees protect your cocoa from extreme heat, block strong winds from damaging the branches, and drop leaves that rot into rich natural fertilizer for your soil.
ga: Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni amɛbuɔ o-cocoa lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekafite tsei lɛ aniji. ni ehaa baai ni miifite lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa, ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the black spots on my cocoa pods are caused by disease or just rain damage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewɔ ni ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo lɛ nɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Black Pod disease produces soft, spreading dark spots that often develop a white, powdery coating in wet weather. Weather damage stays dry and localized, and will not spread rapidly from pod to pod across your farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli akɛ nɔ ko ni yɛŋ ni tamɔ powda yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni efiteɔ lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ he kome. Ni egbɛ eshwaŋ oya kɛjɛ pod kome mli kɛya pod kroko mli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What brings mirid bugs to my cocoa farm, and how do they harm my trees?
ga: Mɛni kɛ kooloi baa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni te amɛmiiye mi tsei lɛ awui amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Mirids (capsids) prefer unshaded, sunny patches in your farm. They bite into young cocoa shoots and pods to suck out sap, causing the shoots to dry up, turn black, and die.
ga: Mirids (capsids) sumɔɔ hei ni hulu bɛ, ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii koni amɛnu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ, ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the small pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Flower drop happens when trees face stress from dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny insects (midges) in the farm to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I trim off the small extra branches growing out from the trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ kɛjɛ mikoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Those extra shoots, called chupons, suck away food and water that the tree needs to grow pods. Removing them helps the tree focus its energy on producing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons nɛɛ shwieɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: What is the right time of year for me to apply fertilizer to my crop?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer at the start of the rainy season when the soil is damp. The moisture helps the roots absorb the nutrients quickly as the crop begins its major growth cycle.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya be mli ni tsei lɛ jeɔ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: How does spreading dry leaves around my crop roots help them survive the dry season?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he fɛɛ he Te mi tsei lɛ ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves acts like a blanket (mulch). It keeps the soil cool and stops moisture from evaporating quickly during hot weather.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. (Mulch) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to harvest my cocoa pods while they are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ oookpa kookoo ŋmeii be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Unripe green pods contain smaller, underdeveloped beans that will not ferment correctly. This results in bitter cocoa beans that buyers will reject or pay less for.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni edako ni nyɛŋ afee ŋmeii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii eŋɔli ni edako lɛ amli. Enɛ haa anáa kookoo ŋmeii ni mli edɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ baakpoo loo amɛbaawo nyɔmɔ fioo.

english: Why do weeds harm my crop so much even when my cocoa trees are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui waa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikoo tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa moŋ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer and moisture from the top layer of soil that your cocoa roots rely on. Thick weeds also trap moisture around tree bases, encouraging fungal diseases to grow.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni o-cocoa shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he. ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa

english: Is it better for me to grow only one crop like rice or mix different crops on my field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutu mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Growing multiple crops protects your family against market price drops or bad weather; if one crop fails or loses value, the other crop can still provide food and income.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oweku lɛ he kɛjɛɔ jara ni baa shi loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ ahe. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kome fite loo sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hu baanyɛ aha niyenii kɛ shika.

english: Can I use the waste water from my fish pond to irrigate and feed my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu fɔŋ ni jɛɔ loo nubu mli lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni mikɛha amɛ niyenii?

english: Yes, fish pond water is rich in natural fish waste and organic matter, which acts as a gentle, free liquid fertilizer that helps crops grow greener and stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, loo nubu mli nu lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ loo mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nu ni mli jɔ, ni tsofai bɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does my rice crop need more water on the field than my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ he hiaa nu babaoo fe mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice plants are uniquely adapted to thrive in flooded or very wet soil, which suppresses unwanted weeds while supplying the continuous moisture rice needs to form filled grains.
ga: Afee ŋmãa tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa lɛ mli nu be fɛɛ be koni efee ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen fertilizer, or the field has poor water flow which prevents the plant roots from taking up food from the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. aloo ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haaa tsei shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ baai yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is the cassava plant's natural defense to save water during hot periods, allowing the main roots underground to stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛha ŋmei tso lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and small harvests.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa, ni akpaa nii fioo.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with aggressive roots that absorb water and soil food faster than domesticated crops, stealing resources from your plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei. ni oju nibii kɛjɛ otsei lɛ amli

english: Can I put fresh manure from my livestock directly onto my young crop plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi aŋɔli hee awo midumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh manure produces intense heat and chemical activity as it breaks down, which can burn young plant roots; it should be dried or composted before putting it on crops.
ga: Manure hee haa dɔlɛ ni naa wa baa, ni kɛ́ efite lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii yɛ tsofai amli. ni baanyɛ ashã tso shishifãi bibii Esa akɛ agbi loo afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ dani adu.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy enough to grow good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, crumbles easily in your hands, holds water after rain without turning to rock, and contains beneficial insects like earthworms.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ, efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni etsɔɔɔ tɛ. ni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ

english: Why do insect pests attack my vegetable leaves more frequently during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa mi-vegetables baai lɛ shii abɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects look for green crops during dry periods because the juicy leaves are their main source of water and food when wild bushes dry up.
ga: Kplukai taoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai ni mli edɔ lɛ ji nɔ titri ni haa nu kɛ niyenii baa kɛ́ koo mli jwɛi lɛ egbi.

english: Why do I need to crack open hard oil palm seeds before putting them in the nursery bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mu tso dumɔwui ni mli wa lɛ ahe dani madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palm seeds have a thick, hard shell that acts like a lock, stopping water and air from getting inside. Cracking or scarifying the shell helps water reach the seed so it can wake up and sprout much faster.
ga: Mu tso mli yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni wa ni mli tse ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmei. Etsiɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekabote mli. Kɛ́ atse ŋshɔŋ loo akumɔ lɛ, ehaa nu shɛɔ dumɔwu lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya kwraa.

english: Why does my valley rice grow so well in flooded water while my maize rots in the same condition?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nu afua mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni tamɔ nɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have hollow air tubes inside their stems that pump oxygen down to their roots underwater. Maize plants do not have these tubes, so their roots suffocate and rot when trapped in standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi ni mli ewo muji yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛkɛjieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Abɛi tsei bɛ nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ amɛkpɛtɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant cassava stems instead of gathering the seeds from the cassava plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei tsei moŋ fe ŋmei dumɔwui ni wɔbaabua naa lɛ?

english: While cassava plants can produce seeds, plants grown from seeds grow slowly and often give poor tubers. Planting stem cuttings guarantees that you get fast-growing, strong roots that are identical to the healthy mother plant.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei tsei baanyɛ awo dumɔwui moŋ, shi tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ daaa blɛoo ni bei pii lɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni ehiii. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ni ooodu lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ obaaná shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛhe wa tamɔ fɔlɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my packaged maize seeds covered in pink powder, and can I wash it off before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ powda ni ji pinki ehà mi-ŋmãa ni akɛwo kotoku mli lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni ani manyɛ mafo he dani madu?

english: The pink powder is a protective coat of fungicide and insecticide. You should not wash it off because it stops soil insects, worms, and fungi from eating or spoiling the seed before it sprouts.
ga: Pink powder ji nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he, tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Esaaa akɛ okɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ ejaakɛ ehaa kooloi bibii, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ loo amɛfiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants roll up during the hot afternoon even after I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ewo amɛnɔ moŋ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in intense afternoon heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and stop water from evaporating too fast. The leaves will open back up when the temperature cools down.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi, ni ekɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Baai lɛ gbeleɔ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why are the yellow flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers must be pollinated by wind movement or visiting insects to form fruit. If the weather is too hot or humid, or if there are no insects around, the plant drops the unpollinated flowers to conserve its strength.
ga: Esa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii ni baasara amɛ lɛ aha tomato fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa Aloo, kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii bɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi ni shwieee nɔ lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them out in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and keeps the surrounding air moist while the cocoa establishes strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ be mli ni kookoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why should I buy a grafted mango shoot instead of just planting the seed from a sweet mango?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ohe mango ni akɛwo mli lɛ moŋ fe ni oookwɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mango ni ŋɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds from a sweet mango often grow into wild-tasting or sour fruit and take up to seven years to produce. A grafted shoot combines a proven sweet branch with strong roots, giving you high-quality fruit in just a few years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni jɛɔ mango ni ŋɔɔ mli lɛ daa kɛfeɔ citrus loo citrus aduawai. ni ehe afii kpawo ni ekɛfee. Nibii ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛ nibii ni ŋɔɔ ni ana he odaseyeli kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa onáa yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ afii fioo komɛi pɛ mli.

english: Why won't my seed yams sprout immediately if I put them back into moist soil right after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mikɛ amɛ ku sɛɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural rest period called dormancy after harvest. The tuber needs time for its internal chemical triggers to reset before it can start sending out new green shoots for the next season.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Bulb lɛ he miihia be ni amɛkɛto amɛmli tsofai ni haa amɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ ekoŋŋ dani amɛje shishi amɛtsu ŋmeii heei kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why am I supposed to pinch off the small extra shoots growing between the stems of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei akutsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and food away from the main stem and flowers. Removing them forces the plant to send all its nutrients into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of unnecessary leaves.
ga: Nakai tsei krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Tomato ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee tomato ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why do people recommend planting plantains alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ mi-cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings die easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and broad leaves that provide temporary shade to protect the cocoa until it grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running out of nitrogen, which maize needs to grow strong. Adding fertilizer or compost near the base helps restore the plant's green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ fata he ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ su eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which direction I plant cassava stick cuttings in the ground?
ga: Ani miduɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: Yes, the growing buds on the cassava stem must point upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots struggle to grow, resulting in weak plants and fewer tuberous roots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ Shoots lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa akɛ ebaakwɛ̃. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni shishifãi fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do I need to build high soil mounds before planting yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔma gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani wɔdu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow long and thick underground and need soft, loose earth to expand. High mounds give the roots space to grow easily without hitting hard, compact soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni ehe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ haa shishifãi lɛ naa he ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my garden crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps moisture in the soil longer during dry periods, prevents weed growth, and protects plant roots from extreme heat.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi adalɛ naa ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he

english: Why is it good to plant beans or cowpeas on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize removes many nutrients from the soil, but cowpeas naturally trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, restoring soil richness for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi tsina ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Small holes are caused by tiny caterpillars eating the foliage. Spraying natural botanical mixtures like neem leaf extract on the leaves protects them from being eaten.
ga: Buji bibii lɛ jɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli, tamɔ neem baa mli nu lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akaye amɛ.

english: Why do small insects attack my harvested maize when I store it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ kɛ́ mikɛto kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weevils enter stored maize if the grain was not dried completely or if moisture is present in the bags. Thoroughly sun-drying grains until hard prevents these pests from multiplying.
ga: Weevils baabote ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli kɛji ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa loo nu yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛhe baawa koni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafee babaoo.

english: Why does rice grow so well in fields covered with standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu damɔ shi yɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Lowland rice plants have stems that can move air down to their underwater roots, while standing water smothers weeds and supplies the high moisture rice needs to produce heavy grains.
ga: Omɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni he hiaa koni ekɛ ŋmãa ni tsii aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees like plantains nearby, the hot sun scorches their leaves, causing them to dry up and fall off.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ shãa baai lɛ, ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why are the stems of my cocoa trees growing thick swollen bumps?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ efuu ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen stems are a clear sign of the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, a disease spread by tiny insects called mealybugs that weakens and eventually kills the tree if not managed.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu lɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbo kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the base of a maize plant mean it lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. The plant is moving its remaining food to the upper leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ adara waa Tso lɛ miitsi niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛmiiya baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my corn leaves and leaving powdery dirt inside the shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tamɔ powder yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that crawls into the center shoot of young maize to feed on tender leaves and leaves behind its droppings.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest when the tubers are under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready when it reaches 9 to 12 months old, and the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off. You can also carefully dig out a bit of soil near the stem to check tuber size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ ayeɔ kɛji eye nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Obaanyɛ okɛ muji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ hu atsu nii. Kwɛmɔ stem lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ona yitso lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto long wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ akpɛtɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to get maximum sunlight, which helps the leaves make food to grow large tubers underground while keeping leaves off the damp soil to prevent disease.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni baaha ŋmeii wuji lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ koni hela akamɔ bo.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small shoots growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ eje kpo.

english: If too many shoots grow around one tree, they steal water and nutrients from the main stem, resulting in small plantain bunches. Pruning extra shoots ensures larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, tso kome Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii. Kɛ́ afolɔ aduawai lɛ amli krokomɛi lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have small nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when temperatures get extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly flooded, which stresses the plant and prevents fruit from setting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee nu afua ni hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa aduawai lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my crops droop and wilt in the afternoon heat even when it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ moŋ?

english: Plants wilt in the hot sun when water evaporates from their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the ground, especially if the soil lacks compost to retain moisture.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli kɛ́ nu lɛ ho kɛjɛ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do I need to leave space between my cassava sticks when planting them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Giving cassava plants enough space lets their roots spread out freely under the ground to grow big, thick tubers. If they are planted too close together, they will fight for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in very thin roots.
ga: Kɛ́ oha o-cassava tso lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi oya koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ waa.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings need shade trees like plantains planted above them when they are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛyiteŋ beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa trees can survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants turn yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen if heavy rains flood the farm and drown the plant roots, preventing them from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii kɛha tsei ni ehe hiaa ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ ko mli nu ni eha tsei shishifãi lɛ shwie nu mli, ni eha amɛnyɛŋ amɛye nii.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil is rich and healthy enough for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa kɛha okwaayeli?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture well without becoming a swamp, crumbles easily in your hand, and contains earthworms or soft organic matter like decayed leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under the leaves and feed on the plant's juice, or by a virus spread by those same pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ nɔŋŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil becomes too dry, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer in the ground. The plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my farm crops droop and look dead during the hot afternoon heat even if I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo mli po

english: In extreme afternoon heat, leaves lose water faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil. The plant droops on purpose to reduce its exposure to the sun and save water, usually bouncing back by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ shi kɛ yiŋtoo akɛ amɛbaahã hulu la lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu nu he. Bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my main crops after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mitso titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to thrive in harsh conditions. Their roots suck up water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to overpower your farm if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛshwere yɛ shihilɛi ni ehiii amli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji ajieee mra.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start to rot in the barn after just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are cut or bruised during harvest, or if they are stored in a warm room without fresh air flowing around them. Fungi enter through the cuts and spoil the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ mli. Fuji lɛ boteɔ pilamɔi amli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why does my maize spoil or turn moldy after I put it in sacks for storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehiɛɔ beni mikɛwo kotokui amli koni akɛto lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize turns moldy if it is put into sacks before it is completely dry. Moisture trapped inside the grain creates a warm environment where fungi and insects thrive and destroy the crop.
ga: Abɛi baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ akɛwo kotokui amli dani egbi kwraa. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ haa shihilɛ mli dɔɔ. he ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why is it important to clear wild bushes and heavy undergrowth before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ abaajie koo mli jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni adu tsei.

english: Heavy bushes block sunlight, steal nutrients from the soil, and hide pests. Clearing them ensures your young crops get enough light, water, and space to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Ju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni okɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ato Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha otsei bibii lɛ aná la, nu, kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara waa.

english: Why is it so difficult to clear land that has been left overgrown for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa waa akɛ aaajie shikpɔŋ ni ashi ashwie shi be saŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Over time, wild plants develop deep root systems and thick stems that make manual clearing hard. Clearing in stages or using proper tools breaks up tough roots and makes soil preparation much easier.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni mli tse ni haa ewaa akɛ amɛaafee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli loo akɛ nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbala shishifãi ni wa lɛ amli ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ afee mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I let weeds grow up to knee-level around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa jwɛi lɛ daraa kɛyashɛɔ mitsitsi nɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ?

english: Tall weeds act as thieves in your farm. At knee-height, they shade young plants and compete aggressively with your crops for soil nutrients and water, which drastically reduces your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. at knee height Amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛhaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha okpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi waa.

english: Does early morning dew on tall weeds help or harm my crops?
ga: Ani leebi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ jwɛi kakadaji anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: While moisture is necessary, heavy morning dew trapped in thick weeds creates a wet, humid environment that encourages fungal diseases to breed and spread to your crops.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ hulutsoo be he miihia moŋ Shi leebi hulutsoo be ni tsii ni ekpɛtɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛfɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã onibii amli.

english: What is mixed undergrowth, and why would I want specific low plants under my crop canopy?
ga: Mɛni ji tso ni efutu ni mɛni hewɔ tsei kukuji pɛ he hiaa mi yɛ mi ŋwɛitsu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Mixed undergrowth refers to short plants or cover crops growing near the ground. Beneficial cover crops stop bad weeds from taking over, protect soil from erosion, and keep the soil moist during hot seasons.
ga: Mixed plantings tsɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shishi loo tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi gbohii anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ shwiemɔ he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are my crops growing very tall and bushy without producing much food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwooo niyenii babaoo lɛ?

english: When plants get too much shade or lack proper pruning, they spend all their energy growing leaves and tall stems to search for sunlight instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo loo amɛfolɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Akɛ hewalɛ ni haa tsei lɛ daraa kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛtao hulu la moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai.

english: How can I manage land clearing if I have a large acreage but very few farm hands?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ wulu shi ŋmɔtsɛmɛi fioo pɛ?

english: Divide your large land into smaller, manageable blocks and clear them one at a time. This prevents cleared areas from growing back into thick bush before you get the chance to plant.
ga: Jaa oshikpɔŋ wulu lɛ mli owo kui bibii amli. ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ ni ajie blɔki kome yɛ be kome mli Enɛ ji koni akɛtsi he ni ajie lɛ lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ jwɛi ni mli edɔ dani oná hegbɛ ni okɛdu nii.

english: What happens to my seeds if I plant them directly into soil full of old roots?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni shishifãi momoi eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Seeds need loose soil to push their young roots through. Planting in root-filled soil prevents proper root growth, making your crops weak and easy to dry out.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse koni amɛtsi shishifãi bibii lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shishifãi eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ gbɔjɔmɔ ni egbiɔ oya.

english: How do I clear weeds around my crops without damaging the roots near the surface?
ga: Majie jwɛi kɛjɛ he ni ebɔle he lɛ. Te ooofee tɛŋŋ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni ofiteee shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ?

english: Use shallow weeding techniques with a light hoe or pull weeds by hand around the base of the plant. Deep digging too close to the stem cuts important feeding roots.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ gbɛ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛtsɔ ŋmei ni mli ejɔ loo jwɛi ni okɛ onine gbala kɛbɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ atsa shi ni ebɛŋkɛ tso lɛ he tsɔ lɛ, ebaafo shishifãi ni he hiaa ni haa niyenii lɛ.

english: Why do some of my young plants fail to stand upright and end up falling over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ adamɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ?

english: Plants fall over when their stems are too thin from overcrowded planting or lack of sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant grows a thick stem that can support its own weight.
ga: Tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shishi lɛ bafee mlɛo tsɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni ebɔle ehe tsɔ loo hulu la ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa tso ni mli tse ni baanyɛ akwɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsitsinɔnii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and space to grow strong stalks and larger, healthier ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii toi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn under intense direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow even though there has been plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Heavy rain can wash nutrients away, so the plant needs compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer to rebuild its green color and fuel growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ koni amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ fuel lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with many leaves, but the tubers underneath are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi yitso lɛ ji bibioo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is heavily fertilized at the wrong time, the cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves and stems instead of storing food down in the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Is it better for my soil if I clear my farmland by burning the dry bush?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni mashã lɛ jie ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Burning may seem fast, but intense heat destroys the rich organic matter and beneficial organisms in the soil. Clearing without burning allows dead leaves to rot naturally, which enriches the soil and retains moisture.
ga: Ekolɛ ebaafee tamɔ nɔ ni shãa oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ni ashãaa lɛ, ebaaha baai ni egboi lɛ afite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa sũ lɛ he feɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called black pod, which thrives in cool, damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excess leaves lets sunlight and fresh air into the farm to stop the dampness that spreads the disease.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛshwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afo baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛtsi hulutsoo ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after I clear the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are native, highly adapted wild plants designed to survive harsh conditions, whereas crop seeds take longer to establish. Clearing weeds early before they drop seed prevents them from multiplying rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe waa. Afee lɛ koni ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Dani amɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ haaa amɛshwere oya.

english: Why are the blossoms dropping off my tomato plants without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or inconsistent watering stresses the tomato plant, causing it to drop flowers to protect itself. Regular watering at the base of the plant during hot spells helps flowers stay attached and turn into fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Ha egbee shi koni ebu ehe. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and curl during the afternoon sun even when the soil feels damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than the roots can pull it from the soil. The plant curls its leaves temporarily to save moisture, usually bouncing back once the evening cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baafolɔ baai lɛ be kukuoo ko koni ekɛto ŋmɔtɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji edɔ.

english: Why does my harvested corn get eaten by small insects while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ye mi-ŋma ni mikpa lɛ beni akɛtoɔ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize weevils lay eggs inside grain kernels while crops are still in the field or in uncleaned stores. Thoroughly drying corn in the sun until hard and storing it in sealed, airtight bags smothers insect pests before they multiply.
ga: Abɛi ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmaa mli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni he tseee mli lolo loo yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulu mli kɛyashi ewa ni akɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum efo mli lɛ amli lɛ, egbeɔ ŋmãa dani amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why does the fertilizer I applied sit on top of the dry soil without helping my crops grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ taraa shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni eyeee ebuaaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer nutrients are locked inside dry granules and cannot do anything on their own. Water is needed to touch the fertilizer and start the reaction that dissolves the nutrients so your crop roots can absorb them.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ehi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ amli, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee nɔ ko. Nu he miihia koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɔ ni ebɔi nifeemɔ ko ni baaha niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ aje shishi koni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Will fertilizer work on my maize farm if I apply it during a dry spell without watering?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mikɛwo mli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni mikɛ nu wooo mli?

english: No, fertilizer stays inactive on dry ground. The nutrients inside the fertilizer only unlock and start working when moisture touches the granules to dissolve them into the soil.
ga: Dabi, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Agbeleɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ naa ni etsuɔ ​​nii kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔi lɛ kpe koni etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers tell us that water 'activates' crop fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ nu ‘haa’ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Water acts like a key for fertilizer. When water touches dry fertilizer, it triggers a reaction that dissolves the solid nutrients so they can move into the soil where plant roots can drink them.
ga: Nu tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ titri ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli. Kɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ kpe Enɛ haa nɔ ko ni haa niyenii mli nibii ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ anu amɛ yɛ lɛ baa.

english: How do my plant roots actually drink in the solid fertilizer granules I spread on my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni mikɛshwãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plant roots cannot feed on solid granules directly. Water must first melt the granules, dissolving the nutrients into liquid form in the soil so the roots can take them in.
ga: Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aye ŋmeii ni wa tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ nu ajie tsofai lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ nu mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. koni shishifãi lɛ abote mli

english: Does fertilizer lose its power or spoil if I leave it sealed in a dry bag for a long time?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli loo ebaafite kɛji mikɛwo kotoku ni egbi mli be kakadaŋŋ?

english: No, dry fertilizer remains completely stable inside a sealed bag because there is no reaction taking place. As long as it is kept away from water, the nutrients stay safely stored inside until you are ready to use it.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ baahi shi kwraa yɛ kotoku ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli. Ejaakɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko baaa Shii abɔ ni akɛto he kɛjɛ nu he lɛ. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baahi mli shweshweeshwe kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ okɛbaatsu nii.

english: Is it fine to keep my bags of fertilizer outside where rain might touch them before planting season?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kotokui ato kpo nɔ yɛ he ko ni nugbɔ baanyɛ anɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ aba?

english: No, you must keep fertilizer dry. Water causes the nutrients inside the bag to react and dissolve early, which means the plant food will wash away before it ever reaches your farm.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ oha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi. Nu lɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni egbɛɔ oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, tsei aniyenii lɛ hoɔ dani eshɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why did my leftover fertilizer turn into hard, sticky lumps inside the sack after the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ kotokui amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Moisture from the rain or damp air got inside the sack and touched the fertilizer. Water starts the reaction that dissolves the nutrients, and when it dries up again, the granules stick together into hard lumps.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni jɛɔ nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ mli lɛ boteɔ kotoku lɛ mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpeɔ. Nu jeɔ nifeemɔ ko shishi ni haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii shwieɔ shi. Ni kɛ́ egbi ekoŋŋ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baakpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why is it best for me to apply fertilizer to my crops right before or after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ anɛ loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires water to start releasing its nutrients. Applying it when the soil is wet from rain ensures the chemical reaction begins immediately, giving your crops quick access to the nutrients.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛje niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ ajiemɔ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tsofa lɛ tsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya.

english: What happens to the fertilizer nutrients if I dissolve the solid granules in a bucket of water before putting it on my crops?
ga: Mɛni baa niyenii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa lɛ wo nu baagi mli dani mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Mixing the fertilizer with water starts the reaction right away, breaking down the solid granules and releasing the nutrients directly into the water so your crops can absorb them immediately.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu nu mli lɛ, ejeɔ nifeemɔ lɛ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Efoɔ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ amli ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛyaa nu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. koni ŋmɔshi nibii anyɛ aŋɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: Why shouldn't I spread dry fertilizer on my farm during the hottest part of a sunny day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Without moisture in the soil, the dry fertilizer will just sit there without reacting or feeding your crops, and extreme sun can cause some of the nutrients to waste away before rain falls to activate them.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ baata jɛmɛ kɛkɛ ni efeee nɔ ko loo ekɛ niyenii haaa onibii lɛ. Ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ niyenii lɛ ekomɛi dani nugbɔ lɛ aba koni ekanya amɛnitsumɔ lɛ.

english: Can I harvest leaves from my yam plants, or will cutting them damage the crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo baai kɛjɛ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ amli? Aloo kɛ́ afo lɛ, ebaafite tso lɛ?

english: You can harvest leaves from yam plants without killing them. A healthy yam plant produces strong foliage early on, allowing you to harvest leaves while leaving the plant able to grow again.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa baai kɛjɛ sweet potato tsei amli ni ogbeee amɛ. Sweet potato tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baawo tsei ni mli wa mra. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa baai lɛ yɛ be mli ni ohaa tso lɛ daa ekoŋŋ.

english: How soon after planting yams can I start gathering the leaves?
ga: Beni adu sweet potato sɛɛ lɛ Etsɛ tɛŋŋ mabɔi baai lɛ anaabuamɔ?

english: You can begin harvesting yam leaves about three months after planting, which is when the plant has produced enough lush leaves for harvesting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oje sweet potato baai lɛ akpamɔ shishi aaafee nyɔji etɛ sɛɛ beni odu lɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei lɛ náa baai eŋɔli ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaakpa.

english: How many leaves can I expect to collect from a single yam plant?
ga: Baai enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ sweet potato tso kome mli?

english: From one healthy yam plant, you can harvest around 250 leaves within the first three months of growth.
ga: Kɛjɛ sweet potato tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli Obaanyɛ okpa baai aaafee 250 yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ ni ekɛdara lɛ mli.

english: Do I need to dig up the whole yam root if I only want to harvest the leaves?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni mahi baai lɛ pɛ mli lɛ, ani esa akɛ mafo shishifã lɛ fɛɛ?

english: No, you do not need to disturb the root. You only cut the leaves and stems above the ground, which allows the root underground to stay safe and continue supporting the plant.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni ogbala shishifãi lɛ amli. Ehe miihia ni ofolɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: If I cut my plant stem right down near the soil, will it grow back?
ga: Kɛji ofo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ni obɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Ani ebaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, many crops will sprout again after being cut at the base. As long as the root system remains healthy underground, the plant will push up fresh new shoots.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ beni afo amɛ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Shii abɔ ni shishifãi lɛ mli wa lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Tso lɛ baatsi ŋmeii heei kɛje kpo.

english: Where is the best place on the plant stem to cut when I want to encourage new growth?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafolɔ tsei lɛ ahe beni miisumɔ ni miwo dalɛ hee he hewalɛ?

english: You should cut the stem low down near its base and remove the top part. This allows the plant's roots to direct energy into sprouting clean new stems.
ga: Esa akɛ ofo tso lɛ shishi ni obɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ojie ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni he tse.

english: How long does it take for a plant to grow back after I cut it down to the base?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani tso ko kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ beni mifo lɛ kɛyashi eshishigbɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It typically takes about three months for the plant to sprout back up and produce a fresh set of leaves ready for another harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ dani tso lɛ daa ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ baai heei krokomɛi ni asaa he kɛha kpamɔ lɛ baa.

english: Do I need to plant new seeds every time I harvest my leafy crops?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni madu dumɔwui heei be fɛɛ be ni makpa tso ni yɔɔ baai lɛ?

english: No, you do not always need to plant new seeds. Certain crops can be cut down to the base and will naturally sprout again from the existing root system.
ga: Dabi, jeee be fɛɛ be ehe baahia ni odu dumɔwui heei. Abaanyɛ afo tsei komɛi kɛyashi amɛshishigbɛ. ni ebaada yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛjɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ momo lɛ amli.

english: What should I do with the stems and tops I cut off during harvesting?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ tsei kɛ ŋmeii ni afo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: You can place the cut plant material back on the soil around your crop. It acts as mulch, breaking down over time to enrich the soil and protect the new sprouts.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tso nibii ni afo lɛ aku sɛɛ awo sũ ni ebɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebu dumɔwui heei ahe.

english: Why does cutting off the top of a crop help it produce more leaves later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ko yiteŋ ni aaafo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehaa baai babaoo shwereɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Removing the old top growth encourages the plant to trigger new shoots from the base, resulting in a fresh and abundant cycle of leaf growth.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii momoi lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛjɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛ haa baai heei ni fa babaoo lɛ daa.

english: Is it better to buy packaged hybrid maize seeds or can I just replant seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛwo kotoku mli loo manyɛ madu dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Packaged certified hybrid seeds are bred to give much higher yields and resist local diseases, whereas saved seeds lose their strength over generations and produce smaller cobs.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwo kotoku mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ewo mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshi helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: How far apart should I space my maize seeds when I am sowing them in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ abɔ he shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ miidu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting maize about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between plants ensures each stalk gets enough sunlight, water, and nutrients without crowding out its neighbors.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ aaafee sɛntimita 75 yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ kɛ sɛntimita 40 yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni akutsoŋbii lɛ kɛ amɛhe wooo mli

english: When is the best time at the start of the rainy season for me to plant my maize?
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa?

english: Maize should be planted right after the first few steady rains arrive so the soil has enough moisture for the seeds to germinate without drying out or getting washed away.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ bei fioo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ loo amɛhooo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen fertilizer or that heavy rains have waterlogged the soil, preventing the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia oŋmɔshi nibii loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce bushy flowers at the very top before any cobs appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Those top flowers are called tassels, and they drop pollen that the wind carries to the silky threads on the lower cobs so that kernels can form.
ga: Atsɛɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ nakai tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ akɛ tassels. Ni amɛshwieɔ ŋmeii ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ woɔ lɛ amɛshwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ anɔ koni dumɔwui anyɛ afee.

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over easily when a strong rain or wind hits the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ba ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize stalks collapse when their root systems are weak, which happens if seeds are planted too shallowly, planted too close together, or lack proper soil support.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. ni adu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni sa ni fiɔ sɛɛ ni bɛ

english: Why do some of my harvested maize cobs have missing seeds at the very tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii yɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Empty cob tips happen when the crop suffers from heat or dry spells during the flowering stage, which prevents full pollination across all the silks.
ga: Bare cob ends baa kɛji tso lɛ kɛ ehe wo latsaa loo hɔmɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ haaa pollination eyi siliki kpãai lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant leguminous crops like cowpeas alongside my main crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa yɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛtsuɔ nii waa lɛ masɛi?

english: Legumes pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds your maize and keeps the farm soil healthy.
ga: Legumes gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa o-ŋmei lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat hole marks into the funnels of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that burrows into the growing center of maize plants and eats the fresh leaves if they are not sprayed or treated early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ mli ni eyeɔ baai heei kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ amɛ tsofa loo atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds while my crop plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops grow slowly at first, so weeds will quickly steal the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your main crop needs to establish strong roots.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa tso ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ he hiaa koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃ lɛ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli.

english: Is it better for me to start farming on a small piece of land before expanding to a full acre?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaaje ŋmɔ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ? Dani ebaagbɛ eshwa kɛyashɛ acreage muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Starting with a small plot lets you learn how the crop behaves, manage pests easily, and care for the plants properly without getting overwhelmed. Once you master a small area, expanding becomes easier and more successful.
ga: Kɛje shishi kɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko Ebaaye ebua bo ni okase bɔ ni tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa. Kwɛmɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ ni okwɛ tso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ohe akawo mli. Kɛji oye he bibioo ko jogbaŋŋ lɛ, shweremɔ bafeɔ mlɛo ni eyeɔ omanye.

english: Why do my maize plants grow so thin and produce small ears when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ toi bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Giving each plant proper space allows it to get enough nutrients to grow strong and yield full, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda waa ni ewo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How deep into the soil should I push my seeds when I am planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Seeds buried too deep will run out of energy before reaching sunlight, while seeds planted too shallow can dry out or be eaten by birds. Planting at a depth about two to three times the size of the seed gives them the best chance to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ hewalɛ baaho dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbi loo okpoi aye amɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee dumɔwu lɛ dalɛ toi 2-3 lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up when I clear all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi be mli ni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves that easily burn under strong, direct sunlight. Taller shade trees protect young cocoa from harsh sun and keep the moisture in the soil, helping the seedlings survive their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and dry out so quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During hot weather, water evaporates rapidly from both the plant's leaves and the surrounding dirt. Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves or grass keeps the soil cool and retains moisture longer.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ baai kɛ muji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fɛɛ mli. Mulching around Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller harvests every year when I keep planting maize in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Maize continuously drains specific nutrients from the ground every season. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores vital nutrients to the soil, keeping it healthy for future crops.
ga: Abɛi yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop to the ground and rot after they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni amɛbɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Tomato stems are often too weak to carry the weight of heavy, ripening fruit. Tying the plants to wooden stakes keeps the leaves and fruits off the damp ground, protecting them from rot and diseases.
