ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye aduawai ni tsii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ fĩ tso ko he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa kɛ aduawai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafite kɛ helai srɔtoi.

english: Why should I pinch off the extra small branches growing on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji bibii lɛ? Ajie nɔ ni yaa hiɛ babaoo yɛ mi tomato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Removing extra side branches allows the plant to redirect its water and food toward developing bigger, healthier fruits instead of wasting energy on excess leaves.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii lɛ yaa yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why is it better for me to start my pepper seeds in a nursery bed before moving them into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young pepper sprouts are extremely delicate and vulnerable to heat and pests. A nursery allows you to give tender seedlings extra care and protection until they grow strong enough to handle the main field.
ga: Pepper bibii lɛ he waaa waa, ni hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya. Nurseries lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni obuɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ he titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny holes suddenly appearing on the leaves of my young cabbage crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii miije kpo trukaa yɛ mi-cabbage tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Small holes are typically caused by young caterpillars or beetles eating the soft leaves. Spotting this early allows you to deal with the pests before they destroy the growing center of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa. Enɛ ni oookadi mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsuɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nii dani amɛfiteɔ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: How do I know the right amount of chemical to mix with water so I do not hurt my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofai ni sa ni akɛfutuɔ nu lɛ? Bɔni afee ni mikaye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui.

english: Every crop chemical comes with specific mixing rules; using too much chemical can burn and damage tender crop leaves, while using too little will not control the pests or diseases effectively.
ga: Tsofa fɛɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emlai ni kɔɔ bɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ahaa lɛ he. Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã ni efite. Yɛ be mli ni akɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, enyɛŋ eye tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the purpose of the small nozzle or tip at the end of my knapsack sprayer?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo ni yɔɔ nozzle bibioo loo tip ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii amli lɛ naagbee lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The nozzle tip breaks liquid chemical into a fine mist, allowing it to spread evenly over all the crop leaves without dripping off onto the ground and wasting money.
ga: Nozzle lɛ naa lɛ gbáa tsofa ni ji nu lɛ mli ni etsɔɔ afua bibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ekɛ ehe wooo shikpɔŋ ni efiteee shika.

english: What happens to the medicine I spray on my crops if it rains right after application?
ga: Mɛni baa tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ beni mikɛshwie nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rain washes the chemical off the plant leaves before the leaves can absorb it or before pests touch it, which makes the treatment useless and requires re-application after the rain stops.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ ahe dani baai lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ loo dani tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe aba. Enɛ haa tsofa lɛ he ehiaaa, ni esa akɛ akɛtsu nii ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ekpa.

english: When is the best time during the day for me to spray my farm with pest medicine?
ga: Mɛɛ gbi mli be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is ideal because high afternoon heat causes the chemical to evaporate too quickly and can scorch delicate leaves.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli Enɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ shwane mli latsaa lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do pests keep attacking my crops even after I have already sprayed the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa efɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Pests often hide on the undersides of leaves or inside stem joints; if the spray misses those specific spots, the pests will survive and continue damaging the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ashishi loo yɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shɛɛɛ nakai hei pɔtɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baahi shi ni amɛya nɔ amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often indicate a lack of soil nutrients, root damage, or fungal diseases like black pod, which require specific targeted treatments to stop from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. shishifãi ni efite loo ŋmeii helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji, ni biɔ ni akɛ tsofa awo he koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: How often should I apply pest medicine to my vegetable farm to keep it safe?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii yɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mahi shi shweshweeshwe?

english: Spraying frequency depends on the crop and pest type, but repeating applications every 14 to 21 days helps catch newly hatched insects that survived the initial treatment.
ga: Bɔ ni afɔɔ tsofa lɛ afɔ̃ɔ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ henɔ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ tsu nii shii abɔ daa gbii 14 kɛyashi 21 lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɔmɔ kooloi ni efɔ ehee ni ye wala yɛ shishijee tsofafeemɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Can I spray pest medicine directly onto the tender young shoots and flowers of my plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Young shoots and flowers are sensitive, so using a spray nozzle that is too close or a mixture that is too strong can burn them, preventing pods or fruit from growing.
ga: Tsobii bibii kɛ fɔfɔi ni nuɔ he No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ loo nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni mli wa tsɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã amɛ. Enɛ haa pod loo aduawai lɛ daaa.

english: Is it better to pour liquid fertilizer directly at the roots or spray it on the leaves?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii awo shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo oookɛshwie baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Leaf spraying works faster for urgent nutrient deficiency, while applying treatments to the root zone allows the plant to absorb nutrients steadily over a longer period.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baatsu nii oya kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ he ehiaaa oya. Yɛ be mli ni akɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tsofa lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ tsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly after I spray them with weedkiller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Some weedkillers only dry out the top leaves while leaving the underground roots healthy, allowing the weed to sprout again shortly after spraying.
ga: Tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ gĩɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshiɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ha jwɛi lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ yɛ be mli ni okɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as the plant's main food for leaf growth. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant the nourishment it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same plot of land three seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ bei etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the earth. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil and starves out pests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear away all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under full sunlight and heat. Keeping taller shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa protects the young plants from harsh sun and helps the soil stay moist until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ latsaa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ni aaaha amɛkwɛ loo dumɔwui ni adu yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around their vegetable beds with dry grass during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai aŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like an umbrella for the soil. It stops the sun from drying out the ground too quickly, keeps the roots cool, and reduces the amount of water you need to give your plants.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu ni he hiaa bo ni okɛhaa otsei lɛ anɔ nu lɛ baa shi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves wide in the sunlight to produce energy. Raising the leaves off the ground with stakes allows the plant to catch maximum sunlight, which travels down to make the underground yam tuber grow big and heavy.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli babaoo yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ adara ni amɛtsii.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small plantain shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mitso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: If too many small shoots grow around the main stem, they steal water, light, and nutrients from the parent plant. Keeping only one or two strong shoots ensures the main stem gets enough food to grow a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdumɔwui wuji ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are my tomato plant flowers falling off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences water stress. If the soil gets completely dry while flowering, the plant drops its flowers to save water for its own survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto nu kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshihilɛ.

english: Why do tiny insects swarm my cowpea plants as soon as the flowers start opening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛbɔi fɔmɔ pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar that naturally attracts pests like thrips and beetles. These insects feed on the flowers, damaging them before they can form healthy seed pods, which is why monitoring plants at the flowering stage is critical.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ nu ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ gbalaa kooloi tamɔ thrips kɛ ladybugs. Kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ fɔfɔi. Feemɔ nibii ni efite lɛ dani amɛfee dumɔwui akui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ tsei anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips hiding underneath the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. As the insects suck the plant juice, the leaves deform and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ amli be mli ni kooloi bibii lɛ nuɔ tso mli nu lɛ Baai lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when the rain is very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When fields remain flooded for too long, water displaces the air in the soil, suffocating the roots and causing rot-causing fungi to multiply rapidly.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ nu eyi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo oya.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of small flowers, but only a small percentage (around 2% to 5%) get pollinated by tiny insects called midges. Unpollinated flowers naturally drop off the tree after a day or two.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ (aaafee 2% kɛyashi 5%) ji nɔ ni ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ amɛmli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ baagbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ sɛɛ.

english: How do cocoa flowers actually turn into full cocoa pods?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni eyi obɔ?

english: Tiny insects called midges carry pollen from one cocoa flower to another. Once pollinated, the flower drops its petals, and the base swells slowly over five to six months into a mature cocoa pod.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ woɔ muji kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Kɛji akɛ pollinated lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. ni shishigbɛ lɛ baafu fiofio nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni eda kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees bloom heavily right after the rains start in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ Ghana amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowering is triggered by changes in weather. The return of soil moisture and higher humidity after a dry season signals to the tree that it has enough water and energy to produce flowers.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ kookoo fɔfɔi baa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa ekoŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ yɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do some of my cocoa flowers dry up and die before developing at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ ekomɛi gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers dry up when the tree lacks adequate water, when there is extreme heat without shade, or when pest attacks and poor soil nutrients prevent the flower from retaining moisture.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tso lɛ he. Be mli ni edɔ waa ni hulutsoo be bɛ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua amɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni esaaa lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why are some of the cocoa pods on my tree very small while others are large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii komɛi ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji bibii waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu dara lɛ?

english: Pod size depends on pollination quality, water availability, and nutrient distribution. If a flower receives plenty of pollen and the tree gets good water and soil nutrients, the pod grows larger. Trees with too many pods may also produce smaller pods due to nutrient competition.
ga: Pod dalɛ damɔ pollination kpakpa nɔ. nu ni yɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ mlijaa Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ ná pollen babaoo ni tsei lɛ ná nu kpakpa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai. Pod lɛ baafee agbo. Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ hu baanyɛ agbɔjɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋshii hewɔ.

english: Why do tiny cocoa pods sometimes turn black and shrivel up while still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Bei komɛi lɛ amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: This is often caused by 'cherelle wilt,' a natural mechanism where the tree thins out excess pods it cannot support. However, it can also be caused by fungal infections like Black Pod disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ‘cherelle wilt’, ni ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shi kɛlɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela hu baanyɛ ekɛba.

english: Why do cocoa pods grow directly on the thick trunk of the tree instead of just the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei akutsei ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally flower and fruit on their main trunks and older woody branches—a trait called cauliflory. This helps the tree support heavy pods and makes flowers accessible to ground-dwelling pollinating midges.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ amɛtso wulu lɛ kɛ amɛniji ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ cauliflower Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ fɔfɔi ni tsii lɛ anɔ, ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛha ŋmeii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa pods change color from green or red to yellow or orange?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu mli lɛ?

english: The color change is the plant's natural sign of maturity. As the seeds inside fully develop and accumulate sugars, the outer husk loses chlorophyll and turns yellow or orange to indicate it is ready for harvesting.
ga: Su tsakemɔ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miida. Beni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ daraa ni amɛbua sugar naa kɛyashɛɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Klorofil ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ he kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Will leaving small or damaged pods on my cocoa trees affect the next flower bloom?
ga: ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ Aloo ŋmɔtɔ ni efite ni eshwɛ yɛ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baaná fɔfɔi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, leaving old or unhealthy pods on the tree wastes nutrients that the tree could use to nourish new flowers. Damaged pods can also harbor diseases that spread to new flowers and healthy pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni egbɔ loo ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii ni ekɛha fɔfɔi heei lɛ aya hiɛ. Pods ni efite lɛ hu baanyɛ ahiɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa fɔfɔi heei kɛ pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why does my cocoa farm yield fewer pods in some years compared to others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo yɛ afii komɛi amli fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Cocoa yields fluctuate based on rainfall patterns, soil fertility, pest populations, and tree fatigue. A tree that produces a massive crop one year often needs time and nutrients to rebuild its energy for future seasons.
ga: Cocoa feemɔ tsakeɔ yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ naa. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe tɔlɛ Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni woɔ ŋmaa babaoo yɛ afi kome mli lɛ he hiaa be kɛ niyenii koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ hee kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and produce food, so when there is not enough in the soil, the plant pulls it from older bottom leaves to feed the younger top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa Tso lɛ gbalaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the bottom tips of my sweet peppers turn black and soft while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell peppers lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit. It usually happens when watering is inconsistent, which prevents the roots from taking up calcium evenly from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from intense heat and bright sunlight. Closing up reduces leaf surface area, which helps the plant save water and prevent drying out during the hottest hours.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛ́ agbe baa lɛ hiɛ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ hiɛ he lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when humidity is extremely low or high. Extreme weather stresses the plant and prevents proper pollination, causing the flowers to fall off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi tsɔ loo eshɛ tsɔ. Kɔɔyɔŋ shihilɛi ni mli wa waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni etsĩɔ pollination ni sa naa. ha fɔfɔii agbo

english: Why does covering the soil around my cassava plants with dry grass keep them healthier in dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass acts as mulch, which traps moisture in the ground, lowers soil temperature, and prevents weed growth, allowing your plants to access water longer during dry spells.
ga: Mulch ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch ni mɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ aba shi ni otsi jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛnáa nu be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning completely black and hard while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛhe wa be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Removing infected pods and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm and keeps the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How do I know if the chemical spray I use on my cabbage will make consumers sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-cabbage lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ aná hela?

english: Every farm chemical has a required waiting period between spraying and harvesting, called a pre-harvest interval. If you wait the specified number of days before picking the crop, the chemical breaks down and the food becomes safe to eat.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ ni amɛmɛ be yɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ teŋ. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ be ni tsɔ nikpamɔ hiɛ lɛ. Kɛji omɛ gbii ayibɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ dani okpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Tsofai lɛ baafite ni niyenii lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ayeɔ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning dark brown and spoiling after just two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots undergo rapid post-harvest deterioration as soon as they are cut from the plant and exposed to air. Storing them carefully or processing them into gari or flour quickly prevents this rapid spoilage.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli ni ajie amɛ awo kɔɔyɔɔ mli pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛto he jogbaŋŋ loo akɛfee gari loo ashikishaŋ oya lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ fitemɔ oya nɛɛ naa.

english: Why does my yam tuber start growing green sprouts in the barn even though it is not in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? No bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yam tubers are living plant stems that enter a natural resting period after harvest. Once this internal rest period ends, warmer temperatures signal to the yam that it is time to grow a new plant, causing sprouts to form.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli ni boteɔ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ mligbɛ hejɔɔmɔ be nɛɛ ba naagbee lɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu tsei heei. ni baaha ekwɛ̃

english: Will picking my tomatoes early while they are still hard green stop them from going bad before reaching the market?
ga: Mi-tomato lɛ ni mifoɔ mra Be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa lolo lɛ, ani ehi akɛ makpa tomato lɛ dani amɛyashɛ jara nɔ?

english: Harvesting at the mature green stage helps fruit survive long transport without getting crushed, but picking them too early before they mature prevents them from developing good color, full flavor, and proper nutritional quality.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa aduawai lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdara lɛ, ehaa anyɛɔ akɛyaa he kroko be kakadaŋŋ ni akumɔɔɔ amɛ. Shi kɛ́ otsi amɛ mra tsɔ dani amɛdara lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaná su kpakpa. ŋmɔlɔ ni eyi obɔ ni eyɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa

english: Why are my old coconut trees turning yellow and dying all of a sudden?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tso momo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Older coconut varieties in Ghana are very vulnerable to diseases like Lethal Yellowing. When the disease infects the tree, it blocks the movement of water and nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow and the tree to die.
ga: Helai tamɔ baa ni gbeɔ mɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ henɔi ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ waa. Kɛ helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ba tsei anɔ lɛ Etsĩɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ gbɛfaa naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: What causes disease to spread so fast across an entire coconut farm?
ga: Mɛni ha hela lɛ gbɛ eshwã oyayaayai yɛ akokoso ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Diseases often spread through insects that fly from tree to tree. If all the trees on your farm are the same older variety without natural defense, the disease moves quickly from one tree to the next.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ koolooi ni foɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji tsei srɔtoi ni etsɛ ni adebɔɔ mli hebuu ko bɛ he. Hela lɛ yaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko mli.

english: Why do some trees on my farm stay healthy while others right next to them dry up and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmasɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Trees can have slight differences in root strength or natural hardiness. A tree with stronger roots or a slightly different genetic makeup can resist soil stress and early infection longer than its neighbor.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ afee srɔtoi fioo yɛ amɛshishifãi ahewalɛ loo amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ mli. Tsei ni shishifãi ni wa loo amɛfɔmɔ nii ni yɔɔ srɔto fioo lɛ baanyɛ adamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ haomɔ kɛ helai ni baa mra lɛ anaa be kakadaŋŋ fe tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer tells me to plant a 'resistant variety'?
ga: Beni mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ bo akɛ odu Mɛni ‘resistant variety’ tsɔɔ?

english: A resistant variety is a plant specially bred to fight off specific diseases that easily kill older crops, allowing your farm to survive outbreaks and produce fruit for many years.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai lɛ ji tsei ni atsɔse amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛkɛwu amɛshi helai komɛi ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etsɛ waa lɛ. Ye obua oŋmɔ lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ helai ni baa lɛ amli ni ewo yibii afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just plant seeds from the old coconut trees my grandfather planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tso momo ko ni mitsɛkwɛ̃ du lɛ mli?

english: Older traditional varieties carry genetic weaknesses against diseases circulating today. Even if the original tree survived, seeds taken from it will likely produce trees that die easily when exposed to current farm diseases.
ga: Kooloi ni edara, ni ji kusum mli kooloi babaoo lɛ ji mɛi ni helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɛnɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ yɛ amɛfɔmɔ su mli. Kɛji akɛ shishijee tso lɛ hi shi po Shi dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ hu baanyɛ agbe tsei lɛ waa kɛ́ helai ba amɛnɔ yɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Is it better to plant local traditional seeds or the new hybrid seedlings from the ministry?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu shishijee dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli loo dumɔwui heei ni akɛfutu mli kɛjɛ sɔɔmɔ nitsumɔ lɛ mli?

english: Hybrid seedlings are tested to resist common local diseases and usually produce fruit much faster and in larger quantities than traditional local seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee tsofa kroko lɛ mli koni ana kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. ni bei pii lɛ ewoɔ yibii oya kwraa kɛ babaoo fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ.

english: How can I be sure that the seedlings I am buying will actually survive local tree diseases?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ baaje maŋ lɛ mli tsei ahe helai amli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You cannot tell just by looking at a young plant. You should buy seedlings from certified government agricultural centers or recognized extension agents who can guarantee the variety's origin.
ga: Onyɛŋ ole kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui kɛjɛ maŋ nɔyeli okwaayeli he ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo mɔ ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ ni baanyɛ ama nɔ mi akɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ jɛ.

english: Can I grow cocoa trees together with coconut trees on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu kookoo tsei kɛ ŋmei tsei yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, planting cocoa under tall coconut trees works well because the coconut palms provide the partial shade young cocoa plants need to survive direct sunlight while maximizing your space.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kookoo ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei kakadaji ashishi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ haa ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo be fã ko ni he hiaa koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, yɛ be mli ni amɛkɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my coconut trees produce fewer and smaller fruits as they get older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tso lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ni ewoɔ bibii beni edaa lɛ?

english: As palm trees age, their root systems become less efficient at pulling nutrients out of the soil, and older varieties naturally lose their vigor over time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ dara lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ jiemɔ mli kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: If my harvest is too small for buyers, is it safe to buy produce from neighboring farms to add to mine?
ga: Kɛji mikpamɔ lɛ faaa tsɔ kɛha hɔlɔ lɛ Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahe nibii ni jɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli koni mikɛfata shika tsuru ŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: It helps you meet buyer demand, but you must be careful. Crops bought from other farms might come from diseased trees or poor varieties, which can lower the overall quality of what you sell.
ga: Eyeɔ ebua bo ni otsuɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ahiamɔ nii ahe nii. Shi esa akɛ okwɛ ohe nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji krokomɛi amli lɛ baanyɛ ajɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ loo tsei srɔtoi ni ehiii lɛ amli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha nɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli aba shi.

english: Young cocoa plants are like baby plants that cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Leaving big trees or planting fast-growing plantains gives them living shade, protecting their delicate leaves until they grow strong enough to withstand the heat.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii tamɔ tsei bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei wuji ni aaashi loo plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ adumɔ baaha hulutsoo aba. Ebuɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo lɛ naa.

english: Why do my young maize plants turn yellow and stay small even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛji bibii lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer early gives the crop the energy it needs to grow tall and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baawo mli mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings fall over and die at the soil line right after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛje kpo lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil is kept too wet, allowing tiny fungi to attack the soft stems of baby plants. Keeping the soil moist but not soaked helps the stem stay firm and healthy as it grows.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Ha ŋmɔtɔ bibioo lɛ Tutua tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi ehiɛ edɔɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhe wa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and light when I plant the cuttings very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ, be mli ni adu tsei lɛ aniji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close, the roots fight each other under the ground for nutrients, water, and space. Giving each plant enough space allows the roots room to expand and store energy, creating large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ he ko. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni amɛtoɔ hewalɛ. ni kɛ yitso agbo baa

english: What happens to my farm soil when I plant cowpeas alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmãa masɛi?

english: Cowpeas feed the soil by taking nitrogen from the air and storing it in their roots. When grown with maize, cowpeas naturally share this soil food, helping the maize grow better without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ, Cowpeas kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni edaa jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmãa ni jara wa tsuuu nii.

english: How do weeds actually slow down the growth of my yam vines?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ aya hiɛ fioo eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal light, water, and soil nutrients meant for your crop. Clearing weeds early ensures your yam vines get all the food they need to build big tubers underground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ mli lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha sweet potato wain tso lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛdu bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or lack of water. Keeping the soil continuously moist with mulch helps the plant retain its flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli, ni no hewɔ lɛ ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes turn black and rot when the rains become very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away calcium from the soil and flood the roots, making it hard for the plant to absorb nutrients. This nutrient shortage causes the bottom of the growing tomato fruit to rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ nu abɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ nɛɛ haa tomato ni miida lɛ shishi shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know my plantain bunch is fully grown and ready to harvest before it spoils?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain tso lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa dani efite?

english: As plantain fruits mature, they change shape from flat and angular to round and plump. When the top leaves start turning yellow and the individual fruits look full, the crop has finished growing and is ready to cut.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantains lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Beni ŋwɛi baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbe naa ni esa akɛ afolɔ.

english: Why do my older cocoa trees stop producing as many pods as they did when they were younger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni edara lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni amɛfeɔ beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ?

english: Over time, old cocoa trees develop thick, overgrown branches that block sunlight and trap moisture, while the soil loses its nutrients. Pruning dead or overcrowded branches lets air and light in, which encourages the tree to grow new flowers and pods.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei momo lɛ feɔ niji ni mli eyi obɔ. ni tsiɔ hulu la naa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ Niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la boteɔ mli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ awo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii heei.

english: Why do my maize plants suddenly turn yellow and dry up before they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa ni amɛmiigbi dani amɛshɛɔ ŋmɔŋ he lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are being damaged by pests like fall armyworms or dry weather. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea early in the season helps keep the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo shishifãi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms efite yɛ fɛ̃i be mli loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ.

english: If my cassava plants look weak and stunted, can I save them with fertilizer, or is it too late?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ Ani manyɛ mawo mli ŋmɔshi nii? Aloo ekpe sɛɛ tsɔ?

english: If the plants are just lacking soil nutrients, organic compost or balanced fertilizer can help them recover. However, if the stunting is caused by cassava mosaic disease, fertilizer won't cure it, and those infected plants must be removed to protect the healthy ones.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Organic compost loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baanyɛ aye abua ni tso lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Shi, kɛji akɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ hewɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ, Fertilizer tsaŋ lɛ. Ni esa akɛ ajie nakai tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ koni abu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: What makes my cocoa trees suddenly stop bearing pods even when I clear the weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ trukaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ amɛhe moŋ? Kookoo tso lɛ

english: Cocoa trees often stop producing fruit due to hidden pests like mirids or fungal diseases like black pod. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight reach the trunk and spraying recommended organic or chemical treatments will help the trees start bearing pods again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei kpaa yibiiwoo yɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ahewɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes small holes in my cowpea leaves, and will it reduce the amount I can harvest?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ cowpea baai amli lɛ baa, ni ani amɛbaahã ŋmaa lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Small holes are caused by chewing insects like caterpillars and beetles eating the leaves. Because leaves act as the plant's food factory, heavy leaf damage starves the plant, resulting in smaller pods and a lower harvest.
ga: Buji bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ yeɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni feɔ buji bibii lɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ niyenii feemɔ tso. Baai ni efite waa lɛ baaha tso lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmaa ni akpaa lɛ faaa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from high heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering during dry spells and using a balanced fertilizer helps the plant hold onto its flowers until they become fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli, ni akɛ tsofa ni ja tsuɔ nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my cabbage plants curl up and feel crisp during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni minuɔ he akɛ mihe ejɔ mi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cabbage leaves curl up in intense heat to prevent water from evaporating too quickly from the plant. Mulching the soil around the plants with grass or leaves helps trap moisture in the soil and prevents this heat stress.
ga: Kaabeji baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ la ni naa wa lɛ mli koni nu akajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ. Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai shwieɔ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why is it bad to plant my tomatoes in the exact same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu tomato yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes in the same spot repeatedly allows tomato-specific pests and soil diseases, like bacterial wilt, to multiply in the soil. Rotating your tomato farm with crops like corn or beans starves those pests and keeps the soil clean.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni kɔɔ tomato pɛ he lɛ aba, tamɔ bacteria wilt. Ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake tomato ŋmɔ Ebaaha nakai ŋmeii lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atse.

english: Why are my groundnuts growing tall and thin instead of producing nuts under my large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii yɛ mitso agbo lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts need full, direct sunlight to make the food required for producing pods underground. Under heavy shade, the plants stretch upward toward the light instead of spreading out and pegging into the soil to grow nuts.
ga: Hulu la he miihia ŋmei tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei feemɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, ngmɛɛ e he nɛ o ngɔ kɛ wo zugba a mi konɛ o kɛ du ngma.

english: How can I make sure my yams grow large and smooth so market women will buy them for a good price?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ baatsɔ agbo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni yei ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ahe amɛ yɛ jara kpakpa nɔ?

english: Yams need deep, soft, and stone-free soil mounds so the tubers can expand without obstruction. Adding potassium-rich nutrients or wood ash to the soil makes the tubers grow thick, smooth, and firm.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni tɛi bɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia sweet potato. koni yitso lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni nɔ ko akatsĩ enaa Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ potassium loo tso sũ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha bulb lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to apply fertilizer to my maize so I don't waste my money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa awo ŋmãa mli? Bɔni afee ni okafite shika?

english: Maize needs fertilizer at two main stages: two weeks after sprouting to build strong roots, and again when the plant is knee-high (around 4 to 6 weeks) to support cob formation. Applying it outside these times leads to wasted nutrients.
ga: Abele he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛi titrii enyɔ nɔ: otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ koni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa aba; kɛ agbɛnɛ hu beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe (aaafee otsii 4 kɛyashi 6) koni eye ebua cob feemɔ. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai nɛɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite.

english: How can I tell if my maize leaves turning yellow is a sign of crop sickness or just lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hela he okadi loo nu ni bɛ kɛkɛ?

english: When crops lack water, the whole leaf usually wilts and turns brown evenly. However, if the lower leaves turn pale yellow starting from the tip along the middle vein while the rest of the plant stays green, it is usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen or that disease has attacked the roots.
ga: Kɛ nu bɛ tsei lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baa muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛyiteŋ kɛyaa fã ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni fãi krokomɛi lɛ Tsei lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo. Bei pii lɛ, eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hela miitutua shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants look healthy in the morning but droop completely during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ leebi lɛ? Shi egbɔjɔɔ kwraa yɛ shwane mli latsaa be lɛ mli?

english: Peppers drop water from their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up during peak sun hours. While minor wilting in severe heat is normal self-defense, constant afternoon drooping often indicates root damage caused by small soil worms or bacterial wilt preventing water transport.
ga: Peppers jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ shwiemɔ fioo yɛ be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni afɔɔ nɔ ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he moŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, shwane mli tsei ni shwieɔ shi ni yaa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi ni sũ mli ŋmeii bibii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tsiɔ nu gbɛfaa naa lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiifee srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading viral infections, or by extreme heat and uneven watering. When leaves curl tightly, the plant is trying to protect itself from losing water, but it also signals that insect control is needed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni eyaaa nɔ lɛ mli Kɛ́ baai lɛ ebɔle ehe waa Tso lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni elaaje lɛ he. Shi etsɔɔ hu akɛ ehe miihia ni akudɔ kooloi bibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct tropical sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and provide broad leaf canopy cover, acting as natural shade umbrellas and maintaining soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines naturally search for height so their leaves can capture maximum sunlight for energy. Lifting the leaves off the damp soil prevents fungal rot and leaf diseases while ensuring the plant produces large tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛha hewalɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baa helai anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce smaller tubers when I leave too many stems growing on one plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso kome nɔ lɛ?

english: A cassava plant shares its food among all its parts. If you allow three or four heavy stems to grow on one root, the plant spends most of its energy feeding leaves and stems above ground rather than storing food down in the cassava tubers.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ jaa eniyenii yɛ fãi lɛ fɛɛ ateŋ. Kɛji oha tsei ni tsii etɛ loo ejwɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ shishifã kome nɔ lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo yeɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmei shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why do the roots of my cassava rot when water collects and stays on my farm after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa ni ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When rainwater settles in the soil for days without draining, it starves the cassava roots of air, causing them to drown, decay, and attract underground fungi that rot the tubers.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu lɛ ta shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbii babaoo ni ejeee kpo. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akashɛ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ebaaha amɛgboi, amɛgboi ni amɛgbala shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: How does bad or contaminated water from nearby gutters affect the food produced by my crops?
ga: Te nu ni mli ewo muji loo nɔ ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ nu ŋshɔi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ saa niyenii ni jɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops drink water from the soil to nourish their leaves and fruits. If water contains harsh chemicals or human waste, plants absorb those toxins into their stems and leaves, which can stunt growth, burn leaf edges, or make the harvested food unsafe to eat.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha amɛbaai kɛ amɛyibii lɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛji tsofai ni mli wa loo adesa jwɛi yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nakai tsofai fɔji lɛ kɛyaa amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dalɛ aya hiɛ, eshã baai lɛ ashishi, loo eha niyenii ni akpa lɛ afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and thin even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal essential plant nutrients and fertilizer out of the soil before your main crops can reach them. They act like unwanted guests eating from the same small bowl of food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani otso titri lɛ baashɛ. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni sumɔɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ tsɛnsi bibioo kome mli.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and pale even after applying fertilizer during a drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe tseee yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo amɛmli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Fertilizer works like sugar in tea; it needs water to dissolve before crop roots can drink it in. When the soil is dry, the plants cannot absorb the solid fertilizer granules, so they remain hungry despite the inputs applied.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ sugar ni yɔɔ tii mli lɛ. Esa akɛ nu lɛ atsɔ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ, tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lolo yɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom while the plant is still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, so when the soil doesn't have enough, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the young growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa Tso lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ koni ekɛha gbekɛbii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my vegetable crops stay greener during hot dry weeks when I cover the ground around them with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli beni mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket over the dirt. It stops the hot sun from evaporating moisture out of the soil, keeping the plant roots cool and hydrated for longer without rain.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa ajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the shade trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like baby human skin—they burn easily under full sun. High heat causes their leaves to lose water faster than their small roots can suck it up, so they need shade from taller trees or plantains until they are mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ abifao hewolo. ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ enɔ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa baai lɛ amli nu shwieɔ shi oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. koni amɛnyɛ amɛnu No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji loo plantains amli kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings fail to grow when I put them in the soil upside down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ekomɛi shwereɔ kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have tiny buds that point upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the new shoots have to waste energy growing downwards and curving back up to find light, which often causes the stem to rot before leaves emerge.
ga: Kasava tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii. tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu ohiɛ shi lɛ Tsobii heei lɛ laajeɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shi ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛna la. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ fiteɔ dani baai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing thick stems and large cobs, they stretch tall to compete for sunlight, leaving little energy to build fat grains.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Mohu ɔ, nyɛ hyɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa. Mohu ɔ, e ngɔ e nɔmlɔ tso ɔ kɛ ya hɛ mi konɛ e kɛ hulu la ɔ nɛ fia a hɛ mi. Kɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ ni eshwɛ ni akɛbaafee fɔ dumɔwui.

english: Why do I need to clear space and put wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni okɛ tsei ama shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up high so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. If the leaves lay on the hot ground, they get shaded by weeds and catch soil diseases, resulting in small tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛji akɛ akɛ baai lɛ wo he ko ni mli edɔ lɛ Jwɛi lɛ feɔ shade ni ekɛ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cut away the small extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain tree, they steal water and food meant for the main plant. Removing extra suckers ensures the main plant gets maximum nourishment to produce a heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ kɛbɔle Dumɔwui titrii babaoo tsɔ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha tso titrii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa niyenii jogbaŋŋ koni ewo plantains babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers, but the flowers drop off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato?

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when weather temperatures get too high or water is inconsistent. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower so it cannot form fruit, causing the plant to drop the useless bloom.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaaa ewo yibii, ni no haa tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking crinkly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves. As the insects feed, they cripple the leaf cells and spread plant viruses that cause the leaves to distort.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. be mli ni kooloi yeɔ niyenii Efiteɔ baa lɛ mli wala yibii ni egbɛɔ tso mli helai ni haa baa lɛ mli tsɔɔ lɛ eshwaa.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea plants mainly when the flowers start showing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ titri beni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ?

english: Insects like flower thrips and pod borers are drawn to cowpea plants at flowering time because the blooms produce sweet nectar and tender tissue. The pests feed on the flowers, which prevents the plant from producing healthy bean pods.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips kɛ pod borers Amɛsumɔɔ cowpea tsei yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Enɛ ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ nu kɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yeɔ fɔfɔi Enɛ haaa tso lɛ afee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young seedlings need different care and fertilizer compared to my fully grown crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi kɛ akɛto mi tsei ni eda lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young crops are like human infants—their roots are delicate and cannot handle strong fertilizers or heavy soil conditions. They need gentle nutrients like phosphorus to build strong roots first, whereas fully grown crops need nitrogen and potassium to build thick stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ tamɔ abifabii. Eshishifãi lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa loo shikpɔŋ shihilɛi ni mli wa lɛ anaa. Niyenii ni mli jɔ tamɔ fɔsfɔs he miihia amɛ koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa klɛŋklɛŋ. Taakɛ tsei ni eda lɛ he hiaa nitrogen kɛ potassium koni amɛfee tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do my young plants die when there is heavy rain, while the mature plants in the same field survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi lolo lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have very short roots and tender stems that easily rot when water sits in the topsoil for too long. Older plants have deeper, stronger root systems that can anchor them and breathe even when the top ground is soaked.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji waa kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni fiteɔ oya kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ amɛ ni amɛmu kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do I need to shade my young cocoa trees when mature cocoa trees grow in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ woɔ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛdara kwraa yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun, causing them to dry up and die. Shading them with plantain trees acts like a canopy, protecting the young plants from harsh heat until their stems and root systems become strong enough for direct sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ gbiɔ ni egboɔ. Shade ni akɛ plantains tsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi amɛshishifã lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni hulu la baanyɛ ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does my maize crop need a different type of fertilizer when it starts flowering compared to when it was small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi beni ebɔi fɔfɔi lɛ fe be mli ni eji gbekɛ lɛ?

english: When maize is small, it spends energy growing leaves and stalks, so it needs nitrogen for greenery. When it begins to flower and form cobs, its nutritional needs change to phosphorus and potassium to fill out heavy, healthy grains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ ji bibioo Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen he miihia kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ. Kɛ ebɔi fɔfɔi ni efee ŋmei lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛyaa phosphorus kɛ potassium nɔ koni ekɛ dumɔwui ni wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are turning yellow because of plant hunger or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso hɔmɔ loo hela hewɔ?

english: When a plant lacks nutrients, the yellowing usually starts evenly on the older bottom leaves because the plant shifts food to its growing top leaves. When a plant is sick from disease, yellowing often appears as random spots, patches, or curling anywhere on the plant.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, Yellow fɔɔ shishijee pɛpɛɛpɛ. yɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ Enɛ ji akɛ, tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii kɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji hela mɔ tsei lɛ, bei pii lɛ, Yellow jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii amli yɛ tso lɛ he fɛɛ he.

english: Why do some crops like cassava need to be planted far apart while maize can be planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ ŋmei, yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava roots spread wide underground to produce large tubers and need plenty of space to gather food without fighting neighboring plants. Maize grows straight up with narrow roots, so plants can stand closer together without stealing each other's nutrients.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji. ni ehe miihia ni amɛná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ niyenii ato ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awuu Abele daa tɛ̃ɛ ni shishifãi lɛ mli tseee. No hewɔ lɛ tsei baanyɛ adamɔ shi ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe ni amɛjuuu amɛhe niyenii.

english: Why do crops planted on one side of my farm grow bigger than the same crops on another side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fa kome lɛ daraa fe tsei ni adu yɛ fa kroko lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Soil nutrition and moisture are not the same across an entire field. Spots where water naturally settles or where decayed leaves gather have richer soil food, while dry or rocky spots give plants fewer nutrients to grow big.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jeee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. He ni nu eyi mli obɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa loo hei ni baai ni egboi buaa amɛhe naa lɛ baaná niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, hei ni egbi loo tɛi yɔɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná niyenii fioo ko pɛ ni ekɛbaatsɔ agbo.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize in the same field, or will they steal food from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpea kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ? Aloo amɛbaashi akaŋ yɛ niyenii he?

english: Cowpeas and maize actually help each other because they feed differently. Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, which naturally feeds the maize and improves overall soil health.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe diɛŋtsɛ. Akɛni amɛyeɔ niyenii srɔtoi hewɔ lɛ Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi.

english: Plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrition. If the plant feels it does not have enough energy or food to feed developing fruit, it sheds the flowers to protect itself.
ga: Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii mli lɛ kpe. Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ ebɛ hewalɛ loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaha eyibii ni miida lɛ, Ebaajie fɔfɔii ni ekɛbu ehe.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ duɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants built to survive tough weather, poor soil, and neglect, so they eat up nutrients rapidly. Farm crops have been bred to produce food rather than fight off harsh environments, so they need human help to clear away weed competition while they are young.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni abɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, kɛ hiɛ ni akuɔ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya. Akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ koni akɛná niyenii moŋ fe ni akɛaawu ashi shihilɛ ni mli wa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, adesai ayelikɛbuamɔ he miihia tsei nɛɛ koni amɛjie jwɛi akaŋshii kɛya be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my maize when the early rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Do not plant with the very first rain because it might be a false start and the heat in the ground will scorch the seeds. Wait until the rain falls steadily for two or three consecutive days so the soil is deep wet and ready to nurture seeds.
ga: Kaadu nii beni nugbɔ nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ ejaakɛ ekolɛ ebaaje shishi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. ni la ni tsoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ashã. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni efee klalo akɛ ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops suffer more when the minor rainy season is shorter than expected?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naa amanehulu babaoo beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need a specific amount of moisture over several weeks to flower and form seeds. When the minor season stops early, plants get stressed before finishing their growth, which causes low yields or empty seed pods.
ga: Tsei lɛ taoɔ nu pɔtɛɛ ko otsii babaoo bɔni afee ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo dumɔwui. Beni akpa be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mra Tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛ dani amɛdaraa. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi loo dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ efolo.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow even when the farm gets enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ani nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil has run out of vital nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil that cannot breathe. Adding compost or well-rotted animal manure gives the plant the food it needs to stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo shishifãi lɛ efo nu mli aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam plants feed heavily and take a lot of strength out of the ground. Legume crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring land fertility for the next season.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji niyenii ni tsii ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsuɔ nii. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, but not when heavy rain is actively falling. Slightly burying the fertilizer near the plant roots prevents running rainwater from carrying it away before the plant can feed on it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi jeee beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ. Kɛ́ ofu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fioo lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho dani tsei lɛ aye.

english: Young cocoa trees are fragile and burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains creates a cool umbrella that protects young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni aaashi loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ haa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, won't I harvest more food from my small plot?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop big, healthy fruits instead of many weak, tiny ones.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni mli wa. Mohu ɔ, yiblii nɛ a he wa we nɛ a ngɛ nyafii fuu ngɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon heat is the plant's natural way of reducing water loss through its leaves. If the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, the plant is fine, but if they stay curled, the roots need watering.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa nu ni elaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi. Kɛji baai lɛ shwieee shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni sa. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ Ehe miihia ni awo shishifãi lɛ hu nu.

english: What causes small worms to hide inside the whorls of my maize and eat the leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abɛi ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, which are destructive caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid by moths. Checking your farm early and using recommended biological control or neem leaf extracts protects the young maize before the damage spreads.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji cutworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli lɛ amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ loo neem baa mli nu lɛ tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmãa bibii ahe dani nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested hybrid corn to plant during the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Saving seeds from hybrid varieties produces weak plants with very low yields in the second generation. Buying fresh, certified seeds every season ensures strong growth and full harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni yibiiwoo ni baa shi waa aba yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ daa be lɛ baaha amɛdara waa ni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is a key nutrient that moves from older leaves to feed young, growing leaves at the top when there is not enough food in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tso lɛ. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli kɛyaa baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii be mli ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the dry season, and does it mean they are dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ egbo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves in dry weather to conserve water and protect itself from hot sun. The plant is not dead; it goes dormant to survive and will quickly sprout fresh leaves once the rains start.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli koni akɛbu nu he ni abu he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebaahi shi ni ehi shi koni ehi shi, ni ebaakwɛ baai heei oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ je shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without making big fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛlɛɔ ni amɛwooo yibii wuji beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to catch sun instead of putting energy into growing strong stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe koni amɛmɔ hulu lɛ moŋ, ni ekɛ hewalɛ fataa tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sun. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and preserving moisture in the soil until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small green droppings inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? yɛ gɔŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides in the central leaf whorl of young maize plants to eat tender leaves. Catching them early and applying control measures during cool hours stops them from destroying the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ amɛ lɛ atsu nii yɛ gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai lɛ amli Ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the roots and tubers of my cassava rot when rainwater stays on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe. When water sits on the farm without draining, it suffocates the roots and creates the ideal environment for harmful soil fungi to cause root rot.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ejeee kpo lɛ Nu lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni efee shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ koni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛhe amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato plants stress, which dries out pollen and prevents fertilization. When the flowers are not fertilized properly, the plant drops them to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa fɔmɔ nii aba. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi ko jogbaŋŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my dry granular fertilizer right before a very heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni ji granular lɛ shwieɔ nɔ dani ahum ni naa wa ko baa?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away fertilizer from the topsoil before plant roots have time to drink it in. Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is already moist after rain so it dissolves smoothly into the root zone.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ mli.Nyɔŋtsere lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ shishifãi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray insect killer on my pepper farm while the plants are full of open flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ ewo fɔfɔi lolo lɛ?

english: Spraying during flowering kills helpful bees and insects that visit the blossoms to pollinate them. Without these insects visiting the flowers, fewer blossoms will develop into healthy pepper fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baa fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛyawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ bɛ ni ayasara fɔfɔi lɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ baatsɔ pepper aduawai ni bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest give me a smaller yield than certified seeds from the agriculture office?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni Bureau of Agriculture lɛ ema nɔ mi lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially produced hybrids trained for high yield and disease resistance. Grains saved from past harvests lose these special strengths over time, leading to uneven growth and smaller yields.
