ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afee lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ amɛhe. Nibii ni ato kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ hewalɛi krokomɛi nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kɛ yibiiwoo ni faaa.

english: Why do I see tiny ant-like insects crawling all over the flowers of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ? Mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ fɛɛ nɔ

english: These tiny insects are often pests like aphids or thrips that are attracted to the sweet sap of crop flowers. They attach themselves to the blossoms to feed, which weakens the flowers and damages them before they can turn into healthy fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ aphids loo thrips. ni gbalaa nu ni jɛɔ tsei fɔfɔi amli Amɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe kɛha niyenii. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfiteɔ dani amɛbatsɔmɔɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Are ants on my crop flowers harmful, or are they just crawling around harmlessly?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mifɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ oshara loo amɛmiikplekeshi kɛkɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he?

english: While ants themselves might not eat the flower directly, they often protect tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids and mealybugs because those pests produce a sweet liquid ants love to eat. When ants are present, it usually means tiny harmful insects are damaging your flowers underneath.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ yeee fɔfɔi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ amɛbuɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids kɛ mealybugs lɛ ahe. No ji akɛ, nakai kooloi lɛ jieɔ nu ko ni ŋɔɔ ni ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛye lɛ kpo. Kɛ́ ŋmeii yɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ oshara. Efiteɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if tiny insects are the reason my crop flowers are turning brown and weak?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kooloo bibioo ko emɔ hela lɛ? Ani enɛ miiha mitso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ miifee ŋmɔtɔ ni egbɔjɔ?

english: Check the flower blossoms closely for tiny moving spots, sticky sap, or curled petals. If insects are feeding on the flower stems and petals, the flowers will look dry, discolored, and weak long before they are supposed to wither.
ga: Kwɛmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ koni ona he ko bibii. ni baanyɛ afã, nu ni shwieɔ shi, loo fɔfɔi ashishifãi ni ebɔle ehe Kɛji kooloi ye fɔfɔi ashishifãi kɛ fɔfɔi ashishifãi lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni egbi, ehiɛ su, ni ebɛ hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani ebaagbo.

english: What causes the healthy-looking flowers on my crops to suddenly fall to the ground?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ trukaa?

english: Flowers drop prematurely when tiny pests bite and damage the thin stem that attaches the flower to the plant. Once that small connection is damaged or infected, the plant can no longer feed the flower, causing it to fall off.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kooloi bibii ŋmɔ ni amɛfite tsei bibii lɛ. ni hiɛɔ fɔfɔii kɛyaa tsei ahe Kɛ nakai tsakpaa bibioo lɛ fite loo hela mɔ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aha efɔfɔi lɛ niyenii dɔŋŋ. ha egbee shi

english: Why is it important for the flowers on my crops to stay healthy and last long on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers are the starting point for your harvest; every pod, grain, or fruit comes from a flower. If flowers fall off early due to insect damage, your plant cannot produce fruit, which leads to a very poor yield.
ga: Fɔfɔi ji shishijee kɛha okpamɔ: pod, dumɔwu, loo aduawai fɛɛ jɛɔ fɔfɔi mli. Kɛji fɔfɔii shwie shi oya yɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahewɔ Otso lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii. ni haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa

english: Can insect damage cause my crop flowers to drop even when the weather is good?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha mitso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ agbo eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hi moŋ?

english: Yes. Even if your crops have enough water and sun, tiny insects feeding inside the flower blossoms will destroy the delicate internal parts of the flower, causing it to drop off regardless of good weather.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nu kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa po lɛ, kooloi bibii ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ baafite fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ha egbee shi ekɔɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpakpai ahe.

english: What is a top spray, and how does it protect my flowering crops?
ga: Mɛni ji tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ ni ehe gbɛi fe fɛɛ? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua ni ebu mi tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe?

english: A top spray is a liquid crop treatment applied directly over the leaves and flower canopy of the plant. It coats the delicate upper parts of the crop to clear away destructive insects and protect the flowers so they can mature.
ga: Top spray lɛ kɛ nu tsuɔ tsei ahe nii. Akɛwoɔ tso lɛ baai kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ekɛ nɔ ko haa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ hei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ koni ekɛshwie kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ, ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi ahe koni amɛshwere.

english: Why should I spray directly on the leaves and flowers instead of just putting chemicals into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ baai kɛ fɔfɔi anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ tsofai baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛkɛ?

english: Tiny insects that destroy flowers live and feed directly on the blossoms and upper leaves. A top spray hits these pests immediately where they sit, stopping the flower damage faster than soil treatments can.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛyeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Spray ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baatutua nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛji amɛtara shi pɛ. Ekpaa fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ oya fe shikpɔŋ nɔ tsamɔi

english: When is the best time for me to spray my crops to stop tiny insects from destroying the flowers?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni kooloi bibii akafite fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when insects are active on the plant canopy and the sun is not too hot. Spraying as soon as you spot tiny insects on the flowers prevents major flower loss.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ tsei anɔ ni hulu lɛ edɔɔɔ tsɔ. Okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ kɛji ona kooloi bibii pɛ. yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi wuji ni elaaje lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: What can I do to make sure the flowers on my farm stay on the plants long enough to form fruit?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahi tsei lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii?

english: You can protect your crop flowers by checking them regularly for tiny pests and using a top spray at the early flowering stage. Keeping the flowers healthy and insect-free allows them to stay on the plant until fruit formation is complete.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu fɔfɔi ni odu lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni oookwɛ daa kɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋwɛi nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ akwɛmɔ mra lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ hi shi jogbaŋŋ ni kooloi bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni amɛbaawo yibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. They need shade from larger trees or fast-growing food crops like plantain to protect them from the harsh sun while their roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo niyenii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ema shi shiŋŋ lɛ.

english: Does my yam crop really need wooden poles to climb on, or can I leave them to spread on the ground?
ga: Mi sweet potato lɛ biɔ tso tso diɛŋtsɛ koni enyɛ ekwɔ. Aloo obaanyɛ oha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need poles to lift their leaves into the sunlight so they can make food for the tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off the damp ground, which prevents fungal diseases and leads to much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ko ni baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la mli koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei ahe tsei kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ekɛ sweet potatoes ni da fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant is hungry for nutrients, especially nitrogen, or that the soil is too dry or too wet. Adding manure or the right fertilizer helps the leaves turn green so the plant can grow strong ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii he miihia tso lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli koni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and lets soil pests and diseases build up. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts helps restore soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil whenever there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the roots need air to breathe. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the cassava stays healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni cassava lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable farm in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the soil absorbs the moisture before the afternoon sun can evaporate it. Watering in hot sun can also stress the leaves and waste precious water.
ga: Nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shwane hulu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efite nu ni jara wa.

english: Will planting my cabbage seeds very close together produce more food for me at harvest?
ga: Ani kaabii dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná niyenii babaoo kɛji akpa?

english: Planting too closely forces plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in tiny, thin leaves instead of big cabbage heads. Proper spacing gives each plant room to produce a large, heavy head.
ga: Amɛdumɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa baa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kaabe yitsei wuji najiaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsu fɛɛ tsu ni daa lɛ náa bulb agboi ni tsii.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoot suckers grow around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Having too many suckers causes them to steal water and food from the main plant, making the fruit bunch very small. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main plant grows big, heavy plantains.
ga: Kpoji babaoo ni amɛwoɔ lɛ baaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Ha aduawai akuu lɛ afee bibioo waa. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ akwɛ̃ agbo ni tsii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning black and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering or a lack of calcium in the soil while the fruit is forming. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant take up nutrients and keeps the fruit healthy.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni tso yibii lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai, ni ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without forming any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot and dry, or if you use too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the plant focus only on growing leaves instead of fruit. Proper watering and balanced plant food help the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ pɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsei aniyenii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and sensitive roots that scorch easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts like a living canopy, protecting the seedlings from heat and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shade tsei. Buu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and weak with very small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops are forced to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and nutrients to grow strong stems and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ Dumɔwui anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield much better when I plant right after the first major rains rather than during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ

english: Seeds need reliable moisture in warm soil to sprout and build deep root systems quickly. Planting immediately after the first major rains ensures the seeds get continuous moisture so they don't dry out and die under the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui hia nu ni mli edɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiŋ ni egbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning yellow from the tips down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ enaagbee kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure restores their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on my land after harvesting a heavy feeder crop like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa kooloi aniyenii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmei?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, leaving the soil tired. Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and lock it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for your next season's crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. haa shikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does covering the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass keep them from wilting in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haaa amɛgboi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves creates a blanket (mulch) that blocks the harsh sun, keeps the soil cool, and prevents water from evaporating quickly so the plant roots stay hydrated longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. (Mulch) Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn soft and rot underground when the rains are heavy?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because waterlogged soil prevents air from reaching the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why does leaving weeds on my farm reduce the final amount of crop harvest I get?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa naagbee ŋmaa ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most farm crops and aggressively steal sunlight, soil water, and fertilizer away from your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures all the nutrients in your soil go directly into growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. ni ekɛ ekãa juɔ hulu la, sũ mli nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛkwɛ tsei.

english: Why should I trim off extra branches and tall water shoots from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni yɔɔ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary branches and shoots allows sunlight and fresh air to pass through the tree canopy, which reduces fungal diseases like black pod. It also directs the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Niji kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ baa shi. Ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ hu tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaves dark droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center of the maize plant and eats tender leaves. Checking your fields early and applying recommended pest control methods protects the growing plant before it is destroyed.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Odumɔi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei ni miida lɛ ahe dani akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow big cobs, so adding well-rotted animal manure or NPK fertilizer helps bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo loo NPK ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do agricultural officers always advise me to plant cowpeas or beans on land where I previously harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa be fɛɛ be akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ tsutsu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. Planting them restores nutrients naturally, so your next crop grows stronger without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but end up with tiny underground tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai bibii shi eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much water or nitrogen, it uses all its food energy to grow tall branches and big leaves above ground instead of storing food below ground in the tubers.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa nine shɛ nu loo nitrogen babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo niji kakadaji kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ oyitsoŋ lɛ

english: Why is it important for me to weed around my young yam vines early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Sweet potato tsei bibii ni yɔɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Young yam shoots grow slowly at first and need maximum sunlight and nutrients. Weeds will quickly steal food and shade the young vines, preventing them from developing thick tubers later.
ga: Sweet potato tsei bibii lɛ daraa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛbiɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii babaoo. Jwɛi juɔ niyenii oya ni ehaa wain tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Koni akafee yitso ni mli wa sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do the young cocoa pods on my trees turn black and shrivel up before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease caused by fungus that breeds in damp, dark places. Pruning extra shade tree branches and clearing weeds allows air and sunlight to dry the cocoa pods and stop the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela ni ŋmei ko ni fɔɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Nibii ni afolɔ koni akɛha hulutsoo babaoo kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily whenever they carry heavy fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni mawo aduawai ni tsii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not go deep into the earth. Once the fruit bunch becomes heavy, wind can easily pull the roots out, so supporting the stem with a strong wooden pole is necessary.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ mli oya. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ tsei ni wa afi tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my oil palm take several years after planting before I can harvest any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm lɛ heɔ afii babaoo yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees spend their first three to four years building deep root systems and a strong trunk to support heavy oil bunches. Good weeding and fertilizer during these early years prepare the tree for heavy production.
ga: Mu tsei heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa ni baaye abua mu ni tsii lɛ. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli Enɛɛmɛi baaye abua ni asaa tso lɛ he kɛha ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off instead of forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Watering regularly at the roots during flowering keeps the plant cool and helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ afɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves or spreading a virus. Spraying with neem oil water or recommended insect sprays helps clear them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu, neem fɔ, loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ kooloi amli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni enɛɛmɛi afee faŋŋ.

english: Why do tiny worms keep eating holes through all my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye bu ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moths lay tiny eggs under the leaves which hatch into hungry caterpillars that eat cabbage leaves. Checking the underside of leaves and removing them early prevents caterpillars from destroying your harvest.
ga: Kplukai lɛ woɔ wɔji bibii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi, ni amɛfɔɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ kaabɛji baai. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni ojie amɛ mra. Ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm yield much more pods when we get good rains early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ kpakpa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need plenty of water during their flowering phase to turn blossoms into pods. Good early rains keep the soil moist, preventing young pods from drying up and dropping off early, which leads to a much bigger harvest.
ga: Cacao tsei he miihia nu babaoo yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛtsɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii. Nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgbee shi oya. Enɛ kɛ kpamɔ ni da kwraa baa.

english: Why do some of the tiny flowers on my cocoa tree trunk dry up and fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii No hewɔ lɛ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi?

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but only a small portion get pollinated by tiny insects called midges. If a flower isn't pollinated, or if the tree experiences heat stress or lacks nutrients, it naturally sheds the flower to save energy.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kplukai bibii pɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ lɛ pollin. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ naa dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why is it wrong for me to harvest my cocoa pods while they are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ makpãa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Unripe cocoa pods do not have enough natural sugar in their sweet white pulp. Without proper sugar levels, the beans will not ferment correctly after harvest, leaving you with bitter, low-quality beans that buyers will reject.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni edako lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli sugar ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛloo yɛŋ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ sugar ni sa bɛ lɛ, Beans lɛ shwieŋ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmeii ni ehiii, ni ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ baakpoo.

english: Can I cut down all the large trees on my farm so my cocoa gets full sunlight all day?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ koni hulu la ashɛ kookoo lɛ nɔ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: No, full sunlight can burn young cocoa leaves and dry out the soil too quickly. Cocoa trees grow best under moderate shade from taller trees, which keep the farm cool, preserve soil moisture, and protect the crop from strong winds.
ga: Dabi, hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ ashã kookoo baai bibii ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Cocoa tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ahe hulutsoo ni sa mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni obu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees need extra plant food or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ he miihia tsei niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi?

english: If your cocoa leaves start turning pale yellow instead of deep green, or if the tree stops producing new shoots and pods, it is usually a sign that the soil has run out of vital nutrients like nitrogen or potassium.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa baai lɛ miije shishi amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ kpa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii heei feemɔ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium lɛ efo.

english: Why do people advise me to plant food crops like beans alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural food source for young cocoa trees, helping them grow faster while also providing food for your household.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha cacao tsei bibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya yɛ be mli ni ehaa oshia lɛ niyenii hu.

english: This is caused by a fungal attack known as Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet and cool conditions. Raindrops splash the fungus from the ground onto the pods, so keeping your farm clear of weeds and pruning extra branches helps air flow and reduces wetness.
ga: Fungal tutuamɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ fɛ̃i mli Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni afo tsei niji krokomɛi amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ aba shi.

english: What causes small brown patches and dry spots on the leaves of my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baa? kɛ hei ni egbi yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Those patches are usually caused by small sap-sucking insects called capsids or mirids. They pierce the stems and leaves to feed, leaving wounds that dry out and damage the young branches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids loo mirids lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. Amɛfoɔ tsei akutsei kɛ baai amli koni amɛtao niyenii. Eshiɔ pilamɔi ni gbɛ́ɔ ni efiteɔ tsei niji bibii.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa tree during pruning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ kookoo tso nɔ yɛ be mli ni mifoɔ tso lɛ?

english: Pruning removes overcrowded branches so sunlight and fresh air can pass through the tree. This reduces fungal diseases and ensures the tree directs its energy into producing large cocoa pods rather than unnecessary leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni eyi obɔ lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔji wuji yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: My cocoa tree is over thirty years old and produces very few pods now; why has it stopped yielding well?
ga: Mi-cocoa tso lɛ eye fe afii nyɔŋmai etɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ amrɔ nɛɛ. Mɛni hewɔ ekpa nitsumɔ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow very old, their roots and internal branches become less efficient at carrying food and water up from the soil. Older trees also become weaker against diseases, causing their natural pod output to drop over time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ egbɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛmli niji lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Tsei ni edara lɛ nyɛɔ helai yeɔ amɛ oya. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli pod ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn the bush on my land after clearing it for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mijie nɔ ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich topsoil and useful insects that feed your crops. Clearing without burning leaves rotting plants on the soil, which acts as natural fertilizer, keeps the soil moist, and protects it from scorching heat.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni egboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ni ashãaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why are crops failing to grow well on land that was previously used for small-scale gold mining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛ shika tsuru ŋmɔji bibii tsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mining washes away the fertile topsoil that plants need for food and packs the remaining earth too tightly for roots to grow. To farm on old mining land, you must loosen the soil deeply and mix in plenty of animal manure or compost.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akuɔ mli lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa ni tsei taoɔ kɛha niyenii lɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Ani oosumɔ ni otsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ momo ni akɛ shika tsuru tsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ? Esa akɛ ogbala shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji babaoo afutu mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tip usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the nutrient that gives plants their green color and strength, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help them bounce back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or irregular watering while the fruit is growing. Watering your garden regularly and adding agricultural lime to the soil prevents this from happening.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo obɔŋ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ okwaayeli mli ŋmei fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaatsi enɛ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees keep shedding their young flowers before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Dani ebaatsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by heavy sunlight, drought, or attacks from tiny insects like mirids (capsids). Providing shade trees and spraying recommended insecticides at the right season will save the flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulu la ni naa wa, hɔmɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ iris (capsids) tutua amɛ. Be mli hulutsoo be kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from the plant leaves. Spraying early with neem oil or targeted pest spray keeps these insects away so the plant can grow healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso baai amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo tsofai krokomɛi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni ato he gbɛjianɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I remove some of the young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: When too many young shoots grow together, they fight with the main tree for food and water. Removing extra shoots and leaving only two or three ensures the main plantain tree produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii lɛ dara yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli tsɔ Ekɛ tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashiɔ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa plantain titri lɛ niji wuji ni tsii shwereɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food that makes the yam tuber grow big underground. Staking lifts the vines off the wet ground, catching more sunlight and preventing foliage diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Na hulu la babaoo ni otsi baa helai anaa

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready for harvesting since the tubers are hidden underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ejaakɛ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready 9 to 12 months after planting, marked by the lower leaves naturally turning yellow and dropping off. You can gently dig up one plant to check if the tubers are thick enough before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Obaanyɛ Ofo tso kome fiofio koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ mli eyi obɔ bɔ ni sa dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops right at the start of the main rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting at the start of the rains allows seeds to sprout in warm, moist soil and build deep roots before any dry spell hits. Early planting also helps crops grow strong before field pests become too numerous later in the season.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ema shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa waa dani ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayi fa tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naagbee.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the roots are sitting in too much water. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving water drainage in the field helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo ŋmɔ mli nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread dry fertilizer right before a very heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa waa lɛ aba?

english: Heavy rain causes surface water runoff, which washes your expensive fertilizer away into nearby bushes or streams before the plant roots can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist or when light rain is expected.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hoɔ. Enɛ hoɔ o-fertilizer ni jara wa lɛ mli kɛyaa tsei bibii loo faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo be mli ni nugbɔ enɛ fioo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees act like umbrellas, providing shade and conserving soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hɔɔŋ ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naa.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and very small or empty cobs. Giving each plant proper space allows it to yield big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ cob yibii babaoo aba.

english: Why is it important to use wooden sticks to stake my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ sweet potato wain tsei atsu nii lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground so they can catch more sunlight to feed the plant and grow bigger tubers underground. It also keeps the leaves dry, preventing fungal diseases that spread on damp soil.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ hu ni amɛgbiɔ. Tsi fungal helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nutrients from the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil, naturally renewing the land for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa jɛmɛ feɔ ehee yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha dumɔwui ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops suffer even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ awui eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds act as thieves on your farm; they steal the plant food, space, and fertilizer intended for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ tsei aniyenii, he ko, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will see the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and the soil around the base of the stem will begin to crack open as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes rotting and turning black while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishigbɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding wood ash or agricultural lime helps solve this.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli fɔ́ daa ni akɛ tso sũ loo okwaayeli mli sũ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my maize leaves and brownish dust inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli kɛ sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mibaai lɛ amli lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the funnel of the plant to eat young leaves. Checking your field early and spraying recommended neem oil or bio-pesticides will protect your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei amli ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛnáaa nu bɔ ni sa?

english: When crops do not get enough water, their leaves wilt, curl, or turn brown and dry up. When they get too much water, their leaves often turn yellow, become soft, and the roots can rot because soggy soil prevents them from breathing.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi, amɛbaakpãtã, loo amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbaagbi. Kɛ́ onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛfeɔ blɛoo, ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ afite ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa amɛmli shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need a steady supply of water to carry nutrients from the soil up into their stems and leaves. During the dry season, intense heat evaporates soil moisture quickly, causing crops to stop growing and wither unless water is provided through irrigation.
ga: Tsei taoɔ nu ni hoɔ daa koni ekɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii kpaɔ shweremɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. ja nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛhaa

english: Why does water sit on top of my field instead of sinking into the ground after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu shwieɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When soil is hard and packed tightly or has high clay content, water cannot easily sink through it. Tilling the land or mixing in organic compost helps loosen the soil so water can drain down to the crop roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle ehe loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ sũ babaoo. Nu nyɛŋ abote mli mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni nu lɛ anyɛ atsɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is a major nutrient plants need to stay green and healthy. Adding manure or compost helps feed the soil and restore healthy leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow small and weak when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, they compete for the same sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each crop enough space ensures every plant gets what it needs to produce a good harvest.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkpamɔ kpakpa aba.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a shade blanket for the soil, keeping it cool and stopping sunlight from drying out the moisture around your crops' roots.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii akɛ shade kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaaa hulu la lɛ afite ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt when the sun is too bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ tsoɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young plants have small root systems and delicate leaves that lose water faster under hot, direct sunlight than their roots can absorb. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young seedlings until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Flowers often drop off when the crop suffers from heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Keeping the water supply steady and feeding the soil helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihe dɔlɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu jɛɛhe ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ koni amɛhiɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn weak even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal the nutrients, water, and sunlight that your crops need. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ waa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do deep roots help my cassava plants stay alive when rain does not fall for weeks?
ga: Te shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii babaoo lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Deep roots act like deep water wells. They reach far into the ground where moisture stays trapped long after the top layer of soil has dried out, allowing the plant to drink during dry spells.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nubu ni mli kwɔ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ he ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ egbi lɛ sɛɛ. Ehaa tsei feɔ nɔ ni anuɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Yellowing and falling leaves on young cocoa trees usually mean they are getting too much direct sun or lack water. Young cocoa needs shade from larger plants like plantains to protect them while their roots establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ cacao tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo loo nu efo amɛmli. Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ.

english: What is causing my cocoa pods to turn black while they are still growing on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Blackening pods are typically caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads in cool, overly wet conditions. Pruning extra branches and clearing weeds lets sunlight and air dry out the trees, reducing the fungus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ni ji black pod lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela baa shi

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall but only producing tiny cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa shi ewoɔ toi bibii pɛ lɛ?

english: Maize grows tall with small cobs when plants are seeded too close together or lack essential soil nutrients like nitrogen. Giving each plant proper spacing and applying fertilizer early ensures big, healthy ears.
ga: Abele daa kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, bɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli mra. Ebaaha toi lɛ afee wuji ni amɛhe awa.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to be dug up from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves start turning yellow and falling off, and the soil right around the base of the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain suckers drying up and turning brown before fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Drying plantain leaves are often caused by dry weather spells or root damage from soil pests. Clearing old fallen leaves and piling mulch around the base keeps the soil moist and root systems healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo shishifãi ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ plantain baai lɛ agbiɔ. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shishifãi lɛ hu hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and showing tiny green bugs underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Curling leaves with small green insects mean aphids are sucking the sap out of your plants. Washing the leaves with a gentle soapy water mixture or neem leaf extract will clear the insects away.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ miimu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ samla kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ Loo neem baa mli nu tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie ŋmeii kɛjɛ mli.

english: Pepper blossoms drop when the plant is stressed by extreme sun heat, dry soil, or a lack of food in the dirt. Keeping the soil regularly watered and adding well-rotted manure helps the flowers stay on.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa, ni akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: What is making large round holes in my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bulɛi wuji ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are caused by caterpillars feeding on the tender foliage. Hand-picking them in the early morning or spraying natural neem-based mixtures will protect your cabbage crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabeji baai amli lɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ onine shwie o-cabbage lɛ nɔ leebi loo okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem ni akɛfutu mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu o-cabbage tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Water pooling means your soil is high in heavy clay or tightly compacted. Digging small drainage trenches and mixing organic compost into the soil helps water flow through easily so plant roots do not rot.
ga: Nu ni abua naa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo ni mli edɔ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ bibioo ko mli ni oootsɔ Ni okɛ organic compost awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ atsɔ mli mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ fiteee.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing short and twisted instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist and deform when the ground beneath them is hard, stony, or not loosened deeply enough. Building high, soft mounds of light soil allows the yams to push straight down easily.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛfiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo egbɛ eshwaaa bɔ ni sa. Diatomaceous shikpɔŋ ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potatoes lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa shi. mlɛo

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to grow healthy green foliage. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the plant recover and make strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the wet ground, exposing leaves to sunlight and preventing fungal diseases caused by humid soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ŋmɛ baai lɛ awo hulu la mli ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I spray water directly on the leaves of my pepper plants during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ nu shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Water droplets on leaves can act like magnifying glasses under bright sunshine, burning the leaf surface. Warm, wet leaves also create the perfect environment for destructive plant diseases and fungi to spread.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi, ni eshãa baa lɛ hiɛ. Baai ni mli edɔ ni efɔ lɛ hu feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ahelai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my tomatoes with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Tomato kɛ jwɛi

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out water in the dirt, keeps weed seeds from sprouting, and breaks down over time to enrich the soil.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to leave big shade trees standing when I clear land for a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã tso agbo ko adamɔ shi? Beni ajieɔ shikpɔŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔji heei?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Tall forest trees act as natural umbrellas, protecting delicate young cocoa plants from harsh sun and heat while maintaining essential humidity in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Koo mli tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Does it matter which part of the cassava stem I cut and plant in the soil?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni mifoɔ ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmei ni mifoɔ ni miduɔ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa?

english: Yes, stem selection matters. The middle section of a mature stem sprouts fastest and produces strong roots, whereas the top tip dries out easily and the thick bottom stem takes too long to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, stem halamɔ he miihia. Tso ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ daa oya fe fɛɛ ni ewoɔ shishifãi ni wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋwɛi naagbee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni shishigbɛ tso ni mli tse lɛ heɔ be babaoo tsɔ dani edaa.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers to dig up and plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafo ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look for maiden or sword suckers, which have narrow, spear-like leaves and broad bases. Avoid suckers with wide, broad leaves because they have weak roots and will produce small, light bunches.
ga: Taomɔ oblayei bibii loo klante ŋmeii, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe ejaakɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbaawo niji bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts alongside my corn will make the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Neighboring crops like corn can feed on this natural fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ aye nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa nɛɛ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my corn leaves with fine powdery dirt inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni muji ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni tamɔ powder yɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding inside the growing leaf funnel. Catching them early allows you to treat the crop with neem seed extract or recommended control sprays before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni naa niyenii yɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ lɛ mra Ehaa okɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe nii dani ofiteɔ he ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why is it bad practice to grow maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that plant needs and allows pests and diseases that prefer maize to build up in the soil, leading to poorer yields each season.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant my seeds immediately after the soil is prepared instead of waiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni misaa shikpɔŋ lɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ?

english: Planting quickly ensures seeds take advantage of existing soil moisture and nutrients, giving them a head start against weeds and preventing the soil from drying out.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ oya lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ he sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaaa sũ lɛ agbi.

english: What happens if I leave too much space between my crop plants in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi gbɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Leaving wide gaps gives sunlight directly to the soil, which encourages aggressive weeds to grow quickly and steal nutrients and water that should go to your crops.
ga: ni eshiɔ gbɛ ni da Ebaaha hulu la lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ woɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛju niyenii kɛ nu ni esa akɛ ebote onibii amli lɛ.

english: Will planting my crops closer together give me a larger total harvest?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni fa babaoo?

english: Proper spacing ensures crops form a thick green canopy that blocks weeds while giving every individual plant enough room, light, and nutrients to produce high yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsiɔ jwɛi anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso he gbɛ, la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai koni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: How does early planting help protect my crops against mid-season droughts?
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua ni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ be teŋgbɛ lɛ he?

english: Early-planted crops establish deep roots early in the season, allowing them to draw water from deep in the soil if rainfall slows down later on.
ga: Tsei ni adu mra lɛ baawo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba shi sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to plan for equipment like tractors before the rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ oto nibii tamɔ traktɔi ahe gbɛjianɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Farm equipment becomes scarce once the rains start. Planning mechanization early guarantees land preparation is completed on time so you do not miss the best planting window.
ga: Okwaayeli he nibii baafee nɔ ni faaa kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ. Gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛ tsɔnei tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ maa nɔ mi kɛtsɔ hiɛ akɛ abaagbe shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ naa yɛ be naa. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ samflɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ kpaaa gbee.

english: How can using farm machines save me money compared to hiring manual labor?
ga: Te tsɔne ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha mikɛ shika akafite kɛ akɛto nitsumɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Mechanization completes large field tasks in hours rather than weeks, reducing long-term labor costs and ensuring crop operations are done uniformly across the whole field.
ga: Tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa anyɛɔ agbeɔ shikpɔŋkuku mli nitsumɔi wuji anaa yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai amli moŋ fe otsii. Enɛ haa nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo baa shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. kɛ nɔmimaa akɛ agbe ŋmɔshi nitsumɔi lɛ anaa pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What does it mean for me to run my crop farm like a business?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ matsu mi tsei ahe ŋmɔ lɛ he nii akɛ jarayeli nitsumɔ?

english: Treating your farm as a business means tracking all money spent on seeds, labor, and tools to ensure that your crop yields generate a clear profit, rather than just food for survival.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ ni ooofee tamɔ jarayeli nitsumɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaakwɛ shika fɛɛ ni ofiteɔ yɛ dumɔwui, nitsulɔi, kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe lɛ mli koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ onibii ni oduɔ lɛ baaha sɛɛnamɔ ni he tse aba. Jeee niyenii kɛha wala kɛkɛ

english: Why should I keep a written record of all money spent on fertilizer and seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋma shika fɛɛ ni mifiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dumɔwui ahe lɛ he wolo?

english: Record-keeping helps you calculate your exact cost of production per acre so you can set fair selling prices and see which crop activities make or lose money.
ga: Nibii ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni obuɔ nibii ni afee lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo pɔtɛɛ yɛ acre kome mli lɛ he akɔntaa. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ oto jarayeli jara ni sa ni okwɛ ŋmɔshi nitsumɔi ni miifee shika loo miifite shika.

english: How does agreeing on a farm business plan help me manage my seasonal expenses?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni mikpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makwɛ be mli shika ni mifiteɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: A seasonal plan details when you will need money for land preparation, planting, and harvesting, preventing mid-season cash shortages that can cause crop failure.
ga: Be mli gbɛjianɔtoo tsɔɔ be mli ni shika he baahia bo kɛha shikpɔŋ he saamɔ, dumɔwui, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ. Tsi shika ni faaa yɛ be teŋgbɛ ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii afite lɛ naa.

english: Why is it important to know my expected harvest yield before I start planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ale yibiiwoo ni akpaa gbɛ dani aje dumɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Knowing your target yield allows you to secure buyers and arrange transportation early, protecting you from losing crop value to rot after harvest.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni otaoɔ ni ole lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni ohiɛɔ mɛi ni baahe nii lɛ amli ni otoɔ nibii ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ mra. Ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe sɛɛnamɔ ni baafite kɛ fitemɔ he yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why are wild animals and insects constantly eating my crops in the field before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi kɛ kooloi bibii yeɔ midumɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli be fɛɛ be dani minyɛɔ mikpaa lɛ?

english: Crops like corn and cassava are rich in food energy and moisture, making them an easy target for pests and animals, especially when natural vegetation in surrounding bushes becomes scarce during dry periods.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ niyenii hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli tsei ni yɔɔ tsei bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ faaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli

english: How can I prevent farm pests from destroying my maize while it is still growing on the stalk?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋma lɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Pests are attracted to the sweet grains as they mature; harvesting the maize as soon as it reaches maturity reduces the time pests have to attack it in the open field.
ga: Gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛyaa dumɔwui ni ŋɔɔ lɛ anɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Abele ni akpaa beni edara pɛ lɛ haa be ni esa akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ awui lɛ atutua abele yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ baa shi.

english: Is it better to store my harvested crops in the farm hut or bring them home immediately?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ baato ŋmɔ mli tsũ bibioo lɛ mli loo akɛya shia amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Bringing harvested crops home allows you to keep a closer eye on them, protect them from field rain and wild animals, and maintain better control over drying and storage conditions.
ga: Okpamɔ lɛ ni okɛbaa shia lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Buu tsei ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli kɛ koo mli kooloi ahe. ni ekwɛ bɔ ni egbiɔ kɛ bɔ ni atoɔ nii ahaa lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my stored corn turn into white powder and get small holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Insects called grain weevils burrow inside dry corn kernels to eat the nutritious center, leaving behind empty husks and fine grain dust.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli koni amɛye ŋmãa ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii. Eshiɔ ŋmei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛ dumɔwui amli sũ kpakpa.

english: How can I keep my harvested food good to eat for many months without it spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ niyenii ni akpa lɛ ato nyɔji babaoo ni efiteee?

english: Drying crops thoroughly under the sun lowers their moisture content, which prevents mold from growing and makes the food uninviting to pests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi lɛ haa hulutsoo baa shi. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii aya hiɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ sumɔɔɔ niyenii.

english: How do I know if my corn is completely dry and safe enough to put into storage bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbi kwraa ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe bɔ ni sa akɛ mikɛbaawo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ mli?

english: Dry corn kernels become very hard and produce a sharp, clear clinking sound when shaken together, showing that enough water has evaporated to prevent rotting.
ga: Abele ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ wa waa ni kɛ́ atswa amɛ ekome lɛ, amɛfeɔ gbee ni naa wa waa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ efo koni ekɛtsi fitemɔ naa.

english: Should I cut down every single tree on my land with my cutlass before planting crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ dade afo tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu?

english: Clearing all trees exposes the soil to hot sun and heavy rain, which damages soil fertility; leaving a few good trees provides gentle shade and protects the land.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Tsei kpakpai ni ajieɔ lɛ Tsei fioo komɛi haa hulutsoo blɛoo ni amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do my crop leaves look scorched after I clear all the surrounding shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mijie shade tsei ni ebɔle mihe lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plants unaccustomed to full sunlight can get heat stress when shade is removed too quickly, causing their leaves to burn and dry out.
ga: Tsei ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ etsɔko amɛhe lɛ baanyɛ ana dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛji ajie hulutsoo be lɛ mra tsɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: How does clearing weeds around my crops help them grow bigger food?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛduɔ niyenii wuji amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your plants, so removing them leaves all the food in the ground for your crops to use.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ojie nakai jwɛi lɛ, niyenii lɛ fɛɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do some trees grow back quickly after I cut them down during land preparation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daa oya nɛkɛ beni mifo amɛ be mli ni misaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Many native trees have deep, strong root systems underground that store food energy, allowing them to shoot up fresh stems even after the top is cut off.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei babaoo yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ. Enɛ haa amɛwoɔ tsei niji heei beni afo amɛyiteŋgbɛ lɛ po sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and lose water faster than their roots can absorb it. Planting shade crops like plantains beside them shields the tender leaves from sunburn and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛfiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baabu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost near the base helps the plant regain its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Which direction should the buds point when I am planting cassava stem cuttings in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei niji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should always be planted with the small buds or 'eyes' pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots must bend around to reach the surface, which weakens the plant and reduces tuber growth.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji okɛ tsei shwieɔ shi Esa akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ abɔle ehe koni eshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha tuber lɛ adalɛ aba shi.

english: What is causing ragged holes and dirt that looks like sawdust inside the funnels of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the maize plant to feed on tender leaves. Applying recommended treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning or late evening helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye nɔ.

english: Fertilizers must dissolve in soil moisture for crop roots to suck them up. Applying fertilizer to completely dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste the fertilizer since it sits unused on top of the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without forming any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme high temperatures can dry out tomato pollen, preventing the flowers from getting fertilized. When pollination fails, the plant naturally drops the unfertilized flowers to save energy.
ga: He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato pollen lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo fɔmɔ Kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii Tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fɔfɔi bɛ mli lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread easily and positions them to catch maximum sunlight. More sunlight allows the leaves to make more food, resulting in larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ, ni ekɛtoɔ he ko ni hulu la lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ nɔ babaoo. Hulu la babaoo haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafee wuji.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans on my farm help the next crop I plant there?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni miduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have beneficial bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the legumes are harvested, this extra nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa Nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.
