english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and weak even if I apply fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong root systems that steal food, fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops. If you do not clear the weeds early, they will eat the fertilizer intended for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi oya lɛ, Amɛbaaye ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop during the hot afternoon even if the soil was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi moŋ?

english: Wilting during hot afternoons is a defense mechanism where plants close small pores on their leaves to prevent excessive water loss. As long as the soil has moisture, the leaves will bounce back upright in the cooler evening.
ga: Gbimɔ yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. he ni tso lɛ tsiɔ bu bibioo ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ naa koni nu akafite fe nine Bei abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ baa lɛ baaku esɛɛ kɛya amɛhe ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight because their roots are small and their leaves lose water faster than they can take it in. Planting shade crops like plantains around young cocoa protects them from direct sun and keeps the air around them moist until they are strong enough.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛbaa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni okwɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ nɔ Ha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi cacao lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is the main nutrient needed for growing green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or adding well-decomposed animal manure will supply the needed nutrient to make them green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ waa ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha amɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield very little if I plant seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee ni ewoɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely together, the plants end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough room and nutrients to grow strong and produce a good harvest.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a widespread pest in Ghana that targets young maize. They hide deep inside the growing tip of the plant to feed, so applying neem oil solution or recommended pesticides directly into the central leaves helps control them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni egbɛ eshwa Ghana ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ koni amɛye niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ mli tsofa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ wo baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the fruit from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa aduawai lɛ adalɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the plant's juices, or by viruses carried by these insects. Controlling these pests early with neem-based sprays helps keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Kudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni neem yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet for a long time during heavy rains because excess water starves the roots of air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily and protects the tubers from rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ amli nu afee shoo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya, ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in direct sunlight to make food that feeds the underground tuber. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground to prevent fungal diseases and helps the plant absorb full light so the yams grow large.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ajie amɛbaai lɛ awo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛjɛ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni eha tso lɛ aŋɔ la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni sweet potato lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a condition called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or when soil moisture keeps changing from wet to dry. Watering your plants regularly and adding agricultural lime to the soil prevents this.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli daa kɛ okwaayeli mli ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, shields the soil from the hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly. It keeps the soil cool and moist for the roots while stopping weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu akatsɔ oya Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why is it beneficial to grow cowpeas or beans together with my maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu cowpeas loo beans kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil, which feeds the maize naturally. Growing them together also covers the ground to keep weeds away and improves soil health.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ Companion planting hu haa ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli koni jwɛi akabote mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I use dirty river water near a galamsey site to water them?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ faa ni bɛŋkɛ Galamsey lɛ mli lɛ wo amɛnɔ?

english: Water contaminated by illegal mining contains harsh chemicals like mercury and cyanides. Using it to irrigate your farm can poison the crops, stunt their growth, turn their leaves yellow, and make the harvested food unsafe to eat.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa tamɔ mercury kɛ cyanide yɛ nu ni shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ mli efite lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛtsu nii ni okɛshwie oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofa awo tsei lɛ amli. shweremɔ blɛoo lɛ baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa niyenii ni akpa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning yellow and burning even though I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa eyɛ mli akɛ miha lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: When crops absorb water mixed with toxic chemicals, the root system gets damaged and burned. The plant can no longer draw nutrients from the soil, causing the leaves to yellow, dry up, and look burnt.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ŋɔ nu ni akɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei efutu mli lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshãa. Tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, egbiɔ ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã.

english: Can chemical water that flows onto my land damage my soil for future farming?
ga: Ani tsofa nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, harmful chemicals from polluted water soak deep into the earth and stay in the soil for a long time. This ruins soil fertility and makes it difficult for new seeds to germinate or grow healthily in future seasons.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara ni jɛɔ nu fɔŋ mli lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni ehiɔ jɛmɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui heei akɛ amɛakwɛ̃ loo amɛkwɛ̃ waa yɛ wɔsɛɛ bei amli.

english: How can I know if my crop is sick from a disease or if it is suffering from bad water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo kɛji akɛ nu bɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ?

english: Plant diseases usually start on a few plants and spread gradually with spots or mold. Chemical damage from polluted water usually affects large areas of crops at once, causing sudden leaf burn, wilting, or stunted growth after watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai jeɔ shishi yɛ tsei fioo komɛi amli ni amɛyaa hiɛ fiofio. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni jɛɔ nu ni mli ewo muji mli lɛ fiteɔ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ahe yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa trukaa, amɛgboɔ, loo amɛdaraaa kwraa kɛ́ awo amɛ nu sɛɛ.

english: Is it safe to sell and eat vegetables grown next to a polluted stream?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaahɔ aduawai ni adu yɛ faai ni mli ewo muji lɛ ahe lɛ ni aye?

english: No, crops absorb whatever is in the soil and water through their roots. Vegetables grown with chemical-polluted water can carry toxic residues inside their stems and leaves, making them dangerous for human consumption.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛgbalaa shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli nibii. Aduawai ni akɛ nu ni tsofai ewo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná tsofai fɔji ni eshwɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. ni ehaa efeɔ oshara kɛha adesai ayeli

english: Why do my young seedlings die immediately after heavy rains wash runoff water into my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ trukaa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rainwater flowing across polluted land carries concentrated chemicals directly onto your farm. Young seedlings have delicate roots that burn and die quickly when exposed to these chemical-heavy runoffs.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ hei ni muji yɔɔ lɛ kɛ tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ yaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji tsofai ni hoɔ babaoo lɛ bote mli.

english: How do chemicals in water affect the way crop roots grow under the soil?
ga: Te tsofai ni yɔɔ nu mli lɛ saa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei shishifãi lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Healthy roots spread out to search for food and moisture, but toxic chemicals destroy root tips. This leaves the plant with short, black, or weak roots that cannot support healthy growth or withstand dry weather.
ga: Shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ taomɔ mli. Shi tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ kuku, ediŋŋ, loo egbɔjɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aye abua ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ loo amɛŋmɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe gbɛ.

english: Can I plant something around my farm to protect my crops from dirty runoff water coming from outside?
ga: Mibaanyɛ makwɛ nɔ ko yɛ he. Ani manyɛ mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ nu fɔŋ ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ he?

english: Yes, planting dense boundary plants like vetiver grass or deep-rooted trees around your farm acts as a natural barrier. These plants slow down chemical runoff and help trap pollutants before they reach your main crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni adu ni eyi obɔ tamɔ vetiver jwɛi loo tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni bɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ haa tsofai lɛ hoɔ fioo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ muji dani amɛshɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if a local stream is safe enough to fetch water for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji maŋ lɛ mli faa ko yɛ shweshweeshwe bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu?

english: If the water is unnaturally muddy, oily, smells strange, or has no living fish, frogs, or insects in it, it is likely polluted with dangerous chemicals and should not be used on crops.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ mli eyi kɛ muji, fɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, loo loo, ŋmeii, loo kooloi bɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ni jeee adebɔɔ nɔ. Etamɔ nɔ ni tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara ewo mli. ni esaaa akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ

english: Why are my cassava and yam tubers much smaller this year despite planting on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava kɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ faaa kwraa afi nɛɛ? Adu yɛ be naa?

english: When plants are continuously exposed to low levels of toxic water or contaminated soil, they spend all their energy trying to survive chemical stress rather than producing large roots and tubers, leading to low harvest yields.
ga: Beni tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu ni yɔɔ gbeyei loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji ni baa shi lɛ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ. Tsei baafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛje tsofai ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ sisi agbo kɛ bulb. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly when the weather gets very hot during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural survival trick to save water. When leaves curl inward, less of their surface is exposed to the sun and dry air, which stops the plant from losing moisture too quickly.
ga: Abɛi baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛbuɔ nu he. Beni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli lɛ, hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ akafite nu oya tsɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from too much water or from lack of rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu babaoo loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii miigboi?

english: When crops lack rain, their leaves get dry, crisp, and wilt down. When crops have too much water sitting around their roots, the leaves turn yellow and stems turn soft or soggy because the roots are drowning and cannot breathe in flooded soil.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nugbɔ lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ. Beni tsei lɛ nu babaoo ebɔle amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ efo nu mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: What causes the flowers on my vegetable crops to fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Flowers usually drop off when the plant suffers sudden stress, such as intense heat, dry soil, or very high winds. If the plant feels it doesn't have enough water or energy to raise a fruit, it drops the flower to save itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ko kpe trukaa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa. Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ ebɛ nu loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni etsa ehe.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even though the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is hungry for key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that too much water has damaged the roots so they can no longer absorb food from the land.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii titrii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu babaoo efite shishifãi lɛ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my crops while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal sunlight, water, and plant food directly from your crops. Removing them early ensures your crop gets all the resources it needs to grow strong and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛ ni ooojie mra Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting the exact same crop on the same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ dumɔ he yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows pests and diseases that attack that crop to build up in the soil. Changing crops starves the pests and lets the soil recover.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei sumɔɔ lɛ afite. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ni ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my crops grow very tall and skinny but fail to give good yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi kɛlɛ waa ni amɛhe ejɔ shi amɛwooo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together or shaded, they stretch upwards competing for sunlight. Because the plant spends all its energy growing tall to reach light, it has no energy left to produce thick stems or heavy fruits.
ga: Beni tsei eyi obɔ loo amɛhe ewo hulu Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛ́ amɛmiida yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná la. No hewɔ lɛ, hewalɛ ko eshwɛɛɛ ni baaha aná tsei ni mli tse loo aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why does planting leguminous crops like beans or groundnuts improve my farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Legume plants have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. This acts as free, natural fertilizer that feeds the crops planted next to them or in the following season.
ga: Legumes yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii. loo be ni baa lɛ mli

english: Why do cassava roots take almost a full year to harvest while maize is ready in a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi muu fɛɛ dani akpaa yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize produces its grain above ground in a quick life cycle, while cassava slowly builds up heavy starch storage roots underground over many months before they are fully mature.
ga: Abɛi woɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni wala sɛɛkuu yaa oya. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ fiofio Efeɔ shishifãi ni kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nyɔji babaoo dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why must I bury seeds at a specific depth in the ground instead of just scattering them on top of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ pɔtɛɛ ko lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ dumɔwui lɛ eshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds left on the surface dry out quickly in the sun or get eaten by birds and ants. Burying them at the proper depth keeps them moist so they can sprout, and anchor their early roots securely in the dirt.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ loo okpoi kɛ ŋmeii ye amɛ. Kɛ́ ofu amɛ yɛ he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni amɛdara. ni emɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and sensitive to strong sunlight. Without shade crops like plantains or shade trees to shelter them, direct heat burns their leaves and dries out the soil, turning the leaves yellow and slowing down their growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa amɛdaraa oya.

english: You should wait until the main rainy season brings steady rainfall for several days to thoroughly soak the soil. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if dry weather returns immediately after.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli koni oná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa gbii babaoo ni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Which direction should I point cassava stem cuttings when putting them into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmei nine lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should always be planted with the buds or nodes pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems struggle to grow properly, leading to weak plants and very small root yields.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ be fɛɛ be ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Ebaawa akɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu faaa kwraa.

english: Why do my young maize plants look pale light-green and refuse to grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ji eŋɔli ni amɛkpooɔ ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Pale green or yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient crops need to grow green leaves and tall stalks. Adding organic manure or appropriate nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni eda kɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei kakadaji. Kɛ́ akɛ organic loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su kɛ dalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it dangerous to let weeds grow close to my young crops during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mahã jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and compete aggressively for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early allows your crops to get all the nourishment they need to build strong stems and roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛma tsei kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in damp, dark, and highly humid conditions. Pruning dense tree branches lets air and sunlight in, which reduces humidity and helps prevent the fungus from destroying your pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, duŋ, kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Tso niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii efiteɔ o-pods lɛ.

english: Is it good practice for me to plant plantain and cassava together on the same plot?
ga: Ani plantains kɛ cassava ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa?

english: Yes, intercropping plantain and cassava works well because cassava roots grow deeper into the ground while plantain provides light shade above. They draw nutrients from different soil levels, allowing you to harvest two useful crops from one plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ plantains kɛ cassava woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ cassava shishifãi lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni plantain lɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ fioo yɛ ŋwɛi. Amɛgbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi anɔ. Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants dry up and drop off without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist by mulching around the base helps the plant retain its flowers and turn them into healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ehaa efeɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and small green worms inside the tops of the plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that feeds on the soft inner leaves of young maize. Spotting them early and applying recommended neem extracts or safe insecticides saves your crop from major damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ ŋmei bibii amli baai lɛ. Kɛ́ ona amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ okɛtsu nii loo tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaye abua ni akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ waa.

english: Why should I start my pepper seeds in a shaded nursery before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ dani mikɛ amɛ aya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are very small and tender, so hot sun and heavy rain in an open field can easily kill or wash them away. A shaded nursery protects young seedlings until they develop strong roots and stems ready for the main farm.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe yɛ mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baanyɛ agbe amɛ loo efo amɛ oya. Tsũ mli ŋmɔ lɛ baabu dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaaná shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔ wulu lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and dry up when I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to hot sunlight, which burns their young leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving selected large shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantain creates a canopy that shelters young cocoa until they mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he waa. Enɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu tsei ni baa be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves are a signal that maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to build green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure near the base of the plant restores healthy green leaf growth.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmeii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ awo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my farm make the soil better for my next corn crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen gas from the air and traps it in the soil through their roots. When the legume crop dies, that trapped nitrogen acts as free fertilizer for the corn planted after it.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei gboi Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmãa ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava producing huge stems and many green leaves, but very tiny tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tso agbo kɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in soil that has excess leafy nutrients, it puts all its energy into leaf growth rather than storing starch in its roots. Balanced nutrients encourage root tuber expansion.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei mli niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Etsɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ kɛyaa baa lɛ dalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, niyenii ni ja lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out short, bent, and ugly instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kukuji, amɛbɔleɔ amɛhe, ni amɛhe bɛ fɛo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers shape themselves according to the soil structure around them. If the soil is hard, stony, or compacted, the growing tuber cannot push downwards easily, so building high, loose earth mounds helps yams grow long and straight.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji nɔ ni feɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shi mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ofee gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-sweet potato lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do the leaves inside the center funnel of my young maize plants suddenly look chewed up with small dots of waste?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ tamɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Aye?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf roll during the heat of the day to feed on new leaves. Checking the funnel early allows you to spray or clear the caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ gbɛ lɛ nɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofa shwieɔ loo ogbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava bushes twisting, turning yellow, and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by the cassava mosaic virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck plant sap. Using virus-free stem cuttings during planting prevents this sickness from starting in your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies plant sap sucker lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni virus bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela nɛɛ akaje shishi yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off to the ground without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the air becomes too hot, or when the plant experiences water stress from dry spells. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the blossoms stay on and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni tsei naa nu he haomɔ kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my green pepper fruits developing soft, pale spots on the side that faces the midday sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili aduawai eŋɔli lɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ su ni tsakeɔ yɛ afã ni kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: This condition is called sunscald, which happens when direct heat bakes the fruit tissue because the plant does not have enough leaf canopy to shade its peppers. Ensuring good leaf growth helps cover and protect the fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ scald. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ha aduawai lɛ amli fãji lɛ shã. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ baai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni daraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ aduawai lɛ teeɔ shi ni ebuɔ he.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and greener than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep root systems naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to steal water and fertilizer faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops the sole access to food in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ pɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant cannot get enough nitrogen from the soil, which is the main nutrient needed for green leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or logs the soil with water, stopping the roots from breathing.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adara lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii loo ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: This is a natural survival defense. The cassava plant droops its leaves to shield them from direct sunlight and reduce water loss through evaporation. Once the sun cools down in the evening, the leaves will stand up again.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ hebuu. Cassava tsei lɛ feɔ amɛbaai lɛ kukuji koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eha nu ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi Kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Baai lɛ baadamɔ shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ tomato ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they face heat stress, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the plant feels stressed by high temperatures, it saves its energy to stay alive rather than putting energy into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha amɛ. Beni tsei nuɔ he akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ miigba amɛnaa lɛ Tsei toɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi wala mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee aduawai

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall and bushy with lots of leaves but very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔji ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen, often from over-using certain fertilizers. High nitrogen encourages leafy branch growth instead of flowering, so the plant forgets to produce fruit.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ daa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ hiɛ kpaa nɔ akɛ ebaawo yibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under the strong sun. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist for the young cocoa trees.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hia kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛha kookoo tsei bibii.

english: Why do my yam vines produce smaller tubers if I do not stake them with sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji mikɛ nine tswaaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up off the ground into the sunlight. Maximum leaf exposure to sunlight lets the plant make plenty of food, which travels down to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ wo hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni eyakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes in the middle of my maize leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The adult moth lays eggs on the maize plant, and the hatched caterpillars hide inside the leaf funnel during the day and feed on the soft growing center during the cool night.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Mots ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa tsei anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai amli lasu tsuji amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni amɛtao niyenii yɛ hei ni gbekɛbii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable roots rot and turn black when rain falls continuously for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ diŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like people do. When water stays pooled in the soil for too long, air cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown, die, and rot from soil fungi.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often only wets the hot surface layer of soil and is followed by intense sun that bakes the ground. Seeds need continuous, deep soil moisture to germinate, so it is safer to wait until the rains become regular.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant the exact same crop on the same farm every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. It also allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are my young maize leaves showing small ragged holes and saw-dust-like waste in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmei bibioo ko yɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central growing whorl of the plant during the day and eat the soft leaves, which weakens the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni no haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning yellowish-green and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: This curling and discoloration is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, caused by a virus spread by whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. It reduces the plant's leaf area, preventing the roots from growing into large tubers.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Nɔ ni kɛ nakai baa ji hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ baa shi Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn turning pale yellow in a V-shape while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishi baai lɛ etsɔ V-shaped pale yellow yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant moves the limited nitrogen it has from its older leaves up to the newer leaves to keep growing.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli kɛyaa baai heei amli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering or long dry periods.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔtɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why should I avoid planting my maize seeds immediately after the very first light rainfall of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui adumɔ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first light rain is often followed by a sudden dry spell. If seeds sprout and the rain stops for a week, the soil dries out and the delicate young roots die before the main rainy season settles.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ahum ni baa trukaa lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsi kome. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil through their root nodules, which naturally improves soil fertility for the neighboring maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ kɛha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my plants with dry grass keep my crops alive longer during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, blocks direct hot sunlight from evaporating soil water, keeping the root area cool and holding moisture in the ground longer.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa kɛjɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to place long bamboo or wood stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ ŋmei loo tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce enough energy to send down to the roots. Staking also lifts leaves off the damp ground, preventing soil diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ahe tsei kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain stem, they fight for water, plant food, and light. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest ones to produce large bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) lɛ daraa kɛbɔleɔ Tso kome lɛ fa tsɔ. Ekɛ nu, tsei aniyenii, kɛ la yeɔ akaŋ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know the right amount of chemical to mix with water so I do not damage my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofai ni sa ni akɛfutuɔ nu lɛ? bɔni afee ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ

english: Using too much chemical can burn crop leaves and damage soil health, while using too little will not clear pests. Always use the specified measuring cup provided by your extension officer to get the exact dosage for your knapsack sprayer.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ. Yɛ be mli ni akɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ nyɛŋ ajie tsɛŋemɔ helai. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ susumɔ kɔɔpoo ni o-extension agent lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ atsu nii koni onine ashɛ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ o-sɛɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray farm chemicals on my field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when weather is cool. High heat during midday can cause the chemical to evaporate too quickly or scorch wet leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ loo eshã baai ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to store leftover mixed farm chemicals in normal drinking bottles?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ baawo nu ni anuɔ daa lɛ mli?

english: Never store farm chemicals in drinking bottles or unlabelled containers because children or family members might accidentally consume them. Keep all chemicals in original containers locked away from food and water.
ga: Kaakɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo nu ni anuɔ loo tsɛnsii ni aŋmalako nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ amli. Ejaakɛ gbekɛbii loo weku mli bii baanyɛ aye lɛ yɛ oshara mli. Ha tsofai fɛɛ awo amɛ shishijee tsɛnsii lɛ amli, ni okɛ niyenii kɛ nu akabote mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that maize plants are lacking important nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the soil is waterlogged. Applying the correct fertilizer at the right time restores healthy green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to insect attacks, extreme heat, or irregular watering. Protecting crops from pests and keeping soil moist helps flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi tutuamɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ kɛ pepper fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains provides living umbrellas that shield young cocoa and retain soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ yucca tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, they compete fiercely for sunlight, groundwater, and nutrients, resulting in small, thin roots. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to build large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee bulbs agboi.

english: Can I just scatter fertilizer on top of dry soil, or do I need to bury it near the roots?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ? Aloo esa akɛ afu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ?

english: Burying fertilizer slightly in the moist soil near the root zone prevents heavy rains from washing it away and stops heat from evaporating nutrients into the air.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko wo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ lɛ. ni ekpaa la ni tsoɔ lɛ koni ekaha niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli

english: How do wild weeds growing close to my crop roots slow down my yield?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni koo mli jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ aha mi yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves by stealing fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight meant for your crops, which weakens the plants and leaves less food for fruit development.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni niyenii fioo pɛ eshiɔ kɛhaa aduawai lɛ akwɛmɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Excess shoots consume nutrients and energy away from the main stem. Removing extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong ones allows the main plant to yield much larger plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajie ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ ajie ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: Why do my farm chemicals lose their power when I leave the bottles sitting outside under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛ́ mishi tɔi lɛ yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight and high temperatures break down the active ingredients in liquid farm medicines, making them weak and ineffective against crop pests and diseases.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni yɔɔ tsofai ni ji nu mli yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsofai nɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai ahe.

english: Should I keep my crop protection medicines in a cool, dark room instead of outside?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ awo tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli ewo duŋ mli moŋ fe kpo nɔ?

english: Yes, storing agricultural chemicals in a cool, dark place protects them from heat and light degradation, preserving their effectiveness until you are ready to use them.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli mli tsofai ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ la ni baafite amɛ lɛ he. Ehaa etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ofeɔ klalo akɛ okɛbaatsu nii.

english: Why should I only spray pest medicine on my crops early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ pɛ?

english: Midday heat causes liquid sprays to evaporate into the air too quickly before working, and strong afternoon sunlight combined with chemicals can scorch plant leaves.
ga: Gbi teŋ latsaa lɛ ha nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani ebɔi nitsumɔ. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shwane mli ni akɛ tsofai fata he lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai.

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves during intense afternoon heat to reduce their surface area, which helps them retain moisture and prevent leaf burn.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa baai lɛ shãaa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without forming fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: High temperatures sterilize tomato pollen, preventing flowers from being fertilized, which causes the unpollinated flowers to drop off the plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbeɔ tomato mli ŋmeii. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo fɔmɔ mli Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni fɔfɔi ewooo mli lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do young nursery seedlings need partial shade instead of direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ he hiaa ni amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have delicate leaf tissue and shallow roots; partial shade keeps soil temperatures low and prevents the sun from drying them out before roots fully develop.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baa fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be fioo yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baa shi, ni ehaaa egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: Why do my stored maize seeds spoil faster when I keep them in a hot, enclosed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni aŋã mli lɛ?

english: Heat traps moisture inside stored grain containers, creating a warm environment where mold and grain-boring insects multiply quickly.
ga: Dɔlɛ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ tsɛnsi ni akɛ dumɔwui lɛ toɔ mli lɛ mli. ni feɔ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ Fungi kɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã oya.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in very hot dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive soil temperature signals to seeds that conditions are too harsh to survive, causing them to stay dormant or die before germination.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ tsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ akɛ shihilɛi lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ehi shi. loo egbo dani ekwɛ̃

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot faster when kept in a warm room without airflow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested yams continue to breathe and produce heat; without cool ventilation, trapped heat accelerates tissue breakdown and fungal growth.
ga: Atomɔ ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ. Dɔlɛ ni abua naa lɛ haa fãji lɛ fiteɔ oya ni ŋmeii lɛ hu daa.

english: Why do my harvested green vegetables turn yellow so quickly when left under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikpaa aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Heat from direct sunlight causes harvested leaves to lose moisture rapidly, breaking down the green chlorophyll pigments and causing premature wilting.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ haa baai ni akpa lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Efiteɔ klorofil ni ji ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa oya.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings wilting and dying when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct heat. They need shade crops, such as plantains or temporary shade trees, planted next to them to block harsh sunlight and keep the soil moist during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛdu tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi koni amɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ

english: How do I know the correct spacing to use when planting my crops in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni esa akɛ atsɔ nɔ midu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants. For crops like cocoa, leaving about 3 meters between trees also allows enough room for air circulation, which prevents disease.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ. kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo Aaafee mitai 3 ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa tsɔɔ mli. ni tsiɔ helai anaa lɛ

english: How can I tell if my farm land is suitable for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: Good cocoa land needs deep, fertile soil that drains water well so roots do not rot. Soil that stays waterlogged or is too rocky will hinder root growth and lead to poor harvests.
ga: Kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni nu baanyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbooo. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ loo tɛi babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ akafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Black pods are usually caused by a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Clearing surrounding weeds and pruning excess branches helps air move through the farm and keeps the pods dry, reducing disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji black pods lɛ baa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ Kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni ŋmeii lɛ ni agbiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: Why is it important for me to prune or cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo maŋɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unproductive, dead, or diseased branches. This directs the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier pods while letting sunlight reach the main stems to discourage pests and fungal growth.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ. gbo loo hela Enɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha hulu la lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he koni enijiaŋ aje wui kɛ ŋmeii ni baa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast around my young plants and slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mihe lɛ? Mi tsei lɛ miifee tsei bibii ni amɛmiiha amɛdalɛ miiba shi.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds regularly gives your main crop full access to the nourishment it needs to grow strong and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi daa lɛ, ebaaha tsei ni okwɛɔ amɛ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do I know when my cocoa soil is running out of nutrients and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ bɛ mi-cocoa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, crop leaves often turn pale or yellow, and trees produce fewer or smaller pods. Applying the right cocoa fertilizer replenishes the essential minerals in the soil so the trees can produce well.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, bei pii lɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni tso lɛ baawo ŋmeii fioo loo bibii. Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nibii ni he hiaa ni baaha tso lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Where can I find reliable, high-quality cocoa seeds or seedlings to start my farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana kookoo ŋmeii loo kookoo dumɔwui ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛje ŋmɔ shishi?

english: You can obtain improved, disease-resistant cocoa varieties through local agricultural extension officers or recognized cocoa farmer cooperatives that distribute certified planting materials.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona kookoo henɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he nitsulɔi loo kookoo okwaafoi akui ni akpɛlɛ amɛnɔ ni hɔ̃ɔ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Why are insects damaging the stems and young pods on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ?

english: Pests like capsids feed on the sap of tender cocoa shoots and pods, causing wounds that weaken the tree and let in diseases. Spraying approved treatments at the right time of year protects the crop from heavy damage.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ kookoo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa pilamɔi ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ baa, ni ekɛ helai baa. Tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ fitemɔ ni mli wa he.

english: How can working with local farmer leaders and extension officers improve my farm's harvest?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni mikɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi ahiɛnyiɛlɔi kɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii aha nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Extension officers and experienced group leaders provide up-to-date training on proper crop care, help troubleshoot disease outbreaks, and connect you to official support programs for farm inputs.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ kuu mli hiɛnyiɛlɔi kɛ tsɔsemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ haa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ he. Ye obua ni atsu helai ni baa lɛ ahe naagba lɛ he nii. ni ekɛ bo tsa yelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the plants lack nitrogen, a vital soil nutrient, or when excess rainwater leaves the roots waterlogged and unable to absorb food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Niyenii nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ ewo nu mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water accumulates in heavy clay soil without proper drainage, or when fungal diseases attack the stem bases during prolonged rainy seasons.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ tutua tso lɛ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my corn seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which results in weak stalks and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni no haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Growing cassava repeatedly on the same plot exhausts specific soil nutrients and causes pests and root diseases to build up in the soil, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shishifãi ahe helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are small worms eating holes into the leaves and cobs of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mibai kɛ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These worms are typically fall armyworms, which hide inside the growing leaf whorls and feed on young crop tissues if not controlled early in the planting season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni afolɔ, ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe fãji kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra yɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested dry beans develop tiny holes and turn to dust in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ebatsɔ sũ yɛ nitoohe

english: Bean weevils lay eggs on the pods or beans, and after harvest, the hatching larvae burrow into the seeds to feed, destroying your stored grain.
ga: Pea ŋmei fɔɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii anɔ. ni yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli koni amɛyana niyenii. Kpata dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmãa baadu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil, which enriches the land and feeds the nearby maize naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛɔ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has lost its strength before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ dani madu nii?

english: Soil is weak if it looks pale and dusty, hardens easily after rain, or if previous crops grew slowly with pale stems and tiny leaves without weeds growing vigorously.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛji etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ sũ. Ewaa oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ dara blɛoo, ni eyɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ baai bibii ni jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ, eda waa.

english: Dry harmattan winds strip moisture from leaves faster than roots can draw water from dry soil, forcing the tree to drop leaves to save itself from dying.
ga: Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛhere ehe kɛjɛ gbele mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when temperatures become excessively hot or when the plant experiences extreme moisture stress during the flowering stage.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni tsei lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ ni naa wa waa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why are some of my tomatoes turning yellow on the plant while others stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ ekomɛi miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu ji ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Tomatoes do not ripen all at the same time. Green tomatoes gradually turn light yellow, then orange, and finally red as they mature. The yellow stage shows that the fruit has stopped growing in size and is beginning to soften and sweeten.
ga: Tomatoi lɛ fɛɛ kwɛɛɛ shikome. Tomato eŋɔli baatsake fiofio kɛya ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse Sɛɛ mli lɛ ebatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni naagbee lɛ, etsɔɔ tsuru kɛji eda kwraa. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ aduawai lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ebatsɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomatoes turn pale yellow on one side instead of turning full red under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ fa kome moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔŋ kwraa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When tomatoes receive too much direct, harsh sunlight without foliage to shade them, they suffer from sunscald. The intense heat destroys the red pigment, leaving pale yellow or tough white patches on the skin.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ ni hulutsoo bɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baatsɔ hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ hulu lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsuru lɛ. Eshiɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I pick all my tomatoes at once, or should I harvest them bit by bit as they change color?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tomatoi lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo esa akɛ mafolɔ amɛ fiofio be mli ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe su lɛ?

english: Harvesting tomatoes in stages as they turn yellow or light orange is best. It frees up energy for the remaining green tomatoes to grow, spreads out your labor, and prevents mature fruits from spoiling on the vine.
ga: Tomato ni akpaa yɛ fãi amli Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tomato lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ehaa tomato eŋɔli ni eshwɛ lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛdaraa. Jaa onitsumɔ lɛ ni otsi yibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it good to mix soft red tomatoes with hard yellow ones in the same basket for market?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafutu tomato tsuru ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ tomato ŋmɔŋ ni wa yɛ tsɛnsi kome mli koni akɛmaje jara nɔ?

english: It is better to separate them. Fully ripe red tomatoes easily crush under weight and release gases that cause firmer yellow tomatoes to ripen and spoil faster than they should.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooogbala amɛteŋ. Tomato tsuru ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ etsitsinɔnii lɛ hewɔ ni ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa tomato ŋmɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ shwereɔ ni egboɔ oya fe bɔ ni esa akɛ efee lɛ kpo.

english: Why are my tomato leaves turning yellow before the fruits are even ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani aduawai lɛ po shwere lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant lacks nutrients like nitrogen or is suffering from excess water around the roots. Correcting the feeding helps the leaves stay green so they can feed the growing fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, loo eyɛ nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Niyenii ni ajajeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli koni amɛye aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Can I sell my tomatoes when they are still yellow, or must I wait until they turn completely red?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ tomato be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi tomato lɛ baatsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ kwraa?

english: Many market women prefer buying yellow tomatoes because they are firmer and survive long transport journeys without getting crushed. They naturally turn red by the time they reach the final consumer.
ga: Jarayeli yei babaoo sumɔɔ ni amɛhe tomato ni ji ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ, ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ shi yɛ gbɛ kakadaŋŋ nɔ ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli. Etsɔɔ etsuru yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji eshɛ naagbee nihɔɔlɔ lɛ he.

english: Why am I struggling to sell my harvest even though I established a regular buyer in the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maya haomɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ mli koni mayahɔ̃ɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Ni miyɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii daa yɛ jara lɛ nɔ?

english: A regular buyer may stop purchasing if there is an oversupply of produce in the market or if consumer demand drops. Relying on a single buyer can be risky, so it is helpful to find multiple sales channels.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii daa lɛ baanyɛ akpa nihɔɔmɔ kɛji akɛ nibii ni fa fe nine yɛ jara lɛ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ ba shi. He ni akɛaafɔ̃ hɔlɔ kome nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara. No hewɔ lɛ, eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ oookwɛ gbɛi srɔtoi ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahɔ̃ɔ nii lɛ amli.

english: How do I decide whether to grow tomatoes for selling in the market or for my family to eat at home?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ makwɛ tomato koni mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ loo mahã miweku lɛ niyenii yɛ shia?

english: Vegetables like tomatoes require money for pesticides and fertilizers, making them ideal cash crops to generate income, whereas staple food crops like cassava or maize are better suited for home food security.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ tomato he miihia shika kɛha tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa efeɔ shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shika ni anáa. be mli ni niyenii ni aduɔ titri tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shia niyenii shweshweeshwefeemɔ.

english: What can I do with my harvested tomatoes when the local market is full and buyers refuse to take them?
ga: Mɛni mifeɔ kɛ tomato ni akpa lɛ beni maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ mɛi ni heɔ lɛ kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaahe lɛ?

english: When fresh markets are flooded, you can process tomatoes into paste or dry them in the sun to sell later when scarcity raises prices, preventing your fresh harvest from going to waste.
ga: Kɛji akɛ jarayelihe hee lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ tomato afee krim loo ogbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni okɛhɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli beni nibii ni faaa lɛ haa jara yaa hiɛ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi nibii heei ni okɛwo mli lɛ anaa koni ekafite.

english: How can I store my harvested tomatoes so they don't rot quickly on hot days?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ ato koni ekafite oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ?

english: Keep harvested tomatoes in well-ventilated wooden crates placed in a cool, shaded area. Avoid packing them tightly in airtight plastic bags, which trap heat and accelerate decay.
ga: Okɛ tomato ni akpa lɛ awo tso adeka ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli mli. Okɛwo he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ plastic kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ amli lɛ he. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ ni ehaa fitemɔ yaa oya.

english: How many times can I reuse planting pieces from my own yam harvest before buying fresh ones?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ mikɛ fãi ni jɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ dani mahe sweet potato hee?

english: You can usually replant seed yams from your own farm for about three crop cycles. After three seasons, hidden diseases build up inside the roots, so buying fresh, clean seed yams helps keep your yields high.
ga: Bei pii lɛ obaanyɛ odu sweet potatoes kɛjɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ mli yɛ aaafee ŋmɔshi nibii 3 mli. Yɛ bei etɛ sɛɛ lɛ, helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni he tse ni afee ehee lɛ ni ooohe lɛ baaye abua ni onibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I clean my cutlasses and farm tools when moving between different crop fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsumɔ mi dadei kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ miitsi ŋmɔji ateŋ?

english: Plant diseases and germs stick to tool blades unseen. Washing your tools prevents you from carrying sickness from infected plants over to your healthy crops.
ga: Tsei ahe helai kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ dɛŋdadei ahe tsɔji ahe ni anaaa. Odɛŋdadei ni ooofɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bo ni okɛ helai akajɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my yams start rotting in the soil even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Underground rot is often caused by diseases carried inside infected seed pieces or dirty soil. Using disease-free seed yams and planting in clean soil prevents tubers from rotting underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni mɔmɔ dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi fitemɔ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni hela bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: What is the benefit of buying certified clean seed yams instead of regular ones from the local market?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni he tse ni yɔɔ odaseyeli he lɛ hemɔ he moŋ fe ni ooohe kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Certified seed yams are multiplied in special sterile conditions without diseases. Market seed yams may look good on the outside but often carry hidden viruses that reduce crop growth.
ga: Akɛ sweet potatoes ni awo he odase lɛ woɔ shihilɛi krɛdɛɛi ni hela bɛ mli lɛ amli. Jarayeli dumɔwui yams baanyɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ, helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni haa tsei adalɛ baa shi lɛ yɛ.

english: What should I do immediately if I notice one of my yam vines turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina akɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ eko etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eegbo?

english: Dig up and burn or bury that sick plant far away from your farm, then wash your hands and tools before touching healthy crops so the sickness does not spread across your field.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ ni oshã loo ofu tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ofɔ oniji kɛ onitsumɔ dadei ahe dani ota ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã nyɛŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams keep getting smaller every season even when I use good fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Reusing old seed tubers year after year allows viruses to slowly build up inside the plant generation after generation. This weakens the crop over time, causing smaller harvests despite fertilizer use.
ga: Dumɔwui ayitsei momo ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa hela lɛ buaa ehe naa fiofio yɛ tso lɛ mli. Yinɔ kɛ yinɔ Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi fioo kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii po.

english: How can I avoid introducing diseases into my farm when I cut seed yams into smaller pieces for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi hela kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mifoɔ sweet potato bibii bibii koni mikɛdu lɛ?

english: Wound surfaces invite disease germs into the tuber. Use a clean, sharp knife, wipe it regularly, and allow the cut surfaces to dry thoroughly before placing them in the soil.
ga: Nɔ ni pila lɛ fɔɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ nine kɛyaa yitso lɛ mli. Kɛ kakla ni he tse ni naa wa atsu nii. Tsumɔ he ni afo lɛ daa ni oha he ni afo lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ dani okɛfu shikpɔŋ.

english: How do I stop soft rot from spreading from one yam to another inside my storage barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli yɛ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ naa?

english: Store only healthy, undamaged tubers in a dry barn, and regularly check and remove any rotting yams so the rot germs do not transfer to neighbor yams.
ga: Kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni efiteee pɛ ato ŋmɔ ko ni egbi mli. ni okwɛ sweet potatoes ni egboi lɛ amli daa ni oshɛrɛ oshwie. Enɛ ji koni akatsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ anɔ kɛya sweet potatoes ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it important to clear out old crop roots and decaying tubers before I start planting a new crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie tso shishifãi momo kɛ ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ dani aje tso hee shishi lɛ?
