english: Old crop debris hides pests and disease germs through the dry season. Removing old stems and roots ensures your new seeds start off in a clean, healthy field.
ga: Tsei ni etsɛ ni egbo lɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ teeɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Shishifãi kɛ shishifãi momo ni ajieɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui heei jeɔ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni he tse, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why does planting yams on the exact same piece of land year after year lead to crop sickness?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai baa lɛ?

english: Yam-specific soil diseases and pests build up in the ground over time. Rotating with different crops like beans or corn starves out these diseases and leaves clean soil for future yam planting.
ga: Helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ŋmeii kɛbaa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ atsakeɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai nɛɛ anaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves dry up during harmattan because direct harsh sunlight and dry winds pull moisture out of the plant faster than the roots can drink it from the soil. Providing shade trees like plantains protects the leaves from burning.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ harmattan beaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tamɔ plantains ni akɛwoɔ shade mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off when the plant is under stress from high temperatures, lack of consistent water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa mli. Nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: What makes the bottom part of my tomatoes turn black and rot before they even get ripe?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-tomato lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant lacks calcium or experiences irregular watering, preventing calcium from reaching the growing end of the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ calcium bɛ tomato tsei amli loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haaa calcium lɛ ayashɛ tso yibii ni miida lɛ naa.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes in the middle of my young maize leaves, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the growing tip (funnel) of the plant. Applying recommended pest controls directly into the leaf funnel early in the morning or late evening helps protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ (cones) ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛwo mli lɛ wo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Is it better for my soil to burn the bushes when clearing my land or to clear without burning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ baashã jwɛi lɛ beni mijieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ? Aloo ajie lɛ ni ashãaa?

english: Clearing without burning is better because burning destroys beneficial soil nutrients, kills helpful soil microbes, and leaves the soil bare and dry. Leaving cleared weeds to decompose creates natural mulch that feeds the soil.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Egbeɔ sũ mli helai bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ gbiŋ ni egbiɔ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli sũ ni haa sũ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my land needs fertilizer before I plant cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu ŋmei?

english: If your cassava leaves look pale green or yellow instead of dark green, or if previous crops on that land grew slowly with small roots, your soil lacks essential nutrients and will benefit from organic manure or balanced fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cassava baai lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ loo kɛji tsei ni tsɔ hiɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ dara blɛoo ni amɛyɛ shishifãi bibii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni obaaná sɛɛnamɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa mli.

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same piece of land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the space after the maize is harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eyeɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Plantain bunches shrink over time when too many suckers grow around the main plant, forcing them to compete for water and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers and keeping only 2-3 stems per stand improves bunch size.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, ni no nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni ajieɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ tsei 2-3 pɛ toɔ shi yɛ shidaamɔhe kome nɔ lɛ haa tsei akuu lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant the seeds I saved from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid maize varieties lose their vigor in the next generation, producing smaller cobs and weaker plants. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures uniform growth, pest resistance, and high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ ŋmãa srɔtoi ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ baaha amɛda daa. Pest ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo

english: How do I know the right time to plant my crops when the early rains are unpredictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu tsei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ mra ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil gets thoroughly wet at a depth of about 10-15 centimeters across several continuous rainy days before planting, rather than planting after the very first light shower.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ jɛmɛ fɛɛ yɛ ŋshɔ ni mli kwɔ aaafee sɛntimita 10-15 mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mli gbii babaoo dani odu. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ahum lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What size of poly bag is best for starting crop seedlings in my nursery?
ga: Mɛɛ poly bag dalɛ sa kɛha dumɔwui ashishijee yɛ mi-nursery lɛ mli?

english: Using a standard 15 by 12-centimeter poly bag gives seedling roots enough room to grow strong without restricting early root development before transplanting.
ga: Kɛ akɛ poly bag ni dalɛ ji 15 x 12 cm ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara waa. ni ekɛtsiii shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa mra dani aduɔ amɛ

english: How should I mix sand and topsoil to make good soil for my seedling poly bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafutu ŋã kɛ ŋwɛi sũ koni mafee sũ kpakpa kɛha poly bags kɛha dumɔwui?

english: Mix clean topsoil with river sand and organic manure to create loose soil that drains water easily while holding enough moisture for seed germination.
ga: Okɛ faa mli ŋã kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ afutu mli koni efee sũ ni hoɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Where is the best place to get clean sand for my crop nursery soil mix?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ ana ŋã ni he tse ni akɛfutu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-nsɛri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Collect clean river sand that is free from salt, trash, and weed seeds, as salty or contaminated sand can burn young roots and stop seeds from sprouting.
ga: Ha faa ŋã ni he tse lɛ aka ŋoo, jwɛi, kɛ jwɛi dumɔwui. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋã ni ŋmei yɔɔ mli loo ŋã ni mli ewo muji baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ekpa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Do my young crop seedlings need a shade canopy above them in the nursery?
ga: Ani mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo yɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, young seedlings need a shade cover made of palm fronds or shade nets to protect their tender leaves from the harsh sun until they get stronger.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ni akɛ ŋmei tsei ahe baai fee loo hulutsoo ŋshɔŋloo ko ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛyashi ebaaná hewalɛ

english: How tall should my seedlings grow before I move them from the nursery to the main farm field?
ga: Te esa akɛ midumɔwui lɛ adara aha tɛŋŋ dani ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are usually ready for field planting when they reach about 15 to 20 centimeters in height and have grown at least 3 to 4 strong, healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛji amɛshɛ aaafee sɛntimita 15 kɛyashi 20 ni kɛ hoo lɛ, amɛyɛ baai ni wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 3 kɛyashi 4.

english: How often should I water my crop seedlings while they are in the nursery bags?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi tso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ nu be mli ni amɛyɔɔ grow bag lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water young seedlings twice daily—early in the morning and late in the afternoon—so the soil stays moist without becoming completely soaked.
ga: Okɛ nu awo tsei bibii lɛ amli shii enyɔ daa gbi. Leebi kɛ shwane Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ni edɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafee tsɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast in my poly bags, and how do I clear them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mi-poly kotokui lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ majie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mihe?

english: Nursery soil is full of nutrients and kept wet, which helps weed seeds sprout fast. Gently pick them out by hand so they do not steal water and food from your crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eyi kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ ni efɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. Okɛ onine atswa amɛ blɛoo koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Is it safe for a pregnant woman on our farm to help mix or spray crop insecticides?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ yei ni hiɛ musu ni yɔɔ wɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afutu loo amɛshwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: No, pregnant women should never handle, mix, or be near agricultural insecticides because chemical fumes and skin contact can cause severe harm to the unborn baby.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ yei ni hiɛ musu lɛ tsuɔ okwaayeli tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe nii, amɛkɛfutuɔ amɛhe, loo amɛhiɔ amɛhe. Ejaakɛ tsofai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ hewolo ni akɛkpeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ awui waa.

english: Why are tiny insects eating the fresh leaves of my young crops, and what should I do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yeɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai heei lɛ? Ni mɛni esa akɛ mafee?

english: Tender young leaves attract leaf-eating pests. You can protect your plants by spraying recommended safe insecticides or natural neem extract early in the morning.
ga: Baai bibii ni darako lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ baa lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu otsei lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ ni oookɛshwie amɛnɔ leebi lɛ nɔ.

english: How deep should I bury the plant when moving a seedling from the poly bag into the farm soil?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu mitsei lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ poly kotokui amli lɛ miiwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Plant the seedling so that the top of its root ball sits level with the field soil. Burying the stem too deep can trap moisture and cause the stem to rot.
ga: Dumɔ dumɔwui ni shishifãi lɛ ayiteŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ekome. Kɛ́ afu tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ emɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eha tso lɛ agbo.

english: How do I care for my small oil palm seedlings so they can grow big and strong?
ga: Mibakwɛ mu tsei bibii lɛ anɔ. Te abaafee tɛŋŋ adara ni aná hewalɛ?

english: Small oil palm seedlings need consistent watering, protection from harsh sunlight with light shade, and regular weeding. Feeding them with good compost or fertilizer early on helps them build deep roots to grow into strong, productive trees.
ga: Oil palm dumɔwui bibii lɛ biɔ ni afɔ amɛ nu daa. Buu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni la fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ. ni ojie jwɛi lɛ daa Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai aha amɛ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni he wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it better to raise my crop seeds in a nursery first before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seeds and sprouts are very delicate and can easily be killed by heat, heavy rain, or pests. A nursery gives them a safe environment with controlled shade and water until they are strong enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni dɔlɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ agbe amɛ oya. He ni akwɛɔ kooloi yɛ lɛ haa amɛnáa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ nu ni akudɔɔ amɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: What happens to my soil when I keep harvesting crops and taking them away every season?
ga: Mɛni baa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikpa miŋmɔshi nii ni mijie amɛ daa be mli?

english: Every crop you harvest takes away nutrients that were inside the soil. If you do not put nutrients back using compost, animal manure, or fertilizer, the soil becomes weak, and your future harvests will get smaller over time.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni okpaa lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ. ni nibii ni abaafee wɔsɛɛ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my palm fruit bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei yibii lɛ?

english: A palm fruit bunch is ready to harvest when its color turns deep orange or red, and when a few mature fruits start dropping naturally to the ground around the base of the tree.
ga: Palm tsei akui lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ. kɛ beni aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ekomɛi bɔi shikpɔŋ ni bɔle adebɔɔ mli tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbee shi lɛ

english: Why are the fruits on my oil palm trees growing very small instead of big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yibii ni yɔɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji bibii kwraa moŋ fe agboi lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees produce small fruits when they lack adequate water, sunlight, or essential soil nutrients. Clearing weeds around the base and applying proper fertilizer helps the tree send food directly into the fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei woɔ yibii bibii kɛji nu ni fa, hulu la loo niyenii ni he hiaa waa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ajiemɔ Konii ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ niyenii yaa aduawai akui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my palm fruits spoil quickly after I cut them down from the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm yibii lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, palm fruits begin to ferment and break down rapidly. Processing them into oil within 48 hours prevents spoilage and gives you higher-quality palm oil that sells for a better price.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa lɛ, ŋmei yibii lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ni efiteɔ oya. Afeɔ lɛ fɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli, ni ehaaa efite ni efee ŋmei fɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni hi fe fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to leave wide spaces between my oil palm trees when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi he ko ni da yɛ mu tsei ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii lɛ?

english: Giving each oil palm tree enough room (about 9 meters apart) ensures that their leaves and roots do not fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, allowing every tree to yield maximum fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ aha mu tso fɛɛ tso he gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa (aaafee mitai 9 kɛjɛ amɛhe) lɛ, ebaaha baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ akatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii. Ha tso fɛɛ tso awo yibii babaoo.

english: Is it helpful to cut off the lower leaves of my oil palm tree?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaafolɔ mu tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Yes, trimming dry or yellowing lower leaves—called pruning—helps the tree direct its energy into developing new leaves and larger fruit bunches, while making it much easier to harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbi loo ni miifee ŋmɔŋ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ pruning lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ nɔ koni ekɛ baai heei kɛ aduawai akui wuji aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How can I protect my young crops from dying during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) holds water in the ground longer, reduces soil heat, and keeps young plants alive when rain is scarce.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha onibii ahe (mulching) lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ aba shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my young palm trees to turn yellow, and how do I fix it?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-palm tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the plant is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is pooling around its roots. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer and improving soil drainage will make the leaves green again.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu ebɔle eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested plantains suddenly turn soft and yellow all at the same time before buyers arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa dani hɔlɔ lɛ bashɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains release a natural gas called ethylene as they mature. When fruits are piled close together, this gas gets trapped and acts like a signal telling all the surrounding fruit to ripen at once. Keeping them spread out in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated space slows down this process.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene kɛji amɛdara. Kɛji akɛ ato aduawai lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Gas nɛɛ mɔ̃ɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ okadi kɛhaa aduawai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. ahoo yɛ be kome mli Kɛ́ ogbɛ amɛ oshwã he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why does my harvested cassava turn black and spoil so quickly if I do not sell it within two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ oya kɛji mikɛ gbii enyɔ hɔ̃ɔɔ lɛ?

english: Unlike yams, cassava roots do not have a protective outer skin to keep them alive after harvest. As soon as you pull cassava from the ground, natural chemical reactions start inside the root to heal the damage, which rapidly turns the white flesh blue-black and ruins the taste within 48 to 72 hours.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ sweet potato lɛ, cassava shishifãi bɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo ni buɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji ogbala ŋmei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ kɛkɛ ni Adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni tsuɔ nii jeɔ shishi yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛtsa nɔ ni efite lɛ. Enɛ baaha loo yɛŋ lɛ atsɔ bluu-diŋŋ oya. ni efiteɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so fast when I pack them in plastic bags to carry to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo plastic kotokui amli koni mikɛmaje jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Even after picking, tomatoes continue to breathe and release heat and moisture. Plastic bags trap this warm air and moisture inside, creating a humid environment where bacteria and mold quickly grow and cause the fruit to rot.
ga: Beni ajie tomato po lɛ, Tomato hu muɔ ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpo. Plastic kotokui lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ baa ni bacteria kɛ fungi daa oya ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize get moldy inside the storage bag even though it felt dry in my hands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ewo muji yɛ nitoo kotoku lɛ mli beni miniji nuɔ he akɛ amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Maize grains may feel dry on the surface, but they can still hold moisture deep inside. When packed tightly in sealed bags, that hidden moisture slowly moves to the outside of the grain, trapped inside the sack where mold can easily grow.
ga: Abele ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ anu he akɛ amɛgbi yɛ amɛhiɛ. Shi enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lolo yɛ emli tɔ̃ɔ. Kɛji akɛ awo kotokui ni akɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baatsi ehe fiofio kɛya ŋmaa lɛ kponɔgbɛ. Ni ekɛ ehe woɔ kotoku lɛ mli, he ni ŋmeii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow and drop off when heavy rains flood the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Heavy rain fills all the tiny air spaces in the soil with water, which starves the roots of oxygen. When root systems cannot breathe, they stop absorbing nitrogen and other essential nutrients from the soil, causing the plant leaves to turn yellow and fall.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ he ko bibioo baa. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu lɛ shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔmɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and burn during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have thin leaves and shallow roots that cannot reach deep groundwater. In full sun, high heat causes the leaves to lose moisture much faster than the young roots can draw it up, scorching the leaf edges.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ, la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ shãa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open right on the stem while they are turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miitswa yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni etsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Fruit cracking happens when a plant absorbs a sudden, large amount of water after a dry spell. The inside of the tomato grows and expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to pop open.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ shwie nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ gbeleɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any fruit during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant and dries up pollen before bees or wind can move it. When fertilization fails, the plant naturally drops the useless flowers so it can save energy and survive the weather.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ dani ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ajie amɛ. Kɛji fɔmɔ nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa amɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my watermelon is fully ripe and sweet without cutting it open?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ watermelon lɛ egbɔ kwraa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ofolɔɔɔ lɛ?

english: You can check two main signs on the vine: first, look at the spot where the melon rests on the ground—it changes from white to a creamy yellow color when ripe. Second, look at the small curly tendril on the vine right next to the fruit; when that tendril turns brown and dry, the melon is ready.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ okadii titrii enyɔ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, kwɛmɔ he ni melon lɛ damɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Amɛtsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eyɛŋ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ krim be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Yɛ wain tso ni bɛŋkɛ aduawai lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ melon lɛ efee klalo.

english: Why do my crop stems grow thin and pale yellow when weeds surround them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni jwɛi ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil fertilizers like nitrogen. When weeds block light and steal nutrients, your crops grow tall and skinny trying to reach the light and lack the nitrogen needed to keep leaves rich green.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ nitrogen. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee bibioo ni amɛmiibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛná la ni nitrogen ni he hiaa koni amɛha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli lɛ bɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my yam plants need big heaps of soil to grow well instead of just planting them directly in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa shikpɔŋ agbo ko koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow downwards and need loose, soft soil to expand properly. Big mounds or ridges give the tubers plenty of room to grow large while protecting them from rot caused by water standing in the field.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ ni ehe miihia ni amɛná shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Gɔji loo ŋmeii wuji haa bulb lɛ gbɛ babaoo ni etsɔ agbo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ ni nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he.

english: Why do yam vines always try to climb up wooden stakes and trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ be fɛɛ be ni ekwɔ tsei kɛ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb so their leaves can reach full sunlight, which the plant uses to make food and grow the big tuber underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also protects the crop from diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛbaa lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Akɛ tsei lɛ hoɔ nii ni aduɔ bulb agboi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe.

english: How do I know if the seed yams I saved are healthy and ready to sprout before I put them in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ dani mikɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy seed yams feel firm to the touch, have clean skin without soft spots, and show small green buds forming at the top. Soft or foul-smelling seed yams are rotten and will not produce a crop.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ ata he. Na hewolo ni he tse ni gbɔjɔmɔ ko bɛ he. ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baa yɛ ŋwɛi Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo ni shãa yams lɛ baagboi ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baaa.

english: How does the yam plant show me that the tubers underground are fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Sweet Potato Tree ni tsɔɔ mi bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: When yams are ready to harvest, the leafy green vines naturally stop growing, turn yellow, and dry up. This signals that the plant has transferred all its energy into the underground tuber.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa wain tsei ni yɔɔ Green-leaved lɛ baakpa shweremɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ etee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do crop seedlings I get from a nursery grow stronger than when I plant seeds directly in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ daa waa fe be mli ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Nursery seedlings are given daily watering, shade, and rich soil during their delicate early days. By the time you plant them in your field, they already have a strong root system ready to absorb water and nutrients quickly.
ga: Akɛ nu woɔ dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ amɛ yɛ mli lɛ anɔ, awoɔ amɛ shade ni awoɔ amɛ fɔ daa gbi yɛ amɛshishijee bei ni mli wa lɛ amli. Kɛji odu amɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛyɛ shishifã ni mli wa ni efee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya.

english: Why do young crop seedlings look weak and droop right after I transplant them into my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock, which happens because moving the plant temporarily disturbs its small roots. Watering seedlings immediately after planting and doing it early in the morning or late in the evening helps them recover fast.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ tso lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ gbaa shishifãi bibii lɛ anaa. its temporary Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ofee nakai leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe awa amɛ oya.

english: What happens to small crop seedlings if they stay inside tiny nursery bags for too long before planting?
ga: Mɛni baa tsei amli dumɔwui bibii anɔ kɛji amɛhi ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui bibii amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani adu?

english: When seedlings stay in small bags too long, their roots get trapped, twist tightly around the bag, and choke themselves. Once planted in the field, these root-bound plants struggle to grow deep roots and can easily fall over.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ hi kotokui bibii lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛhe. Tsɔ kotoku lɛ he jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa onyɛŋ omu Kɛji adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei ni shishifãi nɛɛ ekpɛtɛ amɛhe lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbee shi oya.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without bearing good fruit when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛlɛɛmɔ ni yibii kpakpai jɛɛɛ mli baa lɛ? Akɛni midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hewɔ lɛ

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other for water and food in the soil while their leaves block sunlight from one another. Giving each plant enough space allows it to feed properly and grow strong fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa niyenii ni sa ni ewoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen, which is an important plant food, or that the ground is flooded with water and preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Can yam crops survive on my farm if heavy rains cause standing water on the land for days?
ga: Ani sweet potato tso ko baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo?

english: Yam tubers need air inside the soil to survive. If water sits on the field for several days, the roots and tubers suffocate and quickly rot underground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do I know when my rubber tree is mature enough to start tapping it for latex?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-rɔba tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi tswamɔ?

english: A rubber tree is usually ready for tapping when it is around 5 to 7 years old and the trunk reaches about 50 centimeters in circumference at waist height. Tapping too early can stunt the tree's growth and reduce its total lifespan.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha gbee kɛji amɛye aaafee afii enumɔ kɛyashi kpawo, ni amɛtso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ aaafee sɛntimita 50 yɛ amɛtsitsi nɔ. Kɛ́ atswa tso lɛ oya tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ adalɛ aba shi, ni eha ewala be fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my rubber trees shed all their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi rɔba tso lɛ baa fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Rubber trees naturally drop their leaves during dry periods to save water and protect themselves from high heat. This is a normal protective behavior, and fresh green leaves will sprout once the rains return.
ga: Rɔba tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Enɛ ji hebuu subaŋ ni afɔɔ feemɔ. Ni baai eŋɔli heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: How many years can a single rubber tree keep producing latex for harvest?
ga: Afii enyiɛ rɔbɔt tso kome baanyɛ afee latɛs kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ?

english: If tapped carefully without damaging the inner wood, a rubber tree can yield high-quality latex continuously for 25 to 30 years before production naturally slows down.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee tsei ni yɔɔ Rɔba tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ latex ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba be fɛɛ be afii 25 kɛyashi 30 dani efeemɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from overly rich soil or excess fertilizer, it uses all its energy to grow stems and leaves above ground instead of sending food down to build big root tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei naa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii fe nine loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ tsei ahe baai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni efee shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and drop during the dry harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The harsh harmattan winds dry out the air and soil quickly. Cocoa trees shed leaves during this time to reduce water loss through their foliage so the trunk and root system can survive until rain returns.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from intense sunlight and slow down water evaporation. It is a natural self-defense mechanism against heat stress.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Koni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni eha nu lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Can I grow maize or vegetables between my young tree crops while waiting for them to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo aduawai yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, planting short-term crops like maize or beans between young trees is a great strategy. It brings early harvest and income while protecting the young tree roots from direct heat, as long as you do not plant directly against the tree trunk.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Dumɔwui ateŋ ji gbɛ kpakpa. Ehaa akpaa nii mra ni anáa shika yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Shii abɔ ni okɛduuu tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot while still hanging on the branches?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pod is a common fungal disease spread by water droplets and high humidity under heavy farm shade. Removing affected pods early and clearing excess canopy branches helps keep air moving and stops the fungal spread.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni nu mli nu ni hoɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ mra Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ kpaa.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over before the fruit bunches are fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ yaa nɔ egbeeɔ shi lɛ? Dani aduawai akui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves and shallow root systems that make them top-heavy. They fall easily when high winds blow or if underground pests like root nematodes damage the roots holding the plant in place.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ. Amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa loo kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes lɛ fite shishifãi ni ŋmɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ.

english: How often do I need to water my young oil palm seedlings during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mawo mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Young oil palm seedlings need deep watering about twice a week during dry periods to establish deep roots. Once their root system reaches deeper soil layers after a couple of seasons, they handle dry weather much better on their own.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afɔ mu tsei bibii lɛ anɔ nu waa aaafee shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ ama shi. Beni eshishifãi lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: How do I know if my maize plants actually need chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he miihia mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: When maize lacks nitrogen, the lower leaves start turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips inward. Adding fertilizer gives the crop essential nutrients so it can produce dark green leaves and develop large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baabɔi ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ mligbɛ naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ewo baai ni tsuɔ waa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa aba.

english: Why do my cowpea plants seem to make the soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant harvested and leaves rot, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli kɛ́ akpa tsei lɛ ni baai lɛ fite. Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my cassava crop stay green in the dry season when my maize dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli beni mi-ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store large amounts of water deep underground and the plant can shed leaves to reduce water loss, whereas maize has shallow roots that require steady rain or watering to survive.
ga: Cassava shishifãi toɔ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni tso lɛ baanyɛ ajie baai lɛ koni ekɛba nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ shi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, abele yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni nugbɔ anɛ daa loo afɔ nɔ nu koni ehi shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees turn brown and burn in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiishã yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my vegetable plants turn yellow when there is too much rain on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up air pockets in the soil, essentially suffocating the plant roots. Without air, roots cannot absorb soil nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why is it necessary to mound the soil high before planting my yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Mounding creates soft, loose soil that allows yam tubers to expand freely underground without resistance, while also improving water drainage so the tubers do not rot.
ga: Mounding haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛnaa lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, afeɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: What will happen if I plant my pepper seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ pepper dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they fight over sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. They end up growing tall, thin, and weak, producing very few peppers compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛmiitswa hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋ lɛ, amɛdaraa, amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, drought, or lack of nutrients. The plant drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do my bean plants bend and grow toward one side of the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiida kɛmiiya ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ?

english: Plants naturally lean toward sunlight to produce their food. If big trees or bushes shade one side of your field, the beans will stretch towards the open sun.
ga: Tsei sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ koni amɛná niyenii. Kɛji tsei wuji loo jwɛi tsi ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome naa lɛ Beans lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa hulu la ni mli tse lɛ he.

english: How do weeds reduce my crop yield even if they are not touching my plants directly?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi? Kɛji amɛtaaa mitsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ po.

english: Underneath the ground, weed roots aggressively drink the water and eat the fertilizer you gave your crops, leaving your main crops starved of nutrients.
ga: Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ, jwɛi shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu kɛ miishɛɛ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛhaa onibii lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, niyenii titrii ni oduɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my crops are suffering from a disease or just need more water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ loo nu babaoo he miihia lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: A thirsty crop usually wilts in the heat of the afternoon and revives after watering or rainfall, whereas a diseased plant will show persistent signs like leaf spots, strange colors, rotting parts, or stunting that do not improve with water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli, ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa wala mli ekoŋŋ yɛ nu loo nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baajie okadii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, tamɔ baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, sui ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, kɛ hei ni fiteɔ. loo stunting ni kɛ nu eyaaa hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow and dropping off before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani kpamɔ baa lɛ?

english: Leaves turning yellow prematurely can be a sign of a disease attacking the plant's roots or vascular system, though it can also happen if the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ mra lɛ baanyɛ afee hela ko ni fiteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi loo lá fãji lɛ he okadi. Eyɛ mli akɛ ebaanyɛ eba mli kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ.

english: If I find a sick crop in my field, do I have to cut down my whole farm or just the diseased plant?
ga: Kɛji mina tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani esa akɛ mafo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ pɛ?

english: In most cases, you only need to remove and destroy the specific sick plants and immediate neighboring plants to contain the infection, though severe viral outbreaks may require clearing a larger affected area.
ga: Yɛ bei babaoo mli lɛ, ehe miihia ni ojie tso pɔtɛɛ ni hela mɔ lɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ kɛkɛ koni hela lɛ akpa. Eyɛ mli akɛ hela ni gbeɔ mɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ abi ni ajie hei wuji ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ moŋ, shi

english: Why do extension officers sometimes recommend cutting down healthy-looking trees near a sick tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Some diseases, especially viruses, take time to show visible symptoms. Cutting nearby healthy-looking trees removes plants that might already be secretly infected, stopping the disease from spreading to the rest of the farm.
ga: Helai komɛi, titri lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ, heɔ be dani amɛjieɔ okadii ni kadiɔ mɔ kpo. Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaye abua ni ajie tsei ni ekolɛ hela lɛ emɔ amɛ momo yɛ teemɔŋ lɛ. ni ekpa hela lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ hei krokomɛi.

english: If I cut down a crop because of a bad disease, can I plant the same seed back in that exact spot right away?
ga: Kɛji mifo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hela hewɔ lɛ Ani manyɛ madu shishijee dumɔwui lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ nakai he lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is usually better to wait or plant a different crop type first, because disease organisms can survive in the soil or old roots for months and immediately attack new seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi akɛ ooomɛ loo ooodu tso kroko klɛŋklɛŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, helai ahe nibii baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ loo shishifãi momo amli nyɔji babaoo ni amɛtutua dumɔwui heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Can a plant disease jump from my neighbor's farm into my crops?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ ajɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli aba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Yes, plant diseases can easily spread across neighboring farms through wind, rain splashes, insects carrying pathogens, or even by humans carrying contaminated soil on their boots and tools.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli oya kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ kooloi ni kɛ helai baa lɛ anɔ. aloo adesai po ni woɔ sũ ni mli ewo muji yɛ amɛ atadei kɛ nitsumɔ dadei anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can using the same cutlass on sick crops make my healthy crops sick too?
ga: Ani dagger kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ tso ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mitso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ hu aná hela?

english: Yes, sap and plant fluids stuck to your cutlass or pruning tools can carry bacteria or viruses from a sick plant directly into the cuts of healthy plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei amli nu kɛ nu ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmeii loo nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛya tso ni afolɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: What immediate step should I take when a strange, new crop sickness appears on my farm for the first time?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hela hee ko ba miŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa?

english: You should flag or mark the affected plant, avoid touching other healthy plants afterward, and report the issue right away to an extension officer or agricultural expert to identify it.
ga: Esa akɛ okadi loo okadi tsei ni ena naagbai lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni oootaa he yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ he ni obɔ o-extension agent loo okwaayeli he nilelɔ lɛ amaniɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Who should I inform first when an unusual plant sickness starts spreading across multiple farms in our village?
ga: Namɔ esa akɛ mabɔ he amaniɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ́ tsei ahe hela ko ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ bɔi gbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ ŋmɔji babaoo ni yɔɔ wɔ akrowa lɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: You should inform both your local community leaders to warn neighboring farmers and an agricultural extension officer who can diagnose the disease scientifically and provide proper control methods.
ga: Esa akɛ oha akutsoŋbii ahiɛnyiɛlɔi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ale koni amɛbɔ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ kɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni baanyɛ akwɛ hela lɛ yɛ jeŋ nilee mli ni amɛkɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ hela lɛ aha lɛ kɔkɔ.

english: How can I tell if a crop is recovering from an attack or if it is completely dead?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miihe ajɔ kɛjɛ tutuamɔ mli loo egbo kwraa?

english: A recovering plant will start producing fresh, bright green leaves or new shoots from its stem, while a dead or dying plant will continue to dry up, turn brown or black, and rot.
ga: Tsei ni miiya hiɛ lɛ baabɔi baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ kpojiemɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni egboi loo ni miigboi lɛ baaya nɔ agbi. Tsakemɔ kɛya blɔfo loo ediŋŋ ni efite

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the tall trees away from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains alongside them acts like an umbrella to shield them until they are old enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebaatsu nii akɛ hulutsoo tso kɛyashi tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa.

english: Why does my main plantain stem stop growing leaves as soon as the bunch of plantains appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso titri lɛ kpaɔ baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ kɛji plantain lɛ je kpo pɛ?

english: A single plantain stem is designed to produce only one flower bunch in its lifetime. Once the bunch shows, the plant directs all its food into fattening the fruit rather than making new leaves, and the stem dies after harvest to let the young shoots at the base take over.
ga: Afee plantain tso kome koni ekɛ fɔfɔi akuu kome pɛ awo yɛ ewala be mli. Beni kuu lɛ jie ehe kpo lɛ Tso lɛ kudɔɔ eniyenii fɛɛ kɛyaa aduawai ni woɔ fɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee baai heei. Ni ŋmeii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ koni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ abaye amɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly into tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up when it gets hot to protect themselves from losing too much moisture into the air. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve water during dry periods.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji akɛ amɛdɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and yield small cobs when I plant seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli tse ni ewoɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and soil food to grow thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ Niyenii kɛ Nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why am I seeing ragged holes and brown dirt inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni egbɛ eshwa kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing point of the maize plant to eat soft young leaves, leaving behind its waste which looks like brown dirt.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Eshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer onto my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers must dissolve in water before plant roots can suck them up. Applying fertilizer on bone-dry soil leaves the powder sitting uselessly on top, and strong direct sunlight can burn the roots underneath.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wu yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha powda lɛ ata nɔ ni he ehiaaa. Ni hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land year after year lead to smaller harvests each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Maize continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season without giving anything back. Rotating crops with beans or groundnuts helps put natural nitrogen food back into the earth.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be ni ekɛ nɔ ko haaa. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting and turning dark just two days after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi fitemɔ ni amɛfee diŋŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a protective outer shell like yams, so cutting them from the stalk causes rapid internal chemical changes and exposes them to air rot. They must be processed or cooked within 48 hours.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ amɛhe yɛ kponɔgbɛ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ oya ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ. Esa akɛ atsu he nii loo ahoo yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without producing any tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures become too hot or when water supply drops suddenly, causing stress that stops the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ nu lɛ gbee shi trukaa Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii baa.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to turn pale and grow slowly even when plenty of rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and greedily suck up the nutrients and fertilizer from the soil before your main crops can reach them, effectively starving your plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. ni okɛ hiɛjoomɔ shwieɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani otsei titrii lɛ baashɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why can't I plant all my coconut seedlings very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu mi-kokoo tsei lɛ fɛɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Coconut trees need plenty of sunlight, air, and ground space for their roots to spread. Planting them too close makes them fight each other for water and nutrients, resulting in tall, weak trees that produce very few fruits.
ga: Kokoso tsei taoɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã. Kɛ́ adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei kakadaji ni bɛ hewalɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: If I buy a large batch of coconut seedlings from the same farm, why do some grow much faster than others?
ga: Kɛ mihe ŋmei dumɔwui babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei komɛi daa oya fe ekrokomɛi?

english: Even seedlings from the same mother tree can inherit slightly different strengths, just like human brothers and sisters. Differences in soil depth, water retention, or root handling during transplanting can also make some grow faster.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛ fɔlɔ tso kome mli lɛ po baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto fioo. Tamɔ wɔ adesai nyɛmimɛi hii kɛ yei lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni ahiɛɔ lɛ mli Aloo, shishifãi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi komɛi hu ada oya.

english: What is the best time of year for me to plant new tree seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant seedlings is at the very beginning of the major rainy season. This gives the young roots plenty of soil moisture to establish themselves strongly before the dry harmattan season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee. Enɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛná hewalɛ dani harmatta be ni egbi lɛ aba.

english: How many years will it take for my new coconut seedlings to start producing fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi ŋmei tso hee lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Traditional tall coconut varieties usually take 6 to 8 years to start bearing fruit, while modern hybrid or dwarf varieties can begin producing much faster, often within 3 to 4 years with good care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid loo dwarf henɔi lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi mra kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɔ shi afii 3 kɛyashi 4 kɛji akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: My coconut trees are very old and tall, and they produce very few fruits now. Should I cut them down?
ga: Mi ŋmei tso lɛ egbɔ waa ni ekɛlɛ. Ni amrɔ nɛɛ ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. Ani esa akɛ mafo amɛ?

english: Yes, coconut trees naturally slow down production after about 50 to 60 years. Replacing old, low-yielding trees with fresh, high-yielding seedlings ensures your farm remains profitable over time.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii tsei lɛ baa shi yɛ aaafee afii 50 kɛyashi 60 sɛɛ. Tsei ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii babaoo lɛ atsakemɔ kɛ dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ aná sɛɛnamɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: How do I know when a coconut on the tree is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ akoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa?

english: If you want fresh coconut water, harvest the nuts while they are still green at around 6 to 7 months old. If you want dried coconut meat for oil, wait until the skin turns completely brown at 11 to 12 months.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ŋmei nu ni mli tse Kpamɔ ŋmei lɛ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo, yɛ aaafee nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 7 mli kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛ kopra lɛ atsu nii akɛ fɔ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi hewolo lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa beni eye nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 12 lɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my coconut trees turn yellow and drop off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the tree lacks essential nutrients like potassium or nitrogen in the soil, or that it is stressed from lack of water during a dry spell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo haomɔ ni jɛɔ nu ni bɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ mli baa

english: Why do my coconut tree flowers fall off before they can turn into small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Coconut trees drop their flowers when they do not get enough water or nutrients, as a way to save energy. Applying compost and mulching around the base helps hold moisture in the soil and keeps the flowers on the tree.
ga: Kokoo tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bɔni afee ni akɛ hewalɛ akafite Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or vegetables between my young coconut trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo aduawai. Mi ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping with food crops while coconut trees are young is a great practice. It keeps the weeds down, provides shade and protection for the soil, and gives you food and income while waiting for the trees to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, ni akɛ niyenii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ tsakeɔ be mli ni ŋmei tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi. Ehaa hulutsoo ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ehaa bo niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni omɛɛɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why are the young leaves at the top of my coconut tree opening up with holes and looking chewed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ gbeleɔ kɛ bu ni etamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by pests like the Rhinoceros beetle, which burrows into the growing heart of the palm. Clearing dead wood around the farm and keeping the tree crown clean helps keep these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ rhinoceros ŋmeii, ni boteɔ tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsoi ni egboi ni ajieɔ yɛ Okwaayeli he lɛ ni aaakwɛ koni tsei ahe atse lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land is good for planting my crops before I start clearing it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ko hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Look at the wild plants and trees already growing there. If the natural bushes are thick, green, and tall, it means the soil is fertile and has good moisture for your crops.
ga: Kwɛmɔ koo mli tsei kɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ momo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli jwɛi lɛ mli tse, eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ kakadaŋŋ lɛ, no lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Some people say bad spirits cause crops to turn yellow in certain fields, but what is the real cause?
ga: Mɛi komɛi kɛɔ akɛ mumɔi fɔji lɛ ha nibii ni adu lɛ tsɔ wuɔi yɛ ŋmɔji komɛi amli. Shi mɛni ji nɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni kɛ enɛ baa?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen or holds too much water, not bad spirits. Adding animal manure or fertilizer usually fixes the problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo ehiɛɔ nu babaoo. Jeee mumɔ fɔŋ Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ naagba lɛ he nii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize in the exact same spot on my land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot drains the soil of the specific food that plant needs and lets soil pests build up. Changing crops keeps the soil healthy and full of nutrients.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni eyiɔ obɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: When plants are crowded, their roots compete for the same food and water in the ground, and their leaves fight for sunlight, leaving all of them weak.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ni amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛ fɛɛ amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Weeds are wild local plants that are naturally tough and know how to grab water and plant food from the soil faster than cultivated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛle bɔ ni amɛjieɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my seeds as soon as the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ?

english: Early planting allows young roots to grow deep while the ground is soft and wet, helping the crop grow strong before dry spells or heavy heat set in.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa dani hɔmɔ be loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa baa.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and die right after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving plants causes root shock. Transplanting them during the cool late afternoon or on a cloudy day gives the roots time to adjust without the hot sun drying them out.
ga: Tso lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shwane mli loo gbi ni atatu ewo nɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛtsakeɔ amɛhe ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa amɛgbi.

english: How do I know if my crops are comfortable in the spot where I planted them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi yɛ he ni miduɔ lɛ yɛ lɛ?

english: Comfortable plants show vibrant green leaves, strong stems, and steady growth without early leaf drop, curling, or unusual yellowing.
ga: Tso ko ni yɔɔ hejɔɔmɔ ni jieɔ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ kpo. tso ni mli wa kɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni ehaaa baa lɛ agbo oya, ebɔle ehe loo etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ejaaa.

english: Why do some of my crops need shade while others die if they don't get full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi ahe hiaa hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gboiɔ kɛji amɛnáaa hulutsoo be fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Different crops have different sunlight needs; crops like cocoa need shade when young to prevent heat stress, while crops like cassava need full sun to make food.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ hulu la he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Tsei tamɔ kookoo he hiaa hulutsoo be mli ni amɛdara koni amɛtsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei tamɔ ŋmei he hiaa hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii.

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot when rain sits on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When standing water stays on the field, it smothers the roots and causes them to drown and rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni amɛgboi.

english: How many years does a young cocoa tree take before it starts bearing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso bibioo ko feɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Traditional cocoa trees usually take about 3 to 5 years to mature and produce their first pods, though newer hybrid varieties can start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years under proper care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema cacao tsei lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ hybrid henɔi heei moŋ Amɛbaabɔi pods feemɔ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some cassava varieties take a full year to mature while others are ready for harvest in six months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi heɔ afi muu fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi feɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa yɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava varieties have different growth speeds; fast-maturing varieties are specifically bred to swell their root tubers early, whereas traditional varieties take longer to store energy in their roots.
ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni daa oya lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛha shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ oya. Yɛ be mli ni shishijee henɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why does my oil palm tree take several years in the field before it starts producing fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ yeɔ afii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani ebɔi yibiiwoo yɛ kui amli lɛ?

english: An oil palm tree spends its first 3 to 4 years building a strong root system, trunk, and leaf canopy so that it has enough stored energy to produce heavy fruit bunches continuously.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ dani amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli wa, amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ahe shishi. Bɔni afee ni ená hewalɛ ni abua naa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaya nɔ ewo yibii ni tsii.

english: What is the difference between using seeds saved from my previous maize harvest and buying hybrid maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ hemɔ teŋ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations, resulting in lower yields, whereas hybrid seeds are specially cross-bred for high yields, fast growth, and disease resistance in their first planted season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, amɛdara oya ni amɛnyɛŋ helai ana yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ shweremɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do grafted mango trees produce fruit much sooner than trees grown directly from a seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni akɛwo mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe nɔ ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Grafted mango trees use branches taken from mature trees that are already ready to fruit, skipping the long juvenile growth phase that seedling trees must go through.
ga: Mango tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni eda ni esa akɛ amɛwo yibii lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Tsɔɔmɔ dalɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni tsei bibii tsɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa trees yield heavy pod crops during certain months and stop producing during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei woɔ ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need consistent rainfall to form flowers and develop pods; during the dry season, trees conserve water by shedding leaves and stopping flower production until the rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛfee fɔfɔi ni amɛfee ŋmeii. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei buɔ nu he kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: A plantain stem flowers and fruits only once in its lifetime, so it must be cut down after harvest to allow the sucker growing beside it to take over and produce the next bundle.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afolɔ mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni ajie ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ. Ba ni obaye nɔ ni ojie kuu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ kpo.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep bearing fruit for many months while my maize plants die right after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ woɔ yibii nyɔji babaoo yɛ be mli ni mi-corn tsei lɛ gboiɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize is an annual crop that completes its life cycle in one season and dies, while pepper is a multi-season bush plant that can keep flowering and fruiting continuously if given adequate water and care.
ga: Abɛi ji tso ko ni yeɔ daa afi ni ewala be lɛ gbeɔ naa yɛ be kome mli, ni no sɛɛ lɛ egboɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, pepper ji tso ko ni yeɔ be babaoo ni ebaanyɛ ewo fɔfɔi be fɛɛ be ni ewo yibii kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nu ni sa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves start turning yellow from the bottom while the crop is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛmiijɛ shishi be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks enough nitrogen, forcing the plant to draw nutrients from its lower leaves to feed the new growing leaves and grain head.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛye baai heei kɛ dumɔwui ayitsei.

english: What makes cashew trees start flowering during the dry season when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni haa cashew tsei jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cashew trees use dry weather and cool night temperatures as natural stress signals to trigger flowering so their nuts can mature before the heavy rainy season starts.
ga: Cashew tsei kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni mli ejɔ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli haomɔ he okadii ni amɛkɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ahe hewalɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ aje shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which plants need to grow green leaves. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea early in the plant's life helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Mɛɛ tsei ehe hiaa ni amɛwo baai eŋɔli? Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Curling leaves with yellowish patches are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings is the best way to prevent this issue.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa Ekɛbaa Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly lɛ, ŋmeii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely between waterings. Water your tomato plants regularly and provide light shade during hot dry periods to help the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ. Ha o-tomato tsei lɛ nu daa ni oha amɛ hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the bottom parts of my ripening tomatoes turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo lɛ?

english: This black spot is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven soil moisture and a lack of calcium in the plant. Watering your crops consistently and adding organic compost or lime to the soil prevents it.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa kɛ calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nu ni oooha ŋmɔshi nibii daa ni okɛ organic compost loo lime awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and rotting on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Dark rotting cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp and heavily shaded farms. Pruning shade trees to let in sunlight and clearing weeds around the cocoa trees keeps the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Afolɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni hulu la aba mli ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Cacao ŋmɔji lɛ baaye abua ni kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before the fruit is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be easily weakened by wind or tiny soil pests called nematodes. Supporting heavy bunches with strong wooden props and using clean planting suckers keeps the trees standing.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei bibii lɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ oya. ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes Fiɔ tsei bibii ni tsii ni akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ Ni akɛ vacuum ni he tse tsuɔ nii koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi.

english: Why are holes appearing in my maize stems, causing the stalks to snap?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ mli bu ni haa efoɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in maize stalks are caused by stem borer caterpillars that tunnel inside the plant and make it weak. Applying recommended control treatments into the leaf funnel early in the plant's life protects the stalks.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ jɛɔ stem borers ni boteɔ tso lɛ mli ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔɔ tso lɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my pepper plants staying small and stunted even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ji bibioo ni egbɔjɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ moŋ?

english: Stunted pepper plants are often attacked at the roots by tiny worms or fungi in the soil that stop the plant from taking in nutrients. Rotating your crops each season and adding well-rotted manure helps roots stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii yeɔ dwarf pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, etutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa afi ni okɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil around them without proper drainage. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away so the tubers do not rot.
