ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ. ni nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ mli Kɛ́ aduɔ ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo.

english: Why are my harvested yam tubers splitting open instead of staying smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miijara yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers crack when dry soil suddenly becomes very wet from heavy rain, causing the tuber to swell too fast. Covering the soil with grass mulch keeps the soil moisture balanced throughout the growing period.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ amli fãa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ trukaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. ni haa yitso lɛ fũuɔ oya tsɔ Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen or the soil is too full of standing water, which chokes the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving field drainage helps the leaves turn dark green so the crop can manufacture its food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my maize growing tassels at the top, but no corn cobs are forming along the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ yɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmãa ŋmeii komɛi bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Maize needs plenty of water and soil nutrients right when flowering starts to form cobs. If the plant experiences drought or lacks phosphorus during this critical stage, it puts its remaining energy into top flowers but fails to produce the grain cobs.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii babaoo he miihia ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji ebɔi fɔmɔ pɛ. Kɛji tsei na hɔmɔ loo fɔsfɔs ni faaa yɛ haomɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, Ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔii yɛ nɔ shi enyɛɛɛ ekɛ dumɔwui akui aba.

english: Can I put fresh chicken manure directly onto my crop beds right before planting my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee afata dumɔwui lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Fresh chicken manure is too strong and 'hot' because it releases high amounts of ammonia gas, which burns young crop roots. It must be stored and allowed to dry or compost with dry grass for a few weeks before applying it to the soil.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ‘edɔ’ yɛ ammonia babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ baaha tso bibioo lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ akɛto ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbi loo afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii otsii fioo komɛi dani akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans before my maize crop make the maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei dani adu ŋmei lɛ, ŋmei lɛ mli waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen gas from the air and stores it inside the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on this leftover natural fertilizer, making the maize leaves grow thick and green.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni eshwɛ lɛ. Ehaa ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are small worms creating tiny holes inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ buji bibii yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the tender inner leaves of young maize. Clearing weeds early and applying recommended organic or mild chemical spray directly into the funnel kills them before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi loo tsofai ni waaa ni akɛwoɔ jwɛi lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baagbe amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and thin even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal light, water, and soil nutrients faster than your crop can. Even with good rain, the weeds end up drinking and feeding first, leaving your main crops starved and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ, shi ehi. Jwɛi hu nuɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii klɛŋklɛŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii titrii lɛ ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and skinny with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmli ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Akɛni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hewɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight and space. The plant spends all its energy stretching upward to reach the light instead of building a thick, strong stalk and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la kɛ ŋwɛi he akaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná la. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa nɛ a he wa, kɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa.

english: If I save maize seeds from my last harvest to plant next season, why do they grow weaker than new seeds from the supplier?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ to koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ daaa fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni jɛ mɛi ni kɛ nibii baa lɛ adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds harvested from hybrid crop varieties lose their natural strength and disease resistance in the next generation. Planting fresh certified seeds ensures uniform germination, stronger stalks, and much higher grain yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni ana he odaseyeli ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ daa. tso ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ kɛ ŋmaa yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo

english: Why do my crop leaves droop down in the hot afternoon but stand up straight again by early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, crops lose water fast through their leaves to stay cool, which makes them wilt temporarily to preserve moisture. During the cool night, the roots pull fresh water from the soil to pump the leaves back up by morning.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko bɔni afee ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafite. Gbi gbɛkɛ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Shishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu kpakpa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛpompa baai lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛya ŋwɛi leebi.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the top layer of soil, and how does it harm my crop roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te eyeɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away topsoil because it is loose and light, taking the richest organic nutrients away with the water flow. Without this top layer, crop roots become exposed to harsh sun and lack the food needed to hold the plant steady.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ sũ lɛ nɔ etse ni eyɛ mlɛo. Ejieɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli beni nu lɛ hoɔ lɛ. Kɛji ŋwɛi fã ko bɛ Tso shishifãi lɛ naa hulu la ni naa wa waa ni amɛbɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛha tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: What crops can I plant on my land that I can easily sell to local poultry farmers for good income?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ amɛ maha maŋ lɛ mli kooloi akwɛlɔi lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ koni maná shika kpakpa?

english: Yellow maize and soybeans are heavily demanded by poultry farmers to produce bird feed. Growing these crops guarantees a ready market because livestock farmers constantly need bulk feed throughout the year.
ga: Kooloi akwɛlɔi biɔ ŋmãa ni ji yellow corn kɛ soybean waa koni amɛkɛfee okpoi aniyenii. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa jarayeli ni yɔɔ klalo baa ejaakɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa kooloi akwɛlɔi lɛ he miihia amɛ daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Is there a crop I can plant that grows fast so I do not have to wait many months to make money?
ga: Ani tsei komɛi yɛ ni daa oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛmɛ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛná shika?

english: Short-duration crops like vegetables (pepper, okra, tomatoes) or early-maturing maize varieties yield within 2 to 3 months. This allows you to harvest and earn income multiple times a year compared to long-term tree crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ aduawai (pepper, okra, tomato) loo ŋmãa ni shwereɔ mra lɛ baawo yibii yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ni onáa shika shii abɔ yɛ afi mli kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do poultry farmers prefer buying yellow maize over white maize from us?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi akwɛlɔi sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ fe ŋmãa yɛŋ kɛjɛ wɔdɛŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow maize contains natural pigments called carotenoids. When chickens eat yellow maize, it makes their egg yolks a rich yellow color and gives their skin a healthy golden shade, which buyers in the market prefer.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni atsɛɔ amɛ carotenoids yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ mli. Kɛji kooloi ye ŋmãa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ Enɛ baaha amɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ. ni ehaa amɛhewolo lɛ feɔ shika tsuru su ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ.

english: Why should I plant soybeans on my farm when everyone else is planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu soybeans yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi fɛɛ miidu ŋmãa?

english: Soybeans are high in protein, making them essential for animal feed factories. Additionally, soybean plants trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which makes your farmland richer for future crops.
ga: Protein babaoo yɛ soya mli, ni no hewɔ lɛ ehe hiaa waa kɛha kooloi aniyenii nitsumɔhei. Kɛfata he lɛ, soybean tsei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my maize crops producing small ears with very few grains on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ toi bibii kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Maize produces small ears when it does not get enough nutrients—especially nitrogen—or enough water during its flowering stage. Weeding late also causes weeds to steal food from the maize plants.
ga: Abele baawo toi bibii kɛji enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hu haa jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why does my cassava grow huge leaves above the ground but produce very tiny tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too much water, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of storing energy and starch in the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami kɛ ngmlɛfia ngɛ tso sisije ɔmɛ a mi.

english: Can I grow vegetables between my rows of maize, or will the plants fight each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai yɛ ŋmãa ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ? Aloo tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe baawuu?

english: You can plant short crops like cowpeas or garden eggs between maize rows if you space them properly. The vegetables harvest quickly for cash while the maize takes its time to mature.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kukuji tamɔ tsina loo abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ kɛji okɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛ jogbaŋŋ. Akpaa aduawai oya koni aná shika. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa heɔ be dani eshɛɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland has lost its power to grow profitable crop yields?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ miiho ni ekɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he lɛ?

english: If your crop leaves turn yellowish early in the season, remain stunted, or give lower yields every year despite good rain, the soil has lost vital nutrients and needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ Ehiɛ edɔ lolo loo yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ elaaje ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Which crops can survive on my farm if the rains suddenly stop for weeks?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa otsii babaoo?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and cowpeas have deep roots and tough leaves that store moisture, allowing them to withstand long dry spells far better than crops like maize or leafy greens.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni wa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe tsei tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsei ni yɔɔ baai.

english: Why do my harvested grains get ruined by insects so quickly while waiting for buyers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kpata dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ oya nɛkɛ beni mimɛɔ mɔ ko ni baahe lɛ?

english: Grains spoil when stored while still damp, attracting weevils and mold. Drying your grain thoroughly until it is hard and storing it in airtight bags keeps insects out without chemicals.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa baafite kɛji akɛ akɛto be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo. Egbalaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛhe wa ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ahe ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make green leaves, or the soil is too wet, preventing the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ afee amɛbaai lɛ eŋɔli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the roots inside the ground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen from soil or fertilizer, it puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close to each other, won't I harvest more corn from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes the plants weak and produces thin stalks with tiny or no ears at all.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáa ŋmeii bibii kɛ toi bibii loo amɛbɛ toi ko kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need shade trees planted around them when they are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa ehe hulutsoo be mli ni eji gbekɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that dry out and burn in direct hot sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, keeping the ground cool and moist until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni amɛshãa. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop seeds rot in the soil when I plant immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long hot dry spell. Without continuous rainfall, seeds get trapped in hot, dry soil after starting to germinate and rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ waa nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ yɛ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ kɛ fitemɔ sɛɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to drink before the heat sets in. Afternoon watering causes most water to evaporate quickly into the air before roots can soak it up.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ haa amɛnuɔ nu dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when plants do not get steady water, or when tiny pests attack the flowers before bees can pollinate them.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ Tutuaa fɔfɔii dani ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afee amɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turn black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato eŋɔli shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often because the soil dried out completely while the fruit was developing, preventing the plant from drawing up calcium.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ kwraa beni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back faster than my crops even after I clear and clean the entire field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie he fɛɛ he ni mijie he lɛ ni mijie he lɛ moŋ.

english: Weed seeds can sleep in the dirt for years. Clearing the land exposes them to sunlight and rain, giving them a head start over planted crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa sɛɛnamɔ fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Why is extension officers telling me not to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year pulls the same nutrients out of the soil until it becomes empty, while allowing specific pests and crop diseases to build up in your soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni efeɔ shwɛm. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I plant plantains on the same field as my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ cocoa dumɔwui heei?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and trapping moisture to help the cocoa survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni eye ebua kookoo lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall down during strong winds and rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep into the soil, and the heavy bunches of fruit make the tree top-heavy. Support poles made of bamboo or sturdy wood can prop up the stems and prevent them from falling.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Ni aduawai ni tsii baatsi tso lɛ yiteŋ. Tso ni mli wa ni akɛ ŋmei loo tso fee lɛ baanyɛ afi tso lɛ sɛɛ ni etsi enaa koni ekagbee shi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen or standing in too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving drainage helps the leaves turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo eyɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm turn into a hard crust after rain, making it hard for seeds to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ani ehaa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui akɛ amɛakwɛ̃?

english: Hard crusts form when soil lacks organic matter and dries out quickly under hot sun. Mixing compost, dried grass, or manure into the soil keeps it loose and soft for seeds to break through easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ ni mli wa lɛ baa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, jwɛi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii futu sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bɔdɔɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ abote mli mlɛo.

english: Why does my pepper farm produce healthy green plants, but the fruits stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ faaa kwraa lolo.

english: Pepper plants need specific nutrients like potassium to build large, fleshy fruits. If the soil lacks these nutrients or dries out too often during fruiting, the peppers stay small.
ga: Pepper tsei he miihia niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ potassium, koni amɛfee aduawai agboi ni yɔɔ loo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii nɛɛ loo egbi shii abɔ tsɔ yɛ yibiiwoo be mli lɛ, Peppers lɛ baafee bibii.

english: What causes my cassava leaves to curl up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite?

english: Curled cassava leaves are usually caused by a sickness called Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems prevents this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cassava mosaic disease lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Cocoa pods turn black due to Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during wet and humid weather. Pruning tree branches to let in sunlight and spraying recommended fungicides protects the pods.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ he koni hulu la babaoo aba mli, ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the middle shoots of my maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which feed on the growing centers of maize plants. Spraying approved insecticides or applying neem extracts early in the morning kills them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ neem mli nu tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high or when plants experience dry soil conditions. Watering regularly and mulching around the roots keeps the soil cool so flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ anyɛ afee aduawai.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yams so they do not spoil in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii? koni ekafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up. Leaving tubers in wet ground long after the vine dies causes them to rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛje shishi amɛgbi. Kɛ́ ashi bulb lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ beni wain tsei lɛ egbo be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgboi.

english: Why are the seeds I planted in my nursery refusing to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of soil moisture, proper depth, and warmth to germinate. If they are buried too deep, planted in dry soil, or if the seed quality is low, they will not sprout successfully.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ni sũ mli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. shishijee ni sa kɛ hulutsoo yɛ shweremɔ mli Kɛji afu lɛ tsɔ ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo kɛji dumɔwu lɛ mlihilɛ faaa Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If my planted seeds are taking too long to grow, can I just keep pouring plenty of water on them?
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa lɛ, Ani manyɛ maya nɔ mawo tsei lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Pouring too much water can rot the seeds or wash away the topsoil, causing them to drown rather than grow. Soil needs to be kept gently moist, not waterlogged.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo efɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛmiiya nu mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadara. Esa akɛ afee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ blɛoo, shi jeee ni nu awo mli.

english: Why is it better to raise some crop seeds in a nursery first instead of planting them directly on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: A nursery lets you carefully manage water, shade, and soil conditions for young plants so they can sprout safely before being exposed to the harsher conditions of the open main field.
ga: He ni akwɛɔ tsei lɛ yɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ nu, hulutsoo, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni otsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe dani amɛyashɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji wuji ni agbele naa lɛ amli lɛ amli.

english: How should I care for my crop nursery if the rains fail to fall?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ gbekɛbii ashihilɛhe lɛ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: You should not rely only on rainfall for a nursery. Always set up your nursery close to a water source so you can hand-water the beds regularly using a watering can during dry days.
ga: Esaaa akɛ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ tsɔne ni akɛkwɛɔ gbekɛbii lɛ ama nu jɛɛhe ko masɛi. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ nu awo saatso lɛ nɔ daa yɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: What should I do to save my young sprouts if a dry spell hits right after planting?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni makwɛ tsei bibii anɔ kɛji hɔmɔ ba beni adu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Place a layer of dry grass or leaves around the bases of your seedlings as mulch. Mulch traps moisture in the soil and protects the soil surface from drying out quickly under the hot sun.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai abɔle he. Akɛ tsei bibii ashishi tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Mulch lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ebuɔ sũ lɛ hiɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Does heavy watering make up for poor soil preparation before planting?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ ni asaaa jogbaŋŋ dani aduɔ nii lɛ he nyɔmɔ?

english: No, water alone cannot fix poor soil. If the soil is hard or badly prepared, water will either run off the surface or trap air, preventing the roots from breathing and growing.
ga: Dabi, nu pɛ nyɛŋ asaa shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo asaaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ Nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛdara.

english: Why do extension officers keep changing the recommended dates for us to plant our crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛtsakeɔ gbii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Rainfall patterns in Ghana change from year to year. Advising new planting dates helps align your crop growth with the actual arrival of the rains, protecting your harvest from unexpected drought.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ tsakeɔ daa afi. Gbi hee ni abaadu lɛ he adafitswaa baaye abua ni tso lɛ adalɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni baa lɛ afee ekome. Buu onibii ahe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ he.

english: How do I know the best time to start preparing my nursery for the new season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛsaa mibii akwɛmɔhe lɛ kɛha be hee lɛ?

english: Prepare your nursery a few weeks before the major rains are expected so your seedlings are strong enough to transplant into the field as soon as steady rains begin.
ga: Saamɔ otsu lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba koni odumɔwui lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni okɛwo saatso nɔ pɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ bɔi nɛmɔ daa.

english: Why does following modern land preparation advice feel like it creates extra work for me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ he ŋaawoo ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ feɔ mi tamɔ nɔ ni ekɛ nitsumɔ kroko miiba lɛ?

english: Proper field planning and nursery care take extra time upfront, but this initial effort prevents seed failure, saves money on wasted inputs, and leads to a bigger harvest.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa kɛ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔ heɔ be kroko kɛtsɔ hiɛ. Shi nɛkɛ mra be mli mɔdɛŋbɔɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ dumɔwui ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. Kɛ shika ato nibii ni afee ni afite lɛ ahe. ni ekɛ kpamɔ ni da fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: What happens if I plant my crops without doing proper field planning first?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tsei ni mitooo he ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Planting without planning often leads to poor seed germination, wasted fertilizer, uneven water distribution, and failed crops when weather conditions suddenly change.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni atooo he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haaa dumɔwui akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. wasted fertilizer Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajaaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsake trukaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil, which prevents the maize from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa ŋmãa lɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts together with maize helps the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that can capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which naturally fertilizes neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and becoming small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee bibii ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled and wrinkled leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites that feed on plant sap and transmit leaf-curl viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛhaa helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water during heavy rains or when a soil-borne fungus enters through wounds made by tools or pests.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa mli loo kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bote pilamɔi ni nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛbaa lɛ amli.

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the soil lacks calcium or when water supply to the plant is inconsistent.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni egbo lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ ejaaa.

english: Why do all the small flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ni magbee shi kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni mitsɔko pod?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree experiences water stress, lacks proper nutrients, or when mirid bugs damage the flower stalks.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Niyenii ni sa ni bɛ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ

english: Why do my fruiting plantain trees suddenly fall over even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa eyɛ mli akɛ midaaa moŋ lɛ? He ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa bɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily if microscopic worms called nematodes or root borers destroy their root system, leaving the heavy tree with no support.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo root borers lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsiiɔ ni ebɛ nɔ ko ni ekɛfiɔ shi.

english: Why do my yam vines start drying up early before the yam tubers grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ oya dani sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early if fungal diseases like anthracnose attack the leaves or if there is severe drought during the main tuber formation stage.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baagbi oya kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose tutua tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ loo kɛji hɔmɔ ni naa wa ba yɛ be mli ni tuber lɛ feɔ titri lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants flower well but fail to produce any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ miifɔ jogbaŋŋ shi amɛwooo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas fail to form pods when flower thrips or pod-boring insects eat the flower buds before they can develop into seeds.
ga: Cowpeas nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmeii kɛji fɔfɔi thrips loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ ye ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛtsɔ dumɔwui.

english: Watering in the early morning is best because the soil absorbs the water before the sun evaporates it, and leaves dry quickly during the day, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani hulu lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ. Ni baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain, as the ground underneath is still hot and dry. Wait until the rains become consistent and the soil stays moist for a few consecutive days so your young seeds do not dry up and die.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lolo. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ koni odumɔwui bibii lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and sunlight cause plants to lose water faster than their roots can drink. The plant turns its leaves yellow and drops them on purpose to cut down on water loss and survive the dry spell.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine kɛ hulu la haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Should I burn the dry grass on my farm before planting, or is it better to clear it with a cutlass?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani madu loo ehi akɛ mikɛ tsɔne baafo mli?

english: While burning clears the land quickly, it destroys valuable soil nutrients and kills beneficial insects. Clearing without burning leaves organic matter on the ground, which rots and feeds your soil naturally over time.
ga: yɛ be mli ni la ni ashãa lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Shi efiteɔ sũ mli niyenii ni jara wa lɛ hu, ni egbeɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ hu. Kɛ́ ashɛrɛ ashwie shi ni ashãaa lɛ, ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ baafite yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does my cassava produce smaller tubers every year when I plant it on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil. Without giving the land a rest, rotating crops, or adding manure, the soil becomes weak and cannot feed the new tubers.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsakemɔ hejɔɔmɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee gbɔjɔmɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ bulbs heei anɔ.

english: How does covering my farm soil with dry grass help my plants during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass—a process called mulching—acts like a blanket that shades the ground from the hot sun, keeps moisture trapped in the soil longer, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Mulching ni egbi - nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin but only yield small corn cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii pɛ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight and soil food. They waste all their energy stretching upward to reach the light instead of using that energy to produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ jamɛ a he wami ɔ peeɔ cob blɔki nguanguahi.

english: Can I grow cowpeas together in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is very good for your farm. Cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa.

english: Why do my crop leaves get dark spots and wither after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains leave standing water on leaves and create high humidity, which helps fungal diseases spread quickly. Spacing your crops properly allows wind to flow through and dry the leaves faster.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni egbiɔ baai lɛ oya.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds instead of just planting the seeds saved from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Seeds saved from harvested high-yield crops lose their strength and uniformity in the next generation, resulting in smaller yields and weaker plants. Fresh certified seeds guarantee strong growth and disease resistance.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi. Dumɔwui heei ni ana he odaseyeli haa amɛdalɛ ni mli wa kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot inside the ground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifee klalo akɛ makpa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when the soil holds too much water without draining, or when soil insects bite into the tubers and let disease in. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni ekɛjieee mli. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔ amɛyitsei ni amɛha helai bote mli lɛ. Sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are easily scorched by full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast with broad leaves that provide vital shade and protect the cocoa seedlings while keeping the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo kɛ hebuu ni he hiaa baa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants create green leaves to absorb sunlight, so adding nitrogen fertilizer or compost will help restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli koni amɛhe hulu la. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even though the stems above ground grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Cassava needs loose soil to expand its underground roots. If the soil is hard or compacted, or if there is too much foliage fertilizer, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall leaves instead of swelling its roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse he miihia cassava koni eshishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Aloo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ kɛha baai lɛ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛbaa baai kakadaji moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: What is eating holes in my maize leaves and leaving tiny worms inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu yɛ ŋmãa baai amli? Ni ashi ŋmeii bibii yɛ tso lɛ shishi?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm. They hide inside the plant funnel and stalk during the hot daytime, so applying organic or targeted treatments early in the morning or late evening works best to control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei akui kɛ amɛshishifãi amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ yɛ amɛ nɔyeli mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden heavy watering. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and protecting plants from harsh sun helps flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni mli wa trukaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for next season's crops?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans and groundnuts gather nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decompose, that natural nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as free fertilizer for future crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei lɛ fite lɛ Adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ wɔsɛɛ be mli tamɔ ŋmãa ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my cassava plants yield fewer food tubers when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together, their stems and roots compete for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper space ensures every root has room to expand and absorb nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifã fɛɛ shishifã náa hegbɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn into powder and get filled with tiny bugs in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ miitsɔ powda ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? eyi obɔ yɛ nitoohe

english: Weevils lay eggs inside maize kernels while moisture is still present. If grains are not thoroughly dried before storing or kept in airtight bags, the eggs hatch and the insects eat the inside of the grains.
ga: Weevils woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto loo akɛto vacuum bag mli lɛ, Ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ ni kooloi bibii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: Why is burning bush on my land before planting harmful to my soil's health?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ lɛ yeɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic material, kills beneficial soil organisms that feed crop roots, and dries out the land. Clearing without burning leaves decomposing leaves to enrich the soil and retain moisture.
ga: La ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei shishifãi lɛ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi Efee faŋŋ ni eshãaa baai lɛ, efiteɔ baai lɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why should I wait for the early rains to settle before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam setts need continuous soil moisture to sprout roots and shoots smoothly. Planting too early into hot, dry soil causes the seed tuber to rot or wither before the main rainy season begins.
ga: Sweet potato sets biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ daa koni shishifãi kɛ saji akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ agbo loo amɛgboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why is it important for me to visit my farm regularly instead of just leaving the crops to grow on their own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maya miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: Being on your farm regularly allows you to spot tiny changes, such as early pest attacks or leaf discoloration, before they spread and destroy your entire yield.
ga: Kɛ́ oya oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaaha ona tsakemɔi bibii, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mra. loo baai lɛ ahe su ni tsakeɔ Dani egbɛɔ eshwaa ni efiteɔ onibii fɛɛ.

english: What specific changes on my crops should I look out for when I check my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli esa akɛ makwɛ jogbaŋŋ beni mikwɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You should check for chewed or wilting leaves, unusual spots, strange colored patches, curling foliage, or tiny insects gathering under leaves and around stems.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji baai lɛ egbo loo egbo. Nɔ ko ni ejaaa yɛ. Ayɛ hei ni yɔɔ sui ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe, loo kooloi bibii. Abua naa yɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛ tso lɛ he.

english: How do I know if my crops are being attacked by small pests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii miitutua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Pest damage usually shows as small holes in leaves, yellowing plants, stunted growth, or visible swarms of tiny insects crawling or flying around your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo akɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli, ni haa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo kooloi bibii akuu ko ni abaanyɛ ana amɛ ni amɛmiikplekeshi loo amɛmiifo kɛmiibɔle onibii ahe

english: Why do small pests suddenly appear and spread so quickly across my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii jeɔ kpo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pests reproduce very fast when weather conditions are favorable, and if they are not spotted early through frequent farm checks, a few insects can multiply into a huge invasion in just days.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ oya waa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi hi. Ni kɛji akɛ anaaa amɛ mra Kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ mli Kooloi komɛi baanyɛ atsɔ tutuamɔi wuji yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli.

english: Does seeing a few insects on my plants mean my whole farm is in danger?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mina kooloi bibii fioo komɛi yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ oshara mli?

english: Not immediately, but a few insects are an early warning sign that requires close attention so you can address the issue before it becomes a widespread outbreak.
ga: Ebaaa mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi kooloi bibii komɛi ji mra be mli kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni esa akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ osaa naagbai dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã he fɛɛ he.

english: Who should I report to when I notice strange pests damaging my crops?
ga: Namɔ esa akɛ mabɔ amaniɛ kɛ́ mina kooloi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: You should contact your local agricultural extension officers immediately, as they are trained to identify specific crop threats and guide you on the right solutions.
ga: Esa akɛ oyana okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, atsɔɔ amɛ koni amɛyoo nibii pɔtɛɛ ni woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbeyei, ni amɛtsɔɔ bo tsabaai ni sa.

english: Will an agricultural officer come to inspect my farm if I report a problem with my crops?
ga: Ani okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ baaba ni amɛbakwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mibɔ naagba ko ni kɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he amaniɛ?

english: Yes, extension officers are meant to visit your farm in person to inspect the affected plants, diagnose the exact cause of the damage, and recommend proper treatments.
ga: Hɛɛ, Extension nitsulɔi lɛ ji mɛi ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛyasara oŋmɔ lɛ koni amɛyakwɛ tsei ni ena naagbai lɛ. Kwɛmɔ nɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni kɛ nɔ ni efite lɛ ba. ni amɛtsɔɔ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsaa mɔ lɛ

english: What steps should I take immediately after I notice sick crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni miyɔse ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Take note of where the problem is located, avoid guessing treatments on your own, and immediately notify an agricultural officer to conduct a proper field inspection.
ga: ŋmaa he ni naagba lɛ yɔɔ lɛ oshwie shi. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ bɔ ni ooofee okɛ ohe aye lɛ he susumɔ he. ni amɛha okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ ale amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I just buy any agrochemical from the market to spray on my sick crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahe agrochemicals kɛjɛ jara nɔ koni mikɛshwie mitsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: No, using the wrong chemical can damage your crops or fail to kill the pest. An agricultural officer should first inspect the farm to prescribe the correct medicine for that specific problem.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii loo egbe tsɛŋemɔ helai. Esa akɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ akwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛŋmala tsofa ni sa kɛha naagba lɛ.

english: Where can I get the right medicine to stop pest infestations on my farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana tsofa ni sa ni baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akagbɛ ashwã?

english: Agricultural extension officers can inspect your farm and direct you to the exact, approved crop medicines and correct dosage needed to cure your plants safely.
ga: Okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ akwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni etsɔɔ bo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ tsei ahe lɛ kɛ tsofai ni sa ni he hiaa koni akɛtsa otsei lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are very tender and sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Without shade trees or food crops like plantains to block the sun, the young plants lose water faster than their roots can absorb it, causing the leaves to burn and the plant to die.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛ nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei tamɔ hulutsoo plantains bɛ lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ baafite nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni tsei lɛ gboiɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds blow during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that spread horizontally near the top of the ground rather than growing deep into the soil. When heavy rain softens the soil and wind pushes against the big heavy leaves, the root system cannot hold the weight and pulls out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa baai agboi ni tsii lɛ. Shishifã lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ muji lɛ nɔ ni ejie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil. To protect its new growth, the plant naturally moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the top, which starves the bottom leaves and turns them yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni akɛbu tsei heei ni eda lɛ ahe Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Enɛ baaha baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of surviving heat and drought. The plant sheds leaves to prevent moisture from escaping into the air, entering a resting state while keeping its tubers safe and growing underground until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ akaje kpo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Eboteɔ shihilɛ ni mli wa mli yɛ be mli ni ehaa bulb lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni edaa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and becoming small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. As the insects suck out the sap, the expanding leaves become distorted and curled.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Beni kooloi bibii shwieɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ Baai ni mli elɛɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Extreme heat dries out the pollen inside the flower so it cannot form fruit, causing the plant to drop the useless flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ agbiɔ, ni ehaaa amɛwo yibii, ni no haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my yam plants produce much bigger tubers when I give the vines wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ bulbs ni dara kwraa lɛ beni mikɛ tso ha wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy that fuels tuber growth underground. When vines climb stakes, the leaves spread out toward the light without overlapping, allowing the plant to produce maximum food for larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa tuber lɛ daa. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa la lɛ mli ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo kɛhaa ŋmeii wuji lɛ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts in my field helps my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with tiny beneficial bacteria in the soil to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnut plant dies and decomposes, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ helatsɛmɛi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni emɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛto shishifãi lɛ amli Kɛji ŋmei tso lɛ gbo ni efite Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the soil if I plant immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often moistens only the top layer of dirt while the deep soil stays dry and hot. If a long dry spell follows that first rain, the seeds begin to sprout but run out of water and get cooked by the hot, dry soil underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli fũuɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ kã he egbi ni edɔ. Kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ hɔmɔ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ shi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ haa nu baaje amɛmli ni amɛshwere.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay weak and short even when I use good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ kuku eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kpakpai tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong root systems that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crop plants. Because weeds grow faster, they choke out the crop and take the food your crop needs to grow tall and strong.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni eyeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them out in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong, direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out their roots before they can establish themselves in the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I find small caterpillars hiding inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mikɛ mihe ewo mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer feeding inside the moist central leaves of young maize, chewing through tender tissue before the plant can fully grow.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ baai ni mli efɔ lɛ. Amɛtsɔɔ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ amli amɛyeɔ nii dani tso lɛ daa kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting, curling, and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebɔle ehe, ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus carried by tiny whiteflies that stops the plant from making leaves and growing large tubers underground.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛbaa Enɛ haaa tso lɛ afee baai ni ekwɛɛɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up, causing temporary wilting until temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or a lack of nutrients in the soil needed to support fruit development.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni aduawai akwɛ̃.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas alongside my main crops improve my soil?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally adding essential nutrients to the soil for neighboring crops to use.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Overcrowding forces plants to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving no single plant with enough food to yield well.
ga: Nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa tsei wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei komɛi bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow in a V-shape while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves signal a lack of nitrogen; the plant moves its limited nitrogen supply to the newest growth at the top to keep growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen fioo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛya shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my small vegetable seedlings fall over and rot right at the ground level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ Mine lɛ gbee shi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is called damping-off, a soil fungal disease that attacks soft plant stems when seedling beds are kept overly wet and lack proper air circulation.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ damp-off, ni ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting inside when I store them in a closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ akɛto tsu ko ni aŋã mli lɛ?

english: Stored yams need cool, dry air moving around them to prevent humidity build-up and fungal spores from causing soft rots during storage.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potatoes ni ato lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni egbi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa. Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔtɔ akabua ehe naa ni ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ akafite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my yam crops failing when I plant them close to my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines require full, direct sunlight to develop healthy leaves and large tubers. Plantain trees grow broad, heavy leaves that create deep shade, preventing the yams from getting the sunlight they need to mature.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná baai ni wa kɛ bulbs wuji. Dumɔwui lɛ daa, baai ni tsii ni haa hulutsoo ni mli kwɔ baa. Tsi sweet potatoes lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops waste away when I plant too many different tall crops together in one field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ midu tsei kakadaji srɔtoi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: When tall crops are planted densely together, their broad leaves overlap and block sunlight from reaching the lower layers. This forces sun-loving plants to starve and wither due to a lack of light energy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsei kakadaji ni daraa lɛ feɔ ekome babaoo lɛ Amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shishigbɛ tsũi lɛ ahe. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei ni sumɔɔ hulu lɛ anɔ koni hɔmɔ aye amɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ la hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines stretch so high up their wooden stakes instead of staying on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa tso tso nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally grow upwards toward light. Staking helps the leaves catch direct sunshine cleanly, which fuels the growth of big tubers below the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baatsɔ adebɔɔ naa kɛya la lɛ he. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la ni he tse ni tɛ̃ɛ. ni ji tsofa ni haa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa lɛ

english: Can I plant cassava and yam on the exact same mound or plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: While both can grow in similar soils, cassava roots grow aggressively and take up a lot of space and soil nutrients, which can crowd out yam tubers if they are planted too closely together.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔji ni tamɔ amɛhe nɔ moŋ, Shi ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛheɔ he babaoo kɛ niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ akpɛtɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Which food crops can I safely grow under the heavy shade of mature plantain trees?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii tsei manyɛ makwɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ plantain ni eda lɛ shishi?

english: Shade-tolerant crops like cocoyam and ginger grow well beneath plantain leaves, whereas sun-loving crops like yam or maize will fail to yield properly under that shade.
ga: Tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli, tamɔ kookoo kɛ ŋmei, kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ plantain baai ashishi. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni sumɔɔ hulu la, tamɔ sweet potatoes loo corn Enyɛŋ eba akɛ abaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa yɛ nakai hulutsoo be lɛ shishi.

english: Is it better for me to separate my plantain farm from my yam farm entirely?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ mafo mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ kɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli kwraa?

english: Yes, keeping yams in their own open plot ensures they receive full sunlight all day without competing with the broad leaves and shallow root systems of plantain trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato to he ko lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ akaŋ

english: Why does my cassava survive during dry spells while my other crops wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hu hiɔ shi lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ gboɔ?

english: Cassava has deep, strong root systems that store water and nutrients, allowing it to withstand long dry periods better than crops like yam or leafy vegetables.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni toɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni hulu lɛ egbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei tamɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai ni yɔɔ baai.

english: Why are my cassava tubers smaller than usual when grown right next to plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ kɛ́ adu yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plantain trees take up large amounts of soil moisture and nutrients quickly. This leaves very little nutrition for nearby cassava plants to build large tubers.
ga: Dumɔwui yeɔ sũ mli nu kɛ niyenii babaoo oya. Enɛ haa ŋmeii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ naa niyenii fioo ko pɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: How far apart should I space my plantain suckers when setting up a new farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ abɔ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ miito ŋmɔ hee ko shishi?

english: Plantains should be planted about 3 meters apart. Wide spacing prevents their large leaves from overlapping completely, allowing ground crops to still catch some sunlight.
ga: Esa akɛ adu plantains kɛjɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3. Nɛkɛ gbɛ ni jɛkɛ waa nɛɛ tsiɔ baai wuji anaa koni amɛkafo amɛhe kwraa. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa hulu la fioo lolo.

english: Why do my sun-loving crops grow slowly if I do not trim my plantain leaves regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni misumɔɔ hulu lɛ daa blɛoo kɛji mifolɔɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Overgrown plantain leaves block air movement and sunshine. Trimming old or low-hanging leaves lets light reach the ground so smaller neighboring crops can survive.
ga: Plantain baai ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni yaa lɛ naa. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai ni egbɔ loo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ koni la ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Is there any real nutritional difference between growing white corn and yellow corn for my family?
ga: Ani niyenii mli hewalɛ mli srɔtofeemɔi diɛŋtsɛ yɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ ni aduɔ ahaa miweku lɛ teŋ?

english: Yes, yellow corn contains a higher protein content and additional nutrients compared to white corn, making it a healthier choice for human consumption and family nutrition.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni ji yellow lɛ yɛ protein babaoo kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni fata he kɛ akɛto ŋmãa yɛŋ he. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha adesai aniyenii kɛ weku niyenii.

english: How does consuming yellow corn help improve the health of people in my community?
ga: Te ŋmãa ni ji yellow ŋmãa ni ayeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mɛi ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ aná hewalɛ kpakpa aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Yellow corn is rich in protein and essential vitamins that help build body strength and keep families healthy, which makes it a valuable food crop to grow and eat.
ga: Protein kɛ vitamini ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ ni ehaa weku lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fa babaoo yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii tso ni jara wa ni esa akɛ akwɛ ni aye.

english: Can I feed yellow corn to my farm animals to help them grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ ŋmãa ni ji yellow koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, because yellow corn has a higher protein level than regular white corn, it provides excellent nutrition that helps livestock like poultry and pigs grow stronger and healthier.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmãa ni ji yellow lɛ yɛ protein babaoo fe ŋmãa yɛŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa kooloi tamɔ kooloi kɛ tsinai ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why are traders in coastal towns like Cape Coast and Takoradi always looking for yellow corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ ŋshɔnaa maji tamɔ Cape Coast kɛ Takoradi lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: People living in the Central and Western regions of Ghana have a strong preference for eating yellow corn, so local markets in those coastal cities experience very high demand.
ga: Mɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana teŋgbɛ kɛ anaigbɛ kpokpai lɛ sumɔɔ abele ŋmɔŋ waa. No hewɔ lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli ni yɔɔ nakai ŋshɔnaa maji lɛ amli lɛ he miihia babaoo waa.

english: If I plant yellow corn on my farm this season, will I easily find buyers for my harvest?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli Ani ebaafee mlɛo kɛha mi akɛ mana mɛi ni baahe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, yellow corn is in high demand in Ghana, and large buyers or traders are often willing to purchase a major share—sometimes up to 60% or more—of a farmer's total yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, ataoɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ waa yɛ Ghana. Ni bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nibii loo jarayelɔi wuji lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe nibii babaoo. Bei komɛi lɛ, eshɛɔ 60% loo nɔ ni fe nakai. yɛ okwaafoi lɛ anibii fɛɛ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ mli

english: Why do some grain buyers encourage farmers to plant yellow maize instead of regular white maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi ni heɔ ŋmaa lɛ miiwo okwaafoi hewalɛ koni amɛdu ŋmaa ni ji ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmaa ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni amɛduɔ daa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Buyers prefer yellow maize because it sells faster in major markets, carries higher nutritional value, and satisfies strong consumer demand in urban centers.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ ahɔ̃ɔ oya yɛ jarayeli hei wuji. Eyɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo ni ekɛ jarayelɔi ahiamɔ nii ni mli wa kpeɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: Does yellow corn need a special climate or specific region in Ghana to grow well?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ krɛdɛɛ ko loo kpokpaa pɔtɛɛ ko he miihia ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ yɛ Ghana koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yellow corn grows well in many parts of Ghana, including the southern coastal districts, as long as it receives adequate water and proper soil management during its growth cycle.
ga: Abɛi ŋmɔŋ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana hei babaoo. Nɔ ni fata he ji ŋshɔnaa kpokpaa ni yɔɔ anaigbɛ lɛ Shii abɔ ni nu ni fa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa baaha yɛ shweremɔ be lɛ mli lɛ,.

english: What happens to yellow corn production when the rainfall and growing conditions are good?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmãa ni ji yellow corn lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ jogbaŋŋ ni shihilɛi ni haa ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ yɛ?

english: When weather conditions are favorable and water is abundant, yellow corn produces high yields with rich protein content, giving farmers a large and valuable harvest.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ hi ni nu babaoo yɛ lɛ, Yellow corn woɔ yibii babaoo ni protein babaoo yɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛkpaa nibii wuji ni jara wa.

english: Will I be able to sell my yellow corn crop if many other farmers in my area harvest at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ mi-yellow corn lɛ kɛji okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ kpaa lɛ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Even during abundant harvest periods, demand for yellow corn remains strong in major towns like Cape Coast and Takoradi, so buyers continue to purchase large quantities.
ga: Yɛ kpamɔ be ni fa babaoo lɛ mli po lɛ, mɛi ni taoɔ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa lɛ mli wa yɛ maji wuji tamɔ Cape Coast kɛ Takoradi mli, no hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miihe babaoo lolo.

english: Is it better to sell my harvested corn to local village markets or to travelling traders from bigger towns?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ mahã akrowa lɛ jarayelihe ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ loo mahã jarayelɔi ni jɛ maji wuji amli kɛbaa lɛ?

english: Selling to travelling traders from larger cities can be very profitable because they buy in bulk—often taking more than half your harvest—to supply high-demand markets in urban areas.
ga: Nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ ahaa jarayelɔi ni jɛɔ maji wuji amli lɛ baanyɛ aha aná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo. Ejaakɛ amɛheɔ jarayeli nibii babaoo—bei pii lɛ, amɛheɔ nɔ ni fe nibii ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ fã—koni amɛkɛ jarayeli hei ni mɛi biɔ nibii babaoo yɛ maji wuji amli lɛ aba.

english: How do fertilizers actually help my crops grow better and get energy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo?

english: Just like food gives people energy, fertilizers supply essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. These nutrients act as food for crops, helping them build green leaves, grow strong stems, and yield healthy produce.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii haa gbɔmɛi hewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nyɔŋtsei hu haa niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiam. Nibii nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa baai eŋɔli, amɛshishifãi ni wa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛmli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is hungry for nitrogen. When the soil lacks nutrients, plants cannot create energy properly, causing their lower leaves to turn yellow and stall their growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ Tsei nyɛɛɛ afee hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etsĩɔ dalɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and tall without bearing fruit when planted under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce energy through their leaves. When planted under heavy shade, they stretch upward searching for light instead of using their energy to develop strong stems and fruits.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ekpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eyatao la, ni no najiaŋ lɛ, efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni wa.

english: Is rain water enough for my crops, or do I need to set up a watering system on my farm?
ga: Ani nugbɔ nu lɛ fa kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ loo ehe miihia ni makɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rainfall helps during the wet season, but dry spells can stunt crop growth. Setting up a reliable watering method ensures crops get continuous moisture, giving them the strength to survive heat and keep growing.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ, tsei baanyɛ akpa dalɛ. Nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni atoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli nu baa daa. Enɛ haa tsei hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ dɔlɛ mli ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛdaraa.

english: How can I tell if my crop plants are getting enough water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Thirsty crops will show signs like curling, drooping, or browning leaves. Providing steady water keeps their leaf stems firm and upright, which allows the plant to stay healthy and strong.
