ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ baatsɔɔ okadii tamɔ baai ni ebɔle, ni egbɔjɔ loo ni tsuɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ tsei lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural behavior where the plant reduces its surface area to stop water from evaporating too quickly in the heat. It is a sign that the crop is feeling heat stress and needs moisture.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ko ni tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ kɛji akɛ edɔ. Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikpe dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni ehe miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Plants drop flowers when they do not have enough water or nutrients to support fruit growth. The plant conserves its energy by shedding flowers until conditions improve.
ga: Tsei baashwie fɔfɔii kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ bɛ. Tsei buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant beans or cowpeas alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This provides extra food and strength to nearby crops naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ lɛ naa niyenii kɛ hewalɛ kroko.

english: What is the best way to start planting cassava so I do not lose my crop in the first month?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajeɔ ŋmei dumɔ shishi koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Starting with healthy stem cuttings planted at a slant in loose, weed-free soil right at the start of the rainy season ensures rapid root development and strong early growth.
ga: Je shishi kɛ tso yibii ni mli wa ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ejɔ, ni jwɛi bɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: What makes crops stand strong in the soil during heavy winds and rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii teɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Deep, healthy root systems anchor the plant into the earth. Well-drained, nutrient-rich soil allows roots to spread wide and deep, giving the crop structural strength against storm damage.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa fiɔ tso lɛ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. Ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa kɛjɛɔ ahum ni baafiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my rubber trees seem to draw so much more water from the soil than my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi rɔba tso lɛ gbalaa nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe mi tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Rubber trees need a large amount of water to produce latex, which is mostly liquid sap. Taking in plenty of water allows the tree to build up pressure and yield strong, continuous latex flows when tapped.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia rɔba tsei koni amɛfee latɛs. ni ji mliki ni ji nu babaoo Nu babaoo ni anuɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ ni ebaaha nu ni mli wa ni hoɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ aba kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ.

english: Can I successfully grow rubber trees in a dry region with low rainfall?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu rɔba yɛ hei ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo yɛ lɛ yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: Rubber trees require high amounts of water to produce good latex yields. Planting them in dry areas will severely reduce their growth and production because they cannot get the moisture they need.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia rɔba tsei koni amɛná latɛs kpakpa. Dumɔ yɛ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ baaha dalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo aba shi waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulutsoo ni amɛtaoɔ lɛ.

english: How do I extract latex from a rubber tree without harming or killing the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie latɛs kɛjɛ rɔbɔt tso mli ni miyeee tso lɛ awui loo mifiteee lɛ?

english: Latex is harvested by making light cuts into the bark, which lets the liquid sap bleed out into a container. As long as the main tree remains standing and uninjured deep inside, it will heal and keep producing.
ga: Latex ni akpaa kɛtsɔ tso lɛ yibii ni afoɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ. koni mliki lɛ ajɛ mli kɛya tsɛnsi lɛ mli Be fɛɛ be ni tso titri lɛ baahi shi ni epilaaa yɛ emlibotemɔ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ baaya nɔ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: What actually is the latex coming out of my rubber tree, and how does the tree make it?
ga: Mɛni ji nu ni jɛɔ mi rɔba tso lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Ni te tsei feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛbɔɔ lɛ?

english: Latex is a milky fluid sap created by the rubber tree using soil nutrients and water. The tree naturally produces it to protect and heal bark wounds, which allows farmers to harvest it continuously.
ga: Latex ji nu ni tamɔ mliki ni rɔbɔt tsei kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ. Tsei feɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu pilamɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ahe ni amɛtsa amɛ. Enɛ haa okwaafoi nyɛɔ amɛkpaa nii daa.

english: If a crop demands heavy water and care, does that mean it will give me better harvest returns?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ biɔ nu babaoo kɛ kwɛmɔ Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai?

english: Yes, demanding crops like rubber turn large amounts of water and soil nutrients into valuable yields like latex, rewarding hard-working farmers with strong long-term returns.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ataoɔ waa tamɔ rɔba lɛ tsakeɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii babaoo ewoɔ nibii ni jara wa tamɔ latɛs mli. Ekɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli nyɔmɔwoo ni mli wa woɔ okwaafoi ni tsuɔ nii waa lɛ nyɔmɔ.

english: How long can a single rubber tree keep producing latex before I need to replace it?
ga: Be enyiɛ rɔba tso kome baanyɛ afee latɛs dani ehe baahia ni atsake lɛ?

english: A well-cared-for rubber tree can remain productive for 30 to 50 years, giving you decades of regular harvests from the same standing tree.
ga: Rɔba tso ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii afii 30 kɛyashi 50, ni enɛ baaha oná ŋmaa ni yaa nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ kɛjɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli.

english: Why should I invest in planting tree crops like rubber instead of only growing seasonal crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mishika awo tsei tamɔ rɔbɔt tsei adumɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu be mli nibii tamɔ ŋmãa pɛ?

english: Seasonal crops only provide income for one harvest, but perennial tree crops like rubber stay standing for up to 50 years, creating continuous wealth that can support your children into the future.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be mli lɛ haa anáa shika kɛha kpamɔ kome pɛ. Shi tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ rɔbɔt tsei lɛ baahi shi kɛyashi afii 50, ni ekɛ ninamɔ ni yaa nɔ ni baanyɛ aye abua owɔsɛɛ yinɔi lɛ aba.

english: Will my rubber trees keep providing income every year as long as I do not cut them down?
ga: Ani mi rɔbɔt tso lɛ baaya nɔ ekɛ shika aba afi fɛɛ afi, kɛji mifooo lɛ?

english: Yes, as long as the rubber trees stay standing, healthy, and properly managed, they will consistently produce latex for your family year after year.
ga: Hɛɛ, be fɛɛ be ni rɔbɔt tso lɛ baahi shi, eyɛ hewalɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Rɔba tso lɛ baaya nɔ afee latɛs aha oweku lɛ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why are farmland sales for rubber trees often restricted to specific local areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, ahɔ̃ɔ rɔbɔt tsei yɛ hei pɔtɛɛ komɛi pɛ lɛ?

english: Certain tree crops require specific local climate and soil conditions to thrive, and local traditional systems often restrict long-term land purchases to protected designated agricultural zones.
ga: Tsei komɛi biɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛshwere. Ni bei pii lɛ, akutseiaŋ kusum gbɛjianɔtoi haaa shikpɔŋ ni aheɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ aya okwaayeli hei ni abuɔ he lɛ anɔ.

english: What kind of daily effort is required to maintain a successful rubber farm?
ga: Mɔdɛŋbɔɔ enyiɛ ehe hiaa daa gbi koni anyɛ akwɛ rɔba ŋmɔ ko ni yeɔ omanye nɔ?

english: Rubber farming requires continuous dedication to keep trees healthy, ensure proper water access, and follow systematic tapping schedules to maintain good latex output over many years.
ga: Rɔba ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ hejɔɔmɔ be fɛɛ be koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ ni nu lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni amɛnyiɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni akɛtswaa latɛs lɛ sɛɛ koni amɛha latɛs ni afeɔ lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully mature and ready to be harvested from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves turn yellow and dry, the outer husks turn brown, and the kernels at the tip of the cob become hard with a visible dark spot at their base.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ blɔfo. ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ naagbee lɛ mli wa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii diji ni anaa yɛ amɛshishigbɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my plantain plants sometimes fall off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Plantain flowers drop early without forming fruit when the plant suffers from severe water stress during hot dry spells or when insect pests attack the flower stalk.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbee shi oya ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ ni naa wa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua fɔfɔii ahe tsei

english: Why should I dry my harvested cassava roots before putting them into a processing machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ dani mikɛwo tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Drying cassava removes excess moisture, which prevents the processing machine from clogging and stops the cassava from fermenting or spoiling into poor-quality flour.
ga: Cassava ni agbiɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haaa etsi ehe. ni etsĩ ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ loo efite ni etsɔ ashikishaŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing fewer pods now that they are over ten years old?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ kɛji amɛye fe afii nyɔŋma lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, old branches become overgrown and shaded out, reducing pod production unless you regularly prune dead wood and manage canopy light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ, niji momo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ fe nine ni ehaa hulu tsoɔ. Enɛ haa pod ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi. Ja ofo tsei ni egboi ni okwɛ ŋwɛi kanei anɔ daa.

english: Why do my oil palm seedlings grow very tall and thin when I nurse them under dense shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo waa beni mikwɛɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch upward seeking sunlight when shaded too heavily, making them weak and prone to snapping when transplanted to the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ kɛ́ amɛyɛ hulutsoo be mli tsɔ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebaaku kɛji ajie lɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow and rot during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away essential nutrients from the topsoil and creates waterlogged soil where roots cannot breathe, leading to root rot and yellow leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baa he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What causes my growing tomatoes to turn soft and black on the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha tomato ni midu lɛ miifee blɛoo ni efee ediŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ dani ekwɛ̃?

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium in the plant during fruit development, often triggered by inconsistent watering that prevents roots from absorbing minerals.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be koni shishifãi lɛ akaŋɔ minerals.

english: What happens if I plant my yam setts too close to each other in the mounds?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko mli?

english: Planting yams too close forces the roots to compete for space, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in many small tubers instead of large, healthy ones.
ga: Kɛ́ adu sweet potatoes yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ abɔ he akaŋ koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: How do weeds growing around my cowpea plants slow down their growth?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te mi-cowpea tso lɛ dalɛ miiba shi eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with cowpeas for sunlight, water, and plant food, while also hosting pests that attack cowpea leaves and young pods.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsina ŋmeii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, jɛmɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa cowpea baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɔɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to keep a written record of my planting dates and harvest yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋma gbii ni adu kɛ gbii ni akpaa lɛ he saji awo wolo nɔ lɛ?

english: Keeping simple records helps you track which crops perform best, plan exact dates for fertilizer application, and predict harvest timing to get the best market prices.
ga: Nibii ni aŋmala ashwie shi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Too gbi pɔtɛɛ ni akɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nii lɛ he gbɛjianɔ. ni otsɔɔ kpamɔ bei amli koni onine ashɛ jara ni hi fe fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds blow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the soil. When heavy rains soften the ground, the roots cannot anchor the top-heavy tree against strong winds, especially if it is carrying a heavy bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ tso ni tsii fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Titri lɛ kɛji tso lɛ miitere niji ni tsii.

english: Why does my yam vine need a tall wooden stake to climb on to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni mikɛkwɔ koni maná bulbs agboi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ená hulu la babaoo ni eha ehe atse kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: How do groundnut plants produce their nuts under the soil after flowering above ground?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii beni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Once a groundnut flower is pollinated above ground, it drops its petals and grows a long stem called a peg. This peg bends downward, pushes itself into the soft soil, and swells into the groundnut pod underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei fɔfɔii lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ekɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eyɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg. Abaakumɔ pin nɛɛ shi. Tsi ohe kɛya shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ mli. ni efuɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmei ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into tomatoes during hot dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: High temperatures and dry air stress tomato plants and destroy their pollen. When the flower cannot be pollinated due to extreme heat, the plant sheds it to save water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ pollen. Beni fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ afee pollin yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ Akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ Tsei anɔ koni akɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my young maize crop turn yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tip mean the maize plant is missing nitrogen, an essential plant food. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen out of the soil, causing the plant to pull energy from its lowest leaves to keep new leaves growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbalaa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛ baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my mature cassava tubers rot if I leave them in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mature cassava roots stop growing and absorb excess water when the ground stays wet. Waterlogged soil blocks air from reaching the roots, allowing fungal and bacterial diseases to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni amɛmuɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli kɛ bacteria mli baa lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up right on the tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and overly shaded cocoa farms. The fungus attacks the pod skin, turning it black and killing the beans inside.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni edɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli fe nine lɛ amli. Fuŋ lɛ tutuaa pod lɛ hewolo lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from young shoots, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. The damaged tissue grows unevenly, making the leaf twist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Tisu ni efite lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my rice crop look green and tall but produce empty seed heads at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ekwɛɔ shi eyɛ dumɔwui ayitsei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: If a rice plant suffers from dry spells or extreme heat right when it is flowering, pollination fails. The plant continues to look healthy, but the grain heads fill with empty chaff instead of heavy rice grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo latsaa ni naa wa mli yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, Pollination lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ lolo. Shi dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ ŋmaa ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Why do my crop harvests get smaller every year even when I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ faaa daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot every season drains specific nutrients from the soil faster than the earth can rebuild them. Over time, exhausted soil leads to weaker plants and lower yields unless you add nutrients or rotate crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ ama amɛ ekoŋŋ. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi. Ja okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fata he loo otsake ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to stay green and build strong stalks. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growth stage helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni he hiaa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ená ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he mra yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops if I plant maize in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the ground time to recover. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts naturally restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant cowpeas or groundnuts to make the soil better for other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsina loo ŋmeii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural plant food, leaving rich soil behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ tsei adebɔɔ mli niyenii. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni ashiɔ ahaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my small cocoa pods drying up and turning black on the tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ediŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Black pods are usually caused by a fungal infection that spreads in cool, humid weather, or by natural shedding when the tree has produced more pods than it has water and nutrients to support.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. aloo kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli shwiemɔ nɔ beni tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe nɔ ni nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and becoming small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant's sap, or by a virus carried by those same insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess water fills the soil gaps, suffocating the roots and allowing fungal rots to thrive in the soggy conditions.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baayi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ daa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers drop off without forming fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are no bees around to shake the pollen inside the flower to fertilize it.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛkɛwo amɛmli.

english: Why do my garden vegetable leaves look wilted in the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli aduawai ahe baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water faster through the air than the roots can suck up from the soil. The plant droops temporarily to protect itself from drying out until the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baashwie baai lɛ be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ehe koni ekagbi kɛyashi hulu lɛ baanyɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes in my farm for yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to create food for the tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun and protects them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli, ni ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some plantain suckers grow into strong trees with large bunches while others stay weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi daraa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni he wa kɛ jwɛi wuji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Narrow-leafed 'sword suckers' attached firmly to the mother plant carry strong roots and stored energy, whereas broad-leafed 'water suckers' have weak root connections and produce small bunches.
ga: Klante tso’ ni baai lɛ mli tse ni kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ he waa lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni ekɛ hewalɛ eto, yɛ be mli ni ‘nu tso’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing rice?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Rice grows best in low-lying land or valley bottoms that hold water well and stay moist for long periods, especially soils with high clay content.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa loo jɔɔ lɛ shishi ni nu hiɛɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Titri lɛ shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ sũ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Does rice need to stand in deep water all the time to grow well?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmã awo nu ni mli kwɔ mli be fɛɛ be koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, rice needs very moist or saturated soil, but deep standing water is not always required; young plants can drown if flooded too early.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu. Shi jeee be fɛɛ be nu ni mli kwɔ he hiaa. Tsei bibii baanyɛ agboi kɛji nu lɛ ho oya tsɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice plants turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking food like nitrogen fertilizer, or the plant roots are struggling from lack of oxygen due to stagnant water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miibɔi oxygen ni bɛ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ hewɔ.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my rice field?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi ŋmɔji lɛ amli?

english: Fertilizer is best applied in stages: once during early planting to help root growth, and again when the plant starts branching and forming seed heads.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli: shikome yɛ dumɔ shishijee fãi lɛ amli koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Ni agbɛnɛ hu beni tso lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni efeɔ dumɔwui ayitsei lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that absorb fertilizer and water faster than crops, which is why early clearing is necessary to prevent them from choking your plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie mra koni tsei lɛ akagbɔjɔ lɛ.

english: Why do birds attack my rice farm just when the seeds start showing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi miitutua mi ŋmɔji lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ?

english: Birds target young rice grains because they contain a sweet, soft juice inside before hardening into rice grains; scaring devices or group planting helps reduce the loss.
ga: Okpoi lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ ŋmãa ni bɛ hewalɛ yɔɔ mli. Eyɛ mli dani ewa ni etsɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa. Scare nibii loo kuu mli dumɔ haa nɔ ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my rice break into small pieces when it goes through the milling machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ fãa bibii bibii kɛ́ etsɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice grains break easily if they were harvested too late when overly dry, or dried too quickly under harsh, direct sun before milling.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ fãa oya kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ sɛɛ tsɔ beni amɛgbi tsɔ lɛ. loo egbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi dani ekɛ kɔla awo mli

english: How can I store my harvested rice grain so insects do not eat it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ato koni kooloi akaye?

english: Rice must be dried thoroughly until very hard, stored in clean hermetic bags, and kept off the bare ground on wooden platforms in a dry room.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa waa. Okɛto vacuum kotoku ni mli tse mli. ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ tso ni akɛdamɔ shi yɛ tsu ko ni mli egbi mli.

english: Why do buyers in the market sometimes prefer imported rice over what I grow locally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ fe ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Buyers prefer imported rice mainly because it is thoroughly cleaned of stones and chaff; properly cleaning and destoning your local rice makes it just as desirable.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ titri ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ kɛ ŋmãa lɛ he tse. Omaŋ ŋmãa lɛ he saamɔ kɛ ekpãtãmɔ ni sa lɛ haa anáa babaoo hu.

english: How will selling my harvested crops to processing companies benefit me?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nibii ni mikpaa lɛ ni mikɛbaahɔ̃ɔ nitsumɔhe ko ni feɔ nibii lɛ baaná he sɛɛ kɛha mi?

english: Selling directly to processing companies gives you a reliable buyer who purchases in large quantities at agreed prices, protecting you from quick sales to low-paying middlemen.
ga: Kɛ́ ohɔ̃ɔ oha nitsumɔhe ko ni feɔ nibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa onáa mɔ ni oheɔ oyeɔ ni heɔ nibii babaoo yɛ jara ni nyɛkpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ jarayeli oya kɛyaa mɛi ni woɔ amɛ nyɔmɔ fioo lɛ ateŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to stay green. The plant automatically moves its remaining nitrogen to the young top leaves to keep growing, leaving the older bottom leaves starved.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji tso titri ni esa akɛ akwɛ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak with small harvests when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmaa fioo pɛ ji nɔ ni mikpaa beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, they compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Because no single plant gets enough food, all of them remain weak and produce poor yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ waa. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli ejaakɛ tso ko bɛ ni naaa niyenii ni fa No hewɔ lɛ tsei fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and showing bright yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kpɛɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The disease damages the green leaves, making it hard for the plant to catch sunlight and grow thick tubers.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ fiteɔ baai eŋɔli. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaaná hulu la, ni ehaa bulb lɛ mli shwieɔ shi.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod Disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, damp conditions. Excess shade and weeds trap moisture around the tree, allowing the fungus to attack and destroy the cocoa pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Shade kɛ jwɛi ni fa babaoo lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ, ni no haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tutuaa kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ni egbeɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants bunching up tightly into a ball instead of growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔ he ekome ni efee bɔɔlu yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee agbo lɛ?

english: Tight leaf curling is usually caused by microscopic insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves. They feed on plant sap, injecting saliva that makes the leaves grow distorted and stunted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii waa tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa. Amɛyeɔ tsei amli nu koni amɛkɛshwie ŋmɔtɔ, ni no haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather conditions get too hot or dry. Heat stress stops the flowers from pollinating properly, so the plant sheds them to save energy and water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo egbi. Heat haomɔ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that sit near the surface rather than deep in the earth. When rain saturates the soil, it becomes soft, and a heavy bunch of plantains easily pulls the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, efeɔ blɛoo ni plantain tsei babaoo jieɔ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs when I grow them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Maize needs direct, full sunlight all day to make energy for growing cobs. Under tree shade, the leaves cannot capture enough light, so the plant lacks the energy needed to produce large cobs.
ga: Hulu la he miihia ŋmãa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha ŋmãa lɛ shweremɔ. yɛ tsei ashishi Baai lɛ nyɛŋ aná la ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ tsei bɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam tubers rot when the soil holds too much water and fails to drain properly. Standing water suffocates the roots and tubers, creating ideal conditions for fungal and bacterial decay.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni enyɛɛɛ etsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ baaha shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha fungal kɛ bacteria fitemɔ.

english: How do weeds in my field slow down my crop growth even when there is enough rain?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha mitsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po?

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants that aggressively steal soil nutrients, fertilizer, and water before your crops can reach them, starving your crop plants of essential nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu dani onibii lɛ baashɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ onibii amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like cigars when the afternoon sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ sigaret kɛ́ shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water during extreme heat. It is a natural defense mechanism to survive dry spells, but if they stay rolled up for days, the crop needs urgent watering or rain.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni nu akaje mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛha yiwalaheremɔ yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli. Shi kɛji akɛ akɛto gbii babaoo lɛ, Nu loo nugbɔ he miihia Nibii ni Aduɔ lɛ oya.

english: How do I know if my land is good enough to plant cassava this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Cassava grows best in loose, well-drained soil where roots can easily expand into tubers. If your soil holds too much standing water or is extremely hard clay, the cassava roots will rot or remain small.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ bulbs oya. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo loo eji shikpɔŋ ni wa waa. Ani ŋmei shishifãi lɛ egbo loo amɛji bibii lolo?

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and drooping even though it rained recently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ enɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean too much water around the roots, poor soil nutrients, or a root disease. Too much standing water chokes the plant's roots, preventing them from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii kpakpai. loo shishifã hela Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkamu loo amɛkaye nii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my corn seeds as close together as possible to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant enough space allows it to grow strong and produce larger ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eda ni ewo ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: What can I cover the ground around my crops with to keep the dirt from drying out so fast?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni muji lɛ akagbi oya nɛkɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass, leaves, or leftover stems—known as mulching—acts like a blanket. It shades the soil from the hot sun, keeps the ground cool, and traps moisture longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo tsei ni eshwɛ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do caterpillars eat my young crops faster during dry weather than during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry weather stresses young plants, making them weaker and easier for insects to feed on. Heavy rain often washes away tiny pests and eggs, while hot dry spells allow insect populations to multiply quickly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kooloi lɛ ahe waaa, ni amɛyeɔ mlɛo. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛwuji, yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa kooloi babaoo fɔɔ oya.

english: Is it good to plant beans together in the same field with my corn?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting beans with corn is very helpful because beans take nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the corn while protecting the soil surface.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Ejaakɛ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baaba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa yɛ be kome too mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hebuu

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant sprout quickly while others rot in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni miduɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu fiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of moisture, warmth, and planting depth to sprout. Planting seeds too deep, in overly wet soil, or using damaged seeds causes them to rot before they can grow.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo, dɔlɛ kɛ dumɔ mlibotemɔ teŋ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ tsɔ nɔ Loo dumɔwui ni efite ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell when my yam tubers are ready to be harvested from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When yam plants are ready, the green leaves on the vine will turn yellow and start to dry up naturally. This signals that the plant has finished storing energy down in the tuber.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato tsei lɛ efee klalo lɛ Baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛje shishi amɛgbi. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eyitso lɛ naa.

english: Why does my farm produce fewer bags of crop each year even when the rain falls well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ lɛ miinɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops without adding plant food back, the soil loses essential nutrients. Over time, the land becomes tired and hungry, requiring compost, animal manure, or fertilizer to restore its strength.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛ tsei niyenii fataaa he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. Be ni be hoɔ lɛ, etɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni hɔmɔ baaye lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii koni ekɛ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I plant them in an open clear field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates living umbrellas that give young cocoa the shade and moisture needed to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers advise putting long wooden stakes in the soil for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in the sun to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the hot ground, reduces pest attacks, and ensures maximum sunlight reaches the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi ni oha hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize turning yellow in the shape of a V?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential plant food. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-decayed manure helps the leaves turn healthy green and form big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii agbo.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a crop family that captures natural nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil. Planting them restores natural fertility, leaving the land rich for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans fata tsei aweku ko ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Tsei nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aku sɛɛ aba. ni eshiɔ gbɛ babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Does it make any difference if I plant my cassava cuttings slanting instead of pushing them straight down into the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ mi-cassava niji lɛ du yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛbaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slanting angle encourages tubers to spread out widely and grow closer to the surface, making harvesting easier and allowing roots to anchor firmly against strong winds.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa cassava shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo ni amɛdaraa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ehaa ekpamɔ feɔ mlɛo ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ

english: When crops are crowded, they compete aggressively with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each seed proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food to build strong stems and produce full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko to dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa ni ewo dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the blossoms dropping off my pepper plants without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni pepper ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Providing shade during harsh sun periods and watering consistently helps the flowers stay on and turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Shade yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black rot at the bottom of tomatoes is caused by a lack of calcium and uneven soil moisture during fruit growth. Keeping soil evenly watered and adding compost or lime cures this condition.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ daraa lɛ. Nu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Okɛto he ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo lime afata he koni eye ebua ni atsa hela nɛɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting my crops right after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsei adumɔ he yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by several dry, hot weeks. Waiting until the rains are regular ensures the soil stays consistently moist so tender seedlings don't dry out and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ otsii babaoo ni mli egbi ni edɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do I see small ragged holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ mi-baby corn leaf cones lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows inside young maize leaves to feed. Catching them early and applying safe controls protects the heart of the plant so it can mature.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii amli koni amɛtao niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu tso lɛ tsui he koni enyɛ eda.

english: Why do I need to spray chemical medicine on my mango trees when they start to flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofai afɔ mi mango tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ ebɔi fɔfɔi?

english: When mango trees bloom, insects and fungal diseases target the soft flowers. Spraying medicine protects these delicate flowers so they can successfully stay on the tree and develop into fruits.
ga: Beni mango tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Kooloi bibii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baatutua fɔfɔi bibii. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ buɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɛɛ ahe koni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛye omanye ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I forget to spray my mango trees during the flowering stage?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mihiɛ kpa mi mango tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: If you skip spraying during the flowering stage, pests and diseases will attack the blossoms, causing them to dry up or drop off, which leaves you with very few or no fruits to harvest.
ga: Kɛji otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ he yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ahe be mli lɛ Helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ. Ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ loo amɛshwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa onáa yibii fioo ko loo onáaa yibii ko kwraa ni obaakpa.

english: At what stage of fruit growth should I stop spraying my mango trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ makpa mi mango tso lɛ nɔ tsofa lɛ shwiemɔ?

english: You should continue your spraying routine from the time flowers open until you see the small mango fruits clearly forming and maturing on the branches.
ga: Esa akɛ oya nɔ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ kɛjɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ kɛyashi obaana mango yibii bibii lɛ. Eyɛ niji ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do I have to spray my fruit trees repeatedly instead of just applying the chemical once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔkɛ tsofa afɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ shii abɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ tsofai awo mɔ mli shikome pɛ?

english: Rain, sunlight, and new plant growth wear off the chemical over time. Repeated spraying ensures that the flowers remain protected throughout the entire time they are forming into fruits.
ga: Nugbɔ, hulu la, kɛ tsei heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baaha tsofai lɛ afite yɛ be ni sa mli. shwiemɔ shii abɔ Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi ni abuɔ amɛhe yɛ aduawai lɛ afeemɔ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Is it safe to spray protective medicine directly onto the flowers of my crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afɔfɔi lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, using the correct recommended chemical at the flowering stage is safe and necessary to protect the blossoms from fungal diseases and insects that destroy them.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni ehe miihia koni akɛbu fɔfɔi ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the flowers on my mango tree falling off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mango tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Mango flowers are easily attacked by tiny pests and fungal diseases like anthracnose. Without chemical protection during flowering, the damaged flowers fall off before fruits can form.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose lɛ tutuaa mango fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛji tsofa ko bɛ ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Fɔfɔi ni efite lɛ baagbee shi dani aduawai aba.

english: Why do my mango trees produce plenty of flowers but end up with very few fruits at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Many flowers naturally fail or get eaten by insects before pollination occurs. Protecting the tree with spray during the bloom stage ensures that a higher number of flowers successfully turn into full mangoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi babaoo fiteɔ loo kooloi yeɔ amɛ dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Tso lɛ he ni abuɔ he kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi babaoo baatsɔ mango ni eda.

english: What causes small, newly formed mango fruits to dry up and drop off the tree early?
ga: Mɛni haa mango bibii ni afee ehee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ oya?

english: Uncontrolled fungal infections and insect damage during the flower stage weaken the stem of the young fruit, causing it to wither and drop off before growing big.
ga: Fungal helai ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ lɛ baaha aduawai lɛ ahe tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ha egbo ni egbee shi dani etsɔ agbo.

english: How do insects prevent my fruit tree flowers from turning into actual fruits?
ga: Te kooloi bibii baanyɛ atsĩ miyibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ yibii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Insects feed on the sweet nectar and tender sap inside the flowers, which destroys the reproductive parts of the flower so it cannot develop into a fruit.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ fɔfɔi amli nu kɛ nu ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fãi ni fɔɔ bii lɛ bɔni afee ni enyɛ eda ni etsɔ aduawai.

english: How do I know if my mango flowers have successfully turned into young fruits?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ mango fɔfɔi etsɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo?

english: After the flower petals fade and fall, you will see small green pea-sized bumps growing in their place on the stalk, which indicates that the fruit has successfully formed.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbee shi lɛ Obaana ŋmeii bibii. Mung bean dalɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ egbɛhe yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ aduawai lɛ etsɔ momo.

english: Can I just plant the regular beans I buy from the local food market?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu daa ŋmeii ni miheɔ yɛ niyenii ajarayelihe ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans sold for food in the market are often treated for cooking or may be damaged by insects. Using certified seeds prepared specifically for planting ensures high germination and healthy crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ahoɔ ŋmeii ni ahɔ̃ɔ akɛ niyenii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ koni akɛhoo loo ŋmeii baanyɛ afite. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni asaa he pɔtɛɛ kɛha dumɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: What will happen if I plant bean seeds that have small holes or look eaten by insects?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Aloo kooloo ko ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds eaten by insects usually have damaged embryos or lost food reserves. Planting them leads to poor germination, weak sprouts, or complete crop failure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni kooloi yeɔ lɛ fiteɔ fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ loo efiteɔ niyenii ni ato lɛ. Dumɔ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. loo ŋmɔshi nibii efite kwraa.

english: Why is it safer to buy seeds that have been tested and approved by authorities?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni maŋ onukpai lɛ eka amɛkwɛ ni amɛha he odase lɛ?

english: Tested seeds are inspected to make sure they are free from seed-borne diseases, weeds, and defects, protecting your farm from introducing harmful pests or poor-yielding crops.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yeɔ kaa lɛ mli koni ana akɛ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli kɛbaa, jwɛi kɛ tɔmɔi bɛ mli. Buu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii fioo lɛ ahe.

english: How can bad seeds harm my farm beyond just failing to grow?
ga: Te dumɔwui gbohii baanyɛ aye miŋmɔ lɛ awui aha tɛŋŋ kɛfata he akɛ minyɛɛɛ makwɛ amɛ?

english: Diseased or untreated seeds can introduce fungi, viruses, or pests into your soil, which can spread to other crops and damage your farm's productivity for future seasons.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ loo atsaaa amɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛ fuji, muawai, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi amli ni efite oŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some planting seeds come with a colored coating on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi yɛ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: The colored coating is a protective treatment applied after quality testing to shield the seed from soil insects and fungal infections while it germinates.
ga: Penti ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he lɛ ji tsofa ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ bɔ ni aka bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ akwɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ sũ mli kooloi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Is there a way for me to test my seeds before planting them in the whole field?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maka dumɔwui lɛ makwɛ dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can perform a simple germination test by moistening a small sample of seeds in a cloth for a few days to see what percentage sprouts before investing your labor in planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Feemɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui bibii ni oookɛwo mama mli gbii fioo komɛi koni ona oha mlijaa enyiɛ baakwɛ̃ dani okɛ shika awo dumɔwui amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest sometimes fail to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can suffer hidden damage from pest attack, moisture loss, or disease during storage, which destroys their ability to grow into strong plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite yɛ teemɔŋ kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. ŋmɔtɔ loo hela ni baa shi yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ Enɛ fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaatsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do agricultural officers ensure the seeds sold to farmers are safe to plant?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ aaafee tɛŋŋ amɛkwɛ koni dumɔwui ni ahɔ̃ɔ ahaa okwaafoi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha okwaayeli?

english: Officers perform lab and field tests to check germination rates, seed purity, and freedom from dangerous plant diseases before certifying seeds for sale.
ga: Nitsulɔi lɛ feɔ laboratori kɛ ŋmɔ mli kaai koni amɛkwɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ amɛhaa. dumɔwui ahetsemɔ kɛ heyeli kɛjɛ tso helai ni yɔɔ oshara mli Dani abaaha dumɔwui ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ he odaseyeli

english: How do I tell if a damaged seed is still alive enough to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni efite lɛ yɛ wala ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo ni abaanyɛ adu?

english: If the embryo or growing point inside the seed has been eaten or cracked, the seed is dead and will rot in the soil rather than grow, regardless of how good it looks on the outside.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aye loo akumɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli fɔmɔ kotoku loo he ni edara lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaada. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why is planting tested seed varieties better than planting random seed grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aka amɛ akwɛ lɛ adumɔ hi fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Tested seeds guarantee uniform plant growth, strong resistance to local diseases, and higher yields compared to random market grains whose history and health are unknown.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aka amɛ akwɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ daa daa. Helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahewalɛ ni mli wa. kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo kɛ akɛto jarayeli ŋmaa ni aleee amɛ yinɔsane kɛ amɛhewalɛ he lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when the sun gets very harsh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh sun, the heat burns the leaves and causes them to lose water faster than their roots can take it in, making them yellow and dry up.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ Koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa Dɔlɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha nu lɛ afite oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This yellowing pattern means your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Feeding the soil with urea fertilizer, compost, or animal manure will help restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔji kɛ amɛ baai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ urea, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha shweremɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do I see small holes and tiny dark droppings inside the leaves at the top of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ Yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ amli

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the center of the plant. They feed on the tender young leaves before they unfold, and the droppings are their waste. Treating the center of the plant with neem oil or recommended insecticides kills the pest.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo. Ni ŋmeii ji jwɛi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop lose almost all its leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fite yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves on purpose during dry weather to save water and survive the heat. The plant is not dead; it goes to sleep and keeps its energy stored safely underground in the tubers until the rain returns to sprout new leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni enyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ naa. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebaawɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe yɛ eyitso mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ eba ni ebaakwɛ baai heei.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the ground on wooden stakes gives them maximum sunlight and fresh air, which produces more energy to grow bigger and heavier yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ babaoo baa koni ekɛha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛtsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. When it is too hot or dry, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival instead of spending it on fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite yɛ aduawai ahe lɛ

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying the undersides of the leaves early with neem water helps keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ ohe.

english: Why does my plantain farm produce smaller bunches if I leave all the young suckers growing around the main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mishi tsei bibii komɛi yɛ tso wulu lɛ he hu?

english: When too many young shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they steal nutrients, water, and light from each other. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, giving them enough energy to produce big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ Nakai ŋmeii lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ehaa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Maize sucks out the same specific nutrients from the soil every season. Repeating this without break exhausts the land and allows crop diseases to live permanently in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ afee nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ ekoŋŋ ni akpataaa he lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ mli agbɔjɔ, ni ebaaha tsei ahe helai ahi sũ lɛ mli daa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ

english: How does planting groundnuts on my field make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to a special family of plants that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnuts are harvested and the roots rot into the soil, that natural fertilizer stays behind to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts fata tsei akuu krɛdɛɛ ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ he ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmeii ni shishifãi lɛ gboi kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ baakã he ahi shi koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do crops grow much stronger on land that has been left as wild bush for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shwereɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ashi akɛ koo mli jwɛi afii babaoo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Land left untouched as wild bush restores its natural food through fallen leaves and decaying plants. This rested soil acts like a fresh bank of nutrients, giving new crops plenty of food to grow fast and healthy.
ga: Ashiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa he yɛ be mli ni koo mli tsei bibii lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛtsɔɔ baai ni egbee shi kɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ. Enɛ haa tsei heei lɛ náa niyenii babaoo koni amɛdara oya ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to leave dry leaves on my farm soil instead of burning everything clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mashi baai ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fe ni mashã nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he tse lɛ?

english: Leaving dry leaves on the ground acts like a cool blanket that traps moisture in the soil, shields young roots from hot afternoon heat, and slowly rots into natural food for your crops.
ga: Baai ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni mli ejɔ, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ebuɔ shishifãi bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shwane mli latsaa he, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests if I plant cassava in the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating different crops gives the soil time to rest and prevents crop-specific pests from building up in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai baabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain stays in the soil too long and suffocates the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ amɛ eŋɔli kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi.

english: Why do young cocoa plants wither and die when I clear all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender stems and shallow roots that burn easily under full sun. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, keeping the air cool and the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by hot weather, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. The plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy so it can survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crops grow slow and weak when I allow weeds to spread across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛgbɔjɔ beni mihaa jwɛi gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal sunshine, soil food, and water away from your crops. Clearing weeds removes this competition so your crops get all the nourishment they need.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛyaa. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ ana niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why do I need to leave wide spacing between my cassava plants instead of packing them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shɔŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ amɛ baabɔ he lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for limited underground space and food. Proper spacing gives each plant room to spread its leaves and form large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni faaa kɛ niyenii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso tsu fɛɛ tsu mli gbɛɔ ebaa lɛ eshwaa ni efeɔ bulbs agboi.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb instead of growing along the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunshine to produce energy for the yam growing underground. Staking lifts leaves off the damp ground into the air and sun, which prevents leaf rot and helps the yam tuber grow very large.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ aya kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa ni eye ebua sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more heavily during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry seasons, wild bushes dry up, so insects move into your green crops looking for moisture and fresh food. The warm weather also causes insect eggs to hatch much faster.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Koo lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ mli egbi. No sɛɛ lɛ, kooloi bibii fãa kɛyaa otsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli ni amɛtaoɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii hee. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ hu haa kooloi bibii afɔ̃ɔ oya kwraa.

english: Which fertilizer should I put on my crops first, NPK or Urea?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli klɛŋklɛŋ, NPK loo urea?

english: You should apply NPK first. NPK helps your plants build strong roots and sturdy stems right at the start, preparing them to draw in nutrients before you push for top leaf growth.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ NPK atsu nii klɛŋklɛŋ. NPK yeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛjɛɔ shishijee. Bɔni afee ni osaa tso lɛ, gbalamɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ dani otsi ŋwɛi baai lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: What happens if I apply Urea on my farm before the crop roots are strong?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ urea tsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli wa?

english: If you apply Urea too early when roots are weak, the plant will try to grow heavy leafy tops without a solid foundation, leading to weak growth that cannot support the crop.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ urea wo mli mra tsɔ beni shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ Kɛ shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ bɛ lɛ, tso lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ baai lɛ atsɔ tsiimɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Can I just apply NPK and Urea at the exact same time when planting?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ NPK kɛ urea atsu nii yɛ be kome mli kɛ́ midu nii?

english: It is best to split the application. NPK needs to go first to build healthy roots and stems, and Urea should come later once the plant is strong enough to develop a large canopy.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojara nibimɔi lɛ amli. Ehe miihia ni NPK aya klɛŋklɛŋ koni efee shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Ni esa akɛ urea aba sɛɛ mli beni tso lɛ mli ewa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ efee ŋwɛi ŋta agbo lɛ.

english: Why is it important for my crop's roots and stems to grow strong before the leaves grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ adara waa dani baai lɛ adara lɛ?

english: Roots and stems act as the foundation. Strong roots absorb water and nutrients from the soil, while strong stems carry those nutrients up and support the weight of heavy leaves and fruit.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shishitoo. Shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni tsei ahe tsei ni wa lɛ woɔ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni amɛfiɔ baai kɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: How do I get my crops to develop big, leafy tops to cover the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná baai agboi ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: To build a full green canopy, you need to apply Urea after your plants have already established a healthy root system and stem using NPK fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji ootao ni ofee ŋwɛi ŋta ni eyi obɔ Esa akɛ okɛ urea awo mli beni otsei lɛ etswa shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛtsɔ NPK ŋtayaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know when my crops are ready to receive Urea fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaaná urea?

english: Your crops are ready for Urea once the stem is firm and the roots are well-established from the initial NPK treatment, showing the plant is sturdy enough to support fast top growth.
ga: Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee klalo kɛha urea kɛ́ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ehi shi shiŋŋ ni shishifãi lɛ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ shishijee NPK tsofafeemɔ lɛ mli, ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do extension officers always advise us to start with NPK fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa be fɛɛ be akɛ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii aje shishi lɛ?

english: NPK provides essential balanced nutrients focused on establishing strong underground roots and robust main stems, giving the crop a solid start in the soil.
ga: NPK haa niyenii ni he hiaa ni sa ni kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni wa kɛ tso titri ni wa amamɔ nɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What work does Urea actually do for my crops when I add it?
ga: Mɛni diɛŋtsɛ urea feɔ kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii? Mɛɛ be mikɛ urea baafata he?

english: Urea supplies nitrogen, which is the primary nutrient responsible for expanding leaf size, creating lush green foliage, and building a wide plant canopy.
ga: Urea haa nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ daraa lɛ. Efeɔ baai eŋɔli ni efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli kwɔ

english: Why is nitrogen so important for the leaves of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitrogen he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ?

english: Nitrogen fuels leafy growth and keeps leaves deep green, which allows the plant to capture sunlight properly to grow well and produce good yields.
ga: Nitrogen haa baa lɛ daa ni ehaa baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni sa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: What will happen to my crop if I give it NPK for the roots but forget to apply Urea?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ NPK ha akɛ shishifãi shi mihiɛ kpa nɔ akɛ mikɛ urea baafata he?

english: If you skip Urea, your plant will have healthy roots and stems, but it will lack the nitrogen needed to form a full green canopy, resulting in small, thin leaf growth.
ga: Kɛji otsi urea naa Otso lɛ baaná shishifãi kɛ shishifã ni mli wa. Shi ebɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, baai lɛ yɛ bibii ni amɛhe yɛ tã.

english: How long does a cocoa tree usually take from planting before it starts producing fruit?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo tso ko jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Traditional cocoa trees usually take 3 to 5 years to start bearing pods, though improved hybrid varieties can start producing fruit in about 2 to 3 years if cared for well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema cacao tsei lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli moŋ, shi kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How many cocoa pods can I expect to get from a single healthy tree in a good year?
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ maná kɛjɛ tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli yɛ afi kpakpa mli?

english: A healthy mature cocoa tree can produce anywhere from 20 to 50 pods per year, depending on the tree variety, soil fertility, rainfall, and how well the farm is maintained.
ga: Kookoo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii 20 kɛyashi 50 yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ afi mli, ni enɛ damɔ tso lɛ henɔi lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ahaa.
