english: How many years can a cocoa tree continue giving me good harvest before it becomes too old?
ga: Afii enyiɛ cacao tso baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii kpakpai dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: A cocoa tree can remain productive for 25 to 30 years or more if it is well-pruned, protected from pests and diseases, and grown in fertile soil.
ga: Cacao tsei baanyɛ awo yibii afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛji akɛ afolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Buu he kɛjɛ kooloi kɛ helai ahe ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ nɔ

english: Why are the cocoa trees on one part of my land growing faster than the trees on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miida oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ he kroko lɛ?

english: Soil fertility, water drainage, and sunlight can vary across the same field. Areas with deeper, darker soil rich in organic matter help trees grow much faster than areas with poor or stony soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu ni hoɔ, kɛ hulu la baanyɛ afee srɔtoi yɛ he kome. Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ, ni mli edɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya fe hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, dark, well-drained, and rich in decayed leaves. It should hold moisture during dry periods without staying flooded or waterlogged during heavy rains.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋ, ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. kɛ baai ni fiteɔ babaoo Esa akɛ ato ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo nu ehiɛɛɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: What can I do to help my cocoa trees if the soil on my farm is weak?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-cocoa tsei lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ?

english: You can improve weak soil by adding organic manure, keeping shade trees to drop leaves for natural compost, mulching around the tree roots, and applying the right fertilizers.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Ha tsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo mli koni amɛshi baai lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Mulch abɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa atsu nii

english: Why does one specific cocoa tree on my farm produce many pods while the trees next to it produce very few?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tso kome ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ? Yibiiwoo fioo ko pɛ

english: Individual trees can perform differently due to differences in seed genetics, localized soil nutrients around their roots, or having better access to water and sunlight.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso baanyɛ atsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli loo nu kɛ hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees bring out pods early before the main harvest season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii dani kpamɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Early rains or natural variations in individual tree genetics can trigger off-season flowering and fruiting, leading to early pod development often called the mid-crop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra loo adebɔɔ mli tsakemɔi ni baa tsei aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ awo fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ he hewalɛ. Enɛ haa mra be mli ŋmeii baa, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ akɛ mid-crops.

english: I see many small flowers on my cocoa trees, so why do most of them fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mi naa fɔfɔi bibioo ko Babaoo yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: It is normal for a cocoa tree to drop up to 90% of its flowers. The tree naturally sheds flowers it cannot feed due to limited water, nutrients, or a lack of insect pollination.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei ni fa fe 90% baawo fɔfɔi. Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ he ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii yɛ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa loo kooloi amli ŋmeii ni bɛ

english: Will trimming branches off my cocoa trees help them produce more pods?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Yes, pruning removes weak or dead branches, allows sunlight and air to circulate through the tree, prevents disease, and directs the tree's energy into growing healthy pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni egboi lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli, etsĩɔ helai anaa, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I clear all the shade trees from my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Shade trees act as living umbrellas that protect young cocoa from sun damage, retain moisture in the soil, and help the plants establish strong root systems.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni mli wa

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop plants right after the first rain season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant in the topsoil and are naturally adapted to absorb water and sprout immediately after rain. Clearing weeds early gives your crops a fair chance to grow without competing for soil nutrients and sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ akaŋ.

english: No, planting crops too close together forces them to compete for water, sunlight, and nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and small or incomplete cobs. Proper spacing gives every plant enough space to produce a full harvest.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ni eshɛɛɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkpaa ekpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines grow plenty of big green leaves, but the tubers under the ground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes plants to direct all their energy into producing leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients downward to build large, healthy tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei tsɔɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ koni amɛfee baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami kɛ baa si konɛ a pee bulb nguahi nɛ a he wa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves is a clear signal that the soil lacks sufficient nitrogen, which maize relies on to grow green and full. Applying compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni egbe naa Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa loo nitrogen ŋmãa tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmãa ekoŋŋ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. kɛ gbɛ ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and developing light green and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with patches are symptoms of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant stem cuttings is the best way to prevent this disease.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll up inward during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes curl their leaves to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun and slow down water loss during extreme heat. As long as the plant unfurls in the cooler evening, it is a normal self-defense mechanism.
ga: Akɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni hulu lɛ akashɛ nɔ ni nu lɛ akafite yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off before any peppers can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or overly heavy chemical feeding. Regular watering and balanced feeding help flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do some of my saved seed grains fail to sprout when I plant them in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds stored in warm or moist places lose their vitality or suffer damage from hidden pests like weevils. Drying seeds thoroughly and storing them in airtight containers protects their power to germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛto hei ni hulutsoo loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ ŋmeii baafite amɛ. Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ tsinsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants scorching and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect them from excessive direct sunlight and hot winds. If they get too much sunlight, their leaves burn and turn yellow. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa trees provides the living canopy they need to stay cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo fioo ko koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ he. Kɛji onine shɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baashã ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaha ŋwɛitsu lɛ aná wala ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi ni ehiɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy periods with high humidity. Clearing tall weeds, pruning dense branches to let air flow through the farm, and removing infected pods early stops the fungus from destroying the rest of your harvest.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. tall weed removal Afoɔ jwɛi ni mli wa koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ jwɛi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekafite onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants staying short with light green leaves instead of growing tall and dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ baa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Light green leaves and stunted growth usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build strong stems and leafy foliage. Applying a balanced fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in the growing cycle helps the corn recover its dark green color and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma amɛshishifãi ni wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli mra yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eku esɛɛ ebatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: What is eating the center of my young maize leaves and leaving ragged holes?
ga: Mɛni ji mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni ayeɔ ni eshiɔ bu ni etse ehe lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that burrow inside the central leaf funnel of the corn plant. Applying recommended pest control treatments or neem leaf extract directly into the central funnel early in the morning or late afternoon effectively stops the caterpillars.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa titri ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Ni akɛ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo neem tso mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ awoɔ tsɔne lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo shwane mli. Ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants have thick leaf bushes above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy developing leaves and branches instead of sending food down into the roots. Avoiding excessive nitrogen fertilizer encourages the plant to store energy in big tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ niji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ baawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava stems curling up and showing yellow patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This pattern is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings from certified extension sources ensures your leaves remain healthy and able to feed the tubers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii kɛyaa tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Kɛ okɛ cassava ni helai nyɛɔ etswaa kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni duɔ ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha otso lɛ tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaanyɛ eye ebua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rains even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? He ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa bɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees easily fall when microscopic worms called nematodes or beetle larvae weaken and bore through their root base under the soil. Trimming away damaged roots and treating plantain suckers properly before planting keeps the root system strong enough to anchor the heavy plant.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo beetle larvae lɛ gbɔjɔ ni amɛbote amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ afo shishifãi ni efite lɛ amli ni akwɛ plantain tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua tsei ni tsii.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start sprouting long shoots before the planting season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ be saŋŋ dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Seed yams naturally wake up from dormancy when exposed to warm temperatures and trapped moisture in storage. Keeping your seed yams on elevated racks inside a shaded, cool, well-ventilated yam barn slows down early sprouting until you are ready to plant.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwo he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli lɛ he. Too atomo dumɔwui yɛ adekai ni awó nɔ yɛ tso ni yɔɔ shade, ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛyashi be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaadu.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress caused by high heat, dry air, or irregular watering. Providing consistent water at the base of the plant and preserving soil moisture with mulch helps flowers stay on the plant and form healthy fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii ahi tso lɛ nɔ ni ewoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my ripening peppers and tomatoes turning dark and leathery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ mi-tomato ni egbɔ lɛ ashishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifee hewolo lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the fruit, which often happens when soil water levels fluctuate sharply. Keeping soil moisture steady through regular watering allows the plant roots to absorb calcium continuously.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsake oya. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɛɔ mli daa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ daa lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ calcium be fɛɛ be.

english: Why should I care about the exact distance between my coconut trees when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu bɔ ni ŋmeii tsei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ he beni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to grow strong. If trees are planted too close, they fight for food, but if spaced correctly, you get the healthiest trees and highest yield per acre.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatswa niyenii he akaŋ. Shi kɛji akɛ gbɛ ni jɛkɛ lɛ ja Obaaná tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ yɛ acre kome mli.

english: What will happen to my farm if I plant an extra coconut tree in between my existing trees?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmei tsei babaoo yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ momo lɛ ateŋ?

english: Adding extra trees increases plant density, which can give you more fruit per acre if your soil has enough water and nutrients. However, if the trees become too crowded, they will block each other's light and reduce individual yield.
ga: Tsei babaoo ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ayi afa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha yibii babaoo aba yɛ acre kome mli kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shi, kɛji tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Tsei lɛ hu baaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaahã amɛhe yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Will planting more coconut trees on my land automatically give me more yield to sell?
ga: Ani ŋmei tsei babaoo ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha maná nibii babaoo ni mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Not always. If you put too many trees in a small area, they starve each other of food and sunlight, resulting in thin trunks and very few fruits per tree. Balance is key to maximum profit.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be ebaa lɛ nakai kɛji akɛ akɛ tsei babaoo wo he ko bibioo. Niyenii kɛ hulu la he hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei bibii kɛ aduawai fioo ko pɛ baa tso kome nɔ. Balance ji nɔ titri ni haa anáa sɛɛnamɔi babaoo.

english: Is it better to plant my coconut trees in measured straight rows or wherever I find space?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei tsei yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ja loo he fɛɛ he ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in measured straight rows ensures every tree receives equal sunlight and soil nutrients. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni asusuɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: Why are extension officers encouraging us to use scientific planting methods instead of traditional ways?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ jeŋ nilee gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ he hewalɛ moŋ fe bɔ ni aduɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ?

english: Scientific methods are tested to find the exact spacing, fertilizer amounts, and care that produce the highest yields and protect crops from disease, helping you earn more from the same piece of land.
ga: Akwɛ jeŋ nilee gbɛi anɔ koni ana gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ, bɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii ahaa kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ ahaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa shika babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: How do farmers in nearby countries like Ivory Coast get higher yields from their coconut farms?
ga: Te okwaafoi ni yɔɔ maji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tamɔ Ivory Coast lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛnáa yibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ ŋmei ŋmɔji amli?

english: Farmers in Ivory Coast often adopt modern high-density planting techniques, improved crop varieties, and strict spacing guidelines that make full use of sunlight and land capacity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ivory Coast lɛ kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni fa babaoo tsuɔ nii. Tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni mli wa ni kɛ hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin instead of strong and thick when they are crowded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo moŋ fe ni eeefee hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are too close together, they stretch upward to fight for sunlight. This uses up all their energy on growing tall stems rather than developing thick trunks and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ nɛɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ moŋ fe ni eeefee tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: How can I tell if the trees on my coconut farm are planted too close together?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ adu mi-kokoo tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If your trees are too close, their leaves will heavily overlap and block the sun from reaching lower branches. You will also notice thin trunks, slow growth, and small numbers of fruit.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛbaai lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe waa ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Obaana tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni amɛdaraa blɛoo, kɛ yibii fioo pɛ.

english: Can I plant other food crops in the empty spaces between my young coconut trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii krokomɛi yɛ he ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ateŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping crops like cassava, maize, or beans in the wide gaps between young coconut trees makes good use of empty land and gives you income while waiting for the coconuts to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutu tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni da yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ lɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ he ni yɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. ni eha bo shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni ŋmei lɛ agbɔ lɛ.

english: How can I get the maximum crop harvest from a small piece of land without damaging the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ? Te abaafee tɛŋŋ afee ni akpataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ?

english: You can maximize a small plot by using precise crop spacing, planting high-yielding crop varieties, and adding manure or fertilizer so the soil stays rich enough to feed all the plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha he bibii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ he pɔtɛɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua tsei lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if the crop I want to plant will bring good money in the market after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni misumɔɔ ni madu lɛ kɛ shika kpakpa baaba jara nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Crops bring higher profits when you choose varieties that local buyers prefer and time your harvest to hit the market during off-peak seasons when supply is low and demand is high.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa sɛɛnamɔi babaoo baa kɛji ohala henɔi ni maŋbii ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ. kɛ be ni okɛkpaa nii lɛ aya jara nɔ yɛ be mli ni nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ faaa ni nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they face heat stress, lack sufficient water, or receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, which causes the plant to focus on growing green leaves instead of developing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Curling and yellow leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni nuɔ baai amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or get eaten by insects so quickly when stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ loo kooloi yeɔ lɛ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize spoils fast in storage when it is not dried completely before bagging, leaving high moisture that encourages mold growth and attracts grain weevils.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ, kɛ́ egbiko kwraa dani awo lɛ kotoku mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa, ni no woɔ ŋmeii adalɛ he hewalɛ ni egbalaa dumɔwui amli ŋmeii.

english: How can I tell if my young cocoa trees are suffering from heat during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miihe dɔlɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa trees show heat stress when the edges of their leaves turn brown and crisp, or when they drop green leaves early to save water and protect their stems from drying out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii jieɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kpo kɛji baai lɛ anaa tsɔ asarasu ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo kɛ́ baai eŋɔli lɛ shwie shi oya koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu tso lɛ shishi koni ekagbi.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark rotten spots at the bottom during the rainy period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Dark spots at the bottom of tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, happen when heavy rains cause rapid growth while preventing the plant from taking up enough calcium from the soil.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ diŋŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha tomatoi kwɛ̃ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tomato tsei anaa koni amɛkajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my farm yield less harvest when I plant maize on the exact same land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil drains the specific nutrients that maize relies on, weakening the soil health unless you rotate with nitrogen-fixing crops like groundnuts or beans.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi damɔ nɔ lɛ hoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ baa shi. No ji ja okɛ tsei ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ amɛhe.

english: What causes my yams to rot in the soil before I even dig them up for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifoɔ amɛ po koni mikɛkpa?

english: Yams rot underground when water pools around the heaps in poorly drained soil, enabling fungal diseases to attack the tubers through small wounds caused by soil pests.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ ehe. Pile yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ kɛtsɔɔ pilamɔi bibii anɔ lɛ baa. ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa

english: What early signs should I look for on my farm to know if pests are starting to destroy my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ mra be mli okadii esa akɛ matao yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miibɔi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afitemɔ?

english: Early signs of pest damage include tiny pinholes in young leaves, dark droppings on stems, or folded leaves glued together with web-like threads where caterpillars hide.
ga: Nɔ ni fata mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai efite lɛ he ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli, ŋmeii ni tsuɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ahe. loo baai ni afolɔ mli ni akɛ kpãai ni tamɔ wɛb ni ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ ekpɛtɛ he.

english: Why do some of my plantain suckers grow tall and strong while others wither and die after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi daraa ni amɛhe wa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers fail to establish if they are infected with soil pests like nematodes before planting or if they are transplanted without trimming off old, damaged roots.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ ale kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes emɔ plantain tsei lɛ amli dani adu loo atsake amɛ ni afolɔɔɔ shishifãi momo ni efite lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains produce broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their early stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants fight over sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin leaves and small tubers instead of large, healthy cassava roots.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawuu yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa baai bibii kɛ bulb bibii baa. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ kaasa agbohi nɛ a he wa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of plant nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and rich in organic matter helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔii kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ kpe. aloo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha ehi shi pɛpɛɛpɛ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense against heat. The tomato plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and conserve water until temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi, ni ekɛ nu ahi shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the soil, leaving it tired. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest produce a smaller yield than certified seeds from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their vigor and vigor-producing traits over generations and can carry hidden diseases from the previous crop. Certified seeds are specially bred and treated for high yields and disease resistance.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ kɛ nifeemɔ sui ni mli wa lɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ aba. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my crops so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ miiba shi waa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential resources like water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from the soil surrounding your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ehaa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if ragged holes on my maize leaves are caused by insects rather than wind or rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-corn baa lɛ mli lɛ jɛ ŋmeii amli? Jeee kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ ni.

english: Insects like the Fall Armyworm chew distinct, uneven holes into the leaves and leave behind soft waste inside the central shoot of the plant, whereas wind and rain create clean tears mainly along the leaf edges.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ yeɔ bu ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli yɛ baai lɛ amli ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ haa ŋmeii ni he tse babaoo baa yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize thoroughly before sealing it in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ dani mikɛwo kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Damp grains create warm moisture inside storage bags, which attracts insects and encourages mould growth. Thoroughly drying grains ensures they remain safe, hard, and free from decay during storage.
ga: Dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ mli. ni gbalaa kooloi bibii ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daa lɛ yaa hiɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe, amɛwaa ni amɛkafiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed away essential nutrients from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the bottoms of my pepper fruits turning black and rotting before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboi dani eshɛreɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering or long dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli loo be kakadaŋŋ ni hulu enyɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves wilt and droop during the hot afternoon even when there is water in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Nɛgbɛ nu yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: During peak heat, crops lose moisture through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil, so they wilt temporarily to save water and protect themselves.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei gboiɔ be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures become extremely high or when plants experience sudden stress from transitioning between dry spells and heavy rain.
ga: Tomato shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ trukaa kɛjɛ tsakemɔ ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa teŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and twisted instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams become small or deformed when the soil is too hard and compact for the tubers to expand easily, or when underground pests damage the growing root.
ga: Sweet potatoes bafeɔ bibii loo efiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. aloo beni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster and greener than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to suck up available soil nutrients and water much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in full sunlight, so fast-growing plantains provide necessary shade and keep the soil cool during the cocoa's early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo lɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant my seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sun, water, and soil food, resulting in tall, weak plants with low yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why should I avoid growing maize on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around their vegetable roots with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) retains moisture by slowing down evaporation, keeps root zones cool, and stops weeds from sprouting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ (mulching) lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow fast. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea when the soil is moist will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing tiny caterpillars to eat holes in the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant. Spraying recommended insecticides early in the morning or late in the evening helps control them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni teɔ shi ewoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking juices from the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early with neem extract or insecticidal sprays allows new leaves to grow flat and normal.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai heei baakwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why shouldn't I put four or five maize seeds into a single planting hole to get more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ dumɔ bu kome pɛ mli koni maná yibii babaoo?

english: When too many seeds are planted in one hole, the plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Planting only two seeds per hole gives each stalk enough room and food to produce big, full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui enyɔ pɛ ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight and burn easily. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or leaving some tall trees gives cocoa plants the shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive their first two to three years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ni amɛshãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashi amɛdamɔ shi lɛ, ebaaha kookoo tsei lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yams need to spread their leaves out in the sun to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking the vines keeps leaves off the ground where they can catch diseases and ensures they get maximum sunlight to build large yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tsei lɛ wo tso mli lɛ, ebaajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, he ni hela baanyɛ amɔ amɛ lɛ. Ni ehaa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo koni amɛkɛdu ŋmeii wuji.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the cool ground allows the roots to absorb water before the hot sun evaporates it. Afternoon watering wastes water and hot water droplets on leaves can damage the plants.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ he ni jɛmɛ ejɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmuɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli shwane mli, nu fɔŋ kɛ nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite tso lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready to harvest between 9 and 12 months after planting, indicated by the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the stem cracking open as the tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ baatswa kɛji bulb lɛ mli fũu.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients during flowering. Mulching around the base and keeping soil consistently moist helps flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I apply fertilizer so that heavy rain does not wash it away from my crop's roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo ŋmɔshi nii koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafɔ̃ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp after a light rain rather than right before a heavy downpour, and bury or cover the fertilizer with a thin layer of soil so it stays close to the roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa najiaŋ lɛ ni okɛ sũ bibioo ko aha loo okɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crop leaves spread out wide instead of staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ egbɛ eshwã babaoo moŋ fe bibii lɛ?

english: Leaves naturally spread out wide to capture as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the plant produce its own food, which allows it to stay healthy and grow larger.
ga: Baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Does getting plenty of sunlight make my crops grow faster and larger?
ga: Ani hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara oya ni amɛdara?

english: Yes, abundant sunlight accelerates the natural processes crops use to make food and grow, causing them to develop faster and reach bigger sizes.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara lɛ yaa oya. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya ni amɛdaraa yɛ dalɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops stretching out towards the open sky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miishɛ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Crops stretch their leaves toward open light to gather maximum sunshine, which provides the energy needed to speed up plant development.
ga: Tsei lɛ gbalaa amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa la lɛ he koni amɛbua hulu la ni fa babaoo naa. ni ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ adara oya lɛ

english: Why do crops grow faster when their leaves are fully open and spread out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa oya kɛ́ amɛbaai lɛ egbele kwraa ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã lɛ?

english: Fully open, spread-out leaves act like larger collection panels for light energy, accelerating internal growth processes and building bigger plants.
ga: Baai ni agbele kwraa ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ panɛl agboi koni amɛbua kane hewalɛ naa. Ha mligbɛ dalɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ aya oya ni oma nitsumɔhe wulu

english: What causes some of my crops to grow unusually huge compared to normal ones?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi daraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ ahe?

english: When a plant receives maximum sunlight, its growth processes accelerate dramatically, leading to exceptionally large plant parts—a condition known as gigantism.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná hulu la babaoo lɛ Dalɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baaya oya waa. Ekɛ tso lɛ fãi wuji babaoo ni ji shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ gigantism lɛ baa

english: Is it normal for a crop to grow extremely large leaves, and what is this called?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baaná baai wuji waa? Ni mɛni atsɛɔ enɛ?

english: Yes, when leaves spread out fully to catch maximum sunlight, it can speed up growth to extreme levels, creating oversized leaves in a phenomenon called gigantism.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni baai lɛ egbɛ eshwã kwraa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eha dalɛ aya hiɛ oya kɛyashɛ he ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa baai agboi baa yɛ nɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ giant foliage mli.

english: What does it mean if an extension officer says my crops are showing 'gigantism'?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ he nitsulɔ ko kɛɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔɔ ‘giant size’?

english: Gigantism means your crop is growing exceptionally large because broad leaf coverage and strong sunlight have greatly accelerated its natural growth rate.
ga: Hugeness tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ daraa babaoo fe tsutsu lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa tso lɛ nɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli dalɛ yaa oya waa.

english: Why do wild plants growing in the bush often have wider leaves than crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baa lɛ da fe tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In unmanaged wild environments, plants stretch and widen their leaves to compete for sunlight, which speeds up their growth and makes them larger.
ga: yɛ koo mli shihilɛ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ mli lɛ Tsei baagbala amɛbaai lɛ amli ni amɛgbala amɛmli koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni eda oya ni eha baai lɛ adara.

english: Why do plants growing in wild conditions seem to develop such huge leaves and stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo mli lɛ yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii wuji nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Wild growth conditions force plants to maximize leaf surface area to grab sunlight, accelerating overall plant development and producing larger stems and leaves.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli dalɛ shihilɛi nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛha baa lɛ nɔ babaoo koni amɛna hulu la. Ehaa tsei lɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ oya ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai wuji baa

english: How does sunlight help my farm crops become bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulu la yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Sunlight powers the plant's food-making process. When wide leaves catch plenty of light, it speeds up growth across the whole plant, making it grow much larger.
ga: Hulu la haa hewalɛ kɛha tso lɛ niyenii feemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ. Kɛji baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ ná la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaha tso lɛ daa oya yɛ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ. ni haa efeɔ agbo kwraa

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing very few pods this year even though the trees look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ ewo ŋmeii fioo pɛ afi nɛɛ? Kɛji tso lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ hewalɛ po

english: Cocoa trees need specific nutrients like phosphorus and potassium to form pods, not just nitrogen for green leaves. Low yield often happens when the soil lacks flowering nutrients, when insects damage the small flowers, or when the tree does not get the right balance of shade and sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei biɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium, koni amɛfee ŋmeii. Jeee nitrogen kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛkɛ. Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa fɔfɔi baa. Be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔi bibii loo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa hulutsoo kɛ hulu la ni sa.

english: Why do small flowers on my cocoa tree fall off before turning into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to pollinate them before they can form pods. If the farm is sprayed with harsh chemicals at the wrong time, or if the soil is too dry during flowering, the unpollinated or stressed flowers will naturally drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni ekɛ amɛ afee pollination dani amɛfee pods. Kɛji ŋmɔ ko shwie tsofai ni mli wa waa nɔ yɛ be ni esaaa mli loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Fɔfɔi ni bɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo nɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, overly humid conditions. It spreads when shade is too dense, trees are unpruned, or rainwater stays trapped on the pods for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyi tsɔ. Afolɔɔɔ tsei ahe. Aloo nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ pod lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Will planting food crops like cassava or maize on the same farm hurt my cocoa yield?
ga: Ani niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baaná mi-kookoo ni mifeɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: Food crops like cassava feed very heavily on soil nutrients and water, which can starve young cocoa trees if planted too close. However, temporary food crops like plantains provide helpful shade and can coexist well if spaced far enough from the cocoa lines.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei yeɔ niyenii mli nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, tsei ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji amɛkɛ kookoo line lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow root systems that burn and dehydrate under direct harsh sunlight. They require shade from trees or crops like plantains during their first two to three years to protect them until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa ni nu fiteɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why does pruning extra branches off my cocoa trees actually increase my cocoa yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso mli lɛ haa kookoo ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-producing branches that steal energy and water from the main tree. It also opens up the canopy so sunlight and fresh air can reach the flowers and pods, which reduces diseases and encourages bigger pod growth.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni wooo yibii ni juɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ niji lɛ. Egbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ hu naa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa helai baa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji lɛ daraa.

english: Why does allowing tall weeds to grow around my cocoa trees reduce the amount of cocoa I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi kakadaji akwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ haa kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Weeds compete directly with cocoa roots for soil fertilizer and moisture. They also create a damp, overgrown environment at ground level where pests and diseases like black pod thrive.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo shishifãi yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nu. Amɛhaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ basabasafeemɔ hu baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ daa yɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn dry and drop off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a survival mechanism for cocoa trees during dry spells. By shedding leaves, the tree reduces the amount of water lost through evaporation so it can keep its trunk and root system alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi ji kookoo tso wala gbɛ nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli. Kɛtsɔ baai ni eshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa nu ni elaajeɔ kɛyaa lasu mli lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akwɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifã lɛ nɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does very heavy rainfall cause my cocoa trees to produce fewer healthy pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fioo lɛ?

english: Excessive rain creates high moisture levels that help fungal diseases spread quickly. Heavy downpours can also wash away tiny pollinating insects and damage delicate cocoa flowers before they can set fruit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ afɔ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛya ni efite kookoo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛwo yibii.

english: How do I know exact moment when my cocoa pods are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods change color distinctively when ripe—green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting when pods show this clear color change ensures the beans inside have full sugar content for proper fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su jogbaŋŋ beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuji loo ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baatsake kɛya ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ. Nikpamɔ beni ŋmeii lɛ etsake amɛsu lɛ faŋŋ lɛ haa kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ náa sugar fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dry at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves. Planting shade crops like plantains around them protects them from heat stress until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be mli ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce a lot of tall stems and leaves, but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai kakadaji babaoo lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lacks proper space, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing food in its underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo he ko ni sa bɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall down so easily when a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that stay near the soil surface. If the soil is waterlogged or damaged by pests, the roots cannot hold the heavy weight of the plant against wind.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ tso lɛ muji ni tsii lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds stop growing under my cassava plants after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kpaɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ ashishi yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: As cassava grows, its wide leaves create a dense canopy that blocks sunlight from reaching the soil floor. Without sunlight, weed seeds cannot germinate or grow.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei miida Ebaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmei ni mli ewo wu ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji hulu la bɛ lɛ Jwɛi dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ loo amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my healthy green cocoa pods suddenly turn black and rot on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ trukaa ni amɛgboi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives and spreads rapidly in high humidity and wet weather when rainwater lingers on the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ehi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small ragged holes in them early in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ amli buji bibii ni bɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by young caterpillars like the fall armyworm, which hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant and feed on the new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ cutworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa heei ni eda lɛ.

english: This is a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize plants move available nitrogen from older lower leaves up to support new top growth when nutrients are low.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eye ebua ŋmeii heei lɛ adalɛ kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my field make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with natural soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground, leaving behind natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ahaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting shoots inside the barn even when I haven't planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni mikwɛɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yams are living tubers that go through a natural rest period after harvest. Once that period ends, heat and moisture in the barn signal to the yam that it is time to start growing again.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni biɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ nakai be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: High temperatures during the hot season cause heat stress, which prevents tomato flowers from properly pollinating. The plant sheds the unpollinated flowers to conserve water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Enɛ haaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Which crops can I plant that will harvest fast so I can get money quickly for urgent family needs like school fees?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu ni baakpa mra bɔni afee ni maná shika oya kɛha miweku lɛ hiamɔ nii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ skul nyɔmɔwoo?

english: Fast-maturing crops like maize, tomatoes, pepper, and cowpeas mature within 2 to 4 months. Planting these short-duration crops allows you to harvest and earn income quickly compared to long-term tree crops like cocoa or oil palm.
ga: Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa, tomato, ŋmãa, kɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 4 mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo nɛɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ni onáa shika oya. Kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmei fɔ he.

english: Why do my cassava plants take nearly a full year to mature while my maize is ready in just three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi muu fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize is a grain crop designed by nature to finish its entire life cycle quickly in one short season. Cassava is a root tuber that spends many months continuously storing starch underground to grow large, edible roots.
ga: Abele ji ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni adebɔɔ fee koni egbe ewala shihilɛ fɛɛ naa oya yɛ be kukuoo mli. Cassava ji shishifã tso ko ni heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani ekɛ starch toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi be fɛɛ be koni shishifãi lɛ adara ni aye nii.

english: Is it good for my land if I plant maize and beans together on the same field?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting maize and beans together is beneficial. Beans take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, which naturally feeds the maize plants and helps you harvest more from a small piece of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa tsei lɛ ni ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa babaoo kɛjɛɔ he bibioo ko.

english: How do I know if my piece of land is suitable for growing cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Cocoa trees need deep, fertile soil that retains moisture well without getting waterlogged, along with good rainfall and partial shade. If your land is overly rocky or holds stagnant water, young cocoa roots will struggle and die.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ lɛ he miihia kooko tsei. kɛfata nugbɔshiimɔ kpakpa kɛ hulutsoo be ko he. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ tɛi babaoo loo nu ni damɔ shi Cocoa shishifãi bibii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing huge green leaves but failing to produce big fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii wuji lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they put all their energy into growing tall stems and thick green leaves instead of flowers. Balancing the soil with phosphorus and potassium encourages flowering and fruit growth.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Kɛ́ akɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium to shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai daa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before the fruits even start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani aduawai po jeɔ shishi ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience heat stress, lack of water, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips. Keeping the soil moist and protecting young plants helps the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni abu tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why does my plantain crop take so many months before the first bunch appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need 9 to 12 months to develop a strong pseudo-stem and enough large leaves to generate the energy required to push out a heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ he miihia nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛná pseudostems ni mli wa kɛ baai ni dara bɔ ni sa ni baaha hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛtsi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ aba.

english: What causes my cabbage leaves to curl up and turn yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni haa cabbage baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, and sap-sucking pests like aphids cause cabbage leaves to lose moisture, curl, and turn yellow. Adding mulch around the plant base keeps the root zone cool and moist.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids haa cabbage baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do buyers sometimes reject some of my harvested yam tubers even when they look big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara moŋ?

english: Buyers reject yams with hidden rot, cuts from digging tools, or pest holes because these flaws cause the tuber to spoil quickly during transport and storage before reaching the market.
ga: Mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ sweet potatoes ni mli ewo muji ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ Afolɔ kɛjɛɔ dɛŋdadei ni akɛtsaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe buji amli Yɛ nɛkɛ tɔmɔi nɛɛ ahewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko kɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize from weevils while waiting for buyers to arrive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mɛi ni baahe nii lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Ensure your maize grains are dried thoroughly until they are hard before storing them in clean, airtight bags or treating them with approved grain protection dust to keep moisture and weevils out.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ o-corn ŋmeii lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani okɛwo kotoku ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli. Aloo okɛ sũ ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛbu he kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why does plowing my farmland deeply with a tractor help my cassava grow better than just digging with a hoe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ trakta tsu miŋmɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi-cassava lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikɛ ŋmei ŋmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Plowing breaks up hard, compacted soil deep below the surface. This creates soft, loose dirt that allows root crops like cassava to easily expand and grow much larger tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa muji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni haa tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya ni amɛkwɛɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do yam crops need big soil mounds when planted in drier regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ŋmɔji wuji he hiaa sweet potato tsei kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ?

english: Large soil mounds act as water storage sponges. They trap underground moisture and protect the developing yam tubers from scorching heat and hard, sun-baked soil.
ga: Muji babaoo ni abua naa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni akɛhiɛɔ nu mli. Amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛbuɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni miiya hiɛ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni hulu lɛ shãa lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly into tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is intense, maize leaves roll up to reduce the surface area exposed to heat. This is the plant's natural mechanism to trap water and stop moisture from escaping into the dry air.
ga: Kɛ hulu la lɛ mli wa lɛ, Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ni hulutsoo lɛ baa lɛ shi. Enɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ emɔɔ nu ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekajo foi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit when the weather becomes extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries up pollen inside tomato flowers, making them infertile. When the plant senses it cannot produce seeds, it drops the flowers to conserve energy and water for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔmɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ Kɛ́ tso ko nu he akɛ enyɛɛɛ ewo dumɔwui Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi hu koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni ehi shi.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted over thousands of years to survive in local soil. Their seeds can wake up and absorb water faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ ni ehe afii akpei abɔ dani amɛhi shi yɛ jɛmɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi ni amɛmɔɔ nu oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen. The plant steals nitrogen from its older lower leaves and sends it to the top to keep new growth alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eha tsei heei ni eda lɛ ahi shi.

english: If I plant cowpeas together with my maize, won't the cowpeas steal food from the maize?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa Ani tsina ŋmãa lɛ ejuŋ niyenii kɛjɛŋ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: No, cowpeas actually feed the maize. Cowpea roots gather nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil, acting as a free natural fertilizer that helps neighboring maize plants grow stronger.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii yeɔ ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ. Cowpea shishifãi buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why do high-yield seeds bought from agricultural offices produce more food than seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni ahe kɛjɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ wo niyenii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Commercial improved seeds are scientifically bred to resist local diseases, endure dry spells, and absorb soil nutrients efficiently, whereas saved seeds lose these strengths over time.
ga: Akɛ jeŋ nilee kwɛɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛi nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: When plants are overcrowded, their leaves block each other from getting sunlight, and their roots fight for the same soil water. This leads to tall, thin, weak stalks with small ears.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ, eyɛ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛ toi bibii baa.

english: Why do caterpillar pests like fall armyworm attack my young maize field so heavily during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall cutworms lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn ŋmɔji lɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warm, dry weather speeds up the breeding cycle of caterpillars. Young maize plants have tender, nutrient-rich leaves that provide easy food for huge numbers of newly hatched pests.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ gbalashihilɛ mli oya. Abɛi tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni haa niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha kooloi babaoo ni efɔ ehee lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots and tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Shade plants like plantains act as umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young trees until they grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra leaves and dead branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei niji ni egboi yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-productive branches so the tree can direct its energy into growing cocoa pods, while also allowing air and sunlight to pass through, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afolɔ mli lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ awo kookoo ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil that gives plants their green color and healthy growth, or that the ground is waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu

english: How does putting dried animal manure in my field help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural nutrients and helps it hold water better, giving your crops a steady supply of food so they grow stronger roots and bigger yields.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ha otsei lɛ niyenii ni yaa nɔ daa. Koni shishifãi lɛ awa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests and diseases that feed on maize to build up in the ground, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Does it really matter how far apart I plant my cassava sticks in the farm?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mikɛ ŋmei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ ha yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia?
