english: Yes, planting cassava sticks too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in smaller root tubers instead of big, healthy ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii baa yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my young crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ beni nugbɔ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong, aggressive roots that absorb water and soil food instantly. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing light and nutrients away from your tender young crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni wa, ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni baanyɛ agbala nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when water is irregular, or when the soil lacks enough nutrients to support the energy needed for fruiting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha yibiiwoo lɛ.

english: Why do my papaya and mango fruits rot on the tree with small worms inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya kɛ mango lɛ miifite yɛ tsei ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Tiny fruit flies pierce the skin of young fruit to lay eggs inside; when the eggs hatch into worms, they feed on the pulp, causing the fruit to spoil and drop before it ripens.
ga: Aduawai amli ŋmeii bibii tsɔɔ aduawai bibii ahewolo mli koni amɛwo amɛwui yɛ mli. Beni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ Ebaaye aduawai lɛ loo. Enɛ ɔ haa nɛ yiblii ɔ puɛɔ nɛ e puɛɔ loko e waa.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my vegetable leaves during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ aduawai ahe baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and humidity during the rainy season create ideal conditions for fungi to grow on wet leaves, causing leaf spots and rot.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ yɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Ekɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing maize or if I should plant a different crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔ loo esa akɛ madu ŋmãa kroko?

english: Different crops require different soil types, depths, and moisture levels. Observing how water drains after rain and testing soil texture helps determine whether demanding crops like maize will thrive or if hardier crops like cassava or sorghum are better suited.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ, mlibotemɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ srɔtoi. Kɛ́ akwɛ bɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ, ni aka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akwɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ana kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ataoɔ waa tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ baashwere. Aloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ji nɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Why do crops in one section of my farm grow tall while the ones in another section stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli lɛ miiya hiɛ waa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ fã kroko lɛ mli lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Soil richness and water retention can vary across a single piece of land. Areas with deeper, nutrient-rich soil or better water drainage will support faster plant growth than areas with rocky, compact, or nutrient-poor soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome mli. Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ Niyenii nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli loo nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɔɔ mli Ebaaye ebua tsei ni amɛdara oya fe hei ni shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, ni mli edɔ loo niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells to reduce water loss through evaporation. This is a survival mechanism that helps the plant protect its underground roots until the rain returns.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahiɔ shi ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why do sorghum and millet survive long dry spells much better than maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Sorghum and millet have deep root systems that can reach moisture deep underground, and their leaves are structured to fold and conserve water during hot weather, unlike maize which requires steady rainfall.
ga: Sorghum kɛ millets yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ he. Ni afee amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛfolɔ amɛhe ni amɛhiɛ nu mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. Ejeee tamɔ ŋmãa, ni biɔ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young pods when the weather gets too hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi lɛ?

english: During extreme drought, cocoa trees drop their young pods to conserve water and energy, prioritizing keeping the main tree alive over producing fruit.
ga: yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛtsɔ jwɛŋmɔ ni akɛaaha tso titri lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ fe yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing many flowers but failing to grow any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii babaoo shi ebɛ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers require proper pollination by wind or insects to turn into fruit, and extreme heat or lack of balanced nutrients can cause flowers to drop before fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ biɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii atsɔ amɛmli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii. Ni latsaa ni naa wa loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ dani aduawai aba.

english: What happens to my yam tubers when water stays flooded on my farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni baa mi sweet potato tubers lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nu ho ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo?

english: Standing water cuts off oxygen to the plant roots in the soil. Without air, root crops like yams cannot breathe and will begin to rot under the ground.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ koni ekɛdu shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ, shishifãi tamɔ ŋmeii nyɛŋ amu. ni ebaaje shishi egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil and feeding surrounding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa tsei ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it harmful to plant pepper on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that target that specific plant family to build up in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tso weku lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds actually slow down the growth of my crops when they grow near each other?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil moisture, space, and root nutrients, effectively stealing the nourishment your plants need to mature.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋwɛi, kɛ shishifãi amli niyenii Enɛ juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the trees and leave the land completely open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei lɛ fɛɛ ni mishiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and hot winds. They need shade crops like plantain or shade trees during their first few years to protect their delicate leaves and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Koni ebu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the maize plant's natural defense against water loss. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the area exposed to the hot sun and retains moisture during dry hours.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ naa. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers instead of producing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. The plant drops flowers to conserve energy for basic survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala.

english: Why do my cassava roots remain very small and woody even though the stem above ground grows very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kwɔ waa moŋ.

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and lacks potassium, or when the ground is too hard. The plant puts all its energy into leaf growth above ground instead of expanding tubers underground.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni potassium hu faaa. aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: How long does it take for exhausted soil to regain its strength if I stop burning the land and leave it to rest?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛji akɛ akpa shãa ni ashi lɛ ni eta shi?

english: When land is left to rest without bush burning, it usually takes 3 to 5 years for decaying leaves, plant roots, and soil microbes to rebuild organic matter and restore natural soil fertility.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi shikpɔŋ ni jwɛi shãaa lɛ Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani baa, shishifãi, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ ama nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear my farm weeds without burning the dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛshãaa jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ?

english: Burning destroys natural plant food, kills helpful soil organisms like earthworms, and leaves the ground exposed to erosion. Leaving cleared weeds to rot turns them into natural fertilizer.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. Egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ sũ mli ŋmeii, ni ehaa sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ha jwɛi lɛ afite ni ebatsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I put three or four seeds into a single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ wo dumɔ bu kome mli?

english: Planting too many seeds together forces the plants to compete against each other for water, light, and nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and very small or empty corn cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, la kɛ niyenii he, ni no haa amɛnáa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to make big soil mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afee shikpɔŋ agbo ko dani adu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Deep, loose mounds create soft soil conditions that allow yam tubers to expand easily underground while protecting them from hot direct sun and flooded soil.
ga: Gɔji ni mli kwɔ ni etse amɛhe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upward and turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curl is commonly caused by a plant virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus interferes with how the plant produces food, stopping fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Virus tsiɔ bɔ ni tsei feɔ niyenii lɛ naa. ni ekpaa aduawai lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of green leaves but very few bean pods during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ hiɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pea pods fioo pɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much soil moisture encourages cowpeas to focus on vegetative growth like stems and leaves rather than flowers. Heavy rains also wash away flower pollen before pods can form.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo baaha cowpea kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama tsei lɛ adalɛ, tamɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu hoɔ fɔfɔi amli muji lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ.

english: How do I know the best month to plant oil palm seedlings on my land in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nyɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu oil palm dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nɔ?

english: Oil palms should ideally be planted at the start of the main rainy season (around April to May) so their roots can establish deeply before the dry season arrives.
ga: Esa akɛ adu mu tso yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. (aaafee April kɛyashi May) koni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ atswa shishifãi babaoo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: How far apart should I space my oil palm trees when I plant them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-oil palm tsei lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ?

english: Oil palms should be planted in a triangular pattern about 9 meters apart so that their large mature fronds get enough sunlight without shading each other out.
ga: Esa akɛ adu mu tsei lɛ yɛ koŋtɛi etɛ mli ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 9 bɔni afee ni baai wuji lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkafee amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can I just collect fallen palm nuts from my old farm to plant new oil palm trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua ŋmei yibii ni egbee shi lɛ anaa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛdu mu tsei heei?

english: It is best not to plant seeds collected from old farms because they often yield low-producing palms; buying certified hybrid seeds from official research institutes gives you trees with much higher oil yields.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ ejaakɛ amɛfɔɔ ŋmei yibii ni baa shi. Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahemɔ haa tsei ni mu babaoo baa lɛ baa.

english: What is the difference between the hard-shell palm nuts and the soft-shell ones?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ateŋ?

english: Hard-shell nuts (Dura) have a thick shell with very little oil flesh, while high-yielding hybrid nuts (Tenera) have a thin shell surrounded by a thick layer of oil-rich pulp.
ga: Nuts (Dura) lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni fɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni ji hybrid nuts (Tenera) ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce a lot of flowers but very few actual fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi anɔkwa yibii akui fioo pɛ?

english: This usually happens due to poor pollination, severe water stress during dry months, or a lack of essential nutrients like potassium and boron in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ pollination ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ mli loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ boron ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young oil palm trees turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen or magnesium, which can be fixed by applying targeted fertilizers or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo magnesium faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ hei pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is causing hole-like damage on the leaves of my young oil palm seedlings?
ga: Mɛni kɛ fitemɔ ni tamɔ bu baa mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ ahe baa lɛ nɔ?

english: Damage on young leaves is often caused by pests like rhinoceros beetles or leaf-miner caterpillars, which can be controlled through clean farm sanitation and approved pest control methods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ rhinoceros ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ baai bibii lɛ baa. Abaanyɛ akudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli hetsemɔ ni he tse kɛ gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant crops like cassava or maize between my oil palm trees while they are still small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ mu tsei lɛ ateŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop food crops like maize or legumes during the first 2 to 3 years to get food and income before the young palms grow large enough to cover the ground with shade.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ koni oná niyenii kɛ shika dani dumɔwui lɛ adara bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ hulutsoo baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I tell when oil palm fruits are ripe enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni oil palm yibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A fruit bunch is ready for harvest when a few loose, reddish-orange palm nuts start dropping to the ground on their own, showing that the oil content inside is at its peak.
ga: Yibii akui lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ beni ŋmei tsuru ni eyi obɔ kɛ niji jeɔ shishi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ mu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ falɛ eshɛ he ni eshɛɔ fe fɛɛ.

english: Why should I use a processing machine instead of pounding palm nuts manually by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ processor atsu nii moŋ fe ni mikɛ mi nine baatswa mi-nuts lɛ?

english: Mechanical processing machines extract significantly more palm oil faster and more hygienically, reducing heavy physical labor and cutting down on fruit waste.
ga: Mshinii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ jieɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo oya ni amɛhe tseee. Ha gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ ni tsii aba shi ni oha aduawai ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do crops planted at the beginning of the major rains in April usually yield better than crops planted later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli yɛ April mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Early planting allows crop roots to settle while the soil is rich in fresh nutrients released after the dry spell, giving the plants a strong start before the heaviest rains or later dry spells arrive.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduɔ shishifãi ni amɛmaa shi yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ niyenii heei ni ajieɔ yɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ loo hɔmɔ be ni ehiii fe fɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing fruits during hot dry months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures stress pepper plants, causing them to shed their flowers to conserve energy and water until weather conditions become more favorable.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop seem to mature and be ready for harvest at the exact same time as everyone else's in my village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edara ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ be kome too mli tamɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ lɛ? Yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli?

english: Cassava growth is driven by seasonal rain patterns, so crops planted around the same rainy cycle naturally follow the same timeline to reach full size.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli lɛ tsirɛɔ cassava dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome mli lɛ nyiɛɔ be kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛshɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and stop growing when there is heavy rain in July?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ July mli lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the plant roots so they cannot take in oxygen or essential nutrients.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ loo niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to minimize their surface area facing the sun, reducing water loss through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba shikpɔŋ ni hulu la lɛ kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. ni eha nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi

english: Why do my maize plants dry up quickly in the dry season even when I water them by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ minine shwieɔ amɛnɔ nu moŋ?

english: Hot dry winds and intense heat cause water to evaporate from the soil and leaves faster than hand-watering can replenish it.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi kɛ latsaa ni naa wa haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe be mli ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nu nɔ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my farm more frequently when the season changes from dry to wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ shii abɔ beni be lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli kɛyaa hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: The warm weather combined with early moisture creates the perfect breeding environment for pests, causing their populations to surge right as tender new plants start growing.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ mra be mli hulutsoo be lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ fɔmɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛyibɔ ​​yaa hiɛ oya beni tsei heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie dormant in the dirt waiting for moisture, allowing them to sprout rapidly and capture soil nutrients faster than cultivated seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi waa ni amɛwɔɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni emɛ ŋmɔtɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil and turn soft much faster in April than during cooler months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya yɛ April mli fe nyɔji ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High ambient temperatures speed up the ripening and natural breakdown process of fruits, causing them to soften and decay quickly if not kept cool.
ga: He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ haa tso yibii lɛ shweremɔ kɛ fitemɔ yaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛfiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛtooo he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting leaves while in storage during September?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ bɔi shweremɔ beni akɛtoɔ yɛ September mli lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures and moisture in the air signal to the yam that conditions are right to start a new life cycle, breaking its dormancy period.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be tsɔɔ sweet potato lɛ akɛ shihilɛi yɛ mli. Ehi kɛha shihilɛ hee shishijee. Kɛtsɔ e-dormancy be lɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees produce large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees build strength during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Beni cacao tso lɛ woɔ hewalɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the hot ground cool, stops water from evaporating too quickly during sunny days, and prevents weeds from taking over your crop field.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hei ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekaha oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick leafy stems, but the tubers under the ground are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together or have too much nitrogen in the soil, the plant spends all its energy growing big leaves and tall stems up top instead of storing food in the tubers underneath.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii kakadaji yɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up into the sunlight so they can make more food for the plant, while also keeping the leaves dry and off the damp soil to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii babaoo amɛha tso lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ agbi ni akaje shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over when heavy winds blow during the fruiting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ yibiiwoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow deep into the ground, and underground pests like microscopic worms can weaken them. Supporting the stem with a strong branched wooden prop prevents heavy fruiting plants from topping over.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ni kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tamɔ ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni tsei ni yɔɔ niji ni mli wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ akagbee shi.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with light green dirt trapped inside the middle funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ muji eŋɔli ni mli tse ni ekpɛtɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide deep inside the growing tip of the maize plant. Clearing weeds and spraying recommended biopesticides early in the morning or late afternoon protects the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Leebi loo shwane jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards into tight knots and turning twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa ni amɛtsake lɛ?

english: Twisted and curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking leaf sap, or viruses spread by whiteflies. Controlling these sap-sucking pests keeps the leaves open and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ anɔyeli yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbeleɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop without forming fruit when temperatures become extremely high, when soil moisture changes too drastically between wet and dry, or when lack of insect visits prevents flower pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni bɛ lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ naa

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape and drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni amɛmiigbi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. Adding organic manure or applying nitrogen fertilizer early in the growing stage fixes this.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Akɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer baafata he mra Yɛ dalɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, abaanyɛ atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: When is the best time during the rainy season for me to put fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is damp but not during heavy downpours. Applying right before a heavy rain washes the expensive fertilizer away, while applying on moist soil allows plant roots to drink it up.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi esaaa akɛ akɛwoɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛwo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi ni amɛnuɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when exposed to full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants originally grow under forest canopies and have tender leaves that dry out quickly. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava to protect them from direct sunlight until their root systems and leaves are strong enough to handle heat.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ashishi, ni amɛyɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo cassava. Koni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he Kɛyashi shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ latsaa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when their fruit bunches start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ eyibii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow, fibrous roots rather than deep taproots. As the heavy bunch of plantains grows at the top, the tree becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wind or heavy rain to pull the shallow roots out of the soil unless you support the trunk with a wooden prop.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni yɔɔ fiber moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji plantains babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooojɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ja okɛ tso fi tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which gives plants their green color and leaf growth. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it, requiring top-dressing fertilizer to fix.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni baai lɛ hu kwɛ̃ɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ mulching fertilizer atsu nii ni akɛsaa naagba lɛ.

english: Why do groundnut flowers bend down and push themselves into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts produce flowers above ground, but the actual nuts grow underground. Once the flower is pollinated, it forms a small stem called a peg that naturally grows downward into the soil so the pod can safely develop in the cool earth.
ga: Peanuts woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, shi nuts diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi pollen lɛ Ebaafee ŋmei bibioo ko. ni atsɛɔ lɛ pins ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ.

english: Why do cowpeas grow so well even in poor soil where my maize fails?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ po nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful bacteria living in their roots. These bacteria take nitrogen gas straight from the air and convert it into plant food, allowing cowpeas to feed themselves even when the soil has few nutrients.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Nɛkɛ muawai nɛɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii. Enɛ haa tsina ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ehe eyɛ mli akɛ niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves toward the sun to catch light and make energy. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ he koni amɛná la ni amɛfee hewalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ tso helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when water sits on the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water floods the field and stays for days, it blocks air from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate, drown, and attract rotting fungi.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu lɛ eyiɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni ehiɔ shi gbii babaoo lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ baatsi enaa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Amɛmuɔ, amɛboteɔ nu mli, ni amɛgbalaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of insects like bees to pollinate them. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids that suck the plant sap, or by viruses spread by these insects. As they feed, the leaves develop unevenly, resulting in a twisted or crinkled shape.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ mli Baai lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni efite loo etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Covering soil with dry plant material (called mulching) acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from evaporating water out of the dirt, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weed seeds from getting light to sprout.
ga: Mulching kɛ tso nibii ni egbi (Atsɛɔ enɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni la shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant food needed for growth. It can also happen if heavy rains flood the field and drown the roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ ko nɔ nu ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi. Tsi niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ naa

english: How does planting cowpeas help make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that catch natural nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and roots decay, that extra plant food stays behind in the dirt to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ egbo Nakai tso niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Which way should I point cassava stems when I am planting them in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ atsɔ nɔ atsɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ?

english: Always plant cassava stems with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems struggle to grow properly and your tuber harvest will be very poor.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cassava tsei ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Ebaawa akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni o-bulb nikpamɔ lɛ baafee gbeyei.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the tubers growing underground. Raising the leaves off the ground on poles helps them catch sunlight easily and keeps leaves safe from soil rot, giving you larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ mlɛo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Ehaa onine shɛɔ sweet potato agbo nɔ.

english: How does covering the dirt around my plantain trees with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, trap moisture during dry days, and blocks weeds from growing and stealing nutrients from your plantains.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii ni yɔɔ plantains lɛ mli lɛ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a water-loving fungus that spreads in cool, damp conditions. Clearing excess shade branches and removing infected pods quickly keeps the trees dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ojie tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ fe nine lɛ oya, ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites. Inspecting the undersides of leaves and using neem oil or soapy water sprays can help control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi ni okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwie nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: What is eating ragged holes into the center leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young corn leaves are typically caused by fall armyworm caterpillars. Checking the central leaf funnel early and applying recommended treatments or neem powder kills the pests before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii loo neem powder lɛ baagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant experiences sudden drought stress. Keeping soil moisture steady with regular watering and mulching helps flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ trukaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if I leave them too long in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When soil stays soaked with water for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing bacteria and fungi to attack and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: People say there are tiny living things in my soil that I cannot see with my eyes, so how do they help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛi komɛi kɛɔ akɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mihiŋmɛii enaaa lɛ nɔ No hewɔ lɛ te amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: These invisible living things are called soil microbes. They act like tiny digestive systems in the dirt, breaking down dead leaves, roots, and manure into small plant foods that your crop roots can easily absorb.
ga: Atsɛɔ nibii ni anaaa nɛɛ akɛ sũ mli nibii bibii. Amɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bibii, ni amɛgbalaɔ baai ni egboi, shishifãi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli amɛfeɔ tsei niyenii bibii. ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ mli mlɛo

english: If I put strong chemical fertilizer on my fields, will it harm the invisible good living things in my soil?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli ni mli wa fata ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ Ebaaye nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ awui. Nɔ ni anaaa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Using small amounts gives crops a quick boost, but putting too much heavy chemical fertilizer without adding manure or organic matter can make the soil too sour and kill off the helpful soil microbes over time.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ fioo ko tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara oya. Shi tsofa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo ni akɛ ŋmeii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmeii tsɔ ni egbe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I properly collect soil from my farm to send to the laboratory for testing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabua shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ koni mikɛmaje laboratori koni aka lɛ akwɛ?

english: Clear away surface weeds, dig a V-shaped hole about hand-depth deep, scrape a thin slice of soil from the side, repeat this in about ten different spots across your field, mix those samples together in a clean bucket, and dry a small portion in the shade before sending it off.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsɔɔmɔ bu ko ni tamɔ V ni miihe ashɛ onine lɛ shishigbɛ, ni okɛ sũ bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ajie. Tĩi mli yɛ hei srɔtoi aaafee 10 yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Okɛ nɔkwɛmɔnii lɛ abɔ he yɛ baagi ni mli tse mli. ni okɛ fã bibioo ko agbi Gbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani okɛmaje.

english: Why do I need to take soil samples from different parts of my field instead of just one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii kɛjɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mafee nɔkwɛmɔnɔ kome pɛ

english: Soil across a single farm is rarely uniform; one corner might be rich while another lacks key plant foods. Mixing samples from several spots gives the laboratory an accurate average picture of your entire farm's health.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ jeee ekome kwraa. Ekolɛ koŋ kome mli nibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekroko nɔ bɛ tsei niyenii ni he hiaa. Nɔkwɛmɔnii ni jɛ hei srɔtoi ni akɛaato he lɛ haa laboratori lɛ naa oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hewalɛnamɔ he mfoniri ni ja, ni ji mlijaa mlijaa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy just by using my eyes and hands?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ mihiŋmɛii kɛ miniji ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Healthy soil typically has a dark brown or black color, crumbles easily in your fingers like fresh cake rather than forming hard blocks, smells like fresh rain, and contains visible creatures like earthworms crawling inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ. Efoɔ mlɛo yɛ nine mli tamɔ keeki hee yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔtɔ ni wa. Ehe ŋmɔlɔ tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛ ehee. Ni bɔɔ nii ni anaa tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ mli lɛ yɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when the farm soil becomes hard and packed down tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Hard, packed soil squeezes out air and water spaces, making it impossible for tender plant roots to push through and search for nutrients or for helpful soil organisms to breathe.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu kotokui amli. Enɛ haa tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nyɛɛɛ abote mli ni amɛna niyenii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he hiaa kɛha mumɔ.

english: Why do crops growing inside a greenhouse need different soil care compared to crops planted in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii sɔrɔtoi ni akɛtoɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Inside a greenhouse, there is no natural rain to wash the soil or weather to break down organic material, so salts from water and fertilizers can build up quickly if you do not monitor and flush the soil regularly.
ga: Yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ ko bɛ ni baaha sũ lɛ ashwie shi loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ko bɛ ni baafite nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni jɛɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ abɔle ehe oya kɛji okwɛɛɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ofɔɔɔ he daa.

english: What happens in the soil when I pile up animal manure and dry grass to make compost for my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mito ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi ahe koni mikɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Invisible microscopic organisms eat and break down the manure and grass, generating heat that kills weed seeds and harmful pests, leaving behind a rich natural fertilizer that improves crop yields.
ga: Adebɔɔ bibii ni anaaa amɛ lɛ yeɔ ni amɛkuɔ ŋmei kɛ jwɛi. Ekɛ dɔlɛ ni gbeɔ jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa. Eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ lɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crops with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Akɛ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Covering the ground acts like a protective shade that stops hot sunshine from drying out soil moisture, keeps the earth cool, and provides a safe home for beneficial soil organisms.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Ye obua ni je lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni oha nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aná shia ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops keep wilting from the roots even when the top soil looks wet and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Harmful microscopic worms or fungal germs hidden deep in the dirt can attack crop roots under the ground, blocking the roots from sucking up water even if the surface soil is wet.
ga: Microworms loo fungal pathogens ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ atutua tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ nu kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do we traditionally cut a single seed yam tuber into many pieces before planting it in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔfoɔ sweet potato tuber kome mli fãi srɔtoi dani wɔduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cutting a yam tuber into smaller pieces (setts) is a traditional way to multiply planting material because each cut section with skin can sprout a new shoot, though it uses up food that could otherwise be eaten or sold.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii ni afoɔ mli bibii bibii (settes) lɛ ji kusum gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nibii babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni afo kɛfata tso lɛ yibii ahe lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii heei. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ niyenii ni abaanyɛ aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ tsu nii po.

english: Is it really possible to grow a whole new yam plant using just a small leaf or vine cutting instead of a heavy tuber?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ baai bibii pɛ atsu nii ni akɛdu sweet potato tso hee kwraa diɛŋtsɛ? Aloo wain tso lɛ ni ooofo yɛ bulb ni tsii waa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, modern yam propagation methods allow farmers to use small vine or leaf-bud cuttings, which sprout roots in a nursery and grow into healthy seed yams without sacrificing whole food tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ sweet potato shwereɔ lɛ haa okwaafoi kɛ wain tsei bibii loo tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai tsuɔ nii. Enɛ baawo shishifãi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eda ni etsɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ dumɔwui ni ekɛ ŋmei muu lɛ fɛɛ shaaa afɔle.

english: How can a tiny leaf or vine cutting have enough strength to produce a full-sized yam tuber later on?
ga: Baai bibii loo wain tsei ni afoɔ Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ efee nɔ ni wa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ sweet potato tubers ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu aba sɛɛ mli?

english: Even a small leaf cutting contains active plant stem cells and sunlight-capturing power; once it forms roots and absorbs soil nutrients, it grows a healthy stem system capable of bulging into a normal tuber.
ga: Baai bibii ni afolɔ po Eyɛ tso mli wala yibii ni tsuɔ nii hu kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛmɔɔ hulu la. Kɛji efee shishifãi ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwie shi lɛ Ebaafee tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmei ni sa.

english: How can I produce more seed yams for my farm if I do not have enough tubers saved from the last harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ? Kɛji mibɛ tubers ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: You can adoption rapid multiplication methods like minisetts or vine cuttings, which allow you to produce dozens of new planting stems from a single mother plant rather than just a few cut tuber pieces.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ he oya tamɔ ŋmeii bibii loo wain tso mli ŋmeii atsu nii. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ofeɔ tsei heei srɔtoi srɔtoi kɛjɛɔ tso kome ni yɔɔ fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofo yitso ni afo lɛ mli fãi fioo komɛi kɛkɛ lɛ,.

english: What is the difference between the yams I harvest to sell in the market for eating and the yams used for planting?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni mikpaa koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ koni miye lɛ yɔɔ srɔto yɛ ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Yams grown for food or market are called 'ware yams' and are harvested large, while 'seed yams' are smaller tubers or specialized cuttings grown specifically to start the next season's crop.
ga: Atsɛɔ sweet potato ni aduɔ kɛha niyenii loo jarayeli akɛ yams. Akpaa ‘container yams’ lɛ babaoo, yɛ be mli ni ‘seed yams’ ji ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni adu pɔtɛɛ koni akɛje be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi.

english: Why am I spending so much of my harvest profit just buying seed yams for the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mikpamɔ mli nyɔmɔwoo lɛ babaoo he ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Traditional planting relies on burying large, edible tubers which reduces what you can take to market, whereas newer leaf and vine propagation methods let you keep your main tubers for eating or selling.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi biɔ ni adu bulbs agboi ni ayeɔ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni obaanyɛ okɛba jara nɔ lɛ baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛi heei ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ baa kɛ wain tso lɛ ashwãa lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ ŋmeii titrii lɛ toɔ koni oye loo ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Will yams grown from tiny leaf cuttings taste the same and be safe to eat like traditional yams?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni adu kɛjɛ baai bibii ni afolɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ baaná ŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni afɔɔ feemɔ daa lɛ?

english: Yes, yams produced from vine or leaf cuttings are naturally identical to those grown from traditional seed tubers and carry the same taste, nutrition, and cooking qualities.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ wain tso loo baai ni afolɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ blema dumɔwui akui amli lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔ, niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome. Ni bɔ ni ahoɔ nii ahaa lɛ hu tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my cut yam pieces sometimes rot in the ground before they ever sprout shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mifo lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cutting open a yam tuber leaves raw exposed flesh that soil insects, bacteria, and fungi easily attack, causing rot before the buds get a chance to sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa loo ni ŋmɔŋ ni kooloi bibii, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ atutua lɛ oya yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa dani fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Why do the head parts of a cut yam tuber sprout faster than the tail parts when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato bulbs ni afo lɛ yiteŋ lɛ daa oya fe tsitsii lɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ lɛ?

english: The 'head' or top end of a yam tuber contains the highest concentration of growth hormones and active buds, making it sprout much quicker than the middle or bottom sections.
ga: Yitso’ loo ŋwɛi naagbee ni yɔɔ sweet potato tuber lɛ mli lɛ ji he ni tsofa ni haa mɔ daa kɛ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ fa babaoo fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya kwraa fe teŋgbɛ loo shishigbɛ fãi lɛ.

english: What extra care do delicate vine cuttings need when planted compared to traditional large seed tubers?
ga: Wein tsei ni afolɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ biɔ hiɛdɔɔ babaoo kɛji akɛ adu kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui agboi ayitsei ahe.

english: Because tiny vine cuttings do not have a large stored water and food supply like tuber pieces, they require nursery shade and constant soil moisture until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Yɛ wein tso lɛ mli tsei bibii ni afo lɛ hewɔ lɛ Nu kɛ niyenii babaoo tamɔ ŋmeii ni abua naa lɛ bɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni aná hulutsoo yɛ ŋmeii akwɛmɔhe lɛ, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ aba daa kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli baawo wu bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too wet, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up necessary nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop if the trees do not get enough moisture, if insect pests like capsids attack them, or if the trees lack proper shade and soil nutrients during the flowering period.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ, kooloi tamɔ capsids tutuaa amɛ, loo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot under the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Underground cassava rot is usually caused by heavy, waterlogged soils during long rainy periods or fungal diseases spread by using infected stem cuttings during planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei fitemɔ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii kɛ nu ni ahiɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ mli. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ nɔ.

english: What is eating small holes in the leaves of my corn plants and leaving dark dirt inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on the central growing shoot of corn plants if not controlled early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm caterpillar, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ kɛji akudɔɔɔ lɛ mra.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds blow in the Ashanti region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa yɛ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over easily because microscopic worms called nematodes or banana weevil borers attack their shallow root systems, weakening the plant's hold in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana borers lɛ tutuaa amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ, ni no haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and soft before they even get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This black soft spot is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering during hot weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why is it important for me to support my yam vines with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves up into full sunlight so the plant can produce more energy, leading to larger tubers underground while preventing leaf diseases caused by contact with damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni fa babaoo bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ajie hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tso helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni akɛkpeɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ naa.

english: How does spreading dry leaves or grass around my crop stems help them survive hot days?
ga: Baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ Te mi ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry organic matter (mulching) covers the soil surface, keeping soil moisture from evaporating in the heat, keeping the ground cool, and stopping weeds from growing.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi (mulch) ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa be mli. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight and stopping the plant from growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips that spread viruses or physically damage tender young leaves while feeding on plant sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai loo amɛfiteɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ be mli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the main rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should wait until the rainy season establishes with two or three heavy, consistent rains that thoroughly soak the soil, rather than planting immediately after the very first light shower.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaje shishi ni nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa ni nɛɔ daa enyɔ loo etɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ obɔ lɛ baa. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ ɔ se amlɔ nɔuu.

english: Why can cassava stay in the soil for months without spoiling before I dig it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ nyɔji babaoo ni egbooo dani atsa lɛ?

english: Cassava stores its food and water deep in its underground roots, which allows the plant to stay dormant and survive long dry periods without dying or rotting.
ga: Cassava kɛ niyenii kɛ nu toɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi. ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli ni egbooo loo egbooo.

english: Why does my plantain tree die after producing only one bunch of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ gboɔ beni ewo ŋmei kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is naturally designed to flower and bear fruit only once in its life. Once harvested, that main stem dies, but new shoots called suckers grow around its base to produce future bunches.
ga: Afee plantain tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Kɛji akpa Tso titri lɛ baagbo. Shi ŋmeii heei, ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛbɔle ehe. base koni ekɛfee bouquets wɔsɛɛ

english: Why do groundnut plants push their stems down into the earth after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers grow above ground, but once pollinated, the plant stems bend down and push under the dirt because groundnut pods need dark, moist soil to develop and mature into nuts.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ abɔi pollen lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when the weather gets too hot, when the air is too dry, or when the plant does not get consistent water, as it tries to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomatoi fɔ̃ɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu daa Enɛ ji akɛ, tomato lɛ miitao ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni ehi wala mli.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on if I want big yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso koni ekwɔ lɛ? Kɛji miitao ŋmɔtɔ agbo ko

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can lift high enough to catch full sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves get, the more food the plant makes to grow a large tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso koni amɛbaai lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Babaoo ni hulu la ni baa lɛ naa lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when the rains are very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean your maize is missing nitrogen. Heavy rains often flood the soil and wash nutrients deep away from the roots, making it impossible for the crop to feed properly.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and soft during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. If your cocoa farm has too much shade or weeds, humidity stays trapped and rots the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛji o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hulutsoo loo jwɛi babaoo lɛ, Moisture baatsi ni eha ŋmɔtɔi lɛ agbo.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekadara lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the plant's juices and transmit viruses that stunt its development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. No shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni ekɛ hela ko ni haa edalɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after I clear and plant my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have adapted over centuries to survive easily in local soils with very little water or food, making them faster to grow than domesticated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi mlɛo yɛ maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji ni nu loo niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Ehaa amɛdaraa oya fe shia tsei

english: Why does my maize fall over easily when a strong wind blows through the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its roots are too shallow in soft soil, when seeds are planted too close together, or when insects eat the roots that anchor the plant to the ground.
ga: Abɛi baashwie eshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli jɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ye shishifãi ni ŋmɛɔ tsei lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with wooden poles instead of letting them crawl on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei awo mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil, exposing them to light and preventing fungal diseases that easily spread on wet ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Okɛwo la mli ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ efɔ lɛ nɔ oya lɛ naa.

english: My plantain plant has grown several small shoots around its base. Should I cut them off or leave them to grow?
ga: Mi plantain lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Tsoi babaoo ebɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he. Ani esa akɛ mafo mli loo mahã eda?

english: You should remove most extra shoots (suckers) and keep only one or two healthy ones. Leaving too many shoots creates competition for water and soil nutrients, resulting in much smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine (ŋmeii) ni okɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba kɛha nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and looking crumpled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus transmitted by insects. Controlling these pests early with neem oil or targeted sprays helps new leaves grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ Ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: I noticed small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my maize plants and leaving tiny waste particles. What is happening to my crop?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmei bibioo ko. Eyeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ jwɛi bibii yɛ esɛɛ. Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest common in Ghana that hides inside the whorl of maize plants. Applying recommended treatments into the center of the plant early prevents them from killing the main growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ. Ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ baatsu nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ mra. Enɛ baatsi enaa koni ekagbe ŋmei titri ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do people recommend that I plant cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have natural root bacteria that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This enriches the soil naturally, helping your maize grow taller and greener without extra fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fataaa he.

english: If I put fertilizer on my crops during heavy rain, will it still help the plants grow?
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Ani ebaaye ebua tsei ni amɛdara?

english: Heavy rains wash granular fertilizer away before plant roots can absorb it, wasting your money. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during torrential downpours, and cover it lightly with topsoil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji granular fertilizer lɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite oshika. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni okɛ ŋwɛi sũ fioo afɔ nɔ

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings drooping and turning brown during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that cannot handle full sunlight and dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains or cassava around young cocoa protects them from intense sun heat until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ kwraa. Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he. Kookoo bibioo lɛ baabu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: My tomato plants have produced plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers drop off without forming tomatoes. Why is this?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato. Mɛni he je nɛ e ba jã a?

english: Tomato flowers drop off without fruiting mainly due to high temperature stress, erratic watering, or poor pollination. Regular watering at the roots and keeping the plant stress-free during flowering helps the fruit stay attached.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii lɛ jɛɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli haomɔ mli titri. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo pollination ni ehiii Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli daa kɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni haomɔ bɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ akpɛtɛ he.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to dig up without disturbing the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ ni ogbalaaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ naa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves yellow and shed, leaving a bare main stem, and the ground surrounding the stem base starts cracking open as the tubers expand beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ fee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ tso titri lɛ efolo. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why does swamp rice thrive in standing water while maize roots rot if water sits on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants possess hollow internal tubes that transport air down from the leaves directly to the roots underwater. Maize roots lack this feature, so standing water cuts off air and suffocates them.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ mligbɛ tsɔnei ni mli ewo muji ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Abele shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ni ehaa mɔ ko nyɛŋ ashɛ ehe.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is short on nitrogen fertilizer or the field has too much standing water, which prevents the roots from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is mature enough to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to place tall sticks next to my yam mounds for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko toɔ ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ masɛi koni wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food, which directly helps the tubers under the ground grow much bigger.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Enɛ baaye abua bulbs ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛdara.

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, damp conditions; clearing weeds and cutting back heavy shade branches lets in air and sunlight to keep pods healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la baa koni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I remove some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain tree, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, resulting in larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ, ŋmeii fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out during flowering, or if you apply too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is mostly caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves, which can also spread plant viruses.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ashwã tsei amli hu

english: Why do my crops droop and look dead during the hot afternoon even if I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: In intense sunshine, plant leaves lose moisture faster than roots can draw it from the soil. As long as the ground has water, the leaves usually stand up again once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, tsei ahe baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be fɛɛ be ni nu yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ teɔ shi ekoŋŋ beni hulu lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds when my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients your crops need to establish strong root systems early on.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa mra.

english: How does mixing dried animal manure into my soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural plant nutrients over a long period while improving the soil's ability to hold onto rainwater during dry spells.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei amli niyenii be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ gbo ni egbo beni mifo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh direct sunlight when they are small. Leaving some shade trees protects them from hot sun and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa roots grow deep enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ beni amɛji bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field with no trees?
