ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in full sunlight and need shade to survive. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby creates a canopy that protects young cocoa leaves from harsh sun and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is essential for leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the crop the food it needs to turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my field after I finish harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas put nitrogen back into the soil naturally. Rotating crops keeps your soil rich without forcing you to spend as much money on chemical fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni enyɛɛɛ onɔ ni okɛ shika babaoo awo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe.

english: Which way up should I place my cassava stem cuttings into the dirt when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, nɛgbɛ esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should always be planted with the small buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down makes it very hard for sprouts to reach the surface and leads to poor root yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu fɔfɔii bibii ni afolɔ yɛ cassava mli lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋwɛi tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ woɔ yibii ni ehiii

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain tree, they steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Cutting back extra suckers allows the parent tree to grow stronger and produce much bigger bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ, Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ adara waa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji babaoo aba.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the tender inner leaves of young maize. Treating the funnel of the plant early with safe insecticides or neem extracts stops them before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ahe baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ ni akɛtsaa tsei ahe mra Ehaa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves get dark spots and rot when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni pepper baai lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close together blocks air flow and traps moisture around the leaves. This damp environment allows fungal diseases to spread quickly from plant to plant, so giving them room to breathe keeps them healthy.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oha ŋmei lɛ he ko ni ekɛmu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight with their leaves. Sunlight allows the plant to produce energy, which travels down into the roots to grow long, thick yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaji lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni yaa shishi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ sweet potato tubers kakadaji ni mli tse.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my vegetable plants help them during dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks direct sunlight from reaching the dirt. This traps moisture in the soil longer so your plants stay hydrated even on hot days.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Tsei baanyɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ po amli.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flower stems down into the earth after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts flower above ground, but the nuts themselves develop underground. Once the flower is pollinated, the plant grows a long stem called a peg that burrows into the soil where the groundnut pod can safely grow.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ Tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Cocoa flowers need pollen transferred to them by small insects or by hand to produce pods. If a flower isn't properly pollinated within a day or two, it dies and falls off the tree without forming a pod.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii biɔ pollen ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa. aloo kɛtsɔ nine nɔ koni akɛfee ŋmeii Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: What is hand pollination, and how does doing it help my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Hand pollination is manually moving pollen from one cocoa flower to another using a small brush or tool. Doing this guarantees that flowers get pollinated, leading to significantly higher numbers of healthy pods on your trees.
ga: Nɔ ni fata nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ he ji ni akɛ niji ajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ brɔsh loo dɛŋdade bibioo ko nɔ. Nakai feemɔ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ baawo ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo baa otsei lɛ anɔ.

english: When is the best time of day for cocoa flowers to be pollinated?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afee kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Early morning is the best time for pollination because cocoa flowers open at night and are fresh in the morning. The cooler morning temperatures also prevent the pollen from drying out before it takes hold.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha pollination. Ejaakɛ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ fɔɔ fɔmɔ gbɛkɛ, ni amɛfeɔ ehee leebi. He ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ leebi lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa pollen lɛ egbiɔ dani eshɛɔ shi.

english: Why do some of my young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up while still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: This is often caused by 'cherelle wilt' or fungal diseases like Black Pod. Cherelle wilt happens when the tree naturally thins out pods because it doesn't have enough water or nutrients to support all of them to maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ‘cherelle wilt’ loo ŋmeii hela ko tamɔ Black Pod kɛ enɛ baa. Cherelle wilt baa kɛji tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua pod muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛyashi eda lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need shade from other trees like plantain or forest trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ he hiaa ni tsei krokomɛi, tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei aná hulutsoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get burnt by intense direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the air humid and the soil moist so young cocoa trees can grow strong roots and foliage.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed many of their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival defense. The tree loses leaves to reduce water loss through evaporation, helping it conserve internal moisture until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ wala mli. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛlaaje kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ mli kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What happens to my crop if I plant my cocoa trees too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When planted too close, cocoa trees fight for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. The lack of air movement between overcrowded trees also creates humid conditions where diseases like Black Pod spread quickly.
ga: Kɛ adu Cocoa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ hu haa kɔɔyɔŋ mli edɔ ni helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why should I cut or prune healthy-looking branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes excess branches so sunlight and air can reach the inner parts of the tree. It forces the tree to direct its energy into producing flowers and pods rather than growing unnecessary leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ mli. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ

english: How does applying fertilizer help my cocoa trees make bigger and heavier pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔi ni tsii?

english: Fertilizer supplies essential food like potassium and phosphorus that soil loses over time. These nutrients nourish the tree so it has the energy to fill pods with large, heavy cocoa beans.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus jɛɛhe. shikpɔŋ ni baafite yɛ be ni sa mli Nɛkɛ niyenii nɛɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ bɔni afee ni ená hewalɛ ni ekɛwo kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ amli.

english: How do pests like mirids or capsids affect the way my cocoa tree yields pods?
ga: Te tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mirids loo capsids lɛ náa bɔ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Mirids suck sap from young cocoa stems and pods, injecting a toxic liquid that creates black wounds. This stops the branches from growing properly and destroys young pods before they can mature.
ga: Mirids nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Nu ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni haa pilamɔi diji baa lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli Enɛ haaa niji lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential food for growth. When the soil doesn't have enough nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has from older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in the soil when water sits around them for too long without draining away, especially during heavy rains. Excess water stops the roots from breathing and encourages fungal diseases.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nu ŋmɛ amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amumɔ kpaa ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when water supply is inconsistent. High heat damages the pollen, causing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy rather than grow fruits it cannot feed.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu aduawai ni ayeee lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive, tender leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the air moist and shielding young cocoa until their roots grow strong enough to withstand full heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni nuɔ he waa, ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nuɔ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during rainy storms right when the bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli be mli ni tsei lɛ aniji jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots like oak trees; they have shallow root mats near the surface. When heavy rain softens the soil and a heavy fruit bunch weighs down the plant, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ odum tsei. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my yams start growing green sprouts while they are stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃mɔ be mli ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally wake up from their resting period (dormancy) after a few months. Warmth and humidity in the storage area signal to the yam that it is time to start growing again, using its stored energy to push out sprouts.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe (dormancy) mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ he ni akɛ nibii lɛ toɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ. Hewalɛ ni abua naa lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii ni akɛtsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up tight and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap underneath the leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects. As the insects suck out moisture and nutrients, the leaves deform and curl up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kɛ́ kooloi lɛ miinu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Baai lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Different crops feed on different soil nutrients. Planting maize continuously exhausts the specific nutrients maize needs, leaving the soil tired. Rotating crops, such as planting beans or cowpeas, helps put nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yeɔ niyenii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ lɛ fitemɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii adumɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh conditions. Their seeds wake up instantly with rainfall and their roots spread fast to swallow up available water and nutrients before cultivated crops can establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Dumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ. Ni eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni amɛmi nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ ama shi.

english: Why is it bad to water my vegetable garden in the middle of the afternoon when the sun is hottest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu shwane be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering under a hot afternoon sun causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before reaching the roots. Drops of water left on leaves can also act like small magnifying glasses, scorching the leaves under intense sunlight.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ afee tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. No haa baai lɛ shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy green growth. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant recover its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ ahe baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my hot pepper plants drop all their flowers without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress or erratic watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot sunny spells helps the flowers stay on the stem and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu ni ejaaa mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl when the plant is stressed by severe heat, erratic watering, or viruses spread by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies. Providing consistent water and protecting young plants from insects helps prevent this.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa miigba tso lɛ naa. Nu ni bɛ faŋŋ loo helai ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nu ni oooha tsei bibii lɛ daa ni obu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I drop three or four maize seeds in a single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ woɔ dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting multiple seeds in one hole forces the seedlings to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks with small ears rather than one strong, high-yielding plant.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni toi bibii yɔɔ mli. Yɛ tso kome pɛ ni he wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do I need to erect tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to generate the energy required to grow large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground where diseases spread and exposes them to the sun.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ. Gbalamɔ ni okɛwo hulu la mli

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a sheltered, cool environment until the cocoa trees grow tough enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa shihilɛ ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo baa. Kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting inside the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in poorly drained soil, encouraging fungal diseases. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do tiny cocoa pods on my trees turn black and shrivel up during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, humid shade. Pruning unnecessary branches and weeding around the base of the trees helps air flow through and dry out excess moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni shade yɔɔ. Niji ni he ehiaaa ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ agbi.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on a plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize drains a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally renewing the soil's fertility for future crops.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it important for me to weed my field when the crops are still tiny rather than waiting until the weeds get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni tsei lɛ darako lɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ baafee wuji?

english: Young crops need all the nutrients, water, and sunlight they can get to build strong roots. Weeding early eliminates competition before the weeds can steal those vital resources from your growing crop.
ga: Tsei bibii hia niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la fɛɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa akaŋshii baa shi dani jwɛi baanyɛ aju nakai nibii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ amli.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting maize too close together makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and very tiny or empty cobs, which lowers your total harvest.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ baaha nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and burn when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and short root systems that cannot handle intense heat. They need shade crops like plantain to protect them from direct sun and preserve soil moisture while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even though the leaves on top are very big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ dara ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or stems are not pruned, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing heavy leaves above ground instead of sending food down to expand the edible root tubers underneath.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo afolɔɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni tsii. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Moŋ lɛ, amɛtsuɔ niyenii kɛyaa shi koni shishifãi ni ayeɔ lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shishi.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the dirt. Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so that the rain does not waste my money?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ akafite bo shika?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist and crops are actively growing, usually a few weeks after sprouting. Applying it on dry soil or right before heavy downpours causes the nutrients to wash away before roots can drink them.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ.

english: In intense sun, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. They temporarily wilt to conserve moisture and usually bounce back once the afternoon heat cools down.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagboi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ni bei pii lɛ, amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛji shwane mli latsaa lɛ ba shi pɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra shoots (suckers) steal water and food from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them leaves only the strongest sucker and allows the main tree to focus its energy on growing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tsoi krokomɛi (tsoji) juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii wuji ni tsii ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it important to trim the lower leaves of my pepper plants off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming lower leaves stops splash-back from rain that carries soil diseases onto the plant. It also helps the plant direct more of its food into making peppers instead of unnecessary leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kpaɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ hu kɛ niyenii babaoo feɔ chili moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai ni he ehiaaa baatsu nii.

english: How do simple weeds slow down my crop growth and reduce the money I make from my farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ aha mi tsei lɛ adalɛ aba shi ni eha shika ni mináa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds grow faster and are stronger than most crops. They aggressively steal the fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight meant for your crops, causing your crops to produce fewer and smaller yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei babaoo. Amɛju ŋmɔshi nibii. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii aggressively Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo.

english: What is eating ragged holes into the leaves of my young maize plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni tɔmɔ yɔɔ he akɛ maye ŋmeii ni etse amɛhe banee yɛ mi-ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is usually caused by fall armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant during the day to stay safe from heat and come out at night to eat the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ latsaa he. ni amɛje kpo amɛbaye baai gbɛkɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to heat and dry out easily under direct sunlight. Providing temporary shade, such as planting plantains nearby, protects their leaves from scorching and keeps the soil moist until the trees are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa, ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni akɛhaa, tamɔ tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shãaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ he baawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ naa.

english: Staking holds yam vines up off the ground so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food. It also prevents the leaves from rotting or catching soil-borne diseases by keeping them away from damp ground.
ga: Akɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ aaawo shikpɔŋ nɔ bɔni afee ni ebaa lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Agbɛnɛ hu, tsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite loo amɛkahe helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni oootsi kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key soil nutrient that helps plants stay green and grow leaves. It can happen when the soil is depleted or when heavy rains wash nutrients away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai. Ebaanyɛ eba kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fite niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land uses up the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. It also allows pests and diseases that prefer maize to multiply and build up in the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii afi fɛɛ afi. Ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ hu faa babaoo ni amɛbuaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans together with my main crops help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni mikɛ miŋmɔ titri lɛ duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and naturally deposit it into the soil through their roots. This enriches the soil, giving nearby crops like maize free fertilizer and improving overall yield.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ baa nii. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ abele ŋmɔshi nibii akafee nɔ ko ni oha nibii ni anáa lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ

english: These are likely fall armyworms, which target the central growing point of the maize plant because the inner leaves are tender and nutrient-rich. Catching and managing them early prevents them from destroying the growing core of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji fallworms ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ emli baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Amɛ ni ooomɔ ni otsu he nii mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ mli fã ni miida lɛ.

english: Excess rainwater trapped in the soil fills up all the tiny air spaces, preventing cassava roots from breathing. This wet, oxygen-poor environment encourages fungi to grow and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni ekpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni ehaaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amu. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli nɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii adalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my tomato plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without producing fruit when the plant experiences extreme heat, prolonged drought, or sudden dry spells. The heat stresses the plant, making it drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa Dɔlɛ haa tsei haoɔ Haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Leaving too many small shoots (suckers) forces them to compete with the mother plant for food and water in the soil. Pruning away excess suckers directs all the plant's energy into growing a bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tso lɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei ni dara ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is already moist after rain, but not during heavy downpours that wash it away. Moisture helps the plant's roots easily dissolve and drink in the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya ni amɛnuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my farmland feel harder and drier to cultivate than it used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe bɔ ni eji afii komɛi ni eho lɛ?

english: Over-farming without resting the land, combined with clearing trees and burning bushes, strips the soil of moisture and natural organic matter, making the earth compact and difficult for crops to grow.
ga: Okwaayeli babaoo ni shikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔɔmɔ bɛ mli Akɛ enɛ fata tsei kɛ tsei bibii ni ashã lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa sũ lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli nu kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewaa kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: What can I do to bring life back to farmland that no longer produces good crops?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mikɛ wala aba okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni wooo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: You can restore tired land by adding organic manure, planting leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts to feed nutrients back into the soil, and avoiding bush burning before planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts ni aduɔ koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ jwɛi lɛ ashãa he dani adu.

english: Why do my crops die quickly when the weather becomes too dry for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboiɔ oya nɛkɛ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Soil that lacks organic matter cannot hold onto rainwater for long. Adding compost or leaving dry foliage on the soil acts like a sponge, helping your crops stay hydrated during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ahi nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo ashi baai ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Are our traditional Ghanaian crops still worth planting compared to new commercial seeds?
ga: Ani wɔ Ghanabii akusum tsei lɛ ahe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ lolo akɛ abaadu kɛ akɛto jarayeli dumɔwui heei ahe?

english: Yes, many traditional local crops are naturally tough, well-suited to our local climate, and resistant to native pests, making them a safe and reliable option for feeding families and selling locally.
ga: Hɛɛ, blema tsei babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni wa. Ehi kɛha wɔmaŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi. ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋbii amli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛha wekui niyenii kɛ jarayeli yɛ maŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some older, traditional seeds survive long dry seasons better than new crop varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni etsɛ, ni ji shishijee dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei heei lɛ?

english: Traditional crop varieties have spent decades adapting to Ghana's rainfall patterns and soil conditions, giving them deep roots and natural resilience that many imported seeds lack.
ga: Kusum tsei henɔi lɛ he afii nyɔŋmai abɔ dani amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo Ghana nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsakemɔ ni dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ bɛ.

english: Is it true that growing traditional crops like cassava or yam drains all the nutrients from my soil?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ blema nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: All crops use soil nutrients, but heavy feeders like cassava pull a lot out over time. If you rotate them with soil-building plants like beans or peanuts, your soil will remain healthy and productive.
ga: Tsei fɛɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Shi tsei ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo tamɔ ŋmei lɛ baajie niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsei ni feɔ shikpɔŋ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, Oshikpɔŋ lɛ baahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaawo yibii.

english: How can I tell if a crop variety will give me good profit before I clear my land to plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ ko baaha sɛɛnamɔi kpakpai aba? Dani abaajie he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ?

english: Look at local market demand throughout the year, transport costs to the market, and how easily the crop can be stored after harvest so you aren't forced to sell cheaply during peak season.
ga: Kwɛmɔ maŋ jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Gbɛfaa kɛmiiya jara nɔ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ mlɛo akɛ abaato ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni ehe akahia ni ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ jara waaa yɛ be mli ni mɛi fa babaoo lɛ.

english: Why are my old saved crop seeds giving me smaller yields every new season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui momo lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ be hee fɛɛ be mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from harvests can weaken over generations if you do not select only the healthiest, strongest plants for seed stock, or if the soil has run out of vital plant nutrients.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee blɛoo kɛji ohalaaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni he wa fe fɛɛ pɛ kɛha dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa

english: What kind of crops should I plant if my land receives very little rain during the farming season?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ madu kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Drought-tolerant crops such as millet, sorghum, cowpeas, and cassava require less water to grow and can survive extended dry periods where other crops fail.
ga: Nibii ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa. Ehe ehiaaa nu babaoo dani ekwɛ̃, ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ he ni tsei krokomɛi nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do crops grow well in some parts of my farm but perform very poorly in other spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi shi ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Soil quality changes across a farm due to water pooling, erosion, shade from trees, or past farming practices. Adding compost to weak spots helps balance out the overall land quality.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su tsakeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. tsei ni shwieɔ shi shade kɛjɛɔ tsei amli loo okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni eho lɛ Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ hei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are these new seed varieties growing much bigger and taller than the local seeds I usually plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ dumɔwui heei nɛɛ daa ni amɛdaraa fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni miduɔ daa lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are specifically bred to absorb soil nutrients more efficiently, allowing them to produce bigger stalks and higher yields than traditional seeds.
ga: Akwɛ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ anáa ŋmeii wuji ni anáa yibii babaoo fe blema dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Are these new, unusually large crop varieties safe for my family to cook and eat?
ga: Ani nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni dara waa nɛɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha miweku lɛ ni amɛhoo ni amɛye?

english: Yes, improved and hybrid crops are rigorously tested to ensure they are safe and healthy for human consumption, often offering the same or better nutritional value as traditional crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, akaa tsei ni atsake amɛ kɛ tsei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ akwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ana akɛ amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ kɛha adesai niyenii. Bei pii lɛ, amɛhaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai loo ni hi fe blema tsei lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers encourage us to plant these new crop varieties on our land instead of our old seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔdu nɛkɛ tsei heei nɛɛ yɛ wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe tsutsu tsei lɛ?

english: New varieties are developed to give higher yields, resist local pests, and survive harsh weather conditions like drought, helping farmers secure better harvests and income.
ga: Amɛmiifee srɔtoi heei koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Eteɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa tamɔ hɔmɔ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnáa yibii kpakpai kɛ shika.

english: Why do insects and worms get inside my maize stalks and cobs before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii boteɔ ŋmãa tsei kɛ ŋmeii amli dani akpaa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm feed on the tender stem and grain tissues inside the plant, where it is moist and safe from weather and predators.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli fãji lɛ. Amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛhe bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do insects swarm my farm in much larger numbers right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ enɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Early rains encourage crops to flush with soft, green shoots, creating abundance of food and ideal moisture for insects to hatch and multiply rapidly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei heei, ni ji eŋɔli. Enɛ haa niyenii babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni kooloi lɛ anyɛ afɔ ni amɛfɔ oya.

english: Why do some of my crop fields attract more bugs than my neighbor's field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbalaa kooloi babaoo kɛbaa mihe fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Insects are drawn to plants that are either stressed from poor soil nutrients or planted with crop varieties that lack natural resistance to local pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii sumɔɔ tsei ni shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni esaaa lɛ haa amɛhaoɔ lɛ. aloo adu tsei srɔtoi ni bɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ jɛmɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why is my crop growing huge leaves but failing to produce any fruits or grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ dara shi enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii loo ŋmaa lɛ?

english: When a crop receives too much nitrogen fertilizer without enough phosphorus or potassium, it spends all its energy producing leaves instead of flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo tsei amli ni phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Will applying chemical fertilizers change the natural taste of my yams or cassava?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baatsake bɔ ni mi-sweet potato loo mi-cassava lɛ ŋɔɔ ha lɛ?

english: When used in the correct recommended quantities, fertilizers simply feed essential nutrients to the soil and will not spoil the natural taste or texture of your crops.
ga: Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ, Fertilizer lɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa pɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni efiteee otsei lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋɔɔmɔ loo bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ha lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and look weak even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of critical nutrients in the soil, such as nitrogen, or that water is sitting around the roots and preventing them from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo akɛ nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle amɛhe. shishifãi kɛ ŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do some crops wither quickly during a dry spell while others stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi gboɔ oya yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Certain crops have deeper root systems or leaves that trap moisture, allowing them to tolerate dry weather much better than shallow-rooted crops.
ga: Tsei komɛi yɛ shishifãi loo baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller, weaker plants and a lower overall yield.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I wait for the main rainy season to settle before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting after just one early rain can cause seeds to sprout and then wither away if a dry spell follows before the true rainy season begins.
ga: Tso kome ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbo kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ba dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ je shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient, or that heavy rains have flooded the roots and stopped them from taking in food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ hoɔ nu ni ehaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛye niyenii.

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, usually happens when there is irregular watering or a lack of available calcium in the soil while the fruit is growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why is my pepper plant growing lots of green leaves but no flowers or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ hiɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo ŋmeii bɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer encourages the pepper plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems rather than producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ woɔ pepper tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, feeding the land so your next crop grows better without as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo tsuuu nii.

english: What are these caterpillars eating the center leaves of my maize, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. You can control them early by applying recommended treatments directly into the central leaves where they hide and feed.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ mra. Okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo teŋgbɛ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ he ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my young crops so much in the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop roots are small and grow slowly, while weeds grow very fast and steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients your crops desperately need to get established.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii ni amɛdaraa blɛoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ waa koni amɛma shi lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves yellow and drop off and the soil around the plant stem begins to crack open from swelling tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some of my crops grow so much better in the forest zones than in drier areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi amli fe hei ni nu bɛ lɛ?

english: Forest zones provide higher humidity, richer soil nutrients, and natural shelter from harsh weather, which allows sensitive crops to grow strong and healthy compared to drier, open regions.
ga: Kooi amli hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ fa babaoo. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ baa nii jogbaŋŋ. kɛ adebɔɔ mli abobaahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ daa waa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛ akɛto hei ni egbi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Can I still harvest good crops in the dry season when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Ani wɔbaanyɛ wɔkpa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lolo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Yes, certain resilient crops or crops planted in suitable forest zones can still produce good yields even during intense sun, provided the soil retains enough moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni adu yɛ kooi ni sa mli lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai lolo yɛ bei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli po. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa mli

english: Why do crops perform differently in different parts of Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ Ghana hei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Each region has different soil types, rainfall amounts, and sun intensity. Crops thrive best when planted in areas that match their specific need for water, shade, and soil quality.
ga: Kpokpaa fɛɛ kpokpaa yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi srɔtoi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ bɔ ni hulu la lɛ tsoɔ waa ehaa. Tsei daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni amɛhiamɔ nii pɔtɛɛ ni kɔɔ nu, hulutsoo, kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa he lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Does it matter if I plant my crops in an area where prɛkɛse trees are growing?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hei ni tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, certain crops avoid places where prɛkɛse trees grow because those areas may have different soil moisture levels, shade patterns, or nutrient balances that do not support that specific crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hei ni tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nakai hei lɛ baanyɛ aná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, hulutsoo, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yeɔ ebuaaa nakai ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can looking at natural trees like prɛkɛse help me choose what to plant?
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsei tamɔ Prixe ni mikwɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mahala nɔ ni madu.

english: Natural trees serve as indicators of soil health and environment. If a wild tree thrives in a spot, it shows what kind of moisture and shade that specific patch of land offers.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ nɔ ni tsɔɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ ha. Kɛji koo mli tsei kwɛ̃ yɛ he ko Ebaatsɔɔ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo henɔ ni he pɔtɛɛ ko yɔɔ.

english: Is it a good idea to plant all my crop seeds at the same time across my whole farm?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ shikome? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Planting everything at once works very well in many regions because all plants receive the same seasonal rain and sunshine together, making care and harvesting easier.
ga: Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni aduɔ shikome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokpai babaoo anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ naa nugbɔ kɛ hulu la yɛ be kome mli. Ehaa kwɛmɔ kɛ kpamɔ feɔ mlɛo

english: Will my crops still do well if I plant them in regions outside their natural forest home?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ lolo kɛji midu amɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ he ko ni tsei yɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Many crops can adapt and yield well outside the forest zone if you clear the land properly, plant at the right time, and manage water and shade carefully.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsake amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ koo lɛ kponɔ kɛji ojie jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli ni okwɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers build temporary shade ceilings over young seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi maa be kukuoo mli ŋwɛitsu yɛ dumɔwui bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Overhead shade ceilings protect tender young plants from burning under direct intense sun and shield them from heavy rain, helping them establish strong roots before full exposure.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋwɛitsu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa dani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ.

english: How does intense heat from the sun affect my crops during the day?
ga: Te hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ saa midumɔ nii ahe yɛ gbi lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extremely hot sun dries out the soil quickly and causes leaves to lose moisture, which can weaken the crop unless it is planted in a forest zone or protected by shade.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa sũ lɛ gbiɔ oya, ni ehaa baa lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ja adu yɛ kooi amli loo abu he yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: How does creating a canopy or ceiling over my plants compare to natural tree shade?
ga: Te ŋwɛi ŋta loo ŋwɛi ŋta ni afee yɛ mi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe ŋmɔlɔ yeɔ egbɔ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Constructed ceilings mimic the natural tree canopy found in forest zones, giving you control over how much harsh sunlight reaches your crops while keeping the ground cool.
ga: Afee ŋwɛitsu lɛ koni ekɛkase tsei ni anaa yɛ kooi amli lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ falɛ, yɛ be mli ni ohaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How do I know when my maize is mature enough to harvest so it stays good until it reaches buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋma lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa? Bɔni afee ni ahi nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi ebaashɛ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: Maize is fully mature when the outer husks turn brown and dry, and a small black mark appears at the base of each grain. Harvesting at this stage prevents mold growth during transport while protecting the grains from field pests.
ga: Abɛi eda kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. Ni okadii diji bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii aya hiɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛ nibii majeɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil and turn dark so quickly after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ duŋ oya beni mifo amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots lack a thick protective skin, causing them to react rapidly with oxygen once exposed to air. This natural decay begins within 48 hours, which is why cassava must be processed or brought to market immediately after harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɛ hewolo ni mli wa ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ haa amɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ feɔ ekome oya kɛ́ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ nɛɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli, no hewɔ ni esa akɛ atsu ŋmei he nii loo akɛba jara nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akpa ŋmei lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits developing black, rotten spots at the bottom while still growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot and happens when the plant cannot transport enough calcium to the developing fruit, usually caused by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant feed calcium to the tomatoes naturally.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot ni ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa aya aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛha tomatoi lɛ calcium yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and produce small, twisted fruits that market women reject?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee aduawai bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? ni yei ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ kpooɔ lɛ

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking nutrients from the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early allows the plant to grow full-sized, smooth peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaha tso lɛ akwɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eye emuu ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers come out watery and light instead of heavy and firm when harvested?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee tsiimɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ akpa lɛ?

english: Yams become watery if harvested too early, before the vines and leaves yellow and die naturally. The plant packs starch into the tuber during its final growth phase, so cutting life short leaves the tuber with too much water and too little starch.
ga: Sweet potatoes baatsɔ nu kɛji akɛ akpa mra tsɔ. dani wain tsei lɛ kɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgboi. Tsei kɛ starch woɔ amɛ bulbs lɛ amli yɛ amɛdalɛ naagbee fãi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei awala be lɛ feɔ kuku. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ aná nu babaoo tsɔ, ni ŋmeii lɛ hu faaa tsɔ.

english: Why do my ginger roots stay small and thin in the soil instead of growing thick and plump?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ginger shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Ginger needs soft, loose soil packed with organic matter to expand underground. If the soil is hard or clay-heavy, it presses against the rhizomes and physically prevents them from swelling into fat, market-quality ginger.
ga: Ginger he miihia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ Emiimɔ rhizome lɛ nɔ ni etsĩɔ enaa koni ekafu ni etsɔ jarayeli nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ji fatty ginger.

english: If I spray pesticide on my vegetable crop, how long do I need to wait before harvesting to sell to buyers safely?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie aduawai anɔ Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ ni akpa ŋmaa lɛ dani ahɔ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe aha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ?

english: Every pesticide has a required waiting period called a Pre-Harvest Interval, usually between 3 to 14 days depending on the product. Waiting the full duration gives the plant time to break down the chemicals so the food is safe for consumers to eat.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ yɛ be ni akɛmɛɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dani kpamɔ be lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yeɔ gbii 3 kɛyashi 14 teŋ, ni enɛ damɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ emɛ kɛyashi eyi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa be ni ekɛgbala tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli koni niyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni mɛi ni yeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye.

english: Why is it wrong for me to dry my harvested cocoa beans directly on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ aaagbi kookoo yibii ni akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Drying cocoa beans on the bare ground exposes them to dirt, stones, animal waste, and harmful soil molds. Buyers require beans dried on elevated bamboo mats so the airflow is clean and the cocoa meets quality regulations for chocolate making.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ haa amɛnaa muji, sũ, kooloi afɔfɔi kɛ sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Mɔ ni heɔ lɛ miisumɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi yɛ ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ. koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anyɛ abɔle ehe ni ehe tse Ni kookoo lɛ ashɛ taomɔ nii ni sa kɛha tsokolate feemɔ lɛ he.

english: How can I keep my plantains from turning yellow and soft too fast during transport to the city market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi plantains lɛ anaa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee blɛoo oya tsɔ beni akɛyaa maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Plantains release a natural ripening gas called ethylene when exposed to heat and sunlight. Transporting green bunches under shade and keeping them cool slows down this gas production, keeping the fruit firm for buyers.
ga: Plantains jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo kɛ́ akɛwo hulutsoo kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei eŋɔlii lɛ tee hulutsoo shishi ni aha amɛfee fɛ̃i lɛ, ebaaha gas ni ajieɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni oha mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ahiɛ aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do small insects appear inside my sealed bags of stored beans and eat holes through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-beans ni mikɛto lɛ kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Bean weevil eggs are usually laid on the pods while still growing in the farm field and carried inside during harvest. Drying the beans thoroughly in the sun and using airtight containers suffocates the eggs before they can hatch and destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmei ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ, ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmeii yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛ nibii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ dani amɛfɔ ni amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient deep down into the soil where young roots cannot reach it yet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ afɔ niyenii nɛɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them refreshes depleted soil naturally, giving free food to the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Tsei nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ ni efite yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ. ni okɛ niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ yaka.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need soft, shaded light to grow without stress. Clearing all large canopy trees exposes fragile seedlings to intense heat and direct sunlight, burning their leaves and drying out the root zone.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia kane ni mli jɔ koni amɛdara ni haomɔ ko akafee amɛ. Tsei wuji fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable crops in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Okɛ nu awo tsei lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli. Aloo ani leebi hi fe no?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because cool soil easily absorbs moisture before the sun gets strong. Watering in the hot afternoon causes rapid evaporation, wasting water and potentially distressing heated plants.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya dani hulu la lɛ mli wa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya. Nu ni afiteɔ ni ebaanyɛ efite tsei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground before it is time for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when heavy water sits in poorly drained soil for too long. Excessive moisture suffocates the tubers beneath the ground and creates an environment where soil fungi thrive and attack the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Fɛ̃i babaoo baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ehaa shihilɛ ko baa ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daa ni amɛtutuaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the underside of fresh leaves, or by a plant virus carried into the crop by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai heei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ kɛyaa tsei amli lɛ nɔ

english: Why are flowers falling off my tomato plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures become excessively hot or when water supply is irregular. When stressed by heat or drought, the plant sheds its blossoms to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛji dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ hao lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller every year on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many sucker shoots are allowed to grow around one main plantain stem, they compete heavily for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves enough energy for the main plant to produce large bunches.
ga: Kɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ, no lɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ waa. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ je shishi ekwɛ̃ beni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers remain alive after harvest and go into a natural rest period. As temperature and humidity change in the storage barn, the tuber breaks dormancy and uses its stored food to sprout new shoots for reproduction.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni amɛboteɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be mli. Kɛji hulutsoo kɛ latsaa ni yɔɔ he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ tsake lɛ Bulbs lɛ yaa wɔɔhe ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmeii heei kɛha fɔmɔ.

english: Why should I leave proper space between my crops instead of planting them close together to get more food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná niyenii babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting crops too closely makes their roots compete fiercely underground for food and water while their leaves block sunlight from each other. Proper spacing ensures every single plant gets enough light and nutrients to yield heavily.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu he akaŋshii mli waa. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii babaoo.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow from the tip inward in a V-shape, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant is moving stored nutrients from its older bottom leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛtee mligbɛ, ni efee V su. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ miitsi niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ kɛmiijɛ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛ ŋwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ aba.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field make my next crop grow better without adding extra fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei loo ŋmei ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmei kroko fataaa he lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the plants die and decompose, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop naturally.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi amli. Kɛ tsei gboi ni amɛfite Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my cassava plants losing all their leaves during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods as a self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss. The tubers beneath the ground remain alive and healthy, and fresh leaves will sprout as soon as the rains start again.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tubers lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: How do I know if the very first rain of the season is enough for me to plant my maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: You should not plant after the first light rain because the soil underneath is still dry and the seeds will scorch. Wait until the rain is heavy enough to soak the ground about a hand's depth deep so the seeds have continuous moisture to germinate.
ga: Esaaa akɛ aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo ni dumɔwui lɛ baashã. Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛyashɛ aaafee tso kome koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark black and rotting while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high moisture and heavy shade. Clearing weeds around the tree base and pruning excess branches allows sunlight and air flow to dry out the pods and prevent infection.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ni afoɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ekɛtsi helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small holes in them and sticky dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Eyɛ jɛmɛ ni muji ko ni shwieɔ shi yɛ jɛmɛ. Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the central leaf whorl to feed on soft new leaves. The dirt you see inside is the caterpillar's waste material.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye baa heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Muji ni onaa yɛ mli lɛ ji ŋmei lɛ sũ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot or when the plant does not get steady water. Stress causes the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy rather than trying to feed growing tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Haomɔ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha tomato ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow crooked when the soil underneath is hard and compact. Building high, loose soil mounds or ridges gives the tubers soft earth so they can expand easily straight downward.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ baakɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni afee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ yitso lɛ afee blɛoo bɔni afee ni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa shi tɛ̃ɛ. mlɛo

english: Why is it better to plant small sword suckers instead of big maiden suckers for my plantain farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmeii bibii moŋ fe ŋmeii bibii wuji kɛha mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Small sword suckers with narrow, spear-like leaves have stronger bulb bases and establish new roots quickly, whereas large suckers lose moisture rapidly through big leaves and take longer to start growing.
ga: Klante suckers bibii ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ lɛ yɛ bulb shishitoo ni wa fe tsutsu lɛ, ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi heei oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii wuji ni nuɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai wuji anɔ, ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that create a living canopy, offering essential shade and keeping the soil cool while the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there is too much direct sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under bright heat. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them from direct sun and keep the soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the corn plant is starving for nitrogen, a key food in the soil. Adding manure, compost, or fertilizer gives the plant the nutrients it needs to turn green and produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛná toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my corn seeds very close together to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Spacing them out properly ensures every plant gets enough resources to grow big and strong.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when it rains too heavily?
