ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them in the soil for too long. Heavy water prevents the roots from breathing, causing underground mold and rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu ni tsii haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why are there small holes inside the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli.

english: This damage is usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which hide in the growing heart of the maize plant and feed on tender leaves before the corn forms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why does my field yield less food when I plant maize in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil until it becomes weak. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts restores rich nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni jara wa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants drop off before growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers from sudden stress, such as extreme heat, too little water, or too much water. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔ trukaa tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu fioo tsɔ. aloo nu babaoo yɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does putting dry leaves on the soil around my plants keep them fresh during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani mitso lɛ haa ehiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry leaves acts like a protective blanket. It stops the sun from drying out the ground quickly, keeping the soil cool and holding water for the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and produce very little food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni niyenii fioo pɛ woɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops, leaving your crops hungry and unable to reach full size.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why does cutting off small extra branches from my tomato plant help me get larger tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii ni eshwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni minine shɛɔ tomato wuji anɔ.

english: Removing unwanted side shoots stops the tomato plant from wasting food on useless leaves, directing all its energy into growing larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni ataooo lɛ, ehaaa tomato tso lɛ afite niyenii yɛ baai ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ anɔ. Ni okɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni okɛha tomato tsei lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees keep falling off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by lack of water, extremely hot sun, dry Harmattan winds, or low soil nutrients like potassium and boron. Providing shade trees and mulching helps the plant retain moisture and keep its flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ miihao. hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium kɛ boron. Shading kɛ mulching yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Is it better to save seeds from my current maize harvest to plant next season or buy fresh certified seeds?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni akɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli loo ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli?

english: Certified seeds from approved dealers give higher yields because they are specially bred for strength and disease resistance. Seeds saved from past harvests lose their vigor in the next generation, resulting in smaller cobs and weaker crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aŋmala he odaseyeli kɛjɛ mɛi ni jaa ni akpɛlɛ amɛnɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ baaha yibii babaoo aba ejaakɛ atsɔse amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛhe wa ni helai akamɔ amɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cassava plants curling up and turning yellow with green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai bibii lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects and contaminated stems. Planting disease-resistant stem cuttings and pulling out infected young plants stops the disease from spreading to the rest of the farm.
ga: Kasava mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei ni mli ewo muji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ hei krokomɛi.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year even when rainfall is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops remove essential food from the soil every time they grow. Without adding animal manure, compost, or fertilizer, and without rotating crops, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot support heavy yields.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni abaadu amɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he ni ŋmɔshi nibii tsakemɔ ko bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow thin, crooked, and bumpy instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ amli tsei, ebɔle, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yam tubers become deformed when planted in hard, compact, or stony soil that stops them from pushing downward easily. Soil pests like tiny root nematodes also feed on developing tubers, causing rough skin and stunted growth.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli edɔ, loo tɛi ni yɔɔ mli ni haaa amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shi mlɛo lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ shishifãi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ Amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ hu. Enɛ haa hewolo nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in the leaves of my young maize plants and leaving dirt inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day and feed on soft leaf tissue, which can destroy the plant if not controlled early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii amli fãji Enɛ baanyɛ akpata tsei ahiɛ kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rotten before they are even ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular—switching between very dry soil and flooded soil stops the plant from absorbing calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ teŋ tsakemɔ baatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkaná calcium jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing plenty of leafy dark green stems but refusing to bring out peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi ewooo pepper lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes pepper plants focus all their energy on leaf growth instead of fruiting. Excessive shade or very hot weather during flowering can also cause the plant to drop its flowers before setting fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha pepper tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashwie shi dani ewo yibii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans beside my maize make the maize look greener and grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ amɛmasɛi? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-abele lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni edaa oya?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. Nearby maize plants absorb this natural fertilizer, making their leaves greener and boosting their growth.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ shwieɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ. Enɛ haa amɛbaai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa amɛdaraa.

english: Why should I prune away some of the young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi amli lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain tree for food, water, and sunlight. Keeping only one main stem and one or two replacement suckers ensures the tree produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tsobii bibii babaoo (tsobii) kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri kome pɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã kome loo enyɔ ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afee kui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer to my cocoa farm when the soil is very dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer cannot work without water. Water acts as the carrier that dissolves fertilizer and delivers its nutrients and energy to the roots, so putting fertilizer on dry ground leaves your crops unable to feed.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ atsu nii kɛji nu bɛ. Nu tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ni oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ baatsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii.

english: Should I wait for the rains to start before spreading fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you should always wait until the soil is moist from rain. Soil moisture allows the fertilizer granules to dissolve so the roots can draw up the nutrients and energy the tree needs to produce cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ omɛ be fɛɛ be kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ mli. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ajie niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛfee kookoo lɛ.

english: Why do fertilizer granules need to dissolve in water before my crops can use them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ awo nu mli dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsu nii lɛ?

english: Plant roots cannot take in solid food. The fertilizer must dissolve in soil water so that the liquid solution can carry essential nutrients and energy through the root system up into the rest of the plant.
ga: Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aye niyenii ni wa. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ nu mli bɔni afee ni nu ni mli tse lɛ anyɛ atsɔ shishifãi lɛ amli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ hewalɛ aya tso lɛ fãi krokomɛi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees look weak and tired even after I bought expensive fertilizer for them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mihe ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa amɛha amɛ moŋ?

english: Just like a person cannot work well on an empty stomach, a cocoa tree gets weak without proper feeding. If the soil lacks water, the tree cannot absorb the fertilizer nutrients, leaving the plant hungry despite the fertilizer being on the ground.
ga: Taakɛ bɔ ni gbɔmɛi nyɛŋ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ musu ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ. Cacao tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ ahaaa amɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ miiye tsei lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Do cocoa trees really need energy like humans do, and where do they get it from?
ga: Cacao tsei he miihia hewalɛ tamɔ bɔ ni adesai he hiaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ni nɛgbɛ amɛnáa amɛhewalɛ kɛjɛɔ?

english: Yes, cocoa trees need energy to grow leaves, flower, and produce pods. They get this energy by absorbing dissolved soil nutrients and water through their roots, which serves as their daily food.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cacao tsei he miihia hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ baai, fɔfɔi ni amɛwo ŋmeii. Amɛnáa hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛtsɔ sũ mli niyenii ni mli ewo muji kɛ nu ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ edaa gbi niyenii lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow even though I applied fertilizer last month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ amɛ wo mli yɛ nyɔŋ ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If there was not enough moisture in the soil after you applied the fertilizer, the roots could not suck up the nutrients. The leaves turn yellow because the tree is starving for energy.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa yɛ be mli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Does soil moisture do more than just keep my cocoa trees cool?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni fe kookoo tsei lɛ ni ehaa amɛhe jɔɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Yes, soil moisture acts as a transport system. It dissolves nutrients in fertilizer and carries that essential energy directly into the tree's roots so it can grow strong and bear good pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo. Ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ adara ni amɛná ŋmeii kpakpai.

english: Will adding extra fertilizer help my cocoa trees survive a dry period without rain?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: No, adding fertilizer during a dry spell will not help. Without soil water to carry the nutrients into the roots, the plant cannot access the fertilizer's energy and will remain hungry.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ eyeee ebuaaa. Kɛji nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aya shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aná ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ kɛkɛ ni hɔmɔ baaye amɛ.

english: What happens to fertilizer if it sits on top of hot, dry cocoa farm soil?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji akɛ akɛwo kookoo ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ?

english: Fertilizer sitting on dry soil sits idle without helping the crop. Without water to carry its energy down to the root zone, your money is wasted because the plant stays unfed.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛji nu bɛ ni baaha hewalɛ aba shi kɛya shishifã lɛ he lɛ Oshika lɛ baafee yaka ejaakɛ ahaaa tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: How does water in the soil help my crops process fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Soil water unlocks the energy inside fertilizer by dissolving it. The water then carries these dissolved food particles directly into the plant's roots, similar to how drinking liquids helps humans digest food.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gbeleɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, nu lɛ kɛ niyenii ni etsɔ mli nɛɛ yaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Etamɔ nu ni anuɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa adesai ni niyenii shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off whenever the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry spells to conserve water and survive drought. The plant is not dead; its roots remain healthy underground, and new leaves will grow back as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Eshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their tiny flowers before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Mɛi enyiɛ dani ebatsɔ pod?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands more flowers than they can support. The tree naturally sheds flowers it cannot feed, especially if there is a shortage of water, soil nutrients, or tiny insects like midges to pollinate them.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ, fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi yɛ e diɛŋtsɛ ehe ni enyɛŋ eye niyenii. Titri lɛ kɛji nu he miihia. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii koni amɛfee pollination

english: Why do my sweet potato vines spread all over the soil before the roots grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes use their leaves to catch sunlight and gather energy first. Once the vines grow strong and spread across the ground, the plant starts sending that accumulated energy down into the roots to form tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la ni amɛbua hewalɛ naa klɛŋklɛŋ. Beni wain tso lɛ daa waa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baaje nakai hewalɛ ni ato lɛ shishi kɛya shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛfee bulbs.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains on the same plot with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce broad leaves that shade young cocoa trees, keeping the soil cool and moist while the cocoa grows.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Is it good for my crops if I plant beans together with my maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa fata ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize helps both crops. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil, which acts as a natural food for the maize while saving you money on commercial fertilizer.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa Ekɛ shika hu toɔ jarayeli ŋmãa he nyɔmɔwoo he.

english: Why do my plantain trees always fall over during heavy rains and winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ yaa nɔ egbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and heavy fruit bunches make the plant top-heavy. Mounding soil around the base and propping the main stalk up with a strong bamboo pole prevents strong winds from uprooting them.
ga: Plantain shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii haa tso lɛ feɔ tsii. heaping dirt around Akɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa woɔ shishi kɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akatswa ni ejie shishifãi lɛ.

english: What causes my tomato leaves to curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a virus, or by intense heat stress. Keeping your plot clear of weeds and protecting young plants reduces the insect population.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ Kɛ́ aha jɛmɛ jwɛi akafee nɔ ko, ni abu tsei bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why are small insects always damaging my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High humidity during the rains creates a damp environment where insects like capsids thrive. Pruning shade trees slightly to let sunlight reach the trunks and clearing old pods keeps these insect populations down.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids baanyɛ akwɛ Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ fioo koni hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishi ni ajie ŋmeii momoi nɛɛ baaha kooloi nɛɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: How can I safely save seeds from my best pepper harvest to plant next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ pepper dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ ato shweshweeshwe koni madu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Take seeds from healthy, fully ripe peppers, wash off the fruit flesh, and dry them thoroughly in a cool, shaded area. Store them in an airtight container mixed with a little dry wood ash to prevent insects from eating them.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Tsɔɔmɔ aduawai lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. ni egbi yɛ he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni akɛ tso sũ ni egbi fioo efutu mli koni kooloi akaye amɛ.

english: Why do my stored yams rot so quickly after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikpa amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are cut or bruised during harvest, or if stored in hot, wet places. Handle tubers carefully, let them dry in the shade for a few days, and store them on elevated wooden racks in a well-ventilated yam barn.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ yitso lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ha ni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii fioo komɛi. ni akɛtoɔ tsei ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains to keep moisture in and protect them until they are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hebuu mli kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tall maize plants fall over in the field after a light rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when planted too shallowly or when they lack strong brace roots near the soil surface, especially if planted in very loose soil without piling dirt around the stem base.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shishifã ni fiɔ sɛɛ ni mli wa ko bɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse waa ni shikpɔŋ ko bɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-pattern starting from the tip, it usually means the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for strong green leaf growth.
ga: Beni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field help my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, leaving free natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ahaa dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce small fruits when there are many little shoots growing around its stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Be mli ni ŋmeii bibii ni miida yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: The small side shoots, called suckers, compete with the main tree for water and food. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the parent plant to put its energy into growing large bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ suckers. Kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ aka akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines produce smaller tubers if I let them crawl on the ground instead of using stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji miha efo shikpɔŋ yɛ tso ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines up so the leaves catch more light and stay free from ground pests.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la babaoo koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná la babaoo ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai akafee nɔ ko.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out too much, or when bees and insects fail to move pollen around inside the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ ajie pollen lɛ kɛbɔle fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like mites or thrips feeding on the underside of leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up all the roots?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni atsaaa shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ?

english: As cassava roots reach full maturity under the ground, the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and shed, leaving fewer leaves near the top of the main stem.
ga: Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Enɛ haa baai fioo pɛ bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi moŋ?

english: On very hot days, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out and usually recovers by evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Why are many farmers in Ghana switching from traditional crops to rubber farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miitsake kɛmiijɛ blema ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛmiiya rɔbɔt ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Rubber trees provide a steady, multi-year income because latex can be harvested continuously for 20 to 30 years, making it a reliable cash crop for long-term export markets.
ga: Rɔba tsei haa shika ni yaa nɔ daa afii babaoo ejaakɛ abaanyɛ akpa latex lɛ be fɛɛ be afii 20 kɛyashi 30, ni no haa amɛfeɔ shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛhaa jarayeli hei ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do international buyers reject some of my harvested crops even if they look fine to me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ mikpamɔi lɛ ekomɛi eyɛ mli akɛ amɛhi jogbaŋŋ yɛ mihiɛ moŋ?

english: Export markets enforce strict standards on chemical residue levels, proper storage materials, and visual defects. Unapproved harvest containers or minor pest traces can cause whole batches to be rejected.
ga: Jarayelihei ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ haa mlai ni mli wa ni kɔɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni eshwɛ lɛ falɛ baa. Nibii ni sa ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe kɛ nibii ni anaaa ni ejaaa Nibii ni akɛkpaa nibii ni bɛ he odaseyeli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha akpoo ŋmɔshi nibii muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn yellow when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to strong direct sunlight and heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides the protective cover and moisture needed during their early years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaha hebuu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over before the fruit is fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems holding up heavy bunches. If microscopic soil pests damage the roots or too many suckers are left growing around the main stem, wind easily pushes them over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hiɛɔ panicles ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ loo ŋmeii komɛi eshwɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ, tso titri ni fa tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatsɔ mli oya.

english: Why are my maize leaves suddenly filled with small ragged holes during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ trukaa lɛ, ŋmãa baa lɛ mli buji bibii ni bɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, a common pest in Ghana that feeds aggressively inside the leaves of growing corn during damp weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm caterpillar, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai ni miida lɛ amli waa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep dropping off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when stressed by high heat or dry soil. Mulching around the roots keeps the soil cool and retains the moisture needed for fruit to set.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Mulching around Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kɛha yibiiwoo lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava grow huge green leaves above ground but produces small root tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages cassava to put energy into growing top leaves instead of storing energy underground. Crops need potassium and phosphorus to grow large tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmei hewalɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ebaa lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekɛto shikpɔŋ shishi. Tsei he miihia potassium kɛ phosphorus koni amɛná ŋmeii wuji.

english: Apply fertilizer when the ground is moist after a light shower, but avoid putting it down right before heavy downpours, which sweep the nutrients away before roots can absorb them.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he dani nugbɔ anɛ waa. Enɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the ground and provides extra nutrients to neighboring maize plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii babaoo.

english: How do I know when my rubber tree is mature enough for latex tapping?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni rɔbɔt tso lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ otswa rɔbɔt?

english: A rubber tree is ready for tapping when the trunk reaches a circumference of about 50 centimeters measured at 1 meter from the ground, which typically takes 5 to 7 years after planting.
ga: Rɔba tsei lɛ efee klalo kɛha gbee kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebɔle ehe aaafee sɛntimitai 50 ni asusu mita kome kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni bei pii lɛ, eji afii 5 kɛyashi 7 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can clearing weeds too roughly around my cassava plants cause them to get sick?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Ani ŋmei tsei babaoo baanyɛ aha amɛye hela?

english: Yes, if cutlasses or hoes scrape the stem or slice the roots, it injures the crop. These wounds weaken the plant's natural defenses, making it easy for harmful fungi and soil rots to enter and destroy the root system.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei kuku ko shwie tso lɛ shishi loo efo shishifãi lɛ. Ebaafite tsei lɛ. Nɛkɛ pilamɔi nɛɛ haa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nibii lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ sũ mli ŋmeii baabote shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt or die right after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ loo amɛgboiɔ trukaa beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Rough handling during transplanting tears the seedling's delicate feeder roots, putting the plant into severe shock. With damaged roots, the plant cannot absorb water or food, making it weak and vulnerable to drying out or catching diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ lɛ, ebaagbala dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi ni yeɔ nii waa lɛ amli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baabote shoofeemɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ efite lɛ Tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu loo niyenii. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyɔɔ oshara akɛ amɛbaagbi loo hela baamɔ amɛ.

english: Can cutting off branches from my pepper plants cause them to catch diseases?
ga: Ani pepper tsei aniji ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba?

english: Yes, tearing stems roughly or using dirty tools leaves open wounds on the plant. Pathogens like bacteria and fungi can easily enter through these fresh cuts and infect the entire crop while its immunity is low.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etseɔ tso lɛ shishi. Aloo nibii ni he tseee ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashi pilamɔi ni agbele yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Muawai tamɔ bacteria kɛ fungi baanyɛ abote mli mlɛo kɛtsɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii heei nɛɛ anɔ. ni egbɛ hela lɛ eshwa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ mli yɛ be mli ni gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ faaa lolo lɛ.

english: Why do pests and diseases attack my crops more during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops lose their natural strength when they are stressed by drought. This drop in plant immunity leaves them unable to fight off insects or fungal spores that are present in the soil and air.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ laajeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. Nɛkɛ gbɔmɔtso mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa ni baa shi nɛɛ haa amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Is it true that healthy crops can defend themselves against insects better than weak ones?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ahe jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, well-fed and undamaged crops naturally produce chemicals that deter pests and help wounds heal. Poorly fed or damaged plants lose this ability, turning them into easy targets for insects.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni tsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsaa pilamɔi. Tsei ni ayeɔ amɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ loo ni efite lɛ bɛ nyɛmɔ nɛɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do heavy rains sometimes cause my crops to start rotting and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Excess water drowns the root system by blocking air in the soil, which severely weakens the plant. The wet conditions allow fungal spores to easily infect these weak, suffocating roots.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ waa. Shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ fungal spores lɛ baatswa shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe nɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my maize crop is actually using the fertilizer I put in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ miitsu nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: A crop that is taking up nutrients well will have deep green leaves, thick stalks, and noticeable weekly growth. If the leaves stay pale green or yellow and growth is slow, the plant is not absorbing the fertilizer properly.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ, amɛshishifãi ni mli tse, kɛ otsi fɛɛ otsi dalɛ ni kadiɔ mɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa fioo lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ eŋɔɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check if my cocoa trees are healthy?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ kɛji mi-kokoo tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ?

english: You should inspect your crops at least once a week. Regular checking helps you see if the trees are growing properly and allows you to catch early signs of pest damage before the issue spreads across the farm.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli shikome yɛ otsi mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ tso lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona kɛji tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni onaa okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai efite mra dani naagba lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are my crops staying small even though I planted them at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ faaa eyɛ mli akɛ midu yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops need healthy soil to feed properly. If the soil lacks nutrients or is too compacted for roots to spread, the plant cannot eat enough to grow, leaving it weak and stunted.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ he miihia tsei koni amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã lɛ, Tsei nyɛŋ aye nii bɔ ni sa kɛkɛ ni amɛdara. ni eha egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ

english: What is the very first sign that my crop is getting sick before it fully dies?
ga: Mɛni ji klɛŋklɛŋ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela mɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani egbo kwraa?

english: The earliest warning signs are usually subtle leaf color changes like yellowing or small spots, slight wilting during the cooler parts of the day, or a sudden stop in new leaf growth.
ga: Kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ mra fe fɛɛ ji baai lɛ ahe su tsakemɔi fioo, tamɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ bibii. Nibii ni shwieɔ shi fioo yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli. loo baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ni kpaɔ trukaa lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They require shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees to protect their leaves from sunburn and keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Does planting a cassava stem slanted in the ground produce better yields than planting it straight up?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni adu ni atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha yibii kpakpai aba fe ni adu lɛ shiŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slant or horizontally allows the roots to grow closer to the topsoil where nutrients are concentrated, producing larger tubers that are much easier to harvest.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ loo he ko ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa bulbs lɛ feɔ wuji, ni ekpamɔ waaa kwraa.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients. Removing them leaves only one main follower shoot, ensuring the parent tree has the strength to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, tso titri kome pɛ baashwɛ. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed animal manure helps restore green growth and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper blossoms drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Consistent watering and balanced fertilization help the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by insect-transmitted viral diseases carried by tiny whiteflies, or by heat stress. Managing pests early and keeping plants adequately watered prevents foliage damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ kooloi amli kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii loo kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli Mra be mli nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ baaye abua ni akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why do yam vines need tall sticks to climb up instead of crawling on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɔɔ ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni amɛaakpã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food that builds tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to light and away from damp ground, which prevents leaf rot and leads to bigger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Staking baaha baai lɛ aje kpo yɛ la mli ni ekɛ ehe akabɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni ekafite ni ebaaha sweet potatoes ni dara lɛ aba.

english: How does growing cowpea or beans in my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop leaves decay, that nitrogen remains in the soil to act as natural food for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso baai lɛ fite Nakai nitrogen lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves showing light yellow patterns and producing tiny roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings. You can prevent it by planting clean, disease-resistant stem varieties recommended by agricultural officers.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei ni tsei ni he tse, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ adumɔ nɔ taakɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ wo ŋaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni muji tamɔ ŋmei yɛ tso lɛ shishi?

english: This damage is caused by stem borer caterpillars that hatch on leaves and tunnel inside the stalk. Applying recommended pest control into the central leaf funnel early in the season kills the larvae before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji stem borers ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ tunnel ni yɔɔ stem lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛyeɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land has the right soil for starting a cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa ni manyɛ maje kookoo ŋmɔ shishi?

english: Cocoa trees prefer deep, well-drained dark soil rich in organic matter that holds moisture without staying waterlogged. If water sits on your land for days after rain, or if the soil is pure sand, cocoa will struggle to grow well.
ga: Cocoa tsei sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni nu emɔɔɔ mli lɛ babaoo yɛ amɛmli. Kɛji nu hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ji ŋã krɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaawa akɛ abaakwɛ Cocoa.

english: How many years will I have to wait after planting before my new cocoa trees start bearing pods?
ga: Kɛ́ midu sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ ni cacao tso hee ko aje shishi ewo ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties take about 3 to 5 years to start producing fruit, but modern hybrid cocoa varieties can start yielding pods in as little as 2 to 3 years if given proper care, shade, and fertilizer.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi amli kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ, aha amɛ hulutsoo, ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli.

english: What is the best month of the year for me to plant young cocoa seedlings in the ground?
ga: Mɛni ji nyɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli ni abaanyɛ adu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: The best time to plant cocoa seedlings is at the start of the main rainy season, usually around May or June in Ghana. This allows the roots to settle deep in moist soil before the harsh, dry Harmattan season starts.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ May loo June mli yɛ Ghana. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ dani Harmattan be ni mli wa ni egbiɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that easily burn under full sunshine. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Should I cut down all the big shade trees on my land before I plant cocoa?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani madu kookoo?

english: No, you should keep some tall forest trees on your farm. Cocoa trees naturally grow best under moderate shade, which protects them from extreme sun, keeps the soil moist, and reduces weed growth.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okɛ koo mli tsei kakadaji ahi oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Cocoa tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be ni sa mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shweremɔ baa shi

english: Why do some of my tiny green cocoa pods turn black and dry up while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Mine lɛ etsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi beni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and overly bushy farms. Pruning tree branches to let in sunlight and air helps prevent the disease from ruining your pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ tsɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ oofolɔ tsei lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akafite otso lɛ mli tsei lɛ.

english: How do spray chemicals protect my cocoa trees from capsid bugs?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu mihe kɛjɛ capsid ŋmeii ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Capsids or mirids are small insects that bite into young cocoa shoots and pods to suck sap, causing branches to die back. Applying approved insecticides at the right time kills these pests and keeps your trees healthy.
ga: Capsids loo mirids ji kooloi bibii ni ŋmɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii koni amɛnu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. ha nine lɛ agbo Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi nɛɛ ni eye ebua ni otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is lacking key soil nutrients like nitrogen, getting too much direct sunlight without shade, or suffering from severe heat and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni enine eshɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be bɛ nɔ. aloo amɛnaa amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce plenty of flowers, but very few of them turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers rely on tiny beneficial insects called midges for pollination. If your farm is too dry or sprayed heavily with the wrong chemicals at flowering time, these insects die off, leaving flowers unpollinated so they drop without forming pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ damɔɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ anɔ. Atsɛɔ nakai midge kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo tsofai ni ejaaa lɛ shwie nɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ baagboi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baafee pollin. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Fertilizer is usually applied twice a year when the soil is moist—first at the beginning of the rainy season to support new flowers, and again mid-season to help the growing pods gain size and weight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli koni akɛfi fɔfɔi heei asɛɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ koni eye ebua ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ni amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I clear all the large shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their leaves from harsh sunlight and to keep the soil moist. Clearing all shade trees exposes young plants to heat stress and drying winds, so planting temporary shade like plantain trees helps them survive and grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hɔɔŋ koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ naa dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa amɛgbiɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shade mli tamɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi ni amɛdara waa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to capture maximum sunlight, which feeds the underground tuber. Staking keeps leaves off the hot ground, protects them from rot and diseases, and allows the yam tubers to grow much larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii Staking baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ fitemɔ kɛ helai ahe. ni eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient needed for healthy green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plants regain their green color and produce full ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmei loo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farm soil richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and the roots rot in the soil, they release this natural fertilizer, which feeds the next crop you plant in that field.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baaha niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable crops with dried leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, shields it from the hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly. It keeps the soil cool and moist, stops weeds from growing, and turns into rich organic manure as it decays.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Koni nu akafee oya Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa kɛji efite.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by several dry days that can scorch new sprouts. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady so your young seedlings have continuous moisture to establish deep roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii babaoo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ be fɛɛ be koni eha odumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: How do I choose the best part of a cassava stem to plant for a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛdu koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: The best cuttings come from the firm middle section of mature, healthy cassava stems. The woody bottom is too old to sprout quickly, and the green top is too tender and dries out easily.
ga: Nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni afolɔ lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei tso ni mli wa ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ. Tso shikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eda oya. ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ darako tsɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and produce very small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiiwo yibii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and plant food in the soil. When weeds grow close to your crops, they steal these vital resources, leaving your plants weak and undernourished.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ Jwɛi juɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, otsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil stress. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers stay on the plant and develop into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ ba amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do tiny insects bore holes into my harvested dried maize, and how can I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitswa bu yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Grain insects called weevils attack stored maize if the grain still contains moisture or is left unprotected. Drying your maize thoroughly in the sun until it is hard, and storing it in airtight sacks or bins, prevents insects from destroying your harvest.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ baatutua ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛji ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ lolo loo ashi lɛ ni abuuu he. Abele ni ooogbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni okɛto kotoku loo tsɔne ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ baatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight because their roots are shallow and leaves burn easily. Plantain trees or shade trees provide living cover to shade the cocoa leaves and retain soil moisture while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni baai lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing along the middle of lower leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is the plant food responsible for green foliage; when missing, the plant pulls nitrogen from old lower leaves to send to new upper growth.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai eŋɔli baa. Kɛji akɛ ebɛ lɛ, tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛmaje ŋwɛi dalɛ hee.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when left in waterlogged soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tuber area.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tuber he lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without developing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdarako ni amɛfeee aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or erratic dry spells. Without consistent moisture and moderate temperatures, the plant drops its flowers to save water and survival energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni bɛ shiŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni tamɔ ekome kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni baaha wala ahi shi lɛ he.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting very small when I allow many shoots to grow around one stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ beni mihaa ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso kome he lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers (shoots) to grow around the main plant causes competition for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Pruning extra suckers to keep only one main stem and one small successor ensures maximum energy goes into building large fruit bunches.
ga: Ha suckers (shoots) babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ he. Enɛ haa akaŋshii baa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ni aaafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ koni ahi tso titri kome pɛ kɛ nɔ bibioo kome ni baaye esɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha akɛ hewalɛ babaoo atsu nii yɛ aduawai akui wuji afeemɔ mli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites, which damage leaf cells and can transmit plant viruses. Applying natural neem oil spray or insecticidal soap controls these small pests early.
ga: Koolooi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips loo mites, ni fiteɔ baa lɛ mli wala yibii ni baanyɛ agbɛ tso mli helai lɛ ashwã lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔ mra.

english: Why do I find small caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that hides in the whorl (funnel) of young maize leaves. Applying biopesticides or clean wood ash directly into the leaf whorls early in the morning kills the pests before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tso sũ ni he tse wo baai lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward maximum sunlight, which fuels large tuber growth underground. Staking also lifts foliage off damp ground, preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaa lɛ amɛshwã koni hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo. Enɛ woɔ bulbs wuji hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi fungal leaf helai anaa.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing large open leaves but refusing to form a tight, round head in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baa lɛ feɔ baai wuji ni agbele shi ekpooɔ akɛ ebaafee yitso ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when they receive excessive nitrogen fertilizer late in growth or when temperatures are too high. Balanced feeding and proper plant spacing encourage inner leaves to curl tightly into a solid head.
ga: Cabbage nyɛŋ ajie eyitso kɛji enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ yɛ be mli ni eda lɛ sɛɛ loo kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Niyenii ni ja kɛ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛfeɔ bulbs ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. Rotating them with heavy feeders like maize naturally replenishes nutrient levels in depleted soil without expensive chemicals.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Niyenii agboi tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii ni faaa lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii.

english: Why must I completely clear out old, tangled weeds and dead crops before putting new seedlings in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe kɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ fɛɛ dani madu dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Clearing out old, muddled growth prevents hidden pests and fungal diseases from transferring to your new seedlings. It also ensures young crops do not have to compete with established roots for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie ŋmɔshi nibii momo ni efite lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ odumɔwui heei lɛ ahe. Ekwɛɔ hu koni ehe ehiaaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni etswa ama shi lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii.

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings directly under old, dying trees without cutting the old ones down first?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ tso momo ko ni miigbo lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni mafolɔko kookoo tso lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: It is best to clear out old or diseased trees first. Old trees suck away precious groundwater and nutrients from the soil, and their falling leaves or branches can crush your fragile new seedlings while they try to grow.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie tsei ni egbɔ loo helai emɔ amɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni tso baai loo niji ni egbee shi lɛ baanyɛ akumɔ odumɔwui heei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: What happens to my plantain seedlings if I leave them sitting on the bare ground for days before planting them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi plantain dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji miha amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ gbii babaoo dani midu?

english: Seedlings left sitting out on the ground lose moisture rapidly through their leaves and bag soil. The heat from the sun can burn their tender roots, making them too weak to survive once you finally put them in the farm pit.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baatsɔ baai kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ nɔ oya. Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã eshishifãi bibii lɛ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ehi shi kɛji okɛwo ŋmɔ mli bu lɛ mli pɛ.

english: Why do overgrown weeds harm my young crops much faster than they harm full-grown plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ yeɔ mitsei bibii lɛ awui oya fe bɔ ni amɛyeɔ tsei ni eda lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Young crops have short roots and small leaves, so they easily get shaded out and starved by fast-growing weeds. Full-grown plants already have deep roots and tall branches that allow them to fight off weed competition.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji kɛ baai bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa efeɔ hulutsoo oya ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ. Tso ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ momo, ni no haa enyɛɔ ewuɔ eshiɔ jwɛi.

english: Is it really necessary for me to struggle and remove big tree stumps before planting my cassava field?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni majie tsei wuji akutsei lɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ dani madu ŋmei?

english: Yes, removing tough stumps clears space for cassava roots to expand fully under the soil. Old stumps left in the ground also rot and attract termites and fungal rots that can attack your fresh crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli gbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Tsoi momo ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu fiteɔ ni egbalaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni baanyɛ atutua onibii heei lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny ears when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtoi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their leaves block each other from getting sunlight, causing them to stretch upward instead of growing strong. Their roots also fight in the soil for the same limited nutrients, leaving little energy to produce good yield.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baabu ehe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ hewalɛ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ hu bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii ni fa fioo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshiɔ koni ekɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when I plant them on an open field with no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are very sensitive to intense sunlight and heat. Without temporary shade plants like plantains to cover them, the hot sun scorches the leaves and dries up the upper soil where their roots are trying to spread.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ, tamɔ plantains lɛ, Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni shishifãi lɛ miitao amɛgbɛ amɛshwã lɛ agbi.

english: Why is it difficult for my newly planted crops to grow if the soil is full of old, hard plant roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni midu ehee lɛ miiye waa akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ tso shishifãi ni egbɔ ni wa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ lɛ?

english: Hard, old roots create a dense barrier under the ground that stops tender new crop roots from going deep to find moisture. Loosening the soil and clearing old roots gives new roots freedom to expand easily.
ga: Shishifãi ni egbɔ ni wa lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi koni ekɛtsi tso shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao ŋmɔtɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ shishifãi momoi lɛ haa shishifãi heei nyɛɔ amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo.

english: Why does my extension officer tell me to remove diseased plants from the field instead of leaving them on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛjie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ amɛshikpɔji lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Diseased plant material left on the ground acts as a home for insects and fungi. When rain falls or wind blows, spores spread from the dead plant debris directly onto your healthy new crops.
ga: Tsei ahe nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shia kɛha kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ, Spores lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni egboi lɛ amli kɛyaa onibii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Should I burn all the brush after clearing my farmland, or is it better to leave the cleared plants to rot into the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ beni mijie he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ loo ehi akɛ maha tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: While burning is fast, leaving cut vegetation to rot naturally creates mulch. This organic cover keeps the soil moist during hot dry spells and feeds essential nutrients back into the soil for your new crops.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ baa oya moŋ Shi kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. ni okɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha otsei heei lɛ.

english: How do I know how much fertilizer I need to buy for my one-acre farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha ŋmɔ ni dalɛ ji acre 1 lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs depend on your land size and crop type. For instance, a standard one-acre maize farm in Ghana usually requires about two bags of NPK fertilizer, applied evenly so you do not waste money or burn the plant roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe hiamɔ nii damɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmɔ ko ni dalɛ ji acre kome ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ biɔ aaafee NPK ŋmãa kotokui enyɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ, no hewɔ lɛ, ofiteee shika loo oshãaa otsei lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller harvests each year even though my land size hasn't changed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi lɛ? Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ tsakeee po.

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land every season drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops, such as planting beans or groundnuts after maize, helps restore nutrients naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ, ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Should I burn the weeds and clearings on my new plot of land before planting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi ni mafo shikpɔŋ hee nɔ dani madu nii?

english: Burning destroys valuable nutrients and helpful organisms in the topsoil. It is better to clear the weeds and allow them to decay naturally on the field to build rich soil manure.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Ehi akɛ ooojie jwɛi lɛ ni oha amɛ fite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni efee shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni baa nii.

english: Why are termite mounds on my land damaging my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miifite mi-cassava tsei lɛ?

english: Termite mounds host thousands of worker termites ruled by a queen. When underground wood is scarce, worker termites attack crop roots for moisture and food; removing the queen or treating the mound protects your cassava.
ga: Termite gɔji lɛ ji he ni nitsulɔi akpei abɔ ni maŋnyɛ ko yeɔ nɔ lɛ yɔɔ. Beni tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ faaa lɛ, Nitsulɔ ŋmeii tutuaa tsei shishifãi koni amɛtao ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ojie maŋnyɛ lɛ loo otsa gɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ o-cassava lɛ he.

english: Are the bees flying around my blooming watermelon crop going to destroy the flowers?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni foɔ kɛbɔleɔ mi watermelon tsei ni miifɔ lɛ ahe lɛ baafite fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: No, bees are friendly worker insects. They move pollen from flower to flower, which is necessary for your watermelon plants to form healthy, big fruits.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ji kooloi ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo. Amɛjieɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Enɛ he miihia koni o-watermelon tso lɛ aná yibii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do I see black ants crawling all over the leaves of my cowpea plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii diji ni miiho yɛ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Ants are usually attracted to tiny insects called aphids that suck sap from your plants and secrete sweet liquid. Controlling the aphids will cause the ants to move away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii sumɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. ni atsɛɔ lɛ aphids Amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu ni ŋɔɔ kpo. Kɛ́ akudɔ ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aya he kroko.

english: Yellow leaves are typically a cry for help showing the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting too much water, which prevents the roots from taking up plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ he bolɔmɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aye tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tso lɛ gbo ni egbo beni mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sun rays. They need temporary shade trees, like plantains, to shield them and trap soil moisture while their roots get established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without forming any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to save water. Covering the soil around the plant stem with dry grass helps keep the roots cool and retains water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa ashɛrɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi koni nu akafite. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ tsei ni egbi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay very thin when I plant many cuttings close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo waa beni miduɔ niji babaoo yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space for its roots to swell into large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my maize plants start wilting even when the soil still feels slightly moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo lolo lɛ?

english: Maize plants need a steady supply of water to transport nutrients. During very hot days, leaves lose water faster than roots can pull it from deeper soil, causing the plant to roll its leaves to conserve moisture and protect itself.
ga: Nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he miihia ŋmãa tsei koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya. Yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni ebu ehe.

english: How does providing a little bit of water during dry periods help my crops yield better?
