ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu fioo ni mikɛhaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Even small amounts of moisture during dry spells prevent crops from going into stress, allowing them to keep photosynthesizing so their flowers and grains can form properly instead of stunting.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko po shwie shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ akahao amɛhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛfeɔ fotosintɛsis. Enɛ ji koni fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ afee jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my corn cobs coming out small with missing kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ daraaa ni ŋmeii lɛ bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Missing kernels usually happen when hot, dry weather strikes during the flowering stage, preventing proper pollination when silks emerge on the cob.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ba yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni akafee pollination ni sa beni siliki miida yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my corn leaves turn pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate that the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, which often happens when there is either too little water for roots to feed or too much water washing nutrients away.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ nɔ. aloo nu babaoo yɛ mli ni enyɛŋ etsu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he nii

english: How do I know when my maize is completely ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the surrounding husk turns brown and dry, the kernels become hard, and a small black mark appears at the base of each kernel.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni ŋmei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi, ni ŋmei lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii diji. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi.

english: Why does soil on land that has been sitting unused for a long time become so hard to farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuuu nii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ okwaayeli wa lɛ?

english: Unused land exposed to intense heat hardens because the topsoil loses organic matter and natural earthworms, causing the soil particles to pack tightly together and block water absorption.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuuu nii ni hulutsoo be ni naa wa waa yɔɔ mli lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ baafite lɛ. Enɛ haa sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaaa nu abote mli.

english: What happens to crop roots if I plant on land that has poor drainage and standing water?
ga: Mɛni baa shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu damɔ shi lɛ nɔ?

english: When water sits on the land without draining, crop roots cannot get the oxygen they need to survive, which causes root rot and prevents the plant from growing strong.
ga: Beni nu yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my crops so the water isn't wasted?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu koni mikafite nu?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening gives water time to soak deep into the root zone before the heat of the sun evaporates it.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ náa be ni ekɛboteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ dani hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How does using simple water pumps or irrigation allow me to farm throughout the entire year?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu pɔmp loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi yɛ okwaayeli mli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Irrigation supplies water directly to your crops when rainfall stops, allowing you to grow and harvest crops like corn continuously, even during the dry season.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu baa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Enɛ haa oyaa nɔ oduɔ nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni okpaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli po.

english: Why do crops planted too close together produce a smaller harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their root systems compete for the same limited water and nutrients in the soil, resulting in thinner stems and smaller cobs or fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni faaa lɛ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo. ni ŋmei loo aduawai lɛ ji bibioo

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build strong green leaves. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has to the new top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves yellow and weak.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee Tso lɛ baajie emli nibii lɛ fioo kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Shi shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the branches without ever forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ shi amɛwooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or lack of water, which prevents the flower from pollinating itself. Without successful pollination, the plant sheds the flower to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee amɛhe pollen. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when the rainy season gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil just like they need water. When water stays trapped in heavy soil without draining away, it suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungus to grow, which causes the cassava tubers to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tamɔ bɔ ni amɛhe hiaa nu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni nu ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ baagboi.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out thin and twisted instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni efiteɔ lɛ? Yɛ ŋmɔtɔ agbo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yam tubers twist and stay small when the soil beneath them is hard and compacted, making it difficult for the root to push down and expand. Loose, deep soil or raised mounds allow the yam to expand freely into a large, smooth shape.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaatsi amɛhe kɛya shi ni amɛmli amɛshwã. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when the hot sun comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji hulu lɛ shã amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have thin leaves and soft roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They lose water through their leaves faster than their tiny roots can drink it from the dry ground, so they need shade trees around them to block the harsh heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛlaajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ fe amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ. Amɛbaanu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ gbiŋ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo ni ebɔle amɛhe koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees snap or fall over so easily during heavy rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ fãa loo egbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems filled with water. When the soil becomes soft from rain and a heavy bunch of fruit grows at the top, the top-heavy plant loses its balance easily unless supported by a wooden prop.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni mli tse ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewɔ ni aduawai babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ. Tsei ni amɛyitsei tsii lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛhe oya, ja akɛ tso fiɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops very close together so I can get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other, and their roots fight for the same water and soil food. Giving each plant enough space reduces this competition so every plant can grow to its full size.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba shi bɔni afee ni tsei fɛɛ adara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to feed my crops without buying expensive testing tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni miheee kaa nibii ni jara wa?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, feels soft and crumbly in your hands, holds moisture well without staying muddy, and contains living creatures like earthworms. Earthworms are a great natural sign that the soil has plenty of organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. E nuɔ he kaa e ngɛ bɔdɔ nɛ e ngɛ tsɔe ngɛ nine mi. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa efee muji. Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ji adebɔɔ mli okadi kpakpa ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nibii babaoo ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do insects attack my crops much more heavily during dry spells than during rainy weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli fe otsii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: During dry spells, crops become thirsty and stressed, making them weaker and less able to defend themselves. Insects are attracted to these weak plants because they seek out the sweet sap inside to survive the hot weather.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baaye kumai ni amɛhao. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ efã ehe. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii sumɔɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ nɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛmiitao nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after I clear my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh conditions and sprout instantly as soon as rain and sunlight hit bare ground. Crops need more care because they spend their energy making fruits and seeds rather than aggressive roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji nugbɔ kɛ hulu la ba shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ pɛ. Tso lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ dumɔwui fe bɔ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and intense heat. They require shade from nurse crops like plantains or tree canopies to protect their delicate leaves and keep the soil moist until their roots grow deep enough to survive the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛkwɛɔ amɛ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ashishi koni amɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why does placing dry grass or leaves around the base of my crops help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with organic material, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, keeps the roots cool, prevents weeds from taking over, and slowly adds nutrients back into the soil as it rots.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akatsɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fiofio beni egboɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential food for green growth. Adding compost, well-rotted animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Koolooi amli ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli Loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Growing them alongside or after maize naturally feeds the soil, giving the maize extra nutrients to produce better yields.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo esɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ naa niyenii krokomɛi ni haa ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems very close together so I can fit more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ makwɛ tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to form large, healthy tuber roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ shishifãi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Extra suckers steal water and nutrients away from the main mother plant. By cutting away all but one or two strong suckers, the main plant gets all the energy it needs to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Afoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ, ja eko loo enyɔ pɛ. Tso titri lɛ nine shɛɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee plantains akui wuji ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground to prevent diseases and ensures maximum sun exposure for larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni eha niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akabote mli. ni eye ebua ŋmeii wuji ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa? Yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that eats the growing tips of maize. Catching them early allows you to spray recommended treatments or neem extracts before they destroy your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa loo neem mli nu lɛ shwieɔ nɔ dani efiteɔ onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in soggy, waterlogged soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting your cassava on top of raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching around the roots helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the young flowers and small green nuts dropping off my coconut trees before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii tsei anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Coconut trees often shed their young flowers and immature nuts when they experience sudden water stress during dry seasons, lack potassium in the soil, or suffer from sap-sucking insect pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi bibii kɛ amɛ ŋmeii ni edako lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛna nu he haomɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo naagbai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli baa

english: How can I store my harvested coconuts so they stay fresh and don't spoil while I wait for buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ato koni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkafite be mli ni amɛmiimɛ mɛi ni baahe lɛ?

english: Mature coconuts last longest when kept inside their intact husks and stored off the damp ground in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated area away from direct sunlight.
ga: Kokooi ni eda lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ fe fɛɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto amɛmli ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ mli. Ni okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. Ekɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ teŋ jɛkɛ

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow and dying off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves in maize usually points to a lack of nitrogen in the soil or roots suffocating in excessively waterlogged soil during heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni miihoso yɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ fe nine lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why is my cassava producing very leafy bushes but small tubers underneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to send energy into leaf growth instead of tuber development; balanced potassium levels are required for big tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ ehewalɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmeii. Potassium ni falɛ ni ja lɛ he miihia waa kɛha yitsei wuji.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree during rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water mold fungus that spreads in humid, heavy shade; opening up the shade canopy and frequently plucking off diseased pods helps stop the spread.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli efɔ, ni mli wa mli. Gbelemɔ ni agbeleɔ hulutsoo be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ shii abɔ Ebaaye ebua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over during windstorms even when the fruiting bunches are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ ahum be mli eyɛ mli akɛ kui lɛ daraaa lolo lɛ?

english: Plantains easily blow over when underground pests like nematodes or banana stem borers eat away at the roots, weakening the plant's anchor in the soil.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa plantains kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo banana stem borers ye amɛshishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my tomatoes crack open on the vines just as they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ tswaa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Fruit cracking happens when plants receive a sudden rush of heavy rain or heavy watering after a dry spell, causing the inside of the fruit to expand faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo nu babaoo ha tso lɛ trukaa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso yibii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies transmitting plant viruses, or by extreme heat and drought stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei amli helai lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ mli.

english: Will planting groundnuts between my maize rows help or harm my maize yield?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ baaye abua loo ebaaye mi ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ awui?

english: Planting groundnuts alongside maize helps the crop because groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Kɛ́ aduɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable farm early in the morning or during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning allows roots to absorb moisture before the sun gets hot, preventing extreme water loss from evaporation and avoiding hot-soil root shock.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ amɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Etsiɔ nu ni fiteɔ waa lɛ naa kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Can I grow food crops in small empty spaces around my house or compound?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii yɛ he bibioo ko. Mishia loo akutso lɛ he?

english: Yes, crops like pepper, garden eggs, tomatoes, and leafy vegetables grow very well in small backyard spaces or even in old sacks filled with rich soil as long as they get direct sunlight and regular watering.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, tomato, kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛtsu bibioo ko mli loo yɛ kotoku momo ko ni sũ ni baa nii eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli po mli. Shii abɔ ni hulu la lɛ baashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni awoɔ lɛ nu daa lɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my crop seeds too deep into the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu aduawai dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they run out of stored energy before they can reach the surface to get sunlight, which causes them to rot underneath the soil instead of sprouting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ Hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baaho dani eshɛ ŋwɛi koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃.

english: Why should I plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight; plantains grow very quickly and produce large leaves that shield the young cocoa seedlings from heat while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai wuji ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is a key plant nutrient, or that the soil is overly soaked with water, which chokes the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ko bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ kɛ nu. ni haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans helps make the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans take natural nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which leaves extra plant food in the soil for heavy-feeding crops like maize to use later.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei aniyenii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni akɛbaatsu nii sɛɛ mli.

english: How does spreading dry grass or dead leaves around the base of my crops help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass around your crops, called mulching, blocks the hot sun from drying out the ground, prevents weeds from growing, and decomposes into extra food for the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni ooogbɛ oshwã onibii lɛ ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he

english: How do I know when cassava in my farm is ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest around 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves start to turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle he lɛ Tso wulu lɛ miije shishi egbɛ eshwa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the daytime heat becomes too intense, when the soil drops below a required moisture level, or when the plant lacks sufficient nutrients to support fruit growth.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ba shi kɛyashɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ataoɔ lɛ shishi loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: What causes small holes and rough edges on the leaves of my crops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Holes in leaves are caused by chewing insects such as caterpillars or beetles eating the plant leaves, which reduces the plant's ability to manufacture food from the sun.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt and droop during the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In strong afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil, but they normally recover as temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I plant them in an open field without tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in harsh sunlight. Planting tall crops like plantains around them provides living shade and traps moisture, protecting the cocoa plants until their roots are deep enough to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ ehe lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Ebuɔ cacao tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ ehiɔ shi.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow, the plant is starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to stay green. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen out of the soil, so the plant steals food from its old leaves to feed the top leaves.
ga: Beni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ Tsɔɔ akɛ tsei he miihia nitrogen. Amɛji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce big green leaves above ground but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava plants focus on leaves instead of roots when they receive too much leafy fertilizer (nitrogen) or are planted too close together. Spacing them properly and using balanced soil nutrients forces the plant to send its energy down into swelling the tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ haa amɛbaai lɛ feɔ nɔnyɛɛ moŋ fe amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ́ amɛná baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii (nitrogen) babaoo loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ atsu hewalɛ kɛya shi kɛyashi bulb lɛ baafu.

english: Why should I cut off the small side shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main stem. Removing all but one or two strong shoots ensures the main plantain tree gets enough food to grow big, healthy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii titrii lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Why do I need to trim unwanted branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji ni ataooo kɛjɛ cacao tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes crowded and dead branches so sunlight and fresh air can flow through the tree. Good air flow prevents black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more flowers and pods.
ga: Tso ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni mli ewo muji ni egboi lɛ koni eha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ black pod hela naa ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off without making any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Extreme weather stresses the plant, causing it to discard its flowers to conserve water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ashwie koni nu akafite.

english: Why do I need to heap loose soil around the base of my groundnut plants after they bloom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔle muji ni etse ehe lɛ he lɛ? Peanut tso shishitoo beni fɔfɔi lɛ efo sɛɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they grow stems called pegs that must push downward into the earth to grow nuts. Soft, mounded soil makes it easy for the pegs to enter the ground and build healthy pods.
ga: Beni ashɛɔ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ ahe pollination sɛɛ lɛ, Stems baakwɛ̃, ni atsɛɔ lɛ pegs, ni esa akɛ ashɛre awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baagbee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do I have to put wooden poles in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves produce food through sunlight. Staking lifts the vines high off the ground so all leaves catch maximum light, sending food down to build larger yam tubers in the soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛtsɔɔ hulu la nɔ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa aná la ni fa fe fɛɛ. ni etsuɔ ​​niyenii kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why is it bad for my yield if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the same specific soil nutrients year after year and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth, reducing your harvest.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ He kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ okpamɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetable garden early in the morning rather than in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu woɔ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli babaoo leebi fe shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering in the afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate in the heat before reaching the roots. Morning watering lets plants absorb moisture before the sun gets strong and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko kɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni enáa nu dani hulu la lɛ mli wa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed the new top leaves, showing you that the soil needs fertilizer or well-rotted manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Koni etsɔɔ bo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted at the start of the main rainy season when the ground is moist. This helps the stems grow strong roots quickly so the plant can survive during drier periods later on.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa oya bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ bei ni mli egbi babaoo mli yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why am I finding small holes in the center leaves of my young maize plants early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ leebi?

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are often caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which feed at night and early in the morning when it is cool. Checking the middle roll of the plant early helps you spot them before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni tsuɔ nii gbɛkɛ kɛ leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni ona amɛ dani amɛfite fãi ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: In hot afternoon heat, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it from the soil. If the leaves perk back up in the cool evening, the plant is fine; if they stay wilted, it could be a sign of disease in the roots.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ kwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, Tso lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji etee nɔ egbo lɛ, ekolɛ eji shishifã hela he okadi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather is too hot or when they do not get enough water. Extremely hot temperatures prevent the flowers from pollinating properly, causing the plant to shed them to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ nu koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Planting maize seeds too close together forces the plants to fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin plants with small or empty corn cobs instead of healthy, big cobs.
ga: Abele dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Moŋ lɛ, eji ŋmãa agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the stems and branches of my cocoa trees swelling up in some places?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛniji lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hei komɛi lɛ?

english: Swollen branches on cocoa trees are a sign of the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is carried from tree to tree by tiny insects called mealybugs. Infected trees produce fewer pods and must be removed to protect the rest of the farm.
ga: Cocoa tso niji ni efuu lɛ ji cocoa bud hela lɛ he okadi ni efuu. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs lɛ woɔ enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ koni abu ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: How can I tell when my yams are fully grown under the ground and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the green leaves and vines on top of the soil start turning yellow and drying up. This shows that the plant has stopped growing and has stored all its energy in the tuber below.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ miito ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dried grass help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around I duɔ mi ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dried grass, known as mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the earth. It traps moisture in the soil, keeps the roots cool, and gradually rots into natural food for your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni fiofio lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha onibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Applying organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer can help restore their dark green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ akɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekɛ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest when I plant maize on the exact same patch of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the ground time to recover. It also allows pests and soil diseases that feed on maize to build up in that field.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What is making small holes in the center leaves of my young maize, and why does it destroy the plant so quickly?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa gbekɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ Ni mɛni hewɔ egbeɔ tsei oya nɛkɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the fall armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep whorl of maize leaves to feed on soft tissue. Catching them early with recommended sprays or neem treatments prevents them from killing the growing point of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni ji cutworm caterpillars, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, neem tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbe tso lɛ hei ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the soil when the rains are heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater stays on the land for too long, it drowns the roots and creates wet conditions that allow rot fungi to attack the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my field?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani minine shɛɛɛ ŋmaa babaoo nɔ kɛjɛŋ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close actually reduces your total yield. When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other for water and nutrients, and their leaves shade each other from sunlight, leading to smaller plants and weaker harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi. Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to cut wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food. Guiding the leaves upward on stakes allows them to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large underground tubers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ wo tso ko nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ náa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I remove the extra young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Young plantain shoots steal water and nutrients from the main stem. By removing all but one or two strong shoots, the mother plant can direct all its energy into producing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Plantain bibii lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Tso nyɛ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cocoa plants need tall shade trees growing near them while they are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ? be mli ni eji bibioo lolo lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Tall shade trees act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa plants can survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my pepper plants keep them from dying during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛfataa mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ haaa amɛgboi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, shields the dirt from direct sun heat. It stops water from evaporating quickly and keeps the roots cool and moist.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ oya, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without turning into peppers during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When the weather gets extremely hot, pepper plants become stressed and cannot easily turn pollen into fruit. The plant drops its blossoms to save energy and protect itself until cooler weather returns.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsake pollen lɛ amɛfee aduawai mlɛo. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Do I need a flooded swamp field to grow rice in Ghana, or can I plant it on dry upland soil?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ ko ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia mi koni manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ Ghana? Aloo ani manyɛ makwɛ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ?

english: You can grow rice on dry upland soil as well as in flooded lowlands. Upland rice varieties are specifically bred to rely on rainfall, while lowland rice thrives in waterlogged areas. Choosing the right seed variety for your field type is what determines success.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ gɔŋ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Akwɛ ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa folo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu shwieɔ shi lɛ. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni sa kɛha oŋmɔ henɔ lɛ ni oooha lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ omanyeyeli.

english: Why do some people prefer local Ghanaian rice over imported rice, and how does it affect how I grow it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi sumɔɔ Ghana maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa fe ŋmãa ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ? Ni te enáa bɔ ni miduɔ nii mihaa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Local Ghanaian rice varieties are naturally adapted to the local climate and soil, often offering richer flavor and higher nutritional value. While they might require specific sun-drying and milling methods after harvest, they are often more resilient to local weather conditions.
ga: Ghana maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa henɔi srɔtoi Ejɛ adebɔɔ mli ekɛ ehe kpãa maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛfɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo. Eyɛ mli akɛ gbɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbiɔ hulutsoo be kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aba yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ moŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to produce green leaves. Heavy rains can wash nutrients out of the soil, so applying manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their dark green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers stress from extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to move pollen around. Keeping the soil moist and avoiding heavy chemical sprays that scare away bees will help the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ye dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ he amanehulu. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bɛ ni baajie pollen lɛ kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ owo ŋmeii lɛ ahe gbeyei lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: If I plant my cassava stems closer together, will I harvest more tubers?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe lɛ Ani mana yitsei babaoo?

english: Planting cassava too close together forces the plants to compete for light, water, and soil nutrients. This causes tall, thin stems with small tubers. Giving each plant enough space (about 1 meter apart) allows the roots room to expand into large tubers.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ha tso lɛ afee kakadaŋŋ ni efee mlɛo ni ehiɛ yitso bibioo. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa (aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe) lɛ, ehaa shishifã tsu lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmei agbo.

english: Why is burning the bushes on my farm before planting season bad for my crop yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ashãa dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: While burning clears the land fast, the heat destroys good soil organisms like earthworms and burns away organic matter that holds plant nutrients. Burning also leaves topsoil exposed, so rain easily washes away the fertile soil.
ga: Beni shãa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ oya lɛ, Dɔlɛ lɛ kpataa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni toɔ tsei amli niyenii lɛ. Shãa hu jieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kpo. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Why do small caterpillars show up to eat the middle leaves of my maize after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii baayeɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These are typically Fall Armyworms, which hatch quickly when warm weather follows rain. The adult moths lay eggs on the leaves, and the young caterpillars crawl into the central leaves (the whorl) where the plant is softest and easiest to eat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni fɔɔ oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Akpɔlɔi ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ (whorl) he ni tso lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ ni eyeli waaa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do birds only start attacking my rice field when the grains turn pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi jeɔ shishi amɛtutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: As rice matures, the grains fill with a soft, sweet liquid starch that hardens into rice grains. Birds target the crop during this 'milky stage' because the grains are soft, nutritious, and easy for them to eat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa ni mli tse ni mli ŋɔɔ ni mli wa ni etsɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa. Okpoi baakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ ‘miliki stage’ nɛɛ mli ejaakɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli yɛ blɛoo. niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni eyeli waaa

english: Saving seeds from hybrid crop harvests is not recommended because the seeds lose their hybrid strength in the second generation. Planting saved hybrid seeds results in uneven growth and lower yields compared to buying fresh certified seeds each season.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ ajie dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ akpamɔ mli ejaakɛ amɛbaafite tsofa ni akɛfee ekome lɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he hewalɛ ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why does my harvested rice spoil and smell moldy after I put it into bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔlɔ beni mikɛwo kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Rice spoils in storage when it is put into bags while still holding too much moisture. Trapped moisture allows mold and bacteria to grow quickly, so you must sun-dry your grains thoroughly until they are hard before packing them.
ga: Omɔ fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛ́ akɛwo kotoku ko ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo mli. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ daa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ogbi ŋmaa lɛ kɛyashi ebaawa dani okɛwo tsɔne mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive. In full sunlight, their delicate leaves get scorched and dry out quickly. Leaving mature shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa protects the young plants from harsh direct heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji akɛ hulu la ni fa lɛ fɛɛ ba lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu lɛ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and soft during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet and damp weather. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to move through the farm, drying off the pods and slowing down the disease.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa hela shishijee sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning light green and yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tips usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow fast, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or decomposed manure will help them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the soil well-aerated.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ baa.

english: Is it really necessary for me to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking yam vines lifts their leaves up into the sunlight so the plant can make more food. When leaves stay shaded on the ground, the plant cannot produce large, healthy yam tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la nɔ koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. Beni baai lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo shishi lolo lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants instead of forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences sudden water stress. When the plant gets stressed, it drops flowers to save energy and protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa. Kɛ tsei miihao Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite ni ebu ehe.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from the undersides of the leaves. Spraying with neem water or an appropriate insecticide controls these pests and protects the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do people recommend planting groundnuts or beans in the same farm with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer enriches the soil and helps nearby crops like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi tsɔne titri lɛ eje kpo.

english: If too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they steal food and water from the main tree. Leaving only two or three strong suckers allows the main plant to focus its energy on growing large bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ gbɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛfeee nɔ ko lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa jwɛi agbo ko ni ekwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my farm when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in soil moisture for plant roots to absorb it. Spreading fertilizer on dry soil can burn the roots and waste the fertilizer since the crop cannot take in dry chemical granules.
ga: Esa akɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli awo sũ mli nu mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the plant food responsible for deep green leaves and strong growth, so when the soil runs out, the plant takes nitrogen from its lower leaves to feed new growth, causing the older leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji tso lɛ niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ etee Tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai momo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does planting beans alongside my maize crop help my farm produce better?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. When planted with maize, they share this extra fertilizer naturally, helping the maize grow stronger without needing as much expensive commercial fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa Amɛbaajara ŋmãa krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ jarayeli ŋmãa ni jara wa waa atsu nii.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to strong direct sunlight and heat. Without shade crops like plantains or tree canopies to filter the sun and keep the ground cool, the delicate leaves dry out quickly and the plant loses more water than its small roots can absorb.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɛ lɛ, Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni tso lɛ fiteɔ nu babaoo fe eshishifãi bibii lɛ. lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the ground stays soaked with excess rainwater for days, air cannot reach the plant roots. The underground cassava tubers starve of oxygen and get attacked by soil fungi that thrive in wet conditions, leading to root rot.
ga: Beni nugbɔ nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ tsei shishifãi ahe. Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn crop suddenly filled with ragged holes and small brown dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni etse kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize foliage with tiny brown droppings inside the leaves are signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central leaf funnel during the day and chew through the emerging leaves as the plant tries to grow.
ga: Buji ni atse yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli ni ŋmãa bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Ni ooohi tsei lɛ amli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni miiba lɛ be mli ni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding on the leaf juices underneath, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. The damaged leaf tissue grows unevenly, causing it to roll up into small cups.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips, thrips, loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Baa lɛ mli fãji ni efite lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Ehaa efoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔpoo bibioo mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or water is inconsistent. Extreme heat stresses the plant, making pollen dry up so the flowers cannot form seeds, causing the plant to shed the blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ agbiɔ kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I plant my maize seeds too close together in a row?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo yɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This stress results in weak, thin stems and very small cobs because no single plant gets enough resources to form full grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ahaaa tso ko nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo dumɔwu ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why should I wait for rain or wet soil before applying my granular fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ dani mikɛ granular fertilizer awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so that plant roots can absorb the nutrients. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil leaves raw salts directly against the roots, which can draw moisture out of the plant and burn it.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei ni afee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ abɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli ni eha eshã.

english: Why do weeds harm my crop growth even when I put plenty of fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ awui lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo ŋmɔji lɛ amli moŋ.

english: Weeds are naturally tougher and grow faster than cultivated crops. When you add fertilizer without clearing weeds first, the weeds eat up the extra fertilizer faster than your crops can, growing bigger and taller to steal both soil nutrients and sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli ni ogbeee jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ Jwɛi lɛ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aye. ni ebaatsɔ shɔŋŋ ni eya shɔŋŋ koni eju sũ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la fɛɛ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my young crops when I clear all the grass and weeds from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ beni mijieɔ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When land is cleared completely bare, there are no plant roots or leaf cover to slow down rain. Heavy rainwater rushes quickly across the bare ground, carrying away topsoil, seeds, and young plants instead of soaking into the dirt.
ga: Kɛji ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse lɛ, tsei shishifãi loo baai komɛi bɛ ni baaha nugbɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ, dumɔwui, kɛ tsei bibii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: How can I make shallow water channels on my farm to direct rainwater away from my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee nubu ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛjie nugbɔ nu kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli?

english: You can dig shallow ditches called drainage furrows along the edges of your fields, following the natural slope of the land. These furrows collect excess rainwater and safely lead it away from your planting areas before it causes flooding.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nubu ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ nu homɔ ŋshɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anaa, ni nyiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ buaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe dani nu afua baa.

english: What happens to crop roots when rainwater sits on my field for many hours after a storm?
ga: Mɛni baa shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo yɛ ahum ko sɛɛ?

english: Crop roots need air just like humans do. When rainwater sits on the soil for too long without draining, it cuts off the oxygen supply, causing the roots to drown, rot, and turn yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi hu he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli lɛ ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ mli lɛ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough water after the first rain for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni manyɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi?

english: Scoop up a handful of soil from a few inches deep and squeeze it in your hand. If it forms a soft ball that holds together without water dripping out, the ground has enough moisture for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ sũ ni mli kwɔ fioo ko kɛjɛ mli ni okɛmimɔ oniji amli. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops look wilted even when there is standing rainwater on top of the farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: When the soil is completely soaked and flooded, the damaged roots can no longer absorb water or nutrients properly. As a result, the crop starves and wilts despite being surrounded by water.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu loo niyenii kpakpa dɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nu ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: What can I cover my soil with after clearing land so the heavy rain does not ruin the earth?
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii agbe naa lɛ, mɛni abaanyɛ akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? No hewɔ lɛ nakai nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: You can cover the soil with dead leaves, grass, or crop stalks (called mulching). This protective layer breaks the impact of falling raindrops, slows down flowing water, and helps the soil absorb moisture gently.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ baai, jwɛi, loo tso shishifãi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Nɛkɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he nɛɛ fiteɔ nibii ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ feɔ lɛ. Ha nu lɛ atsɔ blɛoo ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ atsu nii blɛoo

english: Why should I build a small covered shelter on my farm before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa shĩa bibioo ko? Yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi?

english: A dry farm shelter gives you a safe place to store harvested crops, seeds, and tools during sudden rainstorms, preventing your harvest from rotting or getting ruined by moisture.
ga: Okwaafoi ashihilɛhei ni egbi lɛ haa onáa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, dumɔwui, kɛ nibii ni akpa lɛ ato yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ mli. Etsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkafite loo ŋmɔtɔ akafite amɛ.

english: Why is it a bad idea to put fertilizer on my crops right before a big rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain water moving across the ground will wash loose fertilizer off the field before the plants can absorb it, wasting your money and leaving your crops without food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ahe dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Efiteɔ shika ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do large trees on my farm survive heavy flooding while my maize plants easily fall over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ wala yɛ nu afua ni naa wa mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo lɛ?

english: Large trees have deep, woody taproots that anchor them deep into the soil and absorb water slowly. Maize has shallow roots near the surface, which get easily loosened and uprooted when topsoil becomes muddy and wet.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni tamɔ tsei ni ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛmɔɔ nu blɛoo. Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Amɛbaagbee shi oya ni amɛbaashishifãi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ batsɔ muji ni edɔ.

english: How long does it take for rain to soak deep into cleared soil compared to land covered in bushes?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse mli shɔŋŋ? Kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni tsei bibii ehà nɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: On land covered with bushes, rain soaks into the soil almost immediately because roots create pathways for water. On cleared, packed soil, water stays on top and moves slowly across the surface, taking hours to soak in deeply.
ga: Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni jwɛi ehà nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aaafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ gbɛ kɛhaa nu. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni mli edɔ nɔ Nu lɛ hiɔ ŋwɛi ni eyaa blɛoo. across the surface Eheɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo dani eboteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa waa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to make leaves green and healthy. Adding compost or proper fertilizer gives the soil the nitrogen it needs to make the leaves green again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I have to use wooden stakes to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso atsu nii koni mikɛwo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up toward the sun to make food for the tubers. Lifting the vines off the ground also stops wet soil from causing rot and disease on the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ ewo ebaa lɛ nɔ koni hulu lɛ ajie ehe kpo bɔni afee ni eha bulb lɛ niyenii. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai aba baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts or beans on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a family of crops that trap nutrient-rich nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize afterward, the maize feeds on those natural nutrients left behind.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baaye adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop manage to stay green and grow even when rain does not fall for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko otsii babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep roots that reach deep underground for hidden water, and it can shed some of its leaves during dry periods to conserve moisture until rain returns.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni ekɛ nu ato. Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwie amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save seeds from my current maize harvest to plant for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from harvested crops lose their strength over generations, leading to smaller yields and weaker plants. Certified fresh seeds are specifically prepared to grow strong, resist local diseases, and produce heavy yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi. Afee dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ he gbɛjianɔ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ waa. helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo

english: How do weeds harm my crops if there is plenty of soil for all of them?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha amɛ fɛɛ lɛ yɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that act like thiefs on your farm. They quickly steal the fertilizer, sunlight, and water meant for your crops, causing your crops to grow weak and small.
ga: Jwɛi ji jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, hulu la, kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant feels stressed by extreme hot weather, dry soil, or a lack of essential soil nutrients. Giving the plants consistent water and shade during intense heat helps flowers stay on and produce fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wither and die when water sits pooled around them after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu ebɔle amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air underground just like humans need air to breathe. When rain water forms ponds on your farm and cannot drain away, it cuts off air to the roots, causing them to drown and rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi. Taakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa adesai koni amɛmu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ nubu ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli lɛ. Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ.

english: Why is it better to clear bush grass by hand instead of burning it off before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ akɛ nine baakpa jwɛi moŋ fe ni oooshã dani odu lɛ?

english: Burning grass destroys valuable organic material that feeds the soil and kills good insects like earthworms. Leaving cut grass to decompose creates natural compost that keeps soil rich and retains rain water.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ, ni egbeɔ kooloi kpakpai tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii. Jwɛi ni afo lɛ ni ashiɔ koni egbo lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli.

english: Why does my land produce a smaller yield when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?
