english: Crops like maize take specific nutrients out of the soil each season. Planting the same crop on the same spot continuously drains those specific nutrients without giving the soil time to replenish, which leads to weak growth and lower harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ atsɔ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛwo mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but producing very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant puts most of its energy into growing top leaves and stems rather than storing starch in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eŋwɛi baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing from the bottom leaves upward usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. The plant moves the limited nitrogen it has from older, lower leaves to feed the young leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my field?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani minine shɛɛɛ ŋmaa babaoo nɔ kɛjɛŋ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close forces your crops to compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants that yield smaller grains or fruits overall.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ dumɔwui bibii loo aduawai fɛɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops so quickly even when there is enough rainfall for everyone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miitutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha mɔ fɛɛ mɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most domesticated crops, allowing them to steal essential soil nutrients and sunlight before your crops can use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe shia tsei babaoo. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni he hiaa kɛ hulu la dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea ni mikɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means they can take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer in the soil, sharing useful plant food with nearby maize.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ abaanyɛ ajie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni atsake lɛ afee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ tsei niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni akɛ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ jaa nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground when there is heavy rain late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Excessive water fills up air gaps in the soil, preventing root tubers from breathing and creating a damp environment where rot-causing fungi thrive.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ baanyɛ adara yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any tomatoes form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or lack of consistent water stresses the plant, causing it to shed flowers to save energy and protect its own survival rather than produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ daa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛbu amɛwala he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves when the hot dry wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi bɔi tswaa lɛ?

english: The dry wind pulls moisture out of cocoa leaves faster than the roots can drink from the dry ground, forcing the tree to drop leaves to prevent complete dehydration.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafo emli kwraa.

english: Why are small worms hiding inside the central leaves of my young maize plants and chewing holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm target the tender central leaves of young maize because those growing shoots are soft, sweet, and rich in nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli ŋɔɔ, ni amɛmli niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen. The maize plant automatically moves nutrients from its older bottom leaves up to the younger top leaves to keep growing, leaving the lower ones to starve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay thin and woody even after staying in the ground for over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei yɛ be mli ni mikɛ nɔ ni fe afi po ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to expand if the soil is too hard and compact, or if the soil lacks potassium. Hard soil physically stops roots from swelling, while potassium is the main nutrient cassava uses to store starch.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ alɛɛ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium Shikpɔŋ ni wa yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Yɛ be mli ni potassium ji niyenii titri ni ŋmei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛtoɔ ŋmei.

english: Why do my bean plants grow plenty of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Giving crop plants too much nitrogen causes them to put all their energy into leafy foliage instead of flowering. Beans need balanced nutrients, especially phosphorus, to trigger flower and pod formation.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha efite ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ tsei ahe tsei ahe moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi. Nuts he miihia niyenii ni ja. titri lɛ fɔsfɔs Koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii afeemɔ mli hewalɛ

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and cool conditions. When cocoa trees are planted too closely or not pruned, sunlight and air cannot dry out the wet pods, allowing the fungus to grow.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ, ni jɛmɛ ejɔ kɛji adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ loo afolɔɔɔ amɛ. Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haŋ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ adara.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling up and turning twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites, or a virus they transmit. The feeding damages leaf tissues, causing them to curl up and restrict plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Niyenii fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize stalks break and fall over easily before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa oya ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Weak stalks occur when plants are crowded too closely together and compete for sunlight, or when pests like stem borers tunnel inside the stalk, weakening its structural strength against wind.
ga: Tsoi ni bɛ hewalɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛmiitswa hulu la he akaŋ. aloo be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii shwieɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hewalɛ ni tsũ lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛteɔ shi ewoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up completely before the rainy season is over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi kwraa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa naagbee lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines is often caused by fungal leaf spot diseases or underground microscopic worms called nematodes that attack the root system, preventing the plant from absorbing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal leaf spot hela loo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ, ni haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni miduuu tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when temperatures get extremely high or when the soil dries out completely. Heat and drought stress prevent proper pollination, forcing the plant to drop flowers to save water.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ haomɔ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees shed most of their leaves when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during severe dry spells as a natural survival mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation, helping the main stem stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ehiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit when planted under tall shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Plantains require full sunlight to produce the energy needed for fast growth. Heavy shade slows down their growth rate and delays fruit production because the crop cannot perform enough photosynthesis.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia plantains koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya. Shade ni mli wa lɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi ni ehaa aduawai ni anáa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee fotosintɛsis bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, a key food in the soil that keeps leaves green, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava sticks too close to each other on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to tall, thin stems with very small tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bulbs bibii waa yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops wilt and droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil was damp in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi po

english: Crops lose water through their leaves faster under the hot sun than their roots can drink from the soil, so they droop temporarily to save moisture until the air cools down.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, no hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: How do I tell if the holes in my pepper leaves are caused by insects or a disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ kooloi loo helai ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ pepper baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Holes with clean, chewed edges are caused by insects eating the leaves, while dark spots that dry up and fall out leaving brown-ringed holes are caused by diseases like fungi or bacteria.
ga: Bu ko ni ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli tse ni atsɔ mli. Kplukai ni yeɔ baai lɛ kɛbaa He ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ mli egbi ni egbeeɔ shi. Helai tamɔ ŋmei loo helatsɛmɛi amli buji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops when I plant on the same plot year after year without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ beni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Planting on the same land every season drains the specific foods that crops need to grow, leaving the soil tired and weak unless you rest the land or put organic matter back into it.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa Seasons lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sũ lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni egbɔjɔɔ. Ja okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli efata he ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it good for my main crop if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts trap natural plant food from the air and put it into the soil, which helps feed neighboring crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔ̃ɔ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ niyenii haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of yellow flowers but no tomatoes are forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo shi tomato ko bɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers fail to turn into fruit when extreme heat destroys the pollen, or when there are no beneficial insects like bees around to move the pollen within the flower.
ga: Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee aduawai kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpata fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, bɛ he fɛɛ he koni amɛtsi pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than the crops I planted after clearing my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally tough and can sleep in the soil for years, ready to sprout instantly and drink up water and fertilizer before your planted crops have time to grow roots.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Efee klalo akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni enu nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani tso lɛ aná be ni ekɛ shishifãi akwɛ̃.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantain trees planted next to them during their first few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii amli yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight, so broad-leaf plants like plantains provide living umbrellas that shelter the young cocoa and keep the surrounding soil cool.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ tamɔ plantain lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔlɔ aha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli ajɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise cutting off cassava stems a few days before digging up the tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afolɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ gbii 2-3 dani akumɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cutting the stems signals to the plant to stop sending energy to its leaves and instead lock nutrients into the underground tubers, helping the cassava stay fresh longer after harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ ekpa hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa baa lɛ mli lɛ, ni no najiaŋ lɛ, emɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa cassava ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: High afternoon heat or too much leaf fertilizer can cause tomato plants to drop their flowers. When it gets too hot, the pollen dries up, so the flowers cannot form tomatoes and drop off.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ afɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ lɛ Pollen lɛ baagbi. Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ afee tomato ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. The plant wilts to protect itself from heat, but it usually recovers by evening when temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tsei gboɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɛɔ shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why does my yam plant need a tall wooden stake to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground to prevent rot and helps the plant produce more energy to grow bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni akafite, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo baa koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants leaves turn brown and drop when there are no shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight. Without shade from trees like plantains, the harsh sun burns their leaves and dries out the young plant.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei tamɔ plantains lɛ ahe hulutsoo bɛ lɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ agbi.

english: Why do cowpea plants make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina tsei baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plant harvest is done, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as natural food for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbe naa Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden eggs developing a white dust on top of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ sũ yɛŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This white dust is a fungal sickness called powdery mildew. It happens when plants are packed too closely together and moist air gets trapped around the leaves without good air flow.
ga: Nɛkɛ sũ yɛŋ nɛɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Ebaa kɛji akɛ akɛ tsei ebɔ amɛhe tsɔ. ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ baai lɛ ahe ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa eyaaa mli.

english: Why do I see small chewed holes all over the leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ani okɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day and feed on the young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow pale and skinny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that quickly steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, leaving your plants starving and weak.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ oya. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: How do I know if my cassava tubers are mature underground without digging them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ amɛ efoŋ?

english: When cassava is ready for harvest, the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, the main stem thickens, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Tso lɛ mli tsɔne titri lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why is it risky to plant my maize seeds before the major rains fully begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: If seeds get only a small amount of early rain, they will open up and start to grow, but if the rain stops for several days, the hot dry soil will dry out and kill the young sprout.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ná nugbɔ fioo pɛ mra lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baagbi ni ebaanyɛ egbe tsei bibii.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying fertilizer or compost around the base will help feed the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii baawo Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni eye ebua tso lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow much better when I plant beans on a field where I planted maize last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwere jogbaŋŋ waa beni midu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni midu ŋmeii yɛ mli nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are special crops that capture good nutrients from the air and put them back into the soil. When you plant them, they naturally fertilize the farm for the next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni buaa niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu amɛ Amɛbaaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from under the leaves. Spraying early with neem water or organic pesticide gets rid of them before they stop the plant from bearing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ neem nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ baashwie nɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ dani amɛtsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii.

english: Why do small black bugs destroy my harvested maize even when I keep it inside a closed bag?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji miifite mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛwoɔ kotoku ko mli moŋ?

english: Maize weevils often lay tiny hidden eggs in the corn while it is still in the field. If the grain is not dried very well before bagging, those eggs hatch inside the bag and eat the corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. Akɛtee ŋmãa lɛ mli be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko dani awo amɛ kotoku mli Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, rotten spots at the bottom while still on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the plant doesn't get enough calcium or when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant take up the nutrients it needs to build healthy fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔ amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ mishi ŋmeii bibii ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ

english: The young shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plant for food and water in the soil. Cutting away extra suckers and leaving only one or two allows the mother plant to focus all its energy on making big bunches.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii agbo feemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their small flowers before any pods grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Bei pii lɛ dani pods lɛ baadara?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers if they don't have enough water, shade, or pollinators like tiny midges. Providing good shade trees and keeping the soil moist helps more flowers turn into full cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nu, hulutsoo loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi tamɔ midges bɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kpakpa haa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe kwraa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can tell cassava is ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the roots expand beneath.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ yucca lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: The first rain is often a false start, followed by a long dry spell. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout and then dry up and die before the real rainy season begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs in its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn when there is no shade on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa be mli ni hulutsoo bɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because intense direct sunlight causes them to lose moisture faster than their roots can absorb it, burning the leaves and stress-killing the plant.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa amɛhe shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni ehaa tso lɛ haoɔ.

english: Why should I plant cassava and maize together on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly underground, allowing you to maximize land space and get two separate harvests without the crops crowding each other.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwereɔ babaoo ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ baa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ amɛhe.

english: Why does my maize turn yellow and stop growing when water stays on my field after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa kwɛ̃mɔ beni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like they need water; flooded soil cuts off oxygen to the roots, causing them to drown, rot, and stop feeding the plant.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛkpaa tso lɛ niyenii hamɔ.

english: How do I know if my soil is weak and needs manure before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli dani madu nii?

english: If your previous crop leaves looked pale green or yellow, grew very slowly, or yielded small harvests despite receiving enough rain, the soil has run out of key nutrients and needs manure or compost.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsei ni okɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ ahe baai lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ, amɛdaraa blɛoo waa, loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do armyworms attack my maize farm more when there is a dry spell during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths lay eggs rapidly in warm, dry weather, whereas heavy rain naturally washes away young caterpillars and drowns them inside the maize leaves.
ga: Fɛ̃i be mli ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛboteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies; infected leaves cannot make enough food for the plant, leading to small, stunted tubers.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela, ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Baai ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa aha tso lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni egbɔjɔ baa.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings fall over and rot at the stem right after sprouting in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is a fungal attack known as 'damping-off,' which happens when nursery beds are kept too wet with low airflow, causing tender stems at ground level to rot.
ga: Enɛ ji fungal attack ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Damping’, ni baa kɛji akɛ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔ saatso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ faaa Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Extreme heat makes pollen sterile, preventing flowers from fertilizing and setting fruit, so the plant sheds the unfertilized flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa pollen lɛ feɔ nɔ ni bɛ fɔmɔ nii. Etsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo fɔmɔ nii ni amɛwo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do seeds saved from my harvested maize give me lower yields than packaged hybrid seeds from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni akɛwo kotoku mli ni jɛɔ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially cross-bred for maximum yield in their first planting, but seeds saved from that harvest lose those high-performing traits in the next generation.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ woɔ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ mli. Shi dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite nakai sui ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines and leaves dry up completely before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ egbi kwraa dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: This natural drying up means the yam plant has finished storing energy into the underground tuber and has reached full maturity, signaling that it is ready for harvest.
ga: Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato tsei lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni amɛtoɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ naa. ni eda kwraa Otsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes or frames to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso loo trellis ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight. Setting up wooden stakes or frames lifts the leaves higher off the ground, allowing the plant to catch full sunlight and make enough food to produce large tubers under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Tso loo ŋtayaa baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fa. ni amɛfee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off some of the lower branches from my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifo mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or overcrowded branches so air and sunlight can reach all parts of the tree. This prevents diseases from spreading and encourages the tree to put its energy into producing bigger fruits.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ haaa hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã, ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ awo yibii wuji.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. Shade trees act as a screen against intense heat and help keep moisture in the soil until the young cocoa trees are mature enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ.

english: Is it helpful to plant plantains on the same farm where I am growing young tree crops?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ makwɛ plantains yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ tsei bibii yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, plantains grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that provide good shade for young seedlings like cocoa or citrus. They also give you food and income while you wait for your main tree crops to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ehaa baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa tsei bibii tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmeii lɛ náa ŋmɔlɔ kpakpa. Amɛhaa bo niyenii kɛ shika hu yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ otso titri lɛ ni eda lɛ.

english: Why should I measure space between my pepper plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu gbɛ ni kã pepper tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ he moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When pepper plants are crowded together, they struggle against each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow strong branches and yield more peppers.
ga: Kɛji abua pepper tsei anaa yɛ kui amli Amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eniji lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my food crops right after clearing the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miniyenii tsei lɛ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with very strong root systems that can easily steal plant food and water from the soil. Clearing them early gives your main crops a fair chance to take root without being choked.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli wa waa ni baanyɛ aju tsei aniyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii titri lɛ aná hegbɛ ni ewo shishifãi ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ akafo mli.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my vegetable beds with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the soil too fast, keeps the roots cool during hot days, and prevents unwanted weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha hulu lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ naa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry conditions to reduce water loss and protect themselves from drying out completely. Once the rains return, the plant quickly grows fresh leaves and continues growing.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛkagbi kwraa. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often shed their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when they lack consistent water. Keeping the soil evenly moist and giving plants light shade can help the flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu bɛ mli daa. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni aha tso lɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller maize harvests every year if I plant maize on the same plot repeatedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize on the same land every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts restores fertility and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni Seasons lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why does my land seem to lose its power to grow good crops after a few seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ bei fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops pull natural nutrients out of the soil each time they grow. Without adding fertilizer or manure back into the land, the soil runs out of plant food, causing future crops to grow weak.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni adu amɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii efataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my maize so it grows strong?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmã awo ŋmã mli koni ehi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Maize needs fertilizer early when it is a few weeks old to build strong roots, and again when it is knee-high to build energy for forming big, healthy cobs.
ga: Abele he miihia mra be mli ni eye otsii 2-3 koni shishifãi ni wa aba. Ni agbɛnɛ hu, kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ shɛ aaafee tsitsi nɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ni ekɛfee ŋmãa agbo ni mli wa.

english: How does knowing what type of land I have help me choose the right fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ̃ ni miyɔɔ lɛ ni mile lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni mihalaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa?

english: Different types of soil hold water and plant food differently. Understanding your soil helps you pick the exact fertilizer mix your land is missing rather than wasting money on the wrong type.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni shikpɔŋ henɔ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ toɔ nu kɛ tsei ahe niyenii. Kɛ́ onu oshikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni elaaje lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite shika kɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient it needs from the soil or fertilizer to stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my crops are thriving or if they are struggling to grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ loo amɛmiibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Thriving crops grow steadily with firm green leaves and sturdy stems, while struggling crops remain short, get discolored or curled leaves, and wilt easily.
ga: Tsei ni shwereɔ lɛ baaya nɔ ada kɛ baai eŋɔli ni wa kɛ tsei ni wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni miitao lɛ baakã he ahi shi kuku. Baai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni egboɔ oya

english: Why does my maize grow tall but still produce small or empty cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa shi ewoɔ dumɔwui bibii lolo lɛ? Aloo pod ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli?

english: A maize plant can grow tall with just water and sunlight, but it needs rich soil nutrients like phosphorus and nitrogen at the flowering stage to fill out full, heavy cobs.
ga: Abɛi baanyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ hulu la pɛ nɔ. Shi ehe miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa babaoo tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ nitrogen yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do weeds on my farm cause my crops to produce less food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo niyenii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops, leaving your plants with less food and energy to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What does spraying chemical treatments actually do to help my crops thrive?
ga: Mɛɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ ni mitsei lɛ daraa?

english: Spraying protects crops by killing insects and diseases that chew on leaves and stems, allowing the plant to focus all its energy on healthy growth.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni shwieɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ni egbeɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ maa dalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ.

english: Why do tiny insects cause my crop leaves to curl up and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiha mitso lɛ baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Pest insects pierce the leaves and suck out the liquid sap inside, which starves the leaf of moisture and nutrients, causing it to curl and dry up.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ boteɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛmuɔ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ akaná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii. Ha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi.

english: Why is it important for me to wear boots and long overalls when spraying my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo atadei kɛ atadei ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa miifɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop protection chemicals can soak through ordinary clothes and harm your skin or health, so protective boots and overalls keep dangerous liquid off your body.
ga: Tsofai ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ baanyɛ abote atadei folo amli ni eye ohewolo loo ohewalɛ nɔ awui. No hewɔ lɛ, bɔɔtu kɛ atadei ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ baaha nu ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akashɛ ogbɔmɔtso lɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient plant roots need to make green leaves and build strong stalks. It can also happen when the soil stays too wet for long periods, which smothers the roots and prevents them from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Tso shishifãi haa niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni ehaaa amɛye nii.

english: Why is my cassava growing huge green leaves above ground, but the tubers underneath remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibioo lolo?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in extremely rich soil, it spends all its energy producing leaves and stems instead of storage roots. To get large tubers, cassava needs balanced soil nutrients with plenty of potassium and soft, well-drained soil.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei yɔɔ nɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ tsei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ shishifãi baato. koni ená yitso agbo lɛ, ehe miihia ni Cassava aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛfata he lɛ, potassium babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ fata he.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the plant without ever growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot and dry or when the soil lacks steady moisture. Under severe heat or water stress, the plant cannot support fruiting and sheds its flowers to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ be fɛɛ be Yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ shishi Tsei nyɛŋ aŋmɛ yibiiwoo ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and droop during hot afternoons but look healthy again in the early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli shi ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛ hewalɛ leebi lɛ?

english: In the intense afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water through evaporation faster than the roots can drink it from the soil, causing temporary wilting. Over the cooler night, the roots catch up and refill the plant with water so it stands firm by morning.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli Gbi gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baaje kpo ni amɛkɛ nu awo tso lɛ mli bɔni afee ni edamɔ shi leebi.

english: Why am I advised to plant plantains on the same land where I am establishing new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei heei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and feature broad leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa plants until they grow sturdy enough for full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant the seeds too close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Planting maize too close causes the individual plants to compete aggressively with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This overcrowding produces tall, thin stalks with small or empty cobs, resulting in a smaller total harvest.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso kɛ ehe woɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ fe nine nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fɛɛ ni baa shi.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to hide deep inside the funnel of my young maize leaves and eat holes in them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mli?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, pests that prefer feeding on the tender, new foliage inside the central whorl of the maize plant. Catching them early with appropriate organic or chemical controls keeps them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra kɛtsɔ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning light yellow and green in patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This pattern is a symptom of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a plant virus spread by tiny whiteflies or by planting infected stem cuttings. Using disease-resistant cassava stems and controlling whiteflies keeps your crop healthy.
ga: Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. aloo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ adumɔ nɔ Okɛ ŋmeii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛ whitefly he nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do weeds growing near my crops actually reduce the amount of food I harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni miduɔ nii lɛ masɛi lɛ haa niyenii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop's root zone. Because weeds naturally grow faster and stronger, they shade out young crops and stunt their development if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hia, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa. Amɛhaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛdalɛ naa kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Why do hybrid seeds bought from the store yield more crops than seeds I save from last season's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ nyɔŋ ni ho lɛ mli kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to combine strong traits like disease resistance, drought tolerance, and high yields. When you replant seeds saved from a hybrid crop, those special genetic traits break down, leading to weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni akɛ sui ni mli wa tamɔ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ lɛ afata he. Hɔmɔ he tsuishitoo kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli. Nakai fɔmɔ sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ baafite. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: How can I tell if the crop seeds given to me are good quality before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛhaa mi lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani madu?

english: Good quality seeds are uniform in size, clean, free from insect holes or mold, and come certified by recognized agricultural authorities to ensure high germination.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe, amɛhe tse, ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bɛ mli. ni okwaayeli nitsumɔhe ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ eha he odaseyeli koni ekwɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What should I do if certified seeds given to farmers fail to perform well in my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛhaa okwaafoi lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should report the seed batch to your agricultural extension officer so they can test the seed quality and stop distributing poor performing varieties to other farmers.
ga: Esa akɛ obɔ dumɔwui akuu lɛ he amaniɛ otsɔɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛka amɛdumɔwui lɛ amɛkwɛ ni amɛkpa dumɔwui srɔtoi ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahɔ̃ɔmɔ amɛhaa okwaafoi krokomɛi.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer says a tomato variety is 'cross-bred'?
ga: Kɛji akɛ extension nitsulɔ ko kɛɛ tomato henɔ ko ji ‘hybrid’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: A cross-bred tomato comes from intentionally joining two different parent tomato plants with good traits, like disease resistance and high yield, to produce a stronger crop.
ga: Akɛ tomato tsei enyɔ ni hiɛ sui kpakpai tamɔ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ kɛ yibii babaoo ni amɛwoɔ lɛ feɔ ekome kɛfeɔ tomato ni ji hybrid lɛ. bɔni afee ni aná yibiiwoo ni mli wa

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested cross-bred tomatoes to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid tomato ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato ni madu amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is best not to save seeds from cross-bred tomatoes because the new plants will not grow uniform tomatoes and will lose the strong qualities of the original harvest.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tomato ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ akahere ejaakɛ tsei heei lɛ ekwɛŋ tomato ni yaa nɔ daa, ni amɛbaafite sui ni mli wa ni yɔɔ shishijee ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Are cross-bred tomato seeds safe to plant on my farmland?
ga: Ani tomato dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaadu yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, cross-bred seeds are completely safe; they are developed through natural pollination methods to help farmers get better yields and healthier plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa. Akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ tsu nii kɛfee amɛ koni eye ebua okwaafoi ni amɛná yibii kpakpai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do cross-bred crop varieties often grow better than traditional local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ?

english: Cross-bred crops inherit the best qualities from two selected parent plants, making them better equipped to resist local diseases, pests, and harsh weather conditions.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwo mli lɛ yeɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni ahala lɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ gboshinii, ni no haa amɛhe esa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ.

english: How do tomato plants pollinate and produce seeds without mating like livestock?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tomato tsei lɛ feɔ pollin ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni amɛkɛ amɛhe wooo mli tamɔ kooloi?

english: Tomato plants reproduce through flowers where wind or insects transfer tiny grains called pollen from one flower to another to form fruits containing seeds.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ bii kɛtsɔɔ fɔfɔi anɔ. he ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii tsɔɔ dumɔwui bibii No ji nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli koni efee aduawai ni dumɔwui yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but very few actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers need proper pollination to make fruit, and extreme heat, heavy rains, or a lack of pollinating insects can cause the flowers to fall off before fruiting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ biɔ ni aná pollination ni sa koni amɛwo yibii. Ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo kooloi bibii ni shɛɛɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo dani amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I stop two different crop varieties planted near each other from crossing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsei srɔtoi enyɔ ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ anaa koni amɛkafɔ amɛhe?

english: You can prevent unwanted crossing by leaving sufficient distance between the two crop fields or planting them at different times so they do not flower together.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsĩ ŋmɔji amli fomɔ naa kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni oooshi yɛ ŋmɔji enyɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo dumɔ amɛ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli koni amɛkawo fɔfɔi yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do some tomato varieties ripen early while others take a longer time on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato komɛi shwereɔ oya ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ be babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Different tomato varieties have different growth cycles coded in their nature, meaning some are naturally bred for quick harvesting while others need more time to mature.
ga: Tomato henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ bɔ ni edaraa ehaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ajɛɔ adebɔɔ mli afɔɔ tomato henɔi komɛi koni amɛkpa oya. Yɛ be mli ni tomato komɛi biɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow from the tips downwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost to the soil helps the leaves regain their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave dried crop leaves and straw on top of my field soil instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi kɛ jwɛi yɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã lɛ?

english: Leaving organic materials on the soil acts as mulch, which keeps the ground cool, preserves moisture during hot dry spells, prevents weed growth, and gradually breaks down into natural fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Kwɛmɔ ni fɛ̃i ahi shi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a cleared, open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and heat. Planting companion crops like plantains provides necessary shade and moisture protection during the cocoa tree's early growth stages.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hebuu ni he hiaa yɛ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa mra lɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves with sawdust-like material in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ nɔ ko tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the soft leaves inside the whorl. Early detection and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem-based treatments can control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni abaanyɛ akudɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excessive water collects around them in compacted soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges creates drainage pathways so water moves away and roots remain healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli Kɛ́ aduɔ ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa he kroko ni shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high above the ground to capture maximum sunlight for tuber development. Staking also prevents leaves from rotting on damp soil and reduces ground-based fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha tuber lɛ shweremɔ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do agricultural officers suggest planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally enriches the soil with nutrients that feed the neighboring maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from extreme heat helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when weeds grow close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhe waaa be mli ni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing weeds early ensures that your main crops get all the resources they need to grow thick and productive.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ babaoo ni ewo yibii.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow causes them to compete with the main plant for nutrients and water, resulting in smaller plantain bunches. Pruning down to two or three strong suckers focuses energy on producing larger fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha hewalɛ ahi aduawai wuji ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living shade and traps soil moisture, protecting the young cocoa plants until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Does it matter which direction I insert cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upward. Planting them upside down forces the plant to waste energy re-orienting its shoots, leading to lower yields and weak root growth.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmei lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ tso lɛ daa kɛtee shishi lɛ, ehaa efiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ bɔ ni tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ yaa lɛ tsakemɔ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni shishifãi lɛ hu waaa.

english: Why do I need to clear small shoots around my main plantain stem instead of letting them all grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijaraa tsei bibii ni bɔleɔ plantain tso wulu lɛ he lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã amɛ fɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ekomekomei lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one plantain stem creates competition for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant produces large, healthy bunches.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Plantain kome pɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ to lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ yibii wuji ni he wa.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to build green leaf tissue, so when soil nutrients are low, the plant moves available nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛfee baa eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and shrinking into small clusters?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the sap and transmitting viruses. Managing these pests early prevents stunted plant growth and poor yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ yibiiwoo ni ehiii lɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off unpollinated when weather temperatures get excessively hot or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly. Keeping soil moisture consistent with mulch helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni pollination bɛ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ waa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akɛ mulch tsuɔ nii daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ shi.

english: Why do groundnut plants push their flowers into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts bloom above ground, but once pollinated, the flower stalks bend downward and push themselves into the dirt. The soil provides the dark, protected environment needed for the seed pods to develop.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ ashɛre pollination lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ, ni abuɔ he ni he hiaa kɛha dumɔwui akui lɛ akwɛmɔ.

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to maximum sunlight for food production while keeping foliage off wet soil, which prevents leaf rot diseases and encourages bigger tuber growth under ground.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, tsi sweet potato baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baa lɛ fiteɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, high-humidity weather. Pruning dense branches and clearing weeds improves airflow and sunlight, helping dry out the pods and prevent rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ egbiɔ ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea crop heavily right when the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ waa kɛ́ amɛbɔi fɔmɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar that attracts pests like thrips and pod borers. Inspecting fields early and using safe crop protection just before flowering safeguards the blossoms so pods can form.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ nu ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii dani fɔfɔi lɛ baawo lɛ baabu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni pods lɛ anyɛ afee.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die if I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves are thin and lose water quickly. They need shade crops like plantains to act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and the air cool until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpee hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ amli tseee, ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves when the dry harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is the cassava plant's natural defense mechanism against severe dry weather. By shedding its leaves, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation and survives in a resting state until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji ŋmei tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aba nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ, ni ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency or waterlogged roots. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the maize plant takes whatever nitrogen it has left in its older, bottom leaves and sends it up to keep the young top leaves growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa loo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji nitrogen fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Abɛi baaŋɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli ni ekɛmaje ŋwɛi koni ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: Why does cassava grow well in poor, dry soil where my maize crop fails completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ehiii nɔ aahu akɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Cassava has a very deep, tough root system that can search for water far below the surface, and it stores extra food in its thick roots. Maize has shallow roots and requires rich soil with regular rain to produce good yields.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni wa waa. ni baanyɛ ana nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛ niyenii ni fa fe nine ato shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ amli Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my groundnut flower stems bend down and push themselves into the dirt after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts develop their seeds underground to protect them from heat and pests. Once the yellow flower is pollinated, the stem grows downward into the soil so the nut can safely form and ripen under the dirt.
ga: Peanuts lɛ woɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ wo ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ anyɛ afee ni ekwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why does my plantain tree give very small bunches if I let many small shoots grow around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji miha ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwere lɛ? Ani oooda yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he?

english: The small shoots (suckers) compete with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong shoots, allowing the main stem to send all its energy into making a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ (tso lɛ) kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwɛɔ, ni no haa ŋmeii titri lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without producing any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: High heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from being fertilized. When pollination fails, the plant naturally drops the useless flower to save its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baafite pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaaa enyɛŋ ekɛ fɔmɔ awo mli Kɛ́ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni wooo yibii lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking into small shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by viruses spread by sap-sucking insects that stop the leaves from expanding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tall rice plants fall flat to the ground right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ miigbee shikpɔŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: This issue is called lodging. It happens when rice stems become too weak to hold up heavy grain heads, often caused by applying too much nitrogen fertilizer, planting seeds too close together, or heavy winds.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ wɔɔhe. Ebaa beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli

english: Why do my yam vines produce tiny tubers if I let weeds cover the mounds during the early season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji miha jwɛi lɛ ha gɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra?

english: Yam vines need direct sunshine on their leaves to produce the food needed to grow big tubers below ground. Early weeds steal sunlight and root nutrients, starving the yam plant when it is trying to form tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Jwɛi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ juɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Hɔmɔ yeɔ sweet potato tso lɛ beni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni efee ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow big and green. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the nitrogen they need to recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná nitrogen ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short and bent instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle shi moŋ ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eja lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, and deep soil to push downward easily. If the soil is hard, compacted, or stony, the tubers cannot expand straight down and will grow bent or twisted as they fight the hard ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni ekɛtsi kɛya shi mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ kɛya shi ni amɛbaakoto loo amɛbaatsake amɛhe beni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and heavy shade conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let sunlight in and clearing away infected pods helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji fungal hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ hulutsoo. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices. Spraying the leaves with a mild neem oil water mixture helps get rid of these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Akɛ neem fɔ kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛfutuɔ baai lɛ baashwie nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rains become heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining away. Excess water cuts off air to the roots, causing underground rot, so planting cassava on raised mounds helps rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. rot the underground No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu lɛ atsɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when they don't get consistent water. When the plant feels stressed by intense heat or dry soil, it drops its blossoms to conserve its strength.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo amɛnáaa nu daa. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miigba amɛnaa lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ amɛhewalɛ mli.
