english: Why are my okra plants growing very tall with large leaves, but producing very few okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi okra pods fioo ko pɛ ji nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo?

english: When okra gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows under dense shade, it uses all its power to produce high stems and big leaves instead of flowers and fruit pods.
ga: Kɛ okra nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo eda yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Roselle kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai wuji yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ŋmeii najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants grow big open leaves but fail to form a solid, tight head in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai wuji ni agbele naa shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitso ni mli wa ni mli eyi obɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbage needs cool nights and balanced feeding to form a head. High temperatures or applying too much nitrogen late in the plant's growth forces it to keep expanding its outer leaves instead of wrapping into a tight center.
ga: Kaabaji he miihia gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ kɛ niyenii ni ja koni ekɛfee yitsei. Nibii ni mli edɔ waa loo nitrogen ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ naagbee be mli Enɛ haa ehe bahiaa ni tso lɛ agbala esɛɛ baai lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeekɛ amɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense full sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce large broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and moist air young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni he hia kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen air from the sky and trap it inside the soil. Planting them alongside or after maize naturally enriches the soil food for your maize crop without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo esɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha sũ mli niyenii ni haa oŋmãa tsei lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: How do I know when my plantains are mature enough to harvest so they don't spoil before selling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantains lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa koni amɛkagbo dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Plantains are ready to cut when the fruits change from sharp-cornered to full and rounded, and the top leaves start turning yellow. Harvesting at full green maturity gives you enough days to transport and sell the fruit before it ripens and softens.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji aduawai lɛ tsake kɛjɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtee ŋwɛigbɛ ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nikpamɔ beni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ haa onáa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛbaafã aduawai lɛ ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ dani ekwɛ̃ ni efee blɛoo.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen and soften so quickly when stored together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he kome lɛ?

english: Harvested plantains release a natural gas called ethylene that speeds up ripening. Stacking bunches together in warm, unventilated spaces traps this gas and heat, causing the entire harvest to yellow and soften faster than expected.
ga: Plantains ni akpa lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene, ni haa ekwɛ̃ɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to kui amli yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ, ebaamɔ gas kɛ dɔlɛ nɛɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee blɛoo oya fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ.

english: Can one single plantain stem produce fruit more than once?
ga: Ani plantain kome baanyɛ awo yibii fe shikome?

english: No, a single plantain trunk only fruits once in its lifetime. After you harvest the bunch, that stem dies back, but new side shoots called suckers grow from the roots to produce future harvests.
ga: Dabi, plantain tso kome pɛ baawo yibii yɛ eshihilɛ mli. Beni okpa ŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Nakai tso lɛ baagbo. Shi ŋmeii heei, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii wɔsɛɛ.

english: How many side shoots should I leave around one plantain plant?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi sɛɛ tsei enyiɛ mabɔle dumɔwu kome he?

english: You should keep only 2 to 3 shoots (suckers) of different heights around the mother plant. Leaving too many shoots causes them to fight for nutrients, resulting in weak stems and smaller bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa ŋmeii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ (ŋmeii) ni amɛhe kwɔlɛ srɔtoi yɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why are the plantain bunches on my farm smaller than my neighbor's bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daraaa fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Small bunches usually happen when the plant lacks nutrients or water, or when too many suckers are left around the main stem to steal food away from the growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu. Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii komɛi eshwɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Tso lɛ fa tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ eju niyenii kɛjɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli.

english: Why do farmers plant plantains together with young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ kookoo tsei bibii feɔ ekome kɛduɔ plantains lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist during the cocoa trees' early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves have large surface areas that lose water quickly in hot, dry winds. Yellowing is the plant's way of reducing water loss during dry spells, which can be managed by spreading organic mulch around the root base.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ yɛ he ko ni da ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi mli. Safron ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhaa nu ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ baa shi. Abaanyɛ akwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over on their own when the fruit grows big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ shi beni aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and a heavy bunch makes the plant top-heavy. Wind or pest damage to the roots causes the tree to tip over, which is why farmers use wooden props or bamboo poles to support fruiting stems.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ haa tso lɛ tsiimɔ waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi ni fiteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ hewɔ ni okwaafoi kɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli loo ŋmei tsei fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain fruits split open while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ mli gbalaa be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Fruit splitting happens when a long dry period is suddenly followed by heavy rain. The fruit inside swells very fast with sudden water, stretching and tearing the skin before it can adapt.
ga: Yibii amli gbalamɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ sɛɛ. Yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fũuɔ oya waa kɛ́ akɛ nu eyi mli obɔ trukaa. Hewolo nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa mli dani enyɛɔ etsakeɔ ehe

english: Should I cut off the dark purple flower at the end of the plantain bunch?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ fɔfɔi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ plantain tso lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yes, removing the male purple flower after all fruit hands have formed saves the plant energy. This forces the plant to send all its food straight into plumping up the remaining fruit fingers.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ajie violet fɔfɔi hii lɛ beni aduawai lɛ aniji fɛɛ efee lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ hewalɛ akafite. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ eniyenii lɛ fɛɛ majeɔ tso yibii lɛ aniji ni eshwɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen or is too waterlogged. The plant takes nitrogen from its older lower leaves to keep the new top leaves green, showing that it needs fertilizer or better soil drainage.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛtee ŋwɛi Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ tsɔ. Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni eha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ he miihia.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge leafy stems but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Cassava puts all its energy into growing big leaves and stems instead of tubers when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Balancing soil nutrients allows the plant to send its food down into the roots to build thick cassava tubers.
ga: Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi kɛ tsei ashishifãi moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii beni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee ŋmei shishifãi ni mli tse.

english: Why does putting dry grass on the soil around my crops help them during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ jwɛi woɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a shade umbrella for the soil. It traps moisture in the dirt, keeps the roots cool, and stops the sun from baking the ground dry.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn soft and black before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni eyɛ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes happen when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, which is usually caused by irregular watering. Keeping the soil constantly moist allows the plant to move calcium into the growing fruits.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium yaa aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upward and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or whiteflies attacking the undersides of leaves. Managing these pests early prevents leaf damage and stops viruses from spreading to the rest of the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni tutuaa baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baa ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni ebaatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ hei krokomɛi.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and wilt in the afternoon heat but stand up again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi te shi ekoŋŋ leebi

english: Plants lose water faster through their leaves during the hottest hours than their roots can absorb from the soil. The leaves temporarily wilt to save water, then bounce back overnight as temperatures cool down.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efoɔ ehe ekoŋŋ nyɔɔŋ kome be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear out small shoots from around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Shi mi dumɔwu titri lɛ

english: Leaving too many small shoots, or suckers, forces the main plantain tree to fight for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning extra suckers ensures the main plant gets all the food it needs to produce large bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo loo ŋmeii bibii lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwu titri lɛ awuu kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo tsei wuji.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb tall sticks instead of trailing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaagbala shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing heavy tubers. Staking keeps the leaves high in the air for sunlight and off the wet ground, protecting the plant from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni tsii ni miida lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants drop their flowers before producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa drops its flowers when it gets too hot, stressed, or exposed to full sunlight. Providing shade crops like plantains reduces heat stress and keeps the humidity high enough for flowers to turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ, amɛmiihao, loo hulu lɛ miitso waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ bɔ ni sa koni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Which crops can I plant to get a quick harvest if I only have a short-term land agreement?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu kɛha kpamɔ oya kɛji akɛ miyɛ shikpɔŋ he kpaŋmɔ ni heɔ be kukuoo pɛ?

english: Fast-maturing annual crops like maize, cowpeas, tomatoes, and leafy vegetables mature within 3 to 6 months. Planting these allows you to harvest quickly without waiting years for tree crops to yield on temporary land.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ daa afi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa, tomato, kɛ aduawai ni baa yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 6 mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni omɛ afii babaoo ni okɛdu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rainfall becomes steady. The first rain is often followed by a dry spell, which can dry out and kill your newly germinated seeds in the soil.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans naturally take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which acts as free food to help your maize grow healthier without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ Nuts Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oŋmei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take a very long time to mature and produce a bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants need plenty of water and rich soil to thrive. If planted in poor soil or during dry spells without enough moisture, their growth slows down significantly.
ga: Nu babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa he miihia plantains koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Dalɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with leafy tops but giving me tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of storing food in its root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up and look twisted instead of spreading flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on leaf sap, or by a viral disease spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when there are no insects around to help move pollen within the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ebɔle amɛhe Koni eye ebua ni ajie pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ

english: How can I know if my young cocoa trees are getting too much sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tsɔ?

english: Young cocoa leaves will look scorched, dry out, and turn brown around the edges if exposed to full sunlight without temporary shade plants like plantains to protect them.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni eshã, egbi ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ eshishigbɛ kɛji akɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo shɛ amɛnɔ ni tsei tamɔ dumɔwui ni buɔ amɛhe be kukuoo mli ŋmɔlɔ bɛ mli.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the young maize lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaves to stay green and produce food for the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa bibii amli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni eha tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: What causes my yams to rot inside the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ dani akpaa?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when soil stays waterlogged for too long or when tiny soil pests bore holes into the yam, allowing water and bacteria inside.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ sweet potato mli Enɛ haa nu kɛ helatsɛmɛi ahiɔ mli.

english: Why are my cabbages opening up like bushy leaves instead of forming a hard, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ miigbele tamɔ tsei ahe tsei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee yitso ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form a tight head when temperatures are too high or watering is irregular, causing the plant to spread its leaves outward instead of wrapping them tight.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwereɔ baai lɛ eshwaa kponɔgbɛ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ amɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or it is being attacked by early-stage pests like fall armyworms. Adding manure or fertilizer and checking under the leaves for worms helps them grow green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworm lɛ tutuaa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli ni okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree experiences stress from too much direct heat, lack of shade, or dry soil. High temperatures and lack of moisture prevent the flowers from staying attached and forming pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine mli tɛ̃ɛ, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli. He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ amɛhe ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ akafo.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with lots of leaves, but the roots underground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraaa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are shaded too much, the cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing food in the roots. Cassava needs full sunlight and balanced soil nutrients to build big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tso lɛ ewo hulutsoo tsɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei baato niyenii yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli. Yucca he miihia hulu ni eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Hot midday sun causes water to evaporate from leaves faster than roots can draw water from the soil. Mulching around the base of the plant with dry grass helps keep the soil cool and holds moisture longer so plants do not wilt as quickly.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ egbooo oya.

english: Yam vines naturally search for sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves lifted off the wet ground, preventing leaf diseases and allowing maximum sunlight to reach the plant.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi folier helai anaa ni oha hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over when the fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and get very top-heavy when the bunch grows big or when too many suckers surround the main tree. Cutting away extra suckers and propping up the fruiting tree with wooden poles keeps it upright.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ waa beni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ loo ŋmeii babaoo ebɔle tso titri lɛ he. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ yibii lɛ afi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛhi shi jaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farmland help my maize grow better in the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When the groundnut crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the ground to feed the next crop naturally.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotten before they even get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when watering is irregular. Giving tomatoes steady water and adding poultry manure or lime to the soil prevents this black rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomatoi lɛ anɔ daa ni okɛ kooloi ashishifã loo lime fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ nɛɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves twisting together and looking tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni etamɔ nɔ ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Twisted and stunted pepper leaves are caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the sap of young leaves. Spraying early with neem leaf water or insecticidal soap stops these pests before they ruin the crop.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa. Akɛ neem baa mli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwieɔ nɔ mra. Ekpaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops grow so slowly if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi dumɔwui lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Because weeds grow faster, they steal these resources from young crop seedlings, slowing down their growth until the weeds are removed.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nibii nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui bibii amli. Enɛ haa edalɛ yaa hiɛ fioo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients out of the topsoil or when water sits in the field for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ loo kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up right on the tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ mitso lɛ niji anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, wet, and overly shaded conditions. Pruning extra tree branches lets in sunlight and air, which keeps the pods dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine. Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they get too stressed by intense heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps prevent this blossom drop.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ miihao amɛ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves and spreading plant viruses. Treating the plants with neem oil or insecticidal soap helps clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips, thrips, loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei amli helai lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu tsei ahe nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ajie amɛhe.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when rain water sits in the soil for too long without good drainage, allowing rot fungi to attack the roots. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to run off safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ ŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ni egbo lɛ baanyɛ atutua shishifãi lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my maize seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in tall, thin stalks with very small or empty cobs, reducing your overall harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli. Enɛ haa okpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so leaves get maximum sunlight, which directly feeds the plant and results in larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before the fruit bunch is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plantains often fall over because hidden pests like root nematodes or stem weevils weaken their shallow roots. Using clean suckers for planting and propping up heavy trees with wooden poles prevents them from falling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains gbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem weevils lɛ haa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni he tse tsu nii beni aduɔ ni akɛ tsei ni tsii fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why is planting groundnuts good for my soil before I plant maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ hi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ dani aduɔ ŋmãa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through small root nodules. When the crop is harvested, the natural nitrogen left behind feeds the next crop like maize without extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Akɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my crops still wilt and dry up even when it rains for a few minutes every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ minitii fioo ko pɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Short, light rains only wet the top layer of the soil and quickly evaporate in the sun before reaching the roots. Crop roots need deeper, heavier water penetration to absorb moisture from lower soil layers.
ga: Nugbɔ nɛ fioo be kukuoo ko. Enɛ haa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efoɔ oya yɛ hulu la mli dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Tsei shishifãi biɔ nu ni mli kwɔ ni tsii koni amɛnyɛ amɛjie nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my maize so that the crops do not fight each other for food?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-ŋmã lɛ kɛjɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ tɛŋŋ koni tsei lɛ akatswa niyenii he akaŋ?

english: Planting maize in straight rows with recommended spacing (such as 75 cm between rows and 40 cm between plants) gives each crop enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to produce full, healthy cobs without overcrowding.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ja mli ni akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛto he lɛ (tamɔ 75 cm yɛ ŋta lɛ teŋ kɛ 40 cm yɛ tsei ateŋ) haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ehiɛɛɛ ŋtayaai babaoo.

english: How do I know the correct number of cassava cuttings to plant on my acre of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei shishifãi ayibɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre lɛ nɔ?

english: Calculating your plant population based on standard field spacing (usually 1 meter by 1 meter) allows you to fit roughly 4,000 stands per acre, ensuring maximum root growth without wasting land or crowding the crop.
ga: Kɛji obu otsei lɛ ayibɔ he akɔntaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɛkɛmɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ (bei pii lɛ mita 1 x mita 1) lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ tsei aaafee 4,000 maa acre kome nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛfiteee he ko loo amɛhaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayi obɔ kɛteke nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my young tomato seedlings are growing normally after a few weeks in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Healthy young tomato plants should have firm green stems, bright green leaves without yellow spots, and visible new growth every week; stunted growth or pale leaves usually mean the crop lacks water or key nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ tomato tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná tsei ni wa, eŋɔli. Baai eŋɔli ni mli tse ni ŋmɔŋ bɛ he. ni ona dalɛ hee daa otsi Dalɛ bibioo loo baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ bei pii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii titrii.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops after planting them?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni midu nii sɛɛ?

english: Most crops need their first round of fertilizer about two to three weeks after germination or transplanting, which gives the young root system enough strength to absorb nutrients effectively.
ga: Tsei babaoo he miihia amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii aaafee otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛdu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young pepper plants turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young crops usually point to stress caused by overwatering, poor soil drainage, or a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which slows down the plant's overall development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ haomɔ ni nu ni akɛhaa amɛ fe nine lɛ kɛbaa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my bean plants start to climb and twist around wooden sticks as they grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ miibɔi kwɔɔ kɛmiibɔle ehe lɛ? Tsoi beni amɛdaraa lɛ

english: Climbing bean varieties naturally produce tendrils that reach upward for sunshine; giving them wooden stakes keeps the leaves and pods off the wet soil, protecting them from rot and ground insects.
ga: Beans srɔtoi ni kwɔɔ ni akɛ tsei fee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai kɛ ŋmeii akagbee shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ahe.

english: What should I do if I see small holes appearing in the leaves of my cabbage?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina bu bibioo ko? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ kaabɛji baai anɔ?

english: Holes in crop leaves indicate that caterpillars or insects are feeding on the plants; regularly inspecting your field and applying safe controls early prevents pest populations from destroying the leaves before harvest.
ga: Buu ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii loo kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli daa ni okɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he gbɛjianɔtoi atsu nii mra. Ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ naa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ dani akpa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off the tree before turning into small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when cocoa trees experience severe dry spells, damage from pests like mirids, or poor shade conditions; maintaining proper shade trees helps protect delicate blossoms so they can set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji kookoo tsei lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ afua loo hulutsoo shihilɛ ni ehiii lɛ efiteɔ hulutsoo tso lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting too much water during the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Crops receiving excess water will show yellowing leaves, soft stems, and stunted roots because the flooded soil prevents air from reaching the root zone.
ga: Tsei ni awoɔ amɛ nu fe nine lɛ baajie baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How does making mounds or ridges help my yam crop grow larger tubers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni afee lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi sweet potato tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji?

english: Mounds and ridges loosen the soil so roots can expand without restriction, while also providing good drainage during heavy rains to keep the tubers from rotting underground.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ alɛɛ mli ni nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can get more crops on my small land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they overcrowd each other and fight for the same water, nutrients, and sunlight. This overcrowding makes the plants weak and thin, resulting in small, poor harvests rather than a bigger yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ feɔ amɛhe ekome ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɛkɛ shweremɔ ni fe nine nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ faaa, ni ehiii kwraa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee babaoo lɛ

english: Why do farmers make raised soil mounds before planting cassava or yams in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okwaafoi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛdu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Raised soil mounds loosen the earth so root crops can easily expand and grow large tubers. Mounds also keep excess rain from sitting around the roots, preventing rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei ni shishifãi yɔɔ lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Koni akafee ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crops turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks essential plant nutrients like nitrogen, or that waterlogging is suffocating the roots and preventing them from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miiha shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiiye niyenii ni esaaa.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and short roots that cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They require temporary shade, such as nearby plantain trees, to protect them until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji, ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛ hia hɔɔŋ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ. koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in high heat is a crop's natural defense mechanism to conserve water and stop moisture from evaporating too quickly from its leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛbuɔ nu he ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekajɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat, erratic watering, or when given too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on producing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo kɛ́ enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why are my cassava roots decaying under the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water cannot drain away from heavy rains or when plants are too crowded, creating wet soil conditions where fungi and diseases thrive.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu nyɛɛɛ ajɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli aba loo kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ efɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ helai baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ.

english: How does letting weeds grow close to my crops harm my farm's final harvest?
ga: Te jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ saa miŋmɔ lɛ naagbee ŋmaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, groundwater, and fertilizer away from your crops. Overcrowding your crops with weeds starves the main crop and lowers your total harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la ni he hia, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi wo oŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ, ni ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi.

english: Can I plant beans together with my maize on the exact same farm field?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize works well because beans take nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural food source that helps the maize grow healthier.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil has become too weak to produce good crops without plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai baa kɛji tsei niyenii bɛ mli?

english: If your crops stay short, grow very slowly, have pale yellow leaves, or yield tiny fruits despite getting enough rain, it means the soil lacks nutrients and needs organic manure or compost.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi be kukuoo, edaa blɛoo waa, eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. aloo ewoɔ aduawai bibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell if my oil palm trees are male or female, and why does it matter for my harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-oil palm tso lɛ ji nuu loo yoo? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mikpamɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees produce both male and female flower bunches on the same tree at different times. Female flowers develop into the fruit bunches you harvest, while male flowers produce the pollen needed to fertilize them. Good pollination is required to get full, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei yɛ tso kome nɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Fɔfɔi yei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai akui ni okpaa. yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi hii lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni he hiaa kɛha fɔmɔ lɛ. Pollination kpakpa he miihia koni aná aduawai ni tsiimɔ yeɔ emuu.

english: Do coconut trees need separate male and female trees to bear fruit?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni agbala ŋmei tsei kɛjɛ tsei hii kɛ yei ateŋ koni amɛwo yibii?

english: No, a single coconut tree carries both male and female flowers on the same flowering branch. The male flowers release pollen to fertilize the female flowers on the same tree, so you do not need separate male and female trees to get coconuts.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei tso kome yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei yɛ nine kome nɔ. Fɔfɔi hii jieɔ pollen koni amɛwo fɔfɔi yei yɛ tso kome nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni ogbala tsei hii kɛ yei amli koni onine ashɛ ŋmeii anɔ.

english: Why do some of my pawpaw trees produce plenty of flowers but never bear any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw plants can be male, female, or bisexual. Male pawpaw trees only produce pollen-bearing flowers and will never produce fruit themselves; you need female or bisexual trees in your garden to harvest pawpaws.
ga: Pawpaw tsei baanyɛ afee nuu, yoo, loo nɔ ni kɛ hii feɔ yakayaka nii. Pawpaw tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni pollen yɔɔ mli pɛ, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwooo yibii. Esa akɛ oná tsei ni ji yei loo tsei ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii yɛ obɔɔ lɛ mli koni okɛkpa paw paws.

english: Why does the fertilizer I apply around my crops seem to wash away when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ Miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Leaving fertilizer on top of bare soil leaves it exposed to rain runoff. To prevent it from washing away, dig a shallow ring around the plant, place the fertilizer inside, and cover it back up with soil.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu lɛ atsɔ mli. koni ekɛtsi enaa koni ekaho. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli ekɔɔɔ he ebɔle tso lɛ he ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ sũ aha nɔ

english: Why are my crop roots struggling to grow deep even when the top of the soil looks soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ blɛoo moŋ?

english: Below the loose topsoil, there may be a compacted, hard layer of soil called a hardpan. Digging or plowing deeply breaks this hard layer, allowing roots to push down deeper for water and nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ ni mli tse Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe ni atsɛɔ lɛ hard pan lɛ yɛ. Kɛ́ ootsu nii loo otsu nii kɛya shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaakumɔ nɛkɛ ŋtayaa ni wa nɛɛ. Ha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ mli kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: I sprayed chemical on my crops to kill insects, but nothing happened and the pests are still there—what went wrong?
ga: Mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ koni mikɛgbe kooloi bibii. Shi nɔ ko bako ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ lolo. Meni ba?

english: Pesticides can fail if they are mixed with the wrong amount of water, sprayed during the heat of the day when chemicals evaporate quickly, washed off by rain, or if the pests have built resistance to that chemical.
ga: Ekolɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ nu ni esaaa futu mli. Okɛ tsofai lɛ afɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni tsofai lɛ shwieɔ oya lɛ anɔ. ni nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ etswa nakai tsofa lɛ he hewalɛ

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulched helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do some cassava plants produce large tubers while neighboring ones yield almost nothing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji shi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ wooo nɔ ni miihe ashɛ eko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tuber production depends on the health of the stem cutting planted, weed competition, and soil looseness. Healthy, disease-free cuttings planted in loose, fertile soil direct more energy into swelling their roots.
ga: Tuber feemɔ damɔ nine ni miida lɛ hewalɛnamɔ nɔ. Jwɛi akaŋshii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tsofai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni helai bɛ mli ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baa nii amli lɛ baatsɔɔ hewalɛ gbɛ koni eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ babaoo.

english: Why are my neighbor’s crops yielding much more than mine even though we planted the same seeds at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe mi nɔ lɛ? He ni wɔduɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Seed quality is only part of crop success. Differences in crop yield usually come down to field care, such as regular weeding, correct plant spacing, timely fertilizer application, and proper soil moisture control.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ omanye lɛ fã kome pɛ. Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli yibiiwoo mli lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ nɔ, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ nɔ. tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni ja Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ be naa ni akudɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ

english: How does cutting off extra branches from my fruit trees help them produce bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahe niji ni fa fe nine ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii wuji?

english: Pruning removes weak or unnecessary branches that consume water and nutrients. By cutting them off, the tree directs all its food and energy into growing larger, healthier fruit on the remaining branches.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni he ehiaaa ni yeɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. kɛtsɔ efomɔ nɔ Tso lɛ heɔ eniyenii kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ koni eha niji ni eshwɛ lɛ adara ni amɛwo yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I feed the leaves of my harvested crops to my livestock?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ baai ni akpa lɛ abahã mikooloi lɛ?

english: Yes, leaves from crops like cassava, cowpea, and groundnuts are full of nutrients and make excellent fodder for animals like goats and sheep, helping you save money on feed.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei mli lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni eji niyenii kpakpa kɛha kooloi tamɔ tooi kɛ tooi, ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ shika toɔ niyenii he.

english: How can using plant parts for other farm uses help me save money?
ga: Tso lɛ fãi ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛha nitsumɔi krokomɛi Te Okwaayeli baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni mikɛ shika ato?

english: By using crop leaves for animal feed and stems for replanting or mulching, you create a full circle where nothing on your farm goes to waste.
ga: Tso baai ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ kooloi aniyenii kɛ shishifãi kɛha dumɔ najiaŋdamɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ni akɛhaa. Obaafee kooyigbɛ he ko ni nɔ ko nɔ ko eshwɛɛɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What is kunkuntire, and how should I select it for planting cassava?
ga: Mɛni ji Kunkun Tire ni te esa akɛ mahala tɛŋŋ ni makwɛ ŋmei?

english: Kunkuntire refers to healthy cassava stem cuttings. You should select strong, mature stems free from pests and diseases so that your new plants start with good vigor.
ga: Kunkuntire shishi ji ni afolɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ kɛha hewalɛnamɔ. Esa akɛ ohala tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eda ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai bɛ mli. Koni oha otso hee lɛ aje hewalɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to follow step-by-step guidelines when planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ kuku kɛ kuku nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Following practical, recommended steps—such as proper spacing, correct planting depth, and timely weeding—ensures crops grow uniformly and produce high yields.
ga: Nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee yɛ nitsumɔ mli lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ, tamɔ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa dumɔ mlibotemɔ ni ja kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be ni sa mli Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ daraa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How does doing my farm work properly at the beginning save me from exhaustion later?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsu miŋmɔ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ shishijee koni mikɛhere mi kɛjɛ tɔlɛ mli sɛɛ mli?

english: Clearing land properly and spacing crops correctly early on reduces weed competition, making regular farm maintenance much easier and less tiring on your mind and body.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa jwɛi akaŋshii baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ mli saamɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. ni tɔlɔ fioo yɛ ojwɛŋmɔ kɛ ogbɔmɔtso fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers ask us to adopt new farming methods instead of relying only on old habits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ biɔ ni wɔkɛ okwaayeli gbɛi heei atsu nii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ ohe aaafɔ̃ sui momo anɔ lɛ

english: Newer, tested farming procedures help protect crops from changing weather, improve soil fertility, and increase harvests compared to traditional methods.
ga: Okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoi heei ni aka amɛ akwɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ ni eha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ kɛ akɛto blema gbɛi ahe

english: Why do crop leaves sometimes turn yellow or drop off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Leaves drop or change color when crops lack nutrients like nitrogen, receive too little water, or are attacked by pests and diseases.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, ni nu fioo pɛ amɛnáa. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa amɛ

english: Why are my crops growing unevenly even though I planted them on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ tamɔ bɔ ni miduɔ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Uneven crop growth usually happens because seeds were planted at different depths or because soil fertility and moisture vary across different spots in your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei adalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa ejaakɛ aduɔ dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ. Aloo akɛni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Where can I go to learn the correct practices for taking care of my farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ maya koni makase nifeemɔi ni ja ni akɛkwɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: You can learn proper techniques by attending community farmer field demonstrations, speaking with local agricultural extension officers, or joining local farmers' cooperatives.
ga: Obaanyɛ okase ŋaai ni sa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi ni akutsoŋbii okwaafoi feɔ lɛ amli ni okɛ ohe aaawo mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ lɛ agba sane. loo okɛ ohe awo maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi akuu ko mli

english: How do I know if my crops are developing on the right track during the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Healthy crop progression shows steady growth, strong stem development, and vibrant foliage without signs of wilting, spots, or pest damage.
ga: Tso lɛ hiɛyaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsɔɔ dalɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Tso lɛ tso lɛ dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ miishɛɛ ni okadi ko bɛ he akɛ egbo, he ko, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight because their leaves are tender and lose moisture very quickly. Planting quick-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts like a living umbrella, lowering the soil temperature and keeping the air moist so the cocoa can survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ ji bibii ni amɛmli shwieɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔ ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ baa shi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow tall. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its deep green color and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why does planting maize on the same piece of land every year give me smaller harvests each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo fioo baa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests that target that crop to build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills the soil with nitrogen and breaks the cycle of pests.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ nakai nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nitrogen ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together to get a bigger harvest from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops end up fighting each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing ensures every single plant gets enough space and resources to grow strong stems and produce maximum yield.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baawu koni hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings rot in the ground while others sprout quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings rot if they are taken from weak or diseased plants, or if they are planted upside down. Planting healthy, mature stem cuttings right side up—with the buds pointing upward toward the sky—allows roots and leaves to form naturally without trapping moisture that causes rot.
ga: Cassava tsei ni afo lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni egbɔjɔ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Aloo kɛji akɛ adu kɛtee shishi Adu niji ni eda, ni he wa ni kwɛɔ ŋwɛi. ni fɔfɔii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Enɛ baaha shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ afee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛmɔmɔɔɔ nu ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants rot at the base and die during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shishigbɛ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants hate standing water around their roots because flooded soil starves the root system of air and invites fungal infections. Planting peppers on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away, keeping the roots safe from rotting.
ga: Pepper tsei sumɔɔɔ nu ni damɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe, ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in cool, wet, and overly shaded environments. Pruning excess branches from cocoa trees allows sunlight and fresh air to dry out the farm, creating an environment where the fungus cannot easily grow.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kookoo tsei lɛ aniji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni ŋmei nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ mlɛo.

english: Weeds act like intruder plants that steal food, water, and sunlight away from your main crop. Because weeds grow aggressively, they starve your crops, leaving them too weak to build large roots, leaves, or fruits.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei ni shwereɔ, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya Ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee shishifãi, baai, loo aduawai wuji.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat stress or irregular watering. When a plant gets too hot or dried out, it drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself from dying.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo egbi tsɔ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with tall wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need to lift their leaves high into the sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to light and off the wet soil where diseases can attack them.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ nɔ koni amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ shɛɔ la he ni ejɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ, he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. baanyɛ atutua

english: Is it better for me to spray chemical fertilizers or liquids on my crops early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makɛ tsofa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ leebi loo shwane mli.

english: Early morning is best because the air is cool, wind is low, and plant leaves open their tiny pores to absorb liquid easily before the hot sun dries it up.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli waaa, ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni agbeleɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ nu oya dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ agbi amɛ.

english: Should I water my crops early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Early morning watering is ideal because it gives plants moisture for the hot day ahead and allows excess water on the leaves to dry off, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi maŋkpa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ehaa tso lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ kɛha gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ gĩɔ Koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa lɛ akafee nɔ ko

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In intense midday heat, plants temporarily close their leaf pores to conserve water and protect themselves, making them look wilted until the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ ŋaa amɛbaai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli be kukuoo ko koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛbu amɛhe. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulu lɛ haa amɛhe jɔɔ.

english: How do I correctly apply fertilizer to my crops so that the roots actually get the nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer a few centimeters away from the plant stem in a shallow ring or hole, then cover it with soil so rain does not wash it away or heat evaporate it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo tso lɛ shishi sɛntimita fioo komɛi yɛ ŋwɛi loo bu ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ sũ aha nɔ koni nugbɔ akashwie tsei lɛ loo dɔlɛ akafo mli.

english: Can I use the same machine to apply fertilizer on different types of crops like maize and cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsɔne kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ awo ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa mli?

english: Yes, but you must adjust the machine's settings and nozzles to match the proper spacing and required fertilizer amount for each specific crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ otsake tsɔne lɛ kɛ nozzle lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ koni ekɛ gbɛ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Can I use a mechanical planter machine on a field that still has small tree stumps and stones?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni ŋmeii kɛ tɛi bibii yɔɔ mli lolo lɛ atsu nii?

english: No, planting machines need well-cleared and loose soil; stumps and stones can break the machine parts or cause seeds to be planted at uneven depths.
ga: Dabi, ehe miihia ni mɔ ni duɔ nii lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni etse ehe. Tɛi kɛ tɛi baanyɛ akumɔ tsɔne mli nibii loo eha adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko.

english: What happens to my farm soil if I keep applying chemical fertilizer every single season?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo mli daa be?

english: Continuous chemical fertilizer use without adding organic manure can make the soil acidic over time and kill helpful earthworms, eventually reducing soil fertility.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii be fɛɛ be ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee acidic yɛ be ni sa mli. ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ Enɛ haa yɛ naagbee lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni baa shi lɛ baa shi.

english: What is the best way for me to prepare and plant plantain suckers on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ masaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Dig deep holes, mix the soil with well-rotted animal manure, trim old roots from the sucker, and plant it firmly upright so water collects around the base.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu ko ni mli kwɔ ni okɛ kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ afutu shikpɔŋ. Kpɔ̃ɔ shishifãi momo lɛ kɛjɛ su lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, du lɛ shi shiŋŋ bɔni afee ni nu abua naa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall down when strong winds blow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep, and heavy fruit bunches make the tree top-heavy; planting them too shallowly makes them easy targets for storm winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Ni aduawai akui ni tsii haa tso lɛ yiteŋ feɔ tsii. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni ahum baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are yellowing because of lack of food or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ efee ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni bɛ loo hela hewɔ?

english: Nutrient shortages usually cause whole leaves to turn light green or yellow evenly, while diseases usually create irregular spots, patches, or rotting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ haa tso lɛ baa muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse, yɛ be mli ni helai Bei pii lɛ, ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off when the afternoon sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants experience extreme stress and shed their blossoms to save water and energy, which stops them from producing fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ naa haomɔ ni naa wa ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. ni haaa enyɛ ewo yibii lɛ

english: How does intense sunlight affect the leaves and skin of my sweet peppers?
ga: Te hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ saa ŋmeii ahe baai kɛ amɛhewolo he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extreme heat causes sunscald, which leaves white burned patches on pepper fruits and causes leaves to wilt and turn yellow because the plant cannot stay cool.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ kɛ hulutsoo baa. Enɛ haa shãa he okadii yɛŋ baa ŋmɔtɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ. Ni enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ akɛni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahi e-fɛ̃i lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings grow thin and weak instead of strong and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui bibii lɛ miidara ni amɛmiifee mlɛo ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch out thin and tall when they are struggling to find the right balance of light, but protecting them under mild shade helps them build thick stems and healthy roots.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛya shɔŋŋ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛna kane ni sa lɛ. Shi abu he yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse lɛ shishi Ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: What is a net house, and how can it help my vegetables grow better?
ga: Mɛni ji trellis ŋmɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-vegetables lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: A net house is a structure made with mesh fabric that shields crops from harsh direct sunlight and keeps destructive insects out while allowing air to flow freely so plants stay cool.
ga: Trellis greenhouse ji nɔ ko ni akɛ mesh mama fee ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. ni oha kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akabote mli yɛ be mli ni ohaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ oya. Koni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i

english: Do crops grown inside a covered structure need less watering than open field crops?
ga: Ani tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ tsũi ni akɛ nɔ ko eha nɔ lɛ amli lɛ biɔ nu fioo fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, covered structures reduce direct heat and wind exposure, which slows down water loss from both the plant leaves and the soil, keeping the moisture in longer.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ tsũ lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ baa shi tɛ̃ɛ. ni haa nu ni jɛɔ tso lɛ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ baa shi Ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why are some vegetable farmers using covered structures instead of open fields in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai okwaafoi komɛi kɛ tsũi ni aha nɔ tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ najiaŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Covered structures protect delicate crops from heavy seasonal rains and intense dry season sun, allowing farmers to grow quality produce like cucumbers and peppers continuously throughout the year.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛha he lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be mli kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛduɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ kukumba kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do heavy rains cause my cabbage and pepper leaves to rot so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa mi-cabbage kɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Raindrops splash soil and fungal spores onto plant leaves, and the prolonged wetness gives diseases the perfect environment to infect and rot the plant.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ shwieɔ sũ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ. Ni ŋmɔtɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ahe helai kɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Why do tiny insects like whiteflies multiply so fast on my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ faa oya yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Whiteflies thrive in hot, dry weather where rain cannot wash them off, allowing them to rapidly multiply, suck plant sap, and spread viral diseases.
ga: Whiteflies lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. akɛ nugbɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ahoo amɛ Enɛ haa amɛshwereɔ oya, amɛnuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: How does putting a mesh cover over my vegetable bed reduce my need for chemical sprays?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ akɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ha aduawai ashikpɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he ahia lɛ shi?

english: The fine mesh acts as a physical barrier that stops insect pests from reaching your plants to lay eggs, drastically reducing pest damage without relying heavily on chemicals.
ga: Kpoji bibii lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ tso lɛ he koni amɛwo amɛwui. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa shi kwraa ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai anɔ waa.

english: How does heavy tropical rainfall harm my young vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ mi-aduawai bibii lɛ awui?

english: Powerful rainstorms beat down on soft young plants, bruising their leaves, snapping weak stems, and washing away topsoil and fertilizers away from the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ tswa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ni efite amɛbaai lɛ. Ekumɔ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die whenever the hot dry sun comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted next to them to act as natural umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I clear the weeds around my crops instead of just letting them grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and plant food in the soil. Clearing weeds leaves more nutrients for your crops so they can grow faster and produce a larger harvest.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii babaoo. Koni tsei lɛ adara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and looking stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient, or that the soil is too dry. Adding compost or proper fertilizer gives them the food they need to turn dark green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛ niyenii ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or insect attacks. Keeping the soil evenly moist and protecting the farm from pests will help the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ. loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi shi daa ni abu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What makes my cassava roots rot underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates in the soil without draining away properly, creating condition where harmful fungi thrive. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain safely away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ adara yɛ mli lɛ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to wait for the main rains before sowing my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seeds require steady, reliable moisture to germinate and establish roots. Planting in dry soil causes seeds to dry up or get carried off by insects before the rain arrives.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo kooloi bibii baaŋɔ amɛ kɛya dani nugbɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller produce if I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same water and soil nutrients underground. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough room and food to produce large, healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is healthy enough for good crop growth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy soil feels dark, crumbly, and holds moisture well like a squeezed damp sponge. Soil that is hard like rock or washes away easily like sand needs organic manure or compost added to improve its richness.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ duŋ, ekpɔtɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu tamɔ sponji ni mli efɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa tamɔ tɛ loo ni shwieɔ shi oya tamɔ ŋã lɛ biɔ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ.

english: Why do insects keep eating holes in my vegetable leaves even after I water the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-vegetables baai lɛ amli lolo beni mikɛ nu ewo ŋmɔ lɛ mli po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Watering cleans dust off leaves but does not deter insect pests like caterpillars or beetles. Using recommended natural extracts or approved treatments helps protect the leaves from pests.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi etsĩii kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa. Kɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die while the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ?
