english: Sudden wilting in damp soil is often caused by soil-borne bacteria or fungi blocking the water vessels inside the plant stem. Rotating your crops each season stops these diseases from building up in the dirt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai nɛɛ akabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight. They need partial shade from plantains or forest trees to keep the soil moist and protect their young leaves from sun damage until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo kɛjɛ plantains loo koo mli tsei amli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la he kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the leaf tips inward when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to grow leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant what it needs to regain its green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa mligbɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with lots of leaves but only produce tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen or is too hard, cassava puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots. Soft, well-tilled soil helps the cassava tubers expand naturally.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ wa tsɔ Yɛ niyenii ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. Stress causes the plant to shed its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Haomɔ haa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the top leaves of my young maize crops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ

english: Ragged holes in young maize are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant during the daytime and eat the tender leaf tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ baai bibii amli fãji.

english: Leaf curl in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the leaf juices, or by a virus carried by these insects. Removing damaged plants early helps keep the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Tsei ni efite lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Should I sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is risky to plant immediately after the first rain because early rains are often followed by hot dry spells. If the soil dries out before the second rain, your germinating seeds will dry up and die.
ga: Eyɛ oshara akɛ ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi dani nugbɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can spread out to catch as much sunlight as possible. The more sunlight the leaves catch, the more food they make to feed and swell the yam tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Babaoo ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, Babaoo ni obɔɔ baai lɛ, babaoo ni obaanyɛ ofee niyenii. ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even if they are growing a small distance away from them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo pɛ moŋ?

english: Weed roots spread far beneath the ground and aggressively steal water and plant food out of the soil before your crop's roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ ohe.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays behind as free food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shi akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or taller forest trees to protect their delicate leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei kakadaji koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants form larger tubers when their leaves catch plenty of sunlight. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so leaves get maximum light and stay clean from soil-borne rot and diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ bulbs wuji kɛji amɛbaai lɛ ná hulu la babaoo. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. koni baai lɛ aná la babaoo ni eha ehe atse kɛjɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant moves the little nitrogen it has to the newer, upper leaves to stay alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land help my soil grow better maize next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmãa kpakpa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays behind in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Does it matter which direction I insert my cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the small growth buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If planted upside down, the stems struggle to sprout, resulting in weak growth or dead cuttings.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Ebaawa akɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ŋmeii ni gboi lɛ baa.

english: Will I get more garden eggs if I plant my seeds very close together to fill up all the space?
ga: Ani maná ŋmeii babaoo yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛwo he ni yɔɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too close causes crops to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Spacing garden eggs properly gives each plant room to grow strong branches and produce more fruits.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ abɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ to abɔɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ niji ni mli wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Leaving too many suckers forces them to compete with the main plant for food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, which leads to larger bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ amɛshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Why do the roots of my cassava plants rot when heavy rain leaves standing water on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu hiɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water covers the soil for extended periods, it cuts off oxygen, causing the tuber roots to suffocate and decay.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Enɛ haa bulb lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, dry air, or irregular watering can stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers to conserve energy instead of setting fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomatoi lɛ ajie fɔfɔii koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites, or a virus transmitted by insects. Protecting the plants early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei ahe ni abuɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are the stems and branches of my cocoa trees swelling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji lɛ efuu ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. When a tree gets infected, its sap vessels swell and block nutrients, causing the tree to slowly decline and stop producing pods.
ga: Enɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Kɛji tso lɛ he hela lɛ Milk ducts lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni etsĩɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ naa. Ha tso lɛ aba shi fiofio ni ekpa ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ

english: What causes tiny brown spots and powdery patches on the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baa? kɛ powda yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: Surface spots and patches on leaves are usually caused by tiny pests or fungal infections feeding on the leaf surface. Treating the crop early with neem oil or appropriate fungicide protects the leaves so the plant can make food and produce healthy peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ he ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni sa nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii ni ekɛ chili ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, usually from high heat or inconsistent watering. The plant drops its blossoms to conserve energy and survive when environmental conditions are unfavorable.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi kɛji shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli wa waa.

english: Why are the outer leaves on my plantain trees turning yellow and snapping near the trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing and snapping leaves in plantains are often caused by Fusarium wilt, a soil fungal disease. The fungus enters through the roots and blocks the plant's water channels, causing the lower leaves to starve of moisture and collapse.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fusarium, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekumɔ lɛ baa. Fɔ̃ɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ nu gbɛi lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkuɔ shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants look wilted during the day even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: Wilting in moist soil is often caused by root-knot nematodes, which are microscopic worms in the soil. They attack the roots and cause them to form swollen knots or galls, preventing the roots from drinking water even if the soil is wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, root-knot nematodes, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ baa. Amɛtutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni efuu baa. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkanu nu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the ground before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ mafo amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil holds too much water and cannot drain properly. Waterlogged soil prevents oxygen from reaching the roots, allowing destructive soil fungi to grow and spoil the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni enyɛɛɛ etsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ji oxygen lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ daa ni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tip inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiya mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom signal that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need for leaf growth. Just as poor nutrition makes a person sick, nutrient-poor soil causes visible weakness in the plant.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni baai lɛ adara lɛ Taakɛ niyenii ni esaaa haa gbɔmɛi hela mɔɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ hu haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ gbɛ ni kadiɔ mɔ nɔ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and crooked instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep, and well-mounded soil to expand smoothly underground. If the soil is hard, compacted, or stony, the developing tuber cannot push through easily and ends up deformed or small.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni ashɛrɛ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmeii ni etsɔ hiɛ lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli mlɛo ni amɛbaagbe naa ni amɛfite loo amɛbaafee bibii.

english: Maize leaves curl inward during hot afternoons to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This natural behavior helps the crop trap moisture and stop water from evaporating too quickly during heat stress.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli subaŋ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantain leaves act as a living umbrella, providing shade and keeping the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa plants establish their roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain tso lɛ baai ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stems when planting them in the dirt?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni atsɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ he gbɛ nɔ beni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes the plant to waste energy growing stems in the wrong direction, leading to weak growth and low yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ shwere ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot when heavy rain falls for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in standing water because wet, airless soil promotes fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden poles to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants rely on stakes to lift their leaves into direct sunlight, which gives the plant energy to grow large tubers underground. Lifting leaves off the damp soil also prevents ground fungal diseases from killing the plant.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shishitoo mla ni ji amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, no hu tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbe tso lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees close to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn and die quickly under intense direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool and damp until they are old enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ baashã oya ni amɛgboi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why is it good to grow cowpeas or beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans trap nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil, naturally feeding the maize. Their broad leaves also cover the ground, preventing weed growth and keeping soil moisture from evaporating.
ga: Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Baai ni mli kwɔlɔ hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa sũ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be ni amɛdaraa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil is running low on nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-based fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure brings back the green leaf color and ensures proper cob development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are all the blossoms dropping off my pepper plants before any peppers can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or dry soil. Covering the dirt around the plant with dried leaves or straw helps retain soil moisture and keeps roots cool.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ mli. Mulching around Dumɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark brown patches and dry up right after rainy days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbiɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rain splatters fungal spores from the soil onto tomato leaves, creating leaf diseases like blight. Spacing plants further apart lets wind dry the leaves faster, reducing fungal outbreaks.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ tomato baai anɔ. Ekɛ tso helai tamɔ tso lɛ he tsɛŋemɔ baa. Gbɛ ni kã tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ da, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ oya. Ha fungal helai ni baa lɛ aba shi

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the tops of my young corn shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These pests are Fall Armyworms that target young corn leaf funnels. Dropping a handful of dry sand mixed with wood ash or spraying recommended neem-based pesticides into the center of the shoot kills them.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋã ni egbi ni akɛ tso sũ efutu mli lɛ fioo ko shwie shi loo okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛ neem fee lɛ shwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil is healthy without using expensive testing tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ tsɔnei ni jara wa ni akɛkaa nii lɛ bɛ mli?

english: Fertile soil usually looks dark in color, crumbles easily when squeezed in your fist, holds moisture without becoming sticky mud, and contains visible life like earthworms.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ fɔɔ su ni yɔɔ duŋ. Efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔlɔ mimɔ mli. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli hu yɛ ni abaanyɛ ana amɛ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii.

english: When I buy oil palm seedlings from market sellers, how can I be sure they will produce good fruit later?
ga: Beni mihe mu tso dumɔwui kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ebaawo yibii yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: You cannot determine fruit quality just by looking at young seedlings. To ensure high yields, you should buy certified hybrid seedlings from recognized agricultural research centers or accredited nurseries rather than uncertified local sellers who may sell mixed or low-yielding varieties.
ga: Onyɛŋ ole bɔ ni tso yibii lɛ hi ha kɛtsɔ tso bibioo lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ kɛkɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ Esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii ni yɔɔ srɔtoi ni aŋmala he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ he ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔhe ko ni awo he odaseyeli. Mohu ɔ, yaa ní ngɛ ma a mi nihɔɔli nɛ a be he womi ɔ a ngɔ nɛ a ma nyɛ maa ju hybrid loo slɔɔtoslɔɔtohi nɛ a woɔ yiblii tsɔ ɔ a ngɔ.

english: Is it good practice for me to dig up self-sown palm seedlings growing under old trees to plant on my new farm?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mafolɔ mi-palm dumɔwui ni mikwɛ yɛ shia lɛ ashishi yɛ tsei momoi ashishi ni madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: No, wild seedlings growing under old trees come from unverified cross-pollination. They often take longer to bear fruit, produce thick-shelled fruits with less oil, and frequently go through long periods of producing only non-fruiting male flowers.
ga: Dabi, koo mli dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei momoi ashishi lɛ jɛɔ cross-pollination ni amako nɔ mi lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii. Yibii lɛ hewolo lɛ mli tse, ni ekɛ fɔ fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii. Ni bei pii lɛ, eheɔ be babaoo dani anáa fɔfɔi hii pɛ ni wooo yibii.

english: Officer, how can I tell if an oil palm tree is male or female before I plant it?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni onukpai lɛ ale kɛji mu tso ji mu tso nuu loo yoo dani amɛdu?

english: At the seedling stage, it is impossible to visually tell whether an oil palm tree will lean towards male or female flowering. Oil palm trees are unique because a single tree produces both male and female flowers at different times as it grows.
ga: yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishijee mli Anyɛɛɛ akɛ hiŋmɛi atsɔɔ kɛji mu tso ko baatsi ehe kɛya fɔfɔi hii loo yei ahe. Mu tsei yɛ srɔto kwraa ejaakɛ tso kome woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei fɛɛ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli beni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do some of my palm trees only produce flowers but never yield any fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ekomɛi fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛkɛ shi amɛwooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees produce separate male and female flower bunches. Male flowers only produce pollen to fertilize female flowers, so when a tree is in a male flowering cycle, it will not carry any fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei woɔ fɔfɔi ni ji hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Fɔfɔi hii feɔ pollen pɛ koni amɛkɛ fɔfɔi yei abɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ nuu fɔfɔii agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli lɛ, aduawai akuu ko kwraa bɛ.

english: Do palm trees stay male or female for their whole life, or can a tree change over time?
ga: Palm tsei baanyɛ afee nuu loo yoo yɛ amɛshihilɛ be fɛɛ mli. Aloo ani tsei baanyɛ atsake yɛ be kɛ bei amli?

english: An oil palm tree does not stay strictly male or female forever. A single tree goes through natural cycles where it produces male flowers for a period and then switches to producing female fruit-bearing flowers, depending on rainfall, age, and tree health.
ga: Mu tsei jeee hii kɛ yei fɛɛ anɔ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛya naanɔ. Tso kome tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔi ni ji hii lɛ amli yɛ be ko mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsakemɔ kɛya fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai yei afeemɔ nɔ. Edamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, afii ni tsei lɛ eye kɛ amɛhewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my palm trees need male flowers on the farm if only the female flowers produce fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm tso lɛ he hiaa fɔfɔi hii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Be mli ni fɔfɔi yei pɛ woɔ yibii?

english: Female flowers cannot develop into oil-rich fruit bunches without pollen. Male flowers release pollen that tiny insects and wind carry to female flowers to fertilize them so they can grow into healthy palm bunches.
ga: Pistil fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee aduawai ni fɔ eyi mli obɔ kɛji pollen bɛ mli. Fɔfɔi hii jieɔ pollen ni kooloi bibii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ woɔ lɛ kpo. Atswaa fɔfɔi yei lɛ koni ekɛ fɔfɔi yei lɛ afɔ. bɔni afee ni eda ni etsɔ tso ni mli wa

english: Why do two palm trees I planted on the same farm on the same day yield very different amounts of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei enyɔ ni midu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ woɔ yibii sɔrɔtoi kwraa lɛ?

english: If the seedlings came from uncertified or mixed seed sources, their genetic traits will differ. Just like children from the same parents grow differently, mixed palm seeds will grow at different rates and produce varying amounts of male and female flowers.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ jɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ odaseyeli loo dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli. Genetic sui lɛ baafee srɔtoi. Taakɛ gbekɛbii ni jɛ fɔlɔi kome mli lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Palm dumɔwui ni efutu lɛ daa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei ayibɔi srɔtoi.

english: Why do my young tree crops drop all their early flowers without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ miiho amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Dropping early flowers is normal for young trees because they are not yet strong enough to support heavy fruit. It can also happen if the crop suffers from heat stress, lack of water, or poor pollination during the flowering period.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ mra lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ tsei bibii amli ejaakɛ amɛhe waaa lolo bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa dɔlɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii yɛ fɔfɔi be mli.

english: If my oil palm tree is currently producing only male flowers, is there anything I can do to make it produce fruit bunches?
ga: Kɛji akɛ amrɔ nɛɛ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ lɛ, Ani ehe miihia ni mafee nɔ ko koni ewo fɔfɔii babaoo?

english: Yes, you can encourage female flowering by reducing stress on the tree. Applying proper fertilizers (especially potassium), clearing weeds, watering during dry spells, and pruning dead leaves help the tree gain the energy needed to produce female fruit bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ owo pistils lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛtsɔ haomɔ ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli (titri lɛ potassium) ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni akɛyeɔ jwɛi nɔ Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli Ni baai ni egboi ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo aduawai yei akui.

english: What is the difference between the wild palm trees growing in the bush and the improved farm varieties?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ koo mli ŋmei tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei mli kɛ ŋmɔ mli tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Wild palm trees usually have thick shells with small oil-producing flesh and yield unpredictably. Improved farm varieties (hybrids like Tenera) have thin shells and thick fruit flesh, producing significantly more palm oil and consistent fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koo mli tsei lɛ ahe tsɔi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ hei bibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba yɛ mli. Okwaafoi srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ (hybrids tamɔ Tenera) lɛ yɛ tsitsii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ aduawai amli ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmei fɔ babaoo kɛ aduawai akuu ni yɔɔ ekome.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the early rains start coming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Early rains can be deceiving; planting after just one heavy rain can destroy your seeds if a dry spell follows. Wait until the rains become steady and consistent over a week so the soil holds enough moisture for seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ. Dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ akpata odumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa ni eya nɔ otsi kome. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds as close together as possible so I can get more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Giving each plant enough space allows its roots to spread, resulting in larger, healthier crops and a bigger total harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni okpa nii babaoo

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key soil nutrient needed for leaf growth. Applying manure or the right fertilizer will give the plant the food it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and look like they are dying during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves droop in extreme heat as a natural defense to protect the plant from losing too much water. By exposing less leaf surface to the hot sun, the plant saves water until the temperature cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Tsei buɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ kɛtsɔ baa lɛ nɔ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ hulu la fioo ko nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does adding animal manure to my field actually help my crops grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Animal manure acts like rich food for the earth. It slowly releases essential nutrients into the soil and helps the ground hold onto rainwater longer, keeping your crops fed and watered between rains.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii babaoo jɛɛhe kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ fiofio kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do weeds in my farm lower my crop yield even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and act like thieves in your farm. They quickly drink up the water and suck away the soil nutrients meant for your crops, leaving your plants weak and unable to produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ nu oya ni amɛmuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over, while making pests feel at home. Switching to crops like beans or groundnuts every other season helps fix nitrogen back into the dirt naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai nuɔ he akɛ amɛyɛ shia. Ni aaatsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii adumɔ nɔ daa be lɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last maize harvest grow weaker plants than certified seeds from agro-dealers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔ fe dumɔwui ni okwaayeli mlijalɔ lɛ wo he odase lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are bred in controlled settings specifically for high energy, pest resistance, and high yield. Saved seeds lose those strong traits over generations, leading to uneven growth and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ anɔ yɛ he ko ni akudɔ lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛha hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui ni mli wa lɛ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee kɛ ŋmaa bibioo baa.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat holes in the fresh center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets young maize. Checking your crops early and applying recommended natural remedies or safe sprays in the center whorl of the leaf will stop them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa titri ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are some of my crops staying short and stunted even though the rains have been good this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi faaa ni amɛgbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be nɛɛ mli moŋ?

english: Stunted growth during good rains usually means something is wrong underground—such as soil that is packed too hard for roots to stretch, root-eating pests, or a complete lack of nutrients in the dirt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shweremɔ ni akpaa yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nɔ ko etɔ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe. Kooloi ni yeɔ shishifãi loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwraa

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and getting yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves curling and turning yellow is usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried by tiny whiteflies. It slows down plant growth and reduces root yield if infected stems are used for planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni yɔɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ fioo akɛ mɛi ni hiɛɔ lɛ Ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ehaa shishifãi ni baa shi lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ akɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ tsu nii kɛdu.

english: Why do my maize leaves get brown spots and dry up during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Brown spots on wet maize leaves are often caused by leaf blight, a fungal disease that spreads fast in humid weather. Planting with enough space between crops allows air to dry the leaves and reduce disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa sɛɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Dumɔ ni gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my crop is sick from a virus or just wilting from heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ emɔ hela kɛjɛ hela ko mli loo amɛmiigbo kɛkɛ kɛjɛ latsaa mli?

english: Heat causes the whole plant to droop evenly during hot sunshine and recover at night, while a virus causes permanent leaf twisting, yellow patterns, or stunted growth that stays even after heavy rain.
ga: Dɔlɛ lɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ. amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛhe wa amɛ gbɛkɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hela lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ daa, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo amɛkwɛɛɛ kwraa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa po sɛɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping all their flowers without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛduuu tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when the air gets too hot, when water is lacking, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant focus on growing big green leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, kɛ́ nu faaa, loo kɛ́ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my pepper plants remain very small and weak even after I feed them fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo amɛmli moŋ?

english: Stunted pepper plants often suffer from invisible soil pests like root-knot nematodes or viral infections that block roots from taking up water and nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni anaaa, tamɔ root-knot nematodes loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ yeɔ dwarf pepper tsei lɛ anɔ amanehulu. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea crops produce plenty of green leaves but almost no seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi eshwɛ fioo ni dumɔwui ŋmɔji bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce too many leaves and few pods when planted in soil with excess nitrogen or when planted too close together, which prevents sunlight from reaching the lower branches to trigger flowering.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ baai babaoo tsɔ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Enɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe ni ekɛ fɔfɔi aba.

english: Why do cocoa trees produce fewer pods when all the big forest trees around them are cleared?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni koo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ daa lɛ? Ani ajie fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli?

english: Young and mature cocoa trees need partial shade to stay cool; direct hot sun stresses the plant, burns leaves, and attracts destructive insects like mirids.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii ni eda lɛ he miihia hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i. Hulu la ni mli edɔ, ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tsei haoɔ, eshãa baai, ni egbalaa koolooi ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ glase ni edɔ.

english: Why are my plantain stems bending over and leaves snapping off before fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni baai lɛ fãa dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: This snapping happens when plantain roots are destroyed by root weevils or fungal diseases like Black Sigatoka, which cut off water supply and weaken the plant frame.
ga: Nɛkɛ fãmɔ nɛɛ baa kɛji akɛ shishifãi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka, ni fiteɔ nu ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ fãji lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ fite dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why does an extension officer need to cut off sick leaves and take them away from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ afo helatsɛmɛi ahe woji ni amɛjie kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Taking leaf samples lets experts inspect the plant closely under a microscope or test it to identify whether the problem is caused by bacteria, fungi, or a virus before giving you the right treatment.
ga: Baai ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋaalelɔi kɛ tsɔne bibioo ko ni akɛkwɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ kwɛɔ tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ loo kaa koni amɛna kɛji helatsɛmɛi, ŋmeii, loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ naagba lɛ ba. Dani ebaaha bo tsofa ni sa

english: Why do my yam vines turn black and die early long before the tubers are big enough?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ oya dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa lɛ?

english: Early blackening of yam vines is caused by yam anthracnose, a fungal disease that spreads quickly in rain showers, stopping tubers from growing to their full size.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni ji anthracnose lɛ haa ŋmeii tsei lɛ feɔ diŋ mra. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ mli. Enɛ haaa yitso lɛ adara kɛyashɛɛɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi be mli ni ekã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads during wet weather, or 'cherelle wilt,' which is the tree's natural way of shedding extra pods it cannot support.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Fungal hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli, loo ‘cherel wilt’, ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejieɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni enyɛŋ eye ebua lɛ.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my young maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛtee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ amli

english: Your maize is likely attacked by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which eat the center growing leaves (whort) and need early treatment with recommended sprays or neem extracts before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tutuaa o-abele lɛ. (caterpillars) ni ehe miihia ni akɛ neem spray loo tsofa ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ajieɔ he ŋaa lɛ atsu he nii mra dani akpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl tightly upward and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the sap and transmitting viruses, which stops normal leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ kpaɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot and smell bad underground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water deprives the roots of air, allowing soil fungi to multiply and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ babaoo ni amɛgbalaa ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plants without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when temperatures get too high, when the soil alternates between too dry and too wet, or when insects fail to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ tsɔ teŋ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do my yam plants grow much better when I give them tall wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ha lɛ lɛ? Ha amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves higher into direct sunlight for photosynthesizing food, while keeping the leaves off wet soil where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, ni amɛwoɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ aya nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee amɛ niyenii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during light rain and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and microscopic worms (nematodes) or stem borer insects often eat into the roots and corm, weakening the tree's anchor in the ground.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni ŋmeii bibii (Nematodes) loo kooloi ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ osɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when planted in open fields without tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under direct intense sunlight; tall shade plants like plantains shield them from heat and help keep the air moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains lɛ hu tsiɔ dɔlɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tseɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry leaves and grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai kɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil (mulching) acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the earth, cools down root temperatures, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli latsaa lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why does adding dried chicken manure to my farm work better for crop growth than planting in bare soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ akɛ tsina ŋmei ni egbi fata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chicken manure adds key nutrients like nitrogen to the soil while improving the soil's ability to hold water and feed helpful soil organisms.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa niyenii haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their foliage and stems are tender. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them protects them from heat stress and keeps the soil moist while they build strength.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahewɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ yɛ be mli ni etswaa hewalɛ emaa shi lɛ

english: Why are the leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso ni miida lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer at the right growth stage helps the leaves green up and photosynthesize properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni efee fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller yields when I plant cassava on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Cassava heavy feeds on soil nutrients every season. Continuous planting on the same spot exhausts the soil, which is why rotating crops with legumes like beans or cowpeas helps restore natural fertility.
ga: Cassava yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli. Tsei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land make the soil better for my next crop season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina ŋmei ni adu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have friendly bacteria in their root nodules that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. When the roots decay after harvest, this natural fertilizer remains in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ helai ni haa mɔ he feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers turning soft and rotting in the ground after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess standing water prevents oxygen from reaching the roots, causing suffocation and root rot diseases. Cassava needs well-draining soil so water moves away easily without drowning the underground tubers.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ baa. Cassava biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli oya ni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieee nu mli.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant sheds flowers to conserve energy for basic survival.
ga: Tomato baagbee shi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up during the hot afternoon even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Leaf curling in high temperatures is a natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to sunlight to protect itself from losing water faster than roots can absorb it.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ he yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei baa amɛhiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni amɛfiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ lɛ he.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I harvest more crops from my land?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ, Ani mikɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmaa lɛ eyaaa hiɛ?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in thin, weak stalks and smaller cobs, whereas proper spacing allows each plant to yield fully.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná yibiiwoo ni fa.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rain and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the ground. As heavy fruit bunches grow, the plant becomes top-heavy, so propping the stems with sturdy wooden poles prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tso ni mli wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekaje shishi.

english: What is eating small holes in the leaves of my young maize and leaving dark dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of young maize to feed on tender growth. Applying recommended control measures directly into the central funnel protects the plant's growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye ŋmãa ni mli tse lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ tso lɛ tsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees look weak or stressed right after I finish plucking the pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ loo eyɛ haomɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ajie ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Plucking pods takes away stored energy from the tree and leaves small wound spots. The tree experiences temporary shock while it works to heal those spots and build up new energy for future growth.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ, ejieɔ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli, ni ehaa pilamɔ bibioo ko baa. Tso lɛ baaná be kukuoo mli shoofeemɔ beni etsuɔ ​​nii koni etsa nakai hei lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ hee aba kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli dalɛ lɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa tree if I pull the pods off with my hands instead of cutting them?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ minine jie ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafolɔ amɛ?

english: Pulling pods tears the flower cushion on the bark where future pods grow. Using a sharp knife or hook makes a clean cut that prevents permanent damage to future harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ agbala ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ kushin yɛ he ni wɔsɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne loo ŋmei ni naa wa tsu nii lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ he tseɔ. Enɛ baatsi nɔ ni baafite wɔsɛɛ ŋmaa lɛ naa daa.

english: Is it safe to leave broken cocoa pod husks lying near my growing trees after harvest?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaashi kookoo ŋmɔji ni ekumɔ yɛ tsei ni miida lɛ ahe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving husks on the farm floor attracts pests and breeds diseases like black pod fungus, which can easily spread to your healthy, growing cocoa trees.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ekɛ helai tamɔ black pod fungus baa, ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ oya.

english: How many times in a year should I clear the weeds around my cocoa trees?
ga: Esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei yɛ afi mli?

english: Clearing weeds about three times a year is ideal because it stops aggressive weeds from stealing water, sunlight, and soil food from your cocoa crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ aaafee shii etɛ yɛ afi mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ehaaa jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ aju nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ o-cocoa tsei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why does my soil feel weak even though I clear weeds from my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Clearing weeds removes competition, but every harvest takes nutrients out of the earth. Without returning goodness to the soil through compost or fertilizer, the land gradually loses its strength.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛyaa. Shi kpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kpakpa ekoŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli fiofio

english: Will trimming off extra branches from my cocoa trees hurt the crop?
ga: Ani niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Light pruning helps by allowing air and sunlight to reach all parts of the tree to prevent disease, but cutting off too much at once will shock the tree and lower your yield.
ga: Tso lɛ he nibii ni afolɔ fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni ehaa eshɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe koni helai akamɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ ofolɔ babaoo shikome lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ he afee shoo ni ebaaha onibii ni oooha lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do some of the tiny young pods on my cocoa tree dry up and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji lɛ No hewɔ lɛ ani mi-cacao tsei lɛ egbi ni amɛji ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is called cherelle wilt. It is the tree's natural way of dropping extra pods it cannot afford to feed when it experiences heat, drought, or lack of nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ eshwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye niyenii kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be, hɔmɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa plants struggle to survive when there are no big trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight because it burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil around their roots before they grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ ebaashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ agbi dani amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ.

english: Dropping leaves is a survival trick trees use during dry weather to reduce water loss, though keeping shade trees nearby helps protect them from losing too many leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ko ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni nu egbiɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyɛ mli akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ bɛŋkɛ moŋ Enɛ baaye abua ni ebaatsi baai babaoo ni elaaje lɛ naa.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce thousands of flowers, but only a few turn into real pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: The tree produces many flowers to attract tiny pollinating insects, but it naturally sheds the flowers that do not get pollinated or that the tree is too weak to feed.
ga: Tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo koni amɛkɛgbala fɔfɔi bibii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ Fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollination lɛ baagbee shi. Aloo tso lɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye nii.

english: Why do buyers in the market prefer long-grain rice over the local varieties I grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa ni ŋmãa kakadaŋŋ yɔɔ mli fe maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Long-grain rice stays firm and fluffy without sticking together when cooked, which many urban buyers prefer for popular dishes like Jollof, even though local rice varieties often have richer natural flavor and higher nutrient levels.
ga: Omɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee kɛji ahoo. Maŋtiase mli jarayelɔi babaoo sumɔɔ ŋmãa srɔtoi ni ehe gbɛi tamɔ Jollof, eyɛ mli akɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni naa wa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo moŋ.

english: Why do some of my rice plants grow very tall leaves but fail to produce heavy grain heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa shi ewooo dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer makes rice plants waste energy growing excess green leaves instead of flowers and grains. Balanced feeding, especially with phosphorus and potassium, helps the plant focus on forming full grains.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛduɔ baai eŋɔli ni fa fe nine yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmaa najiaŋ. Niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa titri lɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing high-yielding rice?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Rice grows best in fertile soils that retain water well, such as clay-rich soil in low-lying valley bottoms (inland valleys), or fields where water can be easily supplied and kept around the roots during growth.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ eyi nɔ obɔ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. (mli jɔɔ lɛ) loo ŋmɔji ni abaanyɛ aná nu yɛ mli mlɛo ni akɛto shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested produce spoil so quickly before I can get it to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya dani eyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested crops continue to breathe and generate heat. Leaving them under direct sun, packing them too tightly in sacks without air movement, or delaying transport traps heat and moisture, which causes fast rotting.
ga: Tsei ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛfeɔ dɔlɛ. Shi ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Akɛwo kotoku ko ni mli wa tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli mli. Aloo sɛɛkuu ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ lɛlɛ mli lɛ baaha dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i aba. ni haa efiteɔ oya lɛ

english: Why does my local rice break into small pieces when it goes through the milling machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa lɛ fãa bibii bibii kɛ́ etsɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice grains break easily during milling if they are dried too fast in harsh midday sun or milled when the grains are either too wet or too dry. Gentle drying in thin layers helps keep the grains whole.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ fãa oya yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛji amɛgbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli. loo kɔla kɛji dumɔwui lɛ edɔ tsɔ loo amɛgbi tsɔ. Gbi blɛoo yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni abuɔ ŋmaa fɛɛ he.

english: Should I change to growing imported crop seeds or stick with our traditional local seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matsake kɛya dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ anɔ loo makɛ wɔ kusum, ni ji maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi?

english: Imported or improved seed varieties often meet specific market demands in big cities, but local varieties are usually more resistant to local weather and pests. You can start by testing improved seeds on a small plot while keeping your reliable local crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akɛbaa maŋsɛɛ loo ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ jarayeli hei pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ maji wuji amli lɛ ahiamɔ nii ahe nii. Shi he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ kooloi bibii. Obaanyɛ oje shishi kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ akamɔ yɛ he bibioo ko nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ.

english: How can improving my crop management help me earn enough money to build a house for my family?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ bɔ ni mikwɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛma shĩa maha miweku lɛ?

english: Using certified seeds, proper planting distance, and good harvesting methods increases your yield per acre and crop quality, allowing you to sell more produce at premium market prices and increase your overall profit.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii Dumɔ he ni sa Kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ gbɛi kpakpai haa yibiiwoo ni anáa yɛ acre kome mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ onibii babaoo yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ. ni oha sɛɛnamɔi fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young crops turning yellow early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops lack essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is sitting around the roots for too long and preventing the plant from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu eta shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni eha tso lɛ miigbɔjɔ.

english: Why is it better to plant my crop seeds in straight rows instead of scattering them across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu aduawai dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Row planting ensures every crop gets equal access to sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with nearby plants, and it makes weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Row planting haa tsei fɛɛ náa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ Ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my crops look weak even after I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture in the soil to dissolve and reach the roots. If applied during dry spells, or placed too close to the plant stems, it cannot be absorbed properly and can even burn the roots.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ ni eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi loo akɛwo tso lɛ he tsɔ lɛ Enyɛŋ eŋɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ po.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is essential plant food in the soil. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or when weeds steal the food from your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛji jwɛi ju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. When the ground dries out completely between waterings, the plant drops its flowers to protect itself and save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into tight shapes and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves to suck out the sap, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. It prevents the leaf from catching sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ mites loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛmu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Tsi baai lɛ anaa koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot under the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the field and water stays on the ground for too long, the roots drown, allowing soil fungi to infect and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eyi ŋmɔji amli ni nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ hela ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests now compared to five years ago, even though I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe bɔ ni eji afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii moŋ.

english: Soil loses its natural nutrients every time a crop is harvested. If you grow the same crop year after year without adding organic manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil gets tired and empty, leading to poor yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji akɛ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee shoo ni ebaafee shwɛm. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Because no single plant gets enough food, they grow tall, thin, and weak, producing small or incomplete ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ eko kwraa enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛkɛ lɛ tsei lɛ daraa, amɛfeɔ mlɛo, ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni no haa abele toi bibii loo eshɛɛɛ he.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts in my field help improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny knots on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the plants die, this nitrogen stays behind as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Eyɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni egbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air so their leaves can trap as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves create energy, which travels down to make the yam tubers big and heavy underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ agboi ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to survival in your local soil and climate. They absorb water and soil food much quicker than domesticated crops, allowing them to sprout and spread fast.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei. Enɛ haa amɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya.

english: Is it bad to water my vegetable garden in the middle of the day when the sun is hottest?
ga: Ani ejaaa akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Watering in the hot afternoon wastes water because the strong sun evaporates most of it before it reaches the roots. Hot soil can also warm up standing water on leaves, causing plant stress and leaf damage.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baafite nu ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli babaoo baaho dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha nu ni damɔ baai anɔ lɛ adɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure around the base of the plants will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ afata he Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 8 and 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and you can carefully dig around one plant to see if the tubers under the ground are thick enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Ni obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli. Kwɛmɔ tso kome mli jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to heap loose soil around the base of my groundnut plants when they flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa sũ ni mli ewo muji lɛ naa mibɔleɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ shishi beni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: After flowering, groundnut plants produce long stems called pegs that must grow down into the soil to form the nuts underground. Soft, heaped soil makes it easier for these pegs to enter the ground and develop big groundnuts.
ga: Kɛji amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ woɔ tsei kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs. ni esa akɛ adu awo shikpɔŋ mli koni akɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ haa ewaa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baagbee shikpɔŋ ni amɛdara amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I have to put wooden sticks next to my yam vines for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo sweet potato wain tso ko masɛi koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach up into the sunlight so the leaves can make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents diseases and helps you get larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni hulu la ashɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ afee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akamɔ bo ni eye ebua bo ni oná sweet potatoes wuji.

english: What is causing the ragged holes in my maize leaves and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ pores baa ŋmãa baai amli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Ragged holes are usually caused by caterpillars called Fall Armyworms that eat the center leaves of the maize plant. Spraying recommended treatments directly into the center funnel of the plant early in the morning or late evening will help get rid of them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ fall armyworms ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni etse ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ shwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot, or when the plant does not get enough water consistently. Keeping the soil evenly moist and ensuring plants receive morning sunlight will help the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi hulu la lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves. Spraying the undersides of the leaves with a simple neem leaf water extract or insecticidal soap can stop these insects and let healthy leaves grow back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem mli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa kooloi nɛɛ ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct heat and full sun. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that shade young cocoa trees, keeping the soil moist and protecting them during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: If too many shoots grow at the base, they steal food and water from the main plant. Trimming them away so only one or two strong shoots remain ensures the main plant has enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni eshi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do farmers cover the ground around crop stems with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks direct hot sunlight. This keeps moisture in the soil longer after watering, reduces soil temperature, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la ni mli edɔ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni awo mli lɛ sɛɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ aba shi ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃
