english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food plants need to stay green and grow leaves, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help them recover.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni adu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans, cowpeas, and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, that stored food remains in the earth to nourish the next crop you plant there.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei, kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nakai niyenii ni ato lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves during extreme heat to protect themselves from losing water. It is their natural way of sweating less and holding onto moisture until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ latsaa fioo ni aŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant gets stressed by sudden heatwaves or irregular watering. Without a steady supply of water and moderate temperatures, the plant cannot feed the flowers, so it drops them to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni baa trukaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛji nu ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo ni sa bɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aha fɔfɔi lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing shoots in the barn even when they are not in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from their resting phase when warm, humid weather arrives. The tuber uses its internal water and nutrient stores to sprout shoots because it senses that the rainy season is starting.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛ wɔɔ be mli kɛji dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i kɔɔyɔŋ ba. Tui lɛ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ejaakɛ amɛnuɔ he akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide broad shade leaves that act as natural umbrellas, keeping the ground cool and moist while the young cocoa gets established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one plantain tree causes them to steal food and water from each other. Leaving only one main plant and one successor ensures you get big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he Dumɔwu kome pɛ baaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tsei krokomɛi adɛŋ. Tso titri kome pɛ ni oyɔɔ kɛ nɔ ni baaye esɛɛ lɛ haa onine shɛɔ aduawai wuji ni tsii nɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest since I cannot see them under the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ejaakɛ anaaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the main leaves start to yellow and fall off the lower stem, typically around 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety you planted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai titrii lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi kɛjɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ tso srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot continuously exhausts specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and soil diseases that target maize to build up in numbers year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; their roots aggressively absorb water, sunlight, and fertilizer before your crops can reach them, leaving your crops starved of essential nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa ni oduɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen, an essential food for plant leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps the plants regain their deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei ahe baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ su ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any peppers can actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Plants drop flowers when they get too stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of plant food like potassium. Watering regularly during hot dry spells and feeding the soil helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni fe nine, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsei amli niyenii tamɔ potassium ni bɛ lɛ miihao amɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ni okɛ sũ lɛ awo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, ebafeɔ chili ni hi kɛha gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ.

english: Why are little caterpillars eating the inside hearts of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiye mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli tsui lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a pest common in Ghana that hides deep inside maize leaf funnels to eat the soft stem. Spraying a neem water solution or recommended chemical early in the morning reaches them before they ruin the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmeii ahe ŋmeii amli shɔŋŋ koni eye ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Neem nu loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe dani tsei lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and rot when the rain starts falling heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excess rain and wet leaves create the perfect condition for fungal diseases to spread rapidly. Spacing your plants further apart allows wind to dry the leaves quickly, preventing fungi from destroying the crop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Gbɛ ni kã tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ egbiɔ oya. ni etsĩ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa

english: Can I save the seeds from the high-yielding maize I harvested this season to plant again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni mikpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: If you planted hybrid seeds, saving them for the next season results in weaker plants with tiny yields. It is best to buy fresh certified hybrid seeds every season, or use local open-pollinated varieties if you plan to save seeds from harvest.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ Okɛto kɛha be ni baa lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaawo yibii fioo pɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa be mli. loo okɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi ni agbele naa lɛ atsu nii. Kɛji oto gbɛjianɔ koni ohere dumɔwui kɛjɛ kpamɔ mli

english: Intercropping maize and cassava allows you to maximize your land use and reduce farming risk. Maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving space for the slower-growing cassava to expand later without competing for sunlight.
ga: Abele kɛ ŋmei ni ooodu lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa osharai ni yɔɔ okwaayeli mli lɛ baa shi. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Enɛ haa gbɛ haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ sɛɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la he.

english: How can I tell if my crop is dying from too much water or from lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu babaoo loo nu ni faaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ miigboi?

english: A thirsty plant wilts with dry, crispy leaves, while a plant in soggy soil wilts with soft, yellowing leaves and rotting roots. Digging two inches into the soil with your finger lets you feel whether the root area is completely dry or waterlogged.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ gboɔ kɛ baai ni egbi ni ŋmɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ baagboi kɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ shishifãi ni egboi. Tsɔmɔmɔ niji enyɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua bo ni onu he akɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ.

english: Why do weeds on my farm grow much faster than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants designed by nature to grab water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds within the first three to four weeks of planting gives your crops the head start they need to shade out future weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni adebɔɔ fee koni ejie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛjie jwɛi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay very small and thin even after growing for over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nɔ ni fe afi edu amɛ moŋ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil to expand into big tubers. If the land is hard-packed or flooded with water, or if insects continuously strip the leaves, the plant cannot store the starch needed to grow fat roots.
ga: Kassava shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ bulbs agboi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ loo kooloi bibii ŋmɔɔ baai lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ Tsei hu nyɛŋ ato ŋmeii ni he hiaa koni shishifãi ni yɔɔ fɔ lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ ato.

english: Why does my harvested maize get eaten by little insects inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii eyi mi-abele nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ye nii yɛ mi shĩa lɛ mli?

english: Storage insects like weevils multiply quickly when harvested grain still holds hidden moisture inside. Drying your maize in the sun until a grain cracks sharply between your teeth before storing it in airtight bags prevents insects from destroying your yield.
ga: Kplukai ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faa oya kɛ́ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtee mli lolo. Kɛ́ okɛ hulu lɛ miigbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ baatswa yɛ onyanyɔji ateŋ dani okɛwo vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi bibii akafite oŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to heat and burn under full direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava planted nearby to act as umbrellas and protect their leaves until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni amɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put long sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? ni eŋɔ tso nine kakadaŋŋ Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb upward so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight. When sunlight hits all the leaves evenly, the leaves produce the food that travels down into the soil to grow big, healthy yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ hulu la lɛ tswa baai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, baai lɛ woɔ niyenii ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the maize plant is hungry for nutrients, especially nitrogen, from the soil. The plant is taking food from its older bottom leaves and sending it to feed the growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ he miihia niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Tso lɛ miiye niyenii kɛmiijɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni ekɛmiimaje baai ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling up like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl when tiny pests suck the juice out of the young leaf tissue, or when the plant is affected by a plant virus. The curling is the plant's stress response to being damaged.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ miinu nu lɛ kɛjɛ baa bibioo lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yeɔ tsei anɔ hewalɛ. Curling ji bɔ ni tso ko haoɔ ehaa kɛji efite.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and wilt in the hot afternoon sun but stand upright again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi shidaamɔ ni ja ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, leaves lose water into the hot air faster than roots can draw it from the ground. Wilting is the plant's way of conserving moisture, and it recovers when temperatures cool down at night.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Withering ji gbɛ ni tso tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. ni ebaahe ewa lɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive and grow. When excess water stays trapped around the roots for too long, the roots drown, lose oxygen, and begin to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛnáaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ.

english: How do cowpeas or beans help make the soil fertile for my next maize crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When these plants die, the nitrogen stays behind as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ gboi lɛ Nitrogen baakã he ahi shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my tomato plants before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or lack of water. When stressed, the plant sacrifices its flowers to save energy so the main plant can survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei kɛ fɔfɔi shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he bɔni afee ni tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does my main plantain stem grow so many small shoots at its base, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso titri lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? A lot at the the Ni ani esa akɛ majie loo esaaa akɛ majie?

english: Plantain plants produce shoots, called suckers, to continue growing new plants. However, if you leave all of them, they steal food and water from the main mother plant, so you must prune them down to keep the main fruit healthy.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baawo ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii koni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei heei. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛji oshɛrɛ amɛ fɛɛ oshwie lɛ, Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ofolɔ amɛ koni aduawai titri lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my grafted sweet orange tree suddenly growing branches from the bottom that produce sour fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet orange tso ni akɛwo mihe lɛ nine kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ ni ewoɔ yibii ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Grafted orange trees are made by joining a sweet orange branch onto a tough wild rootstock. Branches growing from below the graft line belong to the wild root and produce sour fruit, so they must be cut off.
ga: Akɛ akutu tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ feɔ akutu niji ni ŋɔɔ ni akɛwo shishifã ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tso ni akɛwo mli lɛ shishi lɛ ji koo mli shishifã lɛ nɔ ni ewoɔ yibii ni mli edɔ. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ ajie kɛya.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is missing key nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is sitting around the roots for too long, preventing the plant from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, loo nu eta shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak with small fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛ aduawai bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When planted too closely, crops fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. Instead of growing thick stems and large fruits, they stretch upward to reach the light.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji Moŋ lɛ, ekpãa ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eha la lɛ abote mli.

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread diseases between plants, or by severe heat stress causing the plant to conserve water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa tsei ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa tsei kwɛɔ nu nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I see leaf-eating insects on my crops early in the morning, but they disappear by afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ leebi shi amɛlaajeɔ shwane lɛ?

english: Many crop pests hide during the hottest part of the day to avoid drying out and dying in the sun, coming out only during cooler morning or night hours to feed.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo teeɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛkagbi ni amɛkagboi yɛ hulu lɛ mli. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛyatao niyenii leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ pɛ.

english: Tubers rot underground when water collects in the soil without draining, creating wet conditions where fungal diseases can easily invade and rot the roots.
ga: Tubers lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ baa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ abote mli oya ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ afite.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep dropping off the tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from water shortages, insect damage to the stems, or when the tree senses it lacks the energy to support full pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji amɛkɛ nu ni faaa kpe. Kplukai ni fiteɔ tso lɛ shishi Aloo be mli ni tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ebɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does cutting off unnecessary branches or extra shoots help my crops produce bigger yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa loo tsei ashishifãi krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches prevents the plant from wasting energy on leaves it does not need, allowing it to send food directly into growing larger fruits and seeds.
ga: Kpojiemɔ kroko ni fata he lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni ataooo lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ niyenii majeɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo aduawai kɛ dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why does my crop field dry out so quickly after rain, and how can I keep the ground moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Direct hot sunlight causes soil water to evaporate rapidly. Covering the soil around plants with dry grass or leaves shields the ground and keeps moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops struggle even after I spread fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee basabasa yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that steal water and fertilizer nutrients from the soil before your crop roots have a chance to take them up.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: How do I know if my soil is deep and good enough for growing heavy plantain bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akwɛ dumɔwui ni mli tse?

english: Plantains need dark, rich soil that breaks apart easily and lets rain drain through without pooling, as heavy waterlogged soil causes roots to rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni baa nii lɛ he miihia plantains. Efiteɔ oya ni ehaa nugbɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why must my farm soil be soft before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee blɛoo dani adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Soft soil allows delicate young root sprouts to easily push downward into the ground to find water and nutrients. If the soil is too hard, seeds struggle to sprout and roots cannot grow properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ naa wa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my seeds if I plant them when the ground is hard and dry?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni egbi lɛ?

english: Seeds planted in hard, dry ground usually fail to germinate, or they dry up and die before they can push through the surface because there is no moisture to start their growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu yɛ hei ni wa ni jɛmɛ egbi lɛ kwɛɛɛ loo amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu bɛ ni baaje dalɛ shishi.

english: How can I check if my soil has enough moisture for planting?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ana kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔ?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil in your palm. If it forms a soft ball that holds together without dripping wet water, the moisture is just right for planting your crops.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ fioo ko mli yɛ onine mli. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sa kɛha otsei lɛ akwɛmɔ.

english: What should I do if the rain suddenly stops right after I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa beni midu nii sɛɛ?

english: If a dry spell occurs after planting, try to manually water the seeds if possible, or spread dry grass and leaves (mulch) around the planting spots to trap soil moisture until rains return.
ga: Kɛji hɔmɔ ba yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Bɔɔmɔdɛŋ ni bo diɛŋtsɛ okɛ nu awo dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛji ebaahi. Aloo okɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai afɔ nɔ. (Mulch) yɛ he ni adu nii yɛ lɛ he koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my young seedlings dry up so quickly when it stops raining for just one week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa otsi kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have very shallow root systems that stay near the top layer of soil. Since sunlight dries out the topsoil first during a rainless week, the baby plants quickly lose access to water.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ otsii ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ amli. Tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛná nu oya.

english: Should I keep planting my field if a dry spell begins?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maya nɔ madu nii kɛji ebɔi gbimɔ?

english: No, it is safer to stop planting during a dry spell. Planting without steady rainfall wastes your expensive seeds and labor because the seeds will not receive the water needed to grow.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookpa dumɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ baafite dumɔwui ni jara wa ni ebaafite onitsumɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ anine shɛŋ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops slow down or stop growing during dry weather even when they are not dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ loo amɛkpaa shweremɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa shi lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgbooo moŋ?

english: Crops need water to transport food and nutrients from the soil up into their leaves. During dry periods, plants conserve energy by pausing active growth until water becomes available again.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ amɛdalɛ ni amɛkpaa yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu baa ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does putting dry grass around my crops help protect them from dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ he?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves acts like a blanket that shades the soil from direct sunlight, keeping the soil cool and stopping moisture from evaporating away quickly.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why is it important to use weed control chemicals on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu nii?

english: Applying weed chemicals before planting clears out competing weeds early, ensuring your young crops have full access to soil nutrients, light, and water without fighting other plants.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi tsu nii dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha otsei bibii lɛ ana niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ, la kɛ nu mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsei krokomɛi awui.

english: How long should I wait to plant my seeds after spraying chemical weedkillers on my field?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ ni madu dumɔwui beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ efɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ?

english: You should generally wait several days to a week after spraying so the chemical has enough time to kill the weeds completely without damaging your new seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, esa akɛ omɛ gbii babaoo kɛyashi otsi kome beni okɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsofai lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛgbeɔ jwɛi lɛ kwraa ni amɛfiteee dumɔwui heei.

english: Why do my crop leaves burn when I spray plant medicine during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛtsaa tsei lɛ shwie amɛnɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spraying crop medicine in the hot afternoon sun causes the liquid to evaporate quickly and magnifies the sun's heat on the leaves, which causes chemical burns. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when it is cool.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu lɛ shwie tsei anɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya. ni ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni kɛ tsofai ni shãa lɛ baa Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: How can I tell if the crop medicine I sprayed is actually strong enough to protect my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ abu miŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Effective medicine shows signs within a few days, such as insect pests falling off the leaves, fungal spots stopping their spread, or healthy new shoots emerging from the crop.
ga: Tsofa ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ jieɔ hela lɛ he okadii akpo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Fungal he tsɔi lɛ kpaɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ. loo ŋmeii heei ni mli wa ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or when excessive rain washes the nutrients away beyond the roots' reach.
ga: Abɛi baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa fe shishifãi lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the middle of the day even when the soil still has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, crop leaves lose moisture faster through the air than roots can pull from the ground, so the plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tse lɛ baai lɛ laajeɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi.

english: Extreme atmospheric heat, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects can stress the plant, causing it to drop flowers before fruits can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ faaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná haomɔ Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water-loving fungus that thrives in excess shade and high humidity, spreading rapidly over pods during the heavy rainy season.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ pods lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa beaŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small when I plant the stems close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close, their roots compete fiercely for sunlight, soil space, and nutrients, preventing the tubers from expanding.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ waa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ amɛshwã

english: How does adding organic manure help my crops survive long dry spells?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Organic manure acts like a sponge in the soil, retaining moisture and releasing nutrients slowly so crops can feed even when rain is scarce.
ga: Organic fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii fiofio. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii ana niyenii kɛji nugbɔ faaa po.

english: Why do insect pests attack my pepper farm more heavily during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warm, dry weather speeds up the life cycle of pests like insects, allowing them to reproduce faster while heat stress weakens the natural defenses of the plants.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ kooloi bibii lɛ ashihilɛ yaa oya, ni ehaa amɛfɔɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dɔlɛ mli haomɔ haa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu hewalɛ baa shi.

english: Why does rain shortly after spraying make my weed medicine stop working?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ haaa etsu nii lɛ?

english: Rain washes the liquid medicine off the weed leaves before the plant has enough time to absorb the chemical into its roots and stem.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ tsofa ni ji nu ni yɔɔ jwɛi baai lɛ amli lɛ he dani tsei lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaajie tsofai lɛ awo amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Cocoa naturally grows under the shade of big forest trees. Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and small roots that dry out easily under harsh sunlight, so they need shade plants like plantains to protect them until they grow strong.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kooi wuji lɛ ashishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii. ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ aná tsei tamɔ plantains ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara waa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize are usually a sign that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize regain its rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell before the main rains fully settle. If your seeds sprout during that dry spell, the young roots will dry out and die in the hot soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ baa shi kwraa. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ Shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for the tubers under the ground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground, which prevents leaf rot and disease.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ akafite kɛ helai.

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots fight over the same water and soil nutrients, while their leaves block each other's sunlight. Giving each plant enough space allows it to feed properly and grow bigger fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ abua tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni eyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ daraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing white powdery spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ powda lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with a white powder are caused by tiny sap-sucking pests called cassava mealybugs or whiteflies. They drain the plant's strength, so planting clean, pest-resistant cuttings is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Powda yɛŋ ko ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ kɛbaa lɛ yɛ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli. Atsɛɔ amɛ hu akɛ kasava mealybugs loo ŋmeii yɛŋ. Amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei niji ni he tse ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛŋ adu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Maize sucks out the same specific nutrients from the soil year after year, leaving the ground tired and empty. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients to the soil and stops maize pests from building up.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ tɔlɛ ni efeɔ efolo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ, ni ehaaa ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds steal so much strength from my crops if they are all just plants growing in the same dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiju hewalɛ babaoo kɛmiijɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ? Fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛkɛ ji amɛ.

english: Weeds are wild and grow much faster than crops, so their roots drink up the fertilizer and water in the soil before your crops can reach it, effectively starving your crops of food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli jwɛi ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ nuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I trim off some of the lower leaves and branches from my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-pepper tso lɛ baai kɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Cutting away unnecessary lower branches prevents the plant from wasting energy on extra leaves. Instead, the plant redirects all its food and water into producing bigger, healthier pepper fruits.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Tso lɛ tsɔɔ eniyenii kɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ agbo ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba moŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wither and collapse even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigboi ni amɛmiigbee shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Too much water or waterlogged soil suffocates the plant roots and encourages fungal rot underground. When the roots rot, they can no longer absorb water up to the stem, causing the plant to wither despite the wet soil.
ga: Nu babaoo loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ahe hewalɛ. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ egbo lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛmɔmɔ nu kɛyashɛ tso lɛ shishi dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei gboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are starving for nitrogen in the soil or are not getting enough water to draw up nutrients from the earth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to spread dry grass around our vegetable beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ jwɛi afɔse wɔ aduawai ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating in the heat, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ latsaa be mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in weak, thin stalks that produce tiny cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii feɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of green leaves, but the tubers in the ground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or poor drainage, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or when tiny insects attack the delicate flowers before fruit can form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii baye nɔ. Etutuaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo dani ewoɔ aduawai.

english: Why is it better to water or spray my crops early in the morning rather than in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooofɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu loo oooshwie nɔ leebi fe shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Watering in the afternoon sun causes water to evaporate before plants can drink it, and hot water droplets left on leaves can burn the plant.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tso lɛ nuɔ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashã.

english: Excessive rainfall and wet weather encourage a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads easily when trees are bushy and air cannot flow freely between branches.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ tso lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do I see holes in my cabbage leaves even though I cannot find insects on them during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu yɛ kaabe baa lɛ mli lɛ? Ni akɛ anaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ kaabe baai anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Many crop pests, like caterpillars, hide under the soil or leaves during the hot daylight to avoid heat and predators, coming out only at night to eat.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo, tamɔ ŋmeii, kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi loo yɛ baai amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii gbɛkɛ pɛ.

english: Why do I get a much smaller harvest if I plant seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibiiwoo bibioo kwraa nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni jara waaa kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give strong yields for one generation only; saving and replanting those seeds causes plants to lose vigor and yield poorly.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛha yinɔ kome pɛ. Nakai dumɔwui lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my harvested yams start shooting out fresh sprouts while sitting in the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii heei shweremɔ be mli ni mita ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warm ambient air and moisture signal to the yam root that it is time to start growing into a new plant, ending its resting period early.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsɔɔ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛje shishi amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tso hee. ni ogbe hulutsoo be lɛ naa mra

english: How can I tell when it is the right time to harvest my cocoa pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: You will know it is time to harvest when you inspect your farm and see that the cocoa pods have turned ripe on the trees.
ga: Obaale akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ okpa nii kɛji okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ona akɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ekwɛ̃ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Should I wait until all the cocoa pods on my farm are ripe before I start harvesting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni kookoo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ dani mabɔi ŋmaakpamɔ?

english: No, you should harvest ripe pods quickly as soon as you see them rather than waiting for a large number of pods to ripen all at once.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ oya kɛji ona amɛ pɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ shikome lɛ,.

english: Is it fine to leave ripe cocoa pods on the trees for a long time if I am busy?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛji mibɛ deka?

english: It is not recommended to leave ripe pods on the trees for too long because unharvested ripe pods take up unnecessary space and resources on the farm.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpako lɛ heɔ ŋmɔ mli he kɛ nibii ni he ehiaaa.

english: If only a few cocoa pods are ripe on my trees, should I harvest them immediately?
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ, Ani Esa akɛ Makpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, even if only a few pods appear ripe, it is best to harvest them quickly instead of waiting for the rest of the farm to catch up.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ ekwɛ̃ po. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa oya. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ashɛ he lɛ

english: Is it better to let ripe pods pile up on the tree so I can do one single big harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ maha ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ato tso lɛ nɔ koni manyɛ maná ŋmaa agbo kome?

english: No, waiting for pods to accumulate on the tree is not ideal; harvesting should be done promptly as pods ripen to keep the farm productive.
ga: Dabi, ni ooomɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ jeee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ akpa lɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ pɛ koni ŋmɔ ni woɔ yibii aba.

english: How often do I need to walk through my cocoa farm during the fruiting season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ kookoo ŋmɔ mli yɛ yibiiwoo be mli?

english: You should regularly visit and check your farm so that you can spot ripe pods early and harvest them without delay.
ga: Esa akɛ oyasara oŋmɔ lɛ ni okwɛ mli daa. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ ona ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛmiikwɛ̃ mra. ni akpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: Why is it a problem if my cocoa trees grow too tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji naagba kɛji mi cacao tsei lɛ kɛlɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees grow past a certain height, harvesting the pods becomes very difficult and dangerous because hired laborers become afraid to climb them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da fe he ko lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ akpamɔ wa waa ni eyɛ oshara. Ejaakɛ nitsulɔi ni awoɔ amɛ nyɔmɔ lɛ sheɔ gbeyei akɛ amɛbaakwɔ.

english: Why are farm workers sometimes unwilling to help harvest cocoa from very high trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi sumɔɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa kɛkpaa kookoo kɛjɛɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Workers are often afraid of falling while trying to reach pods on tall trees, which makes it hard to find people willing to climb and harvest them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nitsulɔi sheɔ gbeyei akɛ amɛbaagbee shi beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ tsei kakadaji amli pods lɛ ahe lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaana mɛi ni efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɔ ni amɛkpa lɛ.

english: How does the height of my cocoa trees affect my harvesting work?
ga: Te cacao tsei lɛ akwɔlɛ lɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: As trees grow very tall, reaching the pods gets riskier, making it harder to find farm help to safely cut down the cocoa harvest.
ga: Beni tso lɛ da waa lɛ Pod lɛ he nine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ hu yɛ oshara fe tsutsu lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa waa akɛ aaaná yelikɛbuamɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji amli koni akɛfo kookoo ni afeɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: What main things should I look out for when checking my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa esa akɛ makwɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni mikwɛɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You should check for ripe pods that need quick harvesting and monitor tree growth to ensure the pods remain easy and safe to reach.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ oya ni okwɛ bɔ ni tso lɛ daa ha koni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi ni anyɛɔ ashɛɔ he oya ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does the price of my plantains drop so low when everyone in my district harvests at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ jara baa shi nɛkɛ be mli ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ kpaɔ nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When many farmers bring plantains to market at once, there is more food than buyers need. Sellers lower their prices to sell quickly before the fruits spoil, which drops the overall market price.
ga: Beni okwaafoi babaoo kɛ dumɔwui baa jara nɔ shikome lɛ Niyenii babaoo yɛ fe bɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ. Mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ nii lɛ baa jara lɛ shi koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ oya dani aduawai lɛ agbo, ni no haa jara lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: How can I plant my plantains so that I do not harvest everything at once when prices are low?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ adu plantains ni akpaaa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome beni jara lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: You can practice staggered planting by planting small batches of suckers a few weeks or months apart instead of all in one week. This ensures your harvest is spread throughout the year when market prices are better.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ staggered dumɔ nii akase kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Otsii loo nyɔji fioo komɛi ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ fɛɛ yɛ otsi kome mli lɛ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ajaa okpamɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ be mli ni jara nɔ jara yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested plantains turn soft and yellow so quickly before I can transport them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ oya dani anyɛɔ akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Once cut from the tree, plantains release a natural gas that speeds up ripening. Direct sunlight and heat make the plantain produce more of this gas, causing it to ripen and rot much faster.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, Plantains lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ni haa tso lɛ shwereɔ oya. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ haa plantains lɛ jieɔ gas nɛɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa amɛshwereɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the heavy rains and winds start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and spread near the surface rather than going deep into the ground. When heavy rain softens the soil and a heavy bunch makes the tree top-heavy, strong winds easily pull the roots up.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔ ni ŋmeii ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ ayitsei lɛ nuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi oya.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce much smaller bunches during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains need a continuous supply of water to build big, heavy fruits. During the dry season, the lack of water forces the tree to produce smaller bunches just to survive.
ga: Nu he miihia plantains be fɛɛ be koni enyɛ ewo aduawai wuji ni tsii. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Nu ni bɛ lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbala mli bibii bibii. koni ehi wala mli

english: Why are my plantain bunches small even though the leaves of the tree look big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: Green leaves mean the plant has enough nitrogen, but making big, heavy fruit requires potassium. If your soil lacks potassium, the tree will look healthy but will not have enough nutrients to feed a heavy bunch.
ga: Baai eŋɔli tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shi bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ afee agbo ni etsii lɛ biɔ potassium. Kɛji potassium bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baafee tamɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shi amɛnaŋ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ kuu agbo ko.

english: Why does putting dead leaves and dry grass around the bottom of my plantain tree help it yield better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi fata mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ehaa mi-plantains lɛ yibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dead plant material, called mulching, keeps the soil cool and retains water around the roots. As the leaves decay, they also add natural food back into the soil for the tree.
ga: Mulching kɛ tso nibii ni egbo Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eha nu ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe be mli ni baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Amɛbaaku sɛɛ amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii hu afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛha tsei lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young plantain tree turning yellow and drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can be a sign that the tree lacks essential nutrients, is not getting enough water, or has tiny worm pests in the roots preventing it from sucking up food from the ground.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni anáaa Aloo ŋmeii komɛi yɛ ni gbaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ anaa. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I choose the best plantain shoots from an old farm to start my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantains ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for shoots with narrow, spear-like leaves, often called 'sword suckers.' They have strong roots and produce bigger, healthier bunches than shoots with wide, broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi. Bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ ‘klante ŋmeii’, amɛyɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwoɔ niji ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ.

english: Can I plant crops like maize or cassava together with my young plantains without harming them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni miyeee amɛ awui?

english: Yes, you can intercrop young plantains with maize or legumes in their first few months. This protects the young soil and gives you food while the plantains grow tall enough to shade the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa adu dumɔwui bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli. Enɛ baabu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ he ni eha bo niyenii yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young tomato seedlings wilt and die when I move them directly from the nursery to the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are delicate and need special care before moving to the field. Gradually exposing them to direct sunlight and reducing water a few days before transplanting helps them grow tough enough to survive the harsh sun and field conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahe waaa ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli blɛoo ni okɛ nu lɛ ba shi gbii fioo komɛi dani okɛwo amɛmli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hulu la ni mli wa kɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi amli.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees alongside my newly planted cocoa crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing crops like plantains act as natural nurse plants, providing necessary shade and conserving soil moisture so the cocoa seedlings can survive their early development.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Enɛ ji koni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ shishijee fãi ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli.

english: Why do some crops need wider spacing like 14 feet while others only need 6 feet apart?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ahe hiaa ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni mli kwɔ, tamɔ ninetalɔi 14, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu he hiaa ninetalɔi 6 pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops with large root systems and wide leaf canopies need more room to gather sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting them too close causes them to compete against each other, reducing their overall yield.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi wuji kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ he miihia he ko babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ amɛhe abɔ akaŋ. ni haa nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ baa shi

english: Why is it important to prune or cut away extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo loo ajie niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning directs the plant's food and energy into growing healthy fruits instead of wasteful leaves and stem branches. It also allows air to circulate, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yaa aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ baai kɛ tsei niji ni efite baatsu nii lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa.

english: Why do I need to tie wooden stakes to my pepper and tomato plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei fĩɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Staking keeps fragile plant stems upright, keeping heavy leaves and fruits off the damp ground. This prevents rotting, reduces exposure to soil pests, and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni waaa lɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi jaŋŋ. Etsiɔ baai kɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite. Ha shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aba shi Ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my crops grow much better when I add animal manure to the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure and releases key plant food slowly over time, giving young root systems the nourishment they need to establish strong growth.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmei haa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛo ni ejieɔ tsei amli niyenii kpakpai fiofio. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Enɛ haa shishifã bibioo lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛ dalɛ ni mli wa aba.

english: How can I protect my young crops from leaf-eating insects without spending too much money on chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ ahe ni mikɛ shika babaoo tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ahe?

english: You can protect delicate young plants by using simple low-cost methods like spraying neem leaf extract, picking off pests by hand, and removing visibly diseased plants before infections spread across the farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu otsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ gbɛi fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ. kɛ shika fioo, tamɔ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Ni akɛ niji gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ni hela ni anaa lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ajiemɔ. dani hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young crops with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves acts like a protective blanket that traps moisture in the ground, lowers soil heat, and prevents weeds from taking over around your crops.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ shi ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekaha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off. You can carefully dig around one plant to check if the tubers have reached a good size before harvesting the rest of the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli. Dumɔ tso kome jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji ŋmeii lɛ dalɛ sa dani okpa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: How do I decide which crop variety to choose when planting for the main rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ tsei srɔtoi ni esa akɛ mahala beni miduɔ nii yɛ nugbɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different varieties require different levels of care, maturity times, and field space. Choosing high-yielding or drought-resistant varieties suited to your local environment helps ensure a successful harvest based on the labor and resources you can manage.
ga: Srɔtoi srɔtoi lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛ srɔtoi anɔ. Be ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli hei srɔtoi Nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni sa kɛha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ aye omanye ni damɔ nitsumɔ kɛ nibii ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the right distance to leave between my maize plants when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmãa tsei ateŋ beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Spacing maize properly ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors. If plants are placed too close together, their stalks grow thin and produce tiny ears, while proper spacing yields larger, healthier cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ to he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ baai bibii, yɛ be mli ni kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it better to burn the bushes I clear from my plot or leave them to rot before planting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni mijie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ loo mahã amɛgboi dani madu?

english: Leaving cleared weeds to rot on your plot naturally enriches the soil with organic matter and retains moisture. Burning may seem faster, but it destroys beneficial soil organisms and destroys valuable topsoil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi ni he tse ni amɛgboi yɛ osɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Ekolɛ ebaafee tamɔ nɔ ni shãa oya. Shi efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni efiteɔ niyenii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves turn yellow mainly due to a lack of nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, prolonged dry spells, or pest damage. Adding manure or compost to the soil helps restore healthy green leaves and promotes bigger tubers.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ yɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua bulbs lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani midu pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or unbalanced nutrients. Regular watering during dry weather and mulching around the base of the plant helps keep the soil cool and retains the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii lɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejaaa lɛ ye amɛnɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant plantain suckers right beside young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ plantain dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that scorch under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly with broad leaves that provide vital shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa tree gets established during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwereɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ amli.

english: Which fast-growing crop can I plant to get a quick harvest and make money within three months?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ makwɛ koni maná yibiiwoo oya kɛ shika yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli?

english: Vegetables like okro, spinach, or short-duration maize varieties mature within two to three months. Planting these allows you to harvest quickly and generate cash flow to support longer-term farming activities.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ okra, spinach loo ŋmãa ni yeɔ be kuku lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii oya ni onáa shika ni okɛyeɔ ebuaa okwaayeli nitsumɔi ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just take maize from the food market and use it as seed on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋɔɔ ŋmãa kɛjɛɔ niyenii ajarayelihe lɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii akɛ dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize bought from the food market is meant for cooking and may germinate poorly or produce weak, low-yielding plants. Certified seeds bought from approved dealers are specifically treated to resist local pests and produce uniform, high yields.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa ni aheɔ yɛ niyenii ajarayelihei lɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛhoo nii ni ekolɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ loo ebaaha tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi aba. Akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni jaa ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be.

english: How can I check if my soil is good for crops without paying for expensive tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ shika babaoo akaa lɛ?

english: Good agricultural soil is usually dark in color, crumbly to touch, holds moisture well, and contains earthworms or decayed plant matter. Hard, pale, or very sandy soils usually require added compost or animal manure to grow healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ kɛji akɛ ata he Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei amli nibii ni fiteɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli edɔ, loo ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ashishifã koni tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What is the best weather condition or time of day for me to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo gbi lɛ mli be ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi koni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer should be applied early in the morning or late afternoon when the soil is moist after light rain. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn plant roots, while heavy rains right after application can wash the nutrients away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane mli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afite.

english: What is eating small holes in the middle of my young maize leaves, and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? teŋgbɛ gbekɛbii ŋmãa baa Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworms feeding on the central shoots. You can protect your crop by applying recommended insecticides early or by dropping small amounts of clean sand or wood ash into the leaf funnels.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii mra lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ ŋã loo tso sũ ni he tse fioo ko ni okɛshwieɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on the same land make my soil better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into soil food. When the groundnut plants harvest and decompose, this natural fertilizer stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpa ŋmei tsei lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the crop underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing leaf rot and helping the plant produce bigger tubers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔshi nibii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even though the green leaves on top look very tall and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛlɛ ni amɛhe wa waa moŋ.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and tall stems above ground instead of sending nutrients down to swell the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niyenii kpakpahi kɛ yaa si konɛ e ha nɛ tso ɔ sisi tsɔwi ɔmɛ nɛ a tsɔ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young shoots coming up around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Mi plantain tsei lɛ je kpo.

english: Too many shoots compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, resulting in larger bunches of plantain.
ga: Tsobii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, plantains lɛ baadara babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small young pods during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When water becomes scarce, cocoa trees naturally drop small pods to protect themselves from drying out. This helps the tree conserve water and stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Beni nu faaa lɛ Cacao tso lɛ baashwie ŋmɔtɔ bibii. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ koni obu ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ he Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without producing any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: High heat dries out the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from forming fruit. The plant drops these unfertilized flowers to avoid wasting energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ agbi. tsiɔ yibiiwoo naa Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ nɛɛ koni amɛkafite hewalɛ.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in flooded land while my maize rots if water sits on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ŋmɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rice roots have special internal tubes that carry air from the leaves down to the roots underwater. Maize roots do not have these tubes, so they drown and rot when trapped in standing water.
ga: Omɔ shishifãi yɛ mligbɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ jɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛshwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli.

english: What is eating the center of my young maize plants and leaving small holes in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ bu bibii yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the tight center of young maize leaves during the day, eating the soft leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛje kpo

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekadara lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaf sap and spreading plant viruses. This damages the leaves so they cannot catch sunlight to help the plant grow.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ baafite baai lɛ koni hulu la akashɛ amɛ nɔ koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eda.

english: Why are my dried maize grains turning into dust inside my storage room after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ tsɔɔ sũ yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Small insects called grain weevils burrow into dry maize seeds to lay eggs. The growing larvae eat the inside of the grain, leaving behind hollow shells and powdery waste.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli koni amɛwo amɛwui. Lala ni miida lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli niyenii. Nɔ ni eshwɛ ji ŋshɔŋloo ni mli ewo muji kɛ sũ pɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants turn yellow when rainwater sits on my field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When standing water covers your field, it blocks air from reaching the soil. Plant roots need oxygen to breathe and absorb nutrients; without it, the roots begin to suffocate, causing the leaves to turn yellow and the plant to stop growing.
ga: Kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ dioo lɛ ha ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛmu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ebɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ wuɔfɔ ni tso lɛ kpaa dalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and droop even when the soil around them is completely soaked with water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nu ebɔle shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he lɛ?

english: Excess water drowns the root system and causes root rot. When roots are damaged by sitting in too much water, they can no longer pump water up to the leaves, so the plant wilts as if it were in a dry drought.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ nu babaoo efite shishifãi lɛ Anyɛɛɛ ajie Nu kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ. Tsei lɛ egbi tamɔ nɔ ni yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when the rain water does not drain away quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya?

english: Cassava roots require well-drained soil with air spaces to stay healthy. When water stays in the ground for a long time, rot-causing organisms thrive in the airless soil and attack the tubers, making them spoil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutuaa ŋmeii lɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Which crops can I plant on my land that frequently gets covered in water when the nearby river overflows?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni bei pii lɛ nu haa nɔ kɛji faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ho?

english: Crops like swamp rice and taro (cocoyam) thrive in very wet conditions and can grow in standing water. Land that floods easily is not suitable for crops like maize, cassava, or cowpeas, which drown when covered in water.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ swamp rice kɛ taro (cocoa) shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ waa mli, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwere jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni nu shwieɔ nɔ oya lɛ esaaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa, ni kɛ́ nu bote mli lɛ, amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why can rice plants grow happily in standing water while maize dies in the same conditions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ miishɛɛ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa gboɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni tamɔ nɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special air channels inside their stems that pull oxygen down from the air to their underwater roots. Maize plants do not have these air channels, so their roots quickly suffocate when submerged.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsui krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni gbalaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Abɛi tsei bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji akɛ awo amɛ shishi.

english: If floodwater covers my young cocoa seedlings for two days, can they still survive?
ga: Kɛji akɛ nu shwie mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ gbii enyɔ lɛ, ani amɛbaahi shi lolo?

english: Young cocoa seedlings can usually survive if the water recedes within 24 to 48 hours and air returns to the soil. If the water stays for longer than three days, the roots usually suffer severe damage and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji nu lɛ ba shi yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Kɛji nu lɛ hi shi fe gbii etɛ Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ waa ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to build raised soil mounds or ridges when planting in wet areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afee gɔji loo ŋmeii kɛji akɛ adu nii yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ?
