english: Building mounds raises the main root system of your crops above the ground level. This ensures the roots get plenty of air and stay dry even when water pools in the low channels between the mounds.
ga: Gɔŋ ni ooofee lɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi titri lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛteke shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ nu shwie shi yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ po.

english: How does fast-flowing river water moving across my farmland damage my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ faa mli nu ni hoɔ oya ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miifite mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Fast-moving water washes away the topsoil, which is the rich upper layer containing most of the food and nutrients your crops need. Losing topsoil leaves behind hard, infertile ground that yields poor harvests.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ hoɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ni ji ŋwɛi sũ ni baa nii ni niyenii kɛ nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni laajeɔ lɛ haa hei ni wa, ni baaa yibii kpakpai lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow after floodwater leaves a thick layer of mud on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitao ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni nu afua shi sũ ni mli edɔ yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Flood mud bakes into a hard crust as it dries out. This crust seals the surface, making it difficult for fresh rainwater and air to penetrate the soil and hard for young plant shoots to break through.
ga: Nu afua muji lɛ mli wa ni etsɔɔ ŋmei ni wa kɛ́ egbi. Nɛkɛ ŋshɔŋloo nɛɛ tsiɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa nugbɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa akɛ amɛaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ewa akɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ baabote mli.

english: Why do my crops planted close to the edge of a riverbank fall over during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ faai ahe lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall causes river water to flow faster, which washes away the soil holding the riverbank together. As the soil wears away, the roots lose their grip on the ground, causing the plants to fall over.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ faa lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ oyayaayai. ni hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɛɔ faa lɛ naa lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ fite Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. gbee tsei ashwie shi

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their leaves from harsh, direct sunlight and to keep the soil moist. Leaving big shade trees or planting plantains around them keeps the young cocoa cool and alive during their first few years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the plants are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the food that keeps leaves green and healthy. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer around the base of the plants will bring the green color back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he kɛbɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaha ehiɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: If the early rains stop suddenly after I plant my maize, will my seeds rot under the ground?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa lɛ. Ani dumɔwui lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Seeds need continuous moisture to sprout. If the ground dries out completely right after planting, the seeds can dry up, get eaten by insects, or spoil before they can germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ hu baanyɛ agbi. Kplukai yeɔ lɛ. loo egbo dani ekwɛ̃

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing green and yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers prevents this disease from attacking your farm.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ odu ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela nɛɛ akatutua oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot, when the soil is too dry, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Watering regularly and keeping the root area cool with dry grass mulch helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Nu ni afɔɔ amɛ daa ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does the purple-flowered Striga weed appear mostly on fields where my soil is poor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ ŋmɔji ni ehiii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Striga weed naturally attacks crops growing in tired, weak soil that lacks nutrients. Adding organic manure and rotating your cereal crops with beans or groundnuts builds up the soil so Striga cannot thrive.
ga: Striga jwɛi lɛ tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii kpakpai bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ okɛ organic fertilizer wo mli ni okɛ o-grain ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsake kɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii baaye abua ni ama shikpɔŋ lɛ koni Striga akakwɛ̃.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same plot where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu cowpeas loo peanuts yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akpaa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts put free natural fertilizer back into the soil through their roots. Planting them after heavy feeders like maize fixes the soil so your next crop grows better without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ beni akɛ niyenii agboi tamɔ ŋmãa etsu nii sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when I plant many of them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ? Beni aduɔ tsei babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantain suckers are planted too close, their leaves block each other's light and their roots fight for water and soil food. Giving each plant enough space allows them to grow large leaves and heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe la lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná baai wuji kɛ jwɛi ni mli tse.

english: How do I know that my yams under the ground are completely ripe and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams tell you they are mature when the leaves and vines above the ground naturally turn yellow and dry up. This shows the plant has finished transferring all its food energy down into the root tuber.
ga: Sweet potato kɛɛ bo akɛ egbɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eye omanye ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ ewo shishifã lɛ mli.

english: Why do tiny beetles start destroying my dried maize grains just a few weeks after I put them in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ladybugs bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ ebɔi mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ fitemɔ beni mikɛwo ŋmãa lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ.

english: These grain insects, called weevils, hatch from tiny eggs laid while the maize was drying or inside old sacks. Drying your grain thoroughly until it is hard and storing it in airtight bags chokes the insects and protects your yield.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni hiɛ ŋmaa nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Efɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔŋloo bibioo ko mli. He ni akɛbaawo be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miigbi loo yɛ kotoku momo mli. Kɛ́ ogbi dumɔwui lɛ kɛyashi amɛhe wa ni okɛwo vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi bibii lɛ ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during long dry periods as a natural way to save water and stay alive. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing normally without dying.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni hulu enyɔ shi, ni eji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he ni ehiɔ shi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eda bɔ ni sa ni egbooo.

english: Why do I need to place long wooden sticks next to my growing yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso ko ni miida lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight to make food for their underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground where they can get maximum sunlight and helps prevent leafy rot and diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small young shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ he lɛ.

english: Too many shoots (suckers) steal food and water from the main mother plant. Pruning them so that only one or two strong shoots remain ensures the main tree gets enough nutrients to produce large, heavy bunches of plantains.
ga: Suckers (shoots) babaoo tsɔ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: What causes the small holes in my young maize leaves and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Those holes are usually caused by fall armyworm caterpillars feeding on the soft leaves. You can control them by checking your farm early in the morning and applying recommended organic sprays like neem leaf extract or appropriate insecticides before they multiply.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nakai bu lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oookwɛ leebi lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii dani okɛwo mli babaoo.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani mifee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from intense heat stress, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil moist with organic mulch and supplying proper manure helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ calcium ni esaaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil that blocks water from moving up the plant stem. Removing infected plants immediately and avoiding planting tomatoes in that same spot next season helps stop the spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni haaa nu aya tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ajie tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs fertilizer or compost?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: Signs of tired soil include crops with light green or yellow leaves, thin weak stems, and small yields. Adding well-rotted animal manure or compost puts essential nutrients back into the soil so plants can grow strong.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite lɛ he ji: Tsei ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ mli tse ni ebɛ hewalɛ. ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients like nitrogen out of the soil and allows maize-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and small if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and steal essential sunlight, water, and soil fertilizers meant for your crops. Clearing weeds within the first 3 to 4 weeks after planting gives your young crops the space and food they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa onibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha otsei bibii lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara.

english: Why does my upland rice crop dry up and die if rain does not fall for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ otsii enyɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Upland rice has shallow root systems that cannot reach water stored deep underground during dry spells. Planting right at the start of the rainy season or using simple water harvesting methods keeps the roots moist and protects your yield.
ga: Omɔ ni kɛlɛ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ nu ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ he yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli loo gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ onibii ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow leaves and stalks. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves regain their green color so the plant can make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi Ni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that cannot survive intense direct sunlight and dry heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa from burning heat and keeps soil moisture from evaporating.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ latsaa ni mli egbi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ lɛ mli dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in wet soil, cutting off oxygen and encouraging fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa shi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela baa Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when water supply changes suddenly from wet to dry. The plant drops its flowers to save energy during stress, so keeping soil evenly moist and mulching helps preserve flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he yɛ haomɔ bei amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding underneath the leaf. Spraying appropriate organic or chemical insecticides controls these pests and prevents them from spreading leaf-curl viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ baakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaatsi leaf curl virus lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ naa.

english: Why do my yam tubers split open inside the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams split open when heavy rainfall comes immediately after a long dry spell. The tubers absorb water rapidly and expand faster than their outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to crack.
ga: Sweet potatoes mli gbalaa kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ba amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Tuber lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni epidermis lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong rainstorms blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots near the soil surface, and heavy fruit bunches make the plant top-heavy. Propping up bearing plantain stalks with bamboo or strong wooden poles gives them structural support against wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ni aduawai akutsei ni tsii lɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tsii waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni wa to dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha tsɔne lɛ anyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to local soil conditions, so their seeds germinate quickly and take up water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing light and fertilizer from your young crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I get smaller cobs when I plant my maize seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting with correct spacing ensures every plant gets full sunlight and enough nutrients to develop large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔ ni akɛ gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la ni fa kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does my stored harvested maize turn into powder with small holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ tsɔɔ powda ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Small holes and powdery grain are signs of weevils, which are insects that bore inside dried grain to eat and lay eggs. Properly drying maize to low moisture before storage and using airtight bags or sealed containers prevents weevils from surviving.
ga: Buu bibii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ dumɔwui ni egbi amli koni amɛye ni amɛwo ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi. Ni aaagbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi dani akɛto Ni akɛ vacuum bag loo nɔ ni akɛwo mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkahi shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants rolling up tight like tubes during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons to protect themselves from losing too much water. It is a natural defense mechanism against heat and dry conditions to keep the plant from drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe koni tsei akagbi.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my cabbage leaves and making them look like a sieve?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabii baai anɔ ni eha efee tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii amli?

english: Tiny holes on cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars or diamondback moth larvae feeding on the foliage. Spraying with organic neem liquid or recommended bio-pesticides early in the morning can clear them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo diamondback ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabe baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɛɔ lɛ bio-insecticide lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ ohe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning pale yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often mean the soil is running low on nitrogen. The plant moves the remaining nitrogen to its new top leaves to keep growing, showing that your soil needs compost or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei amli koni eya nɔ eda. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures are extremely high or when watering is inconsistent. High heat damages the pollen, causing the plant to shed the flower instead of forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa waa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: Will planting cowpeas together with my maize reduce my maize yield?
ga: Ani cowpea ni mikɛ ŋmãa baadu lɛ baaha ŋmãa ni miwoɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: No, cowpeas actually help maize. Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for the maize while covering the ground to prevent weeds.
ga: Dabi, cowpea yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ. Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni buɔ he kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ahe.

english: Why did half of the maize seeds I planted fail to come up out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni midu lɛ fã ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they were planted too deep in the dirt, if the soil was too dry, or if insects like ants ate the seeds under the ground before they could sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ, loo kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ye dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I space out my pepper plants instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ abɔ he kroko moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are too close, they fight for sunlight, air, and soil food. Good spacing allows breeze to dry the leaves, which prevents fungal diseases and produces bigger peppers.
ga: Kɛji pepper tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii helai aba, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts under the soil are mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the leaves turn yellow and begin to dry up. You can pull up one test plant; if the inside of the pods has dark brown markings instead of white, they are mature.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Obaanyɛ ogbala kaa nitsumɔhe kome kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli lɛ yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ amɛdara kɛmɔ shi.

english: Why are black spots appearing on my yam leaves during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ diji yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black spots on yam leaves are a sign of a fungal disease called anthracnose, which thrives in wet, humid weather. Spacing plants properly and clearing weeds helps air flow through and dry the leaves faster.
ga: He ni ediŋŋ yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa nɔ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ he okadi. ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei ateŋ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli ni baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya.

english: Why should I clear and prepare my land weeks before planting my crops instead of doing it on the same day I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni masaa he otsii babaoo dani madu nii moŋ fe gbi kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Preparing your land early gives weeds time to die off, allows the soil to loosen up, and helps kill hidden soil pests under the hot sun before you put your fresh seeds into the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mra Enɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ aná be ni amɛgboi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ. Dani okɛ dumɔwui heei baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest often grow poorly compared to certified seeds from an extension agent?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ extension agent lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can carry hidden diseases from the previous season and lose their vitality over time. Certified seeds are specially treated and tested to ensure high germination rates and stronger crop growth.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ baanyɛ atere helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ bei ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛhewalɛ baaje mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Dumɔwui ni awo amɛ he odaseyeli lɛ yaa nɔkwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛ kaa mli koni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo ni tsei lɛ hu daraa waa.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to leave specific spacing between crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato he kroko moŋ fe ni wɔbaadu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough sunlight, air, water, and soil nutrients. Crowded plants compete with each other for food and create damp conditions where fungal diseases spread fast.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii he akaŋ. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when the dry season sun gets too harsh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulutsoo be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young crops have tender leaves and delicate root systems that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can absorb it, requiring shade plants like plantains to protect them.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛlaajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Esa akɛ amɛkɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains atsu nii kɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why shouldn't I water my tomato seedlings in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Watering under a hot afternoon sun causes water to evaporate rapidly before reaching the roots, and water droplets on the leaves can heat up and burn the tender plant tissue. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ adɔ ni ashã tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation from the sun, and prevents weeds from popping up around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Ha nu ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Is it better to wait until I see pests eating my crops before spraying, or should I take protective action earlier?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni kooloi ni yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye dani mikɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ? Aloo esa akɛ mafee nɔ ko ni tsiɔ hela naa mra?

english: Taking preventive action early—such as keeping your farm clean, weeding on time, and planting resistant varieties—stops pest populations from building up, saving you money on expensive chemicals later.
ga: Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa mra, tamɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oooha ehe atse Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ be naa. kɛ srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛduɔ Ebaaye ebua ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ ni abua naa lɛ. Ni ehaa shika ni okɛheɔ tsofai ni jara wa sɛɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to permanently live and build up in your farm's soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hiɔ shi ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so that my crops get the full benefit without wasting it?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ aná he sɛɛ fɛɛ ni mikɛfiteee?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and the crops are actively growing, usually a few weeks after planting. Applying fertilizer on dry soil can burn plant roots, while heavy rain can wash it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo tsei shishifãi lɛ.

english: How should I clean and prepare my storage room before bringing in my harvested corn?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ matsumɔ mi-nitoohe lɛ mli ni masaa he dani makpã mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: You must sweep out all old grain leftovers, seal up wall cracks, and make sure the room is dry before storing fresh harvest. Leftover grains and damp conditions attract insects and rats that will destroy your new crop.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmaa bibii momo lɛ fɛɛ atsu nii. Gbalamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gbogbo lɛ mli lɛ Ni okwɛ koni tsu lɛ mli agbi dani okɛ nibii heei ato. Dumɔwui ni eshwɛ kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ baagbala kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni baafite onibii heei lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and have broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting cocoa seedlings from drying out during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry leaves and cut grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Nibii ni baai egbi kɛ jwɛi ni afolɔ?

english: This practice is called mulching. Covering the ground prevents the hot sun from evaporating soil moisture quickly, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Mulching baatsi hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy growth, so adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mikpa ŋmã yɛ mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize consumes heavy nutrients from the soil, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii ni tsii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ fĩɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them off the damp ground, preventing rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why do small suckers grow around the base of my plantain tree, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ edaa yɛ mi plantain shishitoo lɛ he Ni ani esa akɛ mafo lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers compete with the main plant for nutrients and water. Trimming away extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong replacement shoots ensures the main plant produces large fruit bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ahiɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I clear weeds when my crops are very small instead of waiting until the weeds grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni jwɛi lɛ adara lɛ,.

english: Young crop plants have small roots and struggle to compete with weeds for water, plant food, and sunlight. Early weeding ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need during early growth.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ ashi akaŋ koni amɛná nu, tsei aniyenii, kɛ hulu la. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ amɛ dalɛ shishijee be mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of insect pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ feɔ ekome yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight wrinkled shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early with neem oil or recommended organic sprays protects the leaves.
ga: Koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni oooye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: How can I know that my cassava tubers are mature enough for harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Mature cassava plants typically shed their lower leaves, leaving a bare stem, while the ground around the base of the stem develops noticeable cracks as the tubers swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni edara lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ, ni amɛshiɔ tso ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko yɛ sɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baafee ŋmeii ni kadiɔ mɔ be mli ni bulbs lɛ daa yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted organic manure will help restore the green color and boost crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo humus ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small flowers before they can form pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Dani ebaakwɛ̃?

english: Cocoa trees often shed flowers due to stress from dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or insect pests like mirids. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and controlling pests early helps the tree retain its flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ mli baa lɛ hewɔ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen, ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are mature enough to harvest under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem starts to crack as the tubers swell underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: What causes my tomato leaves to curl up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually a self-defense mechanism against heat stress and loss of moisture, but it can also be caused by insect-borne viruses. Ensuring consistent morning watering and providing light shade helps reduce leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Shi ebaanyɛ ejɛ muawai ni koolooi kɛbaa lɛ hu kɛba. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa leebi kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing lots of green leaves but no fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ebɛ yibii lɛ?

english: Giving pepper plants too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to focus on growing leaves instead of flowers. Switching to a fertilizer richer in phosphorus and potassium encourages flowering and fruit development.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen babaoo ha o-pepper tso lɛ, ebaaha ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo he hewalɛ.

english: Why are my planted seed yams taking a very long time to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi-sweet potato lɛ shwereɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam seed setts sprout slowly if the soil is too dry, overly compacted, or if the seeds were still in their natural dormant stage when planted. Mulching the mounds keeps the soil cool and moist to promote quicker sprouting.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi tsɔ Aloo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ mli lolo beni adu lɛ. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ koni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are tiny insects destroying the flowers of my cowpea crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: These insects are likely flower thrips or aphids feeding on the tender flower buds, which prevents pods from forming. Applying neem seed extract or a recommended organic pesticide early in the morning protects the blossoms.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji fɔfɔii a-thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ, ni no tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee. Kɛ́ okɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ wo mli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: What is the best time of day for me to put fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Applying fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon is best because the soil is cooler and moisture helps the roots absorb nutrients effectively without scorching the plants in direct sunlight.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi loo shwane lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshãaa tso lɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when heavy wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to hold up the weight of heavy fruit bunches, especially in loose soil. Propping up the main stem with bamboo or wooden stakes gives the plant strong physical support until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ lɛ sɛɛ. titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ to ŋmei loo tso he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young rice plants turn brown and rot after standing in deep water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ amɛdamɔ nu ni mli kwɔ mli lɛ?

english: While rice needs water, completely submerging young shoots for extended periods cuts off their oxygen supply, causing roots and stems to decay. Managing drainage channels ensures water stays at a safe, shallow level.
ga: yɛ be mli ni nu he hiaa ŋmãa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii bibii wo nu shishi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi kɛ tsei lɛ fiteɔ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa jɛmɛ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ haa nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni mli ekɔɔɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big trees away from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil before their roots are fully established. Planting shade crops like plantains around young cocoa protects them from harsh sun and holds moisture in the soil.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ plantains yɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot under the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water prevents oxygen from reaching the roots, causing fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ ayashɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight to produce food for the underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the ground and exposes them to sunlight, which results in larger, healthier yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akagbee shikpɔŋ ni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the plant's health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the growing centers of maize plants. Checking crops early and applying approved organic or chemical control measures can stop them before they destroy the yield.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa nibii ni adu lɛ dani amɛfite nibii ni adu lɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. Intercropping them with maize enriches the soil naturally, helping the maize grow better without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni jarayeli ŋmãa babaoo he ehiaaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small, tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe bibii ni etsilɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck sap from leaves and transmit viruses. Spraying neem oil or appropriate insect treatments helps control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ekɛ hela lɛ baa Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences water stress from inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching helps regulate temperature and moisture.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni esaaa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy winds when they start fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni ejeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots, and heavy bunches of fruit make them top-heavy. Supporting the stems with strong wooden poles or bamboo props prevents them from snapping or uprooting in strong winds.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni aduawai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ haa efeɔ tsiimɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: How do I know the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli beni midu nii sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer is best applied when crops have established roots—usually 1 to 2 weeks after germination—and again when they enter rapid growth or flowering stages. Applying it too early can burn young sprouts, and applying it too late will not help fruit production.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii etswa shishifãi—bei pii lɛ, otsi 1 kɛyashi 2 sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ—kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, kɛ́ amɛbote dalɛ oya loo fɔfɔii afeemɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛwo mli oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei bibii lɛ. Ni kɛ akɛtsu nii sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, eyeee ebuaaa ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growing season helps leaves stay green and produce healthy, full corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: When the dry season starts, why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves, and are they dying?
ga: Beni eboteɔ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ efo ni eegbo lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry weather to save water and stay alive. The plant is not dead; the root tubers underground continue to survive and will sprout fresh leaves when the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi lolo ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing a lot of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no bees to pollinate them. Providing light shade and keeping the soil evenly moist helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛbɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking leaf sap, or by viruses spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat so the plant can grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kudɔmɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear away all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikpaa cacao tsei wuji lɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving some taller trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby creates essential shade and traps moisture to help young cocoa trees survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ loo plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa baa ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni eye ebua kookoo tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees yield smaller bunches when I allow many shoots to grow around the main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni miha ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Multiple shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main tree. Pruning away extra suckers so that only two or three remain allows the main plantain tree to grow large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii babaoo juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli bɔni afee ni enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ eshwɛ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwu titri lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ aduawai agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them crawl on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ekpã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves toward the sun, which helps the plant absorb light energy to build larger tubers underground while keeping the foliage away from wet soil diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ kane hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ tsɔnei wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young corn plants and leaving small green dirt inside the shoot?
ga: Mɛni ji mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ muji bibii ni ji eŋɔli yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves (the whorl) to feed on soft foliage. Catching them early with recommended biopesticides or neem extract prevents major crop loss.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli (whorls) koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni baafite lɛ naa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields every year if I plant maize in the exact same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season depletes specific soil nutrients and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi baa shi, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ehaa nitrogen lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my vegetable roots rot and turn black when I water them heavily every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli waa daa gbi lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air just as much as water. Overwatering saturates the soil, suffocates the roots, and creates damp conditions that encourage soil fungi to infect and rot the root system.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu he miihia tsei shishifãi, ni nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli fe nine lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ayi obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛye shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when I clear all the shade trees away from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and need protection from harsh sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting banana plants keeps the air humid and shields the young leaves from burning until the trees are strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni amɛbiɔ ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu banana tsei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ, ni ehaaa tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ ashã kɛyashi tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to cut off branches from my healthy cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kokoo niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so air and sunlight can reach the center of the tree. This stops fungal diseases from breeding and helps the tree put its energy into growing bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ haaa ŋmei lɛ afɔ ni eha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree before they get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, overly shaded conditions. Clearing weeds and removing affected pods early prevents the disease from spreading to healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra kɛ ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ ajiemɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hela akagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How does government spraying help my cocoa farm yield more than when I leave the trees to grow on their own?
ga: Te nɔyeli lɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo fe tsei lɛ ni mashi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Mass spraying kills tiny pests like capsids that suck sap from young shoots and pods. Protecting the trees from insect damage allows flowers to successfully turn into full pods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ waa lɛ baagbe kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Tso lɛ he ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ lɛ he lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ omanye ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant as many cocoa seedlings as possible close together on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close, they steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from each other. Spacing them properly gives each tree enough room to grow wide and produce maximum pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda babaoo ni ekɛ pod yibii babaoo aba.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce smaller harvests even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water and plant food from the soil before your crop can absorb them. They also hide insect pests that attack your plants.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Amɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa otsei lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: Flowers drop when the tree is stressed by lack of water, bad soil health, or insect attacks. Giving the soil proper nutrients and managing pests helps flowers develop into young pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii loo kooloi ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ Niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has lost its strength to grow crops well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ tsei dɔŋŋ?

english: If leaves turn yellow, plants grow very slowly, or yields drop even with good rainfall, the soil has run out of nutrients and needs compost or fertilizer to rebuild its strength.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ Tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa. loo nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ kpakpa nɛɔ moŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ekɛtswa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pluck my cocoa pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Harvest pods when they change color completely from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange. Plucking them too early leaves underdeveloped beans, while leaving them too long causes seeds to sprout inside.
ga: Kpãa ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛji amɛsu etsake kwraa kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Kɛ́ agbala mra tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni edako lɛ daa, yɛ be mli ni kɛ́ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ daa yɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to cover my fresh cocoa beans with plantain leaves for days before drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantain baai haa kookoo yibii heei ahe gbii babaoo dani mikɛ hulu lɛ shwieɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the fresh beans creates heat, which ferments the beans. This critical step develops the rich chocolate flavor, turns the inside brown, and ensures cocoa buyers accept your harvest.
ga: Kɔfi ŋmeii heei ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa ni haa kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ gbɛ ni he hiaa nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ ni mli wa lɛ baa. Tsakemɔ mligbɛ lɛ ni efee blɔfo. ni oha mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ akpɛlɛ nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why can't I harvest all my cassava tubers at once the same way I harvest my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makpa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ shikome tamɔ bɔ ni mikpaa sweet potato lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava rots within two to three days after being dug up, while yams can be stored for months. It is best to harvest cassava gradually only when you need to sell or eat it, leaving the rest safely in the ground.
ga: Cassava lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli beni atsa lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ sweet potato ato nyɔji babaoo. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni okɛ ŋmei Akpa fiofio be mli pɛ ni osumɔɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ loo oye. Kɛtsɔ mɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ ni oooshi amɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How much cassava should I dig up every time I go to my farm?
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmei enyiɛ?

english: You should only harvest the amount of cassava you can sell, eat, or process into gari within 24 to 48 hours so that the tubers do not spoil.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa ŋmei ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ, oye, loo otsu he nii yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli lɛ pɛ. Bɔni afee ni akafite yitso lɛ

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature enough to start harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ?

english: Most cassava varieties are ready for harvest between 9 and 12 months after planting when the leaves begin to yellow and drop, but you can carefully test-dig around one plant to check root size.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ Shi obaanyɛ oka he fɛɛ he okwɛ jogbaŋŋ. tso kome ni akɛkwɛɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ

english: Why do my yams stay fresh in the barn for a long time after harvest while my cassava spoils so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ yɔɔ ehee lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Taakɛ mi-cassava lɛ fiteɔ oya waa lɛ?

english: Yams have a protective outer skin and go into a natural resting state after harvest, whereas cassava tubers have no outer skin protection and suffer internal damage quickly after being separated from the plant.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo ni buɔ mɔ he ni eboteɔ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi bɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo ni buɔ amɛhe. ni efiteɔ emli oya beni ekɛ tso lɛ mli egbala lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Should I grow both yam and cassava on my land, or is it better to stick to just one?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu sweet potatoes kɛ cassava fɛɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ehi akɛ madu eko kɛkɛ?

english: Growing both is ideal because yam gives you a large, lump-sum seasonal harvest for market sales, while cassava acts as a food reserve that can be harvested piece-by-piece throughout the year.
ga: Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ yams woɔ be mli nibii babaoo ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jarayeli hei. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ ni abaanyɛ akpa fiofio yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I improve my cassava cultivation so I get bigger tubers this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ koni maná ŋmeii wuji yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: You can improve your yield by obtaining disease-free stems of improved varieties from extension services, planting stems at a slant in well-drained soil, and keeping the field clean of weeds during the first three months.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hela bɛ mli ni ji ŋmeii ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni ooona kɛjɛ sɛɛkuu nitsumɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Aduɔ tsei lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni oha jwɛi akafee nɔ ni he tse yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli.

english: Does cassava need rich soil and fertilizer to yield well, or will it grow anywhere?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia ŋmei koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai loo ebaakwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: While cassava can survive in poor soils where other crops fail, giving it fertile, well-prepared soil with loose mounds will significantly increase the size and total weight of your harvest.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ, shi Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmei yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ha lɛ, ebaaha okpamɔ lɛ dalɛ kɛ emli tsiimɔ fɛɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: What main economic benefits will I get if I decide to plant yams this year?
ga: Mɛni ji shika gbɛfaŋ sɛɛnamɔi titri ni maná kɛji mikpɛ miyiŋ akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afi nɛɛ?

english: Yam is a high-value cash crop that commands strong market prices, can be stored to sell when prices rise later in the dry season, and provides good household income.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shika helɛtemɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa ni fãa jara ni wa waa. Abaanyɛ akɛto koni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛjara tee hiɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni ekɛ shika kpakpa aba shia lɛ mli

english: What advantages does cassava bring to my household compared to other food crops?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔi ŋmei kɛbaa mishia lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ni aduɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Cassava is a reliable emergency crop because it tolerates poor weather, stays alive in the ground until needed, and can be processed into different saleable products like flour, gari, and starch.
ga: Cassava ji oyaiyeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Ejaakɛ enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ. Ebaanyɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi ehe baahia. ni abaanyɛ afee nibii srɔtoi ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ tamɔ ashikishaŋ, gari, kɛ ashikishaŋ

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off as the plant grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni tso lɛ miida lɛ?

english: This is normal crop behavior showing that the plant is maturing and redirecting its energy away from stem and leaf growth down into enlarging the underground roots.
ga: Enɛ ji tso subaŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miida ni etsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that plants need to make food and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland soil turn hard like a rock after the heavy rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Soil bakes hard when it lacks organic matter like compost, dried leaves, or manure, which work together to keep the soil loose and spongy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ais kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, baai ni egboi loo ŋmɔshi nibii, ni feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, humid conditions when there is too much shade and poor air movement around the trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Beni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu eyaaa tso lɛ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up into tight shapes and turning light yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curl is typically caused by a virus transmitted by whiteflies, tiny insects that suck sap from the plant leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ji kooloo bibioo ko ni shwieɔ tsei ahe baai amli nu lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and watery inside the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater sits in the soil for too long without draining, causing fungi to attack the wet roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ tutuaa shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my pepper plants without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when the heat becomes too intense or when the soil lacks water, dropping blossoms to save their energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ la lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni ehi wala mli.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die early before the tubers under the ground get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ oya dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early when foliage diseases or leaf-eating insects damage the leaves, preventing the plant from feeding the growing tuber below.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ helai loo kooloi bibii fite baai lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to yield fruit compared to plants on neighboring farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers grow slowly when planted in nutrient-poor soil without enough organic fertilizer or when weeds steal water and nutrients from their shallow roots.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo kɛji adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. aloo be mli ni jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is safest to plant after receiving consistent, heavy rains over a two-week period so the soil retains deep moisture to keep young sprouts alive.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii ji beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa be fɛɛ be yɛ otsii enyɔ mli sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni tso bibioo lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly on my farm right after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds remain buried in the soil for years and sprout rapidly as soon as clearing the farm exposes them to sunlight and rain.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji ŋmɔ mli nibii ni ajie lɛ ha hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or companion crops like plantains to keep them cool and retain soil moisture while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛha tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: What will happen to my cassava yield if I plant the stems too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu tsei lɛ ahe tsɔ?

english: Planting cassava too close makes the plants fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, leafy stems with very small tuber roots underneath.
ga: Cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ baa kakadaŋŋ kɛ shishifã bibioo ko ni yɔɔ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from high heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients, as a natural way to conserve energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ hewalɛ toɔ.

english: Why do crops grow much stronger when I mix animal manure into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ daraa waa waa kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, while also helping the soil hold onto moisture longer during dry days.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in that field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon even after I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni awo amɛ nu po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up in extreme heat to reduce their exposure to the sun and stop water from evaporating out of the plant faster than the roots can drink it.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ naa.

english: Why should I wait for the soil to get properly wet from major rains before sowing my seeds instead of planting right after the first light shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A short, light shower only wets the surface. If you plant then, the seed may sprout but quickly dry out and die under the hot sun before full rains arrive.
ga: Shawa kuku ni mli waaa lɛ baaha ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛ. Kɛ́ odu lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi oya ni amɛbaagboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ kwraa.

english: Why do weeds cause my young crops to stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal sunlight, water, and fertilizer nutrients from the soil before your crop's roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do insect pests seem to damage my crops more during dry periods than in the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Hot, dry weather weakens the plant's natural defenses and creates ideal conditions for many insects to reproduce rapidly and feed on plant juices.
