ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ haa tsei ahewalɛ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe lɛ baa shi. ni eha shihilɛ ni sa aba koni kooloi bibii babaoo afɔ́ oya ni amɛye tsei amli nu.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and die when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains beside them creates shade that keeps the soil cool and moist so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. ni ejieɔ tsei kakadaji loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my tall maize plants break and fall over when strong winds blow across my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Strong winds push hard against tall stalks, especially when soil is soft or roots aren't deep enough. Planting trees along the border of your farm creates a windbreak that slows down heavy winds before they hit your crops.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa tsei kakadaji lɛ waa. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa. Tsei ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ baa shi dani enaa oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni efee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava and maize harvests get smaller every year when I plant them in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava kɛ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients. Rotating your crops with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns vital nutrients to the soil and improves your yield.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa onibii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and tear apart during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiitse yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind strips moisture quickly from large leaves, causing them to dry out and split. Covering the soil at the base with dry grass or cocoa pods holds moisture in the roots during dry spells.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai wuji lɛ amli oya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbalaɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmɔji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why should I cover the open ground around my crop roots with dried leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi aha he ni agbele ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering open soil—known as mulching—keeps the hot sun from drying out the earth, protects topsoil from being washed away by heavy rains, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Ale ŋmɔshi nibii ni agbeleɔ naa lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ebuɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Yam plants need their leaves high up in the sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off damp ground to prevent fungal decay.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ hia baai ni yɔɔ hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni fungal rot akafite.

english: Why are my garden egg and tomato plants dropping their flowers before growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant kɛ tomato tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Vegetable plants drop flowers when they suffer from high heat or inconsistent watering. Watering regularly early in the morning helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Aduawai tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Curled, spotted leaves on cassava are often caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties helps keep your crop healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are caterpillars eating holes through the leaves at the center of my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye bu kɛmiitsɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the central funnel of young maize to feed on tender leaves. Checking your fields early and applying botanical solutions like neem extract or recommended sprays can stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli mra ni okɛ tsofai tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Abaanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know if the seeds I saved from my last harvest will actually produce a good yield this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai diɛŋtsɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Not all saved seeds guarantee a good yield. Properly selected, cleaned, and processed seeds from healthy plants yield much more, as they are freer from hidden diseases and have stronger germination rates.
ga: Jeee dumɔwui fɛɛ ni ato lɛ haa yibiiwoo kpakpa baa. Dumɔwui ni ahala jogbaŋŋ, ni atsuu he ni atsu he nii kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ baawo yibii babaoo. Ejaakɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ bɛ mli, ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best way to keep my seeds safe from insects before the planting season starts?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ makwɛ koni midumɔwui lɛ akafee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi adɛŋ dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ aje shishi?

english: Seeds should be thoroughly dried and stored in airtight containers placed in a cool, dry area. Adding dry wood ash or safe storage dust prevents insects from destroying the seeds before it is time to plant.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto tsinsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli ni akɛwo he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi. Tso sũ ni egbi loo sũ ni akɛto he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaye abua ni kooloi akafite dumɔwui lɛ dani dumɔ be lɛ aba.

english: How can I test if my seeds are still alive and ready to grow before I plant my whole field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji midumɔwui lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can perform a simple germination test by putting 10 seeds in a wet cloth for a few days. If 8 or more sprout, your seeds are good quality and ready for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii 2-3 lɛ nɔ. Kɛji 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu.

english: Is it good practice to plant two different crops together in the same plot, or should I keep them separate?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ? Aloo esa akɛ magbala amɛteŋ?

english: Planting compatible crops together (intercropping) can protect your soil, maximize space, and boost total harvest. For example, legumes can fix nitrogen in the soil to help feed neighboring crops.
ga: Tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee ni aduɔ (Alternating cropping) baanyɛ abu shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Ha he ni yɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni oha ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ asaa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni eye ebua tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know the right time to start putting my seeds into the ground when the rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ?

english: Wait until the rain becomes steady and the soil is consistently moist down to a few inches deep. Planting after just one early rain can cause seeds to dry out and die if the rain stops for days.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ abɔi nɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛyashɛ inchi fioo komɛi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ kpa gbii babaoo.

english: Why is proper spacing between my seeds important when I am planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ ni sa ni kã midumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ he hiaa beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Correct spacing ensures that each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors, leading to larger stems and higher yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei wuji kɛ yibii babaoo.

english: What basic steps can I take on my farm to get much larger crop harvests like big commercial farms?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee gbɛi manyɛ matsɔ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ jarayeli ŋmɔ agbo?

english: Combining high-quality seeds, proper soil preparation, correct plant spacing, timely weeding, and balanced fertilizer application maximizes your farm's productivity.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfutuɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kpakpa tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni ja Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be ni sa mli Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii babaoo aba.

english: Why do some of my crops turn yellow and stay small even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellowing and stunted growth usually mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or the right fertilizer will restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ dalɛ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛɛɛ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers recommend buying processed seed instead of just using grain from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ ahe dumɔwui ni afee lɛ srɔtoi yɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ jara nɔ lɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Processed seeds are specifically treated and selected for planting, ensuring uniform growth, disease resistance, and higher yields, whereas market grain is meant for eating and often germinates poorly.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsu he nii lɛ anɔ ni ahalaa amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni akɛdu. Bɔni afee ni ekwɛ akɛ ekwɛ̃ daa, helai nyɛɔ eshiɔ, ni enáa yibii babaoo. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji niyeli ni bei pii lɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What can I do during planting to help my crops develop strong roots that survive dry spells?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ dumɔ be mli koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Planting at the correct depth in well-loosened soil and applying organic matter or phosphorus-rich fertilizer encourages deep root growth, helping plants reach water deep underground during dry periods.
ga: Kɛ́ adu shikpɔŋ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ he ni sa, ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees giving me very small harvests this year compared to before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso momo lɛ wo yibii fioo ko pɛ afi nɛɛ kɛ akɛto tsutsu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce fewer pods as they age or if they are affected by soil exhaustion and diseases. When yields drop drastically despite good weather, it usually means the trees are worn out and need proper rehabilitation or replanting.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni amɛdaraa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nijiaŋwujee kɛ helai náa amɛnɔ hewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ nibii ni afee lɛ ba shi waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpakpai fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni asaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo adu ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know when it is time to cut down my cocoa trees and replant the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ni madu amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If your trees are very old, producing very little fruit for consecutive seasons, or showing signs of incurable diseases like Swollen Shoot, extension officers recommend clearing and replanting the block with improved seedlings.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ egbɔ waa Ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ bei ni nyiɛɔ amɛsɛɛ amli loo hela ko ni anyɛɛɛ atsa lɛ he okadii yɛ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ, shweremɔ he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ ajie tso lɛ ni adu ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it better to replace dead cocoa trees one by one or clear the whole plot to start over?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaatsake cacao tsei ni egboi lɛ komekome loo ajie jɛmɛ fɛɛ koni aje shishi ekoŋŋ?

english: Replacing individual dead trees works well on young farms. However, if a major section of an old farm has stopped producing well, clearing and replanting that whole section gives new hybrid seedlings enough light and space to thrive.
ga: Tsei aŋkroaŋkroi ni egboi lɛ ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji bibii amli. Shi, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ momo ko fã ko ni da ekpa yibiiwoo jogbaŋŋ lɛ, nakai fã muu lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ haa dumɔwui heei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ naa la kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛshwere.

english: How many years does a cocoa tree produce good yields before it starts failing?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ?

english: Cocoa trees generally hit their peak production between 10 and 25 years of age. After this period, pod yields gradually decline unless the farm is well-pruned, fertilized, or eventually replanted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ babaoo beni amɛye kɛjɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 25 lɛ. Yɛ be nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Pod ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi fiofio ja afolɔ mli, awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii, loo yɛ naagbee lɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why am I getting very few pods even though I have planted many cocoa trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛ pods fioo ko nɔ nɛkɛ? Ni mikɛ kookoo tsei babaoo ewo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ momo?

english: Having many trees does not automatically mean high yields. Poor soil nutrients, planting trees too close together, over-shading, or pest attacks like black pod and capsids can prevent trees from producing many pods.
ga: Tsei babaoo ni mɔ ko yɔɔ lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ ebaawo yibii babaoo. Niyenii ni ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Ehaa hulutsoo babaoo loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods kɛ capsids tutuamɔ. Ebaanyɛ etsĩ tso lɛ naa koni ekawo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: What should I do if only one section of my cocoa farm is giving me low yield?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome pɛ woɔ yibii babaoo?

english: You do not need to destroy the whole farm. You can focus on that specific weak section by testing the soil, applying fertilizer, heavy pruning, or replanting just that low-yielding portion.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni okpãtã ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama nakai hei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kaa, ŋmɔshi nibii ni oookɛwo mli, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oookpa waa lɛ nɔ. aloo adu fãi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ pɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Does planting cocoa trees in different batches years apart affect their growth?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ afii babaoo mli lɛ baaná dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, older cocoa trees will cast shade and compete for soil moisture and nutrients, which can stunt the growth of younger seedlings planted right next to them.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ baafee shade ni amɛye akaŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ dumɔwui bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Can I divide my land to grow different varieties of crops or cocoa side by side?
ga: Ani manyɛ majara shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni madu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi loo kookoo yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, dividing your farm into separate plots for different varieties is good practice. It allows you to manage each crop's specific feeding, shade, and spraying requirements more easily.
ga: Hɛɛ, ni oooja oŋmɔ lɛ mli owo oshikifɔɔ mli. kɛha henɔi srɔtoi Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ oookwɛ niyenii, hulutsoo, kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I accurately estimate the size of my cocoa farm to know how many seedlings I need?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ he akɔntaa pɛpɛɛpɛ koni male dumɔwui enyiɛ ni he hiaa mi lɛ?

english: Extension agents use standardized measuring ropes or GPS mapping tools to measure farm boundaries, helping you calculate the exact acreage so you order the right quantity of seedlings and fertilizer.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi kɛ kpãai ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe loo GPS shikpɔŋ he mfonirifeemɔ nibii tsuɔ nii kɛsusuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni obuɔ he pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he akɔntaa. Bɔni afee ni obi ni aha bo dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa.

english: How can working with an extension officer help me fix a failing cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ni mikɛ extension nitsulɔ ko baatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni masaa kookoo ŋmɔ ko ni efite lɛ?

english: Extension officers help diagnose why yields are low, guide you on proper tree spacing, recommend high-yield hybrid seeds, and train you on correct replanting techniques so your farm becomes profitable again.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛnaa nɔ hewɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ faaa lɛ. Wo bo ŋaa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa he. Hybrid dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo. ni etsɔse bo yɛ gbɛi ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ he. Koni oŋmɔ lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ ekoŋŋ

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crop turning yellow and drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore healthy green leaves and strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans help make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with nutrients that future crops like maize or vegetables need.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my crops even when my crops are already big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara momo moŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops regardless of their size. Keeping weeds away ensures your crop gets all the nourishment it needs to produce high yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa waa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni amɛdara ha lɛ he. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ haa onibii lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to expose maximum leaf area to sunlight. Staking allows the leaves to absorb more sunlight and make energy, which helps the underground tubers grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ aya hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ hulu la babaoo ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die if I clear all the tall trees from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mijie cacao tsei kakadaji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Leaving tall shade trees protects young cocoa from harsh heat and retains moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa.

english: Having too many suckers causes them to fight with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring big bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ amɛná ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, no haa amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha plantains akui wuji aba.

english: What causes the leaves on my cassava plants to curl up with light yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni haa yucca tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: This leaf damage is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties prevents this infection from harming your harvest.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Yucca henɔi ni hela lɛ nyɛɔ eyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and curling into tiny balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee bɔɔlu bibii lɛ?

english: Wrinkled leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips. Spraying recommended organic treatments like neem oil or mild insecticides helps stop pest damage.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ ni yɔɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni waaa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Providing steady moisture to the root zone during hot spells keeps the flowers attached so they can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be ha shishifãi lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my harvested yams turn soft and rot quickly after I put them in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya beni mikɛwo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest or kept in hot, unventilated spaces. Storing undamaged tubers on raised wooden racks in a shaded, well-aired barn keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni efiteee lɛ to tso ni awo nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean your cassava is infected by cassava mosaic disease or attacked by sap-sucking insects like whiteflies. Removing infected plants early stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ yucca mosaic hela emɔ o-yucca lɛ loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ etutua lɛ. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni hela akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What causes black spots to appear on my cocoa pods before they turn completely dark and rot?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani amɛfeɔ diŋ kwraa ni amɛgboiɔ?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, shady conditions. Pruning tree branches to let in sunlight and air helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize is getting too much water or not enough water during the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmãa miiná nu babaoo loo eshɛɛɛ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: If maize leaves roll up tightly into pencil shapes during the hot afternoon, the plants are thirsty. If the bottom leaves turn yellow and the ground stays muddy, the soil has too much water and needs channels to drain it off.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abɔle ŋmãa baai lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ ni afee lɛ pɛnsil yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, kumai baaye tso lɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tee nɔ efee muji Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni afee gbɛ ni nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow small and weak even after I clear the bush and weed the field regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ faaa ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi lɛ daa ni mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need nutrients from the soil to grow big and strong. Clearing weeds removes competition, but if the soil itself lacks nutrients, adding compost, animal manure, or fertilizer is necessary to feed the plants.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛhe awa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛyaa. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli lɛ, ehe miihia ni afee Compost, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Is it good for me to plant cowpeas inside the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow better and improves your overall soil fertility.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmãa lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii babaoo.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and slender with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the plants compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. They spend all their energy growing tall to reach light instead of making big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I buy new hybrid maize seeds instead of saving seeds from my last harvest to replant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from a hybrid maize harvest lose their strength in the next season, resulting in uneven growth and smaller yields. Buying fresh hybrid seeds ensures your crop grows strong and yields heavily.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kɛ yibiiwoo ni faaa. Hybrid dumɔwui heei ni ooohe lɛ haa onibii lɛ daraa waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when weather conditions get too hot, when the plant lacks water, or if you apply too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ bɛ nu Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my pepper plants fall off once the peppers start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: When pepper plants start forming fruit, they redirect most of their food and energy into growing the peppers, causing the older, lower leaves to turn yellow and drop off naturally.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ bɔi yibiiwoo Amɛbaajie amɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ babaoo kɛya ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛduɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why must I clear weeds around my young yam mounds before the vines start climbing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Ani okɛ sweet potatoes lɛ ato dani wain tsei lɛ aje shishi amɛfo?

english: Young yam shoots need all the water and soil nutrients they can get to build a strong root system. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing food from the yam before the tubers begin to grow.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli dani ŋmeii lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if my land in Ghana is good enough to grow healthy plantains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu plantains ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Plantains love deep, rich soil that holds moisture well but does not stay waterlogged. If your soil is dark, soft, and drains water easily after rain, your plantains will grow strong stems and produce heavy bunches.
ga: Plantains sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ shi ehiɛɛɛ nu mli. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ baaná tsei ni wa kɛ kui ni mli eyi obɔ.

english: How can I find reliable buyers for my crops before they spoil on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana mɔ ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ enɔ ni baahe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani amɛfite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can connect with local agricultural aggregators, join farmers' cooperatives, or contact farm-gate sales facilitators who link smallholder farmers directly to market traders and processing facilities before harvest time.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ maŋbii ni buaa okwaayeli nibii anaa lɛ abɔ. Okɛ ohe awo okwaafoi akuu ko mli Aloo okɛ okwaafoi agbó naa jarayeli nitsulɔi ni kɛ okwaafoi bibii kɛ jarayeli jarayelɔi kɛ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ tsaa tɛ̃ɛ dani kpamɔ be lɛ abɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up before the crop produces fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani tso lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, isn't getting enough water during dry spells, or is suffering from root damage caused by pests like banana weevils.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, ni enine shɛko nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli. aloo efite shishifãi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ banana ŋmei lɛ kɛba lɛ.

english: Can I plant other quick-growing crops alongside my plantains to support myself while waiting for harvest?
ga: Mibaanyɛ makwɛ tsei krokomɛi ni daa oya. Ani manyɛ mikɛ plantains afee ekome kɛye mihe niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping plantains with short-term crops like beans, cassava, or vegetables provides early food and income while the plantains grow, and legumes can even improve nitrogen levels in your soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei loo aduawai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii kɛ shika jɛɛhe mra yɛ be mli ni plantains lɛ miida lɛ. Ni ŋmeii hu baanyɛ aha nitrogen ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What simple steps can I take to make my plantain suckers produce bigger bunches?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni abaanyɛ afee koni plantain tsei lɛ afee ŋmeii wuji?

english: Prune excess suckers so only two or three strong shoots remain per mat, clear weeds regularly to reduce competition for nutrients, and apply organic manure or compost around the base of the plant.
ga: Kpãa ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi yɛ mat kome mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ daa koni akaŋshii ni kɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he lɛ aba shi. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle tso lɛ shishi.

english: When is the best time of the year to start planting plantains in the Eastern Region?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ aje plantains dumɔ shishi yɛ Bokagbɛ?

english: The best time to plant is at the onset of the main rainy season, typically around April or May, so the young suckers can establish strong root systems before the dry season begins.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ April loo May mli. No hewɔ lɛ, gbekɛbii lɛ baanyɛ ama shishifãi ni mli wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi.

english: Where should I source plantain suckers to avoid bringing diseases onto my farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ maná mi-plantain tsei lɛ koni helai akabote miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Always source suckers from clean, certified nurseries or use tissue-culture seedlings. If taking suckers from an existing farm, choose sword suckers from healthy, high-yielding parent plants that show no signs of disease.
ga: Suction jɛɛhe kɛjɛ he ko ni he tse, ni awo he odase akɛ afɔɔ bii yɛ. aloo okɛ tissue culture dumɔwui atsu nii Kɛji onine shɛ ŋmeii anɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ momo mli Halamɔ klante ŋmeii kɛjɛ nyɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni hela he okadi ko bɛ he lɛ mli.

english: How do I prevent my harvested plantains from ripening too quickly before getting to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-plantain ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ oya tsɔ dani maya jara nɔ?

english: Harvest the bunches while they are still firm and fully green, transport them in cool shaded conditions, and handle them gently to avoid bruising, which triggers rapid ripening.
ga: Kpãa ŋmeii lɛ amli be mli ni amɛyɛ shiŋŋ lolo ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛji eŋɔli lɛ. Okɛya he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni okɛtsu nii blɛoo koni akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni baaha amɛho oya.

english: Do plantains need fertilizer, or can they grow well on ordinary soil alone?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia plantains loo amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse pɛ nɔ?

english: While plantains can grow on natural soil, they feed heavily on nutrients. Adding poultry manure, compost, or balanced commercial fertilizer greatly increases bunch size and crop recovery speed.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ plantains baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ. Shi eyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifã, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayi afa babaoo ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over during strong rains and winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy bunches in high winds. Propping up the fruiting plants using sturdy bamboo or wooden poles helps keep them upright until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii loo tsei ni wa tsu nii kɛdu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize lacks key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or it could be a sign of a fungal disease or root damage preventing the plant from taking in food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo ebaanyɛ efee tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo shishifãi ni efite ni miitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaye nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ he okadi.

english: How do crop diseases spread from my neighbor's farm to my crops?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Plant diseases can travel through the wind, splashing rainwater, contaminated soil carried on farm boots and cutlasses, or insects moving from sick plants to healthy ones.
ga: Tsei ahe helai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji ni woɔ ŋmɔ mli atadei kɛ dadei loo kooloi ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my crops are drooping because of a disease or just because of drought?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji helai loo hɔmɔ kɛkɛ hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbee shi lɛ?

english: Water-stressed crops usually perk up in the cool evening or after rain, whereas disease-infected crops will remain wilted, show leaf spots, or rot even when the soil has water.
ga: Tsei ni nu bɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shi tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baaya nɔ agbi, amɛbaana ŋmɔtɔ, loo amɛbaagboi kɛji akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers but only a few of them turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi fioo pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects like midges to pollinate them. High heat, lack of soil water, or pest attacks can also cause the tree to drop flowers before pods can form.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbee shi dani ŋmeii aba.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce a smaller harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for survival; they steal the groundwater, sunlight, and plant food from the soil that your main crops need to yield well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhi shi. Amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni duɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa ni onibii titrii lɛ baawo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, air, water, and soil nutrients, causing all the plants to stay small and weak.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why is it good to trim off extra non-fruiting branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni wooo yibii kɛjɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming extra branches directs the plant's food and energy straight into developing larger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on useless leaves.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ lɛ yaa tso lɛ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills up air spaces in the soil, suffocating cassava roots and creating a damp environment where rotting bacteria and fungi quickly multiply.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni bacteria kɛ fungi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ yaa hiɛ oya lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither and die under strong sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have short, tender roots that cannot absorb water fast enough to replace what their leaves lose in intense heat, causing them to dry out quickly.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛto nɔ ni baai lɛ laajeɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ni egbi oya

english: Why do crops grown from seeds I saved from my last harvest yield less than bought certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii ni faaa fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and can carry hidden diseases from the previous crop, whereas certified seeds are specially bred for strong growth and high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ aba. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young cocoa trees often mean they are receiving too much direct sunlight or lack essential soil nutrients like nitrogen. Providing temporary shade crops like plantains protects them from harsh heat while they build strong roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ cacao tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ loo amɛbɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Tsei tamɔ plantains ni akɛhaa amɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ be mli ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed so many leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed leaves during dry weather to reduce water loss and protect themselves from heat stress. Leaving cleared weeds around the base of the trees as mulch helps hold moisture in the soil and lowers leaf loss.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Jwɛi ni he tse ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Tsei ashishitoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebaaha baai ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange. Tapping the pod gently will also produce a hollow sound, showing that the beans inside have detached from the outer shell.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Kɛ́ otswa pod lɛ blɛoo lɛ, ebaaha gbee ko ni mli ewo muji aba Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ eje kpo kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop if they are not pollinated by tiny beneficial insects called midges, or if the tree suffers from drought and poor soil fertility. Maintaining mild shade helps keep the farm humid enough for pollinators to survive.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ekɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hɔmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ ahiɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔ lɛ ni enáa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees produce very small pods with tiny beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Small pods usually result from nutrient deficiencies, especially potassium, during pod formation, or when trees are planted too close together and must compete for soil food and light.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods bibii baa. titri lɛ potassium Yɛ be mli ni afeɔ pod lɛ loo be mli ni adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni esa akɛ amɛye niyenii kɛ la he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in dark, damp environments. Pruning extra branches to let air and sunlight through, alongside removing affected pods, helps prevent it from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Afolɔ nibii krokomɛi ni fata he koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Kɛfata he lɛ, ajieɔ pods ni ena naagba lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ gbɛfaŋnɔ naa.

english: When is the right time to spray chemicals on my farm to protect against insect pests?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa?

english: Chemical spraying against pests like capsids should be timed with the major growth seasons when new leaves and pods appear, rather than done continuously, to ensure effectiveness and avoid wasting money.
ga: Esa akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi, tamɔ capsids lɛ ashwie nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni baa kɛ ŋmeii heei jeɔ kpo lɛ akpã gbee. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaaya nɔ lɛ Enɛ haa anyɛɔ atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa afite shika.

english: Should I use chemical fertilizers or manure to make my cocoa trees yield more?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii koni mi-kokoo tsei lɛ awo yibii babaoo?

english: Both are helpful; organic manure improves soil structure and holds moisture over time, while chemical fertilizers quickly supply specific essential nutrients like phosphorus and potassium that boost pod growth.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ he. Organic ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ, yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni he hiaa tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ oya.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster in my new cocoa plot than in my old cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miida oya yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli fe mi-kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have open canopies that allow full sunlight to hit the ground and feed weeds. As cocoa trees grow taller and their branches touch, they block out sunlight and naturally slow down weed growth.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni agbele naa koni hulu la ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ jwɛi babaoo aye abua. Beni kookoo tso lɛ miida ni eniji lɛ taa amɛhe lɛ, Ebaatsi hulu la naa ni ebaaha jwɛi lɛ afee mlɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava inside my established cocoa farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni mito lɛ mli?

english: It is not recommended to plant heavy feeding crops like cassava in mature cocoa because their large roots compete directly with cocoa roots for soil nutrients and water, reducing cocoa pod production.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu tsei ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmei, yɛ kookoo ni eda lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ kɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, kookoo ŋmeii ni afeɔ lɛ ba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and turn yellow when planted in an open field without tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight when they are small. Planting shade trees or plantains nearby provides a protective canopy that reduces sun heat and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes its roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo be mli ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow from the tip towards the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ kɛyashiɔ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow leaves. Adding nitrogen-based fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ ahi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my field make my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei loo ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. When you rotate or intercrop them with maize, they leave behind rich nutrients that act as natural fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ ŋmãa tsake loo okɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa shĩɔ niyenii kpakpai ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks very close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛɔ he yɛ ŋsɔɔdoi amli lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close, the roots compete under the ground for space, water, and nutrients. Giving each cassava stick proper space allows the roots room to spread out and grow into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛaaha ŋmei tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko Enɛ baaha shishifã tsu lɛ mli agbɛ ashwã ni etsɔ ŋmei agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to prune away some of the shoots or suckers from my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii komɛi kɛjɛ mi plantain stand lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: If a plantain tree produces too many suckers, they all compete for food and water from the same root system. Pruning down to one or two strong suckers allows the parent plant to put all its energy into growing big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ wo ŋmeii babaoo Amɛbaatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ kɛjɛ shishifã kome mli. Tso lɛ ni afolɔ koni eshi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ yibii wuji ni tsii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of the leaf, or from a virus transmitted by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early protects the leaves from shrinking and twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli Mra be mli ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ Ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water during flowering. High temperature and drought stress prevent proper pollination, causing the plant to drop its blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ hɔmɔ mli baa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ baa fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings suddenly rot at the stem and collapse overnight in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ fite yɛ shishigbɛ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This issue is caused by fungal diseases known as 'damping off,' which thrive when seedling beds are overwatered, crowded, or lack good airflow. Keeping nursery beds moist but not soaked prevents stem rot.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Damping’ lɛ mli, ni ehiɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ nu eyi dumɔwui asaji amli fe nine, eyi obɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui akwɛmɔ saatso lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i shi ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ akawo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akatse tso lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and capture maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make energy, which is sent underground to build long, thick yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. Akɛ amɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii kakadaji ni mli tse.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn weak and stunted so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, fertilizer, and light from your crops. Because weeds grow aggressively, they starve your main plants of the essential nutrients needed for healthy growth.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya No hewɔ lɛ Amɛjieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛdɛŋ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf yellowing and curling usually mean your cassava has cassava mosaic disease or is lacking nutrients in the soil. Clearing affected plants early and using healthy stem cuttings for planting stops the disease from spreading to the rest of your farm.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ bei pii akɛ o-cassava lɛ yɛ cassava mosaic hela loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ́ adu koni hela akagbɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Can I spray chemical treatments on my crops when they look weak and stressed from the hot sun?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ miihao amɛ?

english: When crops suffer from severe heat stress, applying heavy chemicals or chemical fertilizers can burn them further. It is better to ensure they get shade or mulch to retain moisture first, and apply treatments only during cooler times of the day when the plant is stable.
ga: Beni tsei kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni naa wa kpeɔ Tsofai ni tsii loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ ashã ekoŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ ni akɛ hulutsoo loo ŋmɔtɔ awo tsei lɛ amli koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Ni okɛ tsofa lɛ atsu nii yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni tso lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ pɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward to protect themselves and save water when the afternoon sun is too hot. It is the plant's natural defense against drying out, but if they stay rolled up into the cool evening, it means your farm urgently needs water.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu nu he kɛji shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ he. Shi kɛji akɛ amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli hu? No tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia oŋmɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their young flowers before any pods start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, poor soil food, or insect attack. Providing partial shade with plantain trees and feeding the soil helps the cocoa tree retain its flowers so they can grow into full pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. niyenii ni ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ Ni akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛhaa hulutsoo fã ko kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help refresh my soil for other crops later?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha tsei krokomɛi sɛɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural helpers in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. Planting them cleanses and restores nutrient-poor soil so your next crop can grow strong without relying heavily on store-bought fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbuamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Dumɔ baaye abua ni etsumɔ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii he hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ lɛ he ni ekɛba ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ waa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ nɔ waa.

english: What makes my pepper plants stay small and stunted even when I give them water regularly?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ?

english: Stunted growth often happens when the soil is too hard for roots to spread, or when tiny root pests are damaging the plant from below. Loosening the soil around the base and adding well-rotted manure gives the roots space to breathe and feed properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. aloo be mli ni shishifãi bibii miifite tsei kɛmiijɛ shishi. shikpɔŋ ni bɔle A shishi lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛmu ni amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young plantain suckers turn brown at the tips during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛnaagbee mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Brown tips mean the plantain is losing water through its large leaves faster than its roots can pull it from dry soil. Placing dried grass or leaves around the base of the stem keeps the ground cool and traps moisture inside the soil.
ga: Tips ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ plantain lɛ miiho nu kɛmiitsɔ ebaai wuji lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛaabɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is it good for me to trim off the bottom leaves of my tomato plants as they grow taller?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yes, removing the old bottom leaves keeps fungal diseases from jumping from the soil onto the leaves when it rains. It also allows fresh air to circulate around the main stem so the plant stays clean and healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii helai akajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛba baai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu bɔleɔ tso lɛ tso lɛ he koni eha tso lɛ he atse ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny white flies gathering underneath the leaves of my garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ miibua amɛhe naa yɛ eggplant baai lɛ ashishi yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Whiteflies gather under leaves to suck the sap out of the plant, which weakens it and causes leaves to drop. Washing them off with a light soapy water mix or recommended bio-pesticides early in the morning helps protect your crop's yields.
ga: Whiteflies buaa amɛhe naa yɛ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Okɛ samla kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ afɔ amɛhe. Aloo, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and twisted instead of growing long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams become twisted when the soil in the mound is too hard, rocky, or shallow for the tuber to push through easily. Making high, soft, and clear soil mounds gives the yam tuber enough comfortable space to stretch out smoothly as it grows.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo ekɔɔɔ tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli mlɛo. Gɔŋ ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ blɛoo, ni mli tse ni afee lɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala amɛhe jogbaŋŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Sir, why did the fertilizer I applied on my cocoa farm not work when there was no rain?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ moŋ?

english: Fertilizer needs water in the soil to dissolve properly. Without rain or moisture, the fertilizer stays dry on the ground and the roots cannot suck up the nutrients into the cocoa tree.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ loo hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ, Fertilizer baagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo cacao tso lɛ mli.

english: Sir, when is the best time to put fertilizer on my cocoa trees so I don't waste my money?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo mi-kookoo tso lɛ mli nu? Bɔni afee ni ehe akahia ni mafite shika?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is right at the start of the rainy season when the soil is moist. This allows the water to dissolve the nutrients so the tree can feed on them immediately.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa nu lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ yeɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Sir, why do my cocoa trees yield plenty of pods one year and then very few the next year?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo afi kome mli ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: After a tree gives a heavy harvest, it becomes exhausted and loses a lot of nutrients. If you do not feed it with fertilizer and ensure it gets enough water, it will produce less the following year to rest.
ga: Beni tso lɛ wo yibii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni niyenii babaoo baaje edɛŋ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haaa lɛ ni okwɛ koni ená nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, amɛbaawo yibii babaoo ni amɛkɛbaajɔɔ amɛhe.

english: Sir, how can I tell if my cocoa tree is hungry and needs fertilizer?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ni amɛmiitao ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your cocoa leaves start turning pale yellow, look weak, or if the tree stops producing new leaves and flowers, it is showing you that the soil has run out of food.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse, etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ, loo kɛji tso lɛ kpa baai kɛ fɔfɔi heei feemɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii.

english: Sir, why do my cocoa flowers dry up and fall off before turning into pods?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by lack of water or poor soil nutrients. Supplying the right fertilizer and keeping moisture in the soil helps the flowers stay on and become healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ nu ni bɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ hao amɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Sir, if I put fertilizer on my cocoa trees this year, do I still need to put it again next year?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo kookoo tsei lɛ amli afi nɛɛ, Ani esa akɛ mawo ekoŋŋ lolo yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, because every time you harvest cocoa pods, you are removing nutrients from the farm. Adding fertilizer every year replaces what was taken away so the soil stays fertile.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ Ojieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli daa afi lɛ, ebaaye ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Sir, can I use any type of fertilizer I see in the market for my cocoa farm?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni minaa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛha mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: No, cocoa trees need specific nutrients like potassium and phosphorus to produce good pods. Using the wrong fertilizer might cause the tree to grow big leaves but very few cocoa pods.
ga: Dabi, cacao tsei lɛ biɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus koni amɛfee ŋmeii kpakpai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei ni baai lɛ dara shi kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ aba.

english: Sir, should I drop the fertilizer right near the trunk of the cocoa tree or far from it?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo kookoo tso lɛ shishigbɛ loo yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ?

english: You should place fertilizer in a circle under the edge of the tree leaves, not against the main trunk. The tiny roots that suck up food are spread out under the leafy area, and putting fertilizer on the trunk can burn the tree.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ kokroo nɔ. Kaawo amɛ tsɔne wulu lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi bibii ni nuɔ niyenii lɛ baagbɛ ashwã baa lɛ shishi. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ ashã.

english: Sir, what happens to the food in the soil when the sun is too hot for a long time?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni baa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ enɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: When the sun is too hot and the ground dries up, the soil life slows down and nutrients become locked in dry dirt where plant roots cannot reach them until rain returns.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ Shikpɔŋ wala hu baa shi ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli, ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Sir, how can I help my soil hold water longer so my fertilizer works even if the rain stops early?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra po?

english: You can leave fallen cocoa leaves and cut weeds on top of the soil as mulch. This ground cover acts like a blanket, keeping the soil cool and trapping moisture inside for the roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ oshɛrɛ kookoo baai ni egbee shi lɛ ashwie ni ofolɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil, often because heavy rains washed the nutrients away. Adding well-decomposed manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and fuels healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ejie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ, ni ewo tsei lɛ adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my main crop help feed my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans absorb nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into a natural fertilizer in their roots. When left in the field, they release this nitrogen into the soil, feeding neighboring crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans shwieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi yɛ ŋmɔ mli Amɛjieɔ nitrogen nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni akɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa

english: Why does my fertilizer go to waste if I apply it right before a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-fertilizer lɛ yaa yaka kɛji mikɛtsu nii dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours wash fertilizer away from the crop's root zone before the plant can drink it in. Applying fertilizer when the soil is already damp, but without heavy incoming rain, ensures the roots absorb all the nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli dani tso lɛ nuɔ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo Shi nugbɔ ni naa wa ko bako. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites that suck sap from under the leaves and spread viruses. Clearing surrounding weeds and spraying organic neem oil helps control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ organic neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before any pods form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by dry spells, extreme sun, or pest attacks from insects like mirids. Planting temporary shade trees like plantains and protecting cocoa from pests keeps the flowers attached so they can form pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, hulu la ni naa wa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatu ni ha amɛhe lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ kɛ kookoo hebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes turn black and rot while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happen when plants cannot get enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady prevents this rot and produces firm, healthy fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa egbo ni ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ, ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rainy season is heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, cutting off air to the roots. Planting cassava stems on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ kɛha shishifãi lɛ. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and space to develop large, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up early before the tubers grow big underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Early vine drying is often caused by soil-borne fungal diseases or excessive heat from hot soil. Staking the vines high off the ground and placing mulch around the base keeps the roots cool and disease-free.
ga: Wein tsei lɛ ni agbiɔ mra Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa loo dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ adu wain tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔɔŋ, ni akɛ sũ awo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni helai bɛ amɛhe.

english: Maize insects like weevils bore into dry grains to lay eggs, and their larvae eat the grain from the inside out. Drying maize thoroughly on clean mats and storing it in airtight bags protects the harvest from insect damage.
ga: Abɛi mli kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii shwieɔ dumɔwui ni egbi mli koni amɛwo ŋmeii. Ni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋtayaai ni he tse nɔ ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmãa lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to be harvested from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava generally takes between 8 to 12 months to mature, depending on the variety. You can tell it is getting ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, but the best way is to carefully dig up one root to check if it has reached a good size before harvesting the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei heɔ aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaanyɛ ona akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miisaa amɛhe kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Shi ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsa shishifã kome jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji elɛɛmɔ sa dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted cocoa tree to start producing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing pods in about 2 to 3 years, whereas older local varieties can take 4 to 5 years. Proper weeding, adequate shade control, and regular pruning help young trees produce pods faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ Shade nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa Kɛ tsei ni afoɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii oya.

english: Should I wait for my plantain bunch to turn yellow on the tree before I cut it down?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni plantain tsei lɛ akui lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani mafo amɛ?

english: No, you should harvest plantain bunches while they are still green, as soon as the individual fruits look full and rounded. If you wait until they turn yellow on the tree, birds and pests will damage them and they will spoil quickly before you can sell or eat them.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okpa plantains be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ. Beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ pɛ Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi tsei lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ, Okpoi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baafite ni amɛbaafite oya dani obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ loo oye.

english: Why do some of my maize plants produce large cobs while others right next to them stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, kooloo lɛ ji nɔ ko bibioo kwraa.

english: Variations in cob size usually happen because plants are competing for space, sunlight, water, or soil nutrients. Plants spaced too close together or growing in areas with poorer soil produce smaller cobs compared to well-spaced plants with good nutrition.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ cob lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ baa ejaakɛ tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, hulu la, nu loo niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ tsɔ loo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii lɛ baawo ŋmeii bibii kɛ akɛto tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ jogbaŋŋ ni niyenii kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant experiences stress, usually from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil moist around the root area and providing light shade during very hot afternoons helps prevent flower loss.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha hulutsoo be mli hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop giving fruits during the dry season even when I water them occasionally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ lɛ nu yɛ bei komɛi amli moŋ?

english: Pepper plants need consistent moisture at their roots to produce fruit. Occasional shallow watering during high heat causes the plant stress, making it drop its flowers to save energy until steady water conditions return.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ he miihia ni nu ahi amɛshishifãi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be koni amɛwo yibii. Nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ bei komɛi amli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná haomɔ. Shĩ fɔfɔi lɛ koni okɛto hewalɛ he kɛyashi nu shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: If I plant my crops closer together, will I get a bigger overall harvest from my land?
ga: Kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani mana yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Not necessarily. When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for water, fertilizer, and sunlight, leading to thin stems and small yields. Giving each plant proper spacing results in larger, healthier crops and better total yields.
