ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, no haa tsei lɛ daraa. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni oha nitsumɔ fɛɛ ni hi

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting beans or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps the neighboring maize plants grow stronger without needing as much expensive commercial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdara waa ni jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa he ehiaaa.

english: Will adding a lot of fertilizer right after planting guarantee that I get a bumper harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba?

english: No, fertilizer only works well when applied in the right amount, at the correct stage of growth, and when there is enough water in the soil. Applying too much fertilizer at once or when the ground is dry can burn young crop roots and waste your money.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii jogbaŋŋ pɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli bɔ ni sa. yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli kɛ be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli shikome loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni efite shika.

english: Is it better to buy certified seeds from a dealer or save seeds from my previous maize harvest to plant again?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ loo okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ ato koni okɛdu ekoŋŋ?

english: Buying certified seeds usually gives higher and more reliable yields because those seeds are bred to resist local pests and diseases. Seeds saved from high-yielding hybrid crops often produce smaller, uneven cobs when replanted for a second season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ haa anáa yibii babaoo, ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, atsɔ nakai dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui bibii ni bɛ ekomefeemɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my corn leaves turning pale yellow and dying before the ears even grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani toi lɛ po daa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn is starving for nitrogen in the soil or isn't getting enough water. Adding manure or the right fertilizer early in the season helps the plants stay dark green and produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo tsei lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my young corn leaves to look like they have holes eaten through them overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-baby corn baai lɛ fee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ bu yɛ mli nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide inside the center of young corn plants and chew the leaves at night. Checking your field early and applying recommended pest control like neem extract stops them before they destroy the whole farm.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ gbɛkɛ. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛyeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ atsu nii. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my corn plants roll up their leaves tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves curl up during dry spells to trap moisture and protect themselves from burning in the heat. It is a sign of water stress, showing that the soil needs water or a layer of mulch to keep the roots cool.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛkɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkashã yɛ latsaa be mli. Eji nu he haomɔ he okadi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu loo ŋmɔtɔ he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why should I plant beans or cassava in the same farm with my corn instead of planting only corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei moŋ fe ŋmei kɛkɛ?

english: Planting beans or cassava alongside corn protects you if one crop fails due to bad weather or pests. Beans also capture nitrogen from the air and feed the soil, helping your corn grow much better.
ga: Beans loo cassava ni ooodu yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baabu ohe kɛji ŋmãa kome fite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahewɔ. Beans hu mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: If my corn crop fails completely this season, what fast-growing crop can I plant immediately so my family has food to eat?
ga: Kɛji mi ŋmãa lɛ fite kwraa yɛ be nɛɛ mli Mɛɛ ŋmãa ni daa oya makwɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni maha miweku lɛ niyenii ni amɛye?

english: Crops like cowpeas, sweet potatoes, or short-duration vegetables mature quickly in 60 to 90 days. Planting them right after a main crop failure ensures you harvest food before the next major season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei, ŋmei, loo aduawai krokomɛi ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ daa oya yɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 mli. Kɛ́ odu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ eshɛɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okpa niyenii dani be wulu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: Why do my corn plants struggle to grow big when I put many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ agbo beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds in one hole forces the plants to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting one or two seeds per hole at proper spacing gives each plant room to grow strong.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ ni aaadu yɛ bu kome mli ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why is it harmful to plant corn on the exact same spot on my land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Corn takes the same specific nutrients out of the soil every season, leaving the land weak and encouraging pests to build up in the dirt. Rotating corn with groundnuts or cowpeas refreshes the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I easily tell if my land has good soil for corn before I plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha ŋmãa dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Good corn soil is dark, crumbly, and lets rain soak in without becoming a swamp. If wild weeds on the unplowed land grow thick and dark green, it shows the soil has good nutrients for corn.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa nugbɔ nɛɔ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmei. Kɛji koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni atsuko nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛha ŋmãa.

english: How can I stop insects from destroying my corn after I harvest and store it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni fiteɔ mi-ŋma lɛ naa beni akpa ni akɛto lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Insects like weevils attack corn that is still moist. Drying your harvested corn thoroughly in the sun and storing it in airtight bags (like PICS bags) starves pests of air and preserves your food safely for months.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmãa ni mli edɔ lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (tamɔ PICS kotokui) amli lɛ, ebaabu ehe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he, ni ebaaha oniyenii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why does my harvested corn develop dark mold when I store it inside my home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ waa kɛ́ mikɛto shĩa mli lɛ?

english: Mold grows when corn is stored while still damp or kept in a humid, poorly ventilated space. Sun-drying your corn until the grains are hard and keeping the storage area dry prevents mold from ruining your harvest.
ga: Mold baanyɛ adara kɛji akɛ ajie ŋmãa be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo loo akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ oogbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli tsɔi lɛ mli wa, ni oha he ni okɛtoɔ lɛ mli agbi lɛ, ehaaa ŋmãa akafite onibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and burn easily in harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that create shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why should I let cleared weeds rot on my farm instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ agbo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable nutrients and dries out the earth. Allowing cleared weeds to rot creates natural compost, which keeps the soil moist, rich, and full of helpful soil life.
ga: La ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi ni he tse lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyiɔ obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans on the land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize takes nutrients out of the ground, but crops like groundnuts and beans trap natural nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni okɛ babaoo aku sɛɛ aba oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: How do I know which part of a cassava stem is best to cut and plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ afo ni adu?

english: The middle section of a mature stem is best because the bottom is too woody and the top is too soft. Cut healthy stems and plant them with the growing buds pointing upward so the shoots grow correctly.
ga: Tso ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ ji tsei tsɔ ni ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ hu yɛ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni odu ni ŋmeii ni miida lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi koni ŋmeii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the food that grows big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they catch full sun and stay safe from soil pests and rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la ni yeɔ emuu kɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ fitemɔ he aba.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on young corn leaves. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract can stop them before they damage your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsu nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when the weather is too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when pollinators like bees are absent. Giving them steady water and light shade during hot spells helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomatoi fɔ̃ɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ bɛ daa Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ bɛ lɛ, kɛ́ aha amɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil when I plant immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain often heats up the hot soil without providing lasting moisture, causing seeds to bake or rot. It is safer to wait until the rainy season fully starts before sowing your seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni hiɔ shi daa haaa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shãa loo amɛgboɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi kwraa dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving some big trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains protects them until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni eda lɛ ni aaashi loo tsei ni yɔɔ ekãa ni daa oya lɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni abu tsei nɛɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to make energy. When the vines grow upwards on stakes instead of crawling on the ground, the plant can produce larger tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. Beni wain tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakpã shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ. Tsei baanyɛ afee bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient, or that the ground is waterlogged. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my piece of land produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the soil every season. If you plant the same crop repeatedly without resting the land, rotating crops, or adding compost, the soil gets tired and loses the nutrients needed for a big harvest.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji akɛ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ohe lɛ, tsakemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he Shikpɔŋ lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ agbo lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining away. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow off, keeping the soil moist but safe for the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛha shishifãi lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rains start coming early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa mra lɛ?

english: Planting after the very first rain can be risky because a long dry spell might follow and kill the young sprouts. It is best to wait until the rains are regular and the soil stays consistently moist for several days before sowing.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ baanyɛ afee oshara ejaakɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ agboi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ gbii babaoo dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why are small green caterpillars eating holes through the leaves in the center of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye bu kɛmiitsɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which like to hide and feed inside the soft inner leaves of young corn. Catching them early and applying recommended natural or chemical sprays protects the growing point of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛye nii yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ amli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the plant sap and spread viruses. Spraying the plants with neem oil solution or insect repellent helps keep leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to soaked too quickly. Keeping the soil evenly moist and giving plants adequate care helps the flowers stay on to turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ oya tsɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni akwɛ tso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do weeds sprout up and grow so much faster than my planted crop after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with aggressive roots designed to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get the light, water, and food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli wa yɔɔ mli ni afee koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa tsei lɛ náa la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long should I wait after clearing and burning my land before I can safely plant my crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ beni mijie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni mikɛshã lɛ sɛɛ dani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii shweshweeshwe?

english: It is best to wait about one to two weeks after burning so the heat in the soil cools down, ash settles, and early rains can wash away excess ash salts that might burn young seedlings.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ yɛ shãa lɛ sɛɛ. koni ekɛha la ni mli edɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ajɔ Ashwishwɛ ni shwieɔ shi Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ashwishwɛ mli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why are my maize seeds taking more than a week to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be fe otsi kome dani amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds need consistent moisture and warm soil to wake up. If the soil is too dry or the seeds were planted too deep, germination slows down, though healthy seeds normally sprout within 3 to 7 days under good moisture.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui hia ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛte shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo adu dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Ekwɛ̃mɔ baafee blɛoo. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ dumɔwui kpakpai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 7 mli yɛ hulutsoo be kpakpa shishi moŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves curl up and droop in the hot afternoon even after I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During peak heat, tomatoes lose water through their leaves faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. Curling and wilting is the plant's natural way of reducing water loss, and they normally recover once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa lɛ, Tomatoi shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Curling kɛ wilting ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛi ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhaa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Will crop seeds imported from cold countries abroad grow well here in our hot Ghanaian weather?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maji ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Some foreign seeds struggle in tropical heat and high humidity, causing them to flower too early or rot. It is better to use heat-tolerant hybrid varieties specifically bred for hot climates.
ga: Dumɔwui komɛi ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli. Enɛ haa efɔɔ oya tsɔ loo egboɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ naa ni afɔ amɛ pɔtɛɛ aha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ babaoo baatsu nii.

english: How many years can a cocoa tree keep giving me good yields before it becomes too old?
ga: Afii enyiɛ cacao tso baanyɛ aha mi ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: A cocoa tree starts bearing pods around 3 to 5 years after planting and can remain very productive for 25 to 30 years if properly pruned, shaded, and protected from diseases like swollen shoot.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ lɛ sɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii babaoo afii 25 kɛyashi 30 kɛji akɛ afo amɛ jogbaŋŋ, aha amɛ hulutsoo ni atsĩ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall and thin with few tubers when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ebɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs full sunlight to make food. When shaded by big trees, the plant stretches upward searching for light, spending all its energy on long stems instead of storing energy in tubers underground.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la babaoo koni ehoo. Beni yɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ Tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la. Kɛtsɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ

english: What causes the bottom leaves of my pepper plants to turn yellow and drop off?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, or that waterlogged roots are choking and unable to absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Flowers fall off when plants face stress such as prolonged dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees to fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe, tamɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu hɔmɔ baa. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔmɔ nii tamɔ wuobii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why are my yam tubers growing out crooked and misshapen instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeee nɔ ni ejaaa moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers bend and twist when they hit hard, unplowed soil or underground stones. Deeply tilled soil and soft mounds allow the roots to expand smoothly downwards.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni atsuɔ nii yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ gɔji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shishigbɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky to plant maize immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell before the main rains begin. Planting too early can trick seeds into germinating, only for the young shoots to scorch and die when the rain stops for weeks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ alaka dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃. Tsobii bibii pɛ baashã ni amɛgboi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo.

english: Good cocoa land needs deep, fertile soil that retains moisture well without getting waterlogged. Avoid rocky ground or low-lying areas that flood easily, and look for land with plenty of topsoil.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni tɛi yɔɔ loo hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu shwieɔ shi oya lɛ ahe. Ni otao hei ni sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ fa babaoo yɛ.

english: How do I choose the right cocoa pods to gather seeds for my nursery?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala kookoo ŋmeii ni sa ni mikɛbaabua dumɔwui anaa kɛha mi-nursery lɛ?

english: Always pick healthy, fully ripe cocoa pods from high-yielding, disease-free trees. Avoid pods that show any signs of black pod disease, insect damage, or stunted growth.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, halamɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ekwɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo, ni helai bɛ mli lɛ amli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ pods ni jieɔ black pod hela he okadii, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, loo amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How should I care for young cocoa seedlings in the nursery before moving them to the farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ makwɛ kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ aha tɛŋŋ dani mikɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Keep cocoa seedlings under partial shade, water them regularly in the morning or evening, and protect them from pests. Make sure they are planted in fertile topsoil inside polybags so their roots grow strong.
ga: Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi hulutsoo fioo ko shishi. Nu lɛ daa leebi loo gbɛkɛ. ni obu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe Kwɛmɔ ni odu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛi sũ ni baa nii ni yɔɔ poly bag mli lɛ mli koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of the year to transplant my cocoa seedlings from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie kookoo dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The ideal time to transplant cocoa seedlings in Ghana is at the beginning of the major rainy season, around May or June. This gives the young plants enough rain to establish strong roots before the dry season starts.
ga: Be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ Ghana ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ shishijee. Aaafee May loo June mli Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: How do I safely move cocoa seedlings from the nursery bag to the soil without damaging them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie kookoo dumɔwui kɛjɛ dumɔwui kotokui amli kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe ni mifiteee amɛ?

english: Water the seedlings before moving them, dig a hole slightly wider than the seedling bag, carefully cut off the plastic bag without breaking the soil ball around the roots, place the plant straight in the hole, and firm the soil gently around it.
ga: Okɛ nu awo dumɔwui lɛ amli dani okɛ amɛ aya he kroko. Tsɔɔmɔ bu ko ni mli kwɔ fioo fe dumɔwui kotoku lɛ. Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ afo plastic kotoku lɛ mli ni okafite sũ ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Okɛ tso lɛ awo bu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni okɛ sũ ni bɔle dumɔwu lɛ he lɛ abɔ he blɛoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct hot sun. Planting shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside young cocoa provides shade and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa canopy grows stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ kɛfataa kookoo bibii ahe. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli baawa.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa plants when planting them in the field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ato he ko kɛji midu amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: The standard spacing for cocoa trees is 3 meters by 3 meters (10 feet by 10 feet). Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to produce good yield.
ga: He ni esa akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 3 x mitai 3 (naji 10 x naji 10). Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why is clearing weeds around newly planted cocoa seedlings so important?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ ajie jwɛi ni bɔle kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young cocoa plants and steal the water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Clearing weeds around the base of young seedlings allows them to grow quickly without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe kookoo tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ajiemɔ Tso bibioo lɛ shishitoo lɛ haa tso bibioo lɛ daa oya ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: What kind of assistance can I get from cocoa extension officers when starting my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ manyɛ maná kɛjɛ kookoo he nitsulɔ ko dɛŋ kɛ́ mije ŋmɔ shishi?

english: Extension officers offer advice on proper land preparation, good nursery setup, pest and disease control, and modern farming techniques to help you grow healthy, high-yielding cocoa.
ga: Mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋaawoo yɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kpakpa he. Hesaamɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ helai ahe nitsumɔ kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛ̀i ni baaye abua bo ni okwɛ kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I get reliable farming advice if an extension officer is not able to visit my farm directly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná okwaayeli he ŋaawoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ? Kɛji akɛ extension nitsulɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ayasara miŋmɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ

english: You can access verified agricultural advice through local radio farm programs, mobile phone SMS alerts, community information centers, or by joining local cocoa farmer groups and cooperatives.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona okwaayeli he ŋaawoo ni ama nɔ mi kɛtsɔ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli redio gbɛjianɔtoi anɔ. SMS adafitswaa yɛ tɛlifoŋ nɔ Akutsoŋ Saji Ahe Nitsumɔhe lɛ loo kɛtsɔ maŋ lɛ mli kookoo okwaafoi akui kɛ nitsumɔhe nine ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive because direct, harsh sunlight burns their soft leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: When too many small shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they steal water and plant food from each other. Removing most of the extra shoots leaves just one or two strong ones, which helps the main tree produce much bigger fruit bunches.
ga: Beni ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko yɛ Dalɛ babaoo ni bɔleɔ tso wulu kome he. Amɛbaaju nu ni amɛbaadu niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baashwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ yibii ni ebɔle ehe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants start turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and build leaves. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize grow healthy green leaves again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee baai lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same patch of farmland every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ abaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests and diseases build up in the soil. Rotating maize with crops like beans restores soil nutrients and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farm soil richer?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans and peanuts belong to a family of crops that take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it directly into the soil through their roots. When these roots decay, they leave free nutrients in the ground for your next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei aweku ko ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji shishifãi nɛɛ fite Amɛbaashi niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and well-fed gives the plant enough energy to turn flowers into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni eye niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛtsake efɔfɔi lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open on the plant after a sudden heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa trukaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When a dry spell is followed by heavy rain, the tomato fruit drinks up water too quickly. The inside of the tomato grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst open.
ga: Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛɔ hɔmɔ be lɛ sɛɛ. Tomato nuɔ nu oya tsɔ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do people cover the ground around vegetable beds with dry palm leaves or dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ ŋmei baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai aŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the dirt, keeps the plant roots cool, and blocks weeds from growing and stealing nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Which way am I supposed to push a cassava stem cutting into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, te esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei tsei ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the tiny buds pointing upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the shoots will struggle to reach the light and root growth will be poor.
ga: Esa akɛ adu fɔfɔii bibii ni afolɔ yɛ cassava mli lɛ. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji adu lɛ shishigbɛ Tsobii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛná la ni shishifãi lɛ adalɛ baafee nɔ ni ehiii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny with tiny fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii waa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other and their roots fight over water and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough sunlight and food to produce thick stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong foliage, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea helps restore their green color and growth momentum.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ afee baai ni mli wa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with bushy leaves but giving me tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or the plants are crowded, cassava puts most of its energy into growing branches and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei niji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi tuber lɛ mli yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings have soft leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. They need shade trees or temporary plants like plantains to shelter them from harsh light and keep the air moist until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my garden egg plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi moŋ?

english: On hot days, vegetable leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect the plant from losing more water, and they usually stand up again once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsofa-kɛ-ŋma baa lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni tso lɛ akaje nu mli. ni be fɛɛ be lɛ, eteɔ shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Upward leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. As they feed on the sap underneath the leaves, they distort leaf growth and can spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛyeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ Amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã tsei amli.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with dark droppings inside the shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu ni mli ewo muji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ mfoniri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The worm hides inside the central leaf funnel during the day to feed on tender young leaves safe from sunlight and predators.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii ni hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ bɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off before forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when temperatures get extremely high, when soil moisture changes suddenly from dry to wet, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like calcium and boron.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium kɛ boron.

english: Why are my groundnut pods coming out empty without any nuts inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut pods lɛ mli efee efolo ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut shells, often called 'pops', occur when there is a shortage of calcium in the topsoil during the stage when the pods are expanding underground.
ga: Peanut ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ ‘nut shells’ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shweremɔ be mli ni pod lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Does my yam crop really need wooden stakes to climb, or can I leave the vines on the ground?
ga: Mi sweet potato dumɔ lɛ biɔ tsei ni akɛkwɔɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo manyɛ mashi weintsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to maximum sunlight so they can make food efficiently. Keeping vines off the wet ground also prevents leaf diseases and helps the plant produce much larger tubers.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la babaoo he koni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ tee hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tso lɛ he helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni da fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Too many young shoots compete directly with the parent plantain tree for water and soil food. Leaving only two or three strong suckers allows the main tree to concentrate its energy on producing large fruit bunches.
ga: Tsobii bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ fɔlɔ dumɔwu lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai akui wuji ni ewoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help them regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees get damaged easily by strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first few years.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ kookoo tsei bibii oya. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I know when my cassava stems are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei tsei lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 8 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, or by carefully digging up soil around one plant to check if the roots are thick enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ miikwɛ̃ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni oootsa jogbaŋŋ kɛbɔle tso kome he koni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ edɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ nɔ.

english: What is eating small holes into my maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Botemɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni oshi muji yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana. They hide deep inside the central leaves of the maize plant; catching them early and spraying neem leaf extract or recommended bio-pesticides can protect your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Mɔ amɛ mra. Ni neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛshwie nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal food and water from each other. Leaving only two or three strong suckers allows the main stem to produce larger, heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ ebɔle ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the soil lacks calcium or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet, which stops the plant from taking up nutrients evenly to build healthy fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai daa koni ewo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants block each other from sunlight and fight for water and plant food in the dirt. Proper spacing ensures each plant grows thick stems and full yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe naa kɛjɛɔ hulu la he ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa shishifãi ni mli tse ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops droop and look lifeless in the afternoon even if it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon sun makes plants lose water faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture longer.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mulching around Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds when my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will steal the sunlight, water, and fertilizer meant for your seedlings. Weeding early gives your young crops a strong, undisturbed start.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe tsei bibii. Ni ebaaju hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha odumɔwui lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi waa, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko gbaaa amɛnaa.

english: Why do I need to cut long wooden sticks to stake up my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei kakadaji koni mikɛwo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Staking holds the yam leaves high into the air where they can catch sunlight to make food for the plant. It also keeps the leaves off the wet ground, preventing leaf diseases and leading to bigger yam tubers.
ga: Staking hiɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la koni amɛkɛfee niyenii amɛha tsei Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi shi yɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Tsi baa helai anaa ni ekɛ yam ŋmeii wuji baa

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants grow big and green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure can help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients from the soil, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts actually put good food (nitrogen) back into the ground naturally, making the soil rich for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi naa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ niyenii kpakpa (nitrogen) baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and the plant roots are active, usually two to three weeks after sprouting, so the plants can drink it up easily without burning.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miitsu nii, bei pii lɛ otsii 2-3 sɛɛ beni tso lɛ eje kpo lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anu nu mlɛo ni amɛshãaa.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early and planting disease-resistant seeds keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Early Whitefly Control Ni dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping all their flowers without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry spells, extreme heat, or attack by tiny pests like mirids (capsids). Ensuring proper shade and protecting against pests helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji hulutsoo be, latsaa ni naa wa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ aha fɔfɔi lɛ hulutsoo ni sa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers get watery and rot underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This often happens when water sits around the roots for too long due to poor drainage or heavy rain. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily whenever strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy bunches during storms. Supporting the stems with sturdy bamboo poles (propping) and planting in deep soil keeps them standing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ yɛ ahum be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa (fiɔ sɛɛ) fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ, ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni edamɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and the soil is dry, pepper plants drop flowers to save water and stay alive. Giving them water regularly and light shade helps them hold onto their flowers and produce peppers.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do some of my planted yam setts take a very long time to sprout while others grow quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ekomɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi daa oya lɛ?

english: Yam setts go through a natural resting period called dormancy after harvest. Setts cut from the head of the tuber sprout much faster than setts cut from the middle or tail parts.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Poinsettia ni afo kɛjɛ bulb lɛ yitso mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya kwraa fe poinsettia ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ loo etsitsi mli lɛ.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops—they steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your plants, leaving your crops weak, stunted, and unable to produce well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa onibii ni oduɔ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, egbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods change color when they are ripe, usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from red to orange. Picking them at this stage ensures the beans inside are fully developed and will ferment properly.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. aloo kɛjɛ tsuru mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli Dumɔwui lɛ ahalamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ daraa kwraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my cocoa crop if I leave ripe pods on the tree without picking them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni mifolɔɔɔ amɛ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes them to become overripe, which can lead to the beans sprouting inside or the pod rotting. Overripe pods also attract pests and black pod disease, which can spread to healthy pods.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ashwere fe nine. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli loo ŋmeii lɛ agboi. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hu gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ black pod hela. Enɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How frequently should I go through my farm to pick ripe cocoa pods during the harvest season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayafo kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: It is best to harvest your cocoa farm every two to three weeks during the peak season. Regular picking prevents pods from overripening and keeps fungal diseases from taking hold.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa kookoo ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ. Otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ fa babaoo lɛ Kɛ́ aŋɔ ŋmeii lɛ daa lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ fe nine, ni ebaatsi ŋmeii ahe helai anaa.

english: Why should I cut back or redo old, overgrown branches on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo loo madu tsei niji ni egbɔ ni eda fe nine lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ kookoo tso nɔ?

english: Pruning old branches allows fresh air and sunlight to reach the lower trunk where pods grow. It also encourages the tree to produce new, healthy shoots and reduces dampness that causes pod rot.
ga: Niji momoi ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la shɛɔ shishigbɛ tsei lɛ ahe he ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Ekanyaa tso lɛ hu koni ewo tsei heei ni mli wa. ni eha hulutsoo ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ aba shi

english: Can I bring an old, unproductive cocoa farm back to life, or do I need to clear everything and start fresh?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahã mi-kookoo ŋmɔ momo ni wooo yibii lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ? Aloo esa akɛ mafo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ mli ni mabɔi ekoŋŋ?

english: You can rehabilitate an old farm by removing dead or diseased trees, pruning old stems to encourage new growth, and replacing missing trees with improved seedlings without needing to clear the entire land.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha ŋmɔ momo ko aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. Niji momoi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni ekɛha tsei heei adara ni akɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ awo tsei ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ajie jɛmɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does keeping my cocoa farm clear of tall weeds help my trees produce more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni jwɛi kakadaji ni mikɛhaa mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water and nutrients from the soil that your cocoa trees need to grow strong. Keeping the field clean ensures all the soil nourishment goes into pod production and makes it easier to spot diseased pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ehaa sũ mli niyenii fɛɛ yaa pod feemɔ mli. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaana ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it important to remove damaged or rotten pods from the farm instead of leaving them under the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie ŋmeii ni efite loo efite kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Rotten pods carry spores that cause black pod disease. If left on the ground or tree, rain and wind will spread these spores to healthy cocoa pods nearby.
ga: Spores ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ yɛ pods ni egbo lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ loo tso nɔ Nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ eshwaa kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees look healthier when I clear out the dead wood and debris around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa waa kɛ́ mijie tsei ni egboi kɛ sũ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Removing dead vegetation eliminates hiding spots for pests like capsids and mealybugs. A neat, clear farm allows sunlight to dry up excess humidity that triggers fungal infections.
ga: Tsei ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli tamɔ capsids kɛ mealybugs lɛ. Okwaafoi ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ fɛo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ haa hulu la lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I plant them in open sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sun. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them from heat and retain soil moisture while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ maa lɛ.

english: Trees planted too closely compete for soil nutrients and sunlight, growing tall and thin instead of bushy. The overcrowded canopy also traps moisture, making the trees more vulnerable to diseases.
ga: Tsei ni adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ. Edaa ni ekwɛɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ bushy najiaŋ. Kpo ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hu mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eyeɔ helai srɔtoi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil or is struggling to absorb nutrients due to waterlogged roots. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's life helps the leaves turn dark green so the plant can feed itself and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo enaa naagba yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he yɛ shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aye niyenii ni eda waa.

english: How do cowpea and groundnut plants help improve my soil for the next farming season?
ga: Te tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baafee tɛŋŋ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny bumps on their roots that host beneficial soil bacteria. These bacteria pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural plant food in the soil, which remains behind to nourish your next crop, like maize or cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni ji he ni sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ yɔɔ Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ eshwɛ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn roll up tight into tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward during peak heat to save water. By shrinking the leaf area exposed to the hot sun and wind, the plant slows down water loss through its leaves until the cooler evening arrives.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ latsaa be mli koni amɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ baa lɛ he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni abaaba shi lɛ nɔ. Tsei haa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato plants often drop their blossoms when afternoon temperatures become too hot, or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells followed by sudden heavy watering. Stress causes the plant to abort flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Aloo beni tomato tsei lɛ naa kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa ni nu ni mli wa trukaa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ. Haomɔ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when we get too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil spaces to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the soil without draining away, it suffocates the underground roots and creates the ideal environment for rot-causing fungi to attack.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni efee shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ koni amɛtutua.

english: Why are my seed yams starting to sprout in the storage barn before the rainy season even begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miibɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally exit their resting period (dormancy) after a few months of dry storage as warmth builds up in the air. The tuber senses internal biological timing to start growing, even if it hasn't been planted in moist soil yet.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ jeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ni amɛyɔɔ mli (dormancy) lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni egbi lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Yitso lɛ nuɔ wala yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe ni jeɔ shishi edaa. Kɛji akɛ aduko yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lolo po.

english: Why do many tiny young pods drop off my cocoa trees before growing into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ Mɛi babaoo miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ dani eda ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: This natural shedding is called cherelle wilt. Cocoa trees produce more tiny pods than they can support with available water and nutrients, so the tree naturally sacrifices some young pods so the remaining ones can reach full size.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli shwiemɔ nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii. Nɔ ni fe nɔ ni baanyɛ aye abua nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ eshishifãi bibii lɛ ekomɛi shaa afɔle bɔni afee ni eshishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ ashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily when a strong rain wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that catch wind like a sail, but their roots are shallow. Tiny worms in the soil (nematodes) or banana weevils often feed on the underground root base, weakening the tree's grip on the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ tamɔ ŋshɔ hiɛ lɛlɛ. Shi amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (Nematodes) loo banana ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishitoo nibii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ emɔɔ shikpɔŋ.

english: Wrinkled and upward-curling pepper leaves are usually a sign of tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or a virus spread by whiteflies. The feeding damages the young leaf cells, causing them to distort as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baai ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa Niyenii fiteɔ baa bibii amli wala yibii. ni kɛ sɛɛkuu baa beni edaa lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow and spread so much faster than my planted crop seeds after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya fe dumɔwui ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are wild and tough, adapted over thousands of years to wake up and grab water instantly at the first rain. Planted crops have been domesticated to grow steadily, making them slower out of the gate compared to native weeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ basabasa ni amɛhe wa. Eheɔ afii akpei abɔ dani mɔ ko teɔ shi ni ebuaa nu naa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ. Akwɛɔ tsei yɛ shia mli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara. Enɛ haa ejɛɔ shinaa lɛ naa blɛoo kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ ahe.

english: Excessive rain washes away nitrogen from the soil and floods the roots so they cannot breathe. Without nitrogen and oxygen, maize leaves lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ eyiɔ nu mli bɔni afee ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Kɛji nitrogen kɛ oxygen bɛ lɛ, Abɛi baai lɛ hu baafite amɛhe su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or too much fertilizer. Stress causes the plant to shed flowers to save its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hewɔ. Haomɔ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen or if cassava is planted in deep shade, the plant spends all its energy growing big top leaves instead of storing food in the underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo adu ŋmei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai wuji moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli.

english: What is making small holes in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Small holes and ragged leaves in young maize are usually caused by fall armyworm caterpillars, which crawl into the central funnel of the plant to feed on tender leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii kɛ baai ni etse yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ shi kɛboteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden eggs and pepper plants curling up and drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids sucking sap from the leaf undersides, or transmitting viruses that stop normal leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ baa lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ eshwaa

english: Why do farmers plant plantain trees next to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tso bibioo?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide broad leaf umbrellas that shade the young cocoa and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans on my land make the soil better for maize afterwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni yeɔ kooloi babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing twisted and short instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee kuku moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers deform when they hit hard, stony, or compacted soil underground. Soft, well-mounded soil allows the tuber to push downward smoothly and grow big.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafite kɛji shikpɔŋ ni wa tswa amɛ. tɛi loo shikpɔŋ shishi ni eyi mli obɔ Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ashɛrɛ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shi mlɛo ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the fruits start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that can snap under the weight of heavy fruit bunches, especially if root pests or wet soil have weakened the roots' grip in the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ akumɔ yɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ ashishi. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tsɛŋemɔ helai loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ haa shishifã lɛ nyɛɔ emɔɔ sũ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know that my cassava is fully matured and ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack from the swelling tubers below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni efuu lɛ mli.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛɛ gbɔmɛi akɛ amɛfee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava and maize grow at different speeds and root depths. Maize grows quickly and feeds near the soil surface for an early harvest, while cassava grows deeper and slower, expanding after the maize is cleared without stealing its food.
ga: Cassava kɛ ŋmãa daa oya kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ srɔtoi amli. Abɛi daa oya ni eyeɔ nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ mra. Beni ŋmãa lɛ daa ni eyaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ, Egbɛ eshwa beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ ni ejuuu niyenii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers keep drying up and dying shortly after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers lose water rapidly through their stem cut and leaves. If they are planted in hot weather without shade or a blanket of dried leaves (mulch) over the soil to keep roots moist, they dehydrate before establishing new roots.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli loo baai ni egbi lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná nu dani shishifãi heei aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow at the tips and middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbee kɛ amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which gives plants their green color and leaf strength. Heavy Ghanaian rains often wash nitrogen deeper into the ground, away from young plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa baai eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ. kɛjɛ tsei bibii ashishifãi ahe

english: Why do my plantain leaves shred and turn brown during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ fãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large, tender leaves that lose moisture quickly in dry winds. Leaf splitting is the plant's survival trick to reduce wind resistance and slow down water loss so the main trunk stays alive.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Baai amlijaa ji tso wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni ba kɔɔyɔɔ shitee-kɛ-woo kɛ nu ni laajeɔ blɛoo koni eha tso lɛ yitso lɛ ahi wala mli.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress or sudden water changes. If the soil goes from completely dry to flooded, the plant panics and drops its blossoms to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ haomɔ loo nu tsake trukaa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa kɛtee nu afua mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baashe gbeyei ni amɛbaafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do some of my plantain bunches remain very small even when the stem looks thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ekomɛi ji bibii waa lolo eyɛ mli akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: A plantain forms its fruit bunch deep inside the trunk long before you see it emerge. If the plant lacked water or soil food during that hidden formation stage, the bunch will stay small even if conditions improve later.
ga: Plantains baafee aduawai akui yɛ tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani obaanyɛ ona amɛ ni amɛje kpo. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni efeɔ ehe yɛ teemɔŋ lɛ, kuu lɛ baakã he afee bibioo kɛji akɛ eshihilɛ lɛ tee hiɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli po.

english: This is Black Pod disease caused by a tiny fungus that loves shade, high humidity, and cool moisture. Raindrops splash the fungal spores from the wet soil or infected leaves directly onto the growing pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ Black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei bibioo ko ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo, hulutsoo be babaoo, kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ loo baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars hide deep inside the center whorl of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm feed inside the tight funnel of leaves because it offers soft, tender young plant tissue to eat while protecting them from predators and direct tropical sunlight.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ naa niyenii yɛ baai lɛ amli gbɛ bibii lɛ amli, he ni amɛyɔɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛyeɔ lɛ. Kɛfata he lɛ, ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen and go soft so quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, plantains release a natural ripening gas called ethylene. High temperatures, direct sunlight, and bruised skins cause the fruit to release this gas faster, forcing the whole bunch to soften quickly.
ga: Kɛji akpa Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo. Dɔlɛ ni mli wa, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ Kɛ hewolo ni etse lɛ haa aduawai lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kuu muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ blɛoo oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning dark brown inside just two days after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Unlike yam, cassava roots have no natural resting period after being dug up. The cut root panics without a water supply and begins a natural decay process, making quick processing or eating essential within 48 hours.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ sweet potato lɛ, cassava shishifãi bɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be yɛ be mli ni atsa lɛ sɛɛ. Nu ni bɛ lɛ haa shishifãi ni afo lɛ ahe feɔ gbeyei ni amɛjeɔ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa ehe hiaa ni atsu he nii loo aye oya yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli.
