english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and soft while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast during heavy rains and cool, damp weather. Clearing weeds, pruning dead branches to let sunlight in, and removing affected pods helps keep the rest of the farm dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ. weeding Niji ni egboi lɛ afolɔ koni hulu la abote mli Ni ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet for long periods or when fungal diseases in the soil attack the tubers. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away easily so the roots can breathe and stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ tutua ŋmeii lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya. Koni shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my yam vines get black spots and dry up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgbiɔ dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Black spots on yam leaves are a sign of yam anthracnose, a fungal disease that spreads quickly in humid weather. Staking yams high off the ground keeps the leaves away from wet soil and reduces infection.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ anthracnose hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ o-sweet potato lɛ fɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaha helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and looking crumpled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, mites, or aphids feeding on the sap, or a virus they transmit. Spraying early with neem oil solutions or insecticidal soap helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni yeɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the tip downward along the main vein when the soil lacks nitrogen or when heavy rains wash nitrogen out of the root zone. Applying nitrogen fertilizers like NPK or urea helps the leaves turn deep green again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa shishi yɛ fã titri lɛ he kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my cowpea crop growing a lot of thick green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Cowpeas naturally capture nitrogen from the air. If you add extra chemical nitrogen fertilizer to the soil, the plant focuses all its energy on growing leafy vines instead of producing flowers and pods.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa kroko ni ji nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fata he. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ wain tsei ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do small caterpillars chew ragged holes in the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a destructive pest that hides inside the central leaf funnel of young corn. Catching them early and placing recommended bio-pesticides or clean sand mixed with ash into the leaf funnels helps destroy them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni ekɛ ehe ewoɔ ŋmãa bibii ashishifãi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo ŋã ni he tse ni akɛ sũ efutu mli ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni efite amɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before the fruit bunches are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall because their root systems are naturally shallow and can be weakened further by root pests like nematodes or stem borers. Supporting heavy fruiting trees with bamboo props prevents them from uprooting in strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ amli tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ babaoo. Tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ni akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaje shishi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when the plant lacks enough water, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering and light mulching help keep the plant cool and preserve flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tsei amli loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up when I plant them out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava next to cocoa trees gives them the shade and cool moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ. Kookoo tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hulu la shɛ mihe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or canopy trees to shield them until their roots grow deep enough to handle the heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei bibii koni amɛha amɛha amɛhe aahu kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the bottom up even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the bottom leaves is a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves up to feed the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Rain splashes the fungus from the soil onto lower pods, and lack of pruning keeps the air humid around the trees.
ga: Fɛ̃i ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ duŋ mli kɛ black pod hela baa. Nugbɔ haa ŋmeii ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaaa lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ aya hiɛ. tso ni mli efɔ

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over on its own when the fruit bunch starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbeeɔ shi beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trunks are made of soft leaf layers, not hard wood, and their roots are shallow. As the heavy bunch grows, the top weight easily pulls the whole plant down unless you support it with a strong bamboo prop.
ga: Akɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ plantain tsei lɛ. Jeee tso ni wa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ Beni ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ Muji ni fe fɛɛ lɛ baagbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛba shi mlɛo. Ja okɛ ŋmei tso ni mli wa tsu nii ni okɛfi sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the soil when the rains stay too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave water standing in the soil for days, the roots drown from lack of air and rot-causing bacteria quickly destroy them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ sũ lɛ mli gbii babaoo. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ, ni helai ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ baafite amɛ oya.

english: Why do so many small flowers on my cocoa trunk drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can feed. If the tree lacks nutrients, or if tiny insects called midges do not visit to transfer pollen, the unpollinated flowers simply dry up and drop off.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ baaa koni ebabua pollen naa. Fɔfɔi ni pollin bɛ mli lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: What causes the central leaves of my young maize to look chewed up with dark powder inside?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ feɔ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It crawls into the cool, rolled heart of the young maize plant during the day to feed on soft leaves and leaves behind its waste.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii atsuii ni mli ejɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni eye baai bibii kɛ jwɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests every year when I plant maize on the exact same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the field season after season.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow much smaller if I do not give the vines sticks to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ bibii kwraa kɛji mihaaa amɛ wain tsei ni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to make the food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Without stakes, leaves pile on top of each other on the ground, blocking light from reaching them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe koni akɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Akɛ baai lɛ to shikpɔŋ ni tso ko bɛ he. Kane ni tsiɔ gbɛ koni ekashɛ he

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks the water-carrying tubes inside the plant stem. Even if moisture is in the dirt, the plant cannot drink it, causing leaves to collapse in the sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsiɔ paipii ni kɛ nu yaa tsei amli lɛ anaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ, shi Tsei nyɛŋ anu. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is an important food plants need to grow strong and green. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or using well-rotted animal manure will help bring back their rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea tsu nii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I burn the dry bush on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji mishã tsei ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Burning heat destroys beneficial soil organisms and burns off organic matter that keeps the soil moist and rich. Clearing the land without burning allows dry plant leaves to rot into compost, which feeds your crops naturally.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni shãa lɛ kpataa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ ni eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ ajie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni ashãaa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ baai ni egbi lɛ agbo ni ebatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into loose cups during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi ni etse amɛhe lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon heat is a plant's way of protecting itself from losing too much water to the dry air. If the leaves flatten back out by evening, the plant is doing fine, but if they stay curled constantly, the soil needs more water.
ga: Baai ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkafite nu babaoo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ gbɛ eshwa gbɛkɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ shihilɛ kpakpa mli. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi be fɛɛ be lɛ Nu babaoo he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any fruit develops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruit. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my main crop when I clear a new plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ hee ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, so their seeds sprout quickly and steal water, light, and nutrients before your crops can establish roots. Clearing weeds early gives your cultivated crop the space it needs to win the race for soil nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai dani onibii lɛ baanyɛ aná shishifãi. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ aná hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why do fall armyworms prefer attacking maize crops over other plants on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms sumɔɔ ni amɛtutua ŋmãa fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms love maize because the young leaves inside the plant's funnel are soft, sweet, and offer full protection while they feed. Finding them early inside the leaf funnel allows you to manage them before they destroy the growing point of the plant.
ga: Fall armyworms sumɔɔ ŋmãa ejaakɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe ŋɔɔ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe babaoo beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ. Kɛ́ ona amɛ mra yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ otsuɔ he nii dani amɛfiteɔ hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do the cassava leaves on my farm develop yellow patch spots and start twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves with yellow patches are a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck plant sap. Using disease-resistant cassava cuttings from verified sources prevents this disease from starting on your farm.
ga: Baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Whiteflies bibii ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ okɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni nyɛɔ helai ni jɛ hei ni akwɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela nɛɛ akaje shishi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I grow cassava on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Cassava pulls large amounts of nutrients out of the earth each season, so planting it repeatedly in the exact same place drains the soil and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating cassava with grain or legume crops gives the land time to rest and rebuild its strength.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ Yɛ he ni eyɔɔ tsutsu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kasava ni akɛ ŋmaa loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ ehewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers are fully mature and ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yams indicate maturity when the above-ground vines and leaves stop growing, turn yellow, and begin to dry out naturally. This signals that the plant has transferred all its energy into the tuber below ground and is ready to be harvested.
ga: Atomɔ tsɔɔ akɛ eda kɛji wain tso lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpa dalɛ. etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ewo ŋmeii lɛ amli ni efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there is too much direct sunlight on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow root systems that cannot handle harsh heat. They need temporary shade from crops like plantain or cassava during their early years to retain moisture and survive the hot sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Amɛbiɔ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo cassava mli yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni ehi wala mli kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How does putting dry grass or crop leaves around my crop stems help my field during the dry season?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo tso baai ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tso lɛ shishifãi yeɔ ebuaa mi kooloi alɛɛhe lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the ground, reduces heat on the roots, and stops water from evaporating quickly under the bright sun.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ehaa dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow starting from the bottom leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛmiijɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, a key food crops need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer can restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce shells with no groundnut seeds inside when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni peanut dumɔwui bɛ mli kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut shells, often called 'pops', happen when the soil lacks calcium while the pods are forming underground. Applying wood ash or agricultural lime to the soil helps the plant form healthy, full seeds.
ga: Peanut ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ ‘nut shells’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miifee yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso sũ loo lime fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei ni amɛwo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Removing infected plants early or using mild soaps or neem oil spray helps keep insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra Aloo akɛ samla ni mli ejɔ atsu nii Aloo akɛ neem fɔ afɔ nɔ koni eye ebua ni kooloi akabote mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the soil when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in soggy ground because the roots need air to breathe. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away from the roots during heavy downpours.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees snap or fall over easily when a small wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ fãa loo egbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko pɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when tiny worms called nematodes or banana weevils attack their underground root system, weakening their grip on the soil. Planting clean, healthy suckers in fresh soil helps build strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji ŋmeii bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Ale amɛ akɛ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii, ni amɛtutuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa shi Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi ni wa aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot, when water is inconsistent, or when soil nutrients are unbalanced. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting at the right time of year helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ be fɛɛ be ni adu yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting and going soft while they are inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni amɛmiifee blɛoo yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break dormancy and start sprouting when they feel warmth and light after harvest. Storing yams in a cool, well-ventilated, and shaded barn slows down sprouting and keeps them firm.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, sweet potatoes fiteɔ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ amɛhe edɔ ni amɛkpɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Sweet Potatoes ni Akɛtoɔ Gbɛjegbɛ ni Mli Ejɔ Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ fioo ni ebaaha ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop right after I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni midu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly soak up water and nutrients from newly disturbed soil. Clearing weeds early in the first 3 to 4 weeks allows your young maize plants to get the nutrients they need without fighting for survival.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ hee ni ahao lɛ mli oya. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛwuu koni amɛhi shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava planted alongside them to filter the sunlight and retain soil moisture while the young trees grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ atsu nii ni ekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i nɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my crops at the beginning of the rainy season instead of mid-season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli moŋ fe be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Planting at the start of the rainy season gives your crop's roots enough time to establish deep in the soil while water is abundant, helping the plant survive the harsh dry harmattan season later.
ga: Dumɔ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛshishifãi lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ sɛɛ mli harmattan hɔmɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but most of them dry up and fall off without making pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ babaoo gboɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if they are not pollinated by tiny insects like midges, or if the tree is stressed by lack of water and nutrients. Without pollination, the flower cannot turn into a pod.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli, loo kɛji akɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ pollination bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee pods.

english: How do insects like midges help my crop produce more fruits?
ga: Te kooloi bibii tamɔ midges baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Tiny insects move from flower to flower to feed, carrying dust called pollen on their bodies. This transfers pollen between flowers, which fertilizes them so they can grow into full cocoa pods or fruits.
ga: Kplukai bibii fãa kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli koni amɛyatao niyenii. Amɛyɛ sũ ni atsɛɔ lɛ pollen yɛ amɛhe. Enɛ baaha pollen lɛ aya fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ adara kwraa ni amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmɔji loo aduawai.

english: Why do my crops grow very slowly even though I weed my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo waa eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Removing weeds reduces competition for space, but crops still need essential soil nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus to grow fast. If the soil is exhausted, adding organic compost or fertilizer helps boost growth.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa akaŋshii ni akɛtaoɔ he ko lɛ baa shi. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii hu he miihia sũ mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Kɛha dalɛ oya lɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn pale green when there is too much water on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When water collects on the farm and cannot drain, the plant roots drown and cannot breathe or absorb nutrients properly, causing the leaves to turn pale and growth to slow down.
ga: Beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli. Tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa amɛdaraa blɛoo

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in very wet and shady conditions. Clearing overgrown weeds and harvesting ripe pods regularly reduces water buildup and stops the fungus.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ daa ni akpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni buaa ehe naa lɛ aba shi, ni ebaatsi ŋmeii anaa.

english: Why do I see black ants moving around white sticky insects on my cocoa branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii diji ni miiho kɛmiibɔle mihe lɛ? Kpluka yɛŋ ni shwieɔ mi-kookoo nine lɛ nɔ

english: The white insects are mealybugs that suck sap from your tree and leave a sweet juice that ants love to eat. The ants protect the mealybugs, but the mealybugs can spread destructive diseases like the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus.
ga: Kplukai yɛŋ lɛ ji mealybugs ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛshiɔ wuo ni ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛye lɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛsɛɛ. Aŋkroaŋkroi buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ahe Shi ŋmeii baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni naa wa tamɔ cocoa bud virus lɛ ashwã.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree if I want it to yield more?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni mawo yibiiwoo lɛ mli babaoo?

english: Pruning removes dead or excess branches so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree. This directs the tree's energy into making pods rather than growing useless leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa ni ebaakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do water sprouts keep growing from the base of my tree trunk, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu tso ko miida kɛmiijɛ mitso lɛ shishi lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ majie loo esaaa akɛ majie?

english: Water sprouts are fast-growing shoots that steal water and food away from the main fruiting branches. Removing them early ensures your tree keeps its strength for pod production.
ga: Nu mli dumɔwui ji tsei ni shwereɔ oya ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ niji titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli. Ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. This disease slows down crop growth and reduces harvest, so affected plants should be removed early or replaced with disease-resistant seed sticks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. loo akɛ dumɔwui ni afolɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ awo najiaŋ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet and humid weather. Clearing heavy weeds around the tree and pruning dense branches lets sunlight and air flow through, which stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni tsii ni yɔɔ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haaa ŋmei lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why is my maize growing tall but producing very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa shi ewoɔ toi bibii waa lɛ?

english: Tall maize stalks with tiny cobs usually mean the plants are crowded too close together or the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus. Giving plants proper spacing and feeding the soil helps build bigger, fuller cobs.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni afee ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ nii babaoo.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from prolonged dry weather or lack proper nutrients in the soil. Protecting young trees with shade crops and enriching the soil helps the tree retain its flowers to grow pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Tsei bibii ahe ni akɛ tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi amli koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily before the fruit bunches are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani aduawai akuu lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, making trees fall during strong winds or when tiny soil pests damage root bases. Supporting heavy trees with wooden poles and piling fresh topsoil around the base helps keep them stable.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ha tso lɛ agbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fite shishitoo lɛ. Tsei ni tsii ni akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fiɔ amɛsɛɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ hee ni akɛwoɔ amɛshishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: What is eating large holes in my tomato leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni ye bu agbo ko yɛ tomato baa mli nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: Holes eaten into tomato leaves overnight are usually caused by night-feeding caterpillars like armyworms or cutworms. Checking under leaves early in the morning or using approved organic treatments can protect your plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni taoɔ niyenii gbɛkɛ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yeɔ tomato baai lɛ amli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei lɛ ashishi leebi loo okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Pepper plants wilt in strong midday heat because leaves lose moisture faster than roots can draw water from the soil. The plants usually recover as the evening cools down, but light shade can help reduce heat stress.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baagboi yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli ejaakɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ ahe waa kɛji gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i ba. Shi hulutsoo be ni mli tse lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eba dɔlɛ he haomɔ shi.

english: Why are some of my plant seeds taking much longer to sprout than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi heɔ be babaoo fe ekrokomɛi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Uneven sprouting happens when seeds are planted at different depths or when seed quality is poor. Planting seeds at an even, shallow depth into well-watered soil ensures they germinate together.
ga: Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ loo kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ehiaaa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ekome kɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and bent underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛbɔle shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yams become small or twisted when planted in hard, rocky, or compacted soil. Making high, soft mounds or ridges of loose soil gives the tuber space to expand smoothly into large shapes.
ga: Sweet potatoes bafeɔ bibii loo efiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, tɛi, loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Gɔji ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ haa tuber he lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo ni efeɔ nɔ ko ni da.

english: Who can I report to if my crops develop a strange plant disease I have never seen before?
ga: Namɔ manyɛ mahã lɛ amaniɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ tso hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ hu? ni minako eko dã

english: You can report unknown crop problems to your district Agricultural Extension Officer or send leaf samples to research stations like those in Tafo or Kumasi, where agricultural experts can test the plants and advise on a cure.
ga: Obaanyɛ obɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe naagbai ni aleee lɛ he amaniɛ otsɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ. Aloo okɛ baai lɛ ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii amaje niiamlitaomɔ he ko, tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ Tafo loo Kumasi lɛ. He ni okwaayeli he nilelɔi baanyɛ aka tsei amɛkwɛ ni amɛwo ŋaa yɛ bɔ ni esa akɛ akwɛ amɛ aha lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow even after I buy and apply expensive fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihe ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the soil has too much water, which prevents roots from breathing and taking up nutrients. It can also happen if the fertilizer was applied at the wrong time or got washed away by heavy rains before the plant could absorb it.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli loo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shwie lɛ dani tso lɛ nyɛ eŋɔ.

english: Why does my farmland yield fewer crops now after years of spraying heavy agrochemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli he nii babaoo lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Continuous use of strong chemical sprays without adding organic matter like compost or manure can kill beneficial soil organisms and cause the soil to harden, making it difficult for plant roots to absorb water and natural nutrients.
ga: Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa. Ebaanyɛ egbe shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: How can I tell when my oil palm fruits are ready to harvest so I get the most oil out of them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-oil palm yibii lɛ efee klalo akɛ akpa koni maná mu babaoo?

english: Oil palm bunches are mature when a few loose fruits naturally detach and fall to the ground, and the outer skin of the fruits changes from a dark, blackish color to a vibrant reddish-orange.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ daraa kwraa kɛ́ aduawai lɛ etse. Fioo komɛi gbee shi ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni aduawai lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ediŋŋ ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn hard and woody when I delay harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tsei beni mikɛ be ni mikɛkpaa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: As cassava plants pass their ideal maturity stage, they stop storing soft starch in their roots and start building tough fibers instead to support the older stem, turning the root flesh woody and hard.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ ho edalɛ be ni sa lɛ mli lɛ Amɛkpaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ tsɔji ni wa moŋ koni amɛkɛfi tso lɛ shishifã lɛ sɛɛ Ehaa shishifã lɛ mli fãji lɛ feɔ tso ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and droop during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural survival trick where the plant reduces its leaf surface area exposed to direct sunlight, helping it conserve water and prevent drying out during hot afternoons.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa. Tsei lɛ baaha amɛbaai ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaaa baa lɛ agbi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my young oil palm trees turn yellow and dry up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi oya lɛ?

english: While palms naturally shed their oldest lower leaves, widespread yellowing on young plants usually points to a lack of key nutrients like potassium or nitrogen in the soil.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their small young pods before they can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miishwie amɛbii bibii lɛ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is known as pod wilt, which happens when the tree experiences extreme dry weather stress, insect attack, or simply lacks enough nutrients to feed all the pods it initially produced.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ pod ni shwieɔ shi. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa, kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ mli ŋmeii fɛɛ ni efee yɛ shishijee mli lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce plenty of flowers but drop them all without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ekɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when air temperatures are too hot, when watering is irregular, or when there are no insect pollinators around to fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wo la tsɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni ejaaa Aloo be mli ni kooloi ni feɔ pollin lɛ bɛ he fɛɛ he. Koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔ

english: Why do weeds make my young cocoa seedlings grow so slowly during their first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that rapidly absorb water, sunlight, and soil nutrients right out from under young cocoa plants, starving the young trees during their crucial growth phase.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ oya. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei bibii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into fine powder after keeping them in the barn for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powda kpakpa beni akɛto ŋmɔ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storage pests like maize weevils lay eggs inside the kernels, and when the larvae hatch, they eat the grain from the inside out, leaving behind empty shells that easily crush into powder.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Eshiɔ ŋmei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni fãa oya ni etsɔɔ powda.

english: How can I set up my field so that one main water source can reach all my different farm plots?
ga: Mato ŋmɔji lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ bɔni afee ni nu jɛɛhe titri kome pɛ ashɛ ŋmɔji srɔtoi lɛ ahe. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná minɔ lɛ?

english: You can dig a main central trench or run a main pipe along the border of your farms, then create smaller side channels or tap points to direct water into specific crop sections whenever they need it.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nubu wulu ko yɛ teŋgbɛ loo okɛ paipi wulu ko atsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa. No sɛɛ lɛ, feemɔ sɛɛ gbɛ bibioo ko. loo he ko ni akɛ nu baa koni akɛ nu aya ŋmɔ pɔtɛɛ ko mli be fɛɛ be ni ehe baahia.

english: How far apart should I plant my okra so the plants don't crowd each other?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu okra yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ tɛŋŋ koni tsei lɛ akabɔle amɛhe?

english: Okra should be planted about 60 centimeters apart in rows that are 75 to 90 centimeters apart, giving each plant enough space to branch out and receive sunlight.
ga: Esa akɛ adu okra aaafee sɛntimita 60 yɛ sɛɛgbɛ, sɛntimita 75 kɛyashi 90, koni eha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ niji ajie ehe kpo ni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ.

english: How deep into the soil am I supposed to put okra seeds when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi okra dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Okra seeds should be planted about 2 to 3 centimeters deep into moist soil so they can easily sprout and push through the surface.
ga: Esa akɛ adu okra dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyashɛ sɛntimitai 2 kɛyashi 3 bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to sprout even after I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Seeds often fail to sprout if they are buried too deep, planted in dry soil without enough moisture, or if heavy rain causes the seeds to rot in soggy earth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Aloo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha dumɔwui lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I make sure I am planting healthy seeds and not bad ones?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ midu dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ shi jeee dumɔwui ni ehiii?

english: Select clean, unbroken seeds, and test them by placing them in water; seeds that sink to the bottom are generally healthy and ready to grow, while floating seeds are usually hollow or damaged.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui ni he tse ni etseee. ni akaa lɛ akwɛɔ kɛtsɔ nu mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ Dumɔwui ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi lɛ bei pii lɛ, amɛyɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ dumɔwui ni hoɔ lɛ mli ewo muji loo efite.

english: What special care do seeds need once they reach the germination stage in the field?
ga: Mɛɛ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ he hiaa dumɔwui beni amɛshɛɔ be ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds start sprouting, keep the topsoil consistently moist but not flooded, and protect the soft young shoots from harsh direct sunlight and pests.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ shi nu akaho nɔ. ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it good to start planting fast-growing crops like okra before my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mabɔi tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ okra lɛ akwɛmɔ dani mitsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Starting with fast-growing crops like okra gives you early food and income while your longer-term crops are still establishing themselves on the field.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tso ko ni daa oya tamɔ okra je shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha oná niyenii kɛ shika oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ miitswa amɛhe shi yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lolo.

english: How can I organize my field workers so that planting is done quickly without wasting time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ koni adu nii oya ni mifiteee be?

english: Divide the farm work into simple step-by-step tasks, assigning specific workers to dig holes, others to drop seeds, and others to cover and water them.
ga: Jaa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ awo nitsumɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo mli kɛtsɔ nitsulɔi pɔtɛɛ ni oooha amɛ koni amɛtsa bu lɛ nɔ. Ha mɔ kroko adũ dumɔwui lɛ, ni mɔ kroko hu aha nɔ ni efɔ nɔ nu.

english: How do I know when my crops are ready for buyers who come directly to the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee klalo kɛha jarayelɔi ni baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Crops like okra are ready to sell when the pods are full, bright green, and snap easily when bent, which is the tender stage buyers prefer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ okra lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaahɔ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ eyi obɔ. ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efoɔ oya kɛji ebɔle Enɛ ji gbɛ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow while the plant is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's lifecycle helps restore nutrients and keeps the leaves green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ tso lɛ wala be mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava stems too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava too close causes the plants to fight for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in tall, thin stems with small tubers instead of thick, healthy root crops.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ mli baa ji tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yitsei bibii. Mohu ɔ, tso ɔ ngɛ sisifãhi nɛ mi wa nɛ a he wa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When weather becomes extremely hot and dry, pepper plants drop flowers to conserve moisture and protect themselves from heat stress. Providing shade or regular irrigation during hot spells helps keep the flowers on the plant.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be loo nu shwie nɔ daa yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plant is sick from a leaf disease or just thirsty for water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ emɔ amɛ kɛ baa hela loo kumai miiye amɛ kɛkɛ?

english: A thirsty tomato plant will perk up within a few hours after receiving water. A diseased plant will stay wilted, droop, or display dark spots and yellow patches on its leaves regardless of how much water you give it.
ga: Tomato tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni amɛná nu lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baagboi, amɛbaagbee shi, loo amɛbaaná ŋmɔtɔi diji kɛ ŋmɔtɔi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Nu abɔ ni okɛhaa lɛ kɔɔɔ he eko.

english: Why shouldn't I keep seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ hybrid corn dumɔwui lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed for high yields in their first generation. If you plant the harvested seeds from that crop, the resulting plants lose those special qualities, leading to uneven growth and lower yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ tsɔɔ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ Tsei ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafite nakai nibii krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant groundnuts or beans together with maize in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally pulls nitrogen from the air and feeds it into the soil. This enriches the soil naturally, helping the neighboring maize grow better without extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai krokomɛi fataaa he.

english: Why do my harvested yams start softening and sprouting so fast when stored inside my house?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ blɛoo ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya waa kɛ́ akɛto mishia lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that react to heat and warm air by breaking down internal starch to sprout. Storing them off the ground in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated barn slows down this process and preserves their freshness.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni kɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mligbalamɔ nɔ, ni no haa amɛshwereɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha amɛhi shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha nifeemɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha nɔ ni yɔɔ ehee lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted vegetables right after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe aduawai ni midu yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants natively adapted to the local environment with extensive root systems. They absorb rainwater and nutrients far more aggressively than domestic crop seeds, allowing them to shoot up quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshihilɛ mli ni amɛshishifãi babaoo yɔɔ. Amɛheɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ fe shia dumɔwui. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why does my cocoa tree yield fewer pods when the leaves and branches become too thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ be mli ni baai kɛ eniji lɛ ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Overgrown cocoa branches block sunlight from reaching the trunk and prevent air circulation. This creates dark, humid conditions that encourage fungal diseases like black pod and stop new flowers from growing.
ga: Kookoo niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ akabote mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli edɔ ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji ahe hewalɛ ni ekpaa fɔfɔi heei adalɛ.

english: Why does leaving a portion of my land unused for a year make crops grow better when I plant there again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ mishi mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko ni mikɛtsuuu nii afi kome lɛ, ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu nii yɛ jɛmɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving land fallow allows natural vegetation to decay and return organic matter into the ground. This gives the soil time to rest, rebuild exhausted nutrients, and restore moisture balance naturally.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe. Ha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni efite lɛ afee ekoŋŋ ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli fɛ̃i lɛ aba shi ekoŋŋ

english: Do plantain plants really need a lot of water to grow well?
ga: Ani nu babaoo he miihia plantains diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, plantains require a constant and generous supply of water because their trunk and large leaves store a lot of moisture. Without enough water, their growth slows down significantly.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni yaa nɔ daa ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia plantains. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛtsei wuji kɛ amɛbaai lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Dalɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and look weak during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When rainfall drops, plantains cannot draw enough water from the soil to maintain their heavy leaves and stem structure, causing the foliage to dry out and the plant to lose strength.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ ajie nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ amɛbaai ni tsii kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbiɔ ni tso lɛ he waaa.

english: Why do plantains seem to need more water than many other crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa plantains fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Plantain stems and fruits are mostly made of water, and their roots are shallow, meaning they cannot reach deep underground water sources like some other crops can.
ga: Nu ji nɔ ni akɛfeɔ plantain tsei kɛ amɛyibii babaoo. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛnáaa nu ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tamɔ tsei krokomɛi lɛ.

english: How does watering my plantain farm affect the sweetness and taste of the fruit?
ga: Te nu ni mikɛwoɔ mi dumɔwui aŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa aduawai lɛ amli ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Water helps the plantain plant produce and transport natural sugars into the developing fruit, which makes the plantains taste sweet and rich when they mature.
ga: Nu yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli sugars ni amɛkɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ, ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli kɛ́ eda kwraa.

english: Can giving my plantain crops too little water reduce the size of my harvest?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛwoɔ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ baanyɛ aha mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Yes, water shortages during fruit development lead to smaller stems, fewer fruits per bunch, and thin, lightweight plantains.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni faaa yɛ aduawai lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ haa tsei bibii baa. Yibii fioo komɛi yɛ kuu kome mli kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa

english: Can I manually water my plantain farm using pipes or hoses if it does not rain?
ga: Ani mi diɛŋtsɛ manyɛ mikɛ hose loo hose aha mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Yes, applying water manually through pipes or buckets directly to the base of plantain plants is an effective way to keep them healthy during dry periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ hose loo baagi mli yɛ plantains lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: What should I do to care for my plantains when there is a long break in rainfall?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni makwɛ plantain tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: You should actively irrigate or water your crops regularly and apply organic cover, like dry leaves around the roots, to keep the soil moist until the rain returns.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nu loo okɛ nu awo otsei lɛ amli daa. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ baai ni egbi, abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Should I still water my plantain farm if it only rained a tiny bit earlier in the week?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ fioo pɛ yɛ otsi lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Light rainfall often only wets the surface soil and does not reach deep roots, so you should check the soil depth and provide extra water if the ground is dry below the surface.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ pɛ, shi jeee kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ha, ni okɛ nu kroko aha kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: How can I tell if my plantain plants are getting enough water from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: A well-watered plantain has broad green leaves, a thick firm trunk, and steady new leaves opening, while a thirsty plant shows yellowing or drooping leaves.
ga: Plantains ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii ni mli kwɔ, ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ baai heei ni wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ baaná baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ loo ni shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I trap moisture in the soil around my plantains so water does not evaporate quickly?
ga: Mamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee plantains koni nu akatsɔ oya?

english: Spreading dry leaves, grass, or crop waste around the base of the plantain stem creates a protective layer that keeps the soil cool and holds moisture longer.
ga: Baai ni egboi, jwɛi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Plantain shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land is good for farming before I pay to rent it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ko hi kɛha okwaayeli? Dani obaawo shĩa nyɔmɔ?

english: Look at the wild plants and trees growing naturally on the land; tall, dark green foliage usually signals fertile soil. You can also dig up a handful of earth—if it is dark, loose, and crumbles easily while holding a little moisture, crops will grow well in it.
ga: Naa koo mli tsei kɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Baai kakadaji, ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii. Obaanyɛ otsa shikpɔŋ ko hu kɛji akɛ edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nakai sũ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I only have a small plot of land, can I plant maize and cassava together without them destroying each other?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome ni amɛfiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, maize and cassava work very well together because they grow at different speeds. The maize grows quickly and is harvested within a few months, leaving the cassava with plenty of space and time to mature underground.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ naa hegbɛ kɛ be babaoo ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Can I save seeds from my current maize harvest to plant next season, or do I need to buy new seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei?

english: Traditional local seeds can be saved and replanted, but high-yield hybrid seeds bought from suppliers only produce a strong harvest once. Replanting saved hybrid seeds usually results in weak plants and a very poor yield.
ga: Abaanyɛ ahere maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ ayiwala ni adu ekoŋŋ. Shi dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni kɛ nibii lɛ baa lɛ adɛŋ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo ni mli wa aba shikome pɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛhe saji awo mli ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi waa baa.

english: How deep into the dirt should I put my maize seeds when planting so they do not rot or fail to grow?
ga: Kɛ́ midu nii lɛ, te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ? Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akagbo loo amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Plant maize seeds about two inches deep, which is roughly the length of your thumb up to the first knuckle. Burying seeds too deep wastes their energy before they reach the sun, while planting too shallow leaves them to dry out or be eaten by birds.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee inchi 2, ni ji aaafee oshishifa lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ kɛyashi klɛŋklɛŋ tsitsi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaafite hewalɛ dani eshɛ hulu lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo okpoi aye amɛ.

english: Which crops can I plant that will give a good yield without needing expensive chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu ni woɔ yibii kpakpai ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he?

english: Legumes like cowpeas, groundnuts, and soybeans are excellent choices because they gather nitrogen directly from the air and feed the soil, allowing them to grow well with very little or no chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas, peanuts, kɛ soybeans ji nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛbuaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsofa fioo ko pɛ loo nɔ ko kwraa bɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds always grow so much faster than my crops even when I clear the land completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jɛmɛ fɛɛ moŋ

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally suited to the local soil, so their roots quickly grab up water and food before your young crop roots can spread. Clearing weeds early gives your crops a fighting chance to get established.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni sa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya dani otsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛwuu.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants start to curl up and turn yellow during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to protect themselves and reduce water loss when the sun is too strong. Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant is stressed from lack of water or nutrients, which can be corrected by watering and adding compost.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛha nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao yɛ nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Abaanyɛ asaa enɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the bare dirt around my young plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket that keeps the sun from drying out the soil, keeps the root zone cool, and stops weeds from popping up.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops so it doesn't waste my money?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni mikafite shika?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and when the plants are actively growing, usually a few weeks after planting. Avoid spreading fertilizer right before heavy downpours, as the rain will wash the plant food away before the roots can drink it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛ be mli ni tsei miida jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he dani nugbɔ anɛ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ shwieɔ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of ground every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes in the same spot repeatedly allows tomato-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt, making each new crop weaker. Swapping the land with corn or beans starves those pests and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Enɛ baaha kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni kɔɔ tomato he pɔtɛɛ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii heei fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmeii lɛ, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and dry out. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects the cocoa from harsh sun and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curling and yellowing leaves on cassava are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus weakens the plant, preventing it from making enough food to grow big roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Virus haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi wuji lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What causes my maize plants to turn yellow at the bottom leaves while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi be mli ni amɛmiida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the soil is lacking nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food plant leaves need to stay dark green and grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ni tsei ahe baai lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water. When the plant feels stressed by heat or drought, it drops its flowers to save energy to stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji tsei miihao kɛjɛ latsaa loo hɔmɔ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato koni amɛhi wala mli.
